feat: Memory Statistics and Analytics Dashboard (#203)

* feat: Add storage statistics and unique user retrieval

Introduce abstract methods for retrieving storage statistics and unique
user IDs
in `VectorStoreBase` and `GraphStoreBase`. This commit also includes
general import
cleanup and minor refactoring across core, storage, and server
components.

* feat: Integrate web dashboard

This commit introduces a new web-based dashboard for PowerMem, providing
a user interface to monitor and manage memory data.

- New `dashboard/` directory: Contains a complete React application
  built with Vite, TanStack Router/Query, and Shadcn UI components.
- Build process integration:
  - .github/workflows/publish.yml updated to build the dashboard and
    package its static assets with the Python server.
  - docker/Dockerfile modified to include a frontend build stage,
    ensuring the dashboard is part of the Docker image.
  - pyproject.toml configured to include dashboard assets in the Python
    distribution.
- Server-side serving: src/server/main.py updated to serve the compiled
  dashboard static files under the /dashboard/ endpoint.
- Documentation: docs/development/overview.md updated with instructions
  for building the dashboard locally.

* feat: Add memory statistics and user lookup for PGVector

Implement `get_statistics` and `get_unique_users` methods for the
PGVector
store. This includes adding a `created_at` timestamp column to track
memory age and growth, with a fallback for existing tables.

`get_statistics` provides insights into total count, type distribution,
average importance, top-accessed items, growth trends, and age
distribution of memories.

Minor import reformatting in `oceanbase_graph.py` and test files is
also included.

* revert: Revert format changes

* fix: Improve scope resolution and config loading robustness

*   Make `_determine_scope` more resilient to invalid string inputs and
    ensure
    default scopes are always `MemoryScope` enums, adding 'AGENT' and
    'USER'
    aliases.
*   Safely extract `scope` and `memory_type` values in memory metadata
    to prevent
    AttributeErrors when values are not enums.
*   Refine component provider and configuration retrieval to correctly
    handle
    `None` values and ensure proper fallbacks.
*   Add `provider` and `config` properties to `BaseEmbedderConfig` for
    flexible
    extraction of settings, including those from Pydantic `model_extra`.
*   Enhance test environment cleanup for better isolation.

fix(workbuddy): reduce the host prompt to the submitted turn before recall (#1703)

* fix(workbuddy): reduce the host prompt to the submitted turn before recall

WorkBuddy submits every user message of the session joined into one prompt, and each of
those messages carries its injected context block. For one real session the joined prompt
measured 339526 characters and 413769 bytes, far beyond the 8192 character bound of the
request's query. The hook passed that text through as the retrieval query, so
`/v1/context/prepare` rejected it and the recall came back empty without reporting
anything.

Retrieve with the trailing `<user_query>` element instead. It holds the turn being
submitted, and that turn is what the session's earlier memories should be retrieved
against. A prompt the element cannot be read from falls back to the joined text trimmed to
the request bounds, so the hook keeps working against a host that changes shape.

Report a reduction on stderr: the recall itself fails open, so a query that was silently
rewritten is otherwise invisible.

* fix(workbuddy): validate the host wrapper and decouple capture from recall

Review of #1703 reproduced two defects in the reduction added there.

`_last_user_query` matched the tags wherever they occur, so a prompt quoting this
markup - a user pasting it, or a summary the host writes about this code - was read as
the wrapper and sent a fragment of the quoting sentence as the query. A pair opening
before the current question also dropped that question entirely. The element is now
accepted only where its boundaries match the host's wrapper: the opening tag starts a
line and the closing tag ends the message, with the start of the next host block or the
end of the prompt after it. Candidates are tried from the end backwards, so a later
block that quotes the tags no longer hides the turn before it. A prompt no verified
element can be read from falls back to the bounded joined text.

The `and query` guard added to the recall also gated the Source capture and the optional
flush, so a turn reducing to nothing silently skipped the Source write. Capture is back
under the `scope_id` guard and only the recall depends on a usable query.

Replaying the session transcript of #1702 with the tags quoted in a later block: the
query went from `"`、`_USER_QUERY_CLOSE="` to `缺陷 1 的 hook 侧防御也顺手做`, the turn
the hook retrieved against when the reduction was verified. The new cases in
`tests/workbuddy_plugin/test_hook.py` fail against the previous reduction.

* fix(workbuddy): only trust a wrapper whose closing tag ends its host block

Self-review of the boundary check added here found a false positive left in it.

A pair followed by anything starting with `<` was accepted, but a pair quoted inside
another element is followed by that element's own closing tag. Enumerating all 19
candidate pairs of the session transcript of #1702, 9 of them - every turn the cb_summary
blocks quote - passed the check. That transcript still resolved to the submitted turn
because the last verified pair happened to come after them, so the difference only shows
when a block that quotes the tags arrives after the submitted turn, which is the usual
shape once a session gets long enough to be summarised.

The check now requires the next non-whitespace content after the closing tag to be an
opening tag or the end of the prompt. That separates all 19 pairs of that transcript and
both pairs of the current session: the 5 real wrappers are followed by the next host
block, the 9 quoted pairs by `</previous_user_message>`.

Walking the remainder by index also replaces the `str.strip` and `str.lstrip` copies made
once per candidate. On a 411 KB prompt carrying 2,000 pairs the reduction takes 0.51 ms.

* docs(workbuddy): record the recall query reduction in the hook contract

The Runtime behavior list described Recall as sending the prompt to
`/v1/context/prepare`, which stopped being true when the reduction landed, and the
diagnostics bullet claimed status and byte counts only after the `query_reduction` event
added a source and a truncation flag.

* fix(workbuddy): keep literal tag turns in recall

* fix(workbuddy): pair a recall candidate with its own closing tag

The reduction accepted an opening tag as the host wrapper as soon as any closing tag
after it reached a message boundary. A pair the turn quotes is nested, or left unclosed,
and then a literal opener paired with the host's own closing tag, so the text between the
two became the query. On the fenced example from the review the hook sent
`example</user_query>` followed by the example's closing fence instead of the turn, and an
unclosed literal opener gave the turn up to the bounded fallback, whose tail is the
injected context block rather than the turn.

A candidate now resolves its own close, counting nested pairs as turn content, and a
candidate enclosed by an earlier one gives way to its container. Reading the outer element
covers the case the previous revision left out, where a quoted pair ends exactly where the
next host block opens and no boundary test can separate it from the wrapper. An element no
close balances still ends at the first close that reaches a message boundary, so a turn
whose literal opener is never closed stays whole.

hits.message:
feat(init): AskUserQuestion interactive flow + remote-init mode + dashboard 0.0.0.0 (#1101)

* feat(init): add interactive config prompts with AskUserQuestion support

- Add ask_user() shell function with 3-layer bypass (NON_INTERACTIVE, pre-set
  var, non-TTY) for users running init.sh from a terminal
- Add prompt_user_config() that asks storage backend (sqlite/oceanbase),
  LLM provider (noop/anthropic/openai/...), and embedding provider (local/cloud)
- Wire into init.sh main flow, right before create_env_file, so answers are
  consumed as POWERMEM_INIT_* env vars by the embedded Python config generator
- Enhance /init skill SKILL.md with explicit AskUserQuestion instructions:
  conditional 3-question flow, env-var mapping, and POWERMEM_NON_INTERACTIVE=1
  invocation template for the Claude Code plugin path

* fix(init): refine SKILL.md to skip Storage prompt when server is healthy

When the server is already running and .env has DATABASE_PROVIDER set,
show the current backend instead of asking the user to reconfigure.
Only ask the Storage question when config is genuinely missing.

* feat(plugin): add remote-init short-circuit and 0.0.0.0 default host

init.sh gains a remote-init short-circuit: when POWERMEM_INIT_BASE_URL
(or non-localhost POWERMEM_BASE_URL) is provided, it skips .env, uvx,
and PID management, writing only runtime.env and/or .mcp.json per
POWERMEM_INIT_CONNECTION_MODE (hook|mcp|both, default both).

Dashboard default host changes from 127.0.0.1 to 0.0.0.0, overridable
via POWERMEM_SERVER_HOST, so the dashboard is reachable across
containers / remote hosts by default.

status.sh becomes mode-aware: reads runtime.env (hook_url) and
${PLUGIN_ROOT}/.mcp.json (mcp_url) and reports mode=hook|mcp|both|none.
common.sh gains shared helpers (is_remote_url, is_healthy,
write_runtime_remote) used by both scripts.

* feat(init): AskUserQuestion flow with mode-aware status SKILL

init SKILL.md describes a 3-round AskUserQuestion flow (Storage →
LLM → Embedding) that replaces the shell-level interactive prompts.
Each question is asked only when the relevant config is missing,
and CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT is resolved per-invocation rather than
baked into shell env. When the server is already healthy with a
configured DATABASE_PROVIDER, the Storage question is skipped.

status SKILL.md documents the new hook|mcp|both|none mode reporting
and how to read runtime.env / .mcp.json.

* refactor(embeddings): extract shared model-cache helpers

Move is_model_cached, detect_country, download_via_modelscope, and
bridge_modelscope_to_hf_cache out of pyseekdb_default.py into a new
_model_cache.py module so both pyseekdb_default and huggingface can
share the same CN-mirror download / cache-bridge logic without
duplication. Tests are updated to patch _model_cache instead of
pyseekdb_default internals.

* fix(init): make 0.0.0.0 opt-in via Question 0, restore loopback default

Restore 127.0.0.1 as the script default for POWERMEM_SERVER_HOST so
loopback remains the local exposure model. All-interface binding
(0.0.0.0) becomes an explicit user choice: Question 0 of the
AskUserQuestion flow now splits "Local" into two options —
loopback-only and all-interfaces — and maps the answer to
POWERMEM_SERVER_HOST before invoking init.sh.

Update the uvx-launcher test to assert the new parameterized form
`--host "${POWERMEM_SERVER_HOST:-127.0.0.1}"` instead of the old
hardcoded `--host 127.0.0.1`. Addresses PR #1101 review feedback.

* fix(init): write remote MCP config to user-scope, not plugin cache

Remote MCP mode was writing to $PLUGIN_ROOT/.mcp.json (the plugin cache
dir), which is volatile — wiped on every plugin uninstall+install — so
the user's remote MCP config was lost on reinstalls. It also could not
take effect without a plugin reload.

Register the powermem MCP server in the user-scope config instead, via
the `claude mcp add --scope user --transport http` CLI. The CLI decides
where to store it (typically ~/.claude.json top-level mcpServers) so the
location tracks the current Claude Code version / platform rather than
being hardcoded. Hook-only mode runs `claude mcp remove powermem
--scope user` to disable MCP, preserving any other MCP servers.

Adds write_user_mcp_config / remove_user_mcp_config helpers in common.sh
that wrap the CLI with a PATH check and idempotent remove-then-add.

* fix(init): address PR #1101 review — quote runtime.env, disable hook in MCP mode

Four review issues on the user-scope MCP config commit (9f5ac95):

1. write_runtime_remote wrote URLs/keys bare, so shell metacharacters
   ($, ;, spaces, backticks, quotes) broke sourcing by run-hook.sh /
   status.sh. Switch to single-quoted values with '\'' escaping.

2. status.sh read $PLUGIN_ROOT/.mcp.json for the MCP URL, but that file is
   the volatile plugin-cache config (always empty since 9f5ac95 moved
   writes to user-scope). Read ~/.claude.json top-level mcpServers.powermem.url
   instead — the file the `claude mcp` CLI actually writes to.

3. MCP-only mode wrote nothing to runtime.env, leaving stale
   POWERMEM_BASE_URL from a prior hook/both init. The hook binary then
   ran against the old URL. Now write_runtime_hook_disabled() emits
   POWERMEM_HOOK_DISABLED=1, and run-hook.sh checks that marker after
   loading runtime.env and exits 0 before exec'ing the native binary.

4. common.sh had trailing blank lines at EOF (git diff --check).

Also tightens Round 1 remote follow-up AskUserQuestion wording in
SKILL.md: dedup the two URL placeholder options into distinct HTTP/HTTPS
protocol hints; clarify Hook mode works when auth is disabled or a key
was provided. Both connection mode retained per user request.

Adds regression tests for the quoting, hook-disabled marker, run-hook
early exit, and init.sh mcp-branch wiring.

* fix(init): drop "None" embedding option for OceanBase

OceanBase requires a vector embedding field to store memories, so
embeddings are mandatory. Offering "None" in the AskUserQuestion Round 3
options for the OceanBase storage path would let users pick an invalid
combination. SQLite keeps "None" since it can fall back to non-vector
storage; OceanBase only offers "Built-in seekdb" and "Cloud (<provider>)".

Also clarifies the mapping line: POWERMEM_INIT_EMBEDDING_PROVIDER=none is
now annotated "SQLite only".

hits.message:
fix(mcp): give Review write tools ToolAnnotations so hosts can prompt (#1392)

* fix(mcp): annotate Review write tools so hosts can prompt

`_annotate_mcp_component` promises to "describe the side effects that an
MCP host should use for approval decisions", but its branches only cover
the read-only set, `handoff_current_work`, and `commit_handoff`.
`approve_artifact_candidate`, `reject_artifact_candidate`, and
`revise_artifact_candidate` fall through and are projected with
`annotations: None`, so a host has nothing to key a confirmation prompt
off for the three Review operations that change Candidate state.

Project them with `destructiveHint=True` and add a regression test
mirroring the existing handoff annotation test. The projected tool set is
unchanged; annotations are advisory hints, not an authorization boundary
(RFC 0050).

Relates to #1391.

* fix(mcp): mark Review write tools idempotent per MCP replay semantics

MCP defines idempotentHint by additional environment effect, not by the
retry returning the same successful response. An exact replay of
approve/reject/revise is rejected by the pending-head CAS
(ArtifactCandidateRepository.lock_pending) before any Candidate version,
Artifact revision, index update, or status transition is written, so
repeated identical calls have no additional effect. Requested in review.

fix(workbuddy): keep prompt hooks from stalling on scope reads (#1729)

* fix(workbuddy): keep prompt hooks from stalling on scope reads

WorkBuddy prompt submission should fail open within the scope binding HTTP budget even when a server response stalls after headers arrive.

Constraint: WorkBuddy enforces an outer UserPromptSubmit hook timeout

Scope-risk: narrow

Tested: uv run pytest tests/workbuddy_plugin/test_scope_binding.py -q

Tested: uv run ruff check integrations/workbuddy/plugins/powercontext/scripts/workspace_scope.py tests/workbuddy_plugin/conftest.py tests/workbuddy_plugin/test_scope_binding.py

Tested: uv run ruff format --check integrations/workbuddy/plugins/powercontext/scripts/workspace_scope.py tests/workbuddy_plugin/conftest.py tests/workbuddy_plugin/test_scope_binding.py

Co-authored-by: OmX <omx@oh-my-codex.dev>

* fix(workbuddy): bound hook response reads at every socket receive

f42a2bf4 added an absolute deadline around the scope resolver's response body,
but it still tightened urllib's socket timeout only once per 64 KiB block read.
http.client consumes many socket reads inside a single read call, so a server
that trickles a byte faster than that timeout keeps the caller inside one read
and past its deadline; the observed worst case is the host's 30s
UserPromptSubmit timeout, which is exactly what the change set out to remove.

Reuse the primitives the claude-code and codex scope modules already ship:

- open_bounded runs the request in a daemon worker, so connect and header
  exchange stay inside the caller's budget.
- bind_response_deadline recomputes the remaining time before every receive,
  framing included.

Both now cover the scope resolver and the hook's own recall, capture, and flush
reads. The hook shares them through the installed powercontext_scope_binding
shim instead of carrying its own opener, so the shim forwards them too.
_set_response_timeout reads the socket through a guarded getattr chain, so a
missing fp can no longer raise AttributeError outside the scope client's error
contract.

The deadline test replaces its fake socket with real loopback properties: body
drip, header drip, a large healthy response, an expired deadline, and the hook's
own recall read. The three drip cases fail on f42a2bf4 (3.19s, 3.17s, 3.20s
against a 1.0s assertion) and pass here.

feat(embedder): zero-config startup with built-in default embedder; split .env.example (closes #940 #941 #949 #948 #) (#945)

* feat(embedder): zero-config startup with built-in local default embedder

Closes #940, closes #941.

Previously a fresh MemoryConfig() defaulted to OpenAIEmbeddingConfig and
text-embedding-3-small, which made the "default" path require an
OPENAI_API_KEY before the system could run — no real zero-config story.

This change introduces a built-in default embedder that mirrors pyseekdb's
DefaultEmbeddingFunction (sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2 via ONNX,
384 dims) so PowerMem boots end-to-end with no API key and no external
service. The model auto-downloads to the local cache on first use and runs
entirely locally afterwards. Switching to a production embedder is a single
config field.

Alongside that, .env.example is split into a minimal version (just the LLM
key block, ~5 vars) and .env.example.full (every existing knob, grouped by
component) so first-time users aren't drowned in options. README, README_CN,
and README_JP all point at both files.

Changes:
- New PyseekdbDefaultEmbedding wrapper + PyseekdbDefaultEmbeddingConfig
  registered under provider name "default"
- MemoryConfig.embedder.default_factory now PyseekdbDefaultEmbeddingConfig
- .env.example trimmed to the strictly required keys; full reference moved
  to .env.example.full with an updated header that points back
- README / README_CN / README_JP updated to reflect zero-config defaults
- Unit tests: embedder round-trip, factory registry, and zero-config
  MemoryConfig() (mock pyseekdb so no model download in CI)

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(storage): seekdb as the default vector store, sharing OceanBase backend

Adds `seekdb` as a first-class database provider name, registered to the same
`OceanBaseVectorStore` class as `oceanbase` (SeekDB is OceanBase running
embedded — same engine, same SQL surface, only configuration differs). Promotes
seekdb to the default everywhere it matters:

  - MemoryConfig.vector_store.default_factory: SQLiteConfig -> SeekDBConfig
  - DatabaseSettings.provider env default:     "sqlite"     -> "seekdb"
  - core/memory.py storage_type fallback:      "oceanbase"  -> "seekdb"
  - deprecated create_config() / CreateConfigOptions default also updated

`SeekDBConfig` subclasses `OceanBaseConfig` and only overrides what differs:
provider name, embedded-mode defaults (empty host, on-disk `./seekdb_data`),
and `SEEKDB_*` env var aliases (each falls back to the corresponding
`OCEANBASE_*` alias, so users can flip `DATABASE_PROVIDER` between `seekdb`
and `oceanbase` without rewriting their `.env`). Same treatment for
`SeekDBGraphConfig` on the graph-store side.

.env.example.full reorders the database section to lead with embedded SeekDB,
and `.env.example` (minimal) now advertises SeekDB + the local embedder as the
zero-config defaults. README/CN/JP follow suit.

Tests: 7 new unit tests pin the contract — provider registration, shared
class path between `seekdb` and `oceanbase`, embedded-mode defaults,
SEEKDB_* env aliases, MemoryConfig() default, and DatabaseSettings()
default. Full unit suite: 193 passed (up from 186).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs(brand): lowercase 'SeekDB' -> 'seekdb' in all user-visible text

Per product branding, the canonical spelling is lowercase `seekdb`. This
commit normalizes every user-visible occurrence across the repo:

  - Config templates: .env.example, .env.example.full
  - READMEs: README.md, README_CN.md, README_JP.md
  - Docs: docs/api/0002-async_memory.md
  - Python docstrings, Field descriptions, comments, log/error strings
    in storage/, utils/, cli/, user_memory/, core/memory.py, server/,
    script/

Intentionally kept (these are code identifiers, not documentation):

  - Class names: `SeekDBConfig`, `SeekDBGraphConfig` (renaming would break
    the public API and violate PascalCase convention for Python classes)
  - Env var prefixes: `SEEKDB_*` (matches the existing `OCEANBASE_*`
    convention — ALL_CAPS for env variables is independent of the brand
    spelling)

Tests still green: 193 passed.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* deps: bump pyseekdb floor to >=1.3.0 (latest)

Per product direction, when PowerMem uses seekdb it should default to the
latest seekdb. The previous floor `>=0.1.0` was permissive enough to resolve
to long-superseded releases on fresh installs; bump it to `>=1.3.0` so users
get the current engine (matching what is already installed in CI / dev
environments).

Tests still green: 193 passed.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs(env): reframe .env.example escape hatch as cherry-pick from .full

The previous wording told users to `cp .env.example.full .env` when they
wanted to tune anything, which throws away the curated minimal file and
exposes the wall of knobs we deliberately hid. The new framing matches how
the file is actually meant to be used: keep .env minimal, and additively
pull individual blocks from .env.example.full when the environment offers
stronger infrastructure (OceanBase cluster, hosted embedding LLM, rerank
LLM, etc.) or you need more performance.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs(env): rewrite .env.example* comments — purpose, recommendation, alternatives

Restructures every section's annotations in both files so each variable now
documents three things explicitly:

  1. What the config *does* — the actual effect, not just the field name.
  2. A recommended value with a short reason.
  3. Alternative options so the reader knows the recommendation is a default,
     not a constraint.

In .env.example (minimal), the single LLM block now explains each variable
(provider / key / model) with named alternatives per provider (qwen-plus →
qwen-max / qwen-turbo / gpt-4o / claude-sonnet-4-6 / local Ollama models).

In .env.example.full, every numbered section gets the same treatment:
database providers (with the seekdb ↔ oceanbase symmetry), LLM, embedding,
rerank, agent scoping, Ebbinghaus decay, performance batches/caches, security
+ encryption, telemetry, audit, logging, skill store, graph store, sparse
embedding, query rewrite, HTTP server (bind / auth / rate limit / CORS),
custom prompts. Each section header also briefly states what subsystem the
block configures and when to bother touching it.

No code changes. 193/193 unit tests pass.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(storage): symmetric SEEKDB_* aliases for schema-shape fields

Before this change, a user running DATABASE_PROVIDER=seekdb could configure
the connection (SEEKDB_PATH, SEEKDB_DATABASE, …) and vector index (SEEKDB_
INDEX_TYPE, SEEKDB_VECTOR_METRIC_TYPE, SEEKDB_EMBEDDING_MODEL_DIMS) with
SEEKDB_* keys, but had to drop down to OCEANBASE_TEXT_FIELD / VECTOR_FIELD /
PRIMARY_FIELD / METADATA_FIELD / VIDX_NAME for the table column names. That
asymmetry forced mixed-namespace .env files for anyone integrating with an
existing schema under seekdb — exactly the friction the SEEKDB_* aliases
were introduced to remove.

This commit adds SEEKDB_TEXT_FIELD, SEEKDB_VECTOR_FIELD, SEEKDB_PRIMARY_
FIELD, SEEKDB_METADATA_FIELD, and SEEKDB_VIDX_NAME aliases on SeekDBConfig,
each with the matching OCEANBASE_* alias kept as a fallback for migrations.
.env.example.full documents them in the seekdb section, and the OceanBase
section cross-references back to it.

Tests pin both directions: SEEKDB_* primary wins, OCEANBASE_* fallback
still resolves. Suite: 195 passed (up from 193).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(storage): close last SEEKDB_* parity gaps — pool, sparse, native hybrid

Audit found four OCEANBASE_* env aliases with no SEEKDB_* counterpart:

  - OCEANBASE_POOL_RECYCLE       (pool_recycle)
  - OCEANBA

hits.message:
Production-readiness review: security fixes, bug fixes, and simplification across CLI and templates (#793)

* fix(template-advanced): read JWT secret from env, drop demo leftovers and broken cache

- Sign and verify JWT tokens with settings.secret_key so the SECRET_KEY
  env var actually takes effect; the hard-coded default constant is gone
  and the app now refuses to start without a configured secret (.env_dev
  ships a clearly-labeled dev-only value, .env.prod is gitignored)
- Remove hello-world leftovers (items/version/config/notification/error
  endpoints) and the python-dotenv dependency
- Remove the in-memory cache (ignored TTL, unbounded, served stale lists)
- Migrate deprecated on_event handlers to lifespan
- Store price conversion in one field_validator (round() fixes 25.99
  coming back as 25.98), return ORM rows directly from product endpoints
- Move DATABASE_URL onto Settings, drop SQL echo, standardize Annotated DI
- Tests: 37 -> 24, all meaningful; auth_headers fixture replaces repeated
  register/login; fixed always-true duplicate-user assertion; new tests
  for rate limiting, secret env wiring, and configured-key sign/verify
- READMEs: drop stale caching/async claims, document SECRET_KEY and
  DATABASE_URL truthfully

* refactor(template-advanced): CORS allowlist, OAuth2 flow, and simplification pass

Security/config:
- CORS: replace wildcard origins + credentials (any site could make
  credentialed requests) with a Settings-driven allowlist defaulting to
  http://localhost:3000; credentials disabled (Bearer tokens, not cookies)
- Upload policy raised to config surface: MAX_UPLOAD_SIZE_BYTES and
  ALLOWED_UPLOAD_TYPES constants, upload_dir on Settings, mkdir in lifespan

Simplification:
- Login uses OAuth2PasswordRequestForm + OAuth2PasswordBearer instead of
  hand-rolled Form fields + HTTPBearer; Swagger Authorize button now works
- get_user_by_username helper dedupes the login/get_current_user query;
  db.get() for PK lookup; bounded pagination (skip>=0, 1<=limit<=100)
- Drop send_personal_message pass-through, dead start-ci Makefile target,
  and redundant websockets pin (bundled with uvicorn[standard])
- Consistent status.* enums; stale TODO and price-unit comment fixes

Tests (26):
- conftest.py points tests at throwaway test.db - the suite previously
  wrote to and dropped the developer's dev app.db; *.db now gitignored
- autouse limiter reset gives each test a fresh rate-limit budget
- register() helper and parametrized invalid-registration cases replace
  repeated boilerplate; CORS allowlist tests added (TDD)

README: fix broken uvicorn quick-start command, stale badge, DDoS claim,
commands table, project tree; document CORS_ORIGINS

* fix(template-advanced): replace unmaintained python-jose with PyJWT

python-jose is effectively abandoned with known CVEs; PyJWT is the
maintained standard. The swap is three lines: import, exception type
(JWTError -> jwt.InvalidTokenError), and the dependency pin. encode and
decode call sites are API-compatible and unchanged. HS256 needs no
crypto extra, so the transitive ecdsa/rsa deps drop out of the tree.

Adds test_protected_endpoint_expired_token to pin expired-token
rejection - previously untested and exactly the behavior a JWT library
swap could silently change.

* fix(template-advanced): sanitize client-supplied upload filenames

The upload endpoint interpolated file.filename straight into the
filesystem path, so a name like ../../evil.txt crashed the endpoint
with an unhandled FileNotFoundError (500) and left path handling to
luck. Stored names are now Path(filename).name (directory components
stripped, empty names fall back to "upload") with a uuid4 prefix,
which also replaces the naive isoformat timestamp that embedded ":"
and could collide on concurrent uploads.

Tests: traversal filenames stay inside the upload dir (was RED with
the FileNotFoundError), plus first success-path coverage verifying
stored content and location. Session fixture creates uploads/ since
module-level TestClient never runs lifespan. uploads/ gitignored so
generated projects do not commit uploaded files.

* fix(template-advanced): stop websocket broadcast skipping connections after a dead one

broadcast() removed dead connections from active_connections while
iterating over it, shifting the list so the connection right after a
dead one silently never received the message. Dead connections are now
collected during the send loop and pruned afterwards. The bare except
(which also swallowed CancelledError) is narrowed to Exception,
dropping the noqa: E722 suppression.

Unit test drives ConnectionManager directly with stub websockets:
[dead, live1, live2] - live1 must still receive the broadcast and the
dead connection must be pruned (was RED: live1 got nothing).

* fix(template-llama): honor temperature=0.0 and stop inference blocking the event loop

- generate_answer used `temperature or settings.llm_temperature`, so an
  explicit, valid temperature of 0.0 (greedy decoding) silently fell
  back to the configured default. Both fallbacks now test `is not None`.
  Unit test drives the service with a stub llm (was RED: 0.3 != 0.0).
- question-answering endpoints are now plain `def` instead of
  `async def`: FastAPI runs them in a worker thread, so multi-second
  synchronous llama.cpp generation no longer freezes the event loop
  (previously /health and all concurrent requests stalled during
  generation).

* fix(template-langchain): honor request generation params and stop inference blocking the event loop

- max_new_tokens and temperature were accepted by the request models
  and service signatures but never reached the pipeline, which was
  frozen with init-time values. A _llm_with_overrides helper now
  applies per-request pipeline_kwargs via llm.bind(); temperature
  explicitly sets do_sample (temperature=0.0 means greedy decoding).
  Test pins max_new_tokens=1 to a few characters beyond the echoed
  prompt (was RED: 448 chars came back) - length-comparison assertions
  are unusable here because the model's generation_config enables
  sampling.
- Generation endpoints are now plain `def` instead of `async def` so
  FastAPI runs them in a worker thread and slow synchronous inference
  no longer freezes the event loop.

* fix: nlp service error codes and blocking, CLI git-init and name validation, root config hygiene

template-nlp:
- get_embeddings/calculate_similarity raised their 503 "not initialized"
  inside their own except Exception, so clients received 500; the guard
  now sits above the try (was RED: 500 != 503)
- explicit temperature=0.0 / max_new_tokens / max_length no longer fall
  back to defaults via falsy `or` (was RED: 0.7 != 0.0, proven with a
  stub tokenizer/model)
- all 12 inference endpoints are plain `def` so FastAPI runs them in
  worker threads and inference no longer freezes the event loop

CLI:
- git init runs with cwd=dest_path instead of os.chdir, which
  permanently mutated the process working directory; a nonzero exit now
  prints a warning instead of silently claiming success
- project names must be ASCII Python identifiers and not keywords;
  the old regex accepted 1app/class, generating projects whose own
  imports were syntax errors

root pyproject:
- drop unused colorama and importlib_resources deps (stdlib
  importlib.resources on py>=3.11), unused coverage dev dep, and the
  [tool.black] block (black is not a dependency)
- fix Framework :: Pydantic :: 1 classifier to :: 2

Verified: CLI suite 51 passed, nlp generated-project suite 31 passed,
lint clean, dep sync OK, uv build packages all 46 template files.

* fix: make templates buildable in-place with explicit hatch wheel packages

uv run inside packages/template-* failed with hatchling's "unable to
determine which files to ship" because each template's project name
(e.g. advanced-fastapi-app) doesn't match its module dir (src/advanced),

## Process-triggered gap
`separations/coverage.py` identifies liquid-liquid extraction as a specified component split, not an LLE unit. The phase module has liquid-phase capability, so the missing scope is its validated unit-operation/backend integration, not an assertion that all LLE thermodynamics is absent.

Source audit of core main `cec7e819e47c58ab036dcdcd4aec24810f08474a` (27 October 2026); source/docs inspected, no fresh solver run or blanket validation claim.

- `src/chemeascode/domains/process/separations/coverage.py`
- `src/chemeascode/domains/process/thermodynamics/phase.py`
- `src/chemeascode/domains/process/simulation/schema.py`

## Affected process-library work
- https://github.com/ChemE-as-Code/process-library/issues/170
- https://github.com/ChemE-as-Code/process-library/issues/185
- https://github.com/ChemE-as-Code/process-library/issues/186

These are **conditional prerequisites for the scoped predictive model/engineering claim**, not blockers to references, a brief, BFD or an explicitly sourced empirical inventory. Select route and target first.

## Acceptance checks
- [ ] Choose an actual extraction route before requiring this adapter; some product routes can use other separations.
- [ ] Integrate a bounded equilibrium extraction stage/cascade using existing phase/property services or an established backend, with solvent and interaction-parameter provenance.
- [ ] Benchmark distribution/selectivity, phases, recovery, solvent loss and material/energy closure where evaluable, including failure for no two-phase region.
- [ ] Distinguish predictive extraction from specified splits and separate solvent regeneration from the extraction unit boundary.
- [ ] Add one reproducible positive reference test and meaningful unsupported/failure cases; record solver/data versions, tolerances and independent comparison.
- [ ] Update capability/maturity reporting, docs and the ADR for any public contract change; preserve existing ASU workflows.
- [ ] Link the evidence back to affected library issues and state which target is now supported.

## Coordination
Focused follow-up under #9 and #11; distinguish this implementation/qualification scope from general readiness #27. Reuse existing models and adapters rather than adding equations to skills or library folders. Library discovery trackers: ChemE-as-Code/process-library#306 and ChemE-as-Code/process-library#174.


---
_Comment (2026-10-27):_

Implementation in an earlier PR (`cheme process extract`, ADR 0019). Open gaps: (1) choosing an extraction route is up to the library; none of process-library#170/#185/#186 has selected one. (2) The one qualified system, water + 1-propanol + n-butyl acetate at 323.15 K, is benchmarked against tie lines that its 1-propanol NRTL pairs were partly fitted to. No freely accessible independent data set was found, so this qualifies the correlation as evaluated, not a blind prediction. (3) No energy balance (isothermal; tie-line NRTL does not qualify heats of mixing). (4) Solvent loss is over-predicted (qualified to 0.003 mole fraction absolute).

---
_Comment (2026-10-27):_

Merged in an earlier PR (squash bec7fe3) after an independent review. ADR 0019 records the decision.

**Now supported**
- `cheme process extract` reads `process/extraction.yaml` (`cheme/extraction/v1`). It solves countercurrent liquid-liquid equilibrium stages at one temperature on thermo's NRTL, with either a bundled LLE system or `model:` parameters that carry their source.
- It reports:
  - raffinate and extract
  - per-stage compositions
  - solute recovery and solvent loss
  - distribution coefficient (mass and mole basis) and selectivity
  - component closure (1e-8)
  - `split_to_extract`, for a flowsheet component separator's `basis_source`
  - model, backend and core versions, the parameter source, and the input fingerprints
- `energy: not-evaluated`, with the reason.
- Refusals, each a finding with file, line, rule and hint:
  - no two-phase region (`cheme.extraction-one-liquid`)
  - a missing NRTL pair (never taken as zero)
  - a temperature outside the parameters' range
  - an unknown component or system
  - a schema error
- The flowsheet keeps a specified `component_separator`, so maturity is unchanged. Solvent regeneration is a separate unit.

**Evidence (checked in the review)**
- **NRTL parameters**: Hajjar & Enders, Fluid Phase Equilib. 582 (2024) 114104, Tables 6 and 7 and Eq. (5). I verified them against the KITopen PDF.
- **Tie lines**: Costa et al., J. Chem. Eng. Data 54 (2009) 2845, 323.15 K, from NIST ThermoML je900337a data set 27. I verified them by parsing the file.
- **Benchmark** (`tests/test_extraction.py::test_the_bundled_system_reproduces_the_measured_tie_lines`), as tolerance (worst observed):

  | Quantity | Tolerance | Worst observed |
  |---|---|---|
  | Phase composition | 0.035 mole fraction | 0.029 |
  | 1-propanol distribution coefficient | 10 % | 8.3 % |
  | Selectivity | 15 % | 6.8 % |
  | n-butyl acetate in the aqueous phase | 0.003 abs | 0.0023 |

- Cascade tests check per-stage iso-activity (< 1e-7) and balance. As an independent algorithm check, the liquid split matches thermo's FlashVLN (water + ethyl acetate) to 1e-5.
- **Review fixes**:
  - A failed split of an unstable mixture used to be reported as a converged single liquid, which showed up as a false "no two-phase region" refusal. It is now reported as not converged, with a regression test.
  - The README placement is corrected.

**Remaining gaps (issue stays open)**
- [ ] Choosing an actual extraction route is up to the library. process-library#170, #185 and #186 have not selected one yet.
- The only qualified system is benchmarked against tie lines its 1-propanol pairs were partly fitted to. That qualifies the correlation as core evaluates it, not as a blind prediction. An independent data set, or a qualified system relevant to a library route, is still open.
- No energy balance (isothermal stages). Solvent loss is over-predicted 2 to 8 times, and qualified only to 0.003 mole fraction absolute. NRTL only; no stage efficiency or hydrodynamics.
- The library issues have been told what core now supports.

Build a reproducible CO₂ electrolysis pilot-skid case grounded in the bipolar-membrane experiments of Prats Vergel, Vermaas and colleagues. Demonstrate how a change in required operating duration or measured membrane performance affects cell feasibility, electrolyte inventory, dosing, skid layout and environmental impacts per unit of delivered product.

## Demonstration acceptance criteria
- [x] Reproduce a measured series and a published model trajectory with quantitative discrepancies, pinned inputs and attribution.
- [x] Compare steady and intermittent operation at equal cumulative CO output. Show current, voltage, production, pH and dosing, with measured ranges and extrapolations visible.
- [x] Size two pilot-skid designs from the same product specification. Regenerate the balances, PFD, control P&ID, equipment list, dimensioned 3D layout and inventories from the recorded design basis.
- [x] Change the required run duration and rerun. Report which outputs change, why, and which remain physically invariant. Identify the commit and single rerun command.
- [x] Evaluate the pressure-window study as a separate follow-up for spatial scale-up, with independent evidence for its geometry.

[Experimental paper](https://doi.org/10.1038/s44286-025-00306-7) · [4TU data and scripts](https://doi.org/10.4121/5c4fc325-a71b-4ca8-9c1b-01c0405936a2.v1) · [Pressure-window paper](https://doi.org/10.1021/acssuschemeng.2c00195). Earlier steady-state scope: ChemE-as-Code/core-archive#366.

## Implementation checklist
- [x] Reproduce the Vermaas-group bipolar-membrane CO₂ electrolysis benchmark — https://github.com/ChemE-as-Code/process-library/issues/329 (done: process-library#343)
- [x] Add electrochemical measurement processing and a steady-state cell unit — https://github.com/ChemE-as-Code/core/issues/137 (done: #142)
- [x] Support dynamic electrolysis duties and reservoir or dosing comparisons — https://github.com/ChemE-as-Code/core/issues/138 (done: #146)
- [x] Translate cell operating points into stack sizing and skid equipment inputs — https://github.com/ChemE-as-Code/core/issues/139 (done: #148)
- [x] Compare steady and intermittent CO₂ electrolysis and generate two pilot-skid layouts — https://github.com/ChemE-as-Code/process-library/issues/330 (done: process-library#359, 3D to basic engineering #372; HAZOP drafts #360)
- [ ] Build and reconcile the pilot-skid LCI and compare environmental impacts — https://github.com/ChemE-as-Code/process-library/issues/331 (LCI reconciled and climate-only screening done: process-library#361; multi-category impacts, ecoinvent, openLCA export and the comparative ranking stay open on #331)
- [x] Reproduce the gas-diffusion-electrode pressure window and assess spatial scale-up — https://github.com/ChemE-as-Code/process-library/issues/332 (done: process-library#345)

Start with the experimental reproduction. Develop the steady-state contract against those data, then the dynamic and sizing tools. The two-skid comparison supplies the design basis for LCI/LCA. The pressure-window study is a separate extension.

v1.65.0

🥟 Run tests with Bun

The test runner now runs under Bun. Bun transpiles your TypeScript test files itself, so Playwright does not use Babel or its compilation cache. Pass the --bun flag, because without it bunx playwright test runs on Node.js:

bunx --bun playwright test

Our CI runs the test runner tests under Bun 1.4.3 on Linux. Some features work differently under Bun:

  • There is no watch mode. UI mode does not run tests again when files change, and --only-changed does not follow imports.

  • Console output of a test does not get into the trace and UI mode.

🚨 Reports with only failures

New failures reporter prints failures and successful retries as they occur, followed by a summary, without progress output.

New onlyFailures option of the HTML, JSON and JUnit reporters keeps only tests with unexpected outcomes, flaky tests and interrupted tests:

// playwright.config.ts
import { defineConfig } from '@playwright/test';

export default defineConfig({
reporter: [
['failures'],
['html', { onlyFailures: true }],
],
});

    test('restart the server', { lock: '-exclusive-' }, async () => {
  // No other test runs while this one is running.
});

## Problem
Finding a relief device or instrument along a propagation path is useful for candidate generation, but does not verify a scenario-specific protection claim. Verification must evaluate the applicable configuration and return reproducible engineering evidence.

## Scope
Implementation slice of #249, using the claim/check contract tracked in #261. Reuse the DEXPI traversal and plant-state work in #54, #89 and #141, which was merged into `hazop-as-code`; inspect that branch and reconcile with main before implementation. Do not create a competing graph engine or change the existing propagation semantics silently.

- Represent the configuration being checked: operating mode, relevant valve/blind positions, bypass state, and evidence for those states. Distinguish specified normal state, fail state, assumed state and observed state.
- Implement a bounded first verifier for relief-path connectivity: protected equipment to relief-device inlet and discharge to a declared destination.
- Include branches, isolation devices, blinds, direction constraints and off-page boundaries. Resolve cross-sheet paths only with explicit mapping; unresolved boundaries are insufficient evidence.
- Return a witness path when supported, identified blocking elements for contradictions, and missing/conflicting inputs for insufficient evidence.
- A missing position must not silently become open for safeguard verification. An open bypass route must not be substituted for the claimed relief-device route.
- Keep physical connectivity/configuration checks separate from load, capacity, backpressure and other adequacy checks. Reference #226 results when available; absent or stale required adequacy evidence remains unresolved.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Synthetic fixtures cover available path, closed isolation, blocking blind, unknown position, conflicting configuration, wrong safeguard and unresolved off-page continuation.
- [ ] Two operating modes on the same topology yield independently traceable results.
- [ ] A connected but unsized relief device passes only the connectivity check, with adequacy explicitly unresolved.
- [ ] Results are deterministic, bounded on loops, fingerprint their inputs and require no LLM.
- [ ] Expose via the existing safety CLI/API and reports, with documented scope and reason codes.
- [ ] Include a reusable example of a complete relief route; the fixture qualifies this check, not full-plant safety.

## Boundary
No claim of actual plant availability from a drawing alone; no sizing or certification engine.

**Stacked on #145** (`fix/hazop-coverage-names`): its commit c631eac is the first commit of this branch. Review or merge #145 first; this PR's own change is the last commit.

## Why

AI-drafted HAZOP studies of a crude-oil pump station recover about a quarter to a third of the causes of the team's worksheet. The misses are systematic: about a third of the team's deviations are never developed (mostly temperature and the less common guide words), and whole cause families are rarely considered (external and site causes not once; utility loss, operator and maintenance actions and the plant beyond the boundary at well under half the team's rate). The walk (ADR 0032) only follows equipment failures, so it cannot raise these.

## What

`cheme safety hazop propagate --coverage` runs two more deterministic checks per node with members, each a gap kind of `coverage.yaml` (ADR 0036, Proposed):

- **Deviations** (`kind: deviation`): the (guide word, parameter) pairs the node's members call for by DEXPI class, from a default matrix in core written from general practice (line and piping, vessel, heat exchanger or heater, pump or compressor, relief device, filter or strainer). A project's `safety/deviation-matrix.yaml` (new kind `hazop-deviation-matrix`) replaces it. A pair is a gap unless the node has that deviation with a scenario or `notes`, or the triage decides it; a decision without `guide_word` decides the whole parameter.
- **Cause families** (`kind: cause`): one prompt per node and family that applies, listing the plant items from the P&IDs, the design basis and the cause and effect: `utility` (design basis utilities), `external` (site entries, and fire), `boundary` (off-page connectors in, next to or on a line of the node), `operator` (valves without an actuator, filters, strainers, blinds, hand switches), `control` (controllers, C&E interlocks naming a member). Boundary, operator and control prompts are covered when a scenario names a listed item in `refs`; otherwise the triage decides: `covered` with scenario ids (checked against the node; an unknown id is refused), `dismissed` or `question` with the reason.

Plumbing: the checks run without a failure-mode library (the walk is skipped with a one-line note, only under `--coverage`); the text output groups open gaps by kind; `--json` gains `deviations` and `causes` per node; exit 1 while any gap is open; `--write` writes every kind and keeps decisions of every kind. `Walk.inputs` records the design basis, cause and effect and matrix fingerprints. Schema stays `cheme/hazop-coverage/v1` (additive; old files load as `kind: walk`).

## Tried on a real study (read-only)

Pump station study H-01, 18 nodes (17 with members, N18 global): 168 open = 22 walk top events, 100 deviations, 46 cause families (17 utility, 17 external, 7 control, 4 boundary, 1 operator; 19 more prompts covered by scenario refs).

## Checks

- `pytest tests/test_hazop_propagation.py tests/test_hazop.py tests/test_hazop_frequencies.py tests/test_init_golden.py tests/test_skills.py tests/test_boundaries.py tests/test_hazop_completeness.py`: 130 passed
- `ruff check`, `ruff format --check`; `mkdocs build --strict` exits 0; LF endings.

**Stacked on #89** (base `feat/hazop-propagation-coverage`). Merge #89 first, then retarget this PR to `hazop-as-code`; its own diff is one commit.

## Why

A HAZOP rating's likelihood had two options: a code typed from evidence, or `null`. In practice the evidence is a generic frequency table (LOPA screening values, QRA loss-of-containment frequencies) that every reader maps onto the matrix again by hand, leaving no record of which value was used. hazops-copilot-dev already solves this with a frequency library and frequency bounds per likelihood grade. This brings the engine to core, without the data (no licensed numbers in core) and without an LLM (ADR 0010).

## What changes (ADR 0033)

- **New kind `frequencies`** (`cheme/frequencies/v1`): project data, named by the study's `frequencies:`. It holds `sources` (citation, secondary source, `basis: lopa_ief | qra_loc`), `event_types`, `records` (value per year, optional `per`, conditions, locator, `verified`) and an optional failure mode → event type map. Core ships no data.
- **`max_frequency` on the matrix's likelihood grades**: per year, increasing, with the most likely grade open. It is left out of the matrix fingerprint, so every band already recorded stays current.
- **`frequency:` on a rating**: either `{event_type}`, which takes the screening value (records per item, LOPA records first, the highest; never an average), or `{record}`.
- **`cheme safety hazop rate --write`** derives the likelihood (the first grade whose bound is above the value), writes it in place, and then looks up the band as before. The JSON and text output list the derived likelihoods.
- **Rules:**
  - `hazop-frequency`: a broken link, no library, or a matrix without bounds is an error; an event type with no per-item record, or a per-length record, is info, and the likelihood stays the team's.
  - `hazop-likelihood-derived` (warning): a typed likelihood that differs from the derived one.
- **Skills:** `hazop-risk-classification` now links an event type or record instead of typing a code, and leaves the likelihood null when nothing fits. `hazop-assessment` covers the new rules.

## Fix included: CRLF studies were edited in the wrong place

`rate --write` and `stamp --write` took their YAML positions from the text with translated line endings, then edited the raw text. A study with CRLF line endings was patched at shifted offsets. Positions now come from the text on disk, and `write_bands` is generalised to `write_keys`. These are the four `test_hazop.py` write tests that always failed on Windows; they pass now.

## Checked on a real case

- The pump-station library was converted from hazops-copilot-dev (77 records) and loaded in memory.
- The engine gives the same code as the case's prototype script for 31 of 33 event types.

## Context
Agent design test run of 2026-10-18: six staged headless Claude Code sessions (S1-S6), each followed by an independent reviewer agent, took a 500 t/d GOX air separation unit (ASU-1) from an empty `plantcode init` repo to a basic-engineering sign-off, using plantcode 0.3 (main at 2b7f141). Repository: the ASU-1 agent design test repository (local). The run record is in `reviews/2026-10-18-agent-design-test/` (README.md assessment, stage-reviews.md, prompts/); each stage's session output (`result.json`, `stderr.log`) was kept next to it.

## What happened
The run produced 4 P&IDs, the lists, a layout and a basic-stage sign-off for $29.11 of a $50 cap (S1 $2.18, S2 $5.85, S3 $4.66, S4 $5.64, S5 $5.67, S6 $5.11).
- **The runner is ad hoc and outside any repo.** A local `run_stage.sh STAGE BUDGET PROMPT_FILE` hardcodes the plant repo path, the output directory and an editor extension's claude binary, and passes a hand-written `--allowedTools` list, `--max-turns 200`, `--max-budget-usd` and `--output-format json`.
- **The stage text came from the plan, not the repo.** From S3 on it was one sheet behind: stage-reviews.md S3 says "the stage text said 'draw P-02', but P-02 was already drawn in S2". The S5 prompt still says "Draw P-04", which already existed.
- **The reviewer prompt is not in the record.** prompts/ holds only `S1.txt`..`S6.txt`, although the independent reviewer did the most useful work (scores, acceptable flag, findings, and the hand-over list that became each next `FIX FIRST` block).
- **Every prompt repeats the same text** (the ~2 KB plant specification and the same Rules paragraph; prompts total 25.9 KB).
- **Budgets were tuned by trial.** S2 stopped with about $2.20 left and put off P-03; S6 took 167 turns and $5.11 of $6 because it combined fixes, layout, review and sign-off.

## Why it matters
The test cannot be rerun, or used on another plant, without rebuilding the harness by hand; stale stage text cost turns; the reviewer step that caught the real O2 hazards is undocumented.

## Proposal
Add `docs/agent-design-run.md`, linked from the README, plus template support (e.g. `scripts/agent-run/` in `src/plantcode/template/`):
1. A portable runner (stage id, budget, prompt file, output dir; `claude` from PATH or an env var; allowed tools in one config file) that saves result.json, stderr.log, a launch log and the exact prompt.
2. A stage prompt template: plant spec in one file, rules in AGENTS.md, `THIS STAGE` computed from the repo (STAGES.md, failing gates of `plantcode check --stage <target>`, undrawn sheets; see the `plantcode status` issue), `FIX FIRST` from the previous review's open findings.
3. The independent reviewer prompt (scores per axis: process, safety, drawing, consistency; acceptable flag; findings with severity/location/fix; hand-over list), saved with the stage prompts.
4. Budget guidance: concept about $3; one large sheet per stage at about $6-8; split close-out into layout, then review and sign-off; commit midway.
5. The record layout used here (README assessment, stage-reviews.md, prompts/ including reviewer prompts).
6. Pointers to the branch/merge policy and headless-permissions issues.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `docs/agent-design-run.md` exists and is linked from the README.
- [ ] The runner has no user-specific paths; re-running S1 on a fresh `plantcode init` repo needs only the documented command, a spec file and a budget.
- [ ] The stage prompt template derives `THIS STAGE` from repo state, so an already drawn sheet is not assigned again.
- [ ] The reviewer prompt is in the docs/template and in the documented record layout.
- [ ] Budget guidance per stage type is documented.

Partially addressed in plantcode 0.4 (an earlier PR, merge 874391d7); what is still missing is listed in the PR description under 'Partially addresses #2'. Kept open.

---
_Comment (2026-10-20):_

Lessons from running plantcode 0.4 and 0.5 as headless agent sessions on an API key: 9 sessions, about $60 in total, including the 0.5 phases A and B. They are evidence for this issue's runner recipe.

**What worked**
- **One runner, two scripts.** A runner script (`run_headless.sh NAME WORKDIR BUDGET PROMPT`) reads the key from the macOS Keychain for its own process only. Each session gets `--max-budget-usd`, and a chain script sums `total_cost_usd` from each `result.json` and shrinks or skips later caps. No session ever went over its cap, and every chain stayed inside the total.
- **A user checkpoint after the core phase.** The user's amendments arrived before the expensive work. A session stopped seconds after launch cost almost nothing to restart.
- **Each session gets its own worktree and branch, and nothing is pushed.** The orchestrator re-runs tests, renders and checks before opening PRs.

**What to build into the recipe**
- **Put safety rules in every stage prompt from the start.** "Never `--no-verify`" was only added in phase B, after a phase-A session had bypassed the pre-commit hook. The hook ran an older global plantcode that rejected the newer schema (see an earlier issue, the version requirement).
- **Never accept a session's report on trust:**
  - `num_turns` in `result.json` counts only the last segment when a session ends after a background task: one session showed "1 turn" and $5.23. `total_cost_usd` is cumulative and is the number to use.
  - An integration report once left a `TEST_COUNT` placeholder.

  The orchestrator must re-run the test suite and validate itself.
- **Tool allowlists per stage.** A viewer stage needs `npm`/`npx`, so the runner takes extra allowed tools per session (an `EXTRA_TOOLS` variable). Without them the session hits permission denials.
- **Waiting.** Wait on a done file or a log line (e.g. `exit N in`), never with `pgrep -f`, which matched its own shell in an earlier run and never returned.
- **Point hooks at the right build.** Re-run `plantcode git-setup` with the development build (`uv run --project <worktree> plantcode git-setup`) in plant-repo worktrees, so hooks use the version under test.
- **CI forces coloured help.** Tests that read Rich help text must strip ANSI codes; this failed twice in CI and never locally.

Learnt about this in [Anthropic's blog](https://www.anthropic.com/research/redesigning-source-control) (see paragraph on 'A new level of operational excellence is possible').
A superfan agent apparently 'obsessively focuse[s] on the health of a single component' and 'act[s] like an experienced engineer who has nothing better to do than to refresh charts and look for anything strange'.

## Can we use this to our advantage?

Each person's case study/scope/component could be guarded by a superfan agent.

The main agent could be nudged to use the superfan agents through specifications in **CLAUDE.md**.
This could apply when a certain component changed to check if other components are affected adversely by this change.
This could prevent running extensive case studies to ensure functionality of different components more often than necessary .

## Problem
An instruction to perform an engineering check is not evidence that it ran. Workflow completion needs a structured record of required steps, actual tool results and unresolved work, independently of an agent's narrative summary.

## Scope
Implementation slice under #249 with reusable core contracts. Inspect existing run/provenance records, skills manifests, requirements and review gates before extending them. Demonstrate the first workflow on safeguard verification using #261, #262 and #270.

- Define a versioned workflow contract with stable step IDs, dependencies, required/conditional steps, input profiles and expected output artifacts.
- Pin the workflow version, applicable rule/profile versions, tool versions and engineering-input revisions on each run.
- Record per-step inputs, actual invocation/result references, outputs and outcome: completed, failed, blocked or skipped with a reason.
- Preserve partial runs and distinguish successful tool execution from an engineering finding: a correctly executed check can return a contradiction or insufficient evidence.
- Enforce required-step and output requirements deterministically. An agent summary cannot stand in for missing tool execution or results.
- Record conditional applicability and authorised exceptions explicitly; a skip reason alone cannot waive a mandatory step.
- Retain run history and link its evidence to review handover without turning workflow completion into human acceptance.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A successful demonstration run links every mandatory step to reproducible inputs and actual output evidence.
- [ ] Missing mandatory checks, missing outputs and failed/blocked required steps prevent completion.
- [ ] Unsupported or unresolved applicability is visible rather than silently skipped.
- [ ] A completed check with an adverse engineering finding remains distinguishable from execution failure and from engineering acceptance.
- [ ] Changed inputs or workflow/rule/profile versions make prior completion evidence stale where applicable, integrating #263 and #271.
- [ ] Resuming a partial run preserves history and reuses results only when their dependencies remain current.
- [ ] CLI/report output shows required versus executed steps, reasons for unresolved work and pending human review.
- [ ] Add positive, interrupted, fabricated-summary, skipped-mandatory-step and stale-run fixtures to #264.
- [ ] Document the typed record schema and relationship to existing agent guidance; no second source of engineering calculations.

## Dependencies and boundaries
Build on #264 and #270, with #261/#262 as the first executable workflow. Reuse #271 for rule-version provenance. Workflow completeness, engineering-check outcomes and accountable human acceptance are separate states. No new general-purpose orchestrator is required.

## Context
Agent design test run of 2026-10-18: six staged headless Claude Code sessions (S1-S6), each followed by an independent reviewer agent, took a 500 t/d GOX air separation unit (ASU-1) from an empty `plantcode init` repo to a basic-engineering sign-off, using plantcode 0.3 (main at 2b7f141). Repository: the ASU-1 agent design test repository (local). The run record is in `reviews/2026-10-18-agent-design-test/` (README.md assessment, stage-reviews.md, prompts/); each stage's session output (`result.json`, `stderr.log`) was kept next to it.

## What happened
1. **The template allowlist never applied.** Every stage's `stderr.log` says: "Ignoring 6 permissions.allow entries from .claude/settings.json: this workspace has not been trusted. Run Claude Code interactively here once and accept the trust dialog ...". So `src/plantcode/template/dot-claude/settings.json` had no effect in any stage. Its entries also do not match how agents ran scripts (it allows `uv run python scripts/`; agents ran `python3 scripts/draft_P-0x.py`).
2. **34 permission denials** (`permission_denials` in result.json: S1 3, S2 10, S3 4, S4 6, S5 8, S6 3), although the runner passed its own `--allowedTools`. Most used allowed programs in forms prefix rules do not match:
   - compound commands: `for f in pid/P-0*.xml; do sed ...; done`, `VAR=...; mkdir -p ... && ...`, `git show 9aa9b38:pid/P-01.xml > pid/P-01.xml && python3 scripts/draft_P-01.py ...`;
   - heredocs: `cat > plant.yaml <<'EOF'`, `python3 - <<'EOF'` search-and-replace scripts;
   - in-place rewrites: `sed -i '' ...` on `pid/P-0*.xml` (25,000-54,000-line DEXPI files) and on generator scripts; `awk` over XML line ranges;
   - `cp` of sheets into a scratch directory or from `build/` back into `pid/`.

## Why it matters
Every stage spent turns and budget on denied commands. The agents' first choice for an edit was a shell rewrite of large XML, which is unreviewable and fails silently when a pattern matches zero or several times. Widening the allowlist to `sed -i`, `cp` or `awk` would approve exactly those edits; the fix is mainly guidance.

## Proposal
1. Template `AGENTS.md` ground rules, plus a line in `pid-edit` / `pid-draft`: change files with Edit/Write, never `sed -i`, `awk` or heredocs; one command per Bash call (no loops, `&&` chains, `VAR=...;` prefixes); scratch files in `build/`.
2. Template `dot-claude/settings.json`: allow the read-only commands the run needed (`ls`, `wc`, `head`, `tail`, `sed -n`, `cat`, `cmp`, `git show`) and the supported script runner (see the `plantcode run` issue); deliberately leave out `sed -i`, `cp`, `awk`.
3. README section "Running agents headless": project settings are ignored until the folder is trusted; accept the trust dialog once, or pass the allowlist via `--allowedTools` / `--settings .claude/settings.json`.
4. `plantcode init` prints one line saying `.claude/settings.json` takes effect only once the folder is trusted.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] AGENTS.md and the pid-edit/pid-draft skills state the Edit/Write-only and one-command-per-call rules.
- [ ] Template settings.json allows the listed read-only commands and not `sed -i`/`cp`/`awk`; a test checks it parses.
- [ ] README has the headless section.
- [ ] `plantcode init` prints the trust note; a CLI test covers it.
- [ ] A headless re-run of one ASU stage with the documented flags shows no "Ignoring ... permissions.allow" line and far fewer than the 2026-10-18 denials.

## Context
Agent design test run of 2026-10-18: six staged headless Claude Code sessions (S1-S6), each followed by an independent reviewer agent, took a 500 t/d GOX air separation unit (ASU-1) from an empty `plantcode init` repo to a basic-engineering sign-off, using plantcode 0.3 (main at 2b7f141). Repository: the ASU-1 agent design test repository (local). The run record is in `reviews/2026-10-18-agent-design-test/` (README.md assessment, stage-reviews.md, prompts/); each stage's session output (`result.json`, `stderr.log`) was kept next to it.

## What happened
- The template review skill (`src/plantcode/template/dot-claude/skills/review/SKILL.md`, step 4) defines `| # | sheet | item | finding | severity | proposed action |` plus 'Checked and fine' / 'Not checked': no status, no stable id, no place for earlier findings.
- The agents improvised: `reviews/2026-10-18-design-review-S4.md` numbers findings 1..9 and got an appended "Status of the findings (S6)" table with `closed` / `partly closed`, mostly without commits; `reviews/2026-10-18-o2-safety-review.md` uses F1..F7, a separate S5 status table and inline statuses, some with a commit (521473c), some with only a stage.
- Carry-over was driven by the run's prompts, not the repo: `prompts/S6.txt` item 7 had to ask for "a status section to the S4 design review", and every stage prompt carried a hand-written `FIX FIRST` list.
- Ids collide (`1` vs `F1`); nobody can tell which findings across `reviews/` are open without reading every file. S4 also left F1/F2 listed as open after the fix commit.

## Why it matters
Carry-over was lossy and manual. The independent review findings that mattered most (vent header split, GOX suction vent, compander oil path) only survived because they were copied forward by hand.

## Proposal
In the review skill and `reviews/README.md`:
1. Stable ids unique across the repo, e.g. `<review file stem>#<n>`.
2. A `status` column with a fixed vocabulary: `open`, `closed <commit>` (commit required), `accepted: <reason, by whom>`, `superseded by <id>`; no "partly closed" (split the finding).
3. A required `## Previous findings` section listing every not-closed, not-accepted finding from earlier reviews of overlapping scope with current status and evidence. Earlier records are not edited after commit; each record is a snapshot.
4. Document how to list open findings (a grep on the status column until tooling exists).
5. Optional: `plantcode check`/`status` counts open findings and sign-off refuses while high findings are open (ties into the sign-off provenance issue).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The record format has `id` and `status` columns with the vocabulary and a required Previous findings section; step 5 says how to close a finding.
- [ ] `reviews/README.md` explains the id scheme and how to list open findings.
- [ ] A re-run two-stage agent design run carries findings forward without the prompt asking for status sections, and every closed finding names a commit.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

_Comment (2026-10-19):_

Partially addressed in plantcode 0.4 (an earlier PR, merge 874391d7); what is still missing is listed in the PR description under 'Partially addresses #1'. Kept open.

---
_Comment (2026-10-23):_

Status check (2026-10-23, origin/main 84c0cad): ACs 1 and 2 are done on main. The record format with ids, a `status` vocabulary (`closed <commit>`, `accepted:`, `superseded by`) and a required Previous findings section is in `src/chemeascode/templates/project/reviews/README.md` and the `review` skill. Parsing and open-findings counting is in `src/chemeascode/foundation/reviews.py`, which `cheme status` and the sign-off use. All of it landed with an earlier PR (merge 874391d7). The agent-run reviewer prompt (`scripts/agent-run/reviewer-prompt.md`) asks for this format. Only AC3 is still open: a live, paid two-stage run that carries findings forward. No code change is needed for that, so this stays open until such a run has been made.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

---
_Comment (2026-10-27):_

Re-verified on origin/main cec7e81 (2026-10-27). No code change needed; AC3 is still open.

**AC1 (record format, done):** the `review` skill (`src/chemeascode/project/skills/review/SKILL.md`, step 5) defines the `| id | sheet | item | finding | severity | status | proposed action |` table and a required `## Previous findings` table (`id | finding | severity | status | evidence`). Ids are `<file stem>#<n>`. The status vocabulary is `open`, `closed <commit>` (commit required), `accepted: <reason, by whom>` and `superseded by <id>`, with no "partly closed" (split the finding instead). Step 6, "Closing a finding", says to fix it in its own commit; the next review then lists it as `closed <that commit>` with evidence. `cheme validate` enforces this with `cheme.review-finding-id`, `cheme.review-finding-status` and `cheme.review-previous-missing`, and the sign-off refuses an open high or critical finding, or one closed by a commit that is not in HEAD's history.

**AC2 (README, done):** `src/chemeascode/templates/project/reviews/README.md` explains the id scheme and has a "Listing open findings" section: `cheme status` (`--json`: `reviews.open`) and, by hand, `grep -h '| open |' reviews/*.md`.

**Tests run on Windows:** `tests/test_gates.py -k "review or sign_off or status"`: 17 tests pass. Under `-n 2` on the loaded shared machine, two sign-off tests failed, then passed when run serially. `tests/test_agent_run.py`: 4 pass, 1 skipped, and `test_runner_keeps_a_chain_inside_the_total_cap` fails because it cannot run on Windows (WinError 193; it is on the known Windows baseline list).

## Objective
Audit and extend **the existing** ChemE-as-Code core from reproducible conceptual process models toward coordinated detailed engineering: qualified equipment design/rating, discipline-specific checks, supplier-data integration and reviewable drawings/schedules. This is a roadmap/overview, not a request to implement everything in one PR. Reuse existing functionality and established scientific solvers; avoid duplicating algorithms across skills, examples or repositories.

## Verified baseline and 2026-10-23 refresh (main)
- Existing domain packages: `domains/{process,chemistry,equipment,piping,control,safety,assessment,spatial,experiments,requirements}`; foundation, project, schemas, interfaces, integrations.
- `domains/process`: `model.py`, `build.py`, `propagate.py`, `props.py`, `exergy.py`, `hydraulics.py`, `heat_integration/`, `thermodynamics/` (phase and model selection), provenance, layout.
- `domains/assessment`: equipment costing, estimates, MTO and `lca/{inventory,allocation,impacts,uncertainty,methods,construction,report,gates}`.
- Integrations already present: `dwsim.py`, `brightway.py`, `thermo.py`, `unifac.py`, `rmg.py`, `rdkit.py`, `pydexpi.py`, `nist_kinetics.py`, etc.
- README describes BFD/PFD and DEXPI workflows, stream propagation/properties, 3D layout, cost estimation and datasheets.
**Important:** existence of files is not evidence of validated industrial-grade coverage. Inspect implementation, tests and documented limits before classifying each capability. No wholesale restructuring.

### Confirmed implemented functionality (not necessarily industrially validated)
- `domains/process/simulation/{run,translate,schema}.py` provides **DWSIM-based `cheme process simulate --fill/--check`**, model fingerprint/provenance, non-convergence handling and stale/deviation findings. Do **not** describe rigorous simulation as wholly missing; assess supported blocks, property packages, convergence and solver portability.
- `domains/process/separations/{selection,shortcut}.py` covers selection/shortcut calculations; `heat_integration/pinch.py`, `hydraulics.py`, `exergy.py` and `thermodynamics/{phase,model_selection}.py` already exist.
- `domains/assessment/lca/inventory.py` explicitly **derives an unallocated `lci_dataset`** from process flowsheets, then allocates for an LCA study; modules for allocation, uncertainty, impact assessment and Brightway integration exist. Preserve separation between reusable inventory and study-specific allocation.
- `domains/equipment/sizing.py`, `domains/assessment/{equipment_cost,estimate,mto}.py` provide sizing/estimating foundations; `domains/chemistry/kinetics/` and `integrations/{rmg,nist_kinetics,rdkit}.py` provide reaction-related foundations.
- Concrete regression assets: `examples/process-{recycle,separation,simulation,double-column,...}/`; tests `test_process_simulate.py`, `test_process_props.py`, `test_thermo_phase.py`, `test_separation_selection.py`, `test_pinch.py`, `test_lca_{inventory,allocation,backends,uncertainty}.py`, `test_assessment_equipment_cost.py`.
- **Assessment is based on current code paths and test-file presence, not a freshly executed test suite or solver qualification.** Classify domain maturity only after test execution and reference comparisons.
- The formerly named `example-asu` has **already been renamed to `process-library`** and ASU moved to `processes/asu-1`; use the current location for end-to-end benchmarks: https://github.com/ChemE-as-Code/process-library/tree/main/processes/asu-1

## Workstreams and candidate gaps
| Priority | Area | Audit / desired outcome |
|---|---|---|
| P0 | Unified engineering contract | Stable identities for components, streams, units, reactions, operating conditions; units, provenance, uncertainty, assumptions, result/solver status; versioned schemas and cross-model references |
| P0 | Thermodynamics | Validate EOS/activity models, VLE/LLE/SLE, cryogenics, electrolytes, solids, transport, property ranges; explicit unsupported regimes |
| P0 | Rigorous simulation | Flash, recycle convergence, columns, reactors, compressors, exchangers; compare current propagation with DWSIM and potential IDAES/Pyomo adapter |
| P0 | Reaction engineering | Kinetic/equilibrium networks, heterogeneous catalysis, reactor sizing, sensitivity; assess existing chemistry/RMG work |
| P0 | Equipment & utilities | Realistic equipment sizing, hydraulics, steam/cooling/refrigeration, heat integration; distinguish estimates from design-rated models |
| P0 | TEA / optimization | Extend existing equipment-cost/estimate modules to transparent CAPEX/OPEX, economic scenarios, NLP/MILP/MINLP interfaces |
| P0 | LCI / LCA | Reusable **unallocated multi-output** LCI datasets and process-module derivation; allocation as study-specific choice; background linking and Brightway integration; distinguish foreground vs cradle-to-gate |
| P1 | Dynamic simulation/control | Dynamic models, start-up/shutdown, control studies, OpenModelica/CasADi interfaces |
| P1 | Safety & operability | HAZOP, relief, safeguarding, consequence models, auditable assumptions |
| P1 | Specialized process families | Solids/crystallization, bioprocesses, electrochemistry, polymers, pharma, water treatment, high-pressure/cryogenic systems |
| P1 | Interoperability | Consider IDAES, Cantera, BioSTEAM, CoolProp and other backends only where they fill demonstrated gaps; check licensing and deployment |

## Deliverables
- [ ] Capability matrix **implemented & tested / limited / external adapter / missing** with links to code and tests, not just README claims.
- [ ] Coverage matrix for 12–15 representative processes (ASU, ammonia, methanol, ethanol, ethylene, hydrogen, sulfuric acid, chlor-alkali, wastewater, bioprocess, crystallization, etc.) including required thermo, equipment and solvers.
- [ ] Ranked small follow-up issues for missing P0 capabilities with acceptance tests, ownership and estimated complexity.
- [ ] Versioned model/solver adapter contract proposal; avoid prematurely rewriting current models.
- [ ] Benchmark reference cases with mass/energy closure, convergence diagnostics, validated literature/reference comparisons and provenance.
- [ ] Document where scientific tools live in `core`; agent skills and MCP remain thin discoverable wrappers.
- [ ] Keep IP, licensing, private pyDEXPI dependencies and publication suitability explicit.

## Immediate next steps (avoid duplicate implementations)
- [ ] Run CI/tests and representative ASU DWSIM simulation with pinned backend; record quantitative mass/energy closure, convergence and failure behavior.
- [ ] Audit existing shortcut separation, pinch, exergy, hydraulics, kinetics, sizing, TEA and LCA **before** proposing replacements.
- [ ] Define supported property regimes and unsupported cases, especially cryogenics, electrolyte and solids systems.
- [ ] Build a process-family × physics/solver × validation matrix, prioritize actual blockers and create focused child issues.
- [ ] Align core's model/LCI contracts with the now-implemented Process Library catalog and Brightway export (https://github.com/ChemE-as-Code/process-library/issues/13).

## Acceptance criteria
Roadmap references actual source/test locations, distinguishes working vs experimental, does not regress ASU workflows, and prioritizes the smallest changes needed to support reproducible multi-process studies.
