Build a reproducible CO₂ electrolysis pilot-skid case grounded in the bipolar-membrane experiments of Prats Vergel, Vermaas and colleagues. Demonstrate how a change in required operating duration or measured membrane performance affects cell feasibility, electrolyte inventory, dosing, skid layout and environmental impacts per unit of delivered product.

## Demonstration acceptance criteria
- [x] Reproduce a measured series and a published model trajectory with quantitative discrepancies, pinned inputs and attribution.
- [x] Compare steady and intermittent operation at equal cumulative CO output. Show current, voltage, production, pH and dosing, with measured ranges and extrapolations visible.
- [x] Size two pilot-skid designs from the same product specification. Regenerate the balances, PFD, control P&ID, equipment list, dimensioned 3D layout and inventories from the recorded design basis.
- [x] Change the required run duration and rerun. Report which outputs change, why, and which remain physically invariant. Identify the commit and single rerun command.
- [x] Evaluate the pressure-window study as a separate follow-up for spatial scale-up, with independent evidence for its geometry.

[Experimental paper](https://doi.org/10.1038/s44286-025-00306-7) · [4TU data and scripts](https://doi.org/10.4121/5c4fc325-a71b-4ca8-9c1b-01c0405936a2.v1) · [Pressure-window paper](https://doi.org/10.1021/acssuschemeng.2c00195). Earlier steady-state scope: ChemE-as-Code/core-archive#366.

## Implementation checklist
- [x] Reproduce the Vermaas-group bipolar-membrane CO₂ electrolysis benchmark — https://github.com/ChemE-as-Code/process-library/issues/329 (done: process-library#343)
- [x] Add electrochemical measurement processing and a steady-state cell unit — https://github.com/ChemE-as-Code/core/issues/137 (done: #142)
- [x] Support dynamic electrolysis duties and reservoir or dosing comparisons — https://github.com/ChemE-as-Code/core/issues/138 (done: #146)
- [x] Translate cell operating points into stack sizing and skid equipment inputs — https://github.com/ChemE-as-Code/core/issues/139 (done: #148)
- [x] Compare steady and intermittent CO₂ electrolysis and generate two pilot-skid layouts — https://github.com/ChemE-as-Code/process-library/issues/330 (done: process-library#359, 3D to basic engineering #372; HAZOP drafts #360)
- [ ] Build and reconcile the pilot-skid LCI and compare environmental impacts — https://github.com/ChemE-as-Code/process-library/issues/331 (LCI reconciled and climate-only screening done: process-library#361; multi-category impacts, ecoinvent, openLCA export and the comparative ranking stay open on #331)
- [x] Reproduce the gas-diffusion-electrode pressure window and assess spatial scale-up — https://github.com/ChemE-as-Code/process-library/issues/332 (done: process-library#345)

## Goal

Turn a design objective into reproducible, evaluated candidates and an inspectable trade-off plot: for example, reduce lifecycle climate impact while meeting product specifications and a production-cost ceiling.

**Priority: P1-high.** A focused heat-recovery or electrification case is the preferred first implementation.

## Demonstration story

Start with one baseline plant and a documented set of decision variables or discrete modifications. Evaluate alternatives on the same basis, reject infeasible candidates and display the nondominated feasible candidates. Select one candidate for engineering review and show the changes from baseline.

## Work packages

- [ ] Define typed objectives, bounds, constraints and decision variables, including units, data sources and permissible topology changes.
- [ ] Reuse #33–#43 for alternatives, comparability, assessments and revision diffs.
- [ ] Implement a bounded search or optimization workflow using deterministic engineering evaluations; record solver, budget, termination and evaluation failures.
- [ ] Check product output/specification, mass and energy closure, equipment constraints and model validity before including candidates in the feasible set.
- [ ] Evaluate cost and climate impacts with common boundaries, functional unit, price premises and background scenarios; report explicit exceptions.
- [ ] Show a cost–CO₂ plot with candidate details, binding constraints, assumptions and links to supporting runs.
- [ ] Re-evaluate selected candidates at full model fidelity when screening models or surrogates are used.
- [ ] Include sensitivity to influential prices, emission factors or equipment/model assumptions.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] At least one reproducible example contains multiple feasible candidates and a clear baseline comparison.
- [ ] Infeasible or failed evaluations are recorded and excluded from the feasible frontier.
- [ ] Results are described as best found / nondominated among evaluated candidates unless global optimality is established.
- [ ] Each displayed point traces to inputs, calculations, toolkit/model versions and assessment basis.
- [ ] Any surrogate prediction is labeled and checked with the engineering model before a candidate is recommended.
- [ ] Selecting a candidate produces a reviewable design revision and decision record.

## Dependencies

- #33 — concept alternatives and screening.
- #134 — whole-plant pinch targeting, useful for candidate generation but not proof of achievable savings.
- #112 — LCA rigour.
- #216 — coordinated design updates and engineering diffs.

First scope: one existing process, bounded decisions and two headline objectives. General autonomous superstructure synthesis is a later extension.

Reuse existing functionality and established scientific solvers; avoid duplicating algorithms across skills, examples or repositories.

## Verified baseline and 2026-10-23 refresh (main)

|---|---|---|

## Goal

A TEA in cheme-as-code that is comparable, traceable, uncertainty-aware and decision-led. It must work for a **broad variety of chemical processes**: continuous and batch, several operating cases, material and energy products, emissions, replacements, and so on. It must be shown in the viewer and exercised on a real plant (ASU-1 in process-library).

The core model below and the viewer page (#74) are in place.

## Still to do

**ASU-1 in process-library, from `main`, not from `feat/tea-general`:**
- Re-run `cheme assess tea --write` with the merged core.
- **Respect D-082 on `main`:** GAN is not booked as revenue (the 20 USD/t figure is a
  break-even). Labour is included.
- Bring over from `feat/tea-general` only the **cooling-water price**, a utility cost of
  −12.6 USD/MWh of heat rejected, derived and cited in the yaml:
  - Ulrich & Vasudevan, "How to estimate utility costs", Chem. Eng., April 2006, Table 1,
    grass-roots cooling water: a = 7e-5 + 2.5e-5/q, b = 0.003 (USD/m3);
  - q = 0.244 m3/s, CEPCI 2023 797.9, and a power-station gas price of 2.77 USD/MMBtu (EIA
    Electric Power Annual Table 7.20, 2024) give 0.146 USD/m3;
  - at the 10 K rise, 11.6 kWh/m3.
- Update the DESIGN.md decision (D-082 or a new one) and PROGRESS.md.
- Run `cheme skills update tea`.
- Once CI installs a core with `kind: tea`, add the gate (`require: [tea-current]`, later
  `prices`, `class-stage`).

## Open questions and follow-ups

- **ASU-1:**
  - LOX and LIN have no published merchant price; they stay unpriced (`tea-price-missing`).
  - Owner's cost, contingency, the tax position and the hurdle rate are undecided.
  - The estimate is class 5 at stage basic (`tea-class-stage` warning): the main air compressor
    and the cold box need quotations.
- **Deferred generality** (design synthesis, review 1):
  - campaigns with an LCOP per product (multi-product batch);
  - linked prices (indexed, spread, cost-plus);
  - correlated inputs (Iman-Conover);
  - Nm3 and kmol derived from molar masses;
  - labour roles;
  - shared-facility allocation;
  - utility demand from pinch targets;
  - capacity and demand charges;
  - stack degradation;
  - an LCA-driven carbon credit;
  - hourly price profiles binned into cases.
- **Atlas** (website `apps/atlas`): no economics yet. Mirror the LCA's `values_withheld` for
  example prices.

## What core has

### Increment 1

`domains/assessment/tea/{schemas,model,uncertainty,report,gates}.py` and
`domains/assessment/flows.py` (the terminal rates, shared with the LCA). Main parts:

- `estimate/tea.yaml`: kind `tea`, schema `cheme/tea/v1`, in `LIST_FILES`, so `cheme validate` and
  `cheme schema tea` cover it.
- `cheme assess tea [--json|--csv|--sensitivity|--write|--check|--compare REV]`.
- Gate `kind: tea` (`prices`, `no-example`, `class-stage`, `decision`, `tea-current`).
- `GET /api/tea` with `has_tea`, and the static export.
- Skill `tea`, `docs/framework/tea.md`, template notes in `estimate/README.md`, `STAGES.md` and
  `checks.yaml`.

## Increment 2

### Architecture

The model now works on **priced lines** (`model.Line`): key, rate per operating hour, price,
revenue flag, category, `scales` and `prices` (extra input ids), profile, `rate_id`/`price_id`
(shared drivers).

- `tea/build.py` (new) turns premises into lines and findings. It keeps an input registry: one
  `Reg` per input id with value, unit, status, source, uncertainty and swing. `describe`,
  `specs`, `swings`, scenarios and the tornado all read it.
- `model.evaluate(p, scale, n, lcop=True)` is vectorised over samples. The LCOP is computed only
  when asked: two evaluations when the NPV is linear, a bracketed search when losses are carried
  forward.

### Features (all optional fields, so increment 1's files give identical numbers)

- **Operation and cases:**
  - `cases: [{case, share, prices, source}]`: share-weighted flowsheet cases. A per-case price
    splits the flow into `key~case` lines that share one rate driver and one price driver.
  - `operation.batch` (cycle time, basis hours, trains, batches per year, success rate) and
    `operation.utilisation`.
- **Prices and lines:**
  - `prices[].component` (`key@component`); `conversion` for a unit of the other kind; new units
    lb, st, MMBtu, therm, Nm3, m3, L, gal, bbl, kmol, ea.
  - `basis.unit` and `basis.conversion`: an energy main product gives an LCOE or LCOH.
  - `variable_opex`: per a flow or component, per hour or per batch; categories; a negative
    price is a credit.
  - `emissions`: carbon `price` with a path, `sources` (factor, capture) and `allocation` (free
    allowances with a phase-out). Every emission line takes `price:carbon`.
  - Price paths (`profile`, `escalation`) on prices, variable items, fixed items and the carbon
    price.
- **Events:** replacements every N years or N operating hours, turnarounds with downtime,
  sustaining capital, grants (a negative cost).
- **Finance:** `working_capital_days`; `isbl.scaling` (six-tenths rule at the design capacity)
  and `location_factor`; `losses: carry_forward`; a `depreciation` schedule with write-off of
  the book value left; tax on a salvage gain.
- **Monte Carlo:** `uncertainty.rate_mode: throughput`.
- **Outputs:** `cash_cost` (also a decision metric); `cost_of_production` (per unit by category,
  summing to the LCOP); `lcop_unsubsidised`.
- **Payload:** `/api/tea` gains `operation`, `lines`, `variable`, `emissions`, `events`,
  `cost_of_production`, `results.cash_cost` and more. Flows carry `prices[]`, and their
  `per_year` is now the net income (revenue +, cost −).
- A product with a negative price is carried as a cost line: category disposal, or utility for
  energy such as rejected heat.

## Sources used for ASU-1 premises

- US EIA, Electricity sales, revenue and average price, 2023, Table 4 (industrial 8.04 ¢/kWh)
  and Table 5c (states).
- US EIA, Electric Power Annual, Table 7.20 (gas delivered for generation, 2024).
- Thunder Said Energy, "Costs of cryogenic air separation" (about $200 per t/a capex; about
  $100/t O2 for a 20 % IRR; $20/t N2 as an ammonia-plant break-even).
- Ulrich & Vasudevan, Chem. Eng., April 2006 (utility cost coefficients).
- Towler & Sinnott, Chemical Engineering Design (typical fixed-cost factors).
- Mordor Intelligence, ASU market (2,000 t/d plant, USD 250–300 M; no method stated).

## Goal

DEXPI files are XML today. A git-oriented **DEXPI YAML** serialization, with import and export in pyDEXPI, is under consideration for P&IDs and for DEXPI process models. Core's `process/*.yaml` flowsheet format could later converge with a pyDEXPI process YAML. Whether, when and how to do this is still open.

**Prepared on the framework branch:**
- `domains/piping/dexpi_io.py` is the single load/export path for DEXPI models in the piping domain and the project layer.
- `docs/framework/architecture.md`, section "Possible DEXPI YAML serialization", covers:
  - where the format lives: pyDEXPI owns the format and the round trip, and core only selects it;
  - everything in core that depends on the XML form today;
  - how to keep it replaceable;
  - open questions and a recommended order.

**To decide:**
- [ ] Whether to do it at all, and for which models: P&ID, process, or both.
- [ ] Graphics and drawing data in YAML, or kept in a separate file.
- [ ] Round-trip fidelity and stable ids between XML and YAML.
- [ ] Mixed repositories: an optional `format: xml|yaml` per sheet in `plant.yaml`.
- [ ] What depends on XML today: `fmt`, the textconv git diff, generated-sheet fingerprints, `validate` line numbers, `show file:start-end`, `copy`/`fragment` snippets, the `dexpi-xml`/`pid-edit` skills, and SVG export.
- [ ] A migration command.

**Constraint:** core never uses pyDEXPI's editor commands. DEXPI changes are file edits or generated from YAML.

No implementation is planned yet. This issue tracks the decision.


---
_Comment (2026-10-23):_

## Research note and recommendation (2026-10-23)

**Findings**

- **pyDEXPI has already chosen something else for the git use case.** pyDEXPI-dev ADR 0002, "Comparing model states, and reviewing them in Git" (`docs/mkdocs/adr/0002-model-change-representations.md`, accepted 2026-09-25), considered YAML for the git view and rejected it: "Nested INI and YAML encode the hierarchy in section paths or indentation, so a rename or reparenting rewrites the whole subtree."
  - The ADR adopted a flat, one-block-per-object **text projection** (`pydexpi.versioning`). The projection is not round-trippable, and "the canonical DEXPI file stays the source of truth".
- **Core already uses that projection.** `integrations/git.py` (`readable_projection` → `pydexpi.versioning.model_to_projection(model, id_policy="source")`) is the `cheme textconv` driver behind `pid/*.xml diff=dexpi`. The main argument for YAML, readable git diffs, is therefore already covered without changing the stored format.
- **The YAML pieces do not exist yet.**
  - pyDEXPI-dev has a lossless **JSON** serializer (`pydexpi/loaders/json_serializer.py`). ADR 0002 notes that ids in JSON-kept models are fully stable.
  - There is no YAML loader or serializer, no open pyDEXPI-dev issue for one, and no process-model YAML.
  - Core pins pyDEXPI-dev at `be793a0`.
- **The cost in core is large.** `docs/framework/architecture.md`, section "Possible DEXPI YAML serialization", lists what is XML-bound: `fmt`, `show`, `SheetIndex` line numbers, the authoring API, generated-sheet fingerprints (C14N), the `dexpi-xml`/`pid-edit`/`pid-draft` skills and the snippets. None of it would carry over for free.

**Recommendation: do not pursue DEXPI YAML now. Park this issue as "not planned" and record the reasons:**

1. **P&IDs stay DEXPI XML** in core, and git review uses pyDEXPI's projection (done).
2. **If a non-XML stored form is ever wanted**, start from pyDEXPI's existing JSON serializer, not a new YAML format. The first step would be a pyDEXPI corpus round-trip test (XML → model → JSON → model → XML, `id_diff` empty, drawing kept) over core's template and examples. That test belongs to pyDEXPI, not core.
3. **Process models:** keep `process/*.yaml` as core's own format. It carries per-value provenance (given/assumed/calculated), cases and layout overrides that DEXPI process models lack. Revisit convergence only once pyDEXPI publishes a process-model serialization.
4. **Keep the seam:** `domains/piping/dexpi_io.py`, with the boundary test, is the only load/dump path, so the decision stays reversible.

**Decision needed from the owner:** do you accept closing as "not planned", with P&IDs staying XML, git review via `pydexpi.versioning`, and JSON rather than YAML as the fallback if a stored-format change is ever reopened? Or do you still want a YAML format specified in pyDEXPI? If so, that work should be a pyDEXPI-dev issue, not a core one.

Start from a pinned, reproducible library plant. Request a 20% production increase. Translate the request into an explicit design-basis change, identify affected artifacts, run supported calculations and present the before/after PFD, P&ID, equipment duties, 3D layout, TEA and LCA.

Include a deliberately capacity-limited item, such as a compressor. Report its constraint and compare feasible responses rather than assuming every item scales proportionally.

## Objective
Establish a practical, evidence-based baseline for generating a broad industrial process library with core. Prioritize sourced, balanced conceptual designs across many processes, with deeper engineering for a smaller verified subset.

Audit and extend existing implementations rather than building replacement thermodynamics, reactor or simulation frameworks. This issue focuses on end-to-end reliability and process-family coverage.

Related roadmap: #9. Library: https://github.com/ChemE-as-Code/process-library

## Current baseline and evidence limits
Current main contains thermodynamic model selection and phase calculations, simulation translation for shortcut/rigorous columns and conversion/equilibrium/Gibbs reactors, reaction/catalyst data, fixed-bed calculations, heat integration, equipment sizing, costing, TEA and LCA.
Relevant paths:
- `domains/process/{simulation,thermodynamics,separations}/`
- `domains/process/{reactors,fixed_bed,propagate,hydraulics}.py`
- `domains/chemistry/{properties,catalysts,kinetics,microkinetics,thermochemistry}.py` (kinetics is a package)
- `domains/equipment/`, `domains/assessment/`, `integrations/`

The inspection motivating this issue checked source and repository structure, not solver execution or industrial qualification. File presence is not proof of adequate scientific coverage. The fixed-bed implementation explicitly uses a steady-state ideal-gas, pseudo-homogeneous model with effective particle rates and no separate gas–catalyst gradients; verify suitability case by case.

## 1. Define deliverable maturity and required checks
- [ ] Extend existing library maturity/review metadata rather than adding a competing status system.
- [ ] Define evidence requirements for: sourced process description; balanced conceptual PFD; converged predictive simulation; preliminary/basic engineering package.
- [ ] Keep calculation maturity, artifact completeness and independent review status distinct.
- [ ] Record supported operating cases, assumptions, unresolved dependencies and model limitations.
- [ ] Ensure generated drawings or schema-valid files alone cannot establish calculation maturity.
- [ ] Provide machine-readable check results that the library catalog can summarize.

## 2. Thermodynamic and property coverage
- [ ] Build a mixture × operating range × required property coverage matrix for the benchmark cases.
- [ ] Check availability and provenance of pure-component properties, binary interaction parameters, phase equilibria, enthalpies and relevant transport properties.
- [ ] Investigate electrolytes/aqueous acids, strongly nonideal mixtures, solids/precipitation, heavy petroleum fractions and polymers; classify each as supported, limited, external integration or unsupported based on tests.
- [ ] Record chosen methods, parameter sources, validity ranges and missing data per process.
- [ ] Diagnose extrapolation and unsupported regimes explicitly.
- [ ] Reuse established external property/solver packages where they fill demonstrated gaps.

## 3. Reactor and catalyst credibility
- [ ] Audit existing reactor implementations and their connection to whole-flowsheet calculations.
- [ ] Document assumptions and coverage for high-pressure/nonideal reactions, fixed beds, liquid/slurry systems and fluidized beds.
- [ ] Accept either a supported kinetic/equilibrium model or a sourced conversion-and-selectivity model for conceptual entries; distinguish them explicitly.
- [ ] Require rate-law units, catalyst/rate basis, validity ranges and provenance where kinetics are used.
- [ ] Assess heat release, pressure drop, selectivity and applicable transfer limitations at the level required by the case.
- [ ] Never fill missing kinetics or catalyst performance with unmarked agent-generated values.

## 4. Separation coverage
- [ ] Verify current rigorous and shortcut distillation on reference cases.
- [ ] Assess absorption/stripping, extraction, adsorption cycles, membranes, crystallization, drying and solids handling.
- [ ] Allow explicit empirical/component-split models for initial conceptual designs with a source and operating basis.
- [ ] Keep specified splits visibly distinct from predictive separation models; do not promote their maturity based on convergence alone.
- [ ] Identify the smallest reusable extensions or external adapters required by benchmark failures.

## 5. Whole-plant consistency
- [ ] Check total and component/element balances where applicable, energy closure, and explicit tolerances.
- [ ] Exercise recycles, purge streams, impurity accumulation and convergence/failure reporting.
- [ ] Include relevant steam, cooling, refrigeration, power, wastewater, off-gas and waste boundaries.
- [ ] Check utility temperature/pressure feasibility and prevent double counting of recovered heat.
- [ ] Compare yield, product purity, recovery and specific energy/utility consumption with independent reference ranges.
- [ ] Distinguish numerical convergence from physical validity.
- [ ] Pin model/backend versions and record input fingerprints and reproducible run results.

## 6. Engineering scope and consistency
- [ ] Define which P&IDs, equipment lists, datasheets, layouts and cost outputs are preliminary and which have demonstrated deeper coverage.
- [ ] Cross-check linked equipment/tags, stream conditions, equipment duties and design-basis assumptions across artifacts.
- [ ] Document coverage/limitations for mechanical design, materials/corrosion, relief sizing, controls and dynamic behavior.
- [ ] Leave unsupported deliverables explicitly unresolved rather than generating apparently complete engineering.
- [ ] Preserve separation between structural checks, scientific verification and human approval.

## Representative benchmark campaign
Start with approximately eight cases, using existing library work wherever possible:

Found in the ASU's layout reviews (process-library `reviews/2026-10-24-layout-review23.md`, tracked there as process-library#66).

**What:** `cheme layout build` places a line-mounted instrument at its tap on the pipe, and its cable starts there. No rule checks whether a person can reach the tap or the transmitter. On the ASU, FIC-4148, PIC-4101 and AI-3104 share a point on GOX-4001 at 9.25 m on rack PR1, with nothing to stand on. Valves already have such a rule (D-040: `operator`, access platforms).

**When to do it:** with the next round of spatial or access rules, or when a second plant hits it. The ASU can live with it as an open low finding until then.

**When not:** not as a quick heuristic that floods every plant with findings. It needs a declared way to say *remote mount* or *tap near grade*, like the valve `operator` entries, so that a finding can be answered rather than accepted.

**Done when:** the model reports a transmitter whose tap is out of reach and has no declared remote mount or access, and a plant can answer it in its files.

**cheme-as-code:** 1.12.0 (commit a3b54a82b723eed08b4dabaa7c6184d89fdd4173), pyDEXPI 2.1.0
**Simulator:** DWSIM 10.2.16 (DWSIM route of `cheme process simulate`)
**Operating system:** macOS, arm64

**Describe the problem**

A PFD often shows material connections that the process model does not simulate: the lean and
rich solvent of an absorber whose regeneration is outside the unit, a utility return, a drain to
a closed system. The PFD must show them at the battery limit, without values, on the equipment
they enter.

`process/flowsheet.yaml` has no way to say "drawn, not simulated" for a stream that ends at a
simulated unit:

- a stream from a feed terminal into a simulated unit is a feed of the simulation and must carry
  temperature, pressure, flow and composition (finding `cheme.process-sim-feed-incomplete`,
  chemeascode/domains/process/simulation/translate.py);
- the unit counts every connected material stream against its shape (`translate.SHAPES`), so on
  a unit with a fixed number of inlets (`component_separator`: one) the extra inlet also makes the
  unit unmappable.

The only workaround we found is a separate model step left out of the simulation (`exclude:` in
process/simulation.yaml) between the two terminals, drawn against the real equipment by hand. It
works (cheme skips streams with both ends outside the simulated part), but the connection then
belongs to another node of the model than the equipment it enters.

**Steps to reproduce**

A new plant (`cheme init`), with a vessel U1 fed by a gas and a water, and a third inlet from a
battery-limit terminal F3 that carries no values. process/materials.yaml:

```yaml
schema: cheme/process/v1
kind: materials
components:
  - {id: N2, name: Nitrogen, formula: N2, cas: 7727-37-9, molar_mass: 28.0134}
  - {id: H2O, name: Water, formula: H2O, cas: 7732-18-5, molar_mass: 18.0153}
templates:
  - {id: gas, title: Gas, components: [N2, H2O]}
property_method:
  adapter: thermo
  status: placeholder
```

process/flowsheet.yaml:

```yaml
schema: cheme/process/v1
kind: flowsheet
title: Minimal example
units: {pressure: kPa(a), temperature: K, flow: kg/h, duty: kW, enthalpy: kJ/kmol}
cases:
  - {id: design, description: Design case, default: true}
tolerance: {abs: 1.0, rel: 0.005}
feeds:
  - {id: F1, title: Wet gas, category: raw_material, ports: [{id: out, direction: out}]}
  - {id: F2, title: Water, category: raw_material, ports: [{id: out, direction: out}]}
  - {id: F3, title: "Lean solvent (battery limit, not simulated)", category: utility, utility: {kind: other, level: lean solvent}, ports: [{id: out, direction: out}]}
products:
  - {id: P1, title: Gas, category: product, ports: [{id: in, direction: in}]}
  - {id: P2, title: Liquid, category: product, ports: [{id: in, direction: in}]}
blocks:
  - id: U1
    title: Contact vessel
    class: SeparatingByFlash
    ports: [{id: a, direction: in}, {id: b, direction: in}, {id: c, direction: in}, {id: gas, direction: out}, {id: liq, direction: out}]
steps: []
streams:
  - id: S1
    from: F1.out
    to: U1.a
    template: gas
    state:
      design:
        temperature: {value: 430, provenance: assumed, source: example}
        pressure: {value: 150, provenance: assumed, source: example}
        flow: {value: 1000, unit: kg/h, provenance: assumed, source: example}
        composition: {basis: mole_fraction, values: {N2: 0.7, H2O: 0.3}, provenance: assumed, source: example}
  - id: S2
    from: F2.out
    to: U1.b
    template: gas
    state:
      design:
        temperature: {value: 300, provenance: assumed, source: example}
        pressure: {value: 400, provenance: assumed, source: example}
        flow: {value: 5000, unit: kg/h, provenance: assumed, source: example}
        composition: {basis: mole_fraction, values: {H2O: 1.0}, provenance: assumed, source: example}
  - {id: S3, from: U1.gas, to: P1.in, template: gas}
  - {id: S4, from: U1.liq, to: P2.in, template: gas}
  - {id: S5, title: "Lean solvent to U1 (battery limit, no values)", from: F3.out, to: U1.c, template: gas}
layout: {bfd: {}, pfd: {}}
```

process/simulation.yaml:

```yaml
schema: cheme/simulation/v1
kind: simulation
simulator: dwsim
property_package: Peng-Robinson (PR)
specs:
  U1:
    outlets: {gas: vapor, liq: liquid}
```

`cheme process simulate --check` (exit 1):

```
process/flowsheet.yaml:44: error cheme.process-sim-feed-incomplete [S5]: feed stream S5 (design) lacks temperature, pressure, flow, composition -- give them (provenance given or assumed)
```

Without S5 (and U1's port `c`) the same plant translates and runs on DWSIM 10.2.16.

**Expected behavior**

A way to mark a material stream (or the port it uses) as a battery-limit connection that is drawn
and listed but not simulated: no values required, not counted against the unit's shape, not a
feed or product of the simulation, shown as such in the stream table (for example "n.c."), and
reported by the block balances as outside the simulation instead of "not evaluable". Something
like `simulate: false` on the stream, or a port `kind` for connections outside the model.

**What we do meanwhile**

A model step between the two battery-limit terminals, left out with `exclude:`, drawn against the
real equipment on the PFD by hand; our balance tool lists the two streams as outside the
simulation.

## Problem and intended outcome

We plan to add **Aspen Plus, Aspen HYSYS and Dymola** soon. Core PR #254 introduces useful execution, staging, fingerprinting, evidence and result-publication machinery, but parts remain QSDsan-specific. Extract the reusable machinery now so each subsequent integration implements simulator-specific behaviour without copying the process lifecycle.

Deliver a working refactor with **QSDsan as the first project-worker adapter**, preserving the existing DWSIM/IDAES workflows and the A2/O example. This issue establishes the foundation; it does **not** implement the three commercial simulator adapters.

Related:
- Core #254: https://github.com/ChemE-as-Code/core/pull/254
- A2/O example: https://github.com/ChemE-as-Code/process-library/pull/459
- Dynamic demonstrator #217: trajectory artifacts here should support that later work, without implementing its interactive UI.

### Starting point and dependency

Review based on core PR #254 at `5437b17511b05b0b4316d50c1fcbcff131e67056` and library PR #459 at `c49892e5cf4598317d1d7dfc98207460afa818ed`. Recheck current branches before implementation. Implement on top of #254, or coordinate the extraction into that PR; do not recreate its obsolete initial implementation. Explicitly document the dependency if #254 is still unmerged.

Read repository `AGENTS.md`, `docs/framework/contributing.md`, `architecture.md`, `contract.md` and relevant ADRs first.

## Current code to inspect

Paths below are relative to `src/chemeascode/`:

- `integrations/qsdsan.py`: declared-file staging, interpreter selection, subprocess lifecycle, timeout, response parsing and evidence checks.
- `domains/process/simulation/qsdsan.py`: returned-value validation, protected YAML edits, run-record/evidence publication.
- `domains/process/simulation/worker_model.py`: source ownership, inputs and model fingerprints.
- `domains/process/simulation/backends.py`: backend registry, capabilities, input discovery and preparation.
- `domains/process/simulation/{schema,run,record,translate}.py`.
- `foundation/schemas/run.py`: existing `cheme/adapter-result/v1`, shared beyond process simulation.
- `domains/process/{streams,props,sheets,model_basis}.py`, `project/maturity.py`.
- CLI/API and viewer consumers, especially `SimulationPanel.vue`, stream table, API types and fixtures.
- Existing tests: `test_process_qsdsan.py`, `test_qsdsan_worker_contract.py`, `test_process_wastewater.py`, DWSIM/IDAES regressions.

At the reviewed revision, the QSDsan path requires `solver.name == "QSDsan"` and `status == "converged"`, and writes `integration_completed=True, converged=True`. Its ownership prefix also includes QSDsan. These are concrete coupling points to remove from the shared machinery.

## Required design

### 1. Separate simulator semantics from execution transport

Use a small typed interface and registry, following existing repository conventions. Avoid a plugin marketplace, dependency-injection framework or speculative class hierarchy.

**Simulator adapter responsibilities**
- Validate simulator-specific settings and declare supported modes/capabilities.
- Prepare or identify the model and explicit input/output mappings.
- Operate/translate the native model, interpret simulator diagnostics and map outputs to stable ChemE stream/unit IDs.
- Report actual simulator/version/method and numerical outcome.
- Define the supported publication mapping (e.g. molecular state fields versus measured-basis calculated quantities).

**Execution transport responsibilities**
- Stage declared inputs and invoke the configured execution environment.
- Enforce timeout, collect logs/response/evidence and perform resource cleanup.
- Return a structured execution outcome independent of the simulator's numerical outcome.

**Process-domain orchestration responsibilities**
- Validate case and inputs, fingerprint the model, invoke the adapter/transport.
- Validate outputs, protect authored values, publish results/evidence/run records.
- Supply consistent staleness, CLI, validation, maturity and read-only viewer behaviour.

Keep integration wrappers in `integrations/`; process semantics in `domains/process/`. Foundation must not import process or integration code. Do not move process-specific machinery into foundation just to call it generic.

Implement the existing local Python subprocess transport. Define the seam so a future Windows automation session or remote worker can implement it without changing stream/results consumers. **Do not implement remote scheduling, credentials, RPC or COM automation here.** A simulator must not intrinsically mean "Python module launched on this host".

### 2. Versioned request and result contracts

Use typed, versioned request/response contracts; reuse and carefully extend `AdapterResult` rather than introducing a competing results format.

The request should represent:
- Case/run identity and simulation mode.
- Declared model/data/source inputs and simulator-specific configuration.
- Execution timeout and an assigned evidence destination.
- Explicit mapping/selection information needed to associate results with existing ChemE IDs.

Keep environment selection outside committed engineering data: executable paths, endpoints and credentials are user/deployment configuration. Preserve `CHEME_QSDSAN_PYTHON` for existing users. If a shared executor configuration is added, document precedence and test conflicting/missing settings. Do not permit arbitrary shell command strings in project YAML.

Native model assets must be legitimate declared inputs: e.g. Aspen/HYSYS model files or Modelica sources and initialization data. Fingerprint/copy them as bytes; do not assume all inputs are UTF-8 or require arbitrary binary assets to be embedded in API payloads. Missing assets produce actionable findings.

Document a bounded extension contract for simulator-specific options. Unsupported modes/capabilities must be refused explicitly; do not register nonfunctional Aspen/HYSYS/Dymola adapters as supported.

### 3. Distinguish execution completion from numerical and engineering claims

Define and implement a consistent outcome model covering:
- Execution completed / failed / timed out / refused (and cancellation only if actually implemented).
- Numerical convergence: true / false / not applicable or unknown.
- Dynamic integration: requested interval, achieved end time and whether the requested interval completed.
- Steady-state assessment: independently established / not established / not evaluated, with evidence where available.

A worker exit code of zero alone is not numerical success. A dynamic run reaching its final time is not evidence of steady state. Partial trajectories remain diagnostic evidence and must not silently replace accepted final stream values.

The current AdapterStatus enum has no dynamic "completed" status. Resolve this deliberately in an ADR: introduce an appropriate supported status/fields and update **all** consumers, or use a documented compatible representation that does not assert convergence. Check schema-version/semantic-version requirements; do not silently change the meaning of existing v1 records.

Old DWSIM/IDAES records, including records with only `converged`, must remain readable with their previous meaning. Preserve old QSDsan records without retroactively presenting their legacy convergence flag as independent steady-state evidence. Propagation/property-calculation consumers of AdapterResult must also remain compatible.

### 4. Shared publication and provenance

Extract QSDsan's reusable lifecycle into simulator-neutral functions. Keep backend-specific mapping and units outside the generic executor.

Requirements:
- Both check and fill run against staged inputs; only core publishes accepted results.
- Preserve given/assumed values and values owned by other producers.
- Retain measured bases (mg COD/L, mg N/L, etc.); never treat them as ordinary molecular concentrations without an explicit conversion

## Goal
Demonstrate the principle of engineering intent → structured control specification → generated PLC code → executable behavior tests, using one small, coherent example.

Deliver a convincing, inspectable first draft that shows the potential of ChemE-as-Code. This is an experimental demonstration, not production-ready automation or a claim of validated plant control.

Depends on the control foundations in an earlier issue. Keep the example narrow enough to complete without implementing a general automation platform.

## Demonstration story
Use a pump transferring liquid between two vessels, linked to existing equipment/instrument tags where practical.
A user can inspect the operating narrative, sequence specification, generated Structured Text and a simulation trace showing how the sequence behaves.

Illustrative conditions to finalize explicitly:
- Start request plus specified process/equipment permissives.
- Start command, running feedback and a startup-feedback timeout.
- Normal stop.
- Loss of a running permissive or an equipment fault.
- Latched fault, reset eligibility and deliberate restart.
- Initial/power-restoration behavior without an unintended automatic restart.
Record which conditions are start-only permissives and which are continuously monitored; do not assume they are interchangeable.

## 1. Precise, target-independent source specification
- [ ] Reuse an earlier issue's sequence/state definitions and core's stable IDs/references rather than inventing a second authoritative format.
- [ ] Define states, transitions, priorities, outputs, timers, permissives, fault conditions and reset/restart semantics explicitly.
- [ ] Add a small logical I/O map with names, types, units where applicable, signal polarity and meaning. Physical addresses may remain illustrative/unassigned.
- [ ] Specify simulated task period, scan/update semantics, input sampling and timer behavior.
- [ ] Document contradictory commands, missing/invalid feedback and stop/fault precedence.
- [ ] Identify unresolved assumptions; refuse generation when required behavior is ambiguous.
- [ ] Separate equipment sequence logic from vendor libraries and hardware bindings.

## 2. Draft PLC code generation
- [ ] Generate a readable IEC 61131-3 Structured Text function block and a small example program/harness.
- [ ] Start with one explicitly selected compiler/runtime target after checking availability, maintenance and licence; make no blanket claim of cross-vendor portability.
- [ ] Keep generation in core with a narrow target adapter; no new repository or separate simulation application.
- [ ] Include explicit inputs/outputs/state, initialization, timer use and comments linking code to source state/transition IDs.
- [ ] Keep generated code reproducible and record source fingerprints/generator/target versions.
- [ ] Regenerate from the specification; do not maintain separately edited logic in the generated code.
- [ ] Unsupported constructs and target differences produce explicit diagnostics.

## 3. Executable demonstration and verification
- [ ] Compile and execute generated code using the selected target's simulator/runtime where feasible.
- [ ] If only a Python/reference state-machine simulation is available, label that limitation prominently; it does not prove the generated PLC code executes correctly.
- [ ] Compare generated-code traces against independently specified expected behavior; avoid testing only a generator against its own interpreter.
- [ ] Exercise successful startup, blocked startup, normal stop, startup timeout, running fault/permissive loss, reset refusal, valid reset and deliberate restart.
- [ ] Test startup/power restoration, simultaneous commands and relevant timer/scan-boundary cases.
- [ ] Verify invariants such as output de-energized in stopped/fault states and reset alone not initiating a start, according to the declared example specification.
- [ ] Use deterministic scripted inputs and a simple virtual plant/feedback model. Clearly distinguish simulated signals from physical equipment.
- [ ] Report actual pass/fail and compiler/runtime errors, not a static mock success screen.

## 4. Presentation of the principle
- [ ] Provide one worked example with narrative, structured source, logical I/O map, generated code, test scenarios and execution traces.
- [ ] Generate an accessible report showing state timeline, input/output signals, timer events and transition reasons.
- [ ] If integrated into the existing viewer, add an optional control-demonstration panel only when artifacts exist; use read-only API/snapshot conventions.
- [ ] Allow inspection of a successful cycle and a fault/reset cycle without requiring hardware.
- [ ] Display experimental status, target/runtime, tested behaviors and untested assumptions beside results.
- [ ] Keep full technical artifacts available so the demonstration is reviewable rather than merely visual.

## Scope boundaries
No connection to physical PLCs, deployment, vendor project commissioning, safety PLC/SIS logic, SIL claims, general DCS implementation, controller tuning or full dynamic process simulation.
The example demonstrates equipment sequencing under declared assumptions; production use would require target-specific engineering, independent review and commissioning.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] One end-to-end example can be reproduced from documented commands.
- [ ] A source change produces an understandable code diff and invalidates old run results.
- [ ] Generated code compiles and runs on the named target, or the exact unexecuted portion is clearly identified.
- [ ] Behavior tests cover both nominal and fault/restart scenarios with recorded evidence.
- [ ] The demonstration shows the source-to-code-to-behavior chain clearly and honestly.
- [ ] Core remains usable without the optional PLC compiler/runtime.
- [ ] Document concrete next capabilities suggested by the pilot, without expanding this issue into a general automation platform.

## Suggested small increments
1. Fix the example's behavior and expected traces.
2. Implement the minimal source contract and target-specific generator.
3. Compile/run and verify the scenarios.
4. Add the readable demonstration report and optional viewer presentation.

Related: An earlier issue (narratives, loops and sequences), #11 (process-library evidence and maturity).

## Goal

Demonstrate and qualify ChemE-as-Code for a complete industrial process plant: process design through coordinated detailed engineering, procurement specifications, fabrication/installation packages, control verification and commissioning/handover preparation.

**Priority: P1-high.** Parent: #220; wider capability roadmap: #9.

The acceptance scope is a complete multi-unit plant with utilities and offsites, not a pump/exchanger skid. Small fixtures remain useful for numerical qualification and iterative development.

## Reference project and boundary

Use the existing ammonia library design as the starting reference, after auditing its maturity and sources. Record a sourced capacity, product specification, site design basis and project boundary before claiming completeness. Treat site/geotechnical/environmental inputs absent from evidence as assumptions requiring resolution.

Reference coverage for a natural-gas-based route should include feed treatment, hydrogen/syngas generation, shift and purification, compression, synthesis/recycle, ammonia recovery/storage, and the required utility/offsite systems. Confirm actual route and unit applicability against the selected project basis; do not imply the current library already covers all of these.

Include water/cooling/steam/power and applicable relief/flare/vent, drainage/effluent, fire-protection, access, lifting and maintenance interfaces. Survey missing capabilities and create/link implementation work, including licensed/specialist external tools where required.

## Work packages

- [ ] Audit the current ammonia package and establish an independently defined plant-wide deliverables/check matrix with stable requirements, system boundaries and completion criteria.
- [ ] Define a master configuration and interface register: process conditions, line classes, equipment duties, vendor geometry/connections/loads, control signals, utility supplies and civil loads.
- [ ] Integrate #221–#240 engineering calculations and #241–#252 discipline workflows, with the smallest scientifically valid increments but a plant-scale destination.
- [ ] Generate/reconcile PFDs, P&IDs, line/equipment/instrument lists, datasheets, electrical loads/I/O/cables, layout/GA, piping isometrics/spools/BOMs, supports/foundation interfaces and calculation dossiers.
- [ ] Incorporate supplied or explicitly illustrative vendor packages and technical bid/deviation workflows; never label estimated information supplier-certified.
- [ ] Implement common operating/design/load cases, units, reference states and cross-discipline requirement/constraint checks.
- [ ] Exercise capacity increase, feed/site condition change, vendor revision and utility outage; compare impacts and rerun affected calculations/drawings/reviews.
- [ ] Qualify dynamic/control and equipment-sequence behaviour with actual executable tests where supported; maintain clear boundaries for simulation versus physical evidence.
- [ ] Assemble construction/test packages, commissioning plans and structured handover information; track outstanding physical tests rather than claiming they were performed.
- [ ] Commission independent discipline reviews and record discrepancies, resolution and residual scope; expand capability based on actual gaps.

## Completion gates

1. **Basis and interfaces:** project requirements, applicability and interface ownership defined; missing inputs explicit.
2. **Process and equipment:** reconciled balances, verified methods, equipment ratings and operating limits; supplier dependencies visible.
3. **Disciplines:** applicable mechanical, piping/stress, structural/civil, instruments/control, electrical and protection checks supported and reviewed for the declared scope.
4. **Deliverables:** component/tag/connection/quantity consistency across drawings, schedules, model and procurement records.
5. **Change resilience:** declared plant changes invalidate the right artifacts and produce coherent recomputed revisions without hiding failed/unresolved work.
6. **Release readiness:** every required deliverable/check has evidence and review status; unresolved mandatory items block the corresponding release stage.

## Acceptance evidence

- A reproducible full-plant package with pinned input/tool/model revisions and an explicit achieved versus pending scope matrix.
- Numerical qualification and independent review per method/discipline, not just schema checks or successful artifact generation.
- Quantified reconciliation across mass/energy, pressure networks, loads/reactions, component quantities and signal/connection interfaces.
- Baseline and changed scenarios with actual outcomes, failures, remaining constraints and engineering decisions.
- An honest distinction between design-package readiness, supplier confirmation, approval for construction and physical construction/commissioning evidence.

## Programme management

Deliver in dependency-based phases and reviewable PRs; do not attempt one enormous implementation. Prioritise #241/#242 shared foundations alongside #221–#225 core calculations, then build complete unit/discipline slices into the full reference plant. Track cost/runtime, failures and manual interventions. Broader process coverage follows, with a batch/fine-chemical reference to exercise vacuum/mixing/filtration/drying not represented by ammonia.

## Objective
Model a plant's **outputs that are neither product nor emission** as exchanges whose treatment depends on the system model: spent catalysts and adsorbents, waste oil, sludges, off-spec product, scrap at end of life and recyclable by-products. Then the same unallocated dataset can be linked correctly under cut-off, APOS or consequential modelling.

Part of the LCI database gap analysis (ChemE-as-Code/process-library#43).

## Current state (main, 2026-10-24)
- `DatasetExchange.type` has `output` ("a waste or other output"). In ASU-1 the only outputs are the vent and the condensate (released to the environment) and the heat rejected.
- **Consumables are counted as inputs, but their disposal is not.** ASU-1 replaces 36 t of molecular sieve and alumina every 6 years and uses 2 t/a of lube oil. The spent sieve (landfill or regeneration) and the waste oil (incineration or re-refining) do not appear as outputs.
- End of life is an **avoided-burden credit** (`end_of_life` with `fraction: 0.9`). The process library exports it as proxies of −0.5 kg steel per kg of scrap and −0.7 kg aluminium per kg of scrap, into a database meant to link to **ecoinvent cut-off**. Under cut-off, scrap leaves burden-free and gets no credit. `lci/mappings.yaml` notes this ("drop the exchange for a strict cut-off model") but nothing enforces it.

## Gap
1. Classify outputs as **waste for treatment**, **recyclable material** (cut-off: burden-free), or **by-product with value** (allocation or substitution applies). Use ecoinvent's classification logic (by-product versus waste by economic value) as a reference.
2. Express waste outputs as **technosphere exchanges to a treatment activity** (landfill of spent zeolite, incineration of waste mineral oil, WWTP per m³ or per kg COD, hazardous waste incineration). Sign conventions should be explicit for each background, replacing the install-time sign flip.
3. **System-model-dependent end of life**: one dataset declares the material flows (scrap amount and quality). The export applies cut-off (no credit), APOS or a credit by substitution, per the target database. Never mix: a cut-off database must not contain avoided-burden credits.
4. **Catalysts**: initial charge and periodic replacement (mass, metal content, life) as inputs, and spent catalyst to metal recovery or disposal as outputs. Platinum-group and nickel catalysts can dominate several impact categories.

## Proposed scope
- [ ] `output` exchanges get `treatment: {kind: waste|recyclable|byproduct, route}` and links to a treatment background or an Atlas utility (ChemE-as-Code/process-library#45).
- [ ] `consumables:` and `construction:` get an optional `disposal:` (route and fraction). The engine writes the matching output exchanges, so that what goes in also comes out.
- [ ] `end_of_life` is reformulated as material outputs plus a study-level `system_model` (cut-off, APOS, substitution) that decides credits. process-library export credits are generated only for a non-cut-off target (ChemE-as-Code/process-library#51, ChemE-as-Code/process-library#52).
- [ ] ASU-1: spent adsorbent and waste oil outputs, and recycling credits removed from the cut-off export.

## Acceptance criteria
- A cut-off export contains no negative "avoided" exchanges. Every consumable with a finite life has a disposal output, or a recorded cut-off.

## Related
ChemE-as-Code/process-library#52 (library-wide system model), ChemE-as-Code/process-library#45 (treatment utilities), #16 (mass closure catches missing waste outputs).

Not yet reviewed or merged: the review workflow was stopped to save budget. Next: independent review (domain, correctness, integration), rebase on main, merge.

Capability gap found by the process-library case study for [process-library#335](https://github.com/ChemE-as-Code/process-library/issues/335) (scope tracker process-library#333).

## Gap

cheme has no dynamic process model. Comparing two control structures for a column (here: electrified methanol/water distillation with flash vapour circulation, Cui et al. 2025, doi:10.1016/j.cherd.2025.07.023) needs:

- tray-by-tray column dynamics: holdups, hydraulics (Francis weir or a liquid time constant), energy or constant-molar-overflow balances, and VLE from the property package;
- PI controllers for level, pressure, temperature and composition, wired to the loops of `control/loops.yaml` and the P&ID;
- relay-feedback or Tyreus-Luyben tuning, with the tuning recorded;
- disturbance scenarios (feed composition or throughput steps) with time series of controlled and manipulated variables, such as compressor power.

The case implements a reduced version of this in its own `run.py` (process-library `benchmarks/reproductions/electrified-distillation-control/`). cheme's P&ID authoring covered the loop drawing.

## Scope of a first step

A dynamic unit for a column section and a PI-loop runner that reads `control/loops.yaml`, checked against the case's run: 18 of 19 frozen checks pass, including both direction checks.

`separations/coverage.py` explicitly says there is no isotherm, breakthrough or PSA/TSA cycle model. The generic component separator is classified `specified` by `simulation/translate.py`, even if the surrounding flowsheet converges.

Source audit of core main `cec7e819e47c58ab036dcdcd4aec24810f08474a` (27 October 2026); source/docs inspected, no fresh solver run or blanket validation claim.

## Affected process-library work
- https://github.com/ChemE-as-Code/process-library/issues/173
- https://github.com/ChemE-as-Code/process-library/issues/117
- https://github.com/ChemE-as-Code/process-library/issues/181

These are **conditional prerequisites for the scoped predictive model/engineering claim**, not blockers to references, a brief, BFD or an explicitly sourced empirical inventory. Select route and target first.

## Acceptance checks
- [ ] Define a sourced isotherm/cycle or external performance-model contract with feed conditions, adsorbent, cycle basis, recovery/purity and regeneration utilities.
- [ ] Qualify one bounded PSA or TSA case for recovery, impurity specification, material closure and utility consumption, including operating range.
- [ ] Track adsorbent replacement/regeneration boundary and model fingerprints; distinguish prescribed splits from independently calculated performance.
- [ ] Retain sourced component splits for conceptual scope; do not require this model before a BFD or sourced inventory.
- [ ] Add one reproducible positive reference test and meaningful unsupported/failure cases; record solver/data versions, tolerances and independent comparison.
- [ ] Update capability/maturity reporting, docs and the ADR for any public contract change; preserve existing ASU workflows.
- [ ] Link the evidence back to affected library issues and state which target is now supported.

## Coordination
Focused follow-up under #9 and #11; distinguish this implementation/qualification scope from general readiness #27. Reuse existing models and adapters rather than adding equations to skills or library folders. Library discovery trackers: ChemE-as-Code/process-library#306 and ChemE-as-Code/process-library#174.


---
_Comment (2026-10-27):_

## Status after an earlier PR (merged)

**Now supported in core**
- `process/adsorption.yaml` (`cheme/adsorption/v1`, `cheme schema process-adsorption`) and `cheme process adsorption [--case] [--json]`:
  - an equilibrium **TSA** cycle from sourced isotherms (Langmuir, dual/multi-site Langmuir, Sips, Toth; extended Langmuir/Sips within a layer), each limited to its measured T and partial-pressure range (`cheme.adsorption-isotherm-range` refuses anything outside it);
  - breakthrough at the stoichiometric time less half the measured MTZ;
  - recoveries and product impurity, regeneration heat, hot-purge minima and heater duty;
  - adsorbent inventory and replacement rate, reported as a consumable outside the cycle.
- `performance: external` holds an external model's or vendor's results (PSA included), with their operating range checked. A calculated PSA is refused (`cheme.adsorption-unsupported`).
- Model basis: `adsorption-equilibrium` (predictive, **not simulated**) or `external-performance` (specified). This applies only when the entry qualifies, is fully sourced and the simulator's split agrees within `split_tolerance`; otherwise the unit stays `component-split`. Sourced component splits stay the conceptual representation, and the file is optional. Each unit carries a fingerprint (model `equilibrium-tsa/1`), and `cheme maturity` fingerprints the file. ADR 0024.

**Evidence**
- Reference case `tests/test_adsorption_reference.py::test_the_reference_case_qualifies`: CO2 layer of an ASU front-end on 13X.
  - Isotherm: NASA/TM-2017-219847, Grade 544, 3-site Langmuir (Table 2). Within 3.5 % of 11 measured Table 1 points at the feed states and within 12 % of 9 points at 150–200 °C; each tolerance is the fit's own largest residual in that window.
  - MTZ: 198 mm, US 6,506,236 B2 Example 1.
  - 13X bed properties: IDAES `fixed_bed_tsa0d.py` (Hefti et al. 2015).
  - N2 purge cp: CoolProp 8.0.0, within ±0.01 kJ/(kmol K).
  - Cycle relations are checked against a hand calculation (`tests/test_adsorption.py`). Refusal is tested below 273.15 K feed and above 473.15 K regeneration.
- The reviewer spot-checked the NASA Tables 1, 2 and 4, the patent example and the IDAES parameters against the sources.
- Review fixes:
  - Toth now uses Do's sign of χ.
  - The material balance is labelled as closing by construction (a bookkeeping check, not evidence); negative waste and zero feed are refused.
  - The heat-of-adsorption wording is corrected.
- The CO2 spec in the reference case is met by breakthrough time (about 14 h against the 4 h step); before breakthrough, the equilibrium leak is 0 with a CO2-free purge.

**Remaining gaps (why this stays open)**
- The calculated cycle (breakthrough, recovery, regeneration duty) is not compared with a measured TSA cycle; no open dataset was found. This is the missing "independent comparison" for acceptance checks 2 and 5.
- No PSA cycle model (PSA = external results or a sourced split). No thermal front, breakthrough dynamics or heat losses. No N2/O2 co-adsorption in the reference case (no Grade 544 N2 isotherm), so the CO2 capacity is an upper bound.
- `predictive.model-basis` still fails for adsorbers by design: the calculation is not coupled into the DWSIM solve (possible follow-up, as for the fixed bed in #11).

Closes #180.

## What

- New node-level `energy_port:` on Block and Step. It is left out of the dump when not given. It names the energy stream that carries the model's duty. Without it, propagate uses the node's one **heat stream**: an energy stream to or from a steam, hot-oil, fired-heat, cooling-water, air-cooling or refrigerant utility. Electricity, fuel and terminals without `utility:` are not heat. **A stream to or from another block or step counts as heat only where `energy_port` names it**, because it may be a furnace's heat to a coil, a rectifier's DC power or a turbine's shaft work.
- `cheme process propagate --fill` writes the year-average duty (kW per hour of the flowsheet's flows). The value is `calculated`, with source `cheme process propagate: <model> duty <node> from <streams>` and a fingerprint (`domains/process/duties.py`). Models covered:
  - **isothermal batch / semi-batch**: minus the reaction heat released over the batch, plus each dose warmed to the batch temperature (and passing vent gas, where ideal-gas data exist). An adiabatic batch has no duty.
  - **still**: `sum dHvap_i D_i`, the energy per batch over the batch's hours of flows.
  - **crystallizer** with `energy:`: its lumped duty.
  - **conversion step, batch or continuous**: Hess's path through `heat_of_reaction.temperature`. Inlets go to `T_ref`, the reactions run at `T_ref`, and the outlets go from `T_ref` to their own temperature. This is exact for constant cp. A gas step uses ideal-gas `H(out) - H(in)` instead. A gas step here means no stream is liquid or two-phase and no reaction is liquid or mixed. The step's **other energy streams** (DC power, pump or drive work) bring in `W`, their duties signed by direction, and `Q = H(out) - H(in) - W`. The duty is left unknown (info, nothing written) when another energy stream has no duty, when the heats are given at different temperatures, or when a component is vapour on one side and liquid on the other.
- **Sign**: a duty is positive in its stream's direction, as in `energy.py` and the dryer. If the model's heat runs against the stream, that is a warning and nothing is written.
- **Given or assumed duties** are never overwritten. A mismatch beyond the flowsheet's relative tolerance is a `cheme.process-duty` **warning** naming both values. It comes from `propagate --fill`/`--check` and **from `cheme validate`**, which the library CI runs. Validate derives only in a case where a modelled node's stream holds a duty propagate did not write, or a stream joins two models.
- **Two models on one stream**, e.g. a furnace heating a cracker with both naming the stream in `energy_port`: if they agree within tolerance, the first is written. If they differ, neither is written and a warning names both.
- `validate` adds `cheme.process-energy-port`: an error if the port is not an energy port of the node, a warning if no model of the node gives a duty.
- Flow-style energy streams (`{id: Q1, ...}`) are edited in place.
- `cheme process reactors` shows a batch's or conversion step's model duty, its terms (including `other energy streams`) and its stream. It shows this where the header used to print `duty ?`. `--json` adds `model_duty` only where the model knows a duty, a stream wants one, or there is a note. `cheme process stills` adds the year-average duty.
- Docs: ADR 0059 (nav entry, README row), REFERENCE.md, the process-design skill, CHANGELOG `## Unreleased` (with a behaviour-change note). Example sheets were rebuilt because the generator's code hash changed.

## Behaviour change: library lockstep

On scratch copies of all 73 process-library entries (`main` at cccfb569), I ran `propagate --check` with 1.8.0 and with this branch. **Seven entries go from exit 0 to exit 1**, and `cheme validate` now reports the same `cheme.process-duty` warning for each (it still exits 0). These entries need a library update in lockstep. The fix in each case is to remove the hand duty, correct the model data, or record the difference in DESIGN.md:

| entry / node / stream | hand (assumed) | model | why |
|---|---|---|---|
| benzyl-chloroformate-1 R101 Q2 (semibatch) | 20.03 | 18.7043 | hand value adds a heat of absorption (L-10) |
| sodium-azide-1 R102 Q2 (semibatch) | 126.68 | 126.198 | hand value leaves out the dose's warming |
| ethylene-1 H102 Q102 (firebox) | 195682 | 204845 | the model has no heat losses. Q101/Q104 to the coils are subtracted as other energy streams |
| formic-acid-1 R201 Q10 | 256.5 | 252.331 | dHr is taken at its declared 298.15 K, not at 393 K. Give `temperature: 393.15` if that is meant |
| hydrogen-bromide-1 R101 Q2 | 166.4 | 169.391 | the 3 kW instrument power stream into R101 counts as work in. Move it if it does not reach the fluid |
| hydrogen-chloride-1 R101 Q1 | 2195.1 | 2272.86 | 4.98 kW power in, plus the hand value's 3 % loss |
| phosphorus-oxychloride-1 R201 Q3 | 1912.3 | 1938.82 | continuous conversion step, hand path differs |

The reviewer's earlier list changed:
- **acetic-anhydride-1** (H101 to R101 by Q2) and **chlor-alkali-1** EL301 (DC power Q2 from T301) now get an info: the stream joins another step and is heat only via `energy_port`.
- **thionyl-chloride-1** R102 now gets an info. O2 is vapour in and liquid out, and its `heat_of_reaction` is on the gas basis. The model no longer writes or compares the ideal-gas 61.91 kW.
- **potassium-permanganate-1** EL401 subtracts its DC power Q3 once the cp data are given.
- **sodium-nitrite-1** no longer fails.

`process reactors` text and `--json` change for 44 of the 73 entries (the model-duty line). No other fields of a reactor's entry change.

Unchanged: `cheme process propagate --check` prints the same as 1.8.0 for every example in this repository. `process reactors` changes for process-semibatch (`duty ?` becomes the semibatch model's year average).

## Review fixes (second commit)

1. DC power or shaft work from a block or step is no longer taken as the heat stream. The conversion heat subtracts the other energy streams' signed duties, and a missing one is reported as missing. Tests cover an electrolyser (rectifier step to cell, cooling to CW) and a stream between two steps.
2. A liquid conversion step never takes the ideal-gas branch, and stream phases are now in its fingerprint. Tests cover a liquid step with full ideal-gas data and a component changing phase.
3. Two models on one stream are compared (warning, neither written) or written once when they agree. The test checks both propagate and validate.
4. Hess's path runs through `heat_of_reaction.temperature`. The test expects `(6*-80000 + 10*150*8.15 + (4*150+6*120)*21.85)/3600`. Changing the temperature makes the duty stale and changes the refilled value.
5. CHANGELOG, ADR and the PR now state the continuous conversion steps, the new `--check` exit code and the affected library entries. `validate` reports the comparison. `model_duty` is left out of the reactors JSON where it has nothing to say.

## Tests

`tests/test_duties.py` (18 tests) checks the models against closed forms and the propagate and validate behaviour:
- batch heat = dHr x extent; semi-batch dose term = n cp dT
- still = `sum dHvap_i D_i`, and not stale when the boil-up changes
- Felder's crystallizer
- conversion against Hess through `T_ref`
- the electrolyser's `Q = dH - W`
- stale on more power
- liquid versus gas branch; a phase change
- two models
- comparison and tolerance (propagate and validate), never-overwrite, reversed stream, ambiguity, `energy_port` rules, plants without heat streams, no `model_duty` without heat or stream

The 7 new or changed tests fail on the first commit.

Full suite: 4356 passed, 131 skipped. `ruff` and `mkdocs build --strict` are clean.

## Limits

- One duty per stream. Charge heat-up, still condensers (per-cut duties), agitation in batches and the dryer are not written.
- No heat of absorption, solution or mixing, and no phase change across a conversion step.
- A conversion step's heats are taken on

The rest of core#182 (ADR 0078): a jacket-limited boil-up, activity coefficients in the still, and the reasons there is no reaction in a still.

## What changes

- **Jacket boil-up**: `boilup: {value: UA, unit: kW/K, medium_temperature: K}`, on the still or on a cut, raoult only. The heat input is `UA (T_m - T)` at the still's bubble point, so `V = UA (T_m - T) / lambda(y)` falls as the pot heats.
  - An end at or above the medium's temperature is refused when the flowsheet is read.
  - A residue end the still would reach only above the medium stalls, and the message gives that reason. It no longer reads as a still that boils dry or a crawl on a trace.
  - With `heat_up_time`, the heat-up takes the jacket's own time, `C / UA ln((T_m - T_in) / (T_m - T_0))`.
  - With a time end, `medium_temperature` enters the outlets' fingerprint.
- **Activity coefficients**: `volatility: {model: raoult, activity: unifac}` uses modified Raoult's law with original UNIFAC (thermo, DDBST groups, extra `props`).
  - Each component of the liquid needs its `cas`. `cheme.process-still` reports an error for one without, and a component without UNIFAC groups is refused rather than treated as ideal.
  - The bubble point is iterated against the activity coefficients until it settles to 1e-11.
  - A column takes `gamma_i P_i / P` at the still.
  - `integrations.thermo.unifac_gammas` sets UNIFAC up once per solve and evaluates it with `to_T_xs`, about 40 times faster than setting it up on every call.
  - `process stills` names the model in `detail` and in the assumptions.
- **No reaction in a still**: the ADR gives three reasons.
  - The still integrates over the kmol boiled up, but a reaction runs in time, including during the heat-up.
  - A reaction's heat changes a heat-input boil-up.
  - The motivating case (Boc2O) gives off isobutene and CO2, and the still's total condenser has no gas outlet.
  - A still that is also a reactor stays refused.
- **Not done, with the reasons in the ADR**:
  - NRTL in the still: it needs sourced VLE pairs, and core's NRTL pairs are LLE tie-line fits.
  - The wetted area falling as the pot empties: the vessel is sized from the still's own content, so this would be circular.

Both options are opt-in. A still without them dumps, fingerprints, solves and reports as before. An ideal still runs the same bubble-point code as before.

## Review fixes (fe828ed)

- **A liquid that splits into two is refused.** Before this, UNIFAC gave water 0.1 in toluene at 1 atm a bubble point of 324.1 K. Any mixture of the two boils at or above 357.5 K (the heteroazeotrope), so the result was wrong and came with no warning. The still now raises `StillError` ("the still's liquid splits into two liquids ...") in two cases:
  - at every bubble point where a component's activity `gamma_i x_i` is above 1;
  - at every profile point where Michelsen's tangent-plane test fails. The test runs by successive substitution from each component nearly pure. It also catches a split where every activity stays below 1, such as 1-butanol 0.1 in water at 360 K.

  The message says that `separate_phase` keeps its component from boiling, so it does not model a heteroazeotrope. The cost is about 1.6 times the UNIFAC solve time for methanol-toluene.
- **A pair of UNIFAC groups without parameters is refused.** `unifac_gammas` checks every pair of the liquid's main groups against UFIP and raises `ValueError` naming the pair. Before this, thermo's `from_subgroups` set a missing pair to 0 without a warning (water/iodomethane, main groups 7 and 32).
- **One jacket on every cut** (the same UA and medium) now times the charge's heat-up with the jacket's log-mean, as a jacket on the still does. With the PR test's charge, the result was 2107 s before and is 1542 s now, which matches the exact value. Different jackets on the cuts keep ADR 0068's mean.
- **`process stills` assumptions:**
  - A jacket's boil-up replaces "constant boil-up" in the assumptions, including in the heat-up texts. Where only some boil-ups are jackets, the jacket's text is added next to the constant one.
  - With a column, `activity` adds the modified Raoult's law. The column's volatility text now names the activity coefficients instead of "raoult or constant".
- **A jacket still's stall message** names the medium only when the driving force has fallen below 1 % of what it was at the start of the run. A column crawling on a trace with a jacket far below its medium now gets the pace's message again.
- **`validate`** says "the boil-up in kW/K is not known" for a jacket. Before, it said kW.
- **Docs:** the `heat_up_time` schema description (and the viewer fixture), REFERENCE, the docstrings, ADR 0078, SKILL.md and CHANGELOG now cover the jacket's heat-up, the liquid that splits and the group pairs.
- **Not changed:** `integrations.thermo.unifac_activity_coefficients`, which the liquid-phase reactions' `activity` basis uses, already worked this way before this PR (a missing pair counts as 0). It is left alone to keep this PR focused.

## Tests

`tests/test_still_jacket_activity.py` has 18 tests: the 10 from the first commit plus 8 for the review fixes.

- Water/toluene is refused at water 0.1 and 0.5, and a trace of water dissolves as one liquid. Water's Antoine constants are acetyl-chloride-1's: NIST WebBook, fitted to Stull (1947).
- The tangent-plane test finds the 1-butanol/water split with both activities below 1, and passes 0.01 and 0.6.
- The water/iodomethane group pair is refused.
- One jacket on the only cut gives the exact heat-up time (rel 1e-9). Two different jackets keep the mean.
- The assumptions of a jacket plant, with and without `heat_up`, have no "constant boil-up". A column plant with `activity` lists the modified Raoult's law.
- `validate` names kW/K.
- The batch-rectification crawl with a jacket at 600 K stalls with the pace's message.

## Checks

- `uv run ruff format --check` and `uv run ruff check` pass. `uv run --group docs mkdocs build --strict` passes.
- `uv run pytest -n auto`: 4732 passed, 133 skipped.
- The `examples/process-*` sheets are rebuilt (only `generator_sha256` changes, because `schema.py` changed). `viewer/tests/fixtures/api/yaml-flowsheet.json` is regenerated, and it is the only fixture kept. The skill and init manifests are rebuilt.

I ran every entry of the process library (`origin/main` b54fcaeb, all 122 entries, two separate `git archive` copies) with the pin (`core-pin`, 1.12.0 + #254) and with this branch at fe828ed. ## Objective
Track a later, bounded IDAES integration as an optional core backend. This is deferred work, not a prerequisite for the current process-library release. Do not create a separate simulation application or duplicate the existing reactor engine.

## Existing foundation
Core already has reactor contracts, fixed-bed calculations, propagation, DWSIM integration and shared run-result/provenance conventions. Audit these before implementation. Coordinate with #11.

## Initial pilot
- [ ] Select one sourced exothermic PFR/fixed-bed case with suitable kinetics and thermophysical data.
- [ ] Define the exact model scope: steady state, geometry, rate/catalyst basis, phase/nonideality, energy balance, heat transfer and pressure drop.
- [ ] Implement an optional IDAES adapter using shared core inputs/results. Keep IDAES/Pyomo/solver dependencies optional and out of basic imports.
- [ ] Reuse reaction/property definitions where compatible; diagnose unsupported translations rather than silently approximating them.
- [ ] Compare temperature, composition/conversion, pressure and heat-duty profiles with the existing implementation under matched assumptions.
- [ ] Use independent analytic/reference checks as well as cross-backend comparison; agreement between implementations alone is not validation.
- [ ] Record backend/solver versions, initialization, discretization, tolerances, convergence, input fingerprints and diagnostics.
- [ ] Check spatial-grid refinement and conservation before claiming a credible profile.
- [ ] Demonstrate one bounded optimization only after simulation is verified (e.g. coolant temperature or reactor length subject to a temperature constraint).
- [ ] Document how the reactor connects to whole-flowsheet recycles/separations; do not assume a standalone solve establishes that coupling.

## Boundaries
No broad migration from DWSIM; no new repository or standalone UI. IDAES does not supply missing process-specific kinetics/property parameters. Dynamics, complex multiphase models and generalized process optimization are later extensions.

## Acceptance criteria
A reproducible optional pilot runs from shared inputs, reports failures explicitly, returns versioned profile/run results, passes reference/conservation/grid checks, and works without changing the default backend. Basic core functionality remains usable without IDAES or its solver.

Priority: later integration after current property, workflow and benchmark blockers.
