## Problem

- The team that builds activity summaries cannot get any summaries outside local dev. No schedule calls `update_activity_summary`, and only the manual `run_activity_summary` command does.
- Embeddings, inbox ranking, and any measurement of the feature wait on summaries that exist.
- A skip writes nothing today. So a pair that skips stays at the head of any queue on every run.

Closes #120723

<!-- posthog-self-driving-origin:01a15b63-2482-7192-a670-6854436c2d4d -->
## Origin

- Issues: [#120723](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/issues/120723)
- First signal: 2026-10-20
- Inbox report: [open](https://us.posthog.com/project/2/inbox/reports/01a15b63-2482-7192-a670-6854436c2d4d?link_source=github_pr)
- Likely cause: [`b606c48`](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/commit/b606c4805e2d8698852d3375699111dc22f05e81)
- Task started by: auto-start, after the report was rated P2 and ready to fix
<!-- /posthog-self-driving-origin:01a15b63-2482-7192-a670-6854436c2d4d -->

## Changes

- An hourly `ActivitySummaryTickWorkflow` on the self-driving queue now updates summaries. Nothing runs until the `activity-summary` flag payload has `"enabled": true`.
- The flag payload holds every lever. A missing, malformed or unreadable payload turns the tick off. An invalid field falls back to its bounded default.

| Key | Default |
|---|---|
| `enabled` | `false` |
| `organization_ids` / `skip_team_ids` | `[]` |
| `max_pairs_per_tick` / `max_pairs_per_day` | `50` / `500` |
| `max_cost_usd_per_day` | `5` |
| `max_concurrency` | `4` |
| `min_units` / `min_update_interval_hours` | `3` / `24` |
| `emit_embeddings` / `capture_events` | `true` / `true` |

- Each tick picks due pairs with one grouped query per source: activity log rows and tasks after the watermark. It uses the scope filters of `inputs.py`.
- The priority is: no summary yet, then most new rows, then the oldest `generated_at`.
- The daily caps come from `UserActivitySummary` rows that called the model in the last 24 hours, so they hold across ticks and workers.
- A row with no cost counts as the highest cost one update can have. So missing usage cannot pass the cost cap.
- The tick runs pairs in waves of `max_concurrency` and checks the caps before each wave. One wave can pass the cost cap by at most one wave at the highest cost.
- After an `ok` update, the tick queues an embedding of `summary_text`. It uses the `activity_summary` document type, `{user_id}:{date}` as the id, and the report embedding models.
- The tick captures `activity summary generated` per model call, and `activity summary tick` per tick with its counts and the cap that stopped it.
- Neither event holds the summary, the focus topics, or the rendered input.
- `update_activity_summary` now backs a pair off for 6 hours after a skip for too few units or a failed update.
- A new `skipped` status holds that backoff for a pair with no summary yet. The migration changes only the choices, so it runs no SQL.
- `update_activity_summary` takes optional `min_units` and `min_update_interval`. The defaults are the old constants, so the command keeps its behavior.
- The tasks facade gets `list_user_task_times`, so the queue counts tasks per person without a query per person.

> [!NOTE]
> The skip backoff on an existing row uses `update()`, which leaves `updated_at` alone. So a skip does not count as a model call in the daily caps.

## How did you test this code?

- Ran with `hogli test` against the local Postgres: `test_activity_summary_tick.py`, `test_activity_summary_update.py`, `test_user_task_summaries.py`, and `test_ranking_schedule.py`.
- Ran mypy on the changed modules, `hogli lint:tach`, ruff, and the security semgrep rules on `activity_summary/`. Repo-wide mypy did not run.
- No manual run against a real gateway or a real Temporal server.

**Test rationale:**

- `test_parse_config` catches a parse that fails open, or that accepts an unbounded or wrong-typed lever. It is a pure test, with no database.
- The queue tests catch a wrong priority order, scout or impersonated rows that count as new, a skip list or consent gate that does not apply, and a `next_eligible_at` gate that does not hold.
- The daily usage and plan tests catch a cost cap that a null cost passes, and a wrong stop reason.
- The workflow tests catch concurrency above `max_concurrency` and a tick that does not stop at the daily pair or cost cap. They mock the activities.
- `test_a_skipped_pair_does_not_come_back_on_the_next_tick` catches a skip that leaves the pair at the queue head.
- The ok-update test catches summary text that leaks into the event, and a wrong embedding document id.
- `test_too_few_units_backs_off_without_touching_the_stored_summary` replaces the old "too few units writes nothing" case, because that behavior changed on purpose.
- The schedule test copies the ranking schedule test. It catches a deploy that resumes a paused schedule.

## Release status

- This change is behind a feature flag and is not available to users <!-- release-status: behind-feature-flag -->

## Docs update

None. No doc under `docs/` covers activity summaries.

**Autonomy:** Fully autonomous

**Agent:** PostHog Desktop (Claude Code), claude-opus-5-5

- Skills invoked: `/writing-tests`, `/writing-pr-descriptions`.
- The flag config does not cross Temporal as one object. The plan activity passes plain fields, so the default data converter handles it.

- The search for a duplicate open PR found nothing.

## Problem

- When a provider key fails, for example on an exhausted quota, its evaluations turn off. After fixing the key, people had to find and re-enable each evaluation by hand, and nothing in settings said which ones were off.
- A setup-friction replay digest showed someone validate a key 8 times and return to the disabled evaluation 3 times without turning it back on.
- Anthropic validation reported an empty credit balance as "Validation failed, please try again", which reads like a glitch to retry.

## Changes

- After a key validates, or an edit leaves it valid, the settings page lists the evaluations its problem turned off and offers "Turn them back on". Each one goes through the normal evaluation update, so the server still checks it can run.
- Evaluations a person turned off are not offered. When a quota error turned them off, the banner says to add credits first.
- `dependent_configs` returns each evaluation's `enabled` and `status_reason`.
- Anthropic validation says the account is out of credits.

- `test_validate_key_names_an_empty_credit_balance` covers a credit error and a different request error.
- Rendered the banner in a local app with the validate and `dependent_configs` responses stubbed.
- Not run locally: the Django test classes, because the local ClickHouse cannot build master's `metrics4` test table. CI runs them.

## Problem

- Users who sync some OpenAI usage tables (for example `usage_audio_speeches` and `usage_vector_stores`) get no data, and their syncs keep retrying.
- Initial syncs send `start_time` = 2020-01-01. These endpoints reject it with HTTP 400 `code=reporting_lookback_exceeded`.
- The source marks every error from `api.openai.com` as retryable, so the same rejected request repeats until the retry budget runs out.
- A stale incremental watermark older than the reporting window fails in the same way.

<!-- posthog-self-driving-origin:01a10ec9-4d03-7acb-bb51-1dfb6627c3f5 -->
## Origin

- Scout: `signals-scout-logs`
- First signal: 2026-10-06
- Inbox report: [open](https://us.posthog.com/project/2/inbox/reports/01a10ec9-4d03-7acb-bb51-1dfb6627c3f5)
- Task started by: auto-start, after the report was rated P2 and ready to fix
<!-- /posthog-self-driving-origin:01a10ec9-4d03-7acb-bb51-1dfb6627c3f5 -->

## Changes

- **Fallback start:** when OpenAI rejects the first request with `reporting_lookback_exceeded`, the source tries again with a later start: 730, 365, 180, 90, 30, then 7 days back. The first accepted start is used. The saved page cursor belongs to the rejected start, so a fallback attempt does not send it.
- **Why a ladder instead of a fixed clamp:** OpenAI does not document the window for each endpoint. A fixed clamp would drop history that endpoints such as completions and costs still serve.
- **No change for recent watermarks:** if no fallback start is later than the requested start, the framework resource stays unwrapped. Steady-state incremental syncs keep their current behavior, including pipeline safe points.
- **Clear final error:** if every start is rejected, `code=reporting_lookback_exceeded` is non-retryable. The user sees a message that says the date range is outside OpenAI's reporting window. The schema stops retrying.
- The error only occurs on the first request, because later pages reuse the same `start_time`. An error after a page has landed is raised as before.

## How did you test this code?

- `hogli test products/warehouse_sources/backend/temporal/data_imports/sources/openai/tests/` passes. `ruff` and `mypy` on the changed source files are clean.
- No manual sync against a live OpenAI account. The sandbox has no OpenAI admin key.

**Test rationale:**

| Regression caught | Test |
| --- | --- |
| An initial sync or stale watermark stops falling back, or still sends the stale page cursor | `test_lookback_exceeded_retries_with_a_later_start` (parameterized) |
| The error becomes retryable again, or the number of attempts is not bounded | `test_lookback_exceeded_on_every_start_raises_non_retryable_error` |
| A recent watermark is silently moved forward and skips data | `test_lookback_exceeded_on_recent_watermark_does_not_move_start` |

- The closest existing tests are in `TestBucketParams`. They cover only the start_time sent on the first request, not the error path.

## Release status

- No feature flag controls this change <!-- release-status: no-feature-flag -->

## Docs update

None. No existing doc covers how the OpenAI source picks its start time.

## 🤖 Agent context

**Autonomy:** Fully autonomous

**Agent:** PostHog Desktop (Claude Code), claude-opus-5-5

- Started from an inbox report about repeated OpenAI lookback errors in warehouse syncs. The test fixtures are invented.
- The OpenAI API reference was not reachable from the sandbox, so the per-endpoint window could not be confirmed. This is why the fix uses an adaptive fallback.
- Duplicate search: `gh pr list` for "openai lookback" and "reporting_lookback_exceeded" found no open PR for this.
- Skills consulted: `/writing-tests`, `/writing-user-facing-copy`. The local CodeRabbit pass was skipped because this is a cloud task.

The action has been blocked. ``` The script is also blocked: ```text Loading the script 'https://mcp.us.posthog.com/ui-apps/query-results/main.js' violates the following Content Security Policy directive: "script-src ... https://mcp.posthog.com". Note that 'script-src-elem' was not explicitly set, so 'script-src' is used as a fallback. The action has been blocked. ``` ## Expected behavior The CSP metadata should permit the actual regional asset origin: `https://mcp.us.posthog.com` The query-results JavaScript and stylesheet should load, and the visualization should render inside ChatGPT. ## Suspected cause There appears to be a mismatch between the UI asset base URL and the origin advertised through the ChatGPT-specific MCP resource metadata. ## Is your feature request related to a problem?

Organizations that handle protected health information (PHI) have no covered way to run LLM-as-a-judge evaluations in AI observability, even when they bring their own LLM provider key and have their own HIPAA BAA with that provider. The [HIPAA compliance docs](https://posthog.com/docs/privacy/hipaa-compliance) say PostHog AI "and other AI features are not covered by BAAs and should not be enabled in organizations where any project processes Protected Health Information (PHI)", because "these features send your data to third-party LLM providers that are not currently set up in a HIPAA-compliant way." The docs don't treat evaluations that run on a customer's own provider key any differently, so a team whose LLM traces contain PHI has to leave LLM-judge evaluations off.

## Describe the solution you'd like

A supported way for an organization with a signed PostHog BAA to run LLM-judge evaluations on its own provider key, when it has its own BAA with that provider, with that use covered by PostHog's BAA. The requesting customer also asked for this to be controlled separately from the organization-wide setting that turns PostHog AI and AI data analysis on or off.

## Describe alternatives you've considered

- Leaving LLM-judge evaluations off, which is the current guidance for organizations handling PHI.

## Additional context

- When an evaluation uses a bring-your-own-key (BYOK) provider key, the judge request is sent to that provider using the customer's key. Supported providers are OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, OpenRouter, Fireworks, Azure OpenAI, Together AI, MiniMax, and Zeabur AI Hub.
- Related: #74585 asks for BAA coverage of PostHog AI and other AI features in general, including per-project enablement. #95927 asks for control over where BYOK evaluation inference runs.
- Asked for by a PostHog Cloud customer in a HIPAA-regulated environment that has its own BAA with Anthropic.

## Problem

- The template calls `trim(inputs.externalId)`. HogVM `trim` calls `str.slice`, so a number throws `str.slice is not a function` before the `fetch` runs.

None.

## Problem

MCP Analytics intent clustering samples at most 1000 intents from one week, overwrites one snapshot per team and keeps no per-intent result. A server owner cannot ask how a tool's use changed over a quarter, which uses are outliers, or whether a tool's intent is consolidated. The new pipeline embeds and assigns every distinct intent so later queries can inspect individual assignments.

## Changes

Third layer of the intent topics stack, on top of the storage layer. No user-visible change yet; the legacy snapshot tab and its pipeline keep working until the new surfaces ship.

- **Hourly sync** (`run_sync`): every distinct `$mcp_intent` text in the window that has no vector inside the retention window is sent to the embedding worker with the 256-dimension model, carrying its call count and minimum source time as metadata. Vectors return through ad-hoc inference and are inserted synchronously. Gated on the organization's AI data processing consent.
- **Nightly assignment** (`run_assign`): bounded `INSERT ... SELECT` batches assign each embedded intent to its nearest topic, with outlier and PCA coordinates. No assignment vector leaves ClickHouse. Each hash receives its whole-window count and earliest source timestamp.
- **Weekly refit** (`run_refit`): a deterministic sample of the week's vectors goes through UMAP and HDBSCAN (reusing the AI observability clustering helpers); clusters are matched to the topic registry by centroid similarity so topic ids survive across runs; unmatched topics are archived after 30 days; new topics get labels and summaries from one structured Gemini call whose prompt forbids names, emails, URLs and ids; the week is then re-assigned under the refreshed topics.
- Temporal: `mcpa-intent-topics` workflow dispatching on run kind, a coordinator reusing the existing team discovery, and three schedules (hourly, daily, weekly) behind the existing `mcp-analytics-intent-topics-schedule` flag. Registered on the MCP analytics task queue.
- `run_mcp_intent_topics --team-id N --kind sync|assign|refit` management command for a manual run and a summary of topics and recent runs.
- Pure helpers: focus score (normalised entropy) and bands, drift between two periods, greedy centroid matching with deterministic ties.

- **Assignment memory**: the nightly assignment computes one distance per centroid instead of an `arrayMap` over all centroids. On 20,000 intents and 200 topics in local ClickHouse, the old query ran out of memory above 3 GiB, and the new one peaks at about 70 MiB.
- The Temporal activities call new run functions in the mcp_analytics facade. `tach.toml` declares the dependency on error_tracking's embedding tables.

After the second review round, refits record their own time, re-project surviving topics onto the new basis, keep summaries the labeler skips, and read and write topics through the project team for child environments. Batch queries run on the offline workload.

After the first review: the sync resumes from the last successful window, reads intents in pages, and confirms each synchronous embedding insert before completing its writer registration; run ids are unique per attempt; the fit is written in one transaction; each workflow kind has a timeout that outlasts its retries; the activities run on the database thread pool.

Why: this is the data the dashboard card, the per-tool "How this tool is used" section, the intent map and the MCP query tools in the next layers read from.

**Source correctness:** assignments and refit weights use fresh text, counts, and minimum event time from the same retention-aware events query. Cached embeddings supply only vectors. Bounded source pages cross to the main cluster as typed external tables, so events and embeddings can live on separate clusters.

**Embedding retention:** sync requests carry the earliest contributing event time in both the document timestamp and source metadata. Raw, lazy, and model-specific embedding reads enforce that provenance and the project retention floor, including when columns are renamed. Other embedding products keep their existing behavior. Readers denied `$mcp_intent` also cannot read or count its embedding rows; existing column masks remain in place.

**Writer admission:** runs register under a durable project lock before reading sources. Freezing the project prevents new registrations across its environments. New sync runs explicitly confirm joined inference tasks and synchronous inserts before completing registration. Failed or interrupted runs and legacy Kafka runs remain pending. This is the admission primitive only: legacy producers, queued output, physical erasure, and reopening still need coordinated implementation.

**Controlled embedding writes:** inference uses at most eight requests concurrently and 32 rows per insert, on the offline workload. A scheduling budget preserves the next resume point when an hour is incomplete. Socket timeouts are not total deadlines; timed-out writers remain pending. Production quorum acknowledgments do not prove every replica is ready for erasure.

<details>
<summary>Embedding completion boundary</summary>

Before:
```mermaid
flowchart LR
  Run[Sync run] --> Input[Kafka input]
  Input --> Worker[Embedding worker]
  Worker --> Output[Kafka output]
  Output --> Store[Embedding tables]
  classDef phBlue fill:#1d4aff,stroke:#1d4aff,color:#fff;
  classDef phGray fill:#e5e7eb,stroke:#c7ccd1,color:#000;
  class Run,Worker phBlue;
  class Input,Output,Store phGray;
```

After:
```mermaid
flowchart LR
  Run[Registered sync run] --> Worker[Ad-hoc inference]
  Worker --> Join[Join requests]
  Join --> Store[Synchronous main-cluster insert]
  Store --> Complete[Confirm registration]
  classDef phBlue fill:#1d4aff,stroke:#1d4aff,color:#fff;
  classDef phGray fill:#e5e7eb,stroke:#c7ccd1,color:#000;
  class Run,Worker,Join,Complete phBlue;
  class Store phGray;
```

</details>

The earlier day-sliced assignment benchmark in https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/pull/120769 does not measure this query shape. Whole-window source pages replace day slices to avoid losing counts for intents used on several days. Production-scale performance remains unmeasured.

Before the source repair:
```mermaid
flowchart LR
  Cache[Cached vector, text and count] --> Jobs[Assignment and refit]
  classDef phGray fill:#e5e7eb,stroke:#c7ccd1,color:#000;
  classDef phBlue fill:#1d4aff,stroke:#1d4aff,color:#fff;
  class Cache phGray;
  class Jobs phBlue;
```

After the source repair:
```mermaid
flowchart LR
  Events[Retained events] --> Pages[Whole-window source pages]
  Pages --> Join[Main-cluster vector join]
  Cache[Cached vectors] --> Join
  Join --> Jobs[Assignment and refit]
  classDef phGray fill:#e5e7eb,stroke:#c7ccd1,color:#000;
  classDef phBlue fill:#1d4aff,stroke:#1d4aff,color:#fff;
  class Events,Cache phGray;
  class Pages,Join,Jobs phBlue;
```

## Problem

The activity summary tick (#120746) runs on the self-driving Temporal worker. That worker has no LLM gateway settings, so every summary fails with `GatewayNotConfiguredError` and no summaries are written.

- `build_openai_client` uses the Go AI gateway when `AI_GATEWAY_URL` and `AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY` are set.
- Otherwise it falls back to the Python gateway (`LLM_GATEWAY_URL` and `LLM_GATEWAY_API_KEY`).
- The self-driving worker sets neither pair.

#121011 makes the tick stop early with `gateway_not_configured` instead of failing every pair. It does not make summaries work.

## Fix

Give the self-driving worker the Go AI gateway settings, the same way the general-purpose Temporal worker has them. This is a deployment config change, outside this repository:

- `AI_GATEWAY_URL` in the worker's env for each region, with the `/v1` base path.
- `AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY` from the worker's app secret store, with a gateway key created for this worker.

Use the Go gateway, not the Python one: the Python gateway takes no new callers.

## Verification

- After deploy, the next `activity summary tick` event shows `status_ok` above zero, and `activity summary generated` events appear with token counts.
- `$ai_generation` events with `ai_product=activity_summary` appear.
- `UserActivitySummary` rows have `status=ok` and a `summary_text`.

## Problem

- Saving an LLM judge with a model the team's API key can't use succeeds. The evaluation only errors on its first run, which can be hours later, and the team learns about it by email.
- The API and MCP accept any model string, so this happens even though the UI picker only offers listed models.

## Changes

- After a judge is saved with a new model, a background task sends one tiny test call to that model with the key.
- When the provider says the model doesn't exist, the key lacks access, or the model is unsupported, the evaluation moves to the error state with the same status the run would set.
- The user sees that status on the evaluation within seconds of saving.
- Any other failure, an outage included, leaves the evaluation running.
- The save request never calls the provider, so it can't slow down or block a save.
- It skips unchanged models, decision models and judges with no usable key, and ignores a result for a model that changed while the check ran.

The provider's model list can't do this job. It mixes curated defaults with discovered models, drops fine-tunes, can't list Foundry deployments and falls back to defaults on errors.

## How did you test this code?

**Test rationale:** the task test covers each outcome of the test call (works, not found, unsupported, no access, provider down) and a model changed mid-check. The API test checks that a new model starts the check and an unchanged one doesn't.

Not run: the task against a real provider key.

## Problem

The inbox orders reports the same way for everyone who sees the same set. `view=for_you` selects the reports routed to, claimed by or waiting on a person, and `sort=recommended` orders them by the ranking model's per-report score and priority. Nothing uses what the person is working on.

The per-user activity summary (`products/signals/backend/activity_summary/`) already describes that: themes, the objects they own and watch, and the products they work in. The `prioritizing-my-inbox` skill combines it with the model's predictions, but it runs client-side with several list calls and an LLM pass, so no product surface can use it.

This issue adds the backend builder only: one LLM call that ranks a person's candidate reports using their activity summary and the model's predictions, with a reason for every report. No API in this issue: the endpoint and MCP tool are #126250, and the skill change is #126251.

## Current code

- [`reports_for_person`](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/blob/master/products/signals/backend/briefing_reports.py) defines `for_you`.
- [`views.py`](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/blob/master/products/signals/backend/views.py) holds the list queryset, the `ranking_*` orderings and `sort=recommended` (`_inbox_ranker`, [`ranking/inbox_sort.py`](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/blob/master/products/signals/backend/ranking/inbox_sort.py)).
- [`serializers.py`](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/blob/master/products/signals/backend/serializers.py) already exposes `summary_lead`, `priority`, `ranking` (probability, lift and scored / stale / unscored per outcome), reviewers, claims, PR state and tags on list rows.
- [`facade/api.py`](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/blob/master/products/signals/backend/facade/api.py) `get_activity_summary` returns the caller's summary, or `None` when the team is not enrolled.
- [`activity_summary/summaries.py`](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/blob/master/products/signals/backend/activity_summary/summaries.py) calls the LLM through `build_openai_client`; [`activity_summary/config.py`](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/blob/master/products/signals/backend/activity_summary/config.py) reads limits from a flag payload and fails closed; [`run_activity_summary`](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/blob/master/products/signals/backend/management/commands/run_activity_summary.py) runs one pair by hand. Follow these patterns.

## Proposed behavior

New package `products/signals/backend/personal_ranking/`, entry point `build_personal_ranking(team, user, *, focus=None, dry_run=False)`.

### Candidates

Server-side pools, deduped by report id, capped (default 60):

- `for_you` in `sort=recommended` order, created in the window (default 14 days).
- `for_you` by `-updated_at`, no window, so older reports with new activity are included.
- Reports assigned to the person.
- Actionable reports by `-ranking_action`, and new reports by `-ranking_open`, in the window, when the person can see the ranking model. Skip these pools otherwise; do not fail.

Drop `resolved`, `suppressed` and `failed` reports. Record which pools each candidate came from.

### Prompt input

- The person: headline, profile (capped, default 1,500 characters), themes with mode, strength and last seen, the top names in `computed.owned` and `computed.watched`, products worked in. When there is no ready summary, run anyway on the candidates and the needs-you flags, and mark the result `personalized=false`.
- One compact block per candidate, labelled `c1` to `cN` (never the report UUID): priority, status and PR state, source or scout, created and updated age, title, `summary_lead`, open / action / fix probability and lift (or `unscored` / `stale`), needs-you flags (suggested reviewer, claimed by them, waiting on their input), tags.
- Optional `focus` text from the caller.

### LLM output (structured schema)

- `ranked`: one entry per candidate with `ref`, `rank` (integer), `tier` (`top`, `worth_a_look`, `later`), `reason` (short; names the theme or object that matched; never quotes the profile), optional `matched` (theme label and needs-you kinds, or null). `next_step` only for the top `limit` (default 25).
- `folded`: digest series and duplicate reports folded into one ref, with a reason. Folded refs get no rank.

Every candidate gets a reason, including low-ranked ones, so the stored output explains the whole order.

### Validation and fallback

- Order by the `rank` field, not array position. Renumber duplicate ranks or gaps by (rank, array position) and count them.
- Drop unknown refs. Append candidates the LLM did not rank after the ranked ones, in model order, with `ranked_by="model"`.
- Tier must not rise as rank falls; keep the rank and correct the tier.
- On an LLM error, a timeout (default 30 seconds) or output that fails the schema, return model order with `personalized=false` and a `fallback_reason`. Never raise to the caller.

### Storage and telemetry

- New model `PersonalInboxRanking` (inherit `TeamScopedRootMixin`): `team`, `user`, `created_at`, `input_hash`, `candidate_ids`, `result` (the full ranked list for every candidate, with reasons), `activity_summary_version`, `model`, `prompt_version`, input and output tokens, `cost_usd` (null when usage is missing), `latency_ms`, `status`, `fallback_reason`. One row per build; keep all rows for now.
- `input_hash` covers candidate ids with their status, PR state and score, the summary version, the prompt version and `focus`, so a later caller can tell whether a stored list is still current.
- Capture one `personal inbox ranking built` event per build with ids, counts, latency, tokens, cost, `personalized`, `fallback_reason` and renumber counts. No report text and no summary text in the event.

### Configuration

Read every tunable value from the payload of a new flag (proposed `personal-inbox-ranking`), failing closed like `activity_summary/config.py`: model, pool sizes and window, max candidates, `limit` default and max, reason length per tier, profile cap, timeout. A missing or invalid payload uses code defaults; a kill switch in the payload disables builds.

### Command

`python manage.py run_personal_inbox_ranking --team-id <id> --user-id <id> [--focus "..."] [--dry-run]` prints the ranked list. `--dry-run` writes no row and captures no event.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `build_personal_ranking` returns a ranked list covering every candidate, each with a rank, tier and reason, and stores one row.
- [ ] A person without a ready activity summary still gets a list, marked `personalized=false`.
- [ ] Ranking pools are skipped, not failed, for a person who cannot see the ranking model; EU teams (no scores) work.
- [ ] Pure-function tests cover validation: duplicate ranks, gaps, unknown refs, missing refs, tier order, folded refs, malformed output and timeout fallback.
- [ ] A prompt rendering test checks candidates are labelled `cN`, never by UUID, and that the profile cap holds.
- [ ] The command works with and without `--dry-run`.
- [ ] Mocked LLM calls only in tests; no real network.

## Scope

Backend builder, model, migration, config, event and command only. No endpoint, MCP tool, schedule, cache reuse or sort change; those follow in separate issues. Do not change `sort=recommended` or the ranking model.

## Problem

Evaluation users cannot select OpenAI's native decision models with an existing OpenAI key.
This extends the judge-method selector introduced in #115136.

## Changes

- **Decision model** now offers `gpt-6-luna` under a configured OpenAI key. Keys remain managed in AI provider settings.
- Boolean, categorical, and numerical evaluations use OpenAI's native predicate, choice, and score questions. N/A remains a separate applicability question.
- OpenAI single-selection categories require at least two options.
- Existing OpenAI evaluations keep chat behavior unless they explicitly select the decision method. Models supporting both methods retain their selected key when switching.
- Existing evaluations save only changed fields. Renaming and disabling still work when the flag is off. Re-enabling or changing configuration still validates access.
- Native decisions reuse result validation, full-precision numeric mapping, and terminal error handling. Temporary rate limits and overload responses honor `Retry-After`.
- Native requests use the shared DNS-pinned transport with a 60-second total deadline. Expired requests close their connections; transport failures and redirects retry.
- The adapter uses the installed SDK's public generic POST method, avoiding a repository-wide SDK upgrade. The endpoint remains fixed with redirects disabled.
- OpenAI's [Decisions guide](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/decisions) currently documents `gpt-6-luna`. Native support uses a separate capability declaration; OpenRouter discovery stays catalogue-driven.

OpenAI had no native decision option before this change. The new option and narrow layout:

<summary>Request routing before and after</summary>

Before:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    E[Evaluation] --> L[LLM with explanation] --> C[Chat APIs]
    E --> D[Decision model] --> R[OpenRouter or System One]
    classDef phYellow fill:#f9bd2b,stroke:#f9bd2b,color:#000;

```

After:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    E[Evaluation] --> L[LLM with explanation] --> C[Chat APIs]
    E --> D[Decision model] --> R[OpenRouter or System One]
    D --> O[Native OpenAI Decisions]
    classDef phYellow fill:#f9bd2b,stroke:#f9bd2b,color:#000;

    class C,R,O phRed;
```

## How did you test this code?

**Test rationale:** Native HTTP fixtures catch protocol and answer-identity errors that the existing System One parser tests cannot exercise. Runtime tests extend existing decision-result and rate-limit coverage to OpenAI, including a score just below its passing threshold. API tests cover capability gating and OpenAI's two-option minimum for single selection. Existing picker tests now cover OpenAI key preservation.
Slow-header and trickling-body cases verify the native request deadline and connection cleanup. The existing Temporal retry test covers a 503 with `Retry-After: 60`, preserving key validity.
Detail-save cases check sparse PATCHes, unchanged nested configuration, re-enable errors, and explicit model clearing. Serializer cases verify metadata updates after flag-off without database setup. A synthetic browser story exercises rename, disable, and rejected re-enable through the rendered detail form.

Local validation covers those backend suites, the evaluation and picker Jest suites, repository-wide mypy, frontend type checking, and strict preflight. OpenAPI generation produced no changes. Browser checks exercise method switching, model filtering, empty guidance, and a narrow pane using synthetic stories. No new event reads require a schema-matrix change.

Remaining uncovered adapter lines guard invalid internal questions, empty credentials, and malformed response containers. Native transport and output paths have direct tests.

Live calls with a valid OpenAI key remain untested. CI and patch coverage remain pending.

## Release status

- This change is behind a feature flag and is not available to users <!-- release-status: behind-feature-flag -->

Updated the existing [judge-inputs documentation](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/blob/feat/aio-openai-decisions/docs/internal/ai-observability-judge-inputs.md) with native OpenAI setup, output semantics, and error handling.

## Problem

- AEO checks at most 50 prompts a day, one call at a time, so a prompt set the size of the one we benchmark against (about 1,400 prompts) would take weeks to cover once.
- We want a week of daily data across the whole set on Claude and OpenAI.

## Changes

- A daily run now checks the whole prompt set, up to `AEO_MAX_PROMPTS_PER_RUN` (default 2,000).
- Prompts run in parallel, `AEO_RUN_CONCURRENCY` at a time (default 16). Engine calls run in worker threads; database writes stay on the calling thread, so workers never open Django connections.
- Each worker thread gets its own `requests.Session`, because sessions are not documented as thread-safe.
- One prompt raising an unexpected error is logged and skipped instead of ending the run.
- The Celery soft time limit goes from 4 to 10 hours. At 16 in parallel and about 70 seconds per call, 1,400 prompts on 2 engines takes about 3.5 hours.
- Runs log progress every 100 prompts.

> [!NOTE]
> Cost: measured at about $0.06 per OpenAI check and $0.14 per Claude check, so a full run of about 1,400 prompts is about $280 a day, billed to team 2. The run only affects teams in `AEO_CITATION_TEAM_IDS` with the `aeo-citation-tracking` flag on.

> [!WARNING]
> A deploy that restarts the long-running worker ends a run early. Rows are written per prompt and selection starts from the least recently checked prompts, so the next day's run resumes; nothing is lost, but that day's coverage is partial.

Not checked: gateway rate limits at 16 concurrent calls per engine. The first run's `aeo_citation_check_failed` logs will show any 429s.

## How did you test this code?

- `hogli test products/aeo/backend/test/` passes.
- **Test rationale:**
  - `test_run_records_checks_and_rotates_without_a_team_scope` now runs at concurrency 1 and 4. It catches the pool dropping or duplicating per-prompt writes.
  - New `test_one_prompt_crashing_does_not_end_the_run`. It catches an engine exception in one worker aborting a multi-hour run. No existing test covered engine exceptions in the runner.
- Not run: a production-size run.

## Release status

- This change is behind a feature flag and is not available to users <!-- release-status: behind-feature-flag -->

## Docs update

`products/aeo/README.md`: run size, concurrency and measured cost.

## 🤖 Agent context

**Autonomy:** Human-driven (agent-assisted)

**Agent:** Claude Code, Opus 5.5

- Skills invoked: `/writing-tests`, `/writing-code-comments`, `/writing-pr-descriptions`.
- Costs per check come from the gateway's `$ai_generation` events for the last four days of AEO runs.

## Problem

OpenAI Ads appends a click reference, `oppref`, to the landing page URL of an ad click (`https://example.com/?oppref=gAAAAAb123`). PostHog recognises every other network's click ID as a campaign property — `gclid`, `fbclid`, `msclkid`, `ttclid` and a dozen more — but not this one, so for anyone advertising in ChatGPT the parameter arrives as an ordinary custom property: no first-touch `$initial_oppref`, no taxonomy label, and nothing for the OpenAI Ads conversions destination to read.

The destination itself already documents the gap. Its `oppref` input tells people "PostHog does not capture it automatically, so send it as an event or person property yourself."

This is the server half of the change. The SDK half is [PostHog/posthog-js#5046](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog-js/pull/5046), which captures the parameter from the URL.

## Changes

Each service keeps its own copy of the campaign property list, so `oppref` is added to all of them:

- `nodejs/src/common/persons/person-property-utils.ts` — ingestion now writes `oppref` to `$set` and `$initial_oppref` to `$set_once`, which is what makes the destination's existing input default resolve without user setup.
- `posthog/taxonomy/taxonomy.py` — the campaign list plus a property definition ("OpenAI Ads Click ID"), so the property, its `$initial_` form and its latest-touch form are labelled in filters rather than showing as a raw string. The generated `frontend/src/taxonomy/core-filter-definitions-by-group.json` is rebuilt from it.
- `rust/personhog-common/src/properties.rs` — the event-to-person property allowlist.
- `rust/feature-flags/src/flags/flag_matching_utils.rs` — the event property to `$initial_` mapping used when evaluating flags, so first-touch targeting on OpenAI ad clicks works.
- `rust/property-defs-rs/src/api/v1/constants.rs` — the label alias mirror of the Django taxonomy, array size bumped to 245.

Deliberately out of scope, and not required for the destination to work:

- Session columns (`entry_oppref`, `entry_has_oppref`) and channel-type classification. Both live in the sessions tables and the position-based `entry_channel_type_properties` tuple, so they need a ClickHouse migration plus a decision on which channel an OpenAI ad click belongs to. That is web analytics work.
- `ignore_custom_properties` in `posthog/clickhouse/property_groups.py`. The other click IDs sit there to keep them out of the `custom` property group, but that list is baked into the column DDL, so moving `oppref` into it is a migration rather than a list edit. Until then it lands in the custom group, which is correct, just not optimised.
- The destination template's `oppref` description, which still says PostHog does not capture the value. It stays accurate until a posthog-js release carries the capture, so it is a follow-up rather than part of this diff.

Reference: [oppref on the OpenAI measurement pixel docs](https://developers.openai.com/ads/measurement-pixel) and [the conversions API docs](https://developers.openai.com/ads/conversions-api).

## How did you test this code?

No new tests: the change is six list entries, and each list is already covered by tests that assert the campaign-property behaviour as a whole (for example the `$initial_gclid` assertions in `flag_matching_utils.rs`). A test per list entry would assert the entry, not a behaviour.

What was actually run in the sandbox, which has no Django, Rust toolchain or Node modules for this repo:

- The taxonomy JSON was regenerated through the same `render()` path `bin/build-taxonomy-json.py` uses, so `hogli build:taxonomy-json --check` should be clean.
- The `PROPERTY_DEFINITION_ALIASES` literal was counted after the edit and holds 245 entries, matching the declared size.
- No Python, Rust or `nodejs` test suite was executed locally, and no manual testing was done. CI is the check for all three.

## Automatic notifications

- [ ] Publish to changelog?

## Docs update

The docs for the OpenAI Ads destination will want a note once both halves ship.

## 🤖 Agent context

**Autonomy:** Human-driven (agent-assisted)

**Agent:** PostHog Slack app, Claude Opus 5

- The work started as a scoping question about what supporting an OpenAI ad ID would involve. The split shipped here — capture, first-touch, labels, flag targeting — is the part that needs no migration; everything touching the sessions tables was handed to the web analytics team instead of bundled in.
- `oppref` is placed next to `sccid` in every list to keep the existing per-network ordering rather than sorting the lists.
- No repo skills were invoked. The CodeRabbit CLI is not available in this environment, so no local review pass ran.
- Nothing in this diff or description comes from a non-public source: the parameter name and semantics come from OpenAI's published ads docs and from the destination template already in this repository.

## Problem

A user who runs a playground prompt on an Azure OpenAI key gets an error on every run. Zeabur AI Hub and OpenAI-compatible keys fail the same way.

- The models endpoint labels each model with the provider's display name, for example "Azure OpenAI".
- The run logic lowercased that label into the request, sending `provider: "azure openai"`.
- The completion serializer only accepts enum values (`azure_openai`), so the request fails validation with a 400.
- Providers whose display name lowercases to the enum value (OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, OpenRouter, Fireworks, MiniMax) were unaffected. Together AI worked only because its missing display-name entry falls back to `.title()`, which round-trips to `together_ai`.

Closes #60297

## Changes

- The run logic now maps the display name through the existing `normalizeLLMProvider`, which handles every display form, so Azure OpenAI, Zeabur, and OpenAI-compatible keys can run prompts.
- A model with an unrecognized provider now shows "Pick a different model and try again" instead of sending a request that fails.

No visual changes; the fix removes an error state on Run.

## How did you test this code?

**Test rationale:** New jest case asserts the completion payload carries `provider: "azure_openai"` when the selected model option says "Azure OpenAI" - the exact regression (#60297), previously uncovered. It sits next to the existing payload test (`sends sampling settings in completion request payload`) and reuses its harness; it is not a parameterized row of it because the mocked model and the asserted field differ.

Ran `llmPlaygroundRunLogic.test.ts` (17 tests) in the worktree. Not run: a live completion against a real Azure key (none available); verification is by code reading plus the payload assertion.

## Release status

## Problem

- Teams sending conversions through the OpenAI Ads destination can only match users by click ID, email or external ID.
- [OpenAI's Conversions API](https://developers.openai.com/ads/conversions-api) also matches on hashed phone, first name and last name, and on raw city, region, postal code and country. The template sent none of them.
- A destination whose external ID mapping resolves to a number crashes on `trim()`. #116129 fixed this but did not merge.
- A user testing the destination asked for these identifiers in a support request.

## Changes

- New optional inputs: phone, first name and last name (hashed), and city, region, postal code and country (sent raw). Each defaults to the matching person property, so new destinations send them out of the box.
- A phone number hashes to the digits-only form OpenAI expects. The sample hash in OpenAI's docs is now a test case.
- A phone number without a `+` or `00` country prefix is left out, with a log line, instead of hashed into a value that cannot match.
- Names are lowercased, with all whitespace (including line breaks and Unicode spaces) and ASCII punctuation removed. Phones drop all whitespace too. Non-ASCII letters stay, as OpenAI requires.
- Location values that break OpenAI's format limits are left out: a city or region over 128 characters, an invalid postal code, or a country that is not two letters.
- An email, phone or name that is already a SHA-256 hash passes through. The external ID is always hashed, because a user ID can itself be a 64-character hex string.
- Every request sends `integration_source: 'posthog'`.
- Folds in #116129 (cherry-picked, authorship kept): numeric external IDs no longer crash, and its `update_hog_function_code` entry migrates existing destinations for that fix.

> [!NOTE]
> Location is on by default from GeoIP person properties, as in the Snapchat and TikTok templates. Reviewers may prefer it off by default.

Error responses still log the raw response body. OpenAI does not document its error shape, so the template does not parse it.

Existing destinations keep their saved code apart from the #116129 migration. Migrating them to the new identifiers is a separate follow-up.

## How did you test this code?

- Ran `openai.template.test.ts` locally with `HOG_BYTECODE_CACHE_REQUIRED=true`, as CI does.
- Ran `test_update_hog_function_code.py` locally, including `test_openai_ads_numeric_external_id_migration`.
- Not run: a live request to OpenAI's API.

**Test rationale:** The cases extend the existing identifier table and add a normalization table. Each catches a regression no existing test caught:
- Phone hashing drifting from OpenAI's published sample.
- Name normalization dropping non-ASCII letters, or keeping punctuation, line breaks or Unicode spaces.
- A phone with Unicode spaces being dropped.
- An out-of-limit location value failing the whole conversion.
- A hex-looking external ID passing through unhashed.

**CI report notes:**
- Trunk lane: this PR mixes the Node and backend Python lanes because it folds in #116129, whose template fix and migration belong together.

## Release status

- No feature flag controls this change <!-- release-status: no-feature-flag -->

None. No doc under `docs/` covers this destination.

## Problem

Every AI anomaly detector check (`llm` detector type) is a billable model call through the AI gateway. The judge already refuses to call the model when the organization is over its AI credit budget (`_is_over_ai_credit_budget` in `products/alerts/backend/judge/llm.py`), which pauses the check with the out-of-credits message.

There is no backstop at the gateway for this product:

- The gateway's per-product credit-bucket mapping does not list `alert_llm_detector` (or `alert_investigation_agent`), so the gateway does not enforce AI credits for these calls. If the in-app budget read is stale, or fails open, checks keep spending past the budget.
- If the gateway does refuse a call for credits (HTTP 402), the judge reports it as `LLMDetectorUnavailableError` ("could not reach the model"). The check errors with a misleading message instead of pausing with the out-of-credits message.

## Proposed change

- [ ] Gateway config (deployment values for the AI gateway in both regions): map `alert_llm_detector`, and probably `alert_investigation_agent`, to the AI credits bucket, like the other billable PostHog AI products.
- [ ] `products/alerts/backend/judge/llm.py`: catch the gateway's out-of-credit response (HTTP 402 from the Anthropic client, and from the OpenAI client if a second provider lands) before the generic `LLM_API_EXCEPTIONS` branch, and raise `LLMDetectorPausedError(LLM_DETECTOR_OUT_OF_CREDITS_MESSAGE)`. Paused checks leave the alert enabled, which matches the existing in-app budget path.
- [ ] Same treatment in the investigation agent if it shares the gap.
- [ ] Tests: a 402 from the client yields a paused check with the out-of-credits message, not an errored check.

## Acceptance

- An organization with no AI credits left gets paused AI detector checks with the out-of-credits message, whether the in-app check or the gateway catches it.
- No errored checks carry "could not reach the model" for a credit refusal.

## Problem

- The sandbox sender lets a team without a verified domain email its own members through one shared PostHog SES identity.
- Without a daily limit, one project could send unlimited mail through that identity, or one member could receive a flood of it.
- This PR caps sandbox sends per project and per recipient address each day. A send over either cap skips instead of going out.

<!-- merge-risk -->
> [!WARNING]
> 🟡 **Merge risk: medium** · two-way door (merge-risk rubric)
> - Only sandbox sends claim the caps; own-domain sends do not touch the new code. The caps fail closed: a Valkey error or an invalid cap setting skips every sandbox send.
> - With the switch on, the CDP API opens the SES Valkey pool for test sends. The pool is non-fatal with bounded waits, so an outage skips sandbox test sends instead of stopping the CDP API.
> - **Revert:** `git revert` the merge commit. Leftover bucket keys in Valkey expire on their own.
<!-- /merge-risk -->

## Changes

Right before delivery, every sandbox send, test sends included, claims two daily allowances at once:

| Allowance | Setting (default) | Charged |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Per project | `WORKFLOWS_SANDBOX_DAILY_TEAM_CAP` (25) | One token per recipient copy |
| Per recipient address, across the organization | `WORKFLOWS_SANDBOX_DAILY_RECIPIENT_CAP` (5) | One token per distinct address |

- A reached allowance skips the send with a run log line and a `workflows sandbox email blocked` event with reason `cap_reached`.
- Both allowances are token buckets that refill over 24 hours. One Valkey script claims both or neither.
- The worker gives the claim back when the member recheck after the claim skips the send, or when SES throttles before a retry. Returns are deduplicated and expire after five minutes.
- Recipient keys hash the lowercased address with SHA-256, so the keys hold no address.
- During a Valkey reconnect, an optional pool fails a command at once instead of queueing it. A failed MX cache read or write falls back to DNS and counts `cdp_email_mx_cache_errors_total`.

## Stack

1. #127149 member gate
2. #127150 sandbox route
3. #127151 daily caps ← this PR
4. #127152 sender row
5. #127153 Channels row

- The base is #127150. The three Node layers land first; the sender row and the Channels row build on them.
- A sixth layer, Silthus/posthog#628, opens after #127149 lands, because the stack-depth check allows five open layers.

## How did you test this code?

- **Live run** with the Node cdp-api at this head (`c64edd21351`) behind the public API on a box dev stack: provisioning twice returns one sender row; the first two member sends are delivered through the sandbox SES tenant, configuration set and From address, and the third is skipped by the recipient cap; `outside@example.com` is skipped with the member message; with the worker switch off the member send skips as unavailable. SES got exactly the two delivered sends. Stubs: a local SES endpoint that records each request, a DNS preload that answers an MX record for `example.com`, `workflows-sandbox-sender` answered true, PersonHog off (nothing on the send path reads persons).
- **Live stall run** at this head: a proxy in front of the CDP Redis stalls every blocked-event store call. Two bursts of 15 concurrent non-member sends and a member send all answer within 2.5 seconds, and the member send is still delivered. Exactly ten store calls stall; the other captures give up at their deadline, and no other Redis user waits.
- **Prod shape:** the caps apply only to the `sandbox` provider, which production does not have, so no production send claims a cap. The MX cache change alters only its error path.
- **Outage:** `fails a command at once while an optional pool reconnects instead of queueing it` runs against a real Valkey with the client's connection destroyed. `falls back to DNS and counts the failure when a Valkey command fails` covers the MX cache.
- **CI report:** the duplication warnings name files outside this stack, such as `products/warehouse_sources/`.
- **Review:** GPT-6.1 Sol reviewed the PR and the fixes in several final reads; each finding is fixed in a commit on this stack, and the `posthog[bot]` threads are answered.

**Test rationale:** the `daily caps` block drives real sends through `executeSendEmail` with a real Redis limiter. It catches a send over a cap going out, a repeated address charged twice, and a claim kept after the send skipped. `rate-limiter.service.test.ts` covers `claimAllOrNothing` and `returnClaim` replay and late-return guards, which no send-level test reaches.

## Release status

- This change is behind a feature flag and is not available to users <!-- release-status: behind-feature-flag -->

## Problem

Custom OpenAI-compatible providers introduced in #76553 can keep evaluations and playground requests open without a total deadline or response-size limit.

## Changes

- Custom completions use System One's bounded, DNS-pinned transport with a 60-second total deadline; validation and model listing use 10 seconds.
- Responses stop at 1 MiB, and compressed responses are rejected before decoding.
- Custom providers preserve Temporal cancellation, streaming, and structured-output fallback with SDK retries disabled.
- Online evaluations and taggers retry transient rate limits through Temporal without disabling evaluations or invalidating keys. Authentication and quota failures retain their existing behavior.
- OpenAI clients close after completion, failure, or early stream closure.
- Playground and MCP disconnects release stream slots without waiting for active synchronous reads. The reading worker closes the iterator afterward.
- Response-limit failures skip evaluations as rejected requests. The playground shows the limit or timeout and a next action.
- Mechanical changes share provider HTTP helpers and error handling. Azure clients retain their timeout and retry defaults.

> [!NOTE]
> These limits also apply to custom-provider playground requests. Structured-output fallback can make one additional bounded request.

<details>
<summary>Stream cleanup before and after</summary>

Before:
```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A[Playground disconnect] --> B[Generator finalization] --> C[Connection cleanup]
    classDef entry fill:#f9bd2b,stroke:#f9bd2b,color:#000;
    classDef path fill:#1d4aff,stroke:#1d4aff,color:#fff;
    class A entry;
    class B,C path;
```

After:
```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A[Playground disconnect] --> B[Mark iterator for closure] --> C[Release stream slot]
    B --> D[Worker finishes read and closes connection]
    classDef entry fill:#f9bd2b,stroke:#f9bd2b,color:#000;
    classDef path fill:#1d4aff,stroke:#1d4aff,color:#fff;
    class A entry;
    class B,C,D path;
```
</details>

Provider, transport, streaming, online evaluation, tagger, and shared-caller tests passed. Repository-wide mypy and CI preflight passed. **Test rationale:** Existing tests cover deadlines, response limits, cancellation, structured-output fallback, and disconnect cleanup. Judge and tagger cases now exercise real SDK responses: 429 then 200. Both regression cases failed before the retry fix. Adapter cases preserve authentication and quota errors. ## Problem

When the provider's content filter refuses a tagger or LLM-judge request, the run fails with an error-tracking exception. Customer trace content causes these refusals, so they are not a PostHog defect.

- The OpenAI SDK raises `ContentFilterFinishReasonError` on a `content_filter` finish reason. The shared provider did not map it.
- The fingerprint follows the call stack, so each caller (tagger, event judge, trace judge, OpenRouter path) files its own issue and fires the issue-created alert again.
- A retry sends the same input, so the filter refuses it again.

## Changes

- New `ContentFilteredError` in the shared LLM error taxonomy, with user-facing copy for streaming callers.
- The OpenAI adapter (and adapters built on it, such as OpenRouter) maps `ContentFilterFinishReasonError` to it on the structured-output path.
- Taggers: the refusal takes the existing `tagger_parse_error` skip. That type is already expected control flow, so it stays out of error tracking.
- LLM judges: a per-item skip with `skip_reason="content_filtered"`, and an `llma_eval_errors` metric so refusals stay observable.
- Backfills treat `content_filtered` as covered, like `context_window_exceeded`, because a re-run gets the same refusal. No query change was needed. A test case records the behavior.

## How did you test this code?

- Ran `test_openai_adapter.py` and `test_errors.py` locally. The new adapter test catches the unmapped SDK error.
- Ran `ruff` and `mypy` on the changed modules.
- Did not run the tagger, judge, or backfill tests locally, because they need Postgres and ClickHouse. CI runs them.
- Did no manual testing.

## Release status

- [x] No feature flag controls this change <!-- release-status: no-feature-flag -->
- [ ] This change is behind a feature flag and is not available to users <!-- release-status: behind-feature-flag -->
- [ ] This change makes a previously flagged feature available to everyone <!-- release-status: fully-available -->

## Automatic notifications

- [ ] Publish to changelog?

## Docs update

None.

## 🤖 Agent context

**Autonomy:** Human-driven (agent-assisted)

**Agent:** PostHog Slack app (Claude Code), Opus 5.5

- Raised in a [Slack thread](https://posthog.slack.com/archives/C0A006STKHR/p1790593665074799?thread_ts=1790593665.074799&cid=C0A006STKHR) about a new error tracking issue for this exception.
- A grouping rule now collects these exceptions in one issue. This PR stops them from being raised as exceptions.
- Duplicate search: no open PR handles content-filter refusals.
- No skills from the repo were invoked. The local CodeRabbit pass was skipped because this is a cloud task run.
- Public artifact: no session material is in the diff or the description.

## Problem

- Customers' warehouse syncs were turned off for errors that clear by themselves or that PostHog caused.
- A matched non-retryable error disables the schema. The schema stays off until a person turns it on again.
- A review of recent `schema non-retryable error` events found several of these classes: vendor outages, quotas that reset, a permission that our own code change started to need, and plan-gated tables that every source turns on by default.

## Changes

Affected schemas now stay enabled and show a "this sync tries again" message. Real credential and permission failures still disable the schema.

- **Cloudflare:** a token that can't read DNS analytics now syncs `dns_analytics_report` with zero rows, as the REST path did before the GraphQL move. Other GraphQL errors that hit every zone are retryable. A 401 on `kv_namespaces` and `d1_databases` skips that account, like a 403.
- **Snapchat Ads:** the run refreshes an expired access token. A 401 is retryable. A dead refresh token (`refresh_terminal`) still disables the schema with a reconnect message.
- **OpenAI Ads:** a 403 with body code `server_error` is retryable. Other 403 errors still disable the schema.
- **Linear:** `Linear app not configured` no longer disables the schema. The error means a worker has no Linear client credentials, which is a PostHog fault.
- **Postgres:** `connection timeout expired` and the Supavisor error `too many authentication failures` are retryable. A wrong password still disables the schema on the next run.
- **MySQL:** error 2003 disables the schema only for a refused port, no route, an unreachable network, or an unknown host. Timeouts and resets are retryable. Their message does not show the host.
- **Ahrefs and Snowflake:** quota errors are retryable, because the quota resets on a schedule.
- **Clerk:** `api_keys`, the organization tables and the SSO connection tables sync zero rows when the feature is off on the instance. This uses the existing `gated_feature` skip.
- **Meta Ads:** the free-text `action_attribution_windows` setting is changed to values that Meta accepts. An invalid value no longer fails every Insights request.

The Snapchat token refresh during the run has the most risk. It uses the same pattern as the Pinterest, LinkedIn and YouTube sources. All other changes affect only how errors are classified and which message the user sees.

## How did you test this code?

**Test rationale:** each source's tests now check the new classification. A transient error must not be in the non-retryable map, must be retryable, and must get the retry message. A real auth or permission error must still disable the schema. The Snapchat tests cover the refresh and the dead refresh token. The Clerk tests cover the skip, and negative cases for unrelated 4xx errors. The Meta tests cover the normalization and the dropped values.

- Tests ran for every changed source and for `sources/tests/test_source_error_contract.py`.
- Not run: tests that need a live Postgres database (the Postgres metadata probes and the Clerk webhook templates). The sandbox has no database.
- `clerk/tests/test_clerk.py::TestClerkFilteredEndpoints::test_endpoint_is_filtered_by_its_parent` fails in the sandbox on clean master too, so this change does not cause it.
- This change does not turn on again the schemas that are already disabled.

## Release status

- No feature flag controls this change <!-- release-status: no-feature-flag -->

## Docs update

None.

## Follow-ups not in this PR

- SSH gateway timeouts still disable the schema. The fix belongs in the shared SSH tunnel message or in `Any_Source_Errors`.
- Turn on again the schemas that these error classes disabled.
- Consider a disable only after several consecutive failed runs, so that one short vendor outage cannot stop a sync permanently.

This is a MVP for an activity-summary thing i am exploring

## Problem

- The inbox ranking work needs a per-person activity summary and its vector, and has neither today.
- `activity_summary_inputs` ([#119884](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/pull/119884)) renders one input per (project, member) for the internal cohort, but nothing reads it.
- Nobody can yet rate whether the summaries are right, or test a person vector in ranking.

Closes #119919

<!-- posthog-self-driving-origin:01a1563d-cd88-77db-b645-1119eec49c67 -->
## Origin

- Issues: [#119919](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/issues/119919)
- First signal: 2026-10-19
- Inbox report: [open](https://us.posthog.com/project/2/inbox/reports/01a1563d-cd88-77db-b645-1119eec49c67?link_source=github_pr)
- Likely cause: [`e7f90dfb`](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/commit/e7f90dfb3d7bc1d35a31d06d535e672714b9675f)
- Task started by: a person, from the inbox
<!-- /posthog-self-driving-origin:01a1563d-cd88-77db-b645-1119eec49c67 -->

## Changes

- Two new assets run after the inputs asset, on the same daily partition. The weekly schedule stays stopped, so a person runs them by hand.
- `activity_summaries` writes one LLM summary per inputs row to `activity_summaries/v1/dt=D/`.
  - The call goes through `build_openai_client("signals", ai_product="activity_summary", ...)`, so the deployment picks the Go or Python gateway with no code change.
  - The prompt lives in `prompt.py` behind `PROMPT_VERSION`. The model gets only the rendered input and the pair's previous summary.
  - The previous summary is the pair's successful row in the newest earlier partition, within 60 days. Only earlier partitions are read, so a re-run sees the same input.
  - Normalization follows the issue: word cap, at most 6 focus areas, unknown strength becomes `low`, and a `"None"` `recent_shift` becomes null.
  - A malformed answer is retried once, then written with `status = failed`. When every row fails, the asset fails and leaves the partition alone.
  - Run config: `model` (default `gpt-6-luna`), `use_previous_summary`, two token prices for `cost_usd`, `max_concurrency` (8), `capture_summary_text`.
- Each row captures an `activity summary generated` event into the dogfood project, with counts and drop counts only. Free text needs `capture_summary_text`.
- `activity_summary_embeddings` copies each successful summary's `text-embedding-3-small` vector to `activity_summary_embeddings/v1/dt=D/`.
  - It emits through `emit_embedding_request` with `timestamp` pinned to the partition day, so a re-run replaces its own row.
  - It emits only when `document_embeddings` has no vector of the current text, waits up to 10 minutes, and records `missing_vectors`.
  - A re-run that would write fewer rows than the partition holds is refused. Past the source table's 3-month TTL, lost vectors cannot come back.
- Mechanical: registration in `posthog/dags/locations/signals.py`, a `distinct_id` parameter on `capture_training_events`, the `ci-dagster.yml` path filter for `posthog/api/embedding_worker.py`, and the README section.

> [!NOTE]
> The embedding wait runs inside the asset, so a materialization can take up to `wait_seconds` longer than the LLM step. The job's 60-minute cap leaves room for it.

## How did you test this code?

**Test rationale:** the new cases in `test_activity_summary.py` sit next to the inputs tests and stay at the pure-function level where they can.

- Prompt rendering with and without a previous summary.
- Every normalization rule, malformed answers, `summary_text` determinism, and cost math.
- The retry: one malformed answer retried, two fail the row, a request error fails it without a retry.
- Events carry no free text unless `capture_summary_text` is set.
- Two asset runs against an in-memory S3, with the LLM, Kafka and ClickHouse boundaries mocked:
  - the summaries asset reads only earlier partitions, skips failed previous rows, is idempotent on re-run, and survives a failing capture client;
  - an all-failed run leaves the partition alone;
  - the embeddings asset re-emits only stale or missing vectors, skips failed summaries, and refuses to shrink a written partition.

Not run: a real materialization against the gateway, the embedding worker and ClickHouse, because this sandbox has no running stack. `check-dagster-paths.py`, `hogli lint:workflows` and repo-wide mypy ran locally.

## Release status

- No feature flag controls this change <!-- release-status: no-feature-flag -->

## Docs update

The activity summary section of `products/signals/dags/inbox_ranking/README.md` covers both assets.

## 🤖 Agent context

**Autonomy:** Fully autonomous

**Agent:** PostHog Desktop (Claude Code), claude-opus-5-5

- Started from an inbox report about issue #119919, and followed the issue's spec and the `inbox_ranking` AGENTS.md.
- Skills invoked: `/writing-tests`, `/authoring-ci-workflows`, `/writing-pr-descriptions`.
- Duplicate check: no open PR covers these assets.
- No session material beyond the public issue reaches the code. The test fixtures are invented.

---

## Problem

- Every ReviewHog Flash session pays full price for its first request, even though the main session and the lens sessions of a review send nearly the same 25–50k tokens.
- On gpt-5.6 and later, OpenAI caches only up to the end of the latest message. The rubric (core or lens) came first in the prompt, so no two sessions shared a prefix.
- Codex cannot send OpenAI's explicit `prompt_cache_breakpoint`, and it uses a per-session `prompt_cache_key`. PostHog/ai-gateway#534 adds the breakpoint at a marker line and drops the key.

## Changes

- No change in what a PR author sees: same findings format, same review content.
- The Flash prompt now starts with what every session of a lens part shares: the task, the PR, the diff, earlier findings.
- Then the `<!-- posthog:prompt-cache-breakpoint -->` line, then the session's own guidelines (`core.md` or a lens file), then the finding format.
- The guidelines move from the system prompt slot into `prompt.jinja`, so the executor now skips an empty system prompt instead of joining it with blank lines.
- Without the gateway change, the marker is an inert HTML comment.
- A copy of the marker in PR text (title, description, file names, diff, earlier findings) becomes a quoted form, so the prompt holds exactly one marker, right before the real guidelines.
- Multi-part PRs share less: the two lenses of one part share their prefix, but the main session sees the whole diff and differs.
- The prompt change moves the turn fingerprint, so before and after split cleanly by fingerprint. No version bump, per the rule in `constants.py`.

## How did you test this code?

- Ran locally: `reviewer/tests/test_single_agent_review.py`, `reviewer/tests/test_executor.py`, `tests/test_prompt_injection_guards.py`, `tests/test_review_activity.py`, `tests/test_fingerprint.py`, and the lens prompt test in `tests/test_persistence.py`.
- Rendered a lens prompt and checked the section order: task, PR, diff, marker, guidelines, output format.
- Not checked: cache hits in a real sandbox. That needs ai-gateway#534 deployed. Codex's own prefix (instructions, tools, `AGENTS.md`) must also be byte-identical across sessions, which only production traffic shows.

**Test rationale:** `test_pull_request_text_cannot_add_a_second_cache_marker` fails if PR text can place a marker of its own and pose as the guidelines. `test_main_and_lens_prompts_share_everything_before_the_cache_marker` fails if session-specific text moves above the marker, which would silently bring back the uncached prefix. The closest existing test, `test_diff_shows_only_what_fits_and_marks_the_rest`, checks diff content, not order. Existing tests pass the new `guidelines` argument.

## Release status

- No feature flag controls this change <!-- release-status: no-feature-flag -->

## Docs update

None.

## 🤖 Agent context

**Autonomy:** Human-driven (agent-assisted)

**Agent:** Claude Code, Claude Opus 5.5

- Came out of a cost check on Flash v2. The first request of every session showed zero cache hits. A direct API probe on gpt-6.1-sol showed an explicit breakpoint takes the second and third session from 0% to about 96% cached, and that a per-session cache key cancels it.
- The guidelines moved below the PR context rather than Codex learning a new field. Codex has no way to send the breakpoint (openai/codex#35300), so the gateway does it.
- Kept separate from the coordinator rollout (#115213), so that rollout's cost comparison stays clean.
- Skills: /writing-tests, /writing-pr-descriptions. CodeRabbit CLI pass skipped.

## Problem

The 2d heatmap for SQL insights (requested in #45073, shipped in #45710) plots a numeric value across two categorical columns, but nothing in the demo data shows it off. The SpikeGPT scenario emits `$ai_generation` events from a single hardcoded provider with no task dimension and creates no dashboards, so there is no out-of-the-box example of the provider/task latency comparison the original request describes.

## Changes

- The SpikeGPT simulator now routes each assistant reply through a weighted-random provider (openai, anthropic, google) and emits four generation types (`moderate`, `chat`, `memorize`, `summarize`) with `$ai_span_name` set, using per provider-and-task latency profiles. The shape is intentional: google is fast across the board while anthropic is deliberately slow at summarize, so the heatmap has an obvious hot cell.
- `generate_demo_data --product spikegpt` now creates an "LLM performance" dashboard, set as the project home, with two SQL insights rendered as 2d heatmaps (average latency and total cost by provider and task) plus a generations-by-provider trend.
- `LLM_COSTS_BY_MODEL` gains claude-sonnet-4, claude-3-5-haiku and gemini-2.0-flash entries so the simulator can price the new providers' generations.
- Fixes a pre-existing bug: the chat loop checked for role `human`, but `FAKE_CHATS` uses `user`, so user messages were emitted as bogus `$ai_generation` events and `sent chat message` was never captured.

## How did you test this code?

- New `products/demo/backend/test/test_spikegpt_matrix.py` with two tests. The first catches regressions no existing test covers: a model added to the provider config without a matching cost entry KeyErrors the whole simulation, and dropped provider/task/span properties would silently blank the demo heatmap. It also pins the role fix and that all 12 provider x task cells get data under the committed seed. The second pins the string coupling between each heatmap insight's SQL aliases and its `chartSettings.heatmap` columns, since drift there renders an empty tile with no error anywhere.
- Existing demo tests pass: `test_matrix_manager.py` and `test_hedgebox_matrix.py` (13 tests), covering the shared `SimServerClient` changes.
- `generate_demo_data --product spikegpt --dry-run --seed heatmapdemo --n-clusters 20 --days-past 14` runs clean (1,516 events simulated).
- Not done: a manual UI walkthrough of the rendered dashboard. The environment used for this PR had no full dev stack running the web app.

## Automatic notifications

- [ ] Publish to changelog?
- [ ] Alert Sales and Marketing teams?

## Docs update

No docs reference the demo scenarios; nothing to update.

## 🤖 Agent context

**Autonomy:** Human-driven (agent-assisted)

- Written with an AI coding agent in an interactive session; I directed the scope decisions.
- Main decision: the #45073 visualization itself already exists end-to-end (shipped in #45710), so this PR was scoped to demo data and a dashboard rather than a new chart type. The invented anthropic/google cost entries are demo fiction needed for the provider axis, flagged and explicitly approved during the session.
- Skills invoked: `/writing-tests` before authoring the new tests.

## Problem

- The refresh floor in #131814 refuses new and faster cadences, but views and endpoints already set faster keep running at their cadence. The rollout's last step holds them to the plan floor too.
- A plan downgrade has to reach those schedules without billing carrying a product-specific check.

## Changes

- An hourly task rewrites every saved cadence finer than the organization's plan floor to the floor, then reconciles that DAG. A pin stays.
- The rewrite is permanent. An upgrade or turning the flag off keeps the floor's cadence, and the person picks a faster one again in the picker.
- Each rewrite sends a `data modeling refresh clamped to plan floor` event with the previous cadence, so a wrong rewrite can be undone by hand.
- Managed views keep the cadence their provider declares.
- A reconcile that updates a tier now keeps it paused, so a rewrite never resumes a paused tier.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  subgraph Before
    B1[Billing sync]:::phYellow --> B2[Pending reconcile row]:::phGray --> B3[Celery retry chain]:::phBlue --> B4[Tier schedules]:::phRed
  end
  subgraph After
    A1[Hourly task]:::phYellow --> A2{{Saved cadence finer than plan floor?}}:::phBlue --> A3[Rewrite to floor, reconcile DAG]:::phBlue --> A4[Tier schedules]:::phRed
  end
  classDef phBlue fill:#1d4aff,stroke:#1d4aff,color:#fff;
  classDef phRed fill:#f54e00,stroke:#f54e00,color:#fff;
  classDef phYellow fill:#f9bd2b,stroke:#f9bd2b,color:#000;
  classDef phGray fill:#e5e7eb,stroke:#c7ccd1,color:#000;
```

- What to watch after release: [before and after dashboard](https://us.posthog.com/project/2/dashboard/2302274?tab=group-views) (PostHog staff only).

## How did you test this code?

**Test rationale:** one parameterized sweep test covers a cadence finer than the floor being rewritten with its pin kept, and three cases left alone: at the floor, flag off, and a managed view. Removing the managed-view filter fails it. The tier update test now asserts that a paused tier stays paused.

- Not checked: end-to-end dev-stack behavior, live Temporal writes, and the periodic task entry.

## Release status

- This change is behind a feature flag and is not available to users <!-- release-status: behind-feature-flag -->

## Docs update

- The data warehouse engineering guide describes the hourly rewrite, its event and that it is permanent.

## 🤖 Agent context

**Autonomy:** Human-driven (agent-assisted)

**Agent:** Claude Code, Claude Opus 5.5; earlier package-aware targeting, since replaced: OpenAI Codex, GPT-6

**Skills:** `/stacking-prs`, `/writing-tests`, `/writing-code-comments`, `/writing-user-facing-copy`, `/improving-drf-endpoints`, `/writing-dataclasses`, `/writing-pr-descriptions`, `/django-migrations`, `/running-ci-preflight`, `/verifying-changes`

<details>
<summary>More context for AI agents</summary>

- **Decisions:** rewriting the saved cadence replaces the earlier scheduler-side clamp. One cadence per view removes the `clamp_existing` payload, the effective-cadence API field, the endpoint serving window and the restore-on-upgrade path. The cost is that a rewrite cannot be undone automatically.
- **Decisions:** a periodic data modeling task replaces the billing hook and the pending reconcile table, after review.
- **Known limit:** the endpoint version cap from #131814 still applies until the task rewrites the older versions.

</details>
