### Bug Description

When using `PostHogTraceExporter` from `@posthog/ai/otel` with the Vercel AI SDK, **all custom metadata** set in `experimental_telemetry` is silently dropped by PostHog's `/i/v0/ai/otel` endpoint. This includes:

- **`posthog_distinct_id`** — events get random anonymous UUIDs instead of the provided user ID
- **`functionId`** — not available as a searchable property on the resulting events
- **Custom metadata** (`org_id`, `country_code`, etc.) — absent from event properties

Searching for "distinct" in the `$ai_generation` event properties returns **no results**. The metadata isn't just ignored for attribution — it seems dropped entirely.

The `@posthog/ai` OpenAI wrapper path (which uses `posthog-node` directly with `posthogDistinctId` and `posthogProperties`) works correctly for all of these. The issue is specific to the OTel path.

**Additional note:** The [session replay linking docs](https://posthog.com/docs/llm-analytics/link-session-replay) only show examples using the OpenAI SDK wrapper path (`posthogProperties: { $session_id }`). There's no guidance for the OTel path, and passing `$session_id` in metadata would be dropped too.

## How to reproduce

1. Set up `PostHogTraceExporter` in `instrumentation.ts` per [the docs](https://posthog.com/docs/llm-analytics/installation/vercel-ai):

```ts
import { PostHogTraceExporter } from "@posthog/ai/otel";
import { NodeSDK } from "@opentelemetry/sdk-node";
import { resourceFromAttributes } from "@opentelemetry/resources";

const sdk = new NodeSDK({
  resource: resourceFromAttributes({ "service.name": "my-app" }),
  traceExporter: new PostHogTraceExporter({
    apiKey: process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_POSTHOG_KEY,
    host: "https://us.i.posthog.com",
  }),
});
sdk.start();
```

2. Call streamText or generateText with functionId and metadata:

```ts
const result = await streamText({
  model: openai("gpt-4.1"),
  prompt: "Hello",
  experimental_telemetry: {
    isEnabled: true,
    functionId: "ai-chat",
    metadata: {
      posthog_distinct_id: "my-user-id-123",
      org_id: "org-456",
      country_code: "FR",
    },
  },
});
```

3. Check the resulting $ai_generation event properties in PostHog:
4. 
- posthog_distinct_id is absent, event is attributed to an anonymous UUID
- functionId / feature name is not available as a property
- org_id, country_code are absent


Additional context

- @posthog/ai v7.12.2 (latest)
- ai (Vercel AI SDK) v4.x
- @opentelemetry/sdk-node / @opentelemetry/resources
- Next.js with instrumentation.ts
- PostHog Cloud (US region)

### Debug info

```shell
- [x] PostHog Cloud, Debug information: Session: https://us.posthog.com/project/sTMFPsFhdP1Ssg/replay/019d2a86-447d-7771-af1b-d38dd41f95d7?t=4912
```

hits.body:
## Problem

The AI anomaly detector (`llm` detector type) is pinned to one model, `claude-haiku-5-5` (`LLM_DETECTOR_MODEL` in `products/alerts/backend/judge/llm.py`). We want to know whether another cheap model, starting with `gpt-6-luna`, judges series as well, costs less or more per check, and is faster. Today we can't compare without changing what users see.

A live split (each check or each alert picks a model at random) is the wrong tool:

- Per check, an alert's verdict would flip between models, so notifications flap, and the earlier flags each model is shown would mix both models.
- Per alert, we would be comparing different metrics, so fire rates are confounded.

We need paired comparisons: both models judging the identical input.

Longer term we may let users pick the model per alert (for example a frontier model for a high-stakes metric). We'll wait to see what users ask for before exposing that, but the provider work here should make it a small follow-up rather than another refactor.

## Proposed change

Add an opt-in **shadow** call. The primary model still decides the check. On a sampled share of checks, a second model judges the same input and its verdict is recorded, never acted on.

- [ ] **Model registry instead of one hard-coded model.** The judge is Anthropic-only today: `build_ai_gateway_anthropic_client`, `messages.parse(output_format=LLMDetectionVerdict)` with `thinking` disabled, and `prompt.py` sends the chart as an Anthropic base64 `image` block. Replace the single `LLM_DETECTOR_MODEL` constant with a small registry of supported models, keyed by a stable name. Each entry carries the provider, the model id, the gateway client builder, how the chart image is encoded, how structured output is requested and parsed into `LLMDetectionVerdict`, and any provider quirks (for example Haiku rejecting non-default sampling params). Register `claude-haiku-5-5` (Anthropic, the default) and `gpt-6-luna` (OpenAI via `build_ai_gateway_openai_client`, already used elsewhere in the repo, chart as an image data URL). Same `SYSTEM_PROMPT` and `PROMPT_REVISION` for both. Keep the `ai_product` as `alert_llm_detector`.
- [ ] **One entry point that takes a model name.** The judge's model call takes the registry name, defaulting to Haiku, so the primary model, the shadow model and a future per-alert choice all go through the same code. Do not add a user-facing model field yet; a later per-alert `model` on the `llm` detector config would only need validation against the registry plus UI and MCP schema work.
- [ ] **Controls in the `alerts-llm-detector` flag payload**, so no deploy is needed to start, stop or resize: `shadow_model` (for example `"gpt-6-luna"`), `shadow_rate` (0 to 1), and an allowlist of team ids the shadow runs for. Missing keys mean no shadow. Read it the same way as `max_llm_alerts_per_team`.
- [ ] **Shadow call semantics.** After the primary verdict, on a sampled scheduled check from an allowlisted team, call the shadow model with the same series, chart, instructions and earlier flags. The shadow must never change the check state, notifications, the verdict memo or the earlier flags. Send `X-PostHog-Billable: false`, so the customer is not charged for it. A shadow failure is logged and swallowed. If no model-call slot is free, skip the shadow rather than delay the primary. Do not shadow simulate/preview calls.
- [ ] **Recording.**
  - On both `$ai_generation` events, add `llm_detector_role` (`primary` / `shadow`), `alert_id`, `alert_check_id`, and the parsed `is_anomaly` and `kind`.
  - On the check's `triggered_metadata`, add `model` (the primary model) and a small `shadow` object: model, `is_anomaly`, `kind`, rationale (truncated like the primary), latency in ms, error if any.
- [ ] Tests: the shadow never changes state or notifications; a shadow error leaves the check result untouched; with no payload keys there is no shadow call; the shadow call is non-billable.

## Acceptance

- With the payload set for an allowlisted team, about `shadow_rate` of that team's AI checks carry a `shadow` object, and each has two `$ai_generation` events linked by `alert_check_id`.
- Turning the payload keys off stops shadow calls within the flag cache refresh, with no deploy.
- Customer teams outside the allowlist see no change in behavior, latency or credits.

## Out of scope

- The comparison view and dashboard for the read-out (built in the internal data warehouse), and any decision to switch the primary model.
- A user-facing model picker. Things to settle before adding one: which models to offer, how cost differences show up (credits already scale with model cost, but the per-project cap counts alerts, not spend), and whether a pricier model needs its own cap.

## Problem

- Validation of raw warehouse SQL slows down sharply as nesting depth grows, even for queries it then rejects.

## Changes

- Raw direct queries nested more than 100 levels deep now fail fast with the existing "too complex to validate" error.
- Parentheses, brackets, braces and `CASE … END` count toward the depth.
- A closer with no matching opener never lowers the depth below zero.
- The check is one pass over the lexed tokens, before sqlparse grouping. 100 matches sqlparse's own `MAX_GROUPING_DEPTH`.
- Queries at normal depth see no change.

## How did you test this code?

**Test rationale:** two new tests accept depth 100 and reject deeper input or stray closers. All seven cases fail without the guard. `test_exposes_grouping_errors` mocks `group`, so it sends no real nested input.

- Not run: the wider backend suites.

## Problem

- Trace judges on agent runs answer N/A because they never see the task prompt ([thread](https://posthog.slack.com/archives/C087XQ7K9K7/p1795011878017719)).

- Every long message then keeps 1,000 characters, prompt included, with no sign on the result.

- Judges see repeated messages once, as `[1-17] Same as messages 1-17 of the previous generation's input above`. Only equal messages collapse.
- The trace budget rises to 300,000 characters, falling back to 150,000 when the judge's context window rejects it.
- Results from a cut transcript set `$ai_evaluation_input_truncated: true`.

## Problem

People who send workflow emails see the same preview text twice in Gmail when the email step's Preheader field and the editor's own preview text hold the same copy. Raised in the Slack thread linked below; no issue exists.

## Changes

- An email now shows its preview text once. The send step skips its Preheader span when a hidden element in the html already holds the same text.
- The match ignores case, whitespace and entity spelling. Hidden elements that hold other text or markup do not count, and visible text never counts.
- Mechanical: new `preheader.test.ts`. The size estimate in `ses-html-max-bytes.ts` still counts the span, so it stays an upper bound.
- Hardened per review: the scan is linear in the html size (no rescanning per hidden tag, comment, or unterminated body tag), ignores markup inside HTML comments and Outlook-only conditional branches, skips stylesheet/script contents, keeps offsets in the original string (`toLowerCase()` can change length), and only suppresses the span when the hidden copy precedes all other body text.

## How did you test this code?

Ran `preheader.test.ts`, `ses-html-max-bytes.test.ts` and `sandbox-message.test.ts`; all pass. Broke each guard in `preheader.ts` in turn and saw the matching test fail. Review-round cases were each verified red against the pre-fix code. `preheader-bench.serial.test.ts` pins linear scanning on three adversarial shapes (follows the `email-link-tracking-bench.serial.test.ts` pattern; the quadratic code took 20+ s where the fixed scan takes ~34 ms).

Not run: `email.service.test.ts`, which needs Postgres and Redis that this sandbox lacks.

## Problem

- The Stripe source's payment-method tables make one `/v1/customers/:id/payment_methods` call per customer on every sweep, and most of those calls return nothing. This uses up our users' Stripe read allowance and rate limits.
- Stripe added a gated, undocumented `Customer.has_payment_method` field so we can skip those calls. Context: https://posthog.slack.com/archives/C09J981UHNX/p1794581786066459?thread_ts=1782323971.706099&cid=C09J981UHNX

## Changes

- When the `warehouse-stripe-has-payment-method` flag is on, the `CustomerPaymentMethod` and `CustomerPaymentMethodHistory` sweeps request `expand[]=data.has_payment_method` on their customer listing and skip customers whose value is exactly `false`. `true` and missing values still get the call, so no payment method is dropped.
- When Stripe refuses the expand (an account without access, or access removed mid-sweep), the sweep lists customers again without it. The new listing continues after the last customer already handled. One refusal stops the expand for the rest of the sync.
- The field is never stored, because only the payment-method rows are written. The `Customer` table never requests it.
- The flag is checked only for those two tables, and only when they poll the API.

## How did you test this code?

- New `TestPaymentMethodSweepHasPaymentMethodExpand` cases drive the source through `SourceDriver` against a scripted Stripe API.
- Ran the full Stripe test directory locally, including the object-storage tests against a moto S3 server.
- Not checked against the real Stripe API, because no test account has access yet.

**Test rationale:** The cases catch: skipping a customer whose value is not `false` (data loss), failing the sync or losing customers when Stripe refuses the expand on the first or a later page, sending the expand with the flag off, swallowing unrelated 400s, and storing the field. The nearest tests (`test_balance_history_switch_decides_which_customers_are_swept`, `TestStripeNestedResourceGetRows`) cover the balance-transaction skip only. Each new case fails when the line it guards is broken.

## Release status

- This change is behind a feature flag and is not available to users <!-- release-status: behind-feature-flag -->

## Docs update

- None. The behavior is internal, and the synced data does not change.

**Autonomy:** Human-driven (agent-assisted)

**Agent:** Claude Code, Claude Opus 5.5 (claude-opus-5-5)

**Skills:** None invoked. The agent read the `writing-tests`, `writing-code-comments` and `routing-outbound-api-calls` skill files.

**Security review:** not needed

## Problem

- Web analytics doesn't count anyone for a cohort filter on `$feature_flag_called` when the organization keeps flag calls only in `flag_evaluations` (mode 2) and the cohort is calculated inline.
- Those queries run on the fast database, which turns off the flag-call union. #141524 fixed the same gap for conversion goals.

## Changes

- These cohort filters now count the flag calls in `flag_evaluations`.
- On a team whose flag calls are only in `flag_evaluations`, any cohort filter uses the full database when the query may inline a cohort.
- The check doesn't read cohort definitions. A definition can reference other cohorts that the resolver inlines later, and compiling one builds the full database anyway.
- Other teams, and queries with inline calculation off, keep the fast database.

## Problem

- The data modeling team cannot work out what a materialization run costs. The job row holds ClickHouse CPU and bytes read, and nothing about S3 requests, worker time or files written.
- The need comes from the session that directed this work. No issue is linked.

## Changes

- Nothing changes for users. The API and the Usage tab stay the same.
- The nightly usage collector also stores result bytes, S3 bytes read, and S3 GET and LIST counts per job. It reads them from the query log rows it already uses.
- The materialize, publish and Trino activities add their wall-clock time to `worker_seconds`. `attempts` is saved when an attempt starts.
- The materialize activity records the files that back the table, and the live files the run wrote, rewrites included. Publishing copies every table file, so the same numbers price the copy.
- The activity saves only the job fields it changed, so a stale job in memory cannot undo another attempt's writes.
- A failed write of any of these numbers is reported and never fails or retries the run.
- The migration adds ten nullable columns to `posthog_datamodelingjob`.
- Workflow command sequences do not change. Every write happens inside an activity.

## How did you test this code?

**Test rationale:** the new assertions catch a measure that reads the wrong archive column, worker time that is assigned instead of added, a wrong written-files baseline on a first run or a retry, a batch save that undoes another attempt's write, and a failed measurement that fails the run.

- Not run locally: the wider backend suite.
- Patch coverage: the uncovered lines are covered only by Temporal tests, which the report does not count, or are the two publish activities whose bodies only moved under the timer.
- Call assertions: the one added line reads what error tracking received. That is how the test shows that Postgres rejected the write, which the review asked for.

<details>
<summary>Tests and local runs</summary>

- `test_job_usage.py`: two existing cases extended. One runs the collector SQL against the real archive table, so a wrong column name or aggregate fails it. The other fails when a new measure is left out of the saved fields.
- `test_record_worker_time_adds_up_over_blocks_and_keeps_a_failed_one` (new in `test_utils.py`): no test covered this helper. It needs a job row, so it runs with the database and a patched module clock. It also reads `attempts` while the block runs.
- `test_record_worker_time_keeps_the_block_error_when_its_write_fails` (new, two cases): the block raises and its error comes out. One case makes Postgres reject the attempt number, the other fails the write after the block on a malformed job id.
- `test_the_job_records_the_files_a_run_wrote_and_the_table_it_left` (new in `test_materialize_view_incremental.py`): the existing cases assert table content, not job columns. It runs a rebuild, an update and a second attempt of that update against a real Delta table, and compares the job columns with the object sizes.
- `test_a_batch_save_keeps_what_an_overlapping_attempt_wrote_to_the_job` (new): another writer sets `attempts` between the job load and the batch save, and the value survives.
- `test_a_delta_log_that_cannot_be_measured_leaves_the_run_intact` (new): delta-rs fails to list files, the rows still land and the file columns stay null.
- `test_zero_row_materialization_writes_empty_parquet` (extended): the job counts the empty parquet that publishing copies.
- No test covers a failed save of the file counts, because it needs a mocked `save`.
- Each new assertion was seen failing with its guarded line broken, then passing with the line restored.
- Ran locally: `products/data_modeling/backend/temporal/tests`, the collector tests, the job API and usage API tests, `posthog/test/repo_invariants`, mypy on the changed files, ruff, `hogli lint:tach`, and the devex and security semgrep rules on the changed files.
- No new test files, so test ownership is unchanged.

</details>

## Problem

- Destinations and workflows of an organization that staff deactivated keep running.
- #140265 dropped disabling them by hand: background work checks the organization at run time instead ([thread](https://posthog.slack.com/archives/C0CJM5RT3PE/p1795444549806499), [#project-deactivated-org](https://posthog.slack.com/archives/C0CKH2SFYSG)).

<!-- merge-risk -->
> [!NOTE]
> 🔵 **Merge risk: low**, 🟡 once the switch is on
> - Nothing changes on deploy: the switch defaults off, and the queries stay as they are.
> - With the switch on, every deactivated organization stops sending, including ones deactivated earlier.
> - **Switch-off:** `CDP_SKIP_DEACTIVATED_ORGANIZATIONS`, default off.
> - **Tier:** non-critical

## Rollout

- **Stages:** deploy the Node CDP services, then turn the switch on per region.
- **Decided:** 2026-11-24, the driver moved transformations to #140972 for the ingestion team.
- **Decided:** 2026-11-23, the driver accepted that queued runs of a deactivated organization end as they do for a deleted destination or workflow (see Known issues).
- **Watch:** `cdp_deactivated_organization_not_loaded`.
<!-- /merge-risk -->

## Changes

- The CDP stops loading the destinations and workflows of a deactivated organization. Every path that loads them finds nothing: event triggers, queued runs, webhooks, batch runs and backfills.
- Queued runs end the way they do for a deleted destination or workflow.
- Transformations keep loading here. #140972, stacked on this PR, covers them for the ingestion team.
- Legacy plugin configs and legacy Zapier action webhooks of a deactivated organization stop too. A hidden migrated destination does not fall back to its plugin config.
- Test invocations and the function status route find nothing for a deactivated organization. A test run of an unsaved function or workflow answers 403, because members of a deactivated organization can still reach the API with their session.
- A flip of `is_active` takes effect when the managers' caches refresh: about 2 minutes for workflows, up to about 6 for destinations, and up to about 10 for legacy plugin configs. Reactivation restarts them the same way.

## How did you test this code?

**Test rationale:** the manager tests deactivate an organization in Postgres and check what loads, with the switch on and off, and again after reactivation. Webhook, backfill, legacy plugin and legacy webhook tests go through the production wiring. Each fails with its filter removed.

- CI report, call assertions: the two lines in the legacy consumer test read the batch handler from the Kafka mock, as its neighbouring tests do. All four added lines, there and in the API and backfill tests, assert no outbound fetch, which is the delivery boundary.
- Not checked: a live run on a dev stack.

## Problem

- Plain event projections keyed on `uuid` can fail an incremental run with `DuplicateUniqueKeyError`, and a retry fails the same way.
- The cause: `events` can return one stored event twice before parts merge.

Inbox: [step 1](https://us.posthog.com/project/2/inbox/reports/01a21014-0c68-7d35-8bb0-5fdf6fc5a9a8) of [this plan](https://us.posthog.com/project/2/inbox/reports/01a21010-3966-7e6f-bbb0-5c8efc8c93ae).

## Changes

- These models now keep the first row of each repeated uuid, so the run succeeds.
- Every other model still fails on a repeated key.
- The model must read only the built-in `events` table, with no join, linked field, `ARRAY JOIN`, `arrayJoin()` or aggregate.
- `UniqueKeyTracker` does the dedup, inside its existing memory budget and disk spill.

> [!NOTE]
> An earlier version of this PR rewrote the query into `GROUP BY uuid, timestamp`. Materialization never spills a `GROUP BY` to disk, so large models would run out of memory.

## How did you test this code?

**Test rationale:** Tracker cases cover repeats in memory and on disk. One activity test sends a repeated uuid through both write paths, and fails without the dedup.

- The incremental activity, tracker and eligibility tests passed on the devbox. Not run: the rest of the backend suite.

<details>
<summary>Measured cost per 1M uuid keys</summary>

| Check | In memory | Spilled to disk |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Plain check | 0.08 s | 3.7 s |
| Dropping repeats | 0.14 s | 7.6 s |

</details>

👉 _Stay up-to-date with [PostHog coding conventions](https://posthog.com/docs/contribute/coding-conventions) for a smoother review._

## Problem

- A cold dashboards v2 load spends most of each tile's time building the HogQL database, not in ClickHouse.
- Every target in one `query_batch` request rebuilt it from scratch, so teams with large data warehouses pay that cost once per tile.

## Changes

- Cold v2 boards build the HogQL database once per batch for targets that share its inputs, then share it.
- A batch-scoped registry in `posthog/hogql/database/request_scope.py` keys each build on team, user, access-control scope, normalized modifiers, connection and the other `create_for` inputs.
- Targets with different schema modifiers (new events engine, `personsOnEventsMode`, sessions version) or another user get their own database.
- One thread builds each key under a lock while the others wait. The registry dies with the batch, so no cross-request cache.
- Workers honour the existing `HOGQL_SHARED_INSIGHT_DATABASE_ENABLED` kill switch.
- Calls outside a batch scope are unchanged.

**Test rationale:** the batch test fails if `query_batch.py` stops entering the scope (3 builds instead of 1). ## Problem

- One team's large broadcast can spend the whole "Classify with AI" budget for the day.
- Step 1, part 2 of PostHog/fleet-profile-meikelmosby#8. Merge #139495 first.

<!-- merge-risk -->
> [!NOTE]
> 🔵 **Merge risk: low** · two-way door (merge-risk rubric)
> **Tier:** non-critical
> - A counting bug would skip classifications with a visible warning. Only flagged teams use the step.
> - **Revert:** revert the merge commit.

- Past 50,000 classifications a team-day (UTC), the step skips with a warning, and the run carries on.
- The hogflow worker counts each classification in Valkey before it routes it to the classify queue. Retries do not count.
- Past the cap, the run never joins the queue, so a skip spends none of the shared rate. The step's output is `{category: null, confidence: null, skipped: true}`, with a warning in the run log.
- The skip arrives as a successful answer, so the template does not change.
- `cdp_classify_daily_cap_skipped_total` counts the skips, and `cdp_classify_daily_cap_uncounted_total` counts steps let through unchecked.
- `CDP_CLASSIFY_TEAM_DAILY_CAP` sets the cap. A slow or failing Valkey lets the call through, since the queue's limiter still bounds the rate.

## Problem

- People who turn off a Replay Vision scanner still get scout reports and alerts for it, because its scouts keep running on their schedule.
- The scanner adds no new observations, so those scouts re-read unchanged data on the customer's bill. Raised in #team-self-driving ([Slack thread](https://posthog.slack.com/archives/C0ACRAMJUAG/p1794244243845939?thread_ts=1794244243.845939&cid=C0ACRAMJUAG)).

## Changes

- Disabling a scanner pauses all of its scouts. This covers the UI, the API, MCP, and PostHog AI, because all of them save through the scanner serializer.
- Deleting a scanner pauses its scouts too, so they do not run on with nothing to read.
- When the sweep turns off an unrunnable scanner, it now pauses all of its scouts, not only variant analysis scouts on experiment scanners.
- Re-enabling a scanner does not resume its scouts. The scanner cannot tell which scouts the person had paused on purpose. The scouts tab already shows paused scouts with a resume control.
- Mechanical: `pause_variant_analysis_scouts` becomes the general `pause_scanner_scouts(scanner, tag=...)` in `scout_source.py`.

## How did you test this code?

**Test rationale:** the new parameterized case in `test_scanner_scouts_api.py` fails if a disable or delete leaves the scanner's scouts on, or pauses another scanner's scouts. The closest existing test only covers the tag-scoped variant analysis pause. `test_sweep.py` patches move to the new helper.

Ran `test_scanner_scouts_api.py`, `test_sweep.py`, the enable/disable/delete cases in `test_api.py`, and `hogli lint:tach` locally. No manual UI check was done.

## Release status

- No feature flag controls this change <!-- release-status: no-feature-flag -->

- None.

## Problem

- A planned suggestion to materialize Endpoints needs each endpoint's run timing and ClickHouse cost per run. #139663 adds the `endpoint_runs_hourly` table, but nothing fills it.

## Changes

- A daily Dagster job fills the table from endpoint logs joined to the query log, publishing each UTC day by partition swap.
- A day without runs succeeds, so a broken endpoint log pipeline shows as missing rows, not a failed run.
- Request dimensions and ClickHouse cost are empty for days before #139519 deploys. Older log lines lack the tokens and older queries lack the tag.
- Mechanical: shared publish, schedule and alert helpers now serve both rollups, with the old job's names and messages unchanged.

## How did you test this code?

- New tests run the job on real ClickHouse; each failed with its guarded line broken.
- `test_warehouse_object_reads_daily.py` is unedited and passes.
- Not run: the job on a deployed cluster.

**Test rationale:** the job is new, so no existing test covered it.

<details>
<summary>Regressions the new tests catch</summary>

- A cache hit counts as a run with no ClickHouse cost, and stays out of the per-run cost quantiles.
- Two queries with one execution id count as one run with summed cost.
- A run logged just after midnight joins a query that finished just before it.
- A failed line counts as failed by its prefix, whatever the case of its level.
- A line from before #139519 rolls up with empty request dimensions.
- An `invalid request` line whose free text contains `path=inline` is skipped.
- A redelivered log line counts once.
- Runs in slots 0 and 11 of an hour set exactly those two bits.
- A rerun replaces the day. Empty staging keeps the published day, and fails only when the logs hold runs.
- A day past the query log is refused.
- The endpoint job leaves the logs cluster out of its query log read, and the warehouse reads job keeps it.
- The new test file is owned by `team-data-modeling` through `posthog/dags/owners.yaml`.

</details>

## Problem

- People and agents who write SQL sometimes search the whole `properties` column for text, such as `toString(properties) ILIKE '%pricing%'`.
- The native events table stores properties as JSON subcolumns, so HogQL rebuilds the document for every row the filter scans.
- That costs far more CPU than the same query on the legacy table, and nothing tells the author.

## Changes

- On the native events table, a query that searches the whole `properties` or person properties document now fails with "Can't search the whole properties column. Use the properties you need, like properties.$current_url."
- The check covers `WHERE`, `PREWHERE`, `HAVING`, `QUALIFY` and `JOIN ... ON`.
- It also covers aggregate arguments, such as `countIf(match(toString(properties), ...))`.
- Key reads, JSON function reads, a selected document and `argMax(properties, timestamp)` still work. The legacy table is unchanged.
- The ClickHouse printer raises the error where it emits the rebuilt document.
- Not covered: a document aliased in a subquery and searched outside it.

## How did you test this code?

**Test rationale:** `test_property_types.py` gains rejected and allowed cases next to the existing native-table print tests. They fail if the check is removed or if it starts to reject key reads.

- Not run locally. CI is the first run, with `test-new-events-schema` applied to find existing queries that the check breaks.

## Release status

## Problem

- Evaluation reports render the agent's markdown as written. The agent reads customer traces, so a prompt injection can add phishing links or tracking images.
- A member blocked from a property can read a colleague's cached text view of a trace for an hour.
- Signed-in users can call the paid translation model without a limit.

- The text view cache key hashes the submitted payload, so one member's copy of an event never serves another.
- Translation throttles keep one bucket per member, shared across their keys.
- Deletes two unused sentiment throttles.

## Problem - Teams with business data in the warehouse find a revenue or order drop only when someone opens a chart, then slice it by hand to find the segment behind it. No scout explains a move in business data. ## Changes - A canonical scout, Business metrics, files Inbox reports such as "Net revenue down 22%, 80% from the EU Pro plan", each with three charts: the series with its baseline, the change by the driver dimension, and the series by that dimension. - It watches approved data catalog metrics from two sources: warehouse-backed SQL metrics, and insight-backed metrics read through the typed query runner. A SQL metric computed over raw `events` on the fly is out of scope; a materialized view over events is in. Detection on saved insights that are not metrics stays with the anomaly-detection scout; this scout explains a flagged move and edits that scout's report with the driver table. - Each measure passes four gates: the source is fresh, the series moved against a trend-adjusted baseline at its own grain (daily, weekly, monthly, quarterly), one or two segments explain at least 60% of the move (or the move is broad and large), and findings that share a segment, a mechanism or an onset are joined into one story report. - A metric owner steers the driver analysis with a dimension hint left as a scout note; the scout profiles columns only when no hint exists. - A bundled `scripts/lens.py` (pure stdlib, JSON in and out, batch mode) computes every verdict, so the model feeds rows and reads results. - A query budget bounds each run: 40 query calls, bounded windows, cache-first and incremental series reads, profiles per table, and a size tier that refuses raw scans of very large tables. ## Problem

Teams comparing offline experiments have to weigh several item-level pass rates themselves to decide which run performed better.

## Changes

- Define one experiment score from item scorer statistics. For example, weight accuracy at 60%, grounded answers at 25%, and resolved requests at 15%.

## Problem

A scheduled scout starts a full sandbox run every time it comes due, even when nothing has changed since its last run.
For a scout that watches a rare or bursty thing (new error tracking issues, a CSP violation, a sign-up from a specific domain), most runs find nothing new.
Each of those runs still pays for a sandbox and an agent that orients itself (scratchpad, past runs, project profile, inbox) before it can decide there is nothing to do.
The cost comes from that fixed overhead, not from the data, which is usually a few rows.

That overhead stops owners from running a scout often.
A scout that should look at new error tracking issues every 30 minutes is too expensive at that cadence, so it runs daily and finds things late.

What exists today:

- The coordinator (`products/signals/backend/temporal/agentic/scout_coordinator.py`) dispatches a `RunSignalsScoutWorkflow` child for every due config. Nothing checks whether there is anything to look at.
- The workflow "Run scout" step (`posthog-run-scout.template.ts`) can start a run from an event, and #113324 adds a templated note so the run knows which event fired it. That path needs a workflow per team, drops fires inside its 30-minute cooldown, and passes one event, not everything since the last run.
- `RunSignalsScoutInput.run_note` and `_run_note_section` in `scout_harness/prompt.py` already carry a one-run note into the prompt.

## Proposal

An optional **pre-check** on a scout config: a HogQL query that runs before a scheduled run starts.

- **No rows:** skip the run. No sandbox, no `SignalScoutRun` row, no LLM call.
- **Rows:** start the run. If the owner turns on "pass rows to the run" (on by default), the first rows go into the prompt as data, so the scout starts from what is new instead of orienting from scratch.

The pre-check is deterministic and cheap: one HogQL query, with a timeout and a row cap.
A plain yes/no gate is the special case, for example `SELECT 1 WHERE ...`.

### Example: error tracking every 30 minutes

```sql
SELECT properties.$exception_issue_id AS issue_id,
       count() AS events,
       uniq(person_id) AS users,
       min(timestamp) AS first_seen
FROM events
WHERE event = '$exception' AND timestamp > {since}
GROUP BY issue_id
HAVING min(timestamp) > {since}
ORDER BY users DESC
LIMIT 50
```

Shape only; check it against the schema before it goes in docs. Widen the `HAVING` for reopened or spiking issues.

### Where it runs

Recommended: as the first activity of `RunSignalsScoutWorkflow`, before `run_signals_scout_activity` creates the run row.

- The coordinator tick stays fast, and one slow or failing query cannot hold up the tick.
- Skipped runs never create a `SignalScoutRun`, so they do not count against `max_runs_per_day` (that tally reads run rows).
- The alternative is to evaluate in `_collect_planned_runs` before `_allocate_tick_budget`, so skipped configs do not use a tick slot. That is more coordinator work per tick; worth it only if tick slots become the constraint.

Only scheduled runs evaluate the pre-check. "Run now", workflow runs and check runs (`triggered_by` manual / workflow / check) skip it, because a person or a trigger already decided to run.

### Placeholders

- `{since}`: start time of the last run that actually ran, or the config's `created_at`.
- `{now}`: the evaluation time.

Pass both through HogQL `placeholders`. Do not build the query with string formatting. The query runs as the team, through the normal HogQL path, so it can read only that team's data.

### Bookkeeping for a skipped run

- Advance the dispatch anchor (`last_run_at`, through the existing slot-anchor stamp) so the next tick does not dispatch it again at once.
- Do not move `{since}`. The next run that starts still sees everything since the last real run.
- A skip does not count toward the failure breaker or the inactivity / engagement auto-pause. A correctly quiet scout must not be paused for being quiet.

### Errors and limits

- Timeout of about 10 seconds, a low-priority query tag, and a row cap (for example 50 rows or 8 KB of rendered text, whichever comes first).
- On a query error, run the scout as if there were no pre-check, and record the error. A failing pre-check must not turn the scout off silently.
- After several errors in a row, tell the owner (the same path as #106455).

### Prompt

Render the rows into a `<precheck_result>` block, reusing the run-note path with its own template.
Frame the block as untrusted data, the same way #113324 frames a workflow note, because event properties can contain text from outside the team.
Strip angle brackets, like the workflow note does.

### Optional backstop

`precheck_max_quiet_minutes`: run anyway if the scout has not run for this long, so baselines and scratchpad memory do not go stale. Off by default.

### Config, API, MCP and UI

- `SignalScoutConfig`: `precheck_query` (nullable text), `precheck_pass_rows` (bool, default true), `precheck_max_quiet_minutes` (nullable int). Same edit permission as the rest of the config.
- Serializer fields with `help_text`, so they reach `scout-config-update` in the MCP.
- A dry-run endpoint ("Test check") that returns the rows and whether the scout would run now, also exposed as an MCP tool.
- Scout settings: a collapsed "Run only when" section with the query editor, the toggle and the test button.

### Observability

- One event per evaluation, `scout_precheck_evaluated`, with outcome (`run` / `skip` / `error`), row count and duration.
- Skipped ticks visible on the roster run strip. Without this, a scout that skips looks broken.

## Plan

1. Backend: config fields and migration, the pre-check activity in `RunSignalsScoutWorkflow`, placeholders, skip bookkeeping, prompt block, limits, event.
2. API and MCP: serializer fields, dry-run endpoint and tool, `authoring-scouts` docs with the error tracking example. The docs should help an agent suggest a pre-check when a scout watches something rare or bursty, write it, test it with the dry run, then save it with `scout-config-update`.
3. UI: the "Run only when" section in scout settings and skipped ticks on the run strip.

## Open questions

- Should a skill (canonical scout or store template) ship a default pre-check in its frontmatter, or is it config-only?
- Should the pre-check result be kept on the run row for debugging and evals?
- If a canonical scout ships a default pre-check, the fleet runs one query per due config per tick. Is a single fleet-wide query per scope better there?
- Intervals under 30 minutes need a change to the tick grid. Out of scope here.

## Problem

PostHog AI 2.0 (task origin `posthog_ai`) and the Slack agent (origin `slack`) run in cloud sandboxes. Their tokens already bill into the PostHog AI `ai_credits` meter, but their sandbox compute is not billed anywhere, so that cost is absorbed. The need comes from the PostHog AI 2.0 rollout; there is no linked issue.

## Changes

Nothing changes on merge: the new setting `AI_CREDITS_COMPUTE_BILLED_ORIGINS` is empty by default. Once it is set to `posthog_ai,slack`:

- User-attributed sandbox compute of those origins is added to `ai_credits_used_in_period`, so customers see it on the PostHog AI meter.
- It is priced by the existing compute rate cards, exactly as PostHog Desktop compute is: same cost calculation, same rounding, 1 credit = 1 cent, no markup on top. Token billing keeps its existing markup.
- A new report field, `ai_compute_credits_used_in_period`, shows the compute share of that total.
- Quota limiting counts the compute toward the `ai_credits` limit, and the sandbox compute quota check for those origins reads `ai_credits` instead of `posthog_code_credits`.
- When that quota blocks a task, the denial code is `ai_credits_billing_limit_exceeded` with a PostHog AI usage limit message, not the PostHog Desktop one.

Not changed: PostHog Desktop (`user_created`, `space_setup`) compute billing, and the gateway ledger's `billable` flag.

<details>
<summary>Design notes, double-charging, and open questions</summary>

**How it ships dark**

- `AI_CREDITS_COMPUTE_BILLED_ORIGINS` (env, comma list, default empty). Intended value: `posthog_ai,slack`.
- The compute quota check also still needs `TASKS_COMPUTE_QUOTA_ENFORCEMENT_ENABLED`, as it does for PostHog Desktop.
- Origins PostHog Desktop already bills are dropped from the setting in code, so a misconfiguration cannot put one session on both meters.

**Where the number flows**

- `get_billable_sandbox_compute_usage_by_team` returns a fourth list, `ai_credits`, from a separate scan of `SandboxSession` rows by origin. The PostHog Desktop scan and its three lists are untouched.
- The list travels as `teams_with_ai_compute_credits_used_in_period` through the usage counter service, the daily report, usage reports v2 (an extra key on the existing `sandbox_compute_usage` multi-key query, with the same pre-patch default as its siblings), and quota limiting.
- `_get_team_report` and quota limiting add it to the token credits, mirroring how `posthog_code` credits combine tokens and compute. Readers default a missing key to zero, so counter reports and query results saved by an older worker during a deploy still load.

**Slack provenance**

Slack tasks have no `client_provenance` (Slack is a `TaskClient` but not a `TaskClientProvenance`), and PostHog Desktop billing requires one. The new path ignores provenance and selects on `origin_product` and `user_attributed_at` only. The `slack` origin is reserved for server flows, so a client cannot claim it.

**Double-charging**

- Usage report: the two meters select disjoint origin sets, and `credits` (PostHog Desktop) never includes the new list.
- Gateway ledger: `compute_settlement` marks a debit `billable` only when `is_billable_sandbox_session` holds, which requires `user_created`. That predicate is unchanged, so `posthog_ai` and `slack` debits stay `billable: false` and the usage report is the only place this compute is charged. The settlement reconciliation reads `.credits` only, so it is unaffected.

**Open questions**

- Switch date (Alessandro): when compute billing moves from the usage report to the gateway ledger at `GATEWAY_COMPUTE_BILLABLE_SINCE` (#136349), these origins need the same handover as PostHog Desktop: the ledger starts marking them billable at the instant the usage report stops counting them. Should that reuse `GATEWAY_COMPUTE_BILLABLE_SINCE`, and should the ledger predicate read this setting?
- Billing service (Roy to confirm): believed to need no change, since `ai_credits_used_in_period` is already its usage key, 1 credit = 1 cent, and unknown report fields are stored as-is. Surfacing `ai_compute_credits_used_in_period` there is optional.
- Slack provenance: is origin-only selection right for Slack, or should Slack sessions get a provenance value of their own?
- Scope by origin, not by token product: `signal_report` and `signals_scout` runs whose tokens bill as `posthog_ai` keep unbilled compute. Internal `posthog_ai` and `slack` profile variants are billed, as their tokens are.
- The `/usage` slash command computes AI credits from token events only, so it will under-report once compute is billed.

</details>

## How did you test this code?

Agent-run only: `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` on the touched files (clean, apart from an import-order finding in `test_usage_report.py` that is already on master), and `py_compile`. The Django test suites were **not run**: the session had no Postgres, ClickHouse, or Redis. The new and changed tests are unexecuted until CI runs them. No manual testing.

**Test rationale:** The regressions guarded are compute landing on the wrong meter, PostHog Desktop billing shifting, and the quota check reading the wrong bucket. New cases sit beside the closest existing ones: `test_sandbox_usage.py` (setting off, each origin on, Slack without provenance, Desktop unchanged, Desktop origin listed by mistake), `test_compute_quota.py` (quota routing), `test_usage_report.py` (report fields combine), `test_quota_usage.py` (quota run counts compute), plus key updates in `test_usage_counters.py` and `test_aggregator.py`. They need the database because the selection is a queryset over `SandboxSession`.

## Release status

- No feature flag controls this change <!-- release-status: no-feature-flag -->

Adds a skipped test that records a known HogQL bug. No production code changes.

## Problem

A person writing SQL can give a `WITH` definition the name of a table. When a persons join condition reads that name and the definition sits on an outer SELECT, HogQL reads the real table instead and reports no error.

```sql
WITH events AS (SELECT toUUID('00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001') AS person_id)
SELECT id FROM (
    SELECT p.id AS id
    FROM person_distinct_ids AS d
    JOIN persons AS p ON d.person_id = p.id AND p.id IN (SELECT person_id FROM events)
) AS joined
```

The condition should match one made-up person. The compiled persons lookup reads the project's events table:

```sql
globalIn(id, (SELECT events__pdi.person_id AS person_id FROM events INNER JOIN (...) AS events__pdi ON ... WHERE equals(events.team_id, 1)))
```

With the definition on the SELECT that holds the join, the lookup reads the definition:

```sql
in(id, (SELECT events.person_id AS person_id FROM events))
```

The bug surfaced in the review of #139727 and is listed in #106296.

## Changes

A skipped test asserts that the compiled condition does not read the events table. The fix for the bug removes the skip.

## How did you test this code?

With the skip removed, the test fails on its assertion, because the compiled SQL contains `equals(events.team_id, 1)`. The same query with the definition on the join's own SELECT passes the assertion. Both ran locally, and the test class needs no database.

**Test rationale:** The nearest test, `test_ctes_do_not_shadow_generated_backing_tables`, covers a definition on the join's own SELECT. No test covers a definition on an outer SELECT.

- A lost v2 entry now comes back within 5 minutes. Nothing reads it until #135515 deploys.
- A new task rebuilds each missing entry, at most 100 per run, and pushes its counts as gauges.

```mermaid
flowchart LR

    classDef phGray fill:#e5e7eb,stroke:#c7ccd1,color:#000;
    class Drain,Upkeep phBlue;
    class Legacy,V2 phGray;
```

```mermaid
    Upkeep{{maintain_flag_definitions_v2_cache_entries}} -->|hourly| V2[(flags_with_cohorts_v2.json)]

    class Drain,Upkeep,Repair phBlue;
```

## Problem

The web, mobile and desktop apps and the agent each bundle a copy of the task model catalog. A new model version needs that copy regenerated, and a desktop release, before a picker can show it. The backend no longer reads the catalog, so the copies can also disagree with it.

## Changes

- The catalog's model rows, price tables and effort tables are deleted. The generator now emits only choices: adapters, effort tiers, default models, slider rungs and the families a picker offers.
- Web and mobile read `GET /tasks/models/`. It now also returns each model's cost summary, whether pickers offer it and the cost baseline's name.
- Desktop and the agent read a model's adapter, name, efforts, context window and price from the gateway listing they already fetch. They offer the two newest versions of each allowed family, the rule the backend uses.
- The hand-kept fallbacks are deleted: the web and mobile effort fallback, mobile's retired-model list and the desktop loop picker's offline model list.

Visible:

- Desktop's default Codex model moves from GPT-6 Sol to GPT-6.2 Sol.
- A model the gateway doesn't describe has no effort picker. Today that is GLM-5.2, GLM-5.3 Flash, Kimi and any ChatGPT-plan variant the gateway doesn't list.
- Efforts and prices follow the gateway where the catalog differed. Claude Sonnet 4.6 gains Max, for example.
- DeepSeek rows have no gateway name, so they read "Deepseek V4 Flash 0731".
- Pickers are empty until the listing loads. The web retries a failed load three times.
- The long-context price tier that GPT Sol models showed is gone, because the gateway lists base rates only.
- On the legacy gateway fallback, desktop offers every model that gateway lists and shows no effort picker, because its listing has no families or efforts.

Trade-off: desktop reads the allowed families from its bundle, so a new family still needs a desktop release. A new version of a family doesn't.

## How did you test this code?

The backend, web, mobile, desktop, agent, agent-contracts and harness suites pass locally, and the desktop workspace type-checks. One test checks the agent's offered list against the backend's for the same saved production listing. Not run locally: the desktop SQLite tests, which need a native build this machine lacks. No picker was rendered in a browser or in the desktop app.

CI report: the complexity warnings name functions this PR edits but doesn't restructure. The two call assertions it counts read the request a run sends and the config a session starts with. Its duplicates are two generated OAuth scope files this PR doesn't touch and the report model resolver, which the desktop and web hosts already bound the same way and which gains one line in each here. Its coverage section predates the last pushes. A local run covers every changed line in the three backend modules it lists. The three lines in a test file are a TypedDict's field annotations. The MCP snapshot gains the models tool's `include_unoffered` parameter. The two eager graph roots over budget show the same delta on #139329, which changes eight bytes of web code. The two flaky Playwright tests cover person properties and trace screenshots.

Part of #132210.

hits.body:
## Problem

When the investigation agent calls a fire a false positive and suppresses the notification, the alert still transitions to `Firing`. The next fire on that alert is then treated as "already firing", so it skips the investigation entirely and posts un-gated. A user who turned on `investigation_gates_notifications` gets the worst combination: the first (dismissed) fire is silent, and the second fire, which may be real, arrives with no verdict, no summary, and no chart.

Observed on an hourly anomaly alert on 2026-08-28:

| Check | Detector | Investigation | Notification |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | fired | ran, verdict `false_positive`, `notification_suppressed_by_agent=True` | suppressed |
| 2, one hour later | fired | never started (`investigation_status` is `null`, not `skipped`) | sent synchronously, plain message |

The gate is `should_trigger_investigation` in `posthog/temporal/alerts/investigation.py`:

```python
if previous_state == AlertState.FIRING:
    return False
```

`previous_state` is `alert.state` as read at the top of `evaluate_alert` in `posthog/temporal/alerts/activities.py`. Check 1 set it to `Firing`, and nothing about the false-positive verdict changes that, so check 2 short-circuits before the cooldown in `claim_investigation_slot` is consulted. `null` rather than `skipped` on check 2 confirms it was this branch and not the cooldown.

The rule itself is sound: a continuously-firing alert should not spawn an investigation every interval. It just uses the wrong signal. The alert's `state` says "the detector has been firing"; what the gate wants to know is "did the last delivered outcome tell the user this is an incident". After a suppressed false positive, the user was told nothing, so the next fire is a fresh transition from their point of view.

## Design constraint

The investigation agent is an overlay on the alert state machine, not a participant in it. It reads `alert.state` and the `AlertCheck` history, and it writes only its own fields on the check (`investigation_status`, `investigation_verdict`, `investigation_summary`, `notification_suppressed_by_agent`) plus the decision to hold or release a notification. It never writes `alert.state`, `last_notified_at`, or anything else the state machine in `products/alerts/backend/state_machine.py` owns. Turning the agent off must leave the alert behaving exactly as it did before the agent existed. Any fix here has to keep that property.

## Proposed fix

Keep `alert.state` untouched, and make the gate look at the previous check's outcome instead of only the state.

In `should_trigger_investigation`, when `previous_state == FIRING`, look up the most recent prior `AlertCheck` for the alert. If that check has `notification_suppressed_by_agent=True` (equivalently, `investigation_verdict == false_positive` and no `notification_sent_at`), treat the previous state as `Not firing` and return `True`. Otherwise keep returning `False`.

- The lookup runs inside the same `select_for_update` transaction that `evaluate_alert` already opens, so it is consistent with the check insert that follows.
- `claim_investigation_slot` still applies afterwards. Its one-hour cooldown counts `DONE` checks, so a fire that lands inside the hour after a false-positive verdict is marked `skipped` and delivered un-investigated, the same as today. That is the flapping guard doing its job. If that turns out to be too tight for hourly alerts, the cooldown is the knob to tune, not the gate.
- Nothing about the visible alert state changes. The alert stays `Firing` in the UI, which matches what the detector saw.

Rejected alternative: reset `alert.state` to `Not firing` when a verdict is `false_positive`. That makes the agent a writer of state-machine state, which breaks the overlay constraint above: the UI would disagree with the detector, and disabling the agent would leave alerts in states the state machine never produced.

## Acceptance criteria

- A fire whose previous check was `Firing` with `notification_suppressed_by_agent=True` starts an investigation (subject to the cooldown) and, when gating is on, holds the notification for it.
- A fire whose previous check was `Firing` and was delivered (`notification_sent_at` set) still does not start an investigation.
- A fire whose previous check was `Firing` with verdict `inconclusive` and `investigation_inconclusive_action=notify` (so the notification went out) still does not start an investigation.
- No code path in the investigation layer writes `alert.state` or `last_notified_at`; with `investigation_agent_enabled=False` the check sequence and notifications are byte-for-byte what they are today.
- Unit tests in `posthog/temporal/tests/test_alerts_investigation.py` cover the cases above.

## Refinements

See the first comment: (1) the cooldown must not block the check that directly follows a suppressed one, and (2) cap consecutive dismissals at K and send one digest instead of re-investigating indefinitely.

Both stay inside the overlay. The consecutive-dismissal count is derived from `AlertCheck` rows (consecutive prior checks with `notification_suppressed_by_agent=True` since the last check whose state was `Not firing`), not stored as new alert state. The digest is one released notification and the checks after it are held the same way a suppressed check is held today. The state machine keeps producing its FIRE outcome every interval and never learns any of this happened.

## Out of scope

- Changing the flat cooldown for reasons other than the interval interaction described in the first comment.
- PostHog/posthog#90884 (server-owned chart block); related but independent.

## Related

- #88990 feat(alerts): include the insight chart in investigation Slack alerts
- #90884 feat(alerts): make the insight-alert Slack chart block server-owned

## Problem

- Plain email sends wait behind sends with files on shared workers (who met this in production: unknown).
- Full email workers claim, defer, and spend SES tokens on sends with files; [#140206](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/pull/140206) and [#140208](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/pull/140208) left polling combined.

<!-- merge-risk -->
> [!WARNING]
> 🟡 **Merge risk: medium** · two-way door
> - Gate off: poll SQL, admission and the plans of the changed cancel and release writes match the base layer (shadow diff at `890fa44`); cancel writes clear `file_bytes`.
> - Gate on: splits `file_bytes` rows into a second poll; rows this version canceled and un-deferred overdue rows settle without slots.
> - Mixed versions during the deploy: an old pod's defer or reschedule after a new pod's cancel writes the size back, as every cancel does on the base (cross-version run at `890fa44`). With the gate off the single poll ends such a row at once. If the gate goes on while one is left, it waits for a files slot like a send with files; no row is lost or sent.
> - Drain pre-writer rows and intake first, or legacy sends with files waste tokens in the plain poll.
> - Gate on, by design: a send past the longest wait for room fails before admission even if a slot is free, as the files poll's overdue claim does; both polls draw from one SES bucket, so a bulk plain send can take a token ahead of a due send with files; a files poll throttled by SES stamps its health only between sleeps, as the single base loop does; a workflow that resumes after its last send with files still carries its size, so while the files slots are full it waits for one even when its next step sends nothing; and the second poll adds a query against the shared database each cycle, also when no send with files is due.
> - Uncovered: the production write cost of the cancel and release writes (plans match base on a scratch database), polls claiming concurrently under load, and the size distribution of production rows, which waits for #140206's column.
> - Proof judge (`47bef86`) derived high risk and a one-way door over a cap check `e166aff` reverted.
> - **Switch-off:** `CDP_EMAIL_ATTACHMENTS_SEPARATE_POLL`, default off.
> - **Tier:** critical (a: `services/cyclotron-v2/` and the email consumer)

## Rollout

- **Stages:** deploy [#140206](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/pull/140206) and [#140208](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/pull/140208), verify indexes, drain pre-writer rows and intake, confirm no available email row has both a cancel requested and a size, enable bounded polls, dev burst, then prod.
- **Decided:** cap 2 by driver (reason over default 4: unknown); burst checks plain p95 within 1 s and deferrals under 5% (reasons: unknown).
- **Watch:** plain p95 by `with_files` ([#140205](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/pull/140205)), `cdp_email_attachments_deferral_tokens_total`, and dequeue latency (prod alert PR: unknown).
<!-- /merge-risk -->

## Changes

Plain email sends stop waiting behind sends with files, and full workers spend no SES tokens on them. Canceled and overdue sends with files settle while every slot stays full. Behind `CDP_EMAIL_ATTACHMENTS_SEPARATE_POLL` (default off), `CyclotronV2Worker` polls `file_bytes IS NOT NULL` rows separately while the main poll skips them.

Rejected: admit-or-defer tuning (driver's reason: unknown) and reserved plain SES capacity, because the slot cap bounds claims.

With the gate on, sends with files move to a separate poll.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  Q[(cyclotron_jobs email)] --> M[main poll]
  M -->|plain| P[send plain]
  M -->|with files| R{room for files?}
  R -->|yes| S[send with files]
  R -->|no| D["defer, token spent"]
  D --> Q
  class Q phGray; class M,P,S phBlue; class R phYellow; class D phRed;
  classDef phBlue fill:#1d4aff,stroke:#1d4aff,color:#fff;
  classDef phRed fill:#f54e00,stroke:#f54e00,color:#fff;
  classDef phYellow fill:#f9bd2b,stroke:#f9bd2b,color:#000;
  classDef phGray fill:#e5e7eb,stroke:#c7ccd1,color:#000;
```

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  Q[(cyclotron_jobs email)] -->|"file_bytes IS NULL or canceled"| M[main poll]
  Q -->|"file_bytes set, room > 0"| F[files poll]
  Q -->|"file_bytes set, room = 0, overdue"| O[overdue poll]
  M --> S[send or cancel]
  F --> SF[send with files]
  O --> X["fail unsent, no token"]
  class Q phGray; class M,F,O,S,SF phBlue; class X phYellow;
  classDef phBlue fill:#1d4aff,stroke:#1d4aff,color:#fff;
  classDef phYellow fill:#f9bd2b,stroke:#f9bd2b,color:#000;
  classDef phGray fill:#e5e7eb,stroke:#c7ccd1,color:#000;
```

- The files poll always runs bounded scans on `idx_cyclotron_jobs_email_files_due`, even with bounded settings off.
- Cancel writes in `cancelJobs` clear `file_bytes` so the main poll settles canceled rows.
- Zero-room polls claim overdue rows without tokens. The consumer fails every overdue-claimed send unsent, even when its own clock reads it as not yet overdue.
- Five full minutes (`SLOTS_STALLED_AFTER_MS`) fails health, past the 17-second deadline plus lookups, writes, and flushes.
- Workers that refuse files keep them in the main poll; `room()` keeps master's `maxInFlight < 1` rule.
- Config, queue, and codec wiring is `(mechanical)`; added comments (3% CI warning) explain planner and clock rules.

Depends on: [#140206](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/pull/140206) (open), [#140208](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/pull/140208) (open, base), [#140205](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/pull/140205) (merged, metrics).
Blocks: none stacked (prod alert PR: unknown).

**Read yourself:** [files loop, L417–445](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/blob/928dae20f48bbae0edac57933006698574dd35e5/nodejs/src/cdp/services/cyclotron-v2/worker.ts#L417-L445): skips tokens at zero room, drains overdue rows, stalls health? [fair dequeue SQL, L163–202](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/blob/928dae20f48bbae0edac57933006698574dd35e5/nodejs/src/cdp/services/cyclotron-v2/due-rows-sql.ts#L163-L202): rechecks `file_bytes` without stale-stats scans? [overdue check, L99–117](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/blob/928dae20f48bbae0edac57933006698574dd35e5/nodejs/src/cdp/consumers/cdp-cyclotron-worker-email.consumer.ts#L99-L117): fails overdue claims under clock skew?

## How did you test this code?

**What was proven, and what not**

- ✅ `parameterai[bot]` and `veria-ai[bot]` passed on HEAD `928dae2`; `maxInFlight` note answered in [reply](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/pull/140209#discussion_r4678037004).
- ❌ Receipt, shadow-diff, panel, and judge stop at `47bef86` (13 commits behind HEAD); judge failed there.
- ❌ Dev burst (`live-run`, accepted gap) and `prod-shape` drain check did not run.
- ❌ `Duplication lint` was cancelled at HEAD, so no duplication result exists.

Some metrics fail with a `validation_error` on every recalculation until someone edits them. Each scheduled run, page load heal, or config change still sends them to the calc activity, and the error comes back the same each time.

This is PR 1 of a stack for a pre-run recalculation skip classifier. It stacks on #120818, which stores the calculation key on every `metric_errors` entry. Later PRs add one check each, and the frontend copy for skipped metrics.

<!-- Does this fix an issue? Uncomment the line below with the issue ID to automatically close it when merged -->
<!-- Closes #ISSUE_ID -->

## Changes

<!-- For each change a person can notice, say what they will now see or do differently, not only the code path that does it. Mark the rest as mechanical so a reviewer knows nothing user-visible is hiding in it. -->

<!-- If there are frontend changes, please include screenshots. For a new interaction that one screenshot cannot show, a short GIF or animated WebP of the flow can replace the after screenshot. -->
<!-- PostHog employees: `hogli pr:upload-image <file>` uploads to the public PostHog/pr-assets repo and prints markdown to paste here. Never upload customer data, secrets, or internal info. -->

<!-- If a reference design was involved, include a link to the relevant Figma frame! -->

Discovery now skips a metric whose latest failure is a `validation_error` with the same calculation key as now, behind the `experiments-recalculations-skip-failing-metrics` organization flag. With the flag off (shadow mode), discovery sends `experiment metric would skip` and the metric runs as usual. No frontend changes, so there are no screenshots; PR 2 adds the frontend copy.

### Pure skip modules

`skip_recalculation` holds the `@frozen` types (`MetricKey`, `MetricHistory`, `MetricRunOutcome`, `MetricSkip`) and `find_metric_skips`, which runs the checks in order and keeps the first skip per metric. A check that raises is logged and returns no skip. Every trigger skips, `manual_retry` included, so only a new calculation key ends a skip. `skip_recalculation_checks` holds the one check for this PR. Neither module reads the database.

- `products/experiments/backend/metric_calculation/skip_recalculation.py`
- `products/experiments/backend/metric_calculation/skip_recalculation_checks.py`
- `products/experiments/backend/test/test_skip_recalculation.py`

### Discovery writes the skip

Discovery reads the latest two terminal runs of the experiment in one query and builds a `MetricHistory` per metric. Discovery is per experiment, so a lateral join is not needed. A skip entry from an earlier run reads as the failure it skipped, so the skip holds until the metric changes. Any error in skip planning skips nothing. With the flag on, each skipped metric gets a `metric_errors` entry (`step: "skipped"`, `error_type: "metric_skipped"`, `skipped_error_type`, `skip_reason`, `failed_recalculation_id`, `failed_at`). That entry keeps the frontend gap check from starting a heal loop.

### The calc activity fails the metric early

The calc activity finds the skip entry, sends `experiment metric error` with `error_type: "metric_skipped"`, `skipped_error_type` and `skip_reason`, and returns a failure before any query. The run ends failed, the same as for any other `metric_errors` entry. `metric_skipped` joins `NON_RETRYABLE_ERROR_TYPES`. The workflow code does not change, so no `workflow.patched` gate is needed.

- `products/experiments/backend/temporal/recalculation_logic.py`
- `products/experiments/backend/temporal/models.py`
- `products/experiments/backend/temporal/test_recalculation_activities.py`
- `products/experiments/backend/temporal/ARCHITECTURE.md` (also corrects which failures show "Try again": only a retriable one, and no failure starts a heal)

### Known limit: what the key does not cover

Key version 1 hashes the metric definition, the start date, the stats method, the stored exposure criteria, maturity and the excluded variants. A fix in any of these places keeps the key, so the metric stays skipped:

- The end date and the analysis window.
- Stats settings beyond the method: the Bayesian prior and interval, the frequentist alpha, sequential testing, and the baseline variant.
- CUPED settings.
- The feature flag variants and the aggregation group type.
- Team settings: test account filters, the time zone, and the team defaults for sequential testing and CUPED.
- Definitions the metric references: actions, cohorts, warehouse tables and their schema, property types, and HogQL modifiers.

The shadow events show how often a skip of this kind happens before the flag turns on.

## Problem

A model's adapter, name, reasoning efforts and cost are typed by hand in the task model catalog. Every new version also needs a catalog row before a product can call it or a picker can offer it. The gateway already serves all of this, and the copies have drifted ([thread](https://posthog.slack.com/archives/C0C1T3V1RJA/p1795056481045999), #132210).

## Changes

- The backend reads a model's adapter, name, reasoning efforts and cost multiplier from its gateway row. It reads no catalog row.
- Each agent product names the model families it allows. Its token pin is every version the gateway lists in those families, and its pickers offer the two newest of each.
- A short reserved list holds the exceptions: a trial model, and ids kept for the free tier and older desktop builds. No picker offers one.
- A row that says nothing about reasoning gets no effort picker, and an effort sent for it isn't refused. The gateway lists no reasoning for GLM-5.2 or GLM-5.3 Flash, and shipped desktop builds send efforts for both.
- While the listing can't be read, a family product's token mint fails as retryable. A workflow step is checked against every model its token admits.
- A live run keeps to the versions its token was minted with.
- Rollout flags are keyed by gateway family. Workflows and the run command's model switch now check them too.

Visible: backend pickers lose GPT-5, GPT-5.6 Sol, GPT-6 Sol, Claude Opus 4.8 and Claude Fable 5. Tokens can still call them, and also the older `gpt` versions the gateway lists (GPT-4.1, GPT-4o, GPT-5.1, GPT-5.2). GPT-5.6 cost multipliers drop. The Codex slider rungs move to GPT-6.2 Sol. The fixed pins for onboarding, conversations and the free tier are unchanged.

Trade-off: a trial model the gateway lists in an allowed family is admitted for every agent product unless it's reserved first.

This PR now includes #139330, which is closed.

## How did you test this code?

Every backend test gets a saved copy of the production listing. A snapshot records what each product's token may call and what its picker offers. Table tests cover the adapter rule, partial rows, the three reasoning states, the family rule, reservations, the run stamp, the flag checks and a listing outage at mint. The call assertions the CI report counts read the request sent to the gateway's token endpoint. Not done: a cold cloud start.

CI report: its TypeScript duplicate is two generated OAuth scope files this PR doesn't touch. The only shipped web change here is four model id strings, so the bundle delta, the eager graph delta and the two flaky Playwright tests (login, person properties) don't come from this diff.

## Problem

Cloud runs on the Claude runtime call MCP tools that are set to "needs approval" without asking the user. The gateway proxy then rejects the call. Desktop already asks first.

Refs #76237

## Changes

- Cloud runs now ask with one option, "Yes, and approve this tool in PostHog". On yes, the run saves the approval, then makes the call. Two installations whose names sanitize alike stay ungated.
- An allow saves the approval only when the answer carries `confirmPersistentApproval: true`. PostHog AI and the desktop app send it only when a person clicks an allow option on a prompt marked `persistsApproval`. Anything that answers on its own (PostHog AI tabs loaded before this deploy, auto-approve modes, the Slack permission broker) picks the first allow option, so the option id alone can't show a person approved the tool. Those answers are declined, and the run tells the user to approve the tool in PostHog.
- The approval is saved with the run's credentials, so it's saved only when the person who answered is the user those credentials belong to. The `/command` JWT says who answered, and `/api/users/@me/` says who the run acts as. If a teammate answers, the run declines the same way.
- Saving an approval needs `project:write`, but `/command` needs only `task:write`. So `/command` now returns 403 for a `permission_response` with `confirmPersistentApproval` from a personal API key or OAuth token without `project:write`, before it reaches the sandbox. Browser sessions and the desktop app, whose token holds `project:write`, are unaffected.
- On codex, a decline with a reason reaches codex as a decline, not a cancel, and the reason is added to the running turn. A cancel aborts the whole turn on command approvals, and on MCP prompts the model sees only "user cancelled".
- Background runs and runs with no connected client decline without asking. Slack runs relay the prompt like any other run, and the confirmation check declines the broker's answer.
- The mobile apps don't send the confirmation yet, so allowing a tool from them is declined with the same guidance rather than saved.
- A `PreToolUse` hook forces "ask" for these tools, because `bypassPermissions` skips `canUseTool`.
- Approval states load at startup alongside session setup, capped at 5s so they never delay the run. Past that, tools load ungated. They reload on `refresh_session`, where an installation whose fetch fails keeps its last loaded states.

Out of scope: built-in agent runs (gateway grant URLs), Pi's "allow once", and saving the approval as the person who answered rather than with the run's credentials.

## How did you test this code?

- Ran `agent-server.test.ts` and `posthog-api.test.ts` (301 tests), `tsc` and Biome in the agent workspace, `permissionResponse.test.ts` and the desktop `pnpm typecheck`, and all of `runStreamLogic.test.ts` (416 tests).
- Added codex cases for a command approval and an MCP prompt cancelled with a reason. Each declines and passes the reason on, and each failed with its guard removed. The codex adapter suite passes (397 tests).
- Added `test_command_persistent_approval_requires_project_write`: a `task:write` key gets a 403 and nothing reaches the sandbox, and a key with `project:write` goes through. Without the scope check, the first case got a 200 and was forwarded.
- The new cases each failed without their fix: an allow without the confirmation was saved, PostHog AI sent no confirmation for a person's allow, and the desktop helper didn't exist.
- Earlier rounds: ran the agent workspace's adapter, server and API Vitest suites, plus the full-auto cases in `runStreamLogic.test.ts` and the `toolPolicy.test.ts` table, removing each fix in turn to check its test failed.
- The approval tests answer through the real `permission_response` command with a caller user id and the confirmation flag, including a teammate who allows and an answer with no confirmation. Neither gets the tool approved.
- On a devbox running the real stack, with a DeepWiki installation named "Deep Wiki (test)", I checked the backend calls the agent makes:
  - New tools default to "needs approval".
  - A proxy `tools/call` before approval returns `-32001 "requires approval"`.
  - The agent's `PATCH tools/<name>/` approves the tool, and the same call then reaches the upstream server.
  - The sandbox config uses the raw name `Deep Wiki (test)`, so the agent needs the sanitized key, and its installation regex matches the proxy URL.
- Not checked: a full PostHog AI run with a model, because the devbox has no LLM key.
- Not checked: a team-visible run answered by its own user and by a teammate.
- Not checked: that the SDK calls `canUseTool` after a hook "ask" under `bypassPermissions`. The exec sub-tool gate depends on the same behavior.
- Not checked: a Slack-origin run end to end, or a mobile allow.

**Test rationale:** I added the new cases beside the existing tests for each unit. They cover the gate, the confirmation check, the answering-user check, the excluded run types, the refresh (including a failed fetch that keeps or drops states by installation id), the hook, the policy-load retry, and full-auto leaving the prompt to the user.

**CI report warnings:**

- Call assertions in `agent-server.test.ts` and `approvals.test.ts` read the calls a boundary received: the approval `PATCH`, the prompt relayed to the client, the payload forwarded to the adapter, and the reason handed to codex. Those calls are the unit's output.
- The TypeScript duplication is the per-file `./mcp/tool-metadata` mock that 8 `claude-agent.*.test.ts` files each define. This PR adds two entries to each copy. Moving them to one shared mock factory is a separate test refactor.
- The two over-budget eager graph roots show no change against base. The 216 B bundle growth is the `persistsApproval` checks in `runStreamLogic` and `toolPolicy`.
- The TypeScript complexity warnings are on existing `runStreamLogic` functions. This PR adds one condition to `deliverPermission` and one to the auto-approve check.

## Release status

- No feature flag controls this change <!-- release-status: no-feature-flag -->

## Docs update

None.

**Agent:** Claude Code, Claude Opus 5.5 (`claude-opus-5-5`)

Skills: `/writing-tests`, `/writing-pr-descriptions`, `/writing-code-comments`, `/unslop`.

## Problem

## Changes

- After each quota run, each confirmed disagreement is captured once as a `quota limiting spine mismatch` event, labelled with its cause.
- Report only: no deciding code changes, and a failing comparison cannot fail or skip the run.
- Merge after billing serves `POST /api/internal/limiting`, or each run records a handled exception.

The activity gains one call to billing.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    classDef phBlue fill:#1d4aff,stroke:#1d4aff,color:#fff;
    classDef phYellow fill:#f9bd2b,stroke:#f9bd2b,color:#000;
    Activity[Quota limiting activity] --> Run[Quota run decides and writes limits]
    class Activity phYellow;
    class Run phBlue;
```

After:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    classDef phBlue fill:#1d4aff,stroke:#1d4aff,color:#fff;
    classDef phRed fill:#f54e00,stroke:#f54e00,color:#fff;
    classDef phYellow fill:#f9bd2b,stroke:#f9bd2b,color:#000;

```
