## Problem

Analysts must rerun a notebook and click **Replace rows** before downstream SQL sees fresh results. [#140517](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/pull/140517)

## Changes

An agent can now run a notebook between SQL models in PostHog’s warehouse DAG. For example, SQL totals sales, Python forecasts demand, and SQL lists items to reorder.

- **Declare** a table from a SQL or Python cell and name its upstream models.
- **Refresh** daily or on demand. Each run publishes the cell’s full dataframe.
- **Inspect** failed cells and the last published run. A failed refresh preserves the table and skips dependent SQL.

### Before

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A[Run notebook] --> B[Save or replace rows in browser] --> C[Warehouse table]
    classDef phYellow fill:#f9bd2b,stroke:#f9bd2b,color:#000;
    classDef phBlue fill:#1d4aff,stroke:#1d4aff,color:#fff;
    classDef phGray fill:#e5e7eb,stroke:#c7ccd1,color:#000;
    class A phYellow;
    class B phBlue;
    class C phGray;
```

### After

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A[SQL model: total sales by item] --> B[Notebook Python cell: forecast demand] --> C[demand_forecast table] --> D[SQL model: list items to reorder]
    classDef phYellow fill:#f9bd2b,stroke:#f9bd2b,color:#000;
    classDef phBlue fill:#1d4aff,stroke:#1d4aff,color:#fff;
    classDef phGray fill:#e5e7eb,stroke:#c7ccd1,color:#000;
    class A,D phYellow;
    class B phBlue;
    class C phGray;
```

<details>
<summary>Using the three MCP tools</summary>

Enable `notebook-warehouse-models` for MCP after the Django routes deploy.

| Tool | How to use it for the reorder report |
| --- | --- |
| `notebooks-declare-warehouse-model` | Choose the forecast cell, name its table `demand_forecast`, and pass the sales model’s node ID as an upstream dependency. |
| `notebooks-run-warehouse-model` | Start the model and its upstream dependencies now. After the first publication, reference `demand_forecast` in the downstream SQL model. |
| `notebooks-warehouse-model-status` | Pass the returned `dag_run_id` to see whether the run reached the notebook. Inspect cell errors and the run that produced the current table. |

Each run executes the saved notebook through the selected cell. First publication requires an unused table name. Later refreshes keep the table ID. Runs that share a notebook wait their turn, and previous generations remain readable for 24 hours.

</details>

## How did you test this code?

**Test rationale:** [Warehouse tests](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/blob/87e6096958bc3cec744ba3caafb234df509f0339/posthog/api/test/notebooks/test_warehouse_model.py#L217) cover replacement. [DAG tests](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/blob/87e6096958bc3cec744ba3caafb234df509f0339/products/data_modeling/backend/temporal/tests/test_execute_dag_workflow.py#L635) cover failure propagation.

<details>
<summary>CI advisories and regression coverage</summary>

The warehouse round trip read 14,000 synthetic rows on each of two refreshes. A failed third refresh preserved the second table. A local Temporal test used a stub notebook task to check dependency ordering.

The API test checks that the returned ticket identifies the queued Temporal run and that polling uses the same project, node, and ticket. The workflow tests exercise the receiver. Time-skipping tests cover a busy notebook, downstream failure, and delayed cleanup. A warehouse round trip reads both generations across replacement.

CI measured a 7.7 KiB decrease in total frontend bundle size. Of the two eager roots over budget, logged-out boot had zero growth and the authenticated shell grew 3.5 KiB against the CI baseline. The frontend diff only regenerates the notebook API. No browser code imports the new client functions or schemas. CI also shows changes in the Today sidebar chunks, outside this diff.

The database migration creates one table with a primary key on `node_id`, its node foreign key, and an index on `team_id`. The migration analyzer classified it as safe. Five Chromium cases passed on retry. Two exercise editing or deleting an ordinary notebook. The other three cover person properties, insight titles, and workflow secrets. None of the five exercises model declaration, DAG execution, or warehouse publication.

</details>

## Release status

- This change is behind a feature flag and is not available to users <!-- release-status: behind-feature-flag -->

## Docs update

## Problem

- A marketing email moved to `emails.send` loses its message category: code sends skip opt-outs and carry no unsubscribe link.

<!-- merge-risk -->
> [!NOTE]
> 🔵 **Merge risk: low**, 🟡 at full rollout
> - Code sends without `send.category` and workflow email steps are unchanged, in both regions. The fake SES tests cover them: no List-Unsubscribe header, `{{ unsubscribe_url }}` left as written.
> - Sends with a category reach no team at merge: only the Django PR sends one, behind its flag.
> - Once that flag is on, a marketing send skips opted-out recipients and adds the link and headers. A live send with both PRs covers this.
> - Two-way at merge. Once a team sends categorized email, sent mail can't be recalled.
> - Marketing code sends queue on the bulk lane, as workflow marketing emails do, so a burst can't delay password resets.
> - The preferences link lands in click events when a recipient clicks it, as on workflow marketing emails.
> - **Switch-off:** none here, live on deploy, fix forward. The Django flag `workflows-code-send-categories` decides who sends a category.

## Problem

- The Rust logs consumer must run Hog programs that customers write, and the shared VM is not safe for that. A crafted program can overflow the stack, print gigabytes from a small heap, or leak memory between runs.
- This is the first of four PRs that replace #131041.

## Changes

- A host can step the VM, answer native calls itself, pass globals with ordered keys, read the raw result, and own a bounded regex cache.
- Printing, string building, native results, snapshots, membership tests and equality tests stop at the heap and depth limits.
- Closures compare, print and drop without following their captures, and the VM frees a closure that captures itself.
- A null, a boolean and a container cost 8 bytes of the heap limit, as in the Node VM. Before, they cost 0 or 1.
- A tuple that holds itself prints `null` where it repeats, as an array does.
- A bounded regex cache refuses the counted repetitions that RE2 refuses in Node.
- String functions count UTF-16 units and integer overflow continues as a float, as in the Node VM.
- cohort-core's `EVALUATOR_VERSION` goes to 4, so every stored person record evaluates again.

> [!WARNING]
> cymbal, cohort-core and the `hogvm-node` binding share this VM. The binding runs event transformations in the Node consumer when `CDP_HOG_RUST_VM_EXECUTION_ENABLED` is set. The string, overflow, heap charge and tuple changes apply to all three. Cymbal disables a rule that reaches the heap limit, and the new charge moves that limit down. A review thread asks how cymbal should handle it.

## How did you test this code?

- Ran locally: `cargo test -p hogvm -p cohort-core`, the `hogvm-node` tests, and clippy for hogvm and cohort-core.
- Not run locally: cymbal's tests, which CI runs on this PR, and cohort-core's `tests/postgres.rs`, which needs the Django test database.
- The CI report shows a comment density just under 6%. 49 of the 95 lines give the Hog source of a bytecode constant in a test, as the crate's other tests do. The four PRs together are below 4%.

**Test rationale:** `js_strings_and_limits.rs`, `host_driver.rs` and `async_resume.rs` hold one case for each limit, and each case fails without its guard. Eight of them aborted the test process with a stack overflow before their fix.

## Release status

- No feature flag controls this change <!-- release-status: no-feature-flag -->

## Docs update

- None.

## 🤖 Agent context

**Autonomy:** Human-driven (agent-assisted)

**Agent:** Claude Code, Opus 5.5 and Fable 5.2

**Skills:** `/stacking-prs`, `/writing-pr-descriptions`, `/writing-code-comments`, `/writing-tests`

**Driver checked:** Decided the split of #131041 into four PRs. Not yet checked the diff.

**Security review:** needed

<details>
<summary>More context for AI agents</summary>

- **Session:** https://claude.ai/code/session_017AymvKWGZjo39EYJtPKHgZ, https://claude.ai/code/session_017AymvKLVx6u56rQY3BPqQn
- **Decisions:** the layer is the `rust/common/hogvm` part of #131041 at its last reviewed head, plus the fixes for the review findings on this PR (837a96ebfc6, 916fda3f063, 90136d012a9, c5217895710, 0cc5b09fb69, 4c8fc97eaad, 8786d84d19d, f7ef89affca, 546386738fe, 48666b42a4f, ba1198ba499).
- **Decisions:** master had already taken `EVALUATOR_VERSION` 3 for another change, so this layer takes 4.
- **Decisions:** `Closure` has hand-written `Debug`, `PartialEq` and `Drop` paths, because the derived ones followed reference-counted cells.
- **Decisions:** the shared regex cache is unchanged. A host passes its own `RegexCache` to keep customer patterns out of it.
- **Decisions:** a snapshot measures the stack before `collect_cells` and each closed value before its walk, and refuses a cycle, because the walks in `state.rs` have no guard. They still follow captures. A last measure of all closed values together catches one value that many closures captured.
- **Decisions:** the repeat measure takes a rule from its caller: `jsonStringify` allows a cycle, the printers refuse one inside a SQL value, and the snapshot and `hog_to_json` refuse every cycle. It counts a second reference to one heap string. The SQL printer has no cycle check of its own.
- **Decisions:** `HogLiteral::compare_work` counts what one equality test reads: the top-level pairs of two containers of one length, at 32 bytes each, plus the bytes of same-length strings and of object keys. A nested container compares by its heap reference and counts nothing. `==`, `equals`, `notEquals`, the `in` opcode, `has`, `indexOf` and `in()` refuse more than 64 MiB of that work, and a membership test checks the total after each item.
- **Decisions:** value sizes follow `calculateCost` of the Node VM for a null, a boolean and a container. A slot in an array is 32 bytes, so the charge can be 4 times under the real size.
- **Decisions:** `SetProperty` charges a text key at the length of its text, because the object keeps its own copy. The charge follows the insert.
- **Decisions:** a bounded `RegexCache` limits the compiled size only. A limit on the search cache made `[a-z]{1000}[^a-z]` about 1,000 times slower. The repetition check runs only after a cache miss.
- **Hosts:** `hogvm-node` sets a 64 MiB heap and uses the shared regex cache. The bounded cache and its RE2 repetition rule reach a host only when it passes its own cache, and the binding does not yet. Its `Cargo.lock` is not updated here.
- **Open threads:** how cymbal handles a rule that reaches the heap limit; `in` on a text or object haystack has no compare budget, because its work is linear in one operand; natives such as `upper` copy a shared string with no allocation check; JSON escaping can make `jsonStringify` output 6 times its measured size; a pattern over the cache limit compiles on each call. None changed here. The owner decides.
- **Not bounded:** no clock runs inside one VM step or one native call. Each fix above bounds one operation by size. A new operation whose work grows faster than its operands needs its own bound.
- **Read closely:** `print.rs` (`RepeatMeasure`, `HogQLPrinter`), `context.rs` (`walk_emplacing`), `values.rs` (`Drop for Upvalue`, `Closure`, `size`, `compare_work`), `util.rs` (`RegexCache`), `vm.rs` (`Drop for HogVM`, `snapshot`, `assert_membership_fits`, `SetProperty`).

</details>

## Changes

- Raw direct queries nested more than 100 levels deep now fail fast with the existing "too complex to validate" error.

## Problem

- Plain event projections keyed on `uuid` can fail an incremental run with `DuplicateUniqueKeyError`, and a retry fails the same way.
- The cause: `events` can return one stored event twice before parts merge.

Inbox: [step 1](https://us.posthog.com/project/2/inbox/reports/01a21014-0c68-7d35-8bb0-5fdf6fc5a9a8) of [this plan](https://us.posthog.com/project/2/inbox/reports/01a21010-3966-7e6f-bbb0-5c8efc8c93ae).

## Changes

- These models now keep the first row of each repeated uuid, so the run succeeds.
- Every other model still fails on a repeated key.
- The model must read only the built-in `events` table, with no join, linked field, `ARRAY JOIN`, `arrayJoin()` or aggregate.
- `UniqueKeyTracker` does the dedup, inside its existing memory budget and disk spill.

> [!NOTE]
> An earlier version of this PR rewrote the query into `GROUP BY uuid, timestamp`. Materialization never spills a `GROUP BY` to disk, so large models would run out of memory.

## How did you test this code?

**Test rationale:** Tracker cases cover repeats in memory and on disk. One activity test sends a repeated uuid through both write paths, and fails without the dedup.

- The incremental activity, tracker and eligibility tests passed on the devbox. Not run: the rest of the backend suite.

<summary>Measured cost per 1M uuid keys</summary>

| Check | In memory | Spilled to disk |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Plain check | 0.08 s | 3.7 s |
| Dropping repeats | 0.14 s | 7.6 s |

</details>

👉 _Stay up-to-date with [PostHog coding conventions](https://posthog.com/docs/contribute/coding-conventions) for a smoother review._

## Problem

- Trace judges on agent runs answer N/A because they never see the task prompt ([thread](https://posthog.slack.com/archives/C087XQ7K9K7/p1795011878017719)).
- Each step resends the conversation, so the transcript overflows its 150,000-character budget.
- Every long message then keeps 1,000 characters, prompt included, with no sign on the result.

## Changes

- Judges see repeated messages once, as `[1-17] Same as messages 1-17 of the previous generation's input above`. Only equal messages collapse.
- The trace budget rises to 300,000 characters, falling back to 150,000 when the judge's context window rejects it.
- Results from a cut transcript set `$ai_evaluation_input_truncated: true`.
- Traces still over 150,000 characters after the collapse send up to twice the input tokens to the customer's judge key.

The judge call gains one fallback:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A[Render at 150k]:::phYellow --> B{{Judge}}:::phBlue --> C[Verdict or skip]:::phGray
  classDef phBlue fill:#1d4aff,stroke:#1d4aff,color:#fff;
  classDef phYellow fill:#f9bd2b,stroke:#f9bd2b,color:#000;
  classDef phGray fill:#e5e7eb,stroke:#c7ccd1,color:#000;
```

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A[Render at 300k]:::phYellow --> B{{Judge}}:::phBlue
  B -->|context window exceeded| D[Render at 150k]:::phYellow --> E{{Judge}}:::phBlue --> C[Verdict or skip]:::phGray
  B --> C
  classDef phBlue fill:#1d4aff,stroke:#1d4aff,color:#fff;
  classDef phYellow fill:#f9bd2b,stroke:#f9bd2b,color:#000;
  classDef phGray fill:#e5e7eb,stroke:#c7ccd1,color:#000;
```

## How did you test this code?

**Test rationale:**

- New tests fail if the collapse is off, a changed message collapses, or the context-window fallback retries wrongly.

## Problem

The web, mobile and desktop apps and the agent each bundle a copy of the task model catalog. A new model version needs that copy regenerated, and a desktop release, before a picker can show it. The backend no longer reads the catalog, so the copies can also disagree with it.

## Changes

- The catalog's model rows, price tables and effort tables are deleted. The generator now emits only choices: adapters, effort tiers, default models, slider rungs and the families a picker offers.
- Web and mobile read `GET /tasks/models/`. It now also returns each model's cost summary, whether pickers offer it and the cost baseline's name.
- Desktop and the agent read a model's adapter, name, efforts, context window and price from the gateway listing they already fetch. They offer the two newest versions of each allowed family, the rule the backend uses.
- The hand-kept fallbacks are deleted: the web and mobile effort fallback, mobile's retired-model list and the desktop loop picker's offline model list.

## Problem

The Setup tab (`products/autoresearch/frontend/pipeline/SetupTab.tsx`) shows the two things a new user most needs to read in forms they cannot read.

1. **Populations are raw JSON.** "Training population" and "Inference population" each print the stored definition, for example `{"days":14,"kind":"performed_event_within_days","event":"user signed up","properties":[...]}`. The create form already states the same thing as a sentence ("Predict who among ... will ... within the next ..."). When both populations are equal the JSON is printed twice. Horizon and lookback show as "7d" and "60d".
2. **The default research model reads as a surcharge.** The select shows "Default (Claude Opus 5.5) · 2× cost". The multiplier has no stated baseline, and it sits on the recommended option.
3. **No wording for being over the model limit.** A project above its limit sees "has {used} of {limit} active models" with the first number larger than the second, and no explanation. Pipelines already over the limit keep running, and only new ones are refused, but the page does not say so.

## Changes

Load `/writing-user-facing-copy` and `/writing-ui-components` first.

1. **Definition as a sentence.** Replace the target, horizon, lookback and population rows with one card, "What this model predicts":
   - Sentence: "Among {population}, who will do {target} within {horizon}?" Reuse the create form's population and target wording (`frontend/newModel/`, `frontend/pipelineQuestion.ts`) so the two cannot drift.
   - Rows under it: "Excluded" (property filters in words, for example "People whose email contains @example.com"), "Learns from" ("The last 60 days of outcomes"), "Scores" ("The same group, every day", or the inference population as its own sentence when it differs), "Created".
   - A "Show definition as JSON" toggle keeps the raw value available.

2. **Cost against the default.** State each option's cost relative to the default model: the default shows "(recommended)" and no multiplier; other options show "about {x}× the cost per run" computed from `cost_multiplier` divided by the default's. Same treatment for thinking effort.

- No JSON is visible on the Setup tab until the toggle is opened.
- A pipeline whose training and inference populations are equal states the population once.

## Problem

A model's adapter, name, reasoning efforts and cost are typed by hand in the task model catalog. Every new version also needs a catalog row before a product can call it or a picker can offer it. The gateway already serves all of this, and the copies have drifted ([thread](https://posthog.slack.com/archives/C0C1T3V1RJA/p1795056481045999), #132210).

## Changes

- The backend reads a model's adapter, name, reasoning efforts and cost multiplier from its gateway row. It reads no catalog row.
- Each agent product names the model families it allows. Its token pin is every version the gateway lists in those families, and its pickers offer the two newest of each.
- A short reserved list holds the exceptions: a trial model, and ids kept for the free tier and older desktop builds. No picker offers one.
- A row that says nothing about reasoning gets no effort picker, and an effort sent for it isn't refused. The gateway lists no reasoning for GLM-5.2 or GLM-5.3 Flash, and shipped desktop builds send efforts for both.
- While the listing can't be read, a family product's token mint fails as retryable. A workflow step is checked against every model its token admits.
- A live run keeps to the versions its token was minted with.
- Rollout flags are keyed by gateway family. Workflows and the run command's model switch now check them too.

Visible: backend pickers lose GPT-5, GPT-5.6 Sol, GPT-6 Sol, Claude Opus 4.8 and Claude Fable 5. Tokens can still call them, and also the older `gpt` versions the gateway lists (GPT-4.1, GPT-4o, GPT-5.1, GPT-5.2). GPT-5.6 cost multipliers drop. The Codex slider rungs move to GPT-6.2 Sol. The fixed pins for onboarding, conversations and the free tier are unchanged.

Trade-off: a trial model the gateway lists in an allowed family is admitted for every agent product unless it's reserved first.

This PR now includes #139330, which is closed.

## How did you test this code?

Every backend test gets a saved copy of the production listing. A snapshot records what each product's token may call and what its picker offers. Table tests cover the adapter rule, partial rows, the three reasoning states, the family rule, reservations, the run stamp, the flag checks and a listing outage at mint. ## Problem

Analysts must rerun a notebook and click **Replace rows** before downstream SQL sees fresh results. [#140517](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/pull/140517)

## Changes

An agent can now run a notebook between SQL models in PostHog’s warehouse DAG. For example, SQL totals sales, Python forecasts demand, and SQL lists items to reorder.

- **Declare** a table from a SQL or Python cell and name its upstream models.
- **Refresh** daily or on demand. Each run publishes the cell’s full dataframe.
- **Inspect** failed cells and the last published run. A failed refresh preserves the table and skips dependent SQL.

### Before

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A[Run notebook] --> B[Save or replace rows in browser] --> C[Warehouse table]
    classDef phYellow fill:#f9bd2b,stroke:#f9bd2b,color:#000;
    classDef phBlue fill:#1d4aff,stroke:#1d4aff,color:#fff;
    classDef phGray fill:#e5e7eb,stroke:#c7ccd1,color:#000;
    class A phYellow;
    class B phBlue;
    class C phGray;
```

### After

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A[SQL model: total sales by item] --> B[Notebook Python cell: forecast demand] --> C[demand_forecast table] --> D[SQL model: list items to reorder]
    classDef phYellow fill:#f9bd2b,stroke:#f9bd2b,color:#000;
    classDef phBlue fill:#1d4aff,stroke:#1d4aff,color:#fff;
    classDef phGray fill:#e5e7eb,stroke:#c7ccd1,color:#000;
    class A,D phYellow;
    class B phBlue;
    class C phGray;
```

<details>
<summary>Using the three MCP tools</summary>

Enable `notebook-warehouse-models` for MCP after the Django routes deploy.

| Tool | How to use it for the reorder report |
| --- | --- |
| `notebooks-declare-warehouse-model` | Choose the forecast cell, name its table `demand_forecast`, and pass the sales model’s node ID as an upstream dependency. |
| `notebooks-run-warehouse-model` | Start the model and its upstream dependencies now. After the first publication, reference `demand_forecast` in the downstream SQL model. |
| `notebooks-warehouse-model-status` | Pass the returned `dag_run_id` to see whether the run reached the notebook. Inspect cell errors and the run that produced the current table. |

Each run executes the saved notebook through the selected cell. First publication requires an unused table name. Later refreshes keep the table ID. Runs that share a notebook wait their turn, and previous generations remain readable for 24 hours.

</details>

## How did you test this code?

**Test rationale:** [Warehouse tests](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/blob/87e6096958bc3cec744ba3caafb234df509f0339/posthog/api/test/notebooks/test_warehouse_model.py#L217) cover replacement. [DAG tests](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/blob/87e6096958bc3cec744ba3caafb234df509f0339/products/data_modeling/backend/temporal/tests/test_execute_dag_workflow.py#L635) cover failure propagation.

<details>
<summary>CI advisories and regression coverage</summary>

The warehouse round trip read 14,000 synthetic rows on each of two refreshes. A failed third refresh preserved the second table. A local Temporal test used a stub notebook task to check dependency ordering.

The API test checks that the returned ticket identifies the queued Temporal run and that polling uses the same project, node, and ticket. The workflow tests exercise the receiver. Time-skipping tests cover a busy notebook, downstream failure, and delayed cleanup. A warehouse round trip reads both generations across replacement.

CI measured a 7.7 KiB decrease in total frontend bundle size. Of the two eager roots over budget, logged-out boot had zero growth and the authenticated shell grew 3.5 KiB against the CI baseline. The frontend diff only regenerates the notebook API. No browser code imports the new client functions or schemas. CI also shows changes in the Today sidebar chunks, outside this diff.

The database migration creates one table with a primary key on `node_id`, its node foreign key, and an index on `team_id`. The migration analyzer classified it as safe. Five Chromium cases passed on retry. Two exercise editing or deleting an ordinary notebook. The other three cover person properties, insight titles, and workflow secrets. None of the five exercises model declaration, DAG execution, or warehouse publication.

</details>

- This change is behind a feature flag and is not available to users <!-- release-status: behind-feature-flag -->

## Problem

- The Stripe source's payment-method tables make one `/v1/customers/:id/payment_methods` call per customer on every sweep, and most of those calls return nothing. This uses up our users' Stripe read allowance and rate limits.
- Stripe added a gated, undocumented `Customer.has_payment_method` field so we can skip those calls. Context: https://posthog.slack.com/archives/C09J981UHNX/p1794581786066459?thread_ts=1782323971.706099&cid=C09J981UHNX

## Changes

- When the `warehouse-stripe-has-payment-method` flag is on, the `CustomerPaymentMethod` and `CustomerPaymentMethodHistory` sweeps request `expand[]=data.has_payment_method` on their customer listing and skip customers whose value is exactly `false`. `true` and missing values still get the call, so no payment method is dropped.
- When Stripe refuses the expand (an account without access, or access removed mid-sweep), the sweep lists customers again without it. The new listing continues after the last customer already handled. One refusal stops the expand for the rest of the sync.
- The field is never stored, because only the payment-method rows are written. The `Customer` table never requests it.
- The flag is checked only for those two tables, and only when they poll the API.

## How did you test this code?

- New `TestPaymentMethodSweepHasPaymentMethodExpand` cases drive the source through `SourceDriver` against a scripted Stripe API.
- Ran the full Stripe test directory locally, including the object-storage tests against a moto S3 server.
- Not checked against the real Stripe API, because no test account has access yet.

**Test rationale:** The cases catch: skipping a customer whose value is not `false` (data loss), failing the sync or losing customers when Stripe refuses the expand on the first or a later page, sending the expand with the flag off, swallowing unrelated 400s, and storing the field. The nearest tests (`test_balance_history_switch_decides_which_customers_are_swept`, `TestStripeNestedResourceGetRows`) cover the balance-transaction skip only. Each new case fails when the line it guards is broken.

## Release status

- This change is behind a feature flag and is not available to users <!-- release-status: behind-feature-flag -->

## Docs update

- None. The behavior is internal, and the synced data does not change.

## 🤖 Agent context

**Autonomy:** Human-driven (agent-assisted)

**Agent:** Claude Code, Claude Opus 5.5 (claude-opus-5-5)

**Skills:** None invoked. The agent read the `writing-tests`, `writing-code-comments` and `routing-outbound-api-calls` skill files.

**Security review:** not needed

<details>
<summary>More context for AI agents</summary>

- **Decisions:** A team-level flag evaluated in `stripe_source` on the caller's thread, because the flag check reads the database.
- **Decisions:** The "not granted" result is not cached across syncs. Stripe asked for one refusal per sync at most.
- **Follow-ups:** Create the `warehouse-stripe-has-payment-method` flag in US and EU, then roll out with Stripe.
- **Read closely:** `_list_parents_with_gated_expand` and `_is_gated_expand_refused` in `stripe.py`.

## Problem

- Renaming a model breaks every model whose SQL reads it. The rename dialog only warns that their SQL is not updated.

## Changes

- Renaming a model that other models read now shows each one's SQL before and after, then rewrites them in the same change.
- `rename_plan` returns that plan and a token. `rename` applies it in one transaction, or changes nothing.
- A stale plan returns 409, an unrewritable model returns 400, and missing edit access on any of them returns 403.
- The rewrite splices the parsed query in place and adds no alias. Qualifiers like `old.id` change only in a `SELECT` that reads the model unaliased.
- Rewritten models keep their incremental state, so nothing rebuilds.
- A plain PATCH of the name still works when no model reads it.
- Saved joins that name the model, on either side, are renamed in the same transaction and listed in the plan.
- Before accepting a rewrite, the plan resolves each changed model against the renamed catalog and blocks it when a name would bind to something else.
- MCP gains `view-rename-plan` and `view-rename`.
- Mechanical: regenerated OpenAPI, frontend and MCP clients.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    actor U as You
    participant D as Rename dialog
    participant API as warehouse_saved_queries API
    participant P as Planner (model_rename)
    participant DB as Postgres
    U->>D: Type new name
    D->>D: Validate name as you type
    U->>D: Preview rename
    D->>API: POST rename_plan {name}
    API->>P: plan_model_rename
    P->>DB: Load model, readers, joins
    P->>P: Find, splice, prove, check bindings
    P-->>API: rewrites, blocked, joins, token
    API-->>D: Plan
    D->>U: Diffs, blocked list, joins
    U->>D: Rename and update N views
    D->>API: POST rename {name, plan_token}
    API->>P: apply_model_rename
    P->>DB: Lock rows in pk order
    P->>P: Recompute plan, compare token
    P->>DB: Write name, rewritten SQL, joins, activity log
    API-->>D: Renamed view
    D->>D: Reload views, schema, joins
```

![Rename dialog with a plan](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PostHog/pr-assets/71781670df37cca9606184cd39e33bcc6bfe6c13/2026/11/5446ab39-f754-454d-8432-5b61698344e3.png)

The SQL diff shows a spinner here because Monaco does not load in Storybook.

Not run: a manual rename in a running app.

## Problem

People who send workflow emails see the same preview text twice in Gmail when the email step's Preheader field and the editor's own preview text hold the same copy. Raised in the Slack thread linked below; no issue exists.

## Changes

- An email now shows its preview text once. The send step skips its Preheader span when a hidden element in the html already holds the same text.
- The match ignores case, whitespace and entity spelling. Hidden elements that hold other text or markup do not count, and visible text never counts.
- Mechanical: new `preheader.test.ts`. The size estimate in `ses-html-max-bytes.ts` still counts the span, so it stays an upper bound.

## Context

**Goal:** improve the default prompt, system prompt and detector behaviour that every user gets out of the box. These are changes to the defaults, not tuning for particular alerts.

The sampled alerts nearly all carry hand-written author instructions. Most users will not write any, so judge each change on alerts without instructions too.

We reviewed a week of AI detector checks on internal alerts before the wider rollout of `alerts-llm-detector`. Almost all checks are hourly, all of them run on one model, and none errored. Verdicts are mostly sensible. The items below are small, independent changes. Each one can ship as its own PR.

## 1. Write values as plain decimals

**Problem:** `prompt.py` formats values with `:g`. A count of 1,175,594 reaches the model as `1.17559e+06`, which drops the low digits and makes neighbouring values look identical.

**Change:** add a formatter that writes integers in full, rounds other values of 1 or more to two decimals, and writes small values positionally. Bump `PROMPT_REVISION`.

## 2. Bound the earlier-alerts block

**Problem:** the block lists one rationale for every flagged point in the window, so it grows with the fire rate. On the noisiest alerts it is about three quarters of the prompt. That raises cost, and a wall of earlier "anomaly" reasons pushes the model to flag again.

Two smaller defects in the same block:
- The 200-character cut lands mid-word ("so the elev").
- Old rationales quote values from the time of that check. Those values often no longer match the table, because buckets get revised.

**Change:**
- Keep the most recent N rationales (for example 5). Add a one-line summary such as "this alert flagged 42 of the 168 points in the window, most recently at <date>".
- Cut at a sentence or word boundary.
- Label the quoted numbers as the values at the time of that check.

## 3. Make sustained level shifts consistent

**Problem:** when a series moves to a new level and stays there for days, verdicts flip between `level_shift` and `none` from one hour to the next on the same state. One alert fired on most checks for days on a shift that started early in the window. A similar alert stopped firing on its shift after about a day.

The comparable-points line adds to this. With a 7-day hourly window, the "same weekday" value is the one point from before the shift, so it always reads as a 2-3x jump.

**Change:** decide what a check means during an ongoing shift, then say it in the prompt. Either it means "still anomalous", so it keeps firing and the alert state machine handles renotification, or it means "new or worsening", so it fires once and then only on a further move. Pass the alert's current firing streak as data. Add an eval case for a shift that holds for 1, 3 and 5 days.

## 4. Revisit the hourly lookback

**Problem:** `llm_detector_lookback("hour")` covers 7 days, so "same hour on the same weekday in earlier weeks" has at most one value. Weekly seasonality cannot be learned from that.

**Change:** try 14 days for hourly series. Item 2 frees enough tokens to pay for the extra rows. Compare verdicts on a labelled set before and after.

## 5. Skip re-checks of an unchanged point

**Problem:** about three quarters of hourly points are judged twice. The likely cause is a check cadence shorter than the bucket, but that is not confirmed. The second call sees the same series, give or take a few late events, and disagrees with the first call about 2% of the time. That costs twice as much and can flap.

**Change:** reuse the last verdict when the current point's date matches and the values in the window are within a small tolerance of the last check. The memo key covers `evaluation_id` today, so this needs a second, point-keyed lookup. Cost story: this removes roughly half of the model calls for hourly alerts.

## 6. Escape metadata without quote entities

**Problem:** `html.escape` runs with its default `quote=True`, so HogQL filters in the metric description reach the model as `"` and `'`.

**Change:** use `escape(..., quote=False)`. Only `<`, `>` and `&` matter for keeping data inside its tags. The existing tag-escape test still covers the injection case.

## Out of scope / later

- Measure whether the chart image changes verdicts. It is attached to every call. An ablation on a labelled set would tell us whether it pays for its tokens.

## Problem

- Destinations and workflows of an organization that staff deactivated keep running.
- #140265 dropped disabling them by hand: background work checks the organization at run time instead ([thread](https://posthog.slack.com/archives/C0CJM5RT3PE/p1795444549806499), [#project-deactivated-org](https://posthog.slack.com/archives/C0CKH2SFYSG)).

<!-- merge-risk -->
> [!NOTE]
> 🔵 **Merge risk: low**, 🟡 once the switch is on
> - Nothing changes on deploy: the switch defaults off, and the queries stay as they are.
> - With the switch on, every deactivated organization stops sending, including ones deactivated earlier.
> - **Switch-off:** `CDP_SKIP_DEACTIVATED_ORGANIZATIONS`, default off.
> - **Tier:** non-critical

## Rollout

- **Stages:** deploy the Node CDP services, then turn the switch on per region.
- **Decided:** 2026-11-24, the driver moved transformations to #140972 for the ingestion team.
- **Decided:** 2026-11-23, the driver accepted that queued runs of a deactivated organization end as they do for a deleted destination or workflow (see Known issues).
- **Watch:** `cdp_deactivated_organization_not_loaded`.
<!-- /merge-risk -->

## Changes

- The CDP stops loading the destinations and workflows of a deactivated organization. Every path that loads them finds nothing: event triggers, queued runs, webhooks, batch runs and backfills.
- Queued runs end the way they do for a deleted destination or workflow.
- Transformations keep loading here. #140972, stacked on this PR, covers them for the ingestion team.
- Legacy plugin configs and legacy Zapier action webhooks of a deactivated organization stop too. A hidden migrated destination does not fall back to its plugin config.
- Test invocations and the function status route find nothing for a deactivated organization. A test run of an unsaved function or workflow answers 403, because members of a deactivated organization can still reach the API with their session.
- A flip of `is_active` takes effect when the managers' caches refresh: about 2 minutes for workflows, up to about 6 for destinations, and up to about 10 for legacy plugin configs. Reactivation restarts them the same way.

## How did you test this code?

**Test rationale:** the manager tests deactivate an organization in Postgres and check what loads, with the switch on and off, and again after reactivation. Webhook, backfill, legacy plugin and legacy webhook tests go through the production wiring. Each fails with its filter removed.

- CI report, call assertions: the two lines in the legacy consumer test read the batch handler from the Kafka mock, as its neighbouring tests do. All four added lines, there and in the API and backfill tests, assert no outbound fetch, which is the delivery boundary.
- Not checked: a live run on a dev stack.

## Known issues

- major: `nodejs/src/cdp/services/hogflows/hogflow-manager.service.ts:274` A queued workflow run that wakes while its organization is deactivated is dequeued like a run of a deleted workflow, so its `running` row stays.
- major: `nodejs/src/cdp/services/managers/hog-function-manager.service.ts:236` A queued destination invocation that wakes while its organization is deactivated ends like one of a deleted destination, so it cannot be rerun after reactivation.

## Release status

## Problem

- Plain projections over events never get an incremental refresh suggestion, so each refresh rescans events ([#141674](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/issues/141674)).
- The key tracker checks about 84M event uuids per run. A bigger model would fail its first run.

Inbox: [step 1](https://us.posthog.com/project/2/inbox/reports/01a21014-0c68-7d35-8bb0-5fdf6fc5a9a8) of [this plan](https://us.posthog.com/project/2/inbox/reports/01a21010-3966-7e6f-bbb0-5c8efc8c93ae).

## Changes

- Suggestions can now propose incremental refresh for a plain event projection, keyed on its time column and `uuid`.
- The job first counts the model's rows with `LIMIT 40000001`. Over 40M rows, the suggestion stays a full refresh.
- 40M is half the measured ceiling, for growth and the shared spill disk.
- The count is `Workload.OFFLINE` work, limited to one per team run with a 15 s timeout. A finished count is cached for 7 days.
- This layer needs the layer below.

**Test rationale:** Proposal cases cover the new shape and the shapes that stay `None`. A ClickHouse candidate test checks both sides of the budget, and fails without the gate.

## Problem

A sync opens a fresh error tracking issue whenever its destination (a customer's Postgres or Redshift database) drops the connection and retries exhaust, though it is the destination's infrastructure, not a bug.

The source side already treats "server closed the connection unexpectedly" as expected, skipping error tracking. The destination path had no equivalent.

## Changes

- A destination connect that exhausts retries without a classified configuration problem stays out of error tracking; the run still fails with its actionable message.
- The shared batch consumer's "max retries exceeded" path also consults `is_expected_user_error`, applying classification regardless of retryability.

## Problem

- A cold dashboards v2 load spends most of each tile's time building the HogQL database, not in ClickHouse.
- Every target in one `query_batch` request rebuilt it from scratch, so teams with large data warehouses pay that cost once per tile.

## Changes

- Cold v2 boards build the HogQL database once per batch for targets that share its inputs, then share it.
- A batch-scoped registry in `posthog/hogql/database/request_scope.py` keys each build on team, user, access-control scope, normalized modifiers, connection and the other `create_for` inputs.
- Targets with different schema modifiers (new events engine, `personsOnEventsMode`, sessions version) or another user get their own database.
- One thread builds each key under a lock while the others wait. The registry dies with the batch, so no cross-request cache.
- Workers honour the existing `HOGQL_SHARED_INSIGHT_DATABASE_ENABLED` kill switch.
- Calls outside a batch scope are unchanged.

## Problem

People working out what a materialization run costs can see what ClickHouse read for it. They cannot see what the worker pulled over the network, what it wrote to object storage, or how long it held a worker slot. The need comes from the cost attribution work for data modeling.

## Changes

- Each ClickHouse materialization run now stores six numbers on its job row: response bytes received, Delta files and bytes written, live table files and bytes after the run, and activity seconds.
- The numbers sum over retries, and a failed or cancelled attempt still records them.
- Nothing user-visible changes. The jobs API and the HogQL system table do not expose the columns.
- The shared Arrow stream client takes an optional `on_bytes_received` callback that reports the response size on the wire.
- The migration adds six nullable columns with no backfill.
- An incremental run with several batches undercounts files that a later batch of the same run replaced.
- A failed incremental attempt records no writes.
- The workflow emits the same commands, so running executions replay unchanged.

## How did you test this code?

**Test rationale:** Three regressions, each seen to fail when its guarded line was broken.

- `TestRunUsage::test_a_retried_rebuild_carries_the_usage_of_both_attempts` fails if a retry overwrites the failed attempt's usage. It compares the job row with a listing of the object store. The closest test, `test_no_config_rebuilds_every_run`, asserts table content only.
- `TestRunUsage::test_an_incremental_run_counts_only_the_files_it_added` fails if an incremental run counts the whole table.
- `TestHogqlTableBytesReceived` fails if the callback stops reaching the client. It runs against real ClickHouse.
- `test_astream_query_as_arrow_raises_error_appended_to_stream` gained one assertion: the bytes of a response that fails still count in full.

These need real Delta tables and Postgres because the numbers come from delta-rs, deltalite and a database increment.

## Problem

- AI observability under-reports cost for OpenAI generations with prompts above 272K input tokens, such as GPT-6 Sol (#106645).
- OpenAI bills the whole request at 2x input and cache rates and 1.5x output above that threshold. The cost step only knew one long-context rule, for Gemini 2.5 Pro Preview.

Closes #106645

## Changes

- OpenAI generations above 272K input tokens now show long-context costs, and `$ai_model_cost_used` reads `<model>:large`.
- A per-model threshold table replaces the hard-coded Gemini rule. Gemini keeps its 200K threshold.
- New `:large` rows for 14 OpenAI models: standard, priority and flex rates, from the "Long" view of [OpenAI's pricing page](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/pricing).
- The OpenAI rows apply only when `$ai_provider` resolves to `openai`. Azure, Bedrock and OpenRouter stay flat, because their long-context rates are not published there.
- A name must end at the model or a dated snapshot, so `gpt-5.4-mini` and `gpt-6-sol-pro` keep their own prices.

- `cost-model-matching.test.ts`: `getNewModelName` cases at 272,000 and 272,001 tokens, snapshot names, excluded variants and non-OpenAI providers.
- `manual-providers.test.ts`: `processCost` for `gpt-6-sol` just under and over the threshold, on the standard, flex and priority tiers.
- `manual-providers.test.ts`: every `:large` route must equal 2x input and cache, 1.5x output of the same catalog route. A mistyped rate fails it.
- The new over-threshold cases failed on `master` (10 failures) and pass with the change. The AI cost and `process-ai-event` suites pass locally. ESLint, oxlint and Prettier are clean on the changed files.
- `tsc --noEmit` shows no errors in the changed files. The only errors come from workspace packages that were not built in this checkout.
- Not done: no run against live ingestion, and no check against a real OpenAI invoice.

**Test rationale:** The tests catch three regressions: an over-threshold OpenAI prompt that keeps the flat rate, a sibling model such as `-mini` or `-pro` that gets the wrong long-context rate, and a mistyped rate. The nearest existing tests are the Gemini `getNewModelName` cases, which these extend.

👉 _Stay up-to-date with [PostHog coding conventions](https://posthog.com/docs/contribute/coding-conventions) for a smoother review._

> **Blocked by #133436** (PR #133471). Start after it merges: this issue extends its served sources inputs.

## Problem

`nn_with_prio_ml_features_v1` is the sources recipe plus plain report facts as one-hot buckets: length, judgments, signal count, content counts and authorship, and creation time (`ReportEmbeddingsPriorityMLFeaturesFeatureSet` in `products/signals/backend/ranking/features.py`). Its first read in the experiment lane shows a gain on the `action` head. One partition is not a verdict, but the recipe should be ready to score live, so an online read can start as soon as the offline reads support it.

The sweep cannot build these inputs today:

- The set reads its facts from the state snapshot columns, and those exist only in the dataset.
- The sweep already reads the same facts for each report it scores (`read_report_facts` in `products/signals/backend/ranking/report_facts.py`, from #133435), but it only records them. It reads them after scoring, and no feature set receives them.

## Changes

1. **Build the fact columns from `ReportFacts` at scoring time.** When `as_of` is None, the set builds its `length`, `judgments`, `signals`, `content` and `timing` columns from the report's `ReportFacts` and the report's creation time in UTC. Training keeps reading the state columns. Both paths must go through one function per group that turns raw values into columns, so a bucket boundary cannot differ between training and serving.
2. **Give the scorer the facts before it scores.** When a loaded model's set needs the facts, read them before the feature build and pass them in. Keep one read per call: the recorded `inbox_ranking_report_facts_recorded` event must hold the same values the model read. A call with no such model keeps today's order and cost.
3. **Declare the facts as a served side input.** Extend `_served_extra` and the extras the scorer passes, in the way #133436 does for the sources, so the scorer knows which models need the facts.
4. **A model that cannot get its facts is skipped, not fed zeros.** When the facts read fails for a call, the model is skipped with a reason, as a model without its sources is, and the served model still scores. A null `actionability` or `already_addressed` gives all-zero columns, as in training. `content_recorded` is 1 whenever the facts were read.
5. **No family in this change.** The experiment keeps training as it does. A serving family follows in a separate issue.
6. **Docs.** Update `products/signals/dags/inbox_ranking/README.md` and the nearest `AGENTS.md` where they list the served side inputs.

## Acceptance criteria

- A parity test, parameterized: for the same raw facts, the serving row equals the training row in every group. Cover a value on each bucket boundary, null judgments, a report with no content, and each day-of-week and hour bucket edge.
- A scorer test: a pass whose facts read fails skips the model with a reason and still scores the served model.
- A scorer test: the recorded facts event carries the values the model read, from one read.
- The recipe hash of every existing family is unchanged, and `test_locations.py` passes.
- Importing the sweep still loads neither `onnxruntime` nor `xgboost`.

## Notes

- The facts read runs in the deployment's own region, so the EU mirror needs no new data.
- The facts of a report can change after its first score, and the sweep does not rescore for that. This is accepted for this recipe.
- The repo is public: no team counts, customer names or row volumes in the PR.

## Out of scope

- A serving family, and any promotion.
- Training on the facts recorded at scoring time.
- A rescore when a report's facts change.

## Problem

The activity summary MVP (#119839, #119919, shipped in #119884 and #120034) runs as an offline Dagster job over PostHog's own analytics data. It showed the summaries and their cost are workable, but it cannot become the feature:

- Its MCP input exists only as usage events in one internal analytics project, so it cannot run in-region for any other project.
- It stores summaries as Parquet partitions, not as state a product surface can read or update.
- It cannot run in a local dev stack, so iterating on the filters and the prompt needs a prod run.

The next step builds the core of the feature inside the signals product: one stored summary per (project, user), updated from in-region data, runnable locally from a command.

## Changes

New package `products/signals/backend/activity_summary/`. No new product. No schedule, endpoint or MCP tool in this issue.

### 1. Move the reusable code, then retire the Dagster package

Move these from `products/signals/dags/inbox_ranking/activity_summary/` into the new package: `render.py` and `prompt.py`, the `summarize` and `cost_usd` logic from `summaries.py`, and the input readers `member_tasks` and `member_activity` (with `TASK_ORIGIN_PRODUCTS`) from `dag.py`.

Then delete the Dagster activity summary pipeline. It was an offline MVP, and this package replaces it:

- the `products/signals/dags/inbox_ranking/activity_summary/` package, including its MCP event queries, the cost projection, and the summaries and embeddings assets
- the `activity_summary_job` and `activity_summary_schedule` registration in `posthog/dags/locations/signals.py`
- the activity summary section of `products/signals/dags/inbox_ranking/README.md`
- `products/signals/dags/inbox_ranking/tests/test_activity_summary.py`, after moving the tests that cover the moved code into the new package

The MCP-specific rendering (`McpCall`, `McpSession`, `mcp_unit`, `job_intents` and the MCP drop rules) has no caller once the Dagster package is gone, so drop it too. Git history keeps it for when an in-region MCP source exists. Leave the Parquet partitions the job already wrote in object storage as they are.

### 2. Inputs: tasks and the activity log, in-region only

For one (team, user) and a time window:

- **Tasks:** `list_user_task_summaries` from `products/tasks/backend/facade/user_task_summaries.py`, with the origin products and drop rules the Dagster inputs already use.
- **Activity log:** `ActivityLog` rows for the user in the team, with the existing filters (no `is_system`, no impersonated rows, no `scout:` clients, the tag and auto-named drops).
  - Also read the agent intent at `detail.trigger.payload.intent`. Since #100741 the MCP server sends it with every write it makes, and the activity log stores it on the row. Render it next to the changed object, for example `updated insight "Signup funnel" (agent: <intent>)`, through the same `clean_text` and per-line caps as other free text.
- **No MCP usage events.** Read-only MCP sessions stay out until an in-region source exists.

### 3. Hardening, applied in the moved code

1. **Redact URLs to their host.** `clean_text` strips query strings and fragments, but a secret can sit in a URL path. Replace every full URL with its host, for example `[link example.com]`. Add an invented path secret to the golden fixtures for each input source.
2. **Cap the completion.** Set `max_completion_tokens` from a named constant (around 600). Treat a truncated answer (`finish_reason == "length"`) as malformed, so the existing retry and `failed` paths handle it. Also cap the length of each focus area topic, product and `recent_shift` in `normalize_summary`.
3. **Unknown usage is null, not zero.** When a response has no `usage`, `tokens_in`, `tokens_out` and `cost_usd` are null.

### 4. Model

`UserActivitySummary` in the signals models, team-scoped with `TeamScopedRootMixin`, unique on (team, user). Follow `/django-migrations`.

- **Output:** `summary` (JSON), `summary_text`, `generated_at`, `model`, `prompt_version`, `render_version`
- **Accounting:** `tokens_in`, `tokens_out`, `cost_usd` (all nullable), `inputs_used` (JSON: line counts per section and drop counts per rule)
- **State:** `status` (`ok`, `failed`), `input_watermark` (the newest input timestamp included), `next_eligible_at`
- **Cascades:** deleting the user or the team deletes the row.

No embedding column and no version table in this issue.

### 5. `update_activity_summary(team_id, user_id, *, dry_run=False)`

One update for one (team, user). A command, a later Temporal workflow and the tests can all call it.

1. Skip if the organization has not approved AI data processing, or if `next_eligible_at` is in the future (unless forced).
2. Gather inputs since `input_watermark`. On a first run, gather the last 28 days.
3. If fewer than `MIN_UNITS` (3) units survive the filters, stop and write nothing.
4. Render the input and call the model once through `build_openai_client(product="signals", ai_product="activity_summary", ...)` from `posthog/llm/gateway_client.py`, with the stored summary as the previous summary. Model `gpt-6-luna`. Pass a fixed pipeline distinct id as both `distinct_id` and `user=`. Do not set `$ai_`-prefixed property keys.
5. On success, save the output and accounting, advance `input_watermark`, and set `next_eligible_at` to one day later. On failure, set `status = failed`, record the error, and leave the stored summary and the watermark unchanged.
6. Return a frozen result with the rendered input, the summary, the accounting and the drop counts.

With `dry_run=True`, nothing is written.

### 6. Management command

`run_activity_summary --team-id N --user-id N [--dry-run] [--force]`. It prints the rendered input, the summary, the token counts, the cost and the drop counts per rule. This is the local dogfood loop for the filters and the prompt.

## Acceptance criteria

- The golden-fixture tests for the task and activity log drop rules and rendering move with the code and still pass.
- The Dagster activity summary package, its job and schedule, and its README section are gone. Nothing imports from `products/signals/dags/inbox_ranking/activity_summary`, and `check-dagster-paths.py` passes.
- New tests, with the LLM mocked at the boundary (follow `/writing-tests`):
  - a secret in a URL path never reaches the rendered input
  - a truncated completion is retried, then recorded as `failed`
  - missing usage gives null tokens and cost
  - an activity log row with an agent intent renders it, and one without an intent renders as before
  - fewer than `MIN_UNITS` units writes nothing
  - a successful update advances the watermark, and a failed one does not
  - `dry_run` writes nothing
- The command runs against a local dev stack with a configured gateway.
- No text other than the rendered input reaches the model.

## Out of scope

The daily schedule and per-user workflow, the feature flag, embeddings, the `activity summary generated` event, the read endpoint, the MCP tool, opt-out, and an in-region source for read-only MCP sessions. These are follow-up issues.

## Problem

## Problem - Teams with business data in the warehouse find a revenue or order drop only when someone opens a chart, then slice it by hand to find the segment behind it. No scout explains a move in business data. ## Changes - A canonical scout, Business metrics, files Inbox reports such as "Net revenue down 22%, 80% from the EU Pro plan", each with three charts: the series with its baseline, the change by the driver dimension, and the series by that dimension. - It watches approved data catalog metrics from two sources: warehouse-backed SQL metrics, and insight-backed metrics read through the typed query runner. A SQL metric computed over raw `events` on the fly is out of scope; a materialized view over events is in. Detection on saved insights that are not metrics stays with the anomaly-detection scout; this scout explains a flagged move and edits that scout's report with the driver table. - Each measure passes four gates: the source is fresh, the series moved against a trend-adjusted baseline at its own grain (daily, weekly, monthly, quarterly), one or two segments explain at least 60% of the move (or the move is broad and large), and findings that share a segment, a mechanism or an onset are joined into one story report. - A metric owner steers the driver analysis with a dimension hint left as a scout note; the scout profiles columns only when no hint exists. - A bundled `scripts/lens.py` (pure stdlib, JSON in and out, batch mode) computes every verdict, so the model feeds rows and reads results. - A query budget bounds each run: 40 query calls, bounded windows, cache-first and incremental series reads, profiles per table, and a size tier that refuses raw scans of very large tables. The pre-check reads `system.information_schema.metrics`, so a project with no approved metric never starts a run. - One structured-output record per judged series, so precision and recall are readable from `$scout_structured_output` events. - Mechanical: the fleet roster entry, the architecture tree, and the canonical-set lock test. One measure through the gates: ```mermaid flowchart TD P[a measure due this run]:::phYellow --> G1[gate 1: is the source fresh?

## Problem

The AI judge that confirms z-score flags (#140449, #140500) can reach only the projects listed by id in the `anomaly-scoring` payload. Three things stop it from becoming the default for every scored project.

- **No rollout lever.** `ai_judge.team_ids` is the only way to pick `default-v2`. There is no percentage and no "all projects" setting, unlike scoring itself (`self_driving_organization_percentage`).
- **A profile change discards the stored models.** `load_states` in `products/signals/backend/anomaly_scores/state.py` keeps a state row only when its `profile` equals the insight's resolved profile. A project that moves from `default-v1` to `default-v2` therefore has no state, and every insight goes back to a train step. The local part of `default-v2` is `default-v1`, so the stored models are still valid. A fleet rollout would queue a first train for every scored insight at once.
- **Every score step fetches the full training history.** In `scoring.py`, a profile with an AI member raises `history` to `history_buckets(scoring)` on every score step, so the judge has context. Most score steps flag nothing and make no model call, so the larger query is wasted. This removes much of the saving of the train and score split.

## Changes

1. **A rollout lever for the judge.** Add `ai_judge.organization_percentage` (0 to 100) to the payload. A project scores with `default-v2` when its id is in `team_ids`, or its organization is inside the percentage. Use the same fixed bucket per organization as `organization_rollout_bucket`, so an organization keeps its place as the percentage grows. Add `ai_judge.skip_team_ids` to keep one project on `default-v1`. Per-deployment overrides must keep working, as they do for the other keys.
2. **Stored models survive the profile change, in both directions.** A state row trained under `default-v1` is read by `default-v2`, and the reverse, when the local part of the two profiles has the same identity. Proposed: key the state row by the local part (a model profile name that both profiles share), not by the profile name that the events carry. `plan_run` and `score_ready_by_insight` then return a score step for these insights. Events still record the real profile and detector version.
3. **History is fetched only when the judge needs it.** A score step fetches the same buckets as `default-v1`. When at least one new bucket is flagged and a model call is allowed by the caps, it fetches the judge's history for that insight, then calls the judge. A score step with no flagged bucket runs the same queries as `default-v1`. Count the second fetch in the pick's query cost and CPU spend.
4. **Telemetry to read the rollout.** The tick event reports how many scored projects resolved to `default-v2`. The pick event reports whether the judge's history was fetched.

## Out of scope

- Any change to the judge prompt or its verdicts, including repeated flags for one episode across runs.
- Showing the judge's rationale in the Anomalies tab or in anomaly search.
- Sparse series and data gaps (#138647).

## Acceptance

- With `ai_judge.organization_percentage` at 100 and an empty `team_ids`, every scored project resolves to `default-v2`. At 0 only `team_ids` do. A project in `skip_team_ids` stays on `default-v1` in both cases.
- An insight with a current `default-v1` model gets a score step, not a train step, on its first visit after its project moves to `default-v2`. The same holds when the project moves back.
- A `default-v2` score step with no flagged bucket issues the same queries as a `default-v1` score step for the same insight.
- A `default-v2` score step with a flagged bucket gives the judge as much history as a train step does.
- The caps per insight per run and per project per day still hold, and a project without AI data processing consent still makes no model call.
- A project on `default-v1` scores exactly as before.

Refs #140449.

## Problem

- Layers 1 to 3 (#134629, #134630, #134631) can read a Trino copy of a view, but nothing writes one. Layer 4 is blocked on a question that this sandbox cannot answer.
- No issue states this. It comes from the plan for "Trino builds a view's table, ClickHouse serves it".

## Changes

- Adds `DATA_MODELING_TRINO_OUTPUT_BUCKET_URL`, empty by default, so the path stays off until infrastructure sets it.
- Adds `trino_output_folder`, which returns `<url>/org_<id>/team_<id>/<view>/<run>/`, one folder per run, or `None` when the setting is empty.
- Nothing calls it yet. The Trino write, the table registration and the raw Trino materialize flag are not in this PR.

## Open question: can Trino write Parquet to a ClickHouse-readable prefix?

I could not resolve it here, so this PR stops. Trino is hosted by the control plane. A minted service credential names one catalog per organization, the DuckLake one. The repo has no Trino in the dev stack and no Hive or Iceberg catalog configuration. `docs/internal/hogql-trino-compiler.md` says catalog naming and grants belong to the control plane. These options are unverified:

- **DuckLake `CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE` (today):** DuckLake picks the data path and file names, so a per-run folder is not possible. ClickHouse cannot read that bucket. Replaced files may stay until cleanup, so a glob could double count.
- **Hive catalog with `external_location` and `format = 'PARQUET'`:** writes to a chosen prefix. It needs a Hive catalog, a grant on the output bucket, and non-managed table writes enabled. File names carry no `.parquet`, so ClickHouse needs an explicit format.
- **Iceberg catalog with `location`:** adds metadata and old snapshot files to the prefix.
- **`INSERT` into a registered location:** same catalog need as Hive.

To decide, the control-plane owners need to say which catalogs exist, whether the service credential can write the bucket, whether per-run prefixes work, and who removes old run folders.

Also open:

- The materializer compiles HogQL to Trino. There is no raw Trino SQL path, so `RAW_TRINO_MATERIALIZE_REASON` stays.
- When to export only for ClickHouse readers is undecided. While flagged, every Trino materialization of a flagged team would write the copy.
- An endpoint that reads a raw Trino view cannot be materialized on ClickHouse.

## How did you test this code?

`test_trino_output.py`, run locally with no database. No Trino or S3 was available, so I ran no write.

**Test rationale:** the layout is the contract that infrastructure and the read side share. The test fails if the empty setting stops disabling the copy, or if the org and team segments move.

## Problem

Ordered funnels drop users whose events arrive out of order: a slow request stores step one after step two, which the device captured later (#98250).

## Changes

- New `funnelUseClientCaptureOrder` modifier, off by default, orders funnel steps by the device's capture time (`$client_capture_time`, recorded by #103264).

Autoresearch backlog ids: A136 (PR 1) and A137 (PR 2). Related: A119 (#126759), A120 (#130498), A131 (#133077), A12.

Deliver this as a stack of two PRs. PR 1 is the base and is useful without PR 2. Use `/stacking-prs`.

## Problem

Autoresearch training borrows the PostHog Desktop rules to decide who may start a run. Those rules answer a Desktop question, how an organization pays for Desktop, and they give the wrong answer for autoresearch.

Two paths start a training run, and both call the Tasks gates:

- `start_training` in `products/autoresearch/backend/presentation/views/views.py` calls `code_access_required_response` and `usage_limit_response`.
- `_tasks_gate` in `products/autoresearch/backend/temporal/workflows.py` calls `get_desktop_access_decision` and `task_run_usage_limited` before the daily sweep starts a run.

So autoresearch refuses a training run when any of these is true:

- The organization is on a startup program, or has pending or active prepaid credits (`_funding_decision` in `products/tasks/backend/access.py`).
- Desktop signups are paused for the person.
- The organization is over its Desktop credit budget.

None of these is an autoresearch concern. Training does not bill the organization: the profile in `products/autoresearch/backend/task_profiles.py` sets `billing_product="background_agents"` and `bills_compute=False`. Autoresearch already has its own access flag (`backend/access.py`) and its own per-project limits (`backend/limits.py`).

What a person sees today:

- An organization on a startup program has access to the product, creates a model, and every training start returns HTTP 403. The message names PostHog Desktop and tells the person to select another organization.
- The model page shows only "Could not start training run". The gate puts its message in the `error` field, and `startTrainingFailure` in `products/autoresearch/frontend/autoresearchPipelineLogic.ts` reads `detail`.
- The `autoresearch model action failed` event records the HTTP status only, so the reason is not visible in analytics.
- For the same organization, the sweep skips scheduled training with the reason `PostHog Desktop access: startup_plan`, and nothing shows that in the product.

When the Desktop credit budget goes, autoresearch has no dollar limit of its own. Its limits count runs, iterations and live models. PR 2 adds the dollar limit.

## PR 1: autoresearch decides who may start a training run

1. **One launch gate that autoresearch owns.** Add one function in `products/autoresearch/backend/` that returns why a training run may not start, or nothing. Both `start_training` and the sweep kickoff call it. It checks only:
   - The organization is active and is not pending deletion.
   - The person has autoresearch access (`has_autoresearch_access`).
   - The per-project limits in `limits.py`, as today.

   `_sweep_access_block` already holds the first two checks for the sweep. Reuse it or move it; do not write the rules twice.
2. **Remove the Desktop rules from both paths.** Delete the `code_access_required_response` and `usage_limit_response` calls from `start_training`, and the `get_desktop_access_decision` and `task_run_usage_limited` calls from `_tasks_gate`. Rename `_tasks_gate` if its name is no longer true. Keep the rule that the creator of a pipeline must still have access to the team.
3. **Keep refusing a deactivated organization on `/train`.** Check whether the viewset's permissions already refuse it. If they do not, refuse it in the launch gate with a response that carries a `detail`.
4. **Show the reason for a refusal.** `startTrainingFailure` shows `detail`, then `error`, then the generic message. The other places that start training (the list card, the create form) do the same.
5. **Record the reason.** The `autoresearch model action failed` event for `train` keeps `status` and gains `error_code` when the response body has a `code`. Do not rename the event or its existing properties.
6. **Correct the documents.**
   - The `403`, `429` and `503` descriptions on `start_training` no longer name PostHog Desktop. Load `/improving-drf-endpoints` first and regenerate with `hogli build:openapi`.
   - Check the `autoresearch-train-create` tool description in `products/autoresearch/mcp/tools.yaml`.
   - `products/autoresearch/AGENTS.md` (Feature flag and access), `backend/temporal/AGENTS.md` (the kickoff paragraph that says kickoff applies the Tasks entitlement and usage gates) and `backend/presentation/AGENTS.md`.

Make the sweep change inside the activity. The coordinator workflow's command sequence must not change.

Tests (load `/writing-tests` first, and extend the existing tests for `start_training` and for kickoff):

## Feature request

Let a user pick which model the AI detector uses (the `llm` detector type on insight alerts), per alert. Start with two models only:

| Shown as | Model id | Provider | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Claude Haiku 5.5 | `claude-haiku-5-5` | Anthropic | The default, and what every AI alert uses today |
| GPT-6 Luna | `gpt-6-luna` | OpenAI | New for this detector |

### Why

The AI detector runs on one hard-coded model, `LLM_DETECTOR_MODEL = "claude-haiku-5-5"` in `products/alerts/backend/judge/llm.py`. A user whose metric is judged badly by that model has no second option, and we have no way to learn which model users prefer for which metrics.

#130917 proposed a model registry with shadow calls and was parked until someone asked for a per-alert model choice. This issue is that request, without the shadow part.

### Where the code is

- The judge is Anthropic-only: `build_ai_gateway_anthropic_client`, then `messages.parse(output_format=LLMDetectionVerdict)` with `thinking` disabled (`products/alerts/backend/judge/llm.py`).
- The chart is sent as an Anthropic base64 `image` block (`products/alerts/backend/judge/prompt.py`).
- The detector config has one field, `instructions` (`LLMDetectorConfig` in `frontend/src/queries/schema/schema-general.ts`).
- The API validates the config in `products/alerts/backend/presentation/views/alert.py`. The Max tool in `products/alerts/backend/max_tools.py` is the second writer.
- The editor renders the instructions field in `products/alerts/frontend/views/DetectorSelector.tsx`.
- Read `products/alerts/AGENTS.md` first. Its cost and gating rules all still apply.

### Proposal

**Config and API**

- [ ] Add an optional `model` to `LLMDetectorConfig`, an enum of exactly `claude-haiku-5-5` and `gpt-6-luna`. A config with no `model` means Haiku, so existing alerts need no migration and do not change behavior.
- [ ] Reject any other value with a 400 in the API validator. The Max tool goes through the same validation.
- [ ] Simulate takes the same field, so a preview runs on the model the alert will use.
- [ ] Regenerate the schema and OpenAPI types (`hogli build:openapi`), and update the MCP tool descriptions for alert create, update and simulate, plus `products/alerts/skills/authoring-insight-alerts/SKILL.md`.

**Judge**

- [ ] Replace the single constant with a small registry keyed by model id. Each entry holds the provider, how the client is built, how the chart image is encoded, and how structured output is requested and parsed into `LLMDetectionVerdict`.
- [ ] Add the OpenAI path through the AI gateway. Send the chart as an image data URL. Keep the same `SYSTEM_PROMPT`, `PROMPT_REVISION` and `ai_product` (`alert_llm_detector`).
- [ ] Keep every guard on both paths: the access check, the AI credit budget check, the `X-PostHog-Billable` and `X-PostHog-Privacy-Mode` headers, the gateway credit-refusal handling, the model-call slot, the request timeout and the single in-request retry.
- [ ] The OpenAI call must be attributed and charged to the alert's team, the same as the Anthropic call is through `team_id` today.
- [ ] Use the alert's model in the verdict memo key and in `SeriesJudgment.model`, in place of the constant, so each check records the model that produced it.
- [ ] The Haiku quirks stay on the Haiku entry only (no sampling params, `thinking` disabled). Do not copy them to the OpenAI entry.

**Editor**

- [ ] Add a model select to the AI detector section, next to the instructions field. Default to Claude Haiku 5.5.
- [ ] Show the model on each AI check in the alert history, because an alert's model can change during its life.
- [ ] Follow `/writing-user-facing-copy` for the label and help text.

**Docs and rules**

- [ ] Update the comment on `LLM_DETECTOR_MODEL` and `products/alerts/AGENTS.md`, which both say the model is not exposed per alert.
- [ ] Add the cost story that `AGENTS.md` asks for: calls per check stay at one, so only the price per call changes with the model.

### Constraints

- Two models only. No free-text model id, and no frontier models.
- One model call per check, as today. No shadow call and no fallback from one model to the other. A check that cannot reach a verdict records an error.
- The feature stays behind `alerts-llm-detector`, with the same per-project cap, cadence rules and AI data processing consent check.
- The new OpenAI call site must pass `.semgrep/rules/security/` (see the OpenAI HIPAA-eligible endpoints rule).
- Changing the model on an existing alert does not clear its earlier flags. The prompt still marks the points that earlier AI checks fired on, whichever model produced them.

### Acceptance

- A new AI alert with no model chosen runs on `claude-haiku-5-5`, and an alert saved before this change behaves exactly as it did.
- An alert saved with `gpt-6-luna` is judged by that model on scheduled checks and in simulate. Its check metadata and its `$ai_generation` event both name that model.
- `detector_config: {"type": "llm", "model": "anything-else"}` is rejected on create, update and simulate.
- With the rollout flag off, or with AI credits exhausted, a `gpt-6-luna` alert pauses the same way a Haiku alert does.
- Tests cover: the default, the rejected value, the OpenAI verdict parsing, the memo key changing with the model, and the paused paths on the OpenAI entry.

### Open questions

- Does the organization's AI data processing consent already cover sending alert data to OpenAI, or does the picker need to say which provider each model uses?
- Do the two models cost a similar number of AI credits per check? If not, the editor should say so next to the select.
- Should the allowed models also be listed in the `alerts-llm-detector` flag payload, so one model can be turned off without a deploy? If so, an alert on a model that is turned off should pause (`LLMDetectorPausedError`), not be disabled.

### Out of scope

- Shadow calls and model comparison (#130917).
- A project-level or organization-level default model.
- More than two models.

## Problem

- This PR supersedes #99073, on top of #97761, #97762 and #99037.

- Expanding the bar shows the plan: each scan with its size, its property filters and what each skips, then the join.
- A new `explain-sql` MCP tool returns the same plan without running the query.
- A read the estimate cannot follow, such as a subquery in WHERE, shows as not counted.
- Statistics lookups share one five-second budget.
- Mechanical: regenerated schema, OpenAPI clients and MCP tool schemas.

- Comment density (5%): the comments state estimator assumptions. Left for the reviewer to judge which to cut.
- Backend coverage (93%): most uncovered lines are failure fallbacks in `metadata.py`, `estimate.py` and `statistics.py`. No test was added only to raise coverage.
- Playwright: "Add a new person property" is flaky and unrelated.

</details>

## Problem

- The image export renderer checks only the URL it opens.

## Changes

- Every browser request and WebSocket goes through the existing network check. The instance origin is always allowed.
- A disallowed request is aborted. Exports of allowed pages look the same.
- A redirect hop to a disallowed address fails the export, because Playwright does not route redirect hops.
- Service workers are blocked, because their requests skip the routes.

- A local Chromium run blocked a redirect, a frame navigation and a WebSocket to a disallowed address.
- Not run: the database-backed export suites, because the sandbox has no database.

**Test rationale:** new cases catch a check that admits internal addresses, and a screenshot after a disallowed redirect.

## Release status
