## Problem Every pull request that touches the MCP service waits for a Rust build that recompiles the whole dependency tree, and MCP's `Integration Tests` is the workflow that ends the lane for 8 of the last 40 merged pull requests. Its `Build Rust flags service` step takes a median 175s over 8 recent runs, and it is the longest branch of the `parallel:` block that gates everything after it. `rust-cache` restores `target/` on every one of those runs and cargo still starts from scratch, so the cache is present but useless here. `ci-rust.yml` and `ci-nodejs.yml` already build the same tree through sccache against Depot's shared WebDAV cache: a recent `ci-rust.yml` build was 166 cache hits, 0 misses, 93s of wall clock. ## Changes The MCP integration-test job compiles through sccache under the same `Cargo.lock`-hash key prefix the other Rust workflows use, and prints its numeric counters after the build so any run shows the hit rate. Before: ```mermaid flowchart LR A[cargo build] --> B[rust-cache target/
restores, objects stale] B --> C[every crate recompiles
175s median] C --> D[Start Rust flags service] classDef hot fill:#F54E00,stroke:#F54E00,color:#fff classDef cold fill:#1D4AFF,stroke:#1D4AFF,color:#fff class B,C hot class A,D cold ``` After: ```mermaid flowchart LR A[cargo build] --> B[sccache lookup
Cargo.lock key prefix] B -->|hit| D[Start Rust flags service] B -->|miss, once per lockfile| C[compile and store
in Depot WebDAV cache] C --> D classDef hot fill:#F54E00,stroke:#F54E00,color:#fff classDef cold fill:#1D4AFF,stroke:#1D4AFF,color:#fff class B,C hot class A,D cold ``` Measured on this branch's own runs of `ci-mcp.yml` and on the runs around them: | Measurement | Before | After (warm cache) | | --- | --- | --- | | `Build Rust flags service` | 175s median, n=8 | **114s and 120s**, n=2 | | `Integration Tests` job wall | 540s median, n=19 | **479s and 509s**, n=2 | | sccache counters | not used | 2117 hits, 2 misses, 147 non-cacheable, of 2406 requests | The build step is the branch of the `parallel:` block that gates the rest of the job, so its saving is the job's saving until the next-longest branch, `Run Django migrations` at 81-93s, catches up. The job wall is a 2-sample result, so treat 540s → 479-509s (-6% to -11%) as indicative rather than settled; the build step's -33% is the number with a real before sample behind it. The before sample is the 19 successful `Integration Tests` jobs created between 05:20 and 07:18 UTC today, excluding this branch's own runs, so it is the same hour of the same day on the same runner labels. The first run on a new `Cargo.lock` pays for the misses: that run took 247s, +72s over the median, and filled the cache for every run after it. `rust/Cargo.lock` changed in 42 commits over the last 30 days, so that cost lands about once a day against a saving on every pull request. The `RUSTFLAGS: '-C debug-assertions=no'` on this build keys its objects separately from the release builds in `ci-rust.yml`, so nothing here can serve a release build a debug object. ## How did you test this code? The measurement is this branch's own CI, which is the evidence the numbers above come from: - Cold cache, first run: [run 45771146867 attempt 1](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/actions/runs/45771146867/attempts/1) — 247s build, 462 hits / 1657 misses. - Warm cache, re-run: [attempt 3](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/actions/runs/45771146867/attempts/3) — 120s build, 2117 hits / 2 misses, `Integration Tests` green in 479s. - Warm cache, re-run: [attempt 4](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/actions/runs/45771146867/attempts/4) — 114s build, same counters, `Integration Tests` green in 509s. Local checks: - `hogli` workflow linter: 15 checks passed across 159 workflows. - `cd tools/workflow-plan && npx vitest run`: 623 tests passed, so the job graph and the `parallel:` block are unchanged. Not checked here: this environment cannot build the Rust tree or the dev stack, so the compile itself was only exercised by CI. **Test rationale:** No unit test can observe a compiler cache. The closest existing coverage is the workflow-plan suite, which asserts this file still parses into the expected job graph, and it is the level this change belongs to: two added steps that write env and PATH, with the build command untouched. The hit-rate counters in the log are the regression signal if the cache ever stops working. ## Release status - No feature flag controls this change ## Docs update - None. `docs/internal/ci-things-already-tried.md` records attempts that were reverted or closed, and this one has not been tried in this workflow before. ## 🤖 Agent context **Autonomy:** Fully autonomous **Agent:** Shelley, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash (`deepseek-flash` platform alias) **Skills:** `/authoring-ci-workflows`, `/writing-pr-descriptions` **Driver checked:** No human driver **Security review:** not needed
More context for AI agents - **Session:** nightly CI-speed run, `gh` and the GitHub API for job timings and step profiles. - **Decisions:** Reused the existing `.github/actions/setup-sccache` composite and the `SCCACHE_WEBDAV_KEY_PREFIX=cargo-` convention rather than inventing a key, so this build shares objects with the other Rust workflows. - **Decisions:** Kept `rust-cache`; sccache sits on top of the restored `target/` and only removes the recompile, and the observed warm-cache build is faster with both than either alone would be. - **Decisions:** Added only the numeric counter lines to the log, not `sccache --show-stats` in full, because the full report prints the WebDAV endpoint and token. - **Follow-ups:** The same cold-build pattern exists in `ci-rust-flags-integration.yml`'s `Build Rust services` step, which also has no sccache. - **Read closely:** the key-prefix step must stay before `Install sccache`; the composite sets `RUSTC_WRAPPER` in `GITHUB_ENV` and reads the prefix at server start.

## Problem

- Teams want to send a push notification to one person from their backend, the way they already can with transactional email. The send API in #134034 needs a CDP route to run the push.
- This is the Node half of that stack. It lives in its own PR because the merge queue keeps Node and Python changes in separate lanes.

## Changes

- New CDP route `POST /api/projects/:team_id/hog_flows/:id/transactional_push`. It runs a transactional push's workflow once for one distinct ID, with the caller's `message_data` as variables.
- Django calls it with a token signed with a key only push uses, `WORKFLOWS_TRANSACTIONAL_PUSH_JWT_SECRET`. The email key can't send a push, and the push key can't send an email.
- A token sends to one person, once. A copied token can't be used again or for someone else. If Redis can't record the use within 2 seconds, the send is refused.
- Until `WORKFLOWS_TRANSACTIONAL_PUSH_JWT_SECRET` is set on `cdp-api` and in Django, every push send returns 503.
- A push's data is encrypted whenever `CDP_SEALED_STATE_KEYS` is set, like a transactional email's.
- Without that key, a push marked sensitive gets a 503 and can be sent again. Nothing is queued. It never goes out unencrypted.
- The route refuses a workflow that is off, sends something other than a push, or is over its quota. An `Idempotency-Key` makes a retry return the first send. The intake consumer stores the key with the run, as for transactional email, so two sends with one key at once still send once. The second one can answer 202 in place of 422 when the data differs and both arrive at once. The stored key is a keyed hash, so a login code in the data can't be guessed from it. A retry while the workflow is off gets 400 `transactional_push_paused` from the send API.
- Fixed: a workflow with an API trigger removes the person's properties, so a send key can't read person data through a template. That also removed the device tokens a push step needs, so every push was skipped. The push step now keeps only the device token properties.
- An email send now works when its workflow also has a push step. Only a workflow that sends nothing but pushes is refused. Device tokens go only to a push send of a push-only workflow, so an email send key can't reach them, also when the push step names someone else.
- The workflow worker now counts the `triggered` metric for API runs on any queue, not only the email queue.
- Every push goes through its own Kafka topic, `cdp_intake_transactional_push`, and its own consumer, `cdp-intake-transactional-push`. This follows #141175, which did the same for email. A push backlog never delays transactional email.
- When Kafka is down the send gets a 503 and can be sent again. When the job database is down, the push waits in Kafka.
- `CDP_INTAKE_KAFKA_PUSH_ASYNC_TEAMS` and the direct insert are gone.
- A push sent right after signup now waits for the person's device instead of being dropped. Before, it often ran before the app had registered a device, and the send was skipped for good.
  - When the person or their device doesn't exist yet, the push step tries again after 10, 20, 40, 80 and 160 seconds. That is about 5 minutes in all, then it skips as before.
  - Only API sends wait. A test send, a workflow started by an event, and a device the provider said is gone skip right away.
  - Each wait writes one line to the run log, such as "No device registered for distinct_id X yet; retrying in 10s (attempt 1/5)". The Metrics tab counts the send once, when it finishes. `push_notification_recipient_wait_total` counts the waits by reason.
  - The waits have their own count, so they don't use up the retries for provider errors.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  subgraph Before
    A1[No push route]
  end
  subgraph After
    A2[Push route] --> T2[cdp_intake_transactional_push] --> C2[Push intake consumer] --> Q2[(Job database)]
    E2[Email route] --> T3[cdp_intake_transactional_email]
  end
  classDef phRed fill:#f54e00,stroke:#f54e00,color:#fff;
  classDef phGray fill:#e5e7eb,stroke:#c7ccd1,color:#000;
  classDef phBlue fill:#1d4aff,stroke:#1d4aff,color:#fff;
  class A1,A2,E2 phRed;
  class T2,T3,Q2 phGray;
  class C2 phBlue;
```

## How did you test this code?

**Local stack with the send PRs and the push-only CDP API**, with a local server in place of Apple and Google. The push API used a database role that can only read.

| What was checked | Result |
|---|---|
| Sensitive and normal push, raw Kafka record and job row | Encrypted, no code in plain text, delivered once |
| Encryption key missing, blank or invalid | Sensitive push 503, nothing queued. Email works. Same key later sends once |
| Encryption key differs from the workers' | Accepted, then `failed`. Nothing delivered |
| Kafka paused or stopped while running | 503 after 3 s, email works, all 21 sent once on retry |
| Consumer stopped, or killed mid-batch | All pushes arrive once |
| Job database unreachable from the API | Accepted, delivered once |
| Push API down, hung, slow, killed, wrong key | Email works, retries send once |
| Build before this change and this one, both orders | Every push once, retries recognized, email works |

- API single and batch, UI, MCP, Node and Python SDKs: pushes arrive once. The one-key race gets `push_busy` from the send API's limit. The Node SDK's failing send still ends after 9 s, not 4 s.
- Email against master: answers, sent emails, Kafka records, job rows and usage events match. Email metric counts vary between two runs of master too.
- Node tests for CDP and workflows: 1,009 in parallel and 448 serial pass. Send stack Python push and email tests: 740 pass. 21 in `test_transactional_email_log.py` fail on this machine, and 23 fail on master alone.
- Email while 2,000 pushes a second are tried, with the send API's limit: none lost, p50 85 ms (45 ms with no push), p95 201 ms. At 210 a second: p50 47 ms, p95 92 ms. One machine, not production capacity.

## Problem

- The Rust logs consumer must run Hog programs that customers write, and the shared VM is not safe for that. A crafted program can overflow the stack, print gigabytes from a small heap, or leak memory between runs.
- This is the first of four PRs that replace #131041.

## Changes

- A host can step the VM, answer native calls itself, pass globals with ordered keys, read the raw result, and own a bounded regex cache.
- Printing, string building, native results, snapshots, membership tests and equality tests stop at the heap and depth limits.
- Closures compare, print and drop without following their captures, and the VM frees a closure that captures itself.
- A null, a boolean and a container cost 8 bytes of the heap limit, as in the Node VM. Before, they cost 0 or 1.
- A tuple that holds itself prints `null` where it repeats, as an array does.
- A bounded regex cache refuses the counted repetitions that RE2 refuses in Node.
- String functions count UTF-16 units and integer overflow continues as a float, as in the Node VM.
- cohort-core's `EVALUATOR_VERSION` goes to 4, so every stored person record evaluates again.

> [!WARNING]
> cymbal, cohort-core and the `hogvm-node` binding share this VM. The binding runs event transformations in the Node consumer when `CDP_HOG_RUST_VM_EXECUTION_ENABLED` is set. The string, overflow, heap charge and tuple changes apply to all three. Cymbal disables a rule that reaches the heap limit, and the new charge moves that limit down. A review thread asks how cymbal should handle it.

## How did you test this code?

- Ran locally: `cargo test -p hogvm -p cohort-core`, the `hogvm-node` tests, and clippy for hogvm and cohort-core.
- Not run locally: cymbal's tests, which CI runs on this PR, and cohort-core's `tests/postgres.rs`, which needs the Django test database.
- The CI report shows a comment density just under 6%. 49 of the 95 lines give the Hog source of a bytecode constant in a test, as the crate's other tests do. The four PRs together are below 4%.

**Test rationale:** `js_strings_and_limits.rs`, `host_driver.rs` and `async_resume.rs` hold one case for each limit, and each case fails without its guard. Eight of them aborted the test process with a stack overflow before their fix.

## Release status

- No feature flag controls this change <!-- release-status: no-feature-flag -->

## Docs update

- None.

## 🤖 Agent context

**Autonomy:** Human-driven (agent-assisted)

**Agent:** Claude Code, Opus 5.5 and Fable 5.2

**Skills:** `/stacking-prs`, `/writing-pr-descriptions`, `/writing-code-comments`, `/writing-tests`

**Driver checked:** Decided the split of #131041 into four PRs. Not yet checked the diff.

**Security review:** needed

<details>
<summary>More context for AI agents</summary>

- **Session:** https://claude.ai/code/session_017AymvKWGZjo39EYJtPKHgZ, https://claude.ai/code/session_017AymvKLVx6u56rQY3BPqQn
- **Decisions:** the layer is the `rust/common/hogvm` part of #131041 at its last reviewed head, plus the fixes for the review findings on this PR (837a96ebfc6, 916fda3f063, 90136d012a9, c5217895710, 0cc5b09fb69, 4c8fc97eaad, 8786d84d19d, f7ef89affca, 546386738fe, 48666b42a4f, ba1198ba499).
- **Decisions:** master had already taken `EVALUATOR_VERSION` 3 for another change, so this layer takes 4.
- **Decisions:** `Closure` has hand-written `Debug`, `PartialEq` and `Drop` paths, because the derived ones followed reference-counted cells.
- **Decisions:** the shared regex cache is unchanged. A host passes its own `RegexCache` to keep customer patterns out of it.
- **Decisions:** a snapshot measures the stack before `collect_cells` and each closed value before its walk, and refuses a cycle, because the walks in `state.rs` have no guard. They still follow captures. A last measure of all closed values together catches one value that many closures captured.
- **Decisions:** the repeat measure takes a rule from its caller: `jsonStringify` allows a cycle, the printers refuse one inside a SQL value, and the snapshot and `hog_to_json` refuse every cycle. It counts a second reference to one heap string. The SQL printer has no cycle check of its own.
- **Decisions:** `HogLiteral::compare_work` counts what one equality test reads: the top-level pairs of two containers of one length, at 32 bytes each, plus the bytes of same-length strings and of object keys. A nested container compares by its heap reference and counts nothing. `==`, `equals`, `notEquals`, the `in` opcode, `has`, `indexOf` and `in()` refuse more than 64 MiB of that work, and a membership test checks the total after each item.
- **Decisions:** value sizes follow `calculateCost` of the Node VM for a null, a boolean and a container. A slot in an array is 32 bytes, so the charge can be 4 times under the real size.
- **Decisions:** `SetProperty` charges a text key at the length of its text, because the object keeps its own copy. The charge follows the insert.
- **Decisions:** a bounded `RegexCache` limits the compiled size only. A limit on the search cache made `[a-z]{1000}[^a-z]` about 1,000 times slower. The repetition check runs only after a cache miss.
- **Hosts:** `hogvm-node` sets a 64 MiB heap and uses the shared regex cache. The bounded cache and its RE2 repetition rule reach a host only when it passes its own cache, and the binding does not yet. Its `Cargo.lock` is not updated here.
- **Open threads:** how cymbal handles a rule that reaches the heap limit; `in` on a text or object haystack has no compare budget, because its work is linear in one operand; natives such as `upper` copy a shared string with no allocation check; JSON escaping can make `jsonStringify` output 6 times its measured size; a pattern over the cache limit compiles on each call. None changed here. The owner decides.
- **Not bounded:** no clock runs inside one VM step or one native call. Each fix above bounds one operation by size. A new operation whose work grows faster than its operands needs its own bound.
- **Read closely:** `print.rs` (`RepeatMeasure`, `HogQLPrinter`), `context.rs` (`walk_emplacing`), `values.rs` (`Drop for Upvalue`, `Closure`, `size`, `compare_work`), `util.rs` (`RegexCache`), `vm.rs` (`Drop for HogVM`, `snapshot`, `assert_membership_fits`, `SetProperty`).

hits.body:
## What

Warehouse suggestions never propose an incremental refresh for a plain (non-grouped) projection over `events`. This is a common expensive full-refresh model:

```sql
SELECT toString(uuid) AS id, timestamp AS ts, toString(person_id) AS person_id, properties.$pathname AS pathname
FROM events
WHERE event = '$pageview' AND timestamp >= toDateTime('2026-11-01 00:00:00')
```

`propose_incremental_config` (`products/data_modeling/backend/logic/incremental_eligibility.py`) only proposes for a `GROUP BY` with exactly one time column. For the query above, it returns `None`.

## Why it can't just be proposed as-is

- `check_incremental_eligibility` accepts the plain query with `incremental_key=ts`, `unique_key=(id, ts)`.
- At run time, `UniqueKeyTracker` (`products/data_modeling/backend/temporal/activities/incremental_write.py`) raises `DuplicateUniqueKeyError` when a key repeats in one run's result. The error is non-retryable and the watermark stays, so every later run over that window fails again.
- `events` is a ReplacingMergeTree. Recent, unmerged parts can return a double-stored event twice, and that is exactly the window an incremental run reads.
- Deduping repeated keys in the upsert is not an option. On key alone it hides a wrong config and keeps an arbitrary row. On whole rows it can still fail, and it changes every incremental model.

## Proposed approach

Suggest a grouped rewrite. The grouped form is already eligible and already proposed today, and the `timestamp >= since` predicate is pushed into the `events` scan:

```sql
SELECT toString(uuid) AS id, timestamp AS ts, any(toString(person_id)) AS person_id, any(properties.$pathname) AS pathname
FROM events
WHERE event = '$pageview' AND timestamp >= toDateTime('2026-11-01 00:00:00')
GROUP BY id, ts
```

Grouping guarantees one row per `(id, ts)`, so the run cannot fail on duplicates.

Work needed:
- [ ] data_modeling: a function that rewrites a plain projection into the grouped form (key columns in `GROUP BY`, others wrapped in `any(...)`), and a proposal that returns the config with the rewritten SQL
- [ ] data_modeling facade: edit a saved query's SQL from backend code when a suggestion is accepted. None exists today, and it depends on saved-query version control being in place.
- [ ] warehouse_suggestions: carry the rewritten SQL in `MaterializePayload`, apply it on accept, and keep the "still proposed" check in `accept.py` working against the rewrite
- [ ] Frontend: show the person the rewritten SQL in the materialize suggestion before they accept

Already handled: lookback. Every incremental proposal already gets `RULES.materialize.incremental_lookback_seconds` (3 days) via `_with_refresh_mode` in `products/warehouse_suggestions/backend/logic/candidates/materialize.py`, which covers late-arriving events.

Blocked on saved-query version control.

The failing model count on the data catalog badge and the data modeling node list must agree on which models a user sees. Today two copies of the same rules exist, so a rule added to one copy makes them disagree.

## What is copied

| Rule | Node list (view) | Badge count (logic) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Hidden nodes (deleted views, managed views without the flag, metrics without data catalog access) | `MetricNodeVisibilityMixin._exclude_hidden_nodes` in `products/data_modeling/backend/presentation/views/metric_visibility.py` | `exclude_hidden_nodes` in `products/data_modeling/backend/logic/node_visibility.py` |
| Status of the newest ClickHouse job | `_annotate_latest_job` in `products/data_modeling/backend/presentation/views/node.py` | `_with_latest_serving_status` in `products/data_modeling/backend/logic/node_attention.py` |

The two yes/no checks under the hidden-node rule (`metric_nodes_hidden`, `managed_views_hidden`) already have one copy.

## Why the view cannot call the logic copy

- `data_modeling` is an isolated product. Its views may import only `facade/`.
- `hogli product:lint` rejects a facade function that takes or returns a QuerySet, in `facade/api.py` and in a re-export from `facade/models.py`.

## Fix

Move the node list queryset into `logic/`, so the view gets rows or contracts from the facade. Then delete the view copies.

Found in review of #139525.

Follows #127411.

## Problem

Agents and API callers wait a long time on `GET /signals/reports/for_me/` and the `inbox-reports-for-me` MCP tool.
The endpoint and the tool description both say the call returns at once and does not wait on the model.
The model is not the cost: reads that reuse a stored list and start no wait are slow too.

- On one large production project, these reads took more than ten seconds.
- #127411 measured candidate gathering locally at 36 queries and 0.1s to 0.5s, so the local numbers hide this.
- A call with `wait_seconds` can take much longer than its wait, so MCP clients can time out on the documented maximum of 30.
- Each slow read holds a web worker. The build limits do not cover reads.

The scheduled tick in #127617 checks each person's input hash with the same gathering, so its cost grows with this too.

The cause is not confirmed. `gather_candidates` is the likely place, because every read runs it before the freshness check.

## Proposed behavior

Read `products/signals/backend/personal_ranking/serve.py` and `candidates.py` first.

1. **Measure first.** Time each phase of a read in production: pool queries, report load, priorities, PR state, predictions, needs-you facts, the activity summary read, and the input hash. Record the timings on the `personal inbox ranking read` event, next to `duration_ms`.
2. **Fix what dominates.** Make the slow queries cheaper with better predicates, indexes or fewer pools. Add indexes with a safe migration.
3. **If that is not enough, add a cheap path for a fresh stored list.** Check only the stored `candidate_ids` when the list is inside `freshness_minutes`, and skip the pool queries. A report that is new since the build then joins at the next rebuild, not on this read. Write down this trade-off in the PR, because it changes when a list goes stale.
4. **Bound the whole call.** Measure `wait_seconds` from the start of the request, so that gathering spends the same budget. A call with `wait_seconds` of N returns close to N seconds, with whatever list it has and `building: true`.
5. **Keep the description true.** If a read still cannot return quickly, change "returns at once" in the view and in `products/signals/mcp/tools.yaml`. Regenerate the MCP schema.

Do not read from the Today or Inbox list paths, and do not change the ranking, the prompt or the candidates a build uses.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The read event records the time of each phase, so a production read shows which phase is slow.
- [ ] A read that reuses a stored list runs a fixed number of queries, whatever the number of reports in the project. A test asserts this count.
- [ ] A call with `wait_seconds` set returns within that budget plus a small margin, including gathering time.
- [ ] A stored list still goes stale when a candidate's status, PR state or score changes.
- [ ] The PR states the before and after timings, measured on a project with a large inbox.

## Scope

Backend, plus the tool description if it must change. #127617 edits the same freshness check in `serve.py`, so whichever lands second rebases onto the other. A separate issue covers the extra build that a slow read can queue.

## Problem

Every signals scout run gets the same fixed runtime budget: `DEFAULT_MAX_RUNTIME_S = 15 * 60` in `products/signals/backend/scout_harness/limits.py`. The constant's comment currently says tuning it is a config decision, not a per-run override knob.

That one-size budget no longer fits the fleet:

- The per-scout model pin (#78764) lets an owner run a scout on a slower frontier model. A pinned scout can be doing correct, on-script work and still get killed by `poll_for_turn: timed out after 900s` because a single judging generation takes several minutes. Five such timeouts in a row trip the failure-streak breaker and auto-pause the scout, so a healthy scout+model pairing reads as a broken lane.
- Batch-scale measurement scouts (structured-output judges scoring ~100 entities per run) sit near the wall even on default models.
- Conversely, cheap watchdog scouts that close out in under a minute could take a tighter budget as a cost/safety bound.

## Proposal

Add an optional per-scout max runtime to `SignalScoutConfig`, as an **enum of sanctioned values rather than a free integer**: `5 / 15 / 30 / 45 / 60` minutes.

- Default stays exactly as today: null means 15 minutes, no behavior change for any existing config.
- 60 minutes is the hard upper bound.
- No feature-flag gate. Unlike the model pin this is a general need - some scouts just need longer or shorter runtimes - and an enum with a capped ceiling bounds the blast radius on its own.
- Exposed on the config API / `scout-config-update` like `model` and `network_access`.

An enum keeps validation trivial, keeps the coordinator's capacity math predictable (a run can only hold a sandbox lease for one of five known durations), and leaves room to grow the ladder later without a migration.

## Implementation notes

Both enforcement points are already set per dispatch, so the plumbing is small:

- `start_to_close_timeout` on the agent activity (`temporal/agentic/scout_scheduler.py`) - currently `DEFAULT_MAX_RUNTIME_S + ACTIVITY_SLACK_S`.
- `max_poll_seconds` passed to `MultiTurnSession` (`scout_harness/runner.py`). Note `poll_for_turn`'s own `MAX_POLL_SECONDS` default is already 30 min; scouts pass 900s down.

Things the PR must handle:

- `STALE_RUN_CUTOFF_S` (the orphan reaper) derives from the global ceiling. It must key off the **max allowed** budget (60 min) or the run's own stamped budget, otherwise a legitimately long run gets reaped alive.
- Stamp a non-default budget on the run row `metadata` (like `model` / `runtime_adapter`) and carry it on the `signals_scout_run_started` / `_finished` lifecycle events, so timeout rates stay sliceable across mixed budgets.
- The dropped-finalization salvage window in `custom_prompt_internals.py` is tuned relative to the budget it is given - verify it still fires sensibly at 45-60 min.
- A budget longer than the scout's `run_interval_minutes` self-throttles via the `_has_running_run` single-flight guard; fine, but worth a test and a docs sentence.
- Update the `limits.py` comment that says this is deliberately not a per-run knob.
- Longer leases cost more sandbox time per run; the enum ceiling plus the existing per-team run caps bound this, but the config UI help text should say a bigger budget means a more expensive run.

## Out of scope

- Free-form integer budgets.
- Per-run (as opposed to per-scout) overrides.
- Changing the coordinator tick or the per-team run caps.

## Is your feature request related to a problem?

Approval for AI data processing is a single organization-wide setting: AI features either get access to all project data or are turned off. An organization that wants to use PostHog AI, but needs to keep its own customers' personal data from being sent to the models, has no way to do that today, so it keeps AI features turned off.

## Describe the solution you'd like

A way for admins to control which data AI features can access, so that chosen data, such as customers' personal data, is not sent to the models.

## Describe alternatives you've considered

- [Property access control](https://posthog.com/docs/settings/property-access-control) (Enterprise plan). PostHog AI and PostHog MCP server queries run with the asking member's permissions, so a property hidden from that member is also hidden from the model. This falls short because:
  - Organization admins always have full access, so every property is readable when an admin asks.
  - Rules are set per member or role, not per feature.
- Turning AI data processing off and using the [PostHog MCP server](https://posthog.com/docs/model-context-protocol) with a model the organization picks. No data goes to PostHog's AI providers, but query results still reach whatever model the MCP client uses, and PostHog AI and AI-powered MCP tools are unavailable.

## Additional context

From: https://us.posthog.com/project/2/support/tickets/81420

Related: #68914 (enable or disable AI features per project), #74585 (HIPAA BAA coverage for AI features), #55519 (EU-hosted AI inference).

## Problem

A model with no live version shows one badge ("Bootstrapping") and one line for three different situations, and a person cannot tell which one they are in or when it changes.

- The list card (`TrainingBody` in `products/autoresearch/frontend/AutoresearchModelCard.tsx`) says "Starting the first training run…" whenever there is no live training run. It says this for a model whose first run finished weeks ago, next to "1 run · 19 experiments".
- The banner on the model page (`notLiveExplanation()` in `frontend/trainingScheduleLogic.ts`) says "The next research run tries again." with no date, then prints `not_promoted_reason` verbatim. That text is an internal error string with a sandbox file path and byte counts.
- The Accuracy tab's empty state (`frontend/pipeline/OnlinePerformanceTab.tsx`) offers a "Score now" button when there is no live model to score with.
- "Bootstrapping" (`frontend/PipelineStatusTag.tsx`) is not a word a new user knows.

## Changes

Load `/writing-user-facing-copy` and `/writing-ui-components` first.

1. **Three named states** for a pipeline in `bootstrapping`, decided in `frontend/modelCardState.ts` (extend it and its test) and used by both the card and the status tag:

   | State | When | Tag | Card body |
   |---|---|---|---|
   | Training | `live_training_run` is set | Training | "First training run in progress" plus the existing progress details |
   | Not live yet | no live run, `not_promoted_reason` is set | Not live yet (warning) | "Found a model, but it couldn't go live" plus the next-run line and a "See why" link to the model page |
   | Waiting to train | no live run, at least one completed run, and the project's daily limit is reached (`next_slot_at` from the limits action) | Waiting to train (warning) | "Waiting for a training slot" plus when the next slot opens |

   A pipeline with no run at all keeps a "Starting the first training run…" line.
2. **Next-run line with a date.** Where `next_research_at` is in the past, say "on the next scoring day"; otherwise give the date. Reuse `trainingScheduleStatus()`.
3. **Plain reason, raw text behind a toggle.** Map the known `not_promoted_reason` shapes to a sentence in one function, with the raw string under a collapsed "Technical details":
   - model file over the size cap: "The model file was too large to run every day."
   - feature query over the time limit: "The model's daily query took too long to run."
   - anything else: "The model failed a check before going live."

   Prefer a typed reason code from the backend over string matching if one is cheap to add to the pipeline response. If you add one, regenerate types with `hogli build:openapi`.
4. **Banner actions.** The banner gets a "Run training now" button, with the existing limit `disabledReason`.
5. **Accuracy empty state with no live model:** title "Nothing to check yet", body "This model has no live version, so there are no predictions to check. Once a model goes live, the first check comes {horizon} after its first scoring run." No "Score now" button in that state.

## Acceptance

- A model whose first run completed but did not go live never shows "Starting the first training run…".
- The banner gives a plain sentence and a next-run line. The raw reason is visible only after opening "Technical details".
- No surface offers "Score now" for a model with no live version.
- The word "Bootstrapping" does not appear in the UI.
- Stories cover the three card states. Load `/writing-tests` before changing `modelCardState.test.ts`.

- Why a due training run did not start (A122).
- Changing pipeline statuses in the backend.

Layout only. Dates, times and counts are examples.

## Problem

- Trace judges on agent runs answer N/A because they never see the task prompt ([thread](https://posthog.slack.com/archives/C087XQ7K9K7/p1795011878017719)).
- Each step resends the conversation, so the transcript overflows its 150,000-character budget.
- Every long message then keeps 1,000 characters, prompt included, with no sign on the result.

## Changes

- Judges see repeated messages once, as `[1-17] Same as messages 1-17 of the previous generation's input above`. Only equal messages collapse.
- The trace budget rises to 300,000 characters, falling back to 150,000 when the judge's context window rejects it.
- Results from a cut transcript set `$ai_evaluation_input_truncated: true`.
- Traces still over 150,000 characters after the collapse send up to twice the input tokens to the customer's judge key.

The judge call gains one fallback:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A[Render at 150k]:::phYellow --> B{{Judge}}:::phBlue --> C[Verdict or skip]:::phGray
  classDef phBlue fill:#1d4aff,stroke:#1d4aff,color:#fff;
  classDef phYellow fill:#f9bd2b,stroke:#f9bd2b,color:#000;
  classDef phGray fill:#e5e7eb,stroke:#c7ccd1,color:#000;
```

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A[Render at 300k]:::phYellow --> B{{Judge}}:::phBlue
  B -->|context window exceeded| D[Render at 150k]:::phYellow --> E{{Judge}}:::phBlue --> C[Verdict or skip]:::phGray
  B --> C
  classDef phBlue fill:#1d4aff,stroke:#1d4aff,color:#fff;
  classDef phYellow fill:#f9bd2b,stroke:#f9bd2b,color:#000;
  classDef phGray fill:#e5e7eb,stroke:#c7ccd1,color:#000;
```

## How did you test this code?

**Test rationale:**

- New tests fail if the collapse is off, a changed message collapses, or the context-window fallback retries wrongly.
- Not checked: a real judge on a real agent trace.

## Release status

- No feature flag controls this change <!-- release-status: no-feature-flag -->

## Docs update

- The judge inputs doc and the evaluations skill.

## 🤖 Agent context

**Autonomy:** Human-driven (agent-assisted)

**Agent:** Claude Code, Claude Opus 5.5

**Skills:** `/writing-tests`, `/writing-code-comments`, `/writing-pr-descriptions`

**Driver checked:** Not yet checked by the driver

**Security review:** not needed

<details>
<summary>More context for AI agents</summary>

- **Session:** Claude Code, local worktree.
- **Decisions:** Messages compare as raw dicts, not rendered text, because rendering hides differences such as a changed image.
- **Decisions:** A fixed 300k budget with a 150k fallback replaces a per-model context table, because BYOK judges can be any model.
- **Follow-ups:** Session results do not set `$ai_evaluation_input_truncated`.
- **Follow-ups:** `llma_eval_errors` still counts a context-window rejection that the fallback recovers; the `trace_judge_context_window_fallback` log records the outcome.
- **Follow-ups:** The truncation pass cuts every message over 1,000 characters; cutting the largest messages first would keep more of the prompt.
- **Decisions:** The truncation flag comes from the render the judge receives, which is the marked one when attachments are on.
- **CI report, comment density:** The remaining added comments state reasons the code cannot show: the memory cost of flattening, why the marked render sets the flag, and why the fallback budget exists.
- **CI report, call assertions:** The fallback test reads the prompts sent to the mocked LLM client. That client is the unit's real output, the provider call, so its calls are the outcome.
- **Read closely:** `_with_repeated_input` in `trace_formatter.py` and the fallback in `run_trace_llm_judge`.

</details>

## Context

**Goal:** improve the default prompt, system prompt and detector behaviour that every user gets out of the box. These are changes to the defaults, not tuning for particular alerts.

The sampled alerts nearly all carry hand-written author instructions. Most users will not write any, so judge each change on alerts without instructions too.

We reviewed a week of AI detector checks on internal alerts before the wider rollout of `alerts-llm-detector`. Almost all checks are hourly, all of them run on one model, and none errored. Verdicts are mostly sensible. The items below are small, independent changes. Each one can ship as its own PR.

## 1. Write values as plain decimals

**Problem:** `prompt.py` formats values with `:g`. A count of 1,175,594 reaches the model as `1.17559e+06`, which drops the low digits and makes neighbouring values look identical.

**Change:** add a formatter that writes integers in full, rounds other values of 1 or more to two decimals, and writes small values positionally. Bump `PROMPT_REVISION`.

## 2. Bound the earlier-alerts block

**Problem:** the block lists one rationale for every flagged point in the window, so it grows with the fire rate. On the noisiest alerts it is about three quarters of the prompt. That raises cost, and a wall of earlier "anomaly" reasons pushes the model to flag again.

Two smaller defects in the same block:
- The 200-character cut lands mid-word ("so the elev").
- Old rationales quote values from the time of that check. Those values often no longer match the table, because buckets get revised.

**Change:**
- Keep the most recent N rationales (for example 5). Add a one-line summary such as "this alert flagged 42 of the 168 points in the window, most recently at <date>".
- Cut at a sentence or word boundary.
- Label the quoted numbers as the values at the time of that check.

## 3. Make sustained level shifts consistent

**Problem:** when a series moves to a new level and stays there for days, verdicts flip between `level_shift` and `none` from one hour to the next on the same state. One alert fired on most checks for days on a shift that started early in the window. A similar alert stopped firing on its shift after about a day.

The comparable-points line adds to this. With a 7-day hourly window, the "same weekday" value is the one point from before the shift, so it always reads as a 2-3x jump.

**Change:** decide what a check means during an ongoing shift, then say it in the prompt. Either it means "still anomalous", so it keeps firing and the alert state machine handles renotification, or it means "new or worsening", so it fires once and then only on a further move. Pass the alert's current firing streak as data. Add an eval case for a shift that holds for 1, 3 and 5 days.

## 4. Revisit the hourly lookback

**Problem:** `llm_detector_lookback("hour")` covers 7 days, so "same hour on the same weekday in earlier weeks" has at most one value. Weekly seasonality cannot be learned from that.

**Change:** try 14 days for hourly series. Item 2 frees enough tokens to pay for the extra rows. Compare verdicts on a labelled set before and after.

## 5. Skip re-checks of an unchanged point

**Problem:** about three quarters of hourly points are judged twice. The likely cause is a check cadence shorter than the bucket, but that is not confirmed. The second call sees the same series, give or take a few late events, and disagrees with the first call about 2% of the time. That costs twice as much and can flap.

**Change:** reuse the last verdict when the current point's date matches and the values in the window are within a small tolerance of the last check. The memo key covers `evaluation_id` today, so this needs a second, point-keyed lookup. Cost story: this removes roughly half of the model calls for hourly alerts.

## 6. Escape metadata without quote entities

**Problem:** `html.escape` runs with its default `quote=True`, so HogQL filters in the metric description reach the model as `"` and `'`.

**Change:** use `escape(..., quote=False)`. Only `<`, `>` and `&` matter for keeping data inside its tags. The existing tag-escape test still covers the injection case.

## Out of scope / later

- Measure whether the chart image changes verdicts. It is attached to every call. An ablation on a labelled set would tell us whether it pays for its tokens.

## Problem

- A QA pass of the onboarding graded it 4 to 6 out of 10.

## Changes

- Setup is a three-step wizard: Your website, Review, First results. One field and one button start it.

## Problem

Suggested prompts are the rows above a report's `Ask AI` box: follow-up questions and next-step actions that a reader sends with one click. Today only scouts write them, so most inbox reports have none.

- A report the pipeline writes (signals grouped, then researched) almost never has suggested prompts. These are most of the reports in the inbox.
- A report a scout writes has them about three times in four.
- When research rewrites a scout's report, the scout's prompts are removed and nothing replaces them.

The reader of a pipeline report gets an empty `Ask AI` box on the reports where the next step is least obvious, because no scout framed it.

## Why it happens

`ReportDecision.suggested_prompts` in `products/signals/backend/temporal/summary.py` defaults to `[]`, and its comment says why: the pipeline does not write prompts yet, and prompts a scout wrote belong to the title and summary that the decision replaces. Clearing them is correct. Writing none in their place is the gap.

The research run already produces everything a prompt needs. `ReportPresentationOutput` in `report_generation/research.py` carries the title and summary, and the run knows which questions it left open and what it recommends.

## Proposal

Have the research presentation turn write suggested prompts with the title and summary.

1. Add `suggested_prompts` to `ReportPresentationOutput`, with the same limits scouts have (`MAX_SUGGESTED_PROMPTS`, `MAX_SUGGESTED_PROMPT_LENGTH` in `report_prompts.py`), and run it through `normalize_suggested_prompts` and `suggested_prompts_batch_error`.
2. Pass it through `RunAgenticReportOutput` into `ReportDecision.suggested_prompts`, so the stored set always matches the stored prose. The no-repository branch keeps `None`, because it keeps the existing prose.
3. Reuse the scout guidance for what a good prompt is (`_REPORT_SUGGESTED_PROMPTS` in `scout_harness/prompt.py`) so both authors write to one standard. Move the shared text to one place that both prompts read.
4. Send the prompts through the report safety judge with the title and summary, as scout prompts already are (`_suggested_prompts_signal` in `scout_report/judge.py`). A prompt is sent to an agent run, so it is an injection surface.

An invalid or unsafe prompt set should store no prompts and keep the report. It must not fail the research run.

## Open questions

- Should every report get at least one prompt, or should the research run keep the "write none rather than pad" rule that scouts have? The scout rule exists because an obvious prompt costs a read. For a pipeline report with a clear recommendation, an action prompt is rarely padding.
- An implementable report already has an `implement` action. Should the research run skip the "open a pull request for this" prompt on those and write questions only?
- Which other surfaces show the prompts? The inbox, the desktop app and the mobile app read `suggested_prompts` from the report. The Slack report message does not show them. Out of scope here, but worth a follow-up issue if the answer is "everywhere".
- Cost: the presentation turn writes a few more tokens per report. Expected to be small. Measure it on the first day.

## Acceptance

- The share of pipeline reports that reach the inbox with at least one suggested prompt rises from about zero to a level near the scout rate.
- Suggested-prompt presses rise with it (`Inbox report action` with `question_source = suggested` and no `question_intent`). Coverage with no change in presses means the prompts are not useful, and the guidance needs work.
- A report that research rewrites never shows prompts written for the older prose.
- Tests cover: prompts stored with a fresh title and summary, prompts cleared when research returns none, the no-repository branch keeping what it had, and an over-limit set stored as none.

## Related

- #138185: scout self-improvement reports rarely carry suggested prompts.

hits.body:
## Problem

A scheduled scout starts a full sandbox run every time it comes due, even when nothing has changed since its last run.
For a scout that watches a rare or bursty thing (new error tracking issues, a CSP violation, a sign-up from a specific domain), most runs find nothing new.
Each of those runs still pays for a sandbox and an agent that orients itself (scratchpad, past runs, project profile, inbox) before it can decide there is nothing to do.
The cost comes from that fixed overhead, not from the data, which is usually a few rows.

That overhead stops owners from running a scout often.
A scout that should look at new error tracking issues every 30 minutes is too expensive at that cadence, so it runs daily and finds things late.

What exists today:

- The coordinator (`products/signals/backend/temporal/agentic/scout_coordinator.py`) dispatches a `RunSignalsScoutWorkflow` child for every due config. Nothing checks whether there is anything to look at.
- The workflow "Run scout" step (`posthog-run-scout.template.ts`) can start a run from an event, and #113324 adds a templated note so the run knows which event fired it. That path needs a workflow per team, drops fires inside its 30-minute cooldown, and passes one event, not everything since the last run.
- `RunSignalsScoutInput.run_note` and `_run_note_section` in `scout_harness/prompt.py` already carry a one-run note into the prompt.

## Proposal

An optional **pre-check** on a scout config: a HogQL query that runs before a scheduled run starts.

- **No rows:** skip the run. No sandbox, no `SignalScoutRun` row, no LLM call.
- **Rows:** start the run. If the owner turns on "pass rows to the run" (on by default), the first rows go into the prompt as data, so the scout starts from what is new instead of orienting from scratch.

The pre-check is deterministic and cheap: one HogQL query, with a timeout and a row cap.
A plain yes/no gate is the special case, for example `SELECT 1 WHERE ...`.

### Example: error tracking every 30 minutes

```sql
SELECT properties.$exception_issue_id AS issue_id,
       count() AS events,
       uniq(person_id) AS users,
       min(timestamp) AS first_seen
FROM events
WHERE event = '$exception' AND timestamp > {since}
GROUP BY issue_id
HAVING min(timestamp) > {since}
ORDER BY users DESC
LIMIT 50
```

Shape only; check it against the schema before it goes in docs. Widen the `HAVING` for reopened or spiking issues.

### Where it runs

Recommended: as the first activity of `RunSignalsScoutWorkflow`, before `run_signals_scout_activity` creates the run row.

- The coordinator tick stays fast, and one slow or failing query cannot hold up the tick.
- Skipped runs never create a `SignalScoutRun`, so they do not count against `max_runs_per_day` (that tally reads run rows).
- The alternative is to evaluate in `_collect_planned_runs` before `_allocate_tick_budget`, so skipped configs do not use a tick slot. That is more coordinator work per tick; worth it only if tick slots become the constraint.

Only scheduled runs evaluate the pre-check. "Run now", workflow runs and check runs (`triggered_by` manual / workflow / check) skip it, because a person or a trigger already decided to run.

### Placeholders

- `{since}`: start time of the last run that actually ran, or the config's `created_at`.
- `{now}`: the evaluation time.

Pass both through HogQL `placeholders`. Do not build the query with string formatting. The query runs as the team, through the normal HogQL path, so it can read only that team's data.

### Bookkeeping for a skipped run

- Advance the dispatch anchor (`last_run_at`, through the existing slot-anchor stamp) so the next tick does not dispatch it again at once.
- Do not move `{since}`. The next run that starts still sees everything since the last real run.
- A skip does not count toward the failure breaker or the inactivity / engagement auto-pause. A correctly quiet scout must not be paused for being quiet.

### Errors and limits

- Timeout of about 10 seconds, a low-priority query tag, and a row cap (for example 50 rows or 8 KB of rendered text, whichever comes first).
- On a query error, run the scout as if there were no pre-check, and record the error. A failing pre-check must not turn the scout off silently.
- After several errors in a row, tell the owner (the same path as #106455).

### Prompt

Render the rows into a `<precheck_result>` block, reusing the run-note path with its own template.
Frame the block as untrusted data, the same way #113324 frames a workflow note, because event properties can contain text from outside the team.
Strip angle brackets, like the workflow note does.

### Optional backstop

`precheck_max_quiet_minutes`: run anyway if the scout has not run for this long, so baselines and scratchpad memory do not go stale. Off by default.

### Config, API, MCP and UI

- `SignalScoutConfig`: `precheck_query` (nullable text), `precheck_pass_rows` (bool, default true), `precheck_max_quiet_minutes` (nullable int). Same edit permission as the rest of the config.
- Serializer fields with `help_text`, so they reach `scout-config-update` in the MCP.
- A dry-run endpoint ("Test check") that returns the rows and whether the scout would run now, also exposed as an MCP tool.
- Scout settings: a collapsed "Run only when" section with the query editor, the toggle and the test button.

### Observability

- One event per evaluation, `scout_precheck_evaluated`, with outcome (`run` / `skip` / `error`), row count and duration.
- Skipped ticks visible on the roster run strip. Without this, a scout that skips looks broken.

## Plan

1. Backend: config fields and migration, the pre-check activity in `RunSignalsScoutWorkflow`, placeholders, skip bookkeeping, prompt block, limits, event.
2. API and MCP: serializer fields, dry-run endpoint and tool, `authoring-scouts` docs with the error tracking example. The docs should help an agent suggest a pre-check when a scout watches something rare or bursty, write it, test it with the dry run, then save it with `scout-config-update`.
3. UI: the "Run only when" section in scout settings and skipped ticks on the run strip.

## Open questions

- Should a skill (canonical scout or store template) ship a default pre-check in its frontmatter, or is it config-only?
- Should the pre-check result be kept on the run row for debugging and evals?
- If a canonical scout ships a default pre-check, the fleet runs one query per due config per tick. Is a single fleet-wide query per scope better there?
- Intervals under 30 minutes need a change to the tick grid. Out of scope here.

## Problem

Cloud runs on the Claude runtime call MCP tools that are set to "needs approval" without asking the user. The gateway proxy then rejects the call. Desktop already asks first.

Refs #76237

## Changes

- Cloud runs now ask with one option, "Yes, and approve this tool in PostHog". On yes, the run saves the approval, then makes the call. Two installations whose names sanitize alike stay ungated.
- An allow saves the approval only when the answer carries `confirmPersistentApproval: true`. PostHog AI and the desktop app send it only when a person clicks an allow option on a prompt marked `persistsApproval`. Anything that answers on its own (PostHog AI tabs loaded before this deploy, auto-approve modes, the Slack permission broker) picks the first allow option, so the option id alone can't show a person approved the tool. Those answers are declined, and the run tells the user to approve the tool in PostHog.
- The approval is saved with the run's credentials, so it's saved only when the person who answered is the user those credentials belong to. The `/command` JWT says who answered, and `/api/users/@me/` says who the run acts as. If a teammate answers, the run declines the same way.
- Saving an approval needs `project:write`, but `/command` needs only `task:write`. So `/command` now returns 403 for a `permission_response` with `confirmPersistentApproval` from a personal API key or OAuth token without `project:write`, before it reaches the sandbox. Browser sessions and the desktop app, whose token holds `project:write`, are unaffected.
- On codex, a decline with a reason reaches codex as a decline, not a cancel, and the reason is added to the running turn. A cancel aborts the whole turn on command approvals, and on MCP prompts the model sees only "user cancelled".
- Background runs and runs with no connected client decline without asking. Slack runs relay the prompt like any other run, and the confirmation check declines the broker's answer.
- The mobile apps don't send the confirmation yet, so allowing a tool from them is declined with the same guidance rather than saved.
- A `PreToolUse` hook forces "ask" for these tools, because `bypassPermissions` skips `canUseTool`.
- Approval states load at startup alongside session setup, capped at 5s so they never delay the run. Past that, tools load ungated. They reload on `refresh_session`, where an installation whose fetch fails keeps its last loaded states.

Out of scope: built-in agent runs (gateway grant URLs), Pi's "allow once", and saving the approval as the person who answered rather than with the run's credentials.

## How did you test this code?

- Ran `agent-server.test.ts` and `posthog-api.test.ts` (301 tests), `tsc` and Biome in the agent workspace, `permissionResponse.test.ts` and the desktop `pnpm typecheck`, and all of `runStreamLogic.test.ts` (416 tests).
- Added codex cases for a command approval and an MCP prompt cancelled with a reason. Each declines and passes the reason on, and each failed with its guard removed. The codex adapter suite passes (397 tests).
- Added `test_command_persistent_approval_requires_project_write`: a `task:write` key gets a 403 and nothing reaches the sandbox, and a key with `project:write` goes through. Without the scope check, the first case got a 200 and was forwarded.
- The new cases each failed without their fix: an allow without the confirmation was saved, PostHog AI sent no confirmation for a person's allow, and the desktop helper didn't exist.
- Earlier rounds: ran the agent workspace's adapter, server and API Vitest suites, plus the full-auto cases in `runStreamLogic.test.ts` and the `toolPolicy.test.ts` table, removing each fix in turn to check its test failed.
- The approval tests answer through the real `permission_response` command with a caller user id and the confirmation flag, including a teammate who allows and an answer with no confirmation. Neither gets the tool approved.
- On a devbox running the real stack, with a DeepWiki installation named "Deep Wiki (test)", I checked the backend calls the agent makes:
  - New tools default to "needs approval".
  - A proxy `tools/call` before approval returns `-32001 "requires approval"`.
  - The agent's `PATCH tools/<name>/` approves the tool, and the same call then reaches the upstream server.
  - The sandbox config uses the raw name `Deep Wiki (test)`, so the agent needs the sanitized key, and its installation regex matches the proxy URL.
- Not checked: a full PostHog AI run with a model, because the devbox has no LLM key.
- Not checked: a team-visible run answered by its own user and by a teammate.
- Not checked: that the SDK calls `canUseTool` after a hook "ask" under `bypassPermissions`. The exec sub-tool gate depends on the same behavior.
- Not checked: a Slack-origin run end to end, or a mobile allow.

**Test rationale:** I added the new cases beside the existing tests for each unit. They cover the gate, the confirmation check, the answering-user check, the excluded run types, the refresh (including a failed fetch that keeps or drops states by installation id), the hook, the policy-load retry, and full-auto leaving the prompt to the user.

**CI report warnings:**

- Call assertions in `agent-server.test.ts` and `approvals.test.ts` read the calls a boundary received: the approval `PATCH`, the prompt relayed to the client, the payload forwarded to the adapter, and the reason handed to codex. Those calls are the unit's output.
- The TypeScript duplication is the per-file `./mcp/tool-metadata` mock that 8 `claude-agent.*.test.ts` files each define. This PR adds two entries to each copy. Moving them to one shared mock factory is a separate test refactor.
- The two over-budget eager graph roots show no change against base. The 216 B bundle growth is the `persistsApproval` checks in `runStreamLogic` and `toolPolicy`.
- The TypeScript complexity warnings are on existing `runStreamLogic` functions. This PR adds one condition to `deliverPermission` and one to the auto-approve check.

## Problem

- Data quality checks wait on Python, not ClickHouse. Every check rebuilds the team's whole HogQL database, and traces show the build outlasts the query.

## Changes

- Checks in one batch that run as the same user now share one database, so suites with several checks finish sooner.
- The cache key is the user the check runs as, or the service bypass, so warehouse access control is unchanged.
- A `data_quality.run_check` span shows each check in the batch trace.
- Rejected: merging checks into one query, like dbt's `--batch-tests`. That saves only ClickHouse time.

## How did you test this code?

**Test rationale:** the new batch test fails when the cache key ignores the user (checked by breaking it), or when each check builds its own database again.

Related: #126249, #129256, #123018.

## Problem

The personal inbox ranking prompt never sees what the person did with their inbox reports. It only sees the activity summary, which carries that evidence in a weak form.

- **The summary keeps few inbox lines.** Each summary update renders at most `INBOX_LINES` (6) inbox lines, next to tasks, changes, MCP sessions and opens.
- **The summary turns them into prose.** The ranking prompt gets a headline, a profile, themes and object names. A dismissal as "not relevant", a thumbs down or a claim is at best folded into a theme, and often lost.
- **The summary is older than the inbox.** A summary updates every few days. A ranking is checked every hour. What the person dismissed or claimed this morning does not reach the next build.
- **Nothing links activity to a candidate.** The prompt can't tell that the person already opened `c7` on three days, rated it down, or left a note on it.

So the model ranks from a guess about interests, when the direct evidence exists: `SignalReportAction` rows and the person's work log entries, which `activity_summary.inputs.user_inbox` already reads.

## Proposed behavior

A personal ranking build reads the person's recent inbox activity and shows it to the model as its own block, between the person block and the candidates.

Read `products/signals/backend/personal_ranking/prompt.py`, `logic.py`, `config.py`, and `products/signals/backend/activity_summary/inputs.py` (`user_inbox`) and `render.py` (`inbox_units` and the `_InboxFact` helpers) first.

1. **Read the activity.** Call `user_inbox(team_id, user_id, start, end)` for the last `inbox_activity_days` days. Reuse the rules that the summary applies: drop entries a task or agent wrote, collapse bulk triage into one line, and drop single opens and read-only rows. Then keep only the facts at or above `inbox_activity_min_strength`. The default is `rated`, so opens and Slack discussions stay out unless the payload lowers it.
2. **Render one line per report**, strongest evidence first (`InboxStrength`), then newest, at most `inbox_activity_lines` lines. Each line has the age, the title and what the person did, in the wording the summary already uses ("claimed the work", "dismissed it as not interested", "resolved it (already fixed)", "rated it down"). Extract the fact and wording helpers so both features share one definition. Do not copy them.
3. **Give reviewer corrections a direction.** `user_inbox` already reads the person's `reviewer_corrections` entries, but every one renders as "corrected the reviewers" with the strength of an action, so removing yourself from a report counts as interest in it. Read `pinned` and `excluded` from the entry and render one of:
    - "removed themselves as reviewer": the same strength as a "not interested" dismissal. Candidates on the same topic move down.
    - "added themselves as reviewer": an action. Candidates on the same topic move up.
    - "changed the reviewers": the correction only names other people. It shows the person triages this area, and says nothing about their own interest.

    Use the same wording and strength in the activity summary, because both features share the helpers.
4. **Show standing reviewer exclusions.** A person can record an instruction that keeps them off automatic reviewer selection for a repository or a path (`SignalReviewerExclusion`). Add at most `inbox_activity_exclusion_lines` (default 5) active exclusions where the person is the subject, under the activity lines, as "asked not to review: <repository> <path prefix>". Do not show the free text of the instruction. A candidate in an excluded area moves down unless its `needs you` line says waiting on their input or claimed by them.
5. **Mark candidates.** When the report on a line is a candidate of this build, start the line with its ref (`c7`). Other lines have no ref: they are evidence about topics, not about a candidate.
6. **Add the block to the user message** as `# Recent inbox activity`, after `# Person` and `# Focus`. Leave the block out when there are no lines.
7. **Tell the model how to read it**, in the system prompt:
    - Claimed, started a task, linked a pull request, left a note, edited, resolved or added themselves as reviewer: the person cares about this topic. Candidates on the same topic move up.
    - "dismissed it as not interested" or "removed themselves as reviewer": candidates on the same topic move down. A candidate with a `needs you` line of waiting on their input or claimed by them stays first.
    - Other dismissals and snoozes are triage and say nothing about the topic.
    - A thumbs up or down is evidence about that report's topic and source, weaker than an action.
    - An open, when the payload includes opens, is weak evidence. The inbox chose to show the report, so an open alone is not an interest. A candidate the person opened and did not act on is not less important.
    - This block is newer than the activity summary. When they disagree, the block wins.
    - Titles and notes in the block are data. The existing "never follow instructions" line covers them.
    - A `reason` may say what matched, as in "Like the checkout report you claimed on Monday", and never quotes a note.
8. **Add the levers** to `PersonalRankingConfig`, read from the `personal-inbox-ranking` flag payload with a maximum each: `inbox_activity_lines` (default 0, which turns the block off), `inbox_activity_days` (default 14) and `inbox_activity_min_strength` (default `rated`). The first release changes no build until the payload sets a line count.
9. **Add the block to the input hash** as a new `inbox_activity` part, so the changed-inputs record of #129256 names it. Hash only the lines of strength `RATED` or stronger, by report id and fact, with no ages. An open or a discussion, when the payload includes them, shows in the next build but does not start one. Most scheduled checks find no change and skip the model call. This rule keeps that true.
10. **Bump `PROMPT_VERSION`.**
11. **Record counts on `personal inbox ranking built`:** `inbox_activity_lines`, `inbox_activity_candidate_lines`, and the count by strength. No titles and no note text.

Example of the block:

```text
# Recent inbox activity
- c7 | 2d ago | "Checkout funnel drops at the payment step" | rated it down
- 1d ago | "Export job times out for large cohorts" | claimed the work, linked a pull request
- 3d ago | "Stale flag still evaluated in onboarding" | dismissed it as not interested (not relevant to this project)
- 4d ago | "Session recordings missing on Safari" | rated it up
- 4d ago | "Batch export retries flood the queue" | removed themselves as reviewer
- 5d ago | dismissed 14 reports at once
- asked not to review: example-org/billing-service
```

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] With `inbox_activity_lines` at 0, the user message, the input hash and the build count are the same as today, apart from the prompt version.
- [ ] With a line count set, the block holds at most that many lines, strongest first, and only activity inside `inbox_activity_days`.
- [ ] A line for a candidate report starts with that candidate's ref. A test covers a candidate line and a non-candidate line.
- [ ] Entries that a task or agent wrote, deleted reports, single opens and bulk triage follow the rules of the activity summary. The fact and wording helpers have one definition.
- [ ] A correction where the person removes themselves, adds themselves, or only changes other people renders the matching line. A test covers each. The activity summary renders the same three lines.
- [ ] Active exclusions where the person is the subject show as lines, up to the limit, with no instruction text. A revoked exclusion does not show. An exclusion that changes is part of the input hash.
- [ ] Another person's activity on the same reports never appears. The read filters on the user and the project.
- [ ] A new claim, dismissal, note or rating changes the input hash. A new open alon

## Problem

- Evaluation reports render the agent's markdown as written. The agent reads customer traces, so a prompt injection can add phishing links or tracking images.
- A member blocked from a property can read a colleague's cached text view of a trace for an hour.
- Signed-in users can call the paid translation model without a limit.

- The text view cache key hashes the submitted payload, so one member's copy of an event never serves another.
- Translation throttles keep one bucket per member, shared across their keys.
- Deletes two unused sentiment throttles.

## Problem

The memory upkeep scout (`signals-scout-dreaming`) ships a structured-output schema and writes one record per change it makes.
No scout and no product surface reads those records.
Other scouts learn what the upkeep scout did from its `dream:digest:<skill-name>` entries and from the run prompt's _Memory upkeep_ section.

The records were added to give us data to explore while the scout was new.
They are not part of the scout we plan to release to all teams, so the canonical skill now differs from the release version.
They also cost a few tool calls per run and about 15 lines of skill text.

## Proposed change

Remove the record channel from the canonical skill, so the version we test is the version we release.

In `products/signals/skills/signals-scout-dreaming/`:

- Delete `references/structured-output.schema.json`.
- Remove the `scout-structured-output-schema` frontmatter line from `SKILL.md`.
- Remove the structured-output mentions from the `compatibility` frontmatter.
- Remove the record sentence from the intro ("one structured-output record per change").
- Remove the two record sentences from _Candidates_.
- Remove the record paragraph from _Close out_. Keep the run summary list.
- Reword "Leaving an entry is not a change and gets no record" and "record the skip", so a skipped conflict goes in the run summary.

Elsewhere:

- `products/signals/skills/AGENTS.md`: update the `signals-scout-dreaming/` entry, and the line that says which scouts ship a schema.
- `products/signals/backend/test/test_scout_harness_lazy_seed.py`: delete `test_dreaming_schema_accepts_a_change_record_and_refuses_entry_content`, because it tests the deleted file.

### Configs seeded earlier

A config that was seeded with the schema keeps its copy, and the harness renders the _Structured output_ section from the config, not from the skill.
So a team that already runs the scout would still be told to produce records after this change.

`products/signals/skills/AGENTS.md` says the config API refuses to clear a shipped schema to null on a canonical scout.
Check whether that refusal still applies when the skill no longer ships a schema.

- If the API allows the clear, clear the column on the seeded configs after the skill change is live.
- If it does not, this change needs a data migration that sets `structured_output_schema` to null for this skill's configs.

The scout is withheld fleet-wide, so few configs are affected.

### Also in this change

Remove the line "It names no person." from _Candidates_.
A candidate that names the people in its evidence is easier for an agent to use, and learnings already name people.
Keep the sentence that a person candidate holds routing verdicts only.

## What we lose

- The only structured log of what the upkeep scout changed in other scouts' memory. The digests and the run summary still say what changed, as text.
- Any insight, view or quality check that reads these `$scout_structured_output` events stops getting new rows. Move each one to digests and run summaries, or remove it.

## Done when

- The skill has no schema file, no frontmatter line and no record steps, and the skill sync passes.
- A run on a team that was seeded earlier shows no _Structured output_ section in its prompt and makes no `scout-record-output` call.
- The run summary still lists every change, including skipped conflicts.

## Problem

The activity summary MVP (#119839, #119919, shipped in #119884 and #120034) runs as an offline Dagster job over PostHog's own analytics data. It showed the summaries and their cost are workable, but it cannot become the feature:

- Its MCP input exists only as usage events in one internal analytics project, so it cannot run in-region for any other project.
- It stores summaries as Parquet partitions, not as state a product surface can read or update.
- It cannot run in a local dev stack, so iterating on the filters and the prompt needs a prod run.

The next step builds the core of the feature inside the signals product: one stored summary per (project, user), updated from in-region data, runnable locally from a command.

## Changes

New package `products/signals/backend/activity_summary/`. No new product. No schedule, endpoint or MCP tool in this issue.

### 1. Move the reusable code, then retire the Dagster package

Move these from `products/signals/dags/inbox_ranking/activity_summary/` into the new package: `render.py` and `prompt.py`, the `summarize` and `cost_usd` logic from `summaries.py`, and the input readers `member_tasks` and `member_activity` (with `TASK_ORIGIN_PRODUCTS`) from `dag.py`.

Then delete the Dagster activity summary pipeline. It was an offline MVP, and this package replaces it:

- the `products/signals/dags/inbox_ranking/activity_summary/` package, including its MCP event queries, the cost projection, and the summaries and embeddings assets
- the `activity_summary_job` and `activity_summary_schedule` registration in `posthog/dags/locations/signals.py`
- the activity summary section of `products/signals/dags/inbox_ranking/README.md`
- `products/signals/dags/inbox_ranking/tests/test_activity_summary.py`, after moving the tests that cover the moved code into the new package

The MCP-specific rendering (`McpCall`, `McpSession`, `mcp_unit`, `job_intents` and the MCP drop rules) has no caller once the Dagster package is gone, so drop it too. Git history keeps it for when an in-region MCP source exists. Leave the Parquet partitions the job already wrote in object storage as they are.

### 2. Inputs: tasks and the activity log, in-region only

For one (team, user) and a time window:

- **Tasks:** `list_user_task_summaries` from `products/tasks/backend/facade/user_task_summaries.py`, with the origin products and drop rules the Dagster inputs already use.
- **Activity log:** `ActivityLog` rows for the user in the team, with the existing filters (no `is_system`, no impersonated rows, no `scout:` clients, the tag and auto-named drops).
  - Also read the agent intent at `detail.trigger.payload.intent`. Since #100741 the MCP server sends it with every write it makes, and the activity log stores it on the row. Render it next to the changed object, for example `updated insight "Signup funnel" (agent: <intent>)`, through the same `clean_text` and per-line caps as other free text.
- **No MCP usage events.** Read-only MCP sessions stay out until an in-region source exists.

### 3. Hardening, applied in the moved code

1. **Redact URLs to their host.** `clean_text` strips query strings and fragments, but a secret can sit in a URL path. Replace every full URL with its host, for example `[link example.com]`. Add an invented path secret to the golden fixtures for each input source.
2. **Cap the completion.** Set `max_completion_tokens` from a named constant (around 600). Treat a truncated answer (`finish_reason == "length"`) as malformed, so the existing retry and `failed` paths handle it. Also cap the length of each focus area topic, product and `recent_shift` in `normalize_summary`.
3. **Unknown usage is null, not zero.** When a response has no `usage`, `tokens_in`, `tokens_out` and `cost_usd` are null.

### 4. Model

`UserActivitySummary` in the signals models, team-scoped with `TeamScopedRootMixin`, unique on (team, user). Follow `/django-migrations`.

- **Output:** `summary` (JSON), `summary_text`, `generated_at`, `model`, `prompt_version`, `render_version`
- **Accounting:** `tokens_in`, `tokens_out`, `cost_usd` (all nullable), `inputs_used` (JSON: line counts per section and drop counts per rule)
- **State:** `status` (`ok`, `failed`), `input_watermark` (the newest input timestamp included), `next_eligible_at`
- **Cascades:** deleting the user or the team deletes the row.

No embedding column and no version table in this issue.

### 5. `update_activity_summary(team_id, user_id, *, dry_run=False)`

One update for one (team, user). A command, a later Temporal workflow and the tests can all call it.

1. Skip if the organization has not approved AI data processing, or if `next_eligible_at` is in the future (unless forced).
2. Gather inputs since `input_watermark`. On a first run, gather the last 28 days.
3. If fewer than `MIN_UNITS` (3) units survive the filters, stop and write nothing.
4. Render the input and call the model once through `build_openai_client(product="signals", ai_product="activity_summary", ...)` from `posthog/llm/gateway_client.py`, with the stored summary as the previous summary. Model `gpt-6-luna`. Pass a fixed pipeline distinct id as both `distinct_id` and `user=`. Do not set `$ai_`-prefixed property keys.
5. On success, save the output and accounting, advance `input_watermark`, and set `next_eligible_at` to one day later. On failure, set `status = failed`, record the error, and leave the stored summary and the watermark unchanged.
6. Return a frozen result with the rendered input, the summary, the accounting and the drop counts.

With `dry_run=True`, nothing is written.

### 6. Management command

`run_activity_summary --team-id N --user-id N [--dry-run] [--force]`. It prints the rendered input, the summary, the token counts, the cost and the drop counts per rule. This is the local dogfood loop for the filters and the prompt.

## Acceptance criteria

- The golden-fixture tests for the task and activity log drop rules and rendering move with the code and still pass.
- The Dagster activity summary package, its job and schedule, and its README section are gone. Nothing imports from `products/signals/dags/inbox_ranking/activity_summary`, and `check-dagster-paths.py` passes.
- New tests, with the LLM mocked at the boundary (follow `/writing-tests`):
  - a secret in a URL path never reaches the rendered input
  - a truncated completion is retried, then recorded as `failed`
  - missing usage gives null tokens and cost
  - an activity log row with an agent intent renders it, and one without an intent renders as before
  - fewer than `MIN_UNITS` units writes nothing
  - a successful update advances the watermark, and a failed one does not
  - `dry_run` writes nothing
- The command runs against a local dev stack with a configured gateway.
- No text other than the rendered input reaches the model.

## Out of scope

The daily schedule and per-user workflow, the feature flag, embeddings, the `activity summary generated` event, the read endpoint, the MCP tool, opt-out, and an in-region source for read-only MCP sessions. These are follow-up issues.
