- **Session:** PostHog inbox report implementation from Slack; PostHog MCP, gh, hogli.

## Problem

`inbox-report-actions-run` can start a different suggested prompt from the one the caller picked.

`inbox-report-actions-list` returns each suggested prompt with a `suggested_prompt_index`, and the caller sends that index to the run endpoint.
`resolve_report_task_action` in `products/signals/backend/report_task_actions.py` then reads the prompt at that position in the report's current list.

A scout can rewrite a report's suggested prompts between the two calls.
The index then points at another prompt, or at nothing.
When it points at another prompt, the run starts work that nobody asked for, and the response does not show this.
These runs start in the background and cannot ask a question, so nobody can catch the mismatch before the work starts.

## What to build

1. Let the caller prove which prompt it picked.
   Add an optional `suggested_prompt_text` field to `SignalReportTaskActionRunRequestSerializer`, holding the `text` from the list response.
2. When the field is present and does not match the prompt at that index, start nothing.
   Return an error with a new code, `report_action_prompt_changed`, through `SignalReportTaskActionErrorSerializer`.
   Use the 409 status, and tell the caller to list the actions again.
3. Keep calls without the field working, because existing clients do not send it.
4. Update the `inbox-report-actions-run` description in `products/signals/mcp/tools.yaml`, so that agents pass the text and know how to handle the new error.
   Regenerate the OpenAPI types and MCP schema.

Compare the text exactly.
Do not resolve the prompt from the text alone, because the index still selects the entry and its eligibility.

## Out of scope

- Changing how scouts write suggested prompts.
- The `ask`, `get_it_merged` and `make_it_green` actions, which have no index.

## Tests

Extend `products/signals/backend/test/test_report_task_actions_api.py`:

- A call with text that no longer matches the prompt at that index returns the new error and creates no task.
- A call with no text still runs the prompt at that index.

Related: #119180, #119181.

## Problem

Analysts must rerun a notebook and click **Replace rows** before downstream SQL sees fresh results. [#140517](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/pull/140517)

## Changes

An agent can now run a notebook between SQL models in PostHog’s warehouse DAG. For example, SQL totals sales, Python forecasts demand, and SQL lists items to reorder.

- **Declare** a table from a SQL or Python cell and name its upstream models.
- **Refresh** daily or on demand. Each run publishes the cell’s full dataframe.
- **Inspect** failed cells and the last published run. A failed refresh preserves the table and skips dependent SQL.

### Before

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A[Run notebook] --> B[Save or replace rows in browser] --> C[Warehouse table]
    classDef phYellow fill:#f9bd2b,stroke:#f9bd2b,color:#000;
    classDef phBlue fill:#1d4aff,stroke:#1d4aff,color:#fff;
    classDef phGray fill:#e5e7eb,stroke:#c7ccd1,color:#000;
    class A phYellow;
    class B phBlue;
    class C phGray;
```

### After

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A[SQL model: total sales by item] --> B[Notebook Python cell: forecast demand] --> C[demand_forecast table] --> D[SQL model: list items to reorder]
    classDef phYellow fill:#f9bd2b,stroke:#f9bd2b,color:#000;
    classDef phBlue fill:#1d4aff,stroke:#1d4aff,color:#fff;
    classDef phGray fill:#e5e7eb,stroke:#c7ccd1,color:#000;
    class A,D phYellow;
    class B phBlue;
    class C phGray;
```

<details>
<summary>Using the three MCP tools</summary>

Enable `notebook-warehouse-models` for MCP after the Django routes deploy.

| Tool | How to use it for the reorder report |
| --- | --- |
| `notebooks-declare-warehouse-model` | Choose the forecast cell, name its table `demand_forecast`, and pass the sales model’s node ID as an upstream dependency. |
| `notebooks-run-warehouse-model` | Start the model and its upstream dependencies now. After the first publication, reference `demand_forecast` in the downstream SQL model. |
| `notebooks-warehouse-model-status` | Pass the returned `dag_run_id` to see whether the run reached the notebook. Inspect cell errors and the run that produced the current table. |

Each run executes the saved notebook through the selected cell. First publication requires an unused table name. Later refreshes keep the table ID. Runs that share a notebook wait their turn, and previous generations remain readable for 24 hours.

</details>

## How did you test this code?

**Test rationale:** [Warehouse tests](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/blob/87e6096958bc3cec744ba3caafb234df509f0339/posthog/api/test/notebooks/test_warehouse_model.py#L217) cover replacement. [DAG tests](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/blob/87e6096958bc3cec744ba3caafb234df509f0339/products/data_modeling/backend/temporal/tests/test_execute_dag_workflow.py#L635) cover failure propagation.

<details>
<summary>CI advisories and regression coverage</summary>

The warehouse round trip read 14,000 synthetic rows on each of two refreshes. A failed third refresh preserved the second table. A local Temporal test used a stub notebook task to check dependency ordering.

The API test checks that the returned ticket identifies the queued Temporal run and that polling uses the same project, node, and ticket. The workflow tests exercise the receiver. Time-skipping tests cover a busy notebook, downstream failure, and delayed cleanup. A warehouse round trip reads both generations across replacement.

CI measured a 7.7 KiB decrease in total frontend bundle size. Of the two eager roots over budget, logged-out boot had zero growth and the authenticated shell grew 3.5 KiB against the CI baseline. The frontend diff only regenerates the notebook API. No browser code imports the new client functions or schemas. CI also shows changes in the Today sidebar chunks, outside this diff.

The database migration creates one table with a primary key on `node_id`, its node foreign key, and an index on `team_id`. The migration analyzer classified it as safe. Five Chromium cases passed on retry. Two exercise editing or deleting an ordinary notebook. The other three cover person properties, insight titles, and workflow secrets. None of the five exercises model declaration, DAG execution, or warehouse publication.

</details>

## Release status

- This change is behind a feature flag and is not available to users <!-- release-status: behind-feature-flag -->

## Docs update

[Warehouse modeling guide](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/blob/87e6096958bc3cec744ba3caafb234df509f0339/docs/published/handbook/engineering/data-warehouse.md#L117)

## 🤖 Agent context

**Autonomy:** Human-driven (agent-assisted)

**Agent:** OpenAI Codex, GPT-6

**Skills:** `/improving-drf-endpoints`, `/implementing-mcp-tools`, `/django-migrations`, `/writing-tests`, `/verifying-changes`, `/writing-dataclasses`, `/writing-code-comments`, `/writing-user-facing-copy`, `/run-posthog`, `/writing-clickhouse-queries`, `/isolating-product-facade-contracts`, `/running-ci-preflight`, `/debugging-ci-failures`, `/security-audit`, `/querying-local-postgres`, `/writing-pr-descriptions`

**Driver checked:** Not yet checked by the driver

**Security review:** needed

<details>
<summary>More context for AI agents</summary>

- **Decisions:** Model declarations pin the selected cells and variables. Edits require redeclaration.
- **Read closely:** Publication checks author access again and serializes competing table replacements.
- **Verification:** Automated tests used generated inventory rows and local services. Production sandbox execution is unverified.

</details>

## Is your feature request related to a problem?

Teams compose long prompts in source code and interpolate variables at runtime. The prompt page shows variables, which is useful at a glance for long prompts, but users cannot do much with them in the UI. To test a prompt with real values, they must copy it out and fill the variables by hand.

## Describe the solution you'd like

1. In the playground, let users enter a value for each variable in the prompt and run the prompt with those values.
2. Optionally, save sets of variable values as test inputs, so that users can run the same inputs again after they edit the prompt.
3. Make variables more useful on the prompt page, for example a list of variables with where each one is used. We currently show a list of all variables used in a per-prompt view.

## Describe alternatives you've considered

Interpolation in application code only. This works at runtime, but gives no way to test in PostHog.

## Additional context

From customer feedback on prompt management.

## Is your feature request related to a problem?

The same prompt often needs different wording for different model families (for example one version tuned for one provider and one for another). Today teams must create separate prompts with no link between them, and must keep them in sync by hand.

## Describe the solution you'd like

Prompt variants: a way to create variants of a prompt per model family, and to mark them as related. For example:

- A parent prompt with variants keyed by model family.
- Fetch by prompt name plus model family, with a fallback to the default variant.
- The UI shows the variants side by side, so that users can compare them and keep them aligned.

## Describe alternatives you've considered

Separate prompts with a naming convention. There is no link between them, and nothing shows when one variant is out of date.

## Additional context

From customer feedback on prompt management.

hits.body:
## Problem

When you drop into a task you did not just write, there is no cheap way to learn what it was about. You re-read the run log or the chat. With ten tasks open in the desktop app, that cost repeats every time you switch.

Today nothing maintains a description of the work as it happens:

- `Task.title` is generated once from the opening prompt (`title_generator.py`) and only when the title is empty. Follow-up runs never re-title it, so it drifts from what the task became.
- `TaskRun.output["final_message"]` is the agent's last chat turn, captured verbatim in `relay_sandbox_events.py` with a 20k character cap. It is per run, it is optional, and it is missing whenever the agent ends without a proper closing message or the run is cancelled.
- The terminal transition does bookkeeping only. There is no summarization pass, and we do not want one on the path that must not fail.
- Run logs can be very large. A one-shot summary over the transcript is a research task, not a summarization task, and would pay to reconstruct intent the agent already had in context.

Origin thread: https://posthog.slack.com/archives/C09KTRWD3HD/p1787655148271769

## Proposal

Let the agent maintain a short summary of the task as it works, through a tool it already knows how to call. No server-side inference. A few hundred output tokens per update plus one small write.

This is the same shape as Coder's `coder_report_task` MCP tool ([codersdk/toolsdk](https://github.com/coder/coder/blob/main/codersdk/toolsdk/toolsdk.go)), which has been in production a while. The difference is that theirs is an append-only status feed. Ours should be a replaced summary, so it self-compacts and stays scannable.

### v0 scope (minimal)

Start as small as possible and measure whether agents actually use it before adding any schema or surfaces.

1. **One tool, `task_summary_update(summary)`**, exposed in the sandbox session by the agent-server. It writes `{"summary": text}` into the run's `output` through the existing `set_output` endpoint (`posthog-api.ts` already calls it with the run token). No new endpoint, no migration.
   - Replace, not append. Each call overwrites the whole summary.
   - Hard cap enforced server-side in `validate_set_output`, on the order of 1.5k characters. The cap is what forces the compression that makes it useful. An over-long call returns an error, as Coder does.
   - Tool description carries good and bad examples inline, and asks for a self-contained summary that names the repo, product, files, and PRs explicitly. Retrofitting that across a corpus later is expensive, so it goes in on day one.
2. **One prompt nudge**, in the same slot the loop system prompt uses for "your final message is the run's report" (`loop_runs.py`). Call the tool when the goal changes, when a route is abandoned, roughly every ten turns, and before ending the turn. Keep it cheap.
3. **Carry the summary into follow-up runs.** On a new run for a task that already has a summary on its latest run, put it in the initial context so the agent extends rather than restarts. It is short, so this costs almost nothing, and it doubles as a handoff between runs.
4. **Show it in the desktop sidebar.** Hover on a task row (`TaskRow.tsx`) shows the latest run's summary. Fall back to the first few hundred characters of `final_message` when there is no summary, so the tooltip is never empty.
5. **Measure adoption.** Add `has_summary` to the `task_run_completed` event so we can see what share of runs ever call the tool, and how stale the summary is at completion.

### Suggested summary shape

Light structure inside the cap, so it also works as search and embedding material later:

- What the task is trying to do
- Why, in one line
- Current state, including dead ends and why they were abandoned
- Where: files, branches, PRs
- Open questions or things that need a human

### Explicitly out of scope for v0

- A `Task.summary` column, `summary_updated_at`, and a `summary_manually_set` flag mirroring `title_manually_set`. Do this once v0 shows agents call the tool.
- Exposing the summary on `system.tasks` in HogQL.
- Server-side fallback summarization from the transcript, or a structured digest of files touched, PR state, and CI status.
- Any append-only progress log. The workflow's `_emit_progress` already covers "what is it doing right now".
- Feeding summaries into the context store, embeddings, or clustering.
- Injecting "summary is N turns stale" reminders from `relay_sandbox_events` on `end_of_turn`.

## Why this shape

- The agent knows intent and dead ends for free at the moment they happen. "Tried the Temporal activity route, dropped it because the terminal path cannot take a failure mode" is not recoverable from a log at any reasonable cost.
- Self-reported summaries skew optimistic. That is fine for "what was this about" and not safe as an input to judging whether a run succeeded, so keep it out of quality signals.
- Coder found the tool description alone does not get agents to report often enough. They allowlist the tool and inject the instruction into always-loaded context. Expect to do the same, which is why the prompt nudge is part of v0 rather than a follow-up.

## Later uses this unlocks

- Semantic search over tasks by summary, not just title.
- Scouts that watch your own tasks to learn what you are working on and care about.
- Cheaper input for the context layer to decide what is worth dreaming on.
- Summaries of an "ask about it" session fed back to the scout that raised the report, instead of raw quotes.
- With PostHog AI conversations and tasks converging, a title plus summary per chat that can be embedded and clustered per user.

## Open questions

- Run-level `output["summary"]` in v0 versus a task-level column from the start. Run-level costs nothing today and the latest run's summary is the task summary in practice. The column is the right home once we know the tool gets called.
- Exact cap. Coder uses 160 characters for a status line. A drop-in summary wants more, but not much more.
- Whether to also fold the summary before context compaction, where the agent is already distilling state. Depends on what the agent adapters expose.

## Problem

- AI prompt subscription reports run on gpt-4.1, about 12× the cost of gpt-6-luna.
- Luna alone drops the previous-period comparison that "what changed" prompts need.
- Stacked on PostHog/posthog#134824.

## Changes

- Reports run on gpt-6-luna at low effort and cost about 91% less.
- Planning lists what the prompt asks for, then a check sends only the gaps to one repair call:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A[Event selection] --> B{{Planner}} --> C[Run queries]
  classDef phBlue fill:#1d4aff,stroke:#1d4aff,color:#fff;
  classDef phGray fill:#e5e7eb,stroke:#c7ccd1,color:#000;
  class B phBlue; class A,C phGray;
```

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A[Event selection] --> K{{Coverage list}} --> B{{Planner}} --> X[Plan check]
  X -->|all covered| C[Run queries]
  X -->|gaps| R{{Repair, gaps only}} --> C
  classDef phBlue fill:#1d4aff,stroke:#1d4aff,color:#fff;
  classDef phGray fill:#e5e7eb,stroke:#c7ccd1,color:#000;
  class K,B,R phBlue; class A,X,C phGray;
```

- Results on 10 prompts, local demo data:

| | gpt-4.1 | luna, one pass | luna, multi-pass |
|---|---|---|---|
| Cost per new report | $0.0222 | $0.0017 | $0.0019 |
| Failed queries | 1 | 0 | 0 |
| Prompts better than gpt-4.1 | – | 3 | 4 |
| Prompts worse than gpt-4.1 | – | 2 | 0 |
| Median planning time | 4.9 s | 7.2 s | 10.7 s |

> [!NOTE]
> Every existing subscription re-plans once on its next send (`AI_QUERY_PLAN_VERSION` 9).

<details>
<summary>Per-prompt verdicts</summary>

| Prompt | gpt-4.1 | luna, multi-pass |
|---|---|---|
| Signups and activation, anything unusual | Caught the 4→0 drop | Same, plus activation drops |
| Biggest event growth and drops | Good | Same |
| File uploads vs last period | Good | Same |
| Top 5 pages and changes | Good | Same |
| Weekly actives who came back | Return query failed | Answered |
| Signups vs previous period, sharp days | Flagged day misaligned | Flagged the aligned day |
| Percent change for three events | Good | Same |
| Events that stopped firing | Join bug, empty report | Listed all 12 |
| Features gone quiet | Wrongly said none | Found 1, checked 2 events |

Prices from `nodejs/src/ingestion/pipelines/ai/costs/providers/llm-costs.json`. Costs count cached, output and reasoning tokens. gpt-4.1 had 73% cache hits on planner input, and luna had none. With no cache, gpt-4.1 costs $0.0352. A send that reuses its plan pays only for the summary: $0.0099 against $0.0007.

</details>

## How did you test this code?

**Test rationale:** New tests go red when the plan check stops catching constant queries or dropped comparisons.

## Release status

- No feature flag controls this change <!-- release-status: no-feature-flag -->

## Docs update

- None.

## 🤖 Agent context

**Autonomy:** Human-driven (agent-assisted)

**Agent:** Claude Code, Claude Opus 5.5

**Skills:** `/stacking-prs`, `/writing-code-comments`, `/writing-tests`, `/writing-pr-descriptions`

**Security review:** not needed

<details>
<summary>More context for AI agents</summary>

- **Decisions:** Multi-pass replaced the single planner call instead of sitting behind a flag, because the comparison favored it on every prompt.
- **Decisions:** The plan version bump re-plans old subscriptions so they also gain the comparison coverage.
- **Follow-ups:** Event selection picks too few events for "features gone quiet" prompts. The planner cannot fix that.
- **Follow-ups:** The repair call never fired in live runs. Only unit tests exercise it.
- **Read closely:** `generate_query_plan` and `check_plan_coverage` in `spec_generator.py`.

</details>

hits.body:
## Problem

The AI judgment (`llm`) detector for insight alerts gave a false positive on an hourly dogfood alert. The alert fired on three weekday night hours in a row. The values at these hours were in the usual range for the same hours on recent weekdays, and the weekday daily totals were flat.

The model's rationale compared the current weekday night hour with the lower weekend night level. It also said the level had "stayed elevated for days" and still reported a `level_shift`.

## Root causes

1. **No weekday in date labels.** The point table and the "current point" line use plain ISO labels (for example `2026-11-06 03:00:00`). The model must calculate the weekday itself, and a small model does this badly. As a result, it mixed weekday and weekend points into one baseline.
2. **Same hour last week is just outside the window.** The hourly lookback is 168 points and ends at the current point, so the same hour one week ago is the first point that is cut off.
3. **The prompt gives no method to build a baseline.** The system prompt says that daily and weekly seasonality is normal, but it does not tell the model which points to compare with the current point.
4. **No rule for a "new normal".** The "sustained problem" paragraph tells the model to report a metric that is still abnormal. It does not say that a level that holds for most of the window, and that this alert did not flag, is the baseline.
5. **Author numbers win over data.** The author's instructions gave an approximate level that was out of date. The model used that level instead of the level in the data.

## Proposed fix

All changes are in `products/alerts/backend/judge/prompt.py`, except the optional item 5. No change adds a model call.

1. **Weekday in dated labels.** For intervals of one day or less, show labels like `Fri 2026-11-06 03:00` in the table and in the "current point" line. `triggered_dates` continue to come from `context.dates`, so nothing downstream changes.
2. **Same-slot reference line, computed in code.** Add one line to the human message before the table:
   - Hourly: the values at the same hour of day on earlier days in the window, split into weekdays and weekend days.
   - Daily: the values on the same weekday in the window.
   - Do not add it for undated series or for intervals of one week or more.
3. **System prompt rules:**
   - Build the baseline from comparable points (same hour of day, same type of day). Name that baseline in the rationale.
   - A level that holds for most of the window and that this alert did not flag is the baseline. Report `level_shift` only when the change is recent and the earlier part of the window is at a different level. Make the "sustained problem" paragraph agree with this rule: a sustained problem is still abnormal compared with the level before the change started.
   - Numbers about level in the author's instructions are hints. When the data do not agree, the data define normal. The author's instructions continue to set the direction and how sensitive the alert is.
4. **Bump `PROMPT_REVISION` from 3 to 4.** This already resets the verdict memo.
5. **Optional:** change the hourly lookback in `posthog/tasks/alerts/detector.py` from 168 to 192, so the same hour last week is in the window. Cost: about 14% more input tokens for each hourly check.

## Tests

In `products/alerts/backend/test/test_llm_judge.py`:

- Dated labels have the weekday, for hourly and daily series.
- The reference line is present for hourly and daily series and has the correct values. It is absent for undated series and for weekly series.
- Update the current assertion on the table row for the current point to use the new label.
- The existing test that a `PROMPT_REVISION` change needs a new verdict continues to pass.

## How to verify

- There is no offline eval for this detector yet. Preview one live check on the alert that failed, for the hours that fired. It must not fire.
- After deploy, compare the firing rate of the internal AI judgment alerts for one week before and one week after the change. Look at `$insight_alert_firing` events with `detector_type = llm`.

Context: [Slack thread](https://posthog.slack.com/archives/C0BQ8KW9Q5B/p1793965617614389?thread_ts=1793965617.614389&cid=C0BQ8KW9Q5B)

## Problem

- Nothing reads the observations' rank JSON after the layer below, but three indexes on it still cost about 6.5 GB and write load on every observation update.
- Cold Highlights loads spend most of their time reading candidates' snapshot JSON for an experiment check the entries already make.

## Changes

- Drops `rlo_ranked_count_idx`, `rlo_ranked_contrast_idx` and `rlo_ranked_feed_group_idx` concurrently.
- Hides `watch_rank` from the ORM with `deprecate_field(raise_on_access=True)`, so any leftover access fails loudly.
- Removes the rank copy backfill and the one-off prompt question backfill. The rank backfill now defaults to the 90-day feed window.
- A later migration drops the column, one deploy after this.
- Fixes two Highlights bugs from the layer below: the scanner type filter now keeps inline scanners, and a stale build no longer serves rows outside the load's window.
- Cold Highlights loads get faster with the same cards: the pick fetch skips the snapshot gate, and the endpoint still gates the served page.

## How did you test this code?

**Test rationale:** no migration drift. A new API test fails if a pick from an unreadable experiment takes a page slot.

## Release status

- No feature flag controls this change <!-- release-status: no-feature-flag -->

## Docs update

- None.

## 🤖 Agent context

**Autonomy:** Human-driven (agent-assisted)
**Tool:** Claude Code, Claude Opus 5.5
**Skills:** `/django-migrations`, `/simplify`, `/code-review`

## Problem

- Engineers cannot tell from the query log how often separate queries read the same data.

## Changes

- Every HogQL query gets a `read_signature` tag in `log_comment`. Nothing user-visible changes.
- Queries share a signature when they read the same tables, days and event names. Time of day and filters do not change it.
- Aliases, CTEs, subquery filters and self-joins resolve per SELECT scope.
- Unrecognized `timestamp` or `event` conditions are hashed in, with any timezone conversion kept.
- A fixed work budget caps the cost per query, including each copy made while resolving names.
- A failure leaves the tag empty and never fails the query.
- The v3 archive drops the tag. Stacked #134840 adds the column and migration.

## How did you test this code?

**Test rationale:** Unit cases, including each review finding, catch false and missed matches. The tagging test checks the tag reaches the log and a failure leaves the query working.

- Not checked: production query logs.
- Uncovered lines (19) are defensive fallbacks: unparseable bounds, unknown table keys and visitor no-op returns.
- The Playwright insight failure is unrelated; this diff touches no frontend or insight code.

## Release status

- No feature flag controls this change <!-- release-status: no-feature-flag -->

## Docs update

- None.

## 🤖 Agent context

**Autonomy:** Human-driven (agent-assisted)

**Agent:** Claude Code, `claude-fable-5-1` (signature) and `claude-opus-5-5` (scope rework)

**Skills:** `/writing-tests`, `/writing-code-comments`, `/writing-pr-descriptions`

**Security review:** not needed

<details>
<summary>More context for AI agents</summary>

- **Decisions:** The collector reads each SELECT scope separately, replacing one flat pass that review kept finding gaps in.
- **Decisions:** Bounds with a known timezone are UTC-normalized and marked, so they never match days in an unknown zone.
- **Follow-ups:** The `lc_read_signature` archive column and migration, then measuring overlap per dashboard refresh.
- **Read closely:** `posthog/hogql/cost/read_signature.py`, especially the opaque-hash fallbacks.
- **Public artifact:** Every query in the tests is invented. No query-log content is in the diff.

</details>

hits.body:
## Problem

Scouts have two output channels. The legacy `emit_signal` channel has a durable per-action ledger (`SignalScoutEmission`, one row per finding, written in the same transaction as the run's `emitted_count` bump). The `emit_report` / `edit_report` channel, which canonical scouts now use exclusively, records its actions in three places with three different shapes:

| Record | What it holds | Gap |
|---|---|---|
| `SignalReportArtefact` rows on the report (the report's activity log) | emit: a provenance `note`, a `task_run` link to the scout run, and the status artefacts (`safety_judgment`, `actionability_judgment`, `repo_selection`, `priority_judgment`, `suggested_reviewers`). edit: a `note` whose prose says which fields changed; chart / prompt edits are also notes; reviewer edits append a `suggested_reviewers` status artefact | Edits are untyped. The human edit path (`products/signals/backend/views.py`, report update) writes the typed `title_change` / `summary_change` artefacts with old and new values; the scout path (`scout_report/persistence.py`) writes a `note` with `updated_fields` baked into the text. Attribution is to the `task` FK, so the scout run is only reachable through the emit-time `task_run` artefact; edits carry no run identity. Notes are written only when `attribution is not None` |
| `SignalScoutRun.emitted_report_ids` / `edited_report_ids` | ordered append of authored report ids; deduped set of edited report ids | no timestamps, no record of what changed; the `derived` flags `has_emit_report` / `has_edit_report` are computed from these at finalize |
| `signals_scout_report_emitted` / `_edited` events | `report_id`, `outcome` (`surfaced` / `suppressed` / `gate_skipped`), `skipped_reason`, `updated_fields`, `note_appended`, content | explicitly best-effort ("a capture failure must never fail or mask the emit", `scout_harness/tools/report.py`); the only place `outcome` exists |

`SignalScoutEmission` itself is written only by `emit_finding` and every reader is finding-shaped (emissions endpoints, Slack delivery, the `recent_tag_usage` prompt loop). It is fully blind to the report channel.

Concrete symptom: the `signals_scouts_runs` warehouse view derives `emitted`, `emitted_finding_ids`, `report_ids`, `inbox_urls`, `time_to_first_emit_s`, `emitted_count_mirror` and `emission_count` from the legacy channel, so all of them read 0 / `[]` for every canonical scout run this month while the `has_emit_report` flag and `SignalReport`'s emitting-run linkage show thousands of emitting runs. The view's "per-run report attribution is not possible" caveat is the same defect: the attribution exists in the artefact log, the view reads the retired channel.

Origin: https://posthog.slack.com/archives/C09SK2PAGKF/p1787703636142209 (scout cost-per-unit work on the Scouts dashboard).

## Design evolution

The first cut of this issue proposed a new `SignalScoutReportAction` table as the report-channel sibling of `SignalScoutEmission`. On reading the persistence path that turned out to duplicate a ledger that already exists: every scout emit and edit already lands on the report as an append-only artefact, in the same transaction, which is exactly the durability argument the `SignalScoutEmission` docstring makes. What is missing is not a table but typed shape and a run key. So the proposal is now to make the artefact log the single durable record of scout report actions, and to key the warehouse view on it. The sibling table stays listed as the fallback if the one case the artefact log cannot hold (an emit that produced no report) turns out to matter.

## Proposal

Make `SignalReportArtefact` the single durable record of scout report actions.

### 1. Type the scout's edits (`scout_report/persistence.py`)

- Title / summary edits write `TitleChange` / `SummaryChange` artefacts with the old and new values, the same as the human edit path in `views.py`. Drop the prose `note` for content edits. `edit_report` then produces the same edit history whether a human or a scout made the change, and "what did the scout change" becomes a typed read instead of a note parse.
- Chart and suggested-prompt edits: either add typed content models (`charts_change`, `suggested_prompts_change`, with counts before and after) or keep the note but stamp the counts in a structured field. Preference: typed, for the same reason.
- Annotate (`note` with scout-authored text) stays a `note`; that is what it is.
- Reviewer edits already append a typed `suggested_reviewers` status artefact. No change.

### 2. Keep the run reachable from every scout artefact

- Attribution stays on the `task` FK. For scouts a task is one run in practice, but the mapping is indirect for edits (no `task_run` artefact is written on edit). Add the `task_run` log artefact on the first edit a run makes to a report it did not author, so the Runs section and the activity log surface the editing scout the same way they surface the authoring one. Keying stays `TaskRunArtefact(task_id, run_id, product="signals", type=<scout>)`.
- Write the typed edit artefacts regardless of `attribution`; unattributed today means "system", which is still an edit that happened. Keep the existing attribution when present.

### 3. Emit outcome

- `surfaced` and `suppressed` are already derivable on the report from the status artefacts and `status`. No new column.
- `gate_skipped` creates no report, so there is nothing to hang an artefact on. It stays event-only. If a durable count of gate-skipped emits is wanted later, that is the one case for a run-side row; see the fallback below.

### 4. Repoint the warehouse view (follow-up PR, /phs signals-dwh)

`signals_report_artefacts_base` already mirrors the artefact table for both regions. `signals_scouts_runs` derives `emitted` / `edited` / `report_ids` / `inbox_urls` / `time_to_first_emit_s` from artefacts keyed on the run's `task_id` (via `task_run` artefacts and `task` attribution) instead of `signals_signals_signal` and the `SignalScoutEmission` mirror. Legacy columns are renamed `*_signal_legacy` until the `emit_signal` tail reads 0. This is what unblocks exact per-run cost per report on the Scouts dashboard, which today allocates the whole fleet cost because per-run attribution reads the dead channel.

### 5. Retirement (separate, later)

Once `emit_signal` reads 0 sustained: retire `SignalScoutEmission`, `emitted_count`, `emitted_finding_ids` and their readers. `emitted_report_ids` / `edited_report_ids` stay: they are the GIN-indexed fast lookup that `dismissal_notes`, `billing.py` and `facade/api.py` query, and the source of the `derived` flags.

### Fallback: `SignalScoutReportAction`

If gate-skipped emits need a durable row, or if keying analytics on `task` attribution proves too indirect, add a narrow run-side ledger: `team`, `scout_run` FK, nullable `report` FK, `action` (emit / edit), `outcome`, `skipped_reason`, `created_at`, written in the same transaction as the array append. Not the first move, because it duplicates the artefact log for every case except the no-report one.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Scout title / summary edits write `title_change` / `summary_change` artefacts with old and new values; no content-edit `note` is written
- [ ] Chart and suggested-prompt edits write typed artefacts (or a note with structured counts, if typed is rejected in review)
- [ ] A run editing a report it did not author gets a `task_run` artefact on that report, once per run
- [ ] Typed edit artefacts are written for unattributed edits too
- [ ] Emit path unchanged apart from any shared helper refactor; the `task_run` artefact on emit still carries `run_id`
- [ ] The report activity log renders scout edits the same way it renders human edits (no frontend change expected; verify)
- [ ] Tests: scout title edit yields a `title_change` artefact with the prior title; an unchanged edit writes nothing; an edit by a non-authoring run adds exactly one `task_run` artefact across repeate

Robot: PostHog Slack app.

## Problem

**Why:** Schema and editor users can stall behind unrelated requests that sleep while waiting for concurrency slots.

<!-- posthog-self-driving-origin:01a11888-80ff-7069-acd2-a7c75cc4fb70 -->
## Origin

- Scout: a custom scout
- First signal: 2026-10-07
- Inbox report: [open](https://us.posthog.com/project/2/inbox/reports/01a11888-80ff-7069-acd2-a7c75cc4fb70?link_source=github_pr)
- Task started by: a person, from the inbox
<!-- /posthog-self-driving-origin:01a11888-80ff-7069-acd2-a7c75cc4fb70 -->

## Changes

- Foreground calls reject full limits immediately. The query API keeps HTTP 429 and `Retry-After`.
- Celery and Temporal jobs retain their retry and queue-wait budgets.

## How did you test this code?

- `hogli test posthog/clickhouse/client/test/test_limit.py::TestRateLimit`, Ruff, Oxfmt, and preflight.

**Test rationale:** Extends the full-limiter rejection test across retry and queue modes; factory tests protect background retries.

## Release status

- No feature flag controls this change <!-- release-status: no-feature-flag -->

## Docs update

- Updated the query performance guide.

## 🤖 Agent context

**Autonomy:** Human-driven (agent-assisted)

**Agent:** PostHog Slack app, GPT-6

**Skills:** `/paul-pair`, `/writing-tests`, `/verifying-changes`, `/running-ci-preflight`, `/writing-pr-descriptions`, `/writing-code-comments`, `/writing-dataclasses`, `/announcing-behavior-changes`, `/writing-user-facing-copy`, `/setting-up-devbox`, `/hogli`

**Driver checked:** Not yet checked by the driver

**Security review:** not needed

<details>
<summary>More context for AI agents</summary>

- **Session:** PostHog Slack app; Python 3.14.7.
- **Decisions:** Allow waits only in Celery or Temporal execution. This covers foreground callers without depending on request IDs or new SDK setup.
- **Follow-ups:** After deployment, compare browser p95, eventual completion rates, capacity retries, and worker utilization. Earlier 429 responses are expected.
- **Read closely:** Both wait paths in `RateLimit.use`. Quotas, bypass checks, and slot release remain unchanged.
- **Validation:** The new retry and queue cases failed before the fix. The limiter unit tests use in-memory Redis and a fake clock. Database-backed suites were not run locally because devbox access is unavailable. No endpoint schemas or public types change.
- **CI findings:** Preflight reports complexity 12 for `RateLimit.use`; the base also has complexity 12. No budget or ignore changes are needed. Markdown formatting passed with the pinned Oxfmt version despite preflight lacking a full Node workspace.
- **Trunk lane:** The backend Python lane is expected because this change affects the shared backend concurrency limiter. The CI report's lane warning requires no code change.
- **No duplicate:** Searches for open concurrency-wait and foreground fixes found no matching PR or issue.
- **Public artifact:** Private telemetry informed the diagnosis. No telemetry records, identifiers, or volumes appear in the committed files or this description. Tests use generic limiter inputs.

### Performance proof required before a speed claim

The unit tests prove that foreground admission does not sleep. They do not measure successful schema latency under contention. No end-to-end performance comparison or production canary has run.

1. Compare the PR's base commit and candidate with the same data, cache state, CPU allocation, and worker configuration. Keep the schema request shape identical.
2. First use one HTTP worker. Fill project A's concurrency slots before the measurement, send a contended A request, then send a schema request from project B. Measure B's successful response and the time before Django starts it. The candidate must free the worker promptly while preserving A's capacity response and its retry header.
3. Repeat with the normal worker pool and the same fixed user-action arrival trace. Include callers that honor `Retry-After`. Measure successful B response p50/p95/p99, completed actions, throughput, errors, and timeouts. Measure A's time from its first attempt to eventual success, plus its retries. A faster 429 response does not count as a successful latency improvement.
4. Repeat matched runs in alternating order. Accept the change only when B's successful p95 falls consistently without a loss of successful completion or throughput. Confirm that background retry behavior and concurrency quotas remain intact.
5. Verify the effect in a production canary after approval. Use separate worker pools with stable traffic assignment: a per-request flag in one shared pool also frees capacity for control requests and cannot cleanly measure the effect. Compare browser timings, upstream timings, worker utilization, and eventual completion at matched load.

</details>

## Problem

- A suggested judge can flood a team with false failures on calls its question does not cover. Calibration (#136179) never tests it on those calls, though the evaluation runs on them.

## Changes

- Calibration now tests the judge on calls the review marked not applicable, sharing slots with real passes in proportion. A fail there counts as a false alarm.
- A judge that fails those calls is no longer suggested.
- The published rate now counts every call the review labelled, as the evaluation's own rate does.

## Problem

Warehouse syncs keep running for organizations that are deactivated (`is_active=False`). They call sources, use worker time and can send alerts for an organization that must run no background work.

- Scheduled runs, resets and manual syncs for a deactivated organization now stop before a job is created. The run creates no job row, writes no status, sends no billing or failure alert and adds nothing to the failure streak.
- Nothing is paused or disabled, so syncs continue on their own after reactivation.
- An organization with `is_active=NULL` keeps syncing. If the organization lookup fails, the sync goes ahead, the same as the existing failing-schema deferral.

## Feature request

When a scout writes a report, return the open reports that look related to it, so the scout can check for a duplicate in the same run. Build it as a small set of matching rules, so more rules can be added later without changing the tool contract.

### Why

`scout-emit-report` has no duplicate matcher. The scout prompt tells every report scout to search the inbox before it authors, but that search is the scout's own judgment and uses the scout's own query words. Two scouts that reach the same topic from different sources (for example a Slack thread and the GitHub issue filed from it) can each author a report, and both reports then comment on the same issue.

Some overlaps are exact and need no judgment: two open reports that name the same GitHub issue or the same pull request. Others are a matter of similar wording. Both are useful hints, and more kinds of match are likely later, so the result must not be tied to one kind.

The pieces already exist:

- `search_reports` in `products/signals/backend/report_search.py` embeds a query and ranks reports by `cosineDistance` over the `title_summary_v1` report vectors.
- `open_report_for_source_issue` in `products/signals/backend/source_issues.py` finds open reports that name a GitHub issue.
- `SignalReportPullRequest` gives each pull request one identity per team (`repository`, `number`).
- `scout-emit-report` already returns `quality_hints`: a tuple of small checks that leave the report alone and tell the scout in the tool response (`products/signals/backend/scout_harness/tools/report_quality.py`). The matchers below follow the same pattern.
- The prompt already tells scouts to merge live duplicates with `inbox-reports-merge`.

### Behavior

These are hints. They never block, delay or reject a write, and the scout decides what to do with them.

1. After `emit_report` or `edit_report` persists, run each matcher that applies to that tool.
2. Each matcher returns candidate reports with a reason. Consider only live reports other than the one written. Exclude the statuses in `CLOSED_REPORT_STATUSES`.
3. Combine the candidates by report id. One report can carry several reasons.
4. Order them: reports with an exact reason first, then by similarity, highest first. Return at most 5. Make the limit a module constant.
5. Return them on the tool result as `related_reports`, next to `quality_hints`. Each entry has the report id, title, status, the list of reasons, and the similarity (null when no text matcher found it).
6. An empty list is the normal case and adds no text to the tool response.

### Matchers

Define a matcher as a small frozen object, in the same style as `_QualityCheck`: an id (which is also the reason string), the tools it runs on, and a function that takes the team and the written report and returns candidates. Keep the matchers in one tuple, so adding a rule is one new entry and its test. Do not build a plugin or registration system.

The first three:

| Matcher id | Runs on | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| `same_source_issue` | emit, and an edit that adds a source issue | Another open report names one of this report's source issues. |
| `same_pull_request` | emit, and an edit that adds a pull request | Another open report is linked to one of this report's pull requests. |
| `similar_text` | emit only | Cosine similarity of 0.75 or more on the title + summary vector, for reports authored by a different scout or by the pipeline. |

Notes on `similar_text`:

- Embed the report's title and summary with the same composition as `render_report_documents` uses for `title_summary_v1`. Use the title + summary vector, not the title vector: titles of the same topic from two scouts share few words.
- `_semantic_ranking` returns ids only. Expose the distance (a small helper that returns id and distance pairs), and reuse `NEAREST_REPORTS_SQL` and the existing retry and workload settings.
- Leave out reports authored by the same scout. A scout's own recurring reports (a daily or weekly series) are near-identical to each other and would fill the list on every run. The scout already follows its own series through its run history and scratchpad pointer.
- Make the threshold a module constant.

### Failure and time limits

- Each matcher fails on its own. An error or timeout in one matcher is logged and drops only that matcher's candidates.
- Give `similar_text` a short deadline (about 3 seconds for the embedding call and the vector read together). The exact matchers are indexed Postgres reads.
- The write must succeed and return its normal result whatever the matchers do.
- Skip all matchers for an idempotent replay, a gate-skipped emit, and a private trial run.

### Prompt

Add one sentence to the report-scout prompt in `scout_harness/prompt.py`, near the merge-duplicates guidance: when a write returns `related_reports`, read the closest ones, then merge with `inbox-reports-merge` when they cover the same issue, or say in the run summary why the new report is distinct. Phrase it as guidance, not a rule: a sibling scout may file a different angle on the same topic.

### Measurement

Capture one event for each write that ran the matchers, in the same way as `signals_scout_report_quality_hint`, with the scout properties plus:

- the tool (emit or edit),
- for each matcher: how many candidates it returned, its duration, and whether it failed or timed out,
- the top similarity `similar_text` found, also when it is below the threshold,
- the number of reports returned to the scout.

This shows how often each matcher fires for each scout, and gives the data to tune the threshold.

### Acceptance

- An emit whose text is close to an open report from another scout returns that report with the reason `similar_text` and its similarity.
- An emit, or an edit that adds a source issue, returns another open report that names the same issue with the reason `same_source_issue`.
- An emit, or an edit that adds a pull request, returns another open report linked to the same pull request with the reason `same_pull_request`.
- A report found by two matchers appears once, with both reasons.
- Exact matches sort before text matches.
- Closed, resolved, suppressed and deleted reports are never returned, and the written report is never returned for itself.
- `similar_text` never returns a report authored by the same scout.
- At most 5 reports come back.
- When one matcher fails or exceeds its deadline, the write still succeeds and the other matchers' results are returned.
- The event is captured with the top similarity for an emit below the threshold too.
- A test adds a fourth matcher to the tuple and shows that its candidates appear with its reason, with no change to the tool code.

### Not in scope

- Holding or rejecting a write until the scout confirms.
- `similar_text` on `scout-edit-report`.
- Merging reports automatically.
- Other matchers, for example a shared link in the report text. The matcher tuple is where they go later.

The scout suggestions scan builds the "Suggested for this project" list on the scouts tab. Its prompt describes the scout tools without naming them, so the agent guesses the names. ## Where

- `products/signals/backend/scout_harness/suggestions.py`, in `build_suggestions_prompt`:
  > Use the read-data, insight, dashboard, and signals-scout MCP tools (config list for the fleet, recent runs and reports for what the scouts already surface).

2. In the `scout_chat.py` templates, replace each "signals-scout MCP tools (…)" fallback with the exact `scout-*` tool names it means.

4. Bump the prompt version if the harness tracks one, so the change shows in run analytics.

## Not in scope

- Removing the `signals-scout-*` aliases. Do that after traffic on the old names stops (#126013).

## Done when

- No prompt under `products/signals/backend/` asks for scout tools by the `signals-scout` prefix or by description alone.

## Is your feature request related to a problem?

The chat agent has no scope guard. A question not related to the product (for example, "who is Darth Vader?") reaches the root agent and spends AI credits. The risk is cost and abuse as a free general chatbot.

## Describe the solution you'd like

Two options, which can be done in order.

### Prompt scope block

- Add a static `<scope>` section in the agent prompt.
- On an out-of-scope question the agent gives a short redirect, makes no tool calls, and stops.
- This changes behavior but saves little: the root agent call still happens.

### Gate before the root node

- A cheap model (`gpt-4.1-nano`) classifies each human message as in or out of scope.
- An out-of-scope message never reaches the root agent.
- If the classifier fails or is unsure, the message goes through.
- This adds one model call and some latency to every in-scope message, so it only saves tokens if enough traffic is off-topic.

### Scope definition

- In scope: the user's product, their data, general analytics or experimentation questions, general SQL help, and business questions about their own product.
- Out of scope: trivia, entertainment, homework, personal advice.

## Additional context

- No eval covers off-topic questions today, so add some, including borderline cases that should still be answered.
- This covers the chat agent only. The sandbox runtime, research agent, Slack app, and MCP are not covered.

## Problem

When the report summary workflow cannot select a GitHub repository, it does not park the report quietly. It overwrites the report's title and summary with a stock placeholder and moves the report to `pending_input`:

```
title:   Repository selection required
summary: Could not automatically select a repository: <reason>
```

Source: `products/signals/backend/temporal/summary.py`, the `repo_result.repository is None` branch right after `select_repository_activity`.

This is a dead end, not an intermediate state:

- The workflow returns after marking `pending_input` and never loops. The status table in `SignalReport.transition_to` only re-promotes reports to `candidate` from `potential` or `ready`, so a pending report stays pending until a human dismisses or snoozes it. Connecting GitHub later does not retry it.
- The dominant reason is `No GitHub integration connected to a team/user.` Most projects have no GitHub integration, so for those projects **every** report that clears clustering and safety review ends here. Research never runs.
- The report has no title before research runs, so the user sees the placeholder and nothing about the underlying finding. The clustered signals exist but are only reachable through a HogQL query.
- The Inbox detail view has no "connect GitHub" affordance for this state. The user gets a generic pending badge and a sentence about repository routing.

The inbox-report-rubrics scout flagged this shape as the single largest source of noise reports it sees, tracked in [this Inbox report](https://us.posthog.com/project/2/inbox/01a08a6b-3793-7090-b4bc-2395d2404d0e). The hourly share it measures across projects has held steady for days, which is what you would expect from a structural gap rather than a transient failure.

## Why this exists

The branch has been the intended fallback since agentic report generation landed (#51408). The pending reason was later made explicit so analytics could count it (#77187). Nothing regressed. The design assumed every project has a repository, and the Inbox now serves many projects that do not.

Two other paths in the same product already handle "no repository" without a placeholder:

- **Scout emit** (`products/signals/backend/scout_harness/tools/report.py`) returns `RepoSelectionResult(repository=None, reason="No GitHub integration; report lands without a draft PR.")` and the report lands as `ready`, just without PR autostart.
- **Custom agents** (`products/signals/backend/custom_agent/PLAN.md`, "Simplification history" item 3) removed their synthetic "Repository selection required" report and raise `CustomAgentRepositorySelectionError` instead.

The summary workflow is the one path that still turns a missing repo into a user-facing report.

## Options

**A. Research without a repository (recommended).** When `repo_result.repository is None`, still run `run_agentic_report_activity`, but in an MCP-only mode: no sandbox clone, no code search, no draft PR. The agent researches the signals against PostHog data and writes a real title and summary. The report lands as `ready` with `repo_selection.repository = None`, matching what scout emit already does. Autostart is skipped because there is no repository. The report detail view shows a "connect a repository to get a draft PR" hint on the existing Create PR affordance.

Cost: `run_agentic_report_activity` currently asserts a repository is present and passes it into the sandbox setup, so the activity needs a no-repo branch. The research prompt needs a variant that does not promise code findings.

**B. Hold the report in `candidate` until a repository exists.** Instead of `pending_input`, revert to `candidate` with a `pending_reason` of `repo_selection_required` and have the promotion rules skip teams with no GitHub integration. Add a one-time Inbox banner per project: "Connect GitHub to start receiving reports." When the integration lands, the pending candidates promote on the next cycle.

Cost: reports for repo-less projects never surface at all, so the Inbox is empty for them rather than full of placeholders. Simpler to build than A, but it makes Inbox a GitHub-only feature.

**C. Keep the state, fix the copy and the UI.** Leave the transition as is, but stop overwriting title and summary. Record the placeholder as the `error` field and a `note` artefact only. Render a distinct "Needs a repository" card in the Inbox with a connect-GitHub button and a retry that re-promotes the report to `candidate`.

Cost: the report still shows nothing about the finding. This only makes the dead end look intentional.

## Recommendation

Do A. It is the only option where a project with no GitHub integration gets value from Inbox, and it lines the summary workflow up with the scout-emit path that already exists. B is an acceptable fallback if the MCP-only research variant turns out to be a large piece of work.

Whichever option lands, the `pending_input` transition should stop writing the placeholder title and summary. If the report is not ready, its title should stay empty rather than carry pipeline routing text.

## Out of scope

- The rubrics scout appending hourly "still active" notes to the tracker report. That is a scout steering question, handled with a scout note, not code.
- A repository picker inside Inbox. `DismissCorrectedRepoField` covers the correction case already.

## Acceptance

- A project with no GitHub integration gets `ready` reports with a researched title and summary, and no draft PR.
- No report carries the title `Repository selection required` after this ships.
- The `signal_report_completed` event still records `pending_reason` for the remaining `pending_input` cases, so the analytics that count this shape keep working.
- An existing pending placeholder report is not migrated. It can be dismissed or snoozed as today.

## Problem

Internal test runs of eval suggestions showed three kinds of noisy cards:

- A failed-call card counted calls the app aborted on purpose (`AbortError`) as failures.
- A sensitive-data card counted placeholder addresses on non-English "example" domains.
- Prompt-injection judge cards came from decision-model screening that flags prompts and documents the model was asked to read. The examples did not hold up when checked.

## Changes

- The failed-call check treats `AbortError` as a cancellation, like `CancelledError`.
- The sensitive-data check skips a domain that is only a word for "example" plus a public suffix, such as `exemplo.com.br`. A registrable domain like `customer-example.com` still counts.
- Screening no longer asks about prompt injection, so no judge card is built from it. It can come back once the card's own judge confirms the examples.

## How did you test this code?

**Test rationale:** adapter rows for an aborted call, a placeholder domain and a near miss, and the applicability rows for the new judge lists. Each fails on master except the near miss.

hits.body:
## Problem

Activity summaries update incrementally. `update_activity_summary` (`products/signals/backend/activity_summary/logic.py`) sends the model the stored summary plus only the inputs after the stored `input_watermark`. It reads the full `WINDOW_DAYS` window only on a cold start, when no row exists.

`prompt_version` and `render_version` are stored on each row, but neither the queue (`queue.py`) nor the eligibility check reads them. When either version changes:

- An existing pair's first update under the new version starts from the summary the old version wrote, plus about one day of new inputs. A new output shape (for example a one-page `profile`) starts nearly empty and fills in over days.
- A fix to the inputs (for example the read-limit fix, or a new section such as viewed objects) applies only to inputs after the watermark. The older inputs never reach the new version.
- A pair with fewer than `min_units` new units keeps its old-version summary indefinitely.

While we iterate on the prompt and the inputs, we cannot compare versions, because no row shows what the new version makes from the full window.

## Changes

### 1. A stored summary is stale when its versions differ or it predates a rebuild

Add a pure function in `logic.py`:

```python
def is_stale(stored: UserActivitySummary, rebuild_before: datetime.datetime | None) -> bool
```

It returns true when any of these holds:

- `stored.prompt_version != PROMPT_VERSION`
- `stored.render_version != RENDER_VERSION`
- `rebuild_before` is set and `stored.generated_at` is null or earlier than `rebuild_before`

A row with no summary (`skipped`, or `failed` before any `ok`) is not stale. It is already a cold start.

### 2. A stale pair updates as a cold start

In `update_activity_summary`, when the stored row is stale:

- Read the full `WINDOW_DAYS` window (ignore `input_watermark`).
- Pass `previous_summary=None` to the model.
- Ignore `next_eligible_at` when `stored.status` is `ok`, so the rebuild does not wait for the daily interval. When the status is `failed` or `skipped`, keep the backoff, so a pair that fails does not run on every tick.
- On `ok`, write the current versions and the new watermark as usual. The row is then no longer stale.
- On a skip for too few units, keep the stored summary and back off as today. Do not delete it. Readers can see the old version on the row.

### 3. The queue finds stale pairs and puts them with the cold starts

In `select_pairs` (`queue.py`):

- Count new rows for a stale pair from `window_start`, not from its watermark. `_new_activity_rows` reads the watermark through a subquery. Make that subquery return null for a stale row, so `Coalesce` falls back to `window_start`. Do the same in `_new_tasks`.
- Pass `rebuild_before` from the config into this check.
- Sort stale pairs with the cold-start pairs (no summary). Among them, the most new rows go first, as today.

The existing caps (`max_pairs_per_tick`, `max_pairs_per_day`, `max_cost_usd_per_day`) set the speed of a rebuild. No extra throttle is needed.

### 4. A `rebuild_before` knob in the flag payload

Add `rebuild_before` (ISO 8601 timestamp, default null) to `ActivitySummaryConfig`. It starts a rebuild without a version bump, for example after a model change or a filter fix. An invalid value falls back to null. Pass it from the tick into `update_activity_summary` and `select_pairs`. The `run_activity_summary` command takes an optional `--rebuild` flag that treats the stored row as stale.

### 5. Visibility

- `activity summary generated`: add `rebuild` (bool) and `rebuild_reason` (`prompt_version`, `render_version` or `rebuild_before`).
- `activity summary tick`: add `stale_pairs`, the count of stale pairs among the candidates.

## Version numbers

The rebuild runs only when a change bumps `PROMPT_VERSION` or `RENDER_VERSION`. Several open PRs set the same numbers (#121341, #121378 and #121380 all set `PROMPT_VERSION = 3`, and #121341, #121379 and #121380 all set `RENDER_VERSION = 4`). Each PR that merges after another must take the next number, or the rows of two different versions share one number and no rebuild runs between them.

## Tests

- `is_stale`, parameterized: prompt version differs, render version differs, `generated_at` before `rebuild_before`, `rebuild_before` null, all current.
- A stale `ok` pair with `next_eligible_at` in the future updates, reads inputs from before its watermark, and sends no previous summary.
- A stale `failed` pair inside its backoff does not update.
- `select_pairs` returns a stale pair that has no rows after its watermark, and sorts it with the cold starts.
- Config parsing: a valid, missing and invalid `rebuild_before`.

## Out of scope

- Keeping the summary of the old version. History is #121225.
- Re-embedding old summaries. A rebuilt summary emits a new embedding through the existing path.

## Done when

After a deploy that bumps either version, or after `rebuild_before` is set, every enrolled pair with enough inputs in the window gets a summary from the full window under the current version, at the speed the caps allow, and the tick and per-update events show the rebuild.

## Problem

The activity summary calls one model, the `DEFAULT_MODEL` constant in `products/signals/backend/activity_summary/summaries.py`. Trying another model needs a PR and a deploy, and it switches every summary at once. There is no way to run two models side by side on live traffic and compare their quality, cost, latency and failure rate.

Every other lever of the tick already lives in the `activity-summary` flag payload, parsed in `activity_summary/config.py`. The model does not.

## Change

Add a weighted model split to the same flag payload. An unchanged payload keeps today's behavior: every update uses `DEFAULT_MODEL`.

### Payload

```json
{
  "model_variants": [
    { "model": "<default model>", "weight": 80 },
    { "model": "<candidate model>", "weight": 20 }
  ],
  "model_split_salt": "v1"
}
```

- `model_variants` is a new field of `ActivitySummaryConfig`, a tuple of a frozen `ModelVariant(model, weight)`. Weights are relative, so they do not have to add up to 100.
- The parse keeps the fail-safe rule of the file. It drops an entry with an unknown model or a weight that is not a positive number. When no valid entry is left, the config has no split and the tick uses `DEFAULT_MODEL`.
- `model_split_salt` defaults to a constant. A new salt reassigns every pair, which starts a new experiment.

### Assignment: fixed per pair, not random per update

The flag is read once per tick for one fixed distinct id, so flag variants cannot do the split. The code picks the model from the payload.

A summary update takes the previous summary as input. A random model per update would mix the models inside one summary, and no summary could be attributed to one model. So the model is a fixed function of the pair:

- Bucket = hash of `salt:team_id:user_id`, in the style of `org_rollout.organization_rollout_bucket`. The bucket picks a variant by cumulative weight.
- Put the variants in a stable order (the order of the payload), so raising the weight of the last variant only moves pairs into it.
- One pure function, for example `model_for_pair(config, team_id, user_id) -> str`, used by every caller.

### Allowlist and cost guard

- A model is valid only when it has an entry in `MODEL_PRICES`. So a typo in the payload cannot call an arbitrary model, and every model in a split has a real cost. Adding a candidate model is a small PR that adds its prices.
- `queue.max_update_cost_usd` already takes a `model`. The daily cost guard must use the highest bound among the configured variants, so a more expensive candidate cannot pass `max_cost_usd_per_day`.
- `logic._call_model` must price the call with the prices of the model it used, not of `DEFAULT_MODEL`.

### Wiring

Replace each direct use of `DEFAULT_MODEL` with the model of the pair:

- `logic._call_model` (the call and the cost).
- The `model` field that `logic.update_activity_summary` stores on the row and on the version row.
- The `model` property of the `activity summary generated` event in `tick.py`. It reads `DEFAULT_MODEL` today, so it would report the wrong model for a candidate pair.
- `backfill.py`.
- `run_activity_summary`: add an optional `--model` override, so a developer can build one pair with each model in a dry run without touching the flag.

A model change does not make a stored summary outdated. The next normal update of the pair uses the new model, like a prompt version that ages in. A forced rebuild stays the job of `rebuild_before`.

### What to record

- The row, the version row and the `activity summary generated` event already have `model`. After this change it holds the model that was called.
- Add `model_split_salt` to the event, so two experiments with the same models stay apart.
- Add the configured variants (model and weight) to the `activity_summary_config_read` log line.

## Open questions

- Does each candidate model support the request as sent: a JSON schema `response_format`, `max_completion_tokens`, and the gateway route `signals`? Check each candidate with the dry-run command before it gets a weight.
- Should the embeddings of candidate pairs stay in the same documents as the default model's? They share the embedding model, so the proposal is yes, with `model` in the metadata as today.

## Out of scope

- A per-model prompt, or per-model render limits.
- An automatic comparison or an eval harness. This issue only makes the split and records which model built each summary.
- The personal ranking model (`personal_ranking/config.py`), which has its own config.

## Tests

- `parse_config`: no `model_variants` gives no split; an unknown model or a bad weight is dropped; a list with no valid entry gives no split.
- `model_for_pair`: the same pair and salt always give the same model; over many pairs the shares match the weights; a new salt changes the assignment; raising the last weight only moves pairs into that variant.
- An update of a candidate pair stores the candidate model on the row, prices the call with its prices, and reports it on the event.
- The daily cost guard uses the most expensive configured variant.

## Done when

Adding a second model with a weight to the flag payload makes that share of pairs build with it from the next tick, without a deploy, and the stored rows and the `activity summary generated` event show which model built each summary.

hits.message:
fix(hogql): let trino prune events when a filter truncates the timestamp (#140476)

* fix(hogql): let trino prune events when a filter truncates the timestamp

Data modeling views that filter events with toDate(timestamp),
toStartOfDay(timestamp) or another truncation printed the filter around
the column, as CAST(timestamp AS DATE) or date_trunc(..., timestamp).
Trino cannot skip events partitions for those filters, so each run
scanned far more of events than the ClickHouse build of the same view.

The Trino compile path now keeps each such filter and adds a range on
the bare events.timestamp column next to it. The range is implied by the
filter and widened by one day on each side. A wider range can never drop
a row, so it stays correct whatever time zone Trino applies to the
truncation or to the bound. Bounds that read a column are skipped.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(hogql): cover aliased and zoned bounds in trino timestamp ranges

Three review findings on the events timestamp range pass:

- The pass ran before normalize_trino_ast expanded projection aliases and
  scalar CTEs. A filter such as `WHERE day = '2026-01-01'` over
  `toDate(timestamp) AS day`, or a bound read from a scalar CTE, got no
  range. The pass now runs after that normalization and before the types
  are resolved again.
- A bound with an explicit time zone is cast to a timestamp without a
  zone, so its wall time can sit up to 14 hours from the instant, and
  the session zone adds up to 14 hours more. The one-day slack came after
  the period, so adding a month from February 28 lost the last days of
  March. The slack is now two days and comes before the period. Adding a
  month or a day never decreases a time, so the range stays implied by
  the filter for any pair of zones.
- Copied bounds kept their inline alias definitions, and the second
  resolver pass failed with "Cannot redefine an alias". Alias definitions
  are now removed from the copies.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(hogql): skip trino timestamp ranges for bounds that call rand

The range pass copies the bound into a second predicate. Trino evaluates
each copy on its own, so a bound that calls rand() draws a different
cutoff in the copy, and the added range can drop rows that the original
filter keeps. Bounds that call a nondeterministic function now get no
range. The check reuses is_nondeterministic_function, the list that the
events predicate pushdown already uses.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

---------

fix(devex): disable partial raster in storybook snapshot runs (#134429)

* fix(storybook): disable partial raster in snapshot runs

Chromium re-rasters a partly invalidated tile in place, and the
anti-aliased pixels in that tile (rounded corners, borders) come out a
color level or two off from a full raster. Which tiles get hit depends
on timing, so one story renders slightly different pictures across runs
and visual review flags them as flaky.

--disable-partial-raster makes every raster a full one. It goes through
the per-browser jest-playwright launchOptions key, so WebKit shards
never see the Chromium-only switch.

Local runs of the surveys story file under background CPU priority:
SurveyResults gave 3 distinct pictures per theme in 6 runs without the
switch and 1 with it, and settled on the second capture every time.

fix(mcp-analytics): rank dashboard tools across every tool by inner name (#135579)

* fix(mcp-analytics): rank dashboard tools across every tool by inner name

The toolRows section kept the 50 busiest tools by raw tool name, then the
browser ranked those by error rate and p95. A slow or flaky tool outside
the 50 busiest never reached the cards, and calls made through the exec
wrapper counted under exec instead of the tool they ran.

The section now groups by the inner tool name, as Tool quality does, and
returns the top 8 tools by calls, by error rate and by p95 from one
aggregate, so the events are read once. The 20-call minimum applies in the
query before ranking. The browser keeps one row per tool and ranks as
before.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(mcp-analytics): keep the tool rows columns compatible with cached rows

A toolRows cache entry from before the rankings has five columns, and the
cache key does not change with the section's SQL. With the ranking first,
the new parser read those rows shifted by one. The ranking now comes last,
so the first five columns mean the same in old cached rows, in new rows,
and to a browser still running the previous parser.
