feat(devex): hold desktop and agent releases until the backend runs their commit (#135368)

* feat(devex): hold the desktop release tag until the backend runs its commit

Desktop releases auto-update users twice a day, but nothing made a release
wait for the Django backend it calls. A client could reach users before its
endpoints were deployed, which is why desktop and backend changes had to go
in separate PRs.

- New wait-for-backend-deploy.sh reads the GitHub Deployments the charts
  deploy writes for prod-us and prod-eu (task `deploy`, overridable via
  TASK), takes the newest one that ever reached success as the live build,
  and checks ancestry against the tested commit. A rollback counts as live,
  an in-progress or failed deploy does not.
- `inactive` is ignored on purpose: GitHub's auto_inactive marks every older
  deployment in the environment inactive on any success, whatever its task,
  so Rust records written later under the same environment names would
  otherwise hide the live Django build.
- desktop-tag.yml waits up to 60 min (policy: one prod deploy plus one more
  deploy cycle). A timeout holds the tag for the next scheduled run, an API
  or lookup error fails the job.
- ignore_backend_deploy dispatch input skips the wait for break-glass; the
  release App is not trusted to set it, same as ignore_master_ci.
- Job timeout goes to 95 min: test dispatch + 25 min test wait + 60 min
  backend wait. A quiet-period sleep ends the run, so it does not stack.
- Rust services write no deployment records yet and stay uncovered.

* feat(devex): hold the agent npm release until the backend runs its commit

The agent tag publishes @posthog/agent to npm right away, so it had the
same gap as the desktop release: a client could ship before the Django
endpoints it calls were deployed.

- desktop-agent-tag.yml now resolves the release commit once, waits for
  prod-us and prod-eu to run it via wait-for-backend-deploy.sh (60 min
  policy), then tags that exact commit. Retries of the tag push no longer
  move to a newer master, since that commit would not have been checked.
- The tag is the irreversible step (it triggers the npm publish), so the
  wait sits before it in the tag job, not in desktop-agent-release.yml.
- A timeout fails the job. The run is push-triggered and nothing retries
  it, so a red run is the visible signal; re-run once the backend is live,
  or the next agent merge releases a newer commit that includes this one.
- New ignore_backend_deploy dispatch input for break-glass; dispatches
  already require team-posthog-desktop membership.
- Job timeout goes from 10 to 75 min to fit the wait.

* feat(devex): let desktop and agent PRs carry Django changes

The desktop and agent release tags now wait until prod-us and prod-eu run
a Django build with the release commit, so a PR that changes desktop or
agent code together with the Django endpoint it calls can no longer ship
a client ahead of its backend. Splitting those PRs bought nothing.

- The coupling check now fails only on desktop or agent paths paired with
  rust/**. Rust services write no deployment records yet, so the releases
  cannot wait for them; a follow-up adds those records.
- The generated.ts exemption and the desktop-skip-backend-check label work
  as before.
- products/desktop/AGENTS.md states the new rule.

* chore(devex): skip the backend wait when there is nothing to release

A scheduled desktop run with no desktop commits since the last tag tags
nothing, so waiting up to an hour for the backend only holds a runner. The
agent tag job now only coordinates (wait, then push a tag), so it moves to a
hosted runner like the desktop tag job did in #133985.

* fix(devex): check backend deploy ancestry through the compare API

The wait ran `git fetch` against origin to resolve live shas. The checkout
persisted the release App token for that remote, and App installation
tokens expire after an hour, so a long wait could end in a fetch error
that held the release for the wrong reason.

- Ancestry now comes from `compare/<commit>...<live>`: ahead or identical
  means contained, behind or diverged means not. gh runs on github.token,
  which lives as long as the job, so the script needs no git at all.
- The "commit is in master" precheck uses `compare/<commit>...master`.
- Deployment listing follows pagination, up to 10 pages of 30, so a run of
  failed or in-progress deploys cannot push the live one out of view. Past
  the cap the environment reads as "no live deployment" (a hold).
- Header notes that a rollback done outside the charts deploy writes no
  record, so the script cannot see it.
- Tests drop the temp git repo and serve compare fixtures; new case for a
  live deployment on page 2.

* fix(devex): mint a fresh App token for the release tag push

App installation tokens expire after an hour. Both tag jobs got their
token at the start, and the Desktop Tests wait plus the backend wait can
outlast it, so the final fetch and tag push could run on an expired token.

- A new `Get app token for the tag push` step right before tagging, in
  desktop-tag.yml and desktop-agent-tag.yml.
- Fetch, push and ls-remote after the wait go through an explicit
  x-access-token URL with `-c http.https://github.com/.extraheader=`. The
  checkout persists its token as an extra header for github.com, which
  git sends even with credentials in the URL; the empty value clears it.
- Fetches that run before the wait keep origin, with a comment saying
  why that is still inside the token lifetime.

* fix(devex): pick the live backend build by last update, from trusted records

The charts deploy reuses an existing deployment record when a sha was
deployed before, so a rollback posts success on an old record while the
bad newer record still has success in its history. "Newest created record
that ever succeeded" then picked the bad build.

- Live build = the most recently updated record (updated_at is the time of
  its newest status) whose newest status is success. Lists pages 1-2 of
  30, sorts by updated_at, stops at the first match; none found = hold.
- Only records and statuses created by TRUSTED_CREATOR (default
  deployment-status-posthog[bot]) count. Any token with deployments: write,
  e.g. a PR workflow, could otherwise forge a success.
- The commit-in-master compare retries inside the deadline loop like any
  other error poll; a definitive behind/diverged answer still exits 1 at
  once.
- Tests: rollback reusing an older record, two records left on success
  (newest update wins), forged deployment and forged status, page-2 live
  record. The cross-task inactive case is gone, since charts no longer
  sends auto_inactive.

* chore(devex): poll the backend deploy every two minutes

A poll now costs up to two list calls plus one status call per record
walked, per environment. Polling every 120 s keeps a full one-hour wait
well under the GITHUB_TOKEN hourly limit.

* fix(devex): take the newest trusted deployment as live in the release gate

Review found two ways to make the gate read a stale build. A rollback reused a
record from long ago, which could fall off the pages the gate reads, so a
missed inactive write let it take the previous build as live. And any token
with deployments:write could post a status: the gate read only the newest
status, so one foreign status hid the real live record, and it also moved
updated_at, which the gate sorted by.

charts now gives every deploy its own record (PostHog/charts#20674), so the
newest record in creation order is the live one. The gate keeps the API's
creation order instead of sorting by updated_at, and reads the newest status
that the charts App wrote, ignoring others on top. The charts change has to
land first.

A token with deployments:write could post enough statuses on the live record

feat(subscriptions): gate AI summaries on AI credit budget (#59625)

## Problem

Subscription AI summaries call an LLM on every delivery with **no budget check**. Now that subscriptions are available on the free tier (#59624), an org could keep generating summaries while over its AI credit budget. We should stop generating once an org is over budget — the same way the chat assistant already behaves.

## Changes

Adopt the chat assistant's enforcement pattern (`ee/api/conversation.py`): `is_team_limited(QuotaResource.AI_CREDITS)`, which reads the billing quota-limiting cache (not the retrospective usage query).

- **Enable-time gate** (`SubscriptionSerializer.validate`): raises `QuotaLimitExceeded` (402) when a summary is being toggled *on* while the org is over budget. Reuses the existing "becoming active" check, so grandfathered summaries and unrelated edits are unaffected.
- **Generation-time gate** (`snapshot_subscription_insights`): when over budget, skips the summary and delivers the rest of the subscription (graceful degradation) rather than failing the delivery. **Fail-open** — if the quota lookup itself errors, the summary is generated rather than silently dropped.

## How did you test this code?

I'm an agent (Claude Code) — automated suites I ran locally:

- `ee/api/test/test_subscription.py` — enable-time gate over/under budget, the patch-transition case, and the grandfathering case (unrelated edits while over budget aren't blocked).
- `posthog/temporal/subscriptions/test_snapshot_ai_consent.py` — generation-time skip when over budget, generate when under, and fail-open when the quota check raises.

## Publish to changelog?

No — internal cost-control guard, no user-facing feature.

## Docs update

n/a

## 🤖 Agent context

Authored with Claude Code (human-directed). **Stacked on #59624.**

Investigation that shaped this: the AI credit budget shown in `/usage` is computed by a retrospective ClickHouse query and is **display-only** — the actual enforcement signal is `is_team_limited(AI_CREDITS)`, populated in a Redis set by the billing quota-limiting system and (until this PR) used only by the Max chat assistant. We reuse that chokepoint rather than introducing a bespoke check, so this is the second adopter of an established pattern, not new billing infrastructure. The lookup is cheap (in-process-cached set membership), so it's safe in the per-delivery path. Behaviour differs by context deliberately: a hard 402 at enable-time (API), graceful skip-and-deliver at generation-time (background workflow).

TraceQueryRunner collected every event of a trace, with all prompts and

feat(devex): extend visual review quarantines of stories that still differ (#138108)

* feat(devex): extend visual review quarantines of stories that still differ

Quarantines run out on a fixed date, also when the story still renders
differently on the default branch. Production data shows most such lapses
get re-quarantined by hand (roughly three in four), and PRs fail on the
story in between. Automatic quarantine does not catch these again: a story
that renders one fixed picture in every run (a stale baseline under
quarantine) never renders clean, so it is never proven flaky and fails
every merge queue run after the lapse.

- New rule in auto_extend: an active quarantine that expires within 48
  hours gets a fresh automatic quarantine (14 days) when its story rendered
  `changed` at least once in the last 100 full default-branch runs.
  Otherwise it lapses as planned. Any source counts (human, agent, auto).
- The extension goes through quarantine_identifier, the same path as
  automatic quarantine, so the old row is superseded the usual way. The
  row is locked and re-checked first, so a lift or replace by a person in
  between wins.
- When every recent render is the same changed picture, the reason says
  the baseline looks stale, so a person approves the picture instead of
  waiting for the next expiry.
- Runs from the hourly release task, after the lift. Follows
  auto_quarantine_mode: preview only logs and captures
  vr_quarantine_extend, once a day per story. Extensions skip the daily
  automatic quarantine limit (they hide nothing new) and are capped per
  run by AUTO_QUARANTINE_MAX_STORIES_PER_RUN.
- The owning team gets the quarantine notice, with a lead that says the
  quarantine was extended.
- auto_lift's docstring claimed a relapse needs no handling; corrected.

* chore(devex): trim auto-extend comments and record capture events in tests

The CI report flagged comment density above 3% and call assertions on the
capture mock. Comments that restated field names or the code are gone. The
tests now record the captured event names and assert on them, which is the
rule's real output in preview mode.

* fix(devex): keep visual review extensions out of the daily limit and lift requests

- Extensions no longer count toward the daily limit of automatic quarantines.
  They hide nothing new, and counting them blocked new flakes for a day after
  a batch of extensions. The reason prefix moves to contracts so the limit and
  the notice read one constant.
- An extension moves pending fix-PR lift requests to the new quarantine row.
  On the old row the lift found the quarantine ended and resolved as superseded.
- Only renders against the story's current baseline count. Approving a stale
  picture changes the baseline, so the older changed renders no longer extend
  the quarantine and ping its owners.
- The per-run cap counts handled entries, so preview mode does not report the
  same deduped entries every run while later ones lapse unseen.
- The lift and the extension get separate rate-limit handling, so a rate limit
  in the lift does not skip extensions before an expiry.

* fix(devex): keep lift requests moved by an extension pending across a race

Lift reconcile and the extension run as separate tasks for the same
default-branch run. A reconcile that read a request before the extension
moved it locked the old, ended quarantine and resolved the moved request
as superseded, so the fix PR could no longer lift the story. The request
updates now also match the quarantine they decided on; a moved request
stays pending for the next run.

The extension also locks the run before the quarantine, the same order as
quarantine_identifier, so it cannot deadlock with a manual quarantine.

* fix(devex): verify the default branch before extending visual review quarantines

- The run's branch and commit are client-supplied. Auto-lift and automatic
  quarantine both check the commit against the default branch head on
  GitHub; the extension now does the same, so an off-branch upload that
  names the default branch cannot keep quarantines alive. The lookup runs
  only when a quarantine is due.
- The run lock in the extension is no-key. FOR UPDATE conflicted with the
  KEY SHARE lock a lift request takes when it records the run, which could
  deadlock against a lift that holds the quarantine row.

feat(data-catalog): rank metric search hits by meaning behind a flag (#133537)

* feat(data-catalog): rank metric search hits by meaning behind a flag

Word matching cannot find a metric when the agent uses other words, such as
"subscriber income" for MRR. With data-catalog-metric-semantic-search on and
AI data processing approved, search also ranks metrics by cosine similarity
between the query embedding and a vector stored on each metric.

A Celery task embeds the name, display name, description and unit after a
write that changes them, and backfill_metric_embeddings embeds existing
metrics. The two lanes merge by each hit's best rank, so weak word matches
that both lanes find cannot push down the closest semantic hit. A failed or

feat(replay-vision): summarize any scanner type via reasoning fallback (#67513)

## Problem

A scheduled group summary on a **classifier** (or monitor/scorer) scanner silently skipped with `skipped_empty`. Root cause: synthesis only reads `model_output.summary`, which only the **summarizer** scanner emits — classifier/monitor/scorer observations carry `reasoning` (+ verdict/tags/score) instead, so the fetch found zero usable lines and skipped. (The on-demand Max summary tool already handles all types via `reasoning or summary`; the scheduled path just never got that fallback.)

## Changes

`_fetch_observations` now falls back to `model_output.reasoning` when there's no `summary`, so a group summary works on any scanner type. Behavior for summarizer scanners is unchanged (they still use `summary`).

## How did you test this code?

I'm an agent (agent-assisted, human-driven). Added `test_summarizes_reasoning_when_no_summary` (a reasoning-only observation now feeds the summary instead of skipping empty). 24 synthesis tests pass; ruff + ty clean.

## Automatic notifications

- [ ] Publish to changelog?
- [ ] Alert Sales and Marketing teams?

## Docs update

No docs change needed.

## 🤖 Agent context

**Autonomy:** Human-driven (agent-assisted)

- Tooling: PostHog Code (Claude). Skill: `/writing-tests`.
- Surfaced by a user hitting `skipped_empty` on a classifier action. Chose the reasoning fallback (make summaries work on all types) over restricting summary actions to summarizer scanners, matching the on-demand summary tool's behavior.
- Was stacked on #67493 while both touched `_fetch_observations`; the change is independent (its diff applies cleanly on master), so it's now rebased directly onto master and unstacked.

---

feat(warehouse-suggestions): show more waiting suggestions on request (#132232)

* feat(warehouse-suggestions): show more waiting suggestions on request

People who clear the day's warehouse suggestions saw "All caught up" even
when more suggestions were waiting, because each team gets at most 5 new
suggestions a day. The rest only appeared after the next daily run.

The review dialog and both suggestion strips (Models and Catalog) now offer
"Show more" while suggestions are waiting. A click shows one more batch with
the daily job's limits (5 per batch, 3 open per kind), except the daily count.
Suggestions do not refill on accept: that gives nothing on most days under the
daily limit, and without it the list never ends and each refill notifies
view creators.

- surface_more runs in logic/job.py under the daily job's team config lock,
  with the same rule for pausing (enabled, eligible, no paused_reason).
- It assigns new rows to the view's creator but sends no notification,
  because the person who clicked is already looking at them.
- The count and the pick include only rows on subjects the user can read and,
  per subject kind, act on, matching accept and dismiss.
- The status endpoint returns waiting and can_show_more per surface. The
  frontend reloads it when the last row leaves, because at page load the
  open rows usually fill the per-kind limit.
- The surface to kinds map lives once, in logic/access.py. The list endpoint
  takes surface, and the frontend copy is deleted.
- assign_surfaced takes the team inventory instead of the whole candidate
  context, so a click loads no read history. The inventory loads before the
  lock to keep the lock short.
- The new operation has a disabled MCP entry: agents already list every
  suggestion and gain nothing from a relaxed daily limit.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* chore: update OpenAPI generated types

* fix(warehouse-suggestions): address show more review findings

- Waiting rows now count only when the user can edit the subject, the same
  check accept and dismiss use. A viewer saw suggestions they could not act
  on, and a read-only row could take the last per-kind slot.
- A click picks the batch under the team lock first, then loads definitions
  only for the picked views through saved_query_definitions(ids=...). It no
  longer loads the whole warehouse inventory, so request cost does not grow
  with the warehouse. The daily run still passes its full inventory.
- Rows shown on demand are marked surfaced_on_demand, and the daily run's
  5-a-day count skips them. A click before the 08:30 run no longer uses up
  that day's batch. The column has db_default=False, so inserts from code

- The notice waits for the first list response, so it no longer shows while

- Status reloads only when no decision is still saving, so a slow dismissal

- Show more stays busy until the new list and status arrive, so a second

feat(subscriptions): rate limit test_delivery action (#55357)

## Problem

[PR #55345](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/pull/55345) exposes the subscription `test_delivery` action via MCP. The existing viewset returns 409 when the same subscription has a workflow in flight, but that per-subscription dedupe doesn't stop a caller iterating across many subscriptions (or rotating across personal API keys or OAuth tokens) to spam real email / Slack / webhook recipients. Once this is agent-callable, that abuse shape needs a proper bound.

## Changes

- Add `SubscriptionTestDeliveryThrottle` in `posthog/rate_limit.py` — extends `PersonalApiKeyOrUserRateThrottle` (not the PAT-only `PersonalApiKeyRateThrottle` the sibling throttles use), rate `10/minute`.
- Key the throttle per `team_id` only (drop the `{team_id}_{pk}` the sibling throttles use), so rotating subscriptions *and* rotating API keys both share one team-wide bucket.
- Apply via `throttle_classes=[…]` on `SubscriptionViewSet.test_delivery`.
- Every authenticated caller is subject to the limit: personal API keys, OAuth access tokens (the MCP OAuth flow forwards bearer tokens that aren't PATs), and session-cookie UI users. The sibling throttles only target PATs because they gate expensive read work; this endpoint produces real external side effects so the narrower PAT-only base would leave OAuth callers unthrottled.

## How did you test this code?

Agent-authored — only code-based testing has been done, no manual QA.

- New test `test_test_delivery_throttled_per_team_across_subscriptions_and_keys` in `ee/api/test/test_subscription.py` that rotates across two subscriptions and two personal API keys on the same team to prove the throttle fires regardless of subscription or key rotation; asserts two consecutive 429s (sustained throttling, not a one-shot gate); asserts `mock_client.start_workflow.call_count == 3` (pins that throttling runs before the view handler so no workflow starts on 429); and finally asserts that a session-authenticated request to the same team is also throttled once the bucket is exhausted, pinning the contract that all auth methods share the same bucket.
- Cache is narrowed to just this throttle's key (`cache.delete("throttle_subscription_test_delivery_team_{team_id}")`) with `addCleanup` so the test doesn't pollute sibling tests.
- Postgres isn't available in the agent environment; the test passes `ruff check` and `ruff format` and will run in CI.

## Publish to changelog?

no

## Docs update

No docs impact.

## 🤖 LLM context

Authored by [PostHog Code](https://posthog.com/code). Stacked on #55345 (now merged); QA Swarm review of the parent PR flagged the abuse shape this PR closes. Subsequent QA Swarm on this PR converged on: tighten class comment wording, add explicit reasoning for dropping `pk` vs siblings, strengthen test assertions — addressed. A later human review flagged that the original `PersonalApiKeyRateThrottle` base left OAuth callers unthrottled (MCP OAuth forwards `pha_` bearer tokens that aren't PATs); fixed by switching to `PersonalApiKeyOrUserRateThrottle`.

chore(storybook): support multivariate feature flag variants in stories (#60775)

## Problem

Storybook stories can turn feature flags **on** via the `featureFlags` parameter, but that only expresses booleans. A component gated on a specific **multivariate** flag variant (e.g. an experiment arm) can't be rendered in a story — so its visual-regression snapshots come out empty, silently.

The trap is subtle and bites every multivariate-flag story:

- Calling `featureFlagLogic.actions.setFeatureFlags(...)` imperatively from a story is dropped in the visual-regression runtime. `spyOnFeatureFlags` only merges variant values when the context looks `cloud`/`is_debug`/`test`, and the mocked `_preflight` (which has `is_debug: true`) is never written back to `window.POSTHOG_APP_CONTEXT.preflight` — so the gate stays closed.
- Even with the gate open, `posthog-js` fetches `/flags` and fires `onFeatureFlags`, clobbering whatever the story set back to empty.
- It works in `jest` (`NODE_ENV==='test'` opens the gate), so unit tests stay green while the Storybook render is blank — easy to miss.

## Changes

Makes the existing `featureFlags` story parameter accept a `Record<string, string | boolean>` alongside `string[]`:

- **Boolean entries** still ride `persisted_feature_flags` (the always-merged baseline `featureFlagLogic` reads on mount) — unchanged behaviour.
- **Variant strings** open the `spyOnFeatureFlags` gate (mark the storybook context `is_debug`) and inject through `featureFlagLogic`.
- The **test-only** `posthog.init('fake_token')` branch in `loadPostHogJS.tsx` now sets `advanced_disable_feature_flags: true`, so posthog-js never fetches flags and never clobbers story-set values. The real-token production init is untouched.

Usage:

```ts
// boolean (unchanged)
parameters: { featureFlags: [FEATURE_FLAGS.MY_FLAG] }

// pin a multivariate variant
parameters: { featureFlags: { [FEATURE_FLAGS.MY_FLAG]: 'test_b' } }
```

Also adds the `setting-feature-flags-in-storybook` skill and a `.claude/rules` path-rule so story authors find this instead of re-discovering the trap.

## How did you test this code?

I'm an agent (PostHog Code). I validated the mechanism live, not just in CI:

- Ran Storybook locally and drove the gated consumer story (the promoted-product nav entry, stacked above in #60677) with Playwright. On a fresh build, with `parameters: { featureFlags: { 'promoted-product': 'intent_plus' } }` and **no manual intervention**, the entry rendered correctly; the `control` arm correctly rendered nothing. Before this change the same story rendered an empty wrapper.
- Confirmed the `advanced_disable_feature_flags` change is scoped to the `fake_token` (storybook/test) init branch only — the real-token init is unchanged.
- Existing boolean-`featureFlags` stories are unaffected (booleans never relied on the imperative path).

## Automatic notifications

- [ ] Publish to changelog?
- [ ] Alert Sales and Marketing teams?

## Docs update

No public docs — this is internal Storybook/test tooling. The new in-repo skill documents it for agents and contributors.

## 🤖 Agent context

Extracted from #60677 (the promoted-product experiment, which stacks on top of this and is the first consumer) so the reusable Storybook harness change can be reviewed independently by frontend/infra owners. The root cause was diagnosed by reproducing in a real browser against running Storybook (jest masks it via `NODE_ENV==='test'`), which pinned both the `spyOnFeatureFlags` gate and the posthog-js `onFeatureFlags` clobber.

feat(stamphog): let the trigger label request a re-review in all mode (#140523)

* feat(stamphog): let the trigger label request a re-review in all mode

In all mode every labeled event was dropped, so after a refusal the
only way to get a new verdict without pushing was the API or MCP
request. Agents that re-request reviews by relabeling (the label-mode
habit) lost that path when a repo switched to all mode.

- A labeled event that adds the repo's trigger label now goes through
  the manual request's evidence gate after every existing webhook gate.
  A head with no covering run gets a run, and a delivered refusal is
  reviewed again only on new evidence, up to the per-head cap. A failed
  evidence read re-runs nothing. Any other label stays ignored.
- The run is stamped with the label trigger, so the reviewer is told a
  label requested it. It carries the delivery id, so a retry of the
  same delivery resumes the run instead of reading it as covered.
- A label add that starts no run removes the label again, so the next
  add fires, and upserts the sticky comment with the reason: review in
  flight, already approved, already reviewed (wait or gate), evidence
  unreadable, cap reached, or nothing new.
- No cooldown in all mode; the evidence gate and the cap bound it.
- A published refusal now strips the trigger label in all mode too, so
  an agent's next label add fires an event. Bot admissions stay
  excluded, and so do self-driving runs in all mode, because a label on
  a bot PR starts no review there. remove_pr_label already treats a
  404 as success, and post_verdict is an activity, so no workflow
  patch is needed.
- The verdict hint says "Add the label" instead of "Re-add", since in
  all mode the label may never have been on the PR.

A label add moves no head, so the new skip path retracts nothing: any
standing approval covers exactly the head the label was added on.

* fix(stamphog): harden the all-mode label request path

- Skip a label added to a closed PR. A manual request refuses one, and the
  label path shares its gate, so it must not start a review there.
- Raise when the label cannot come off again, so the delivery retries. A
  label left on the PR could never be added again, which blocks the next
  request.
- Post each rejection notice once per minute per text. The sticky upsert
  reads then creates, so overlapping redeliveries could post two comments.
- Run those GitHub writes on the BATCH lane, so repeated label adds cannot
  use up the reserve that dismissals and verdicts need.
- Create the trigger label for ALL-mode repositories too, since the label
  now requests a re-review there.

* chore(stamphog): trim comments on the all-mode label path

Drop comments that restated a docstring or a test name, and shorten the
ones that edited older notes, so the added comment share stays near the
repo's usual level.

feat: llm override on gateway (#62567)

## Problem

Models not yet present in LiteLLM's upstream cost map are invisible to the gateway even when they are allowlisted in products config. The gateway derives both `/v1/models` responses and billing costs from that map, so a missing entry means the model cannot be routed or priced correctly. `claude-fable-5` is one such model that needs to be available before LiteLLM ships it upstream.

## Changes

Introduces a `model_cost_overrides.py` module containing a `MODEL_COST_OVERRIDES` dictionary of bridge entries for models absent from LiteLLM's upstream cost map. `apply_model_cost_overrides` merges these entries into the live cost map only when the model is not already defined upstream (upstream always wins). This function is called in both `cost_refresh.py` and `model_cost_service.py` immediately after fetching the upstream map, so overrides are applied on every refresh cycle.

`claude-fable-5` is the first entry, with pricing verified against OpenRouter (Anthropic + Bedrock), a 200k context window (the 1M window is a beta-header feature), and prompt caching support. The `ModelCost` TypedDict is extended with `cache_read_input_token_cost`, `cache_creation_input_token_cost`, and `supports_prompt_caching` fields to accommodate these entries.

Each override entry should be deleted once LiteLLM ships the corresponding upstream definition.

## How did you test this code?

New unit tests in `tests/test_model_cost_overrides.py` cover:

- `apply_model_cost_overrides` adds missing models and does not overwrite existing upstream entries.
- The inserted entry is a shallow copy so mutations by LiteLLM internals do not corrupt the shared constant.
- After a mocked `_refresh_cache`, `ModelCostService.get_costs` and `get_all_models` both surface `claude-fable-5`.
- `get_available_models("posthog_code")` includes `claude-fable-5` when the Anthropic key is set and the model is absent from the upstream map.

## Automatic notifications

- [ ] Publish to changelog?
- [ ] Alert Sales and Marketing teams?

## Docs update

## 🤖 Agent context

**Autonomy:** Human-driven (agent-assisted)

The intent was to make `claude-fable-5` routable and priceable in the gateway before LiteLLM ships it upstream. A dedicated overrides module was chosen over inline patching so the bridge entries are self-documenting and easy to prune. The `apply_model_cost_overrides` call was placed after `get_model_cost_map` in both refresh paths to ensure overrides survive every TTL-driven refresh. Pricing figures and token limits were taken from OpenRouter's published Anthropic/Bedrock rates and matched against the existing `claude-opus-4` pattern for the 1M-window caveat.

runs. ci-backend.yml empties that segment whenever the Django suite is
skipped, so the premise was false.

Core Temporal code (materialize_view, queue partition management, the
worker bootstrap), other products and the root conftest executed 29
unwatched files through the facade. A ws-only PR that changed one of
them skipped the tests that run it. The merge queue keeps the isolation
skip, so such a break lands on master and only the hourly full run sees it.

- The guard now resolves every name outside code uses from the facade
  (imports, `_LAZY` maps, re-exports through other modules) to the file
  that defines it, and every file on that path must be an input. It
  fails on a lazy map or import shape it cannot follow.
- Its input is the whole repo, so it moves to posthog/test/repo_invariants
  and runs on every backend PR. The bounded generated-configs check stays
  in the product.
- It reads lazy maps and judges watching with the hogli helpers that
  `product:lint` uses (lazy_reexport_map, unwatched_modules), so the two
  cannot disagree.
- Cost: 56 ws-only commits since Aug 16 touched the added inputs and
  would have run the full suite.

* fix(devex): watch the warehouse_sources admin package

Core's admin tests run this package. `register_all_admin()` imports each
app's admin module through autodiscovery, and
`posthog/admin/test_admin.py::TestProductAdminRegistration` asserts that the
warehouse models register. No contract-check input watched the package, so a
warehouse_sources-only PR that broke it skipped those tests.

Watch the whole package. Its `__init__.py` is the module autodiscovery
imports, and it imports every submodule at module level to fire their
`@admin.register` decorators.

Cost: 3 of the 8 commits that touched the package since Aug 17 changed
nothing outside warehouse_sources.

The usage-based guard does not check this channel. The hoglint level rule
that replaces the guard asks for the same files.

* fix(devex): keep the warehouse_sources watch to Temporal files

The product lint's narrowed-inputs rule (has_narrowed_turbo_inputs)
accepts backend/temporal/ as a wiring location and rejects other
internal files as contract-check inputs. Watching the admin package and
eight non-Temporal facade hand-outs dropped warehouse_sources below the
Isolated rung, so the isolation baseline check failed.

- Drop those nine inputs. They stay unwatched, as on master, until the
  narrowed-inputs rule changes.
- The guard checks only files under backend/temporal/, the files the
  Temporal segment premise is about. Dropping a Temporal input still
  fails it.

fix(data-catalog): load the navigation badge counts in two requests (#139525)

* fix(data-catalog): load the navigation badge counts in two requests

The data catalog badge in the new navigation polled three routes every
five minutes: data_catalog/pending_review, data_modeling_nodes/attention_count
and data_quality_checks/failing_count. Most of each request was fixed
per-request cost, and the three together were the largest web cost of
the data modeling products.

GET data_catalog/attention/ returns the review counts and the failing
model count. Each part keeps its own access check and counts 0 when the
caller may not read it, the same answer the badge gave for a 403. The
route is session-only (scope_object INTERNAL), like attention_count,
because the model count reads no token scopes.

Failing checks keep their own request. data_quality already imports
data_catalog, so a data_catalog import of data_quality closes a product
cycle, and the data quality access rules stay in their viewset.

The failing model count moves into a logic function behind the
data_modeling facade, so attention_count and the new route share it.
The node list still builds its own queryset in the view, because an
isolated product's facade may not take or return a QuerySet.

The old routes stay. They are public API, and open tabs keep the old
bundle until they reload.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(data-catalog): keep the model count when review counts fail

The review counts build the HogQL database on a cache miss, and the
saved-query loop of that build has no try/except, so one broken view
raises. In the combined attention route the error returned a 500, and
the badge kept a stale failing model count. When the counts came from
separate requests, the model count still updated.

The route now records the error and returns pending_review as null with
the model count. The badge keeps its last review counts when it gets
null. A fallback to the old routes would also work, but it adds a
second request path for the same result.

fix(data-modeling): leave models that don't compile out of a manual run (#138905)

* fix(data-modeling): leave models that don't compile out of a manual run

An upstream, downstream or Trino run checked every model in the
selection and raised on the first one whose query did not resolve, so
one broken descendant refused the whole run. When that model came
before a model that reads a denied table, its 400 also hid the denial.

The run now leaves a model that does not resolve out, together with the
selected models that depend on it, and returns them under `skipped`
with the reason. It does not let that model run: resolution stops at
its first error, and a denied saved expression reads as an unknown
field, so its sources are not fully checked, and the managed warehouse
reads them without the caller's access control.

Any edit or table denial in the selection still refuses the run with
403. A run of a model whose own query does not compile returns 400 with
the compile error.

* chore: update OpenAPI generated types

* fix(data-modeling): scope the skipped-node name lookup to the team

  passes against the ledger and approvals now, or the PR changes no

gap and expects the model to find it: reuse and the bot shortcut under the
master config, and two gaps the fixed config still has (a skip-greened
stacked child that is retargeted, a force-push back to a head whose green

feat(mcp): add chartable time series to claude code results (#137529)

* feat(mcp): add chartable time series to claude code results

Claude Code draws charts from tool results in the named-series shape,
{"series":[{"name":"…","data":[[time,value],…]}]}. Our trends tables,
TOON payloads and SQL text tables keep dates and values apart, so it
cannot chart them.

For Claude Code in the terminal, and for Claude Code through a claude.ai
connector, append one named-series JSON block after the existing text
when a result holds values over time. Shapes covered: parallel date and
value arrays (trends, lifecycle, funnel trends, billing, exposures), a
shared axis (app metrics), point lists (metrics), rows with a time column
(MCP analytics, logs and span sparklines), and execute-sql text tables.

Times carrying a UTC offset are written as wall-clock times, and
midnight buckets as dates, because the client draws zoned times in UTC
and no tool result can name another zone.

feat(llm-gateway): add billing-denial error codes and legacy-client shim (#71343)

## Problem

PostHog Code's usage-based billing cutover (#70951) gates unbilled orgs to the free-tier model list, but the gate's 403 goes out as a bare FastAPI `detail` string. Pre-cutover desktop builds classify errors by substring: they treat that 403 as a fatal session error and tear a healthy session down ("Connection lost" + recovery loops), and no client can tell which limit tripped a 429 without parsing prose.

**Why:** installed desktop builds can't be updated in time for the cutover — the gateway's error bodies are the only lever that reaches them, and this can deploy ahead of the model-gate flip.

## Changes

- The free-tier model-gate 403 now uses the standard error envelope with a machine-readable `code: "model_gate"`, and its message carries a `(rate_limit)` suffix — a compat shim that routes pre-cutover PostHog Code clients to their usage-limit modal instead of session teardown (documented inline; remove once those builds roll forward).
- Throttle 429s repeat the reason in `error.message` (SDK error strings often surface only the message) and carry the throttle scope as `error.code` (`billable_credits`, `user_cost_burst`, `user_cost_sustained`, …), so clients can classify the limit cause.

Companion client work: [PostHog/code#3485](https://github.com/PostHog/code/pull/3485) classifies these bodies into cause-aware billing UX.

## How did you test this code?

Automated only: the enforcement-path gate tests now pin the new envelope (`code`, the `(rate_limit)` suffix), the rate-limiting endpoint test pins the message/reason/code shape, and a TestClient-level test pins the gate 403's wire body end-to-end (top-level error envelope with `code: "model_gate"` and the `(rate_limit)` suffix — never `{"detail": ...}` nesting) through the raise site and the exception-handler unwrap together. All would fail if the shim or codes were dropped. Full llm-gateway suite green locally (1239 passed, 50 skipped, 30 xfailed, 22 xpassed).

## Automatic notifications

- [ ] Publish to changelog?
- [ ] Alert Sales and Marketing teams?

## Docs update

None — internal error-body shape.

## 🤖 Agent context

**Autonomy:** Human-driven (agent-assisted)

PostHog Code session. Part of the usage-based billing cutover client plan: this PR makes gateway billing denials classifiable by both pre- and post-cutover desktop builds.

fix(data-modeling): validate a view with the request's hogql database (#138292)

Saving a view built the HogQL database three times: once for the
serializer context, once inside validate_query, and once for the DAG
sync. Each build loads the project's whole catalog from Postgres, so
the cost grows with the number of warehouse tables.

validate_query now resolves against the database the viewset already
built for the same user. Both builds used the same team, user and
default modifiers, so the result is the same.

The DAG sync keeps its own build. It resolves without a user, bypasses
warehouse access control and allows only the data modeling system
tables, so it can see a different set of tables than the saving user.

The three builds on the save path now pass a trigger, so the span and
the hogql_database_build counter name the caller instead of "direct":
saved_query_save, saved_query_dag_sync and
saved_query_breaking_change_check.

hits.message:
fix(data-modeling): publish one materialized table snapshot at a time (#139575)

* fix(data-modeling): publish one materialized table snapshot at a time

Two runs of one model can publish at the same time: a DAG run's child
and a manual run use different workflow ids. Each publish loaded the
backing table row, ran DESCRIBE, the count and the size listing, then
saved its whole in-memory copy. Both copies held the size from before
either run, so each job recorded the same storage growth, and the
publish that saved last won even when it had staged the older folder.
The full save could also write back fields that changed in the
meantime, such as a soft delete.

The end of the publish now runs in one transaction that locks the
table row. It takes the storage delta from the size the locked row
holds, saves the job's delta and only the fields a publish owns, and
skips the save when the table already points at a folder staged later
than its own. The staging time comes from the timestamp in the folder
name, which query_folder_staged_at reads next to the code that names
those folders. A folder with no timestamp never blocks a publish, so
legacy folders keep today's last-save-wins behavior.

asave_datawarehousetable had no other caller, so it is removed. The
locked save keeps passing internally_computed_url_pattern=True.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(data-modeling): lock and write the backing table through its facade

The first version locked and saved warehouse_sources' DataWarehouseTable
from data_warehouse code, which the model-crossing baseline refuses as
a new use of another product's model.

publish_backing_table in the warehouse_sources facade now owns the
locked write: it takes the table id and a BackingTableSnapshot
contract, skips when a later-staged folder is already published, and
returns the size it replaced and whether the columns changed.
create_table builds the snapshot and records the job's storage delta
from the replaced size. The created_via fallback moves with the save,
comment included.

query_folder_state.py joins the backend:contract-check inputs, because
outside tests now reach it through the facade.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(data-modeling): mark and log a publish that a later folder skips

When a later-staged folder is already published, create_table returns
the in-memory table, which holds this run's folder, columns and row
count rather than what the database has. CreateTableResult now carries
a published flag, so a caller can tell the two cases apart, and the
publish activity logs skipped_publish_of_older_staged_folder with the
folder it did not publish.

CreateTableResult moves from a bare dataclass to @frozen, the house
default for result objects.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(stamphog): cut owners whose part only serves the author's feature (#133732)

* feat(stamphog): request platform teams only when shared behavior changes

Reviewer routing requests every owner of changed code and only cuts an
owner whose part is trivial. Platform teams such as agent infra own
code that many products call, so routine use of their code still lands
in their review queue.

A new repo setting, routing_shared_behavior_labels, maps a team slug to
a label. After the normal cut, routing asks the model once more, over
only those teams files, with a stricter test: keep the team only when
its part changes shared behavior (run lifecycle, credentials, billing,
data models, contracts, hot paths). A kept team also gets the label.
Pinned owners, owners whose diff the model did not see, forks, a
failed call and the keep-one-reviewer rule all keep the team, as they
do for the normal cut. The normal cut prompt is unchanged.

* chore: update OpenAPI generated types

* feat(stamphog): filter shared-behavior teams that are the only owner

A pull request with one owner skipped the model and always requested
that owner, so a platform team was still asked on every change that
touched only its code. A listed team that is the only owner now gets
the shared-behavior check, and the keep-one-reviewer rule no longer
brings back a team that check cut. Such a pull request can end with
no review request, and its author picks a reviewer.

* refactor(stamphog): hardcode shared-behavior teams and tidy the routing check

The per-repo setting needed a model field, API wiring and generated
types for one team, so routing now reads a SHARED_BEHAVIOR_LABELS
constant. The only migration left adds the new run-log reasons.

The shared-behavior check now runs as its own step after the normal
cut, so apply_cut_guards is unchanged, and it keeps one reviewer from
the normal cuts when it would otherwise cut everyone. Its outcomes are
logged as shared_behavior_kept, _cut or _no_answer instead of
model_kept. The routing comment says when no review was requested and
names shared-behavior cuts separately. One gateway token now serves
both calls, approved-head routing skips the check, and labels go only
to teams that routing requested.

* refactor(stamphog): strip the shared-behavior cut down to one second pass

Drops the repo setting, label, run-log reasons and migrations. Routing
now runs the normal cut, then asks the model once more about the teams
in SHARED_BEHAVIOR_TEAMS that it kept, and cuts them when their part
leaves shared behavior unchanged. That includes a team that is the only
owner. Forks, truncated file lists, pinned teams and a failed call keep
the team.

* feat(stamphog): use sonnet for the shared-behavior pass and keep data changes

Haiku kept agent infra on PRs that only retired a catalog entry,
removed an unused helper or added an analytics field. Sonnet drops
those. A new rule keeps the team when a change alters what is written
to or deleted from the database, which Sonnet otherwise missed. The
routing token cap rises to 1 USD so the Sonnet call fits.

* fix(stamphog): sum routing token usage and record the second pass in the run log

The shared-behavior pass is a second model call, so the usage it reports
now adds to the first call's instead of replacing it. When it answers, the
run log no longer says the cut step was skipped: the team gets model_kept or
model_cut, and a failed call on a skipped run records no_answer.

* refactor(stamphog): fold the shared-behavior rule into the one cut prompt

Owners of shared code get requested on every pull request that calls their
code, even when the part only serves the author's feature. Instead of a
second model pass for one named team, the general cut prompt now cuts such a
part for every owner, as long as the owner's code works the same for
everyone else. The second pass, its model, the per-team list and the larger
token cap are gone, so routing is back to one haiku call.

* fix(stamphog): keep the never-cut line for any behavior change

The narrowed line ("behaves differently for anyone outside the author's
feature") let the cut model drop owners on risky one-line changes it read
as the author's own feature, such as a csrf_exempt route or a tach exclude.

An offline eval of the cut prompt on Haiku compared master, master plus
the new cut item, and the full earlier change. The new item alone, with
the original never-cut line, roughly triples the trivial requests cut for
team-devex, adds no wrong cuts on the graded set, and keeps the owner on
every planted risky change. This prompt is identical to that evaluated arm.

fix(data-modeling): keep a model's table location when it is renamed (#133713)

* fix(data-modeling): keep a model's table location when it is renamed

A materialized model's storage path ended in its current name, so the
first run after a rename wrote to a new location and rebuilt the table,
and readers looked where no data was yet.

The last path segment now comes from the location recorded on the
backing table. A model that was never materialized, or never renamed,
resolves to the same path as before, so no table moves and nothing is
backfilled.

* fix(data-modeling): rebuild when a watermark is for another table location

An incremental model's saved watermark did not say which table it
described. A renamed model could write to a new location, save a
watermark for that write, and fail before its backing table moved. The
next run then updated the backing table from that watermark and skipped
the rows in between.

The watermark now records its table location, and a run whose location
differs rebuilds the table. Progress saved without a location belongs
to the path that followed the model's name, so a model that was never
renamed keeps updating incrementally.

* chore(data-modeling): delete the test bucket each temporal test creates

The object storage fixture created a bucket per test and never removed
it. Local object storage allocates volumes per bucket, so after enough
runs every write hung and the tests timed out.

The fixture now empties and deletes the bucket it created. A bucket that
existed before the test is left alone.

* refactor(data-modeling): align incremental imports with the contracts move

* fix(data-modeling): carry table_uri on the contracts IncrementalState

* fix(data-modeling): import set_incremental_state through the facade in the temporal test

feat(data-catalog): rank metric search hits by meaning behind a flag (#133537)

* feat(data-catalog): rank metric search hits by meaning behind a flag

Word matching cannot find a metric when the agent uses other words, such as
"subscriber income" for MRR. With data-catalog-metric-semantic-search on and
AI data processing approved, search also ranks metrics by cosine similarity
between the query embedding and a vector stored on each metric.

A Celery task embeds the name, display name, description and unit after a
write that changes them, and backfill_metric_embeddings embeds existing
metrics. The two lanes merge by each hit's best rank, so weak word matches
that both lanes find cannot push down the closest semantic hit. A failed or
slow embedding call leaves word matching only.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(data-catalog): address review findings on semantic metric search

- Give the embedding model and text hash columns a database default, so
  the previous release can still insert metrics during the rollout.
- Skip a stored vector whose text changed since it was made.
- Store a refreshed vector with one conditional update on the embedded
  fields, so an edit during the embedding call cannot be overwritten.
- Defer the vector column when loading the returned metrics.
- Cap metric-list searches per project, because a search can call the
  embedding worker.
- Register the refresh task in the task snapshot.
- Bound the eval's OpenAI client, and store text hashes on seeded vectors.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(data-catalog): throttle metric writes and drop unused facade exports

A metric write that changes its embedded text schedules an embedding call,
so create and update get a per-project throttle pair that also covers
session-authenticated callers. Nothing outside the product used the
embedding exports, and the facade lint rejects one that takes a model.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* chore(data-catalog): pass the flag mock to the list filter test

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(data-catalog): backfill metric embeddings with a beat task

Metrics written before semantic search have no vector, and the management
command needs someone to run it in every region. A beat task now runs
every 10 minutes, picks up to 100 live metrics with no current vector in
organizations that approved AI data processing, and queues their
refreshes 4 seconds apart, so the embedding worker sees a steady trickle.

The task is temporary: once existing metrics have vectors, writes keep
them current, and the task and its schedule entry can go.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(data-catalog): keep confident word matches first and bound the semantic lane

- A confident word match ranks above every meaning-only hit.
- The semantic lane skips teams with more than 2000 embedded metrics, and
  streams vectors instead of holding them all.
- A text change clears the stored vector, so the backfill sweep finds a
  metric whose refresh failed.
- Metric reads no longer load the vector, except the semantic lane.
- Drop the unused embedding_model parameter and hit fields, and name the
  refresh outcomes.
- Test the flag-on search path, its fallback, and where the throttles apply.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(data-catalog): read vectors in one query and keep them on a same-text write

- The semantic lane clears the embedding deferral from metrics_for_team, so
  it no longer loads each vector with its own query.
- A write that resends the same search text keeps its current vector.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* feat(data-catalog): gate the metric embedding backfill behind its own flag

The beat sweep and the backfill command now embed existing metrics only for
teams with data-catalog-metric-embedding-backfill on. A metric write still
embeds that metric with no flag.

fix(data-modeling): infer view columns with describe, not a zero-row run (#137363)

* fix(data-modeling): infer view columns with describe, not a zero-row run

Saving a view read its column types by running the query on ClickHouse with
LIMIT 0. ClickHouse still builds every JOIN right side and every GLOBAL IN set
before it applies the outer LIMIT, so a save over large tables waited for those
reads, and so did the column refresh task that follows a save.

get_columns now prints the query through HogQLQueryExecutor, which keeps the
acting user's warehouse access control and the team's modifiers, then runs
DESCRIBE TABLE (<sql>) on the printed SQL. It uses the same probe the
materialization run already uses: GLOBAL IN downgraded to IN, the two settings
that add GLOBAL back pinned off, and a retry on the untouched SQL when
ClickHouse cannot plan the downgraded one. Those helpers move from the
materialize activity into logic/describe_columns.py so both paths share them,
and the save path and the run agree on types. Scalar subqueries and GLOBAL
JOINs can still run while ClickHouse plans, as they do for that probe today.

A view that calls jev() still runs its model calls first, as before. The
executor clears external tables before it prints, so the result tables are
registered on a database the executor reuses and sent with the DESCRIBE.

The LIMIT 0 rewrite and the IN-subquery visitor are deleted. The ClickHouse
test matrix now asserts, for joins, CTEs, IN and scalar subqueries, COLUMNS(),
unions, the person join, a nested view and a jev view, that the described types
equal the types of running the query, and that DESCRIBE is the only statement.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(data-modeling): return described columns as a dataclass

The column probe returned (name, type) tuples, which the devex semgrep rule
blocks because both elements are strings and can be swapped. The materialize
activity already had a frozen _DescribedColumn for the same pair, so it moves
into logic/describe_columns.py as DescribedColumn and both paths use it.

The product lint requires the contract-check inputs to watch
describe_columns.py, because a data_warehouse test patches it by dotted path.

The DESCRIBE call keeps its f-string with a nosemgrep line: the SQL comes from
the HogQL printer and the values stay parameterized.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(data-modeling): keep the described column type in the facade contracts

The product lint refuses a facade re-export of a data type defined outside
facade/contracts.py, and the materialize activity imports DescribedColumn
through the facade. The dataclass moves to contracts.py.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test(backend): update query snapshots

* fix(data-modeling): keep describe names, skip jev model calls, retry s3 reads

Three gaps in the DESCRIBE column probe, found in review.

The probe downgrades GLOBAL IN to IN to keep ClickHouse from building the set
while it plans. An unaliased output column that contains a GLOBAL IN, such as
countIf(event IN (SELECT key FROM groups LIMIT 5)) where the groups expansion
adds one, is named after its SQL, so the probe reported a name the view does
not have. When the downgrade changes anything, the probe now aliases each
output column whose name changed with the untouched query's name. The
materialization run shares this probe and gets the same fix.

A view with a jev() column ran the jev SELECT and called the model on every
save and column refresh, because the zero-row rewrite was gone. The probe now
plans jev with LIMIT 0 on each jev SELECT, so the model gets no input and the
result tables still carry their types.

The executor retried one transient S3 read error before. The probe now does
the same, so a warehouse sync that replaces files during a save does not fail it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(data-modeling): keep in subqueries empty while planning jev columns

To type a jev() column, the probe runs the jev SELECT as the planner's source
query with LIMIT 0. ClickHouse still builds the full set of an IN subquery
before it applies that limit, so a jev view filtered with IN (SELECT ...) read
the whole subquery on every save and column refresh.

While it plans jev, the probe now also limits every IN subquery to zero rows,
as the zero-row rewrite did before. The DESCRIBE itself does not need this,
because it downgrades GLOBAL IN and pins the settings that add GLOBAL back.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test(backend): update query snapshots

* fix(data-modeling): tag the describe probe and keep its edge cases safe

Four review findings on the DESCRIBE column probe.

The old path ran through HogQLQueryExecutor, which tags each query with
query_type and the tables it reads before it calls sync_execute. The probe
skipped that, so outside tests every view save and column refresh logged a
missing-tag warning and the query log recorded the probe as type Other. The
probe now tags query_type HogQLQuery and the executor's read tags.

The probe renames an output column back to its untouched name when the GLOBAL
IN downgrade changes it. ClickHouse names an unaliased expression after its SQL
with bound values inlined, so the name can contain a percent sign, which the
printer refuses in an identifier. Such a query now describes the untouched SQL,
as the fallback for ClickHouse error 8 does.

Planning jev columns ran the source query with refresh_stale_view_columns left
on, so a missing upstream column could start a nested column refresh inside
this one. The planning executor now turns it off, as the old get_columns did.

The module now defines each helper before its first caller.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(data-modeling): rename described columns instead of aliasing the probe

The probe downgrades GLOBAL IN to IN, which changes the name ClickHouse gives
an unaliased output column that contains one. The probe aliased such columns
with the untouched name, and when that name held a percent sign, which the
printer refuses, it described the untouched query instead. That fallback
brought GLOBAL IN back, so ClickHouse built the whole set during DESCRIBE, the
cost the probe exists to avoid.

The probe no longer aliases anything. Both callers rename the described
columns by position. Where ClickHouse names the column itself, it shortens a
subquery to _subquery_N, so the printer's name for the untouched query does not
match. The described name then differs only by in( against globalIn(, and the
probe puts the GLOBAL prefix back. A column that also holds a plain IN keeps the
printer's name for the untouched query, which is exact for the function calls
the printer aliases.

The type-parity test now also checks that no probe sends globalIn.

feat(data-modeling): tell viewers when the plan slowed a refresh (#136695)

* feat(data-modeling): add a plan-based minimum refresh interval behind a flag

* fix(data-modeling): satisfy devex semgrep rules on the plan floor

* fix(data-modeling): enforce the plan floor only where the scheduler does

The consumer ceiling moved up to the plan floor even while clamp_existing kept
grandfathered consumers at their faster cadence, so an upstream could slow past what
they need. Lift it only by the enforced floor. Pin checks now read targets as the
scheduler honors them. Accept the 24hour floor name, which is how sync_frequency
says daily. Keep schedules unchanged when the flag raises or holds a bad payload,
instead of reading that as no floor and speeding them up.

* fix(endpoints): serve clamped views for the plan floor's interval

A view the scheduler runs at the plan floor kept the freshness window of its
saved cadence, so its endpoint counted the table as stale between runs. Reads
then ran inline and drew the inline rate budget, and the endpoint reported not
ready. The serving decision, the materialized cache TTL and the ready status
now use the coarser of the saved cadence and the floor the scheduler applies.
The saved cadence stays what the API and the activity log report.

* fix(endpoints): satisfy the type check on the version's team

* fix(endpoints): recheck snapshots that serve on the plan floor

A throttle snapshot could keep the plan floor's window for up to an hour after a
plan or flag change removed the floor, so inline reads drew the materialized
rate budget. A snapshot whose window comes from the floor now expires in a
minute, and other snapshots keep their longer lifetime.

* chore(endpoints): drop the plan floor note from the cache timeout comment

* fix(data-modeling): keep a stored cadence saveable when nothing else is allowed

While the plan floor is not enforced, a view with a consumer finer than the
floor has no allowed cadence: the plan blocks the finer ones and the consumer
blocks the coarser ones. The unsatisfiable check ran first, so re-sending the
cadence the view already has failed, against the rule that a cadence saved
before the floor stays saveable.

* fix(endpoints): apply the plan floor only to a declared cadence

The scheduler leaves a node with no cadence unscheduled, so the floor does not
slow it. Widening that version's window served a table no schedule refreshes
for the floor's interval instead of its cache TTL.

A new serving_window property reads the declared target once, so classifying a
request no longer runs that query twice. A test pins the fallback to the
declared window when the flag cannot be read.

* fix(data-modeling): validate pins against saved cadences so lifting the floor restores schedules

* fix(endpoints): keep a saved cadence when a query edit creates a new version

* fix(data-modeling): let teardown run and refuse speed-ups while the plan floor is unreadable

* fix(data-modeling): move schedules onto the new floor when a plan changes

An endpoint's serving window follows the plan floor on the next request, but
schedules only moved on the next edit. A plan change left the two apart, so
requests ran inline until someone saved the view.

update_org_details now schedules a reconcile after commit when the
subscription state changes. It covers only DAGs that already have a schedule,
because a reconcile also moves a DAG onto tiers.

* fix(data-modeling): keep legacy schedules safe and retry the plan change reconcile

A second review of the plan floor fixes found three problems.

The plan change reconcile also matched whole-DAG legacy schedules. Without
seeded targets it would delete them and stop those DAGs. It now covers only
DAGs entirely on tier schedules, and the unreadable floor path leaves legacy
schedules alone.

The reconcile ran once and swallowed failures, and the plan change does not
fire again. It now raises after trying every DAG, so the task retries.

The SDK returns no result, without raising, when flag definitions fail to
load. That read as no floor, so a reconcile could speed up a clamped schedule.
On cloud it now counts as an unreadable floor, unless definitions are loaded
and the flag is gone.

Also pass ids to carry_saved_query_frequency_target, as the product lint asks.

* fix(data-modeling): only count failed flag loads as an unreadable floor

Counting every missing flag result as a failed read let one flag edit block
saves and reconciles for every organization, and refused them on E2E stacks,
which may never load definitions. Only deployed cloud with the SDK enabled and
no definitions now counts as a failed read. A flag whose conditions need data
this read does not send reads as no floor and logs a warning.

Retries also stretch to about three hours, because 31 seconds would lose the
reconcile in any real outage.

* test(data-modeling): cover a reader of a managed view slowed by the plan floor

* refactor(endpoints): return a dataclass from the query change step

* fix(data-modeling): retry stale schedules and keep managed reader cadences

The plan change reconcile runs once, so a stale schedule it could not
delete kept running on the old floor. Report failed deletes and raise so
the task retries.

Readers of a managed view no longer take the plan floor as a source floor.
The floor already blocks those cadences as a plan limit, and only plan
limits let a saved cadence stay, so re-saving a reader returned a 400.

* fix(data-modeling): treat a schedule that is already gone as done

Temporal lists schedules from an eventually consistent store, so a listing can
name a tier that another reconcile just deleted. The plan-floor withdrawal
stopped at that tier and left the cleared node on the tiers after it. A stale
delete counted as a failure, so a converged DAG retried its whole organization.

* fix(data-modeling): retry a reconcile held back by an unreadable plan floor

While the floor cannot be read, slow-downs and re-saves still pass validation,
but the reconcile after commit raises and the error was swallowed. The write
reached the database and never reached the schedules, and no periodic task
reconciles them. A query edit could leave a new endpoint version on no schedule.
The failure now queues a per-DAG reconcile with the same backoff as the
organization task.

* feat(data-modeling): add a reconcile command scoped to organizations

batch_reconcile_teams converts every DAG of a team: it seeds targets, so a DAG
with no schedule can start materializing, and the seeds skip the plan floor.
Moving existing schedules after a flag change needs only the reconcile the plan
change task runs, which leaves those DAGs alone.

* fix(data-modeling): keep cadences below the plan floor off when offering pins

A pin only holds a view back from its consumers, so the backend refuses a pinned
cadence below the floor. The picker offered it because its pin branches ran
first. A selected pinned segment stays clickable so a view can still be unpinned.

* fix(endpoints): preload the organization when loading a version

The serving window reads the organization on every materialized run, even with
the flag off, which added two queries per request on result cache hits.

* fix(data-modeling): refuse unknown organizations in the reconcile command

A malformed id raised out of the loop and lost the failure summary, and a typo
printed success for an organization that does not exist. The command now checks
every id before it reconciles any.

* fix(data-modeling): scope the reconcile retry to its team and queue it when withdrawal fails

The retry task looked a DAG up by id alone. It now carries the team id and filters on it.

An unreadable plan floor queues a retry, but a Temporal failure while taking cleared nodes off their schedules escaped as a different error and queued nothing. It now raises the floor error with the Temporal failure as its cause.

* chore(data-modeling): extract the pin copy from the frequency

fix(data-modeling): start view enrichment only for views it can enrich (#138273)

After a materialization succeeds, the succeed activity decides whether
the workflow starts the semantic enrichment child workflow. It compared
the enrichment hash and checked the AI approval, and nothing else.

The enrichment activity then skips a managed viewset view, a test view
and a view with no stored columns. A skip stores no hash, so the next
run of the same view starts the child workflow again. One day of
production logs showed that nearly every child workflow ended in one of
these skips, and that no LLM pass failed.

The succeed activity now calls view_ready_for_enrichment, the check the
save path already uses, so it reports enrichment_needed only for a view
the enrichment activity processes. The decision stays in the activity
result, so the workflow emits the same commands and needs no patch.

The fixture view in the succeed activity tests has no columns. The tests
that expect enrichment, and the test for an unchanged hash, now store
columns so they still exercise the hash comparison.

The MCP registry ran internal-only behind the mcp-registry flag and has

how to bring it back by reverting this commit.

feat(desktop): read model lists from Django instead of the legacy gateway (#132715)

* feat(desktop): read model lists from Django instead of the legacy gateway

The PostHog Code model pickers still fetched /v1/models from the legacy
Python llm-gateway, which is being retired:

- web port: the task input preview and the Pi model catalog fetched it
  straight from the browser;
- desktop: the auth proxy forwarded /v1/models to legacy when the Go
  credential was blocked, and the pickers fell back to legacy when the
  proxy could not start;
- the API client's cloud task config read it too.

All of these now read GET /api/projects/:id/tasks/models, which serves
the model catalog with each model's context window and plan mark. A new
contracts helper maps that response onto the gateway model shape the
existing option builders, filters and Pi catalog already take, so no
picker logic forks. Served models (GLM, Kimi, DeepSeek) are labelled
"posthog" the way Go labels them, and the web preview now filters by
harness the way desktop does, so they appear there too.

The desktop path through a working Go credential is unchanged.

* fix(desktop): keep plan limits in web model picker and answer catalog read errors

The web preview options now come from the shared cloud task builder, as
desktop's do. Models the plan cannot use keep their restriction metadata,
and the default selection skips them, so a free-plan web user no longer
starts on a blocked model.

The auth proxy now reads the Django catalog body inside its error handler.
A truncated body or invalid JSON returns a 502 instead of leaving the
client request open until it times out.

* fix(agent): read own-subscription Claude model list from Django

A Claude session on the user's own subscription listed its models from
the legacy gateway's /posthog_code/v1/models. It now reads the project's
tasks/models list through the agent's PostHog API client, the same
endpoint and credential the desktop and web pickers use.

The PostHog plan does not bill a subscription run, so plan restrictions
from that list no longer lock models under machine auth. That matches
the unauthenticated legacy fetch, which reported every model as allowed.

* fix(desktop): stop routing gateway calls to the legacy gateway

With no project selected, the desktop started its local proxy against the
legacy gateway. A Go gateway token is minted per project, so there is no
Go route without one: the proxy now refuses with a "select a project"
error instead. The session target no longer carries the legacy gateway
URL it never used, and ensureGatewayProxy drops the API host argument that
only fed it.

The harness posthog provider defaulted to the legacy gateway's
/posthog_code path when given no baseUrl. It now defaults to the Go
gateway host for the region, which routes by credential and header rather
than path. getLlmGatewayUrl and GATEWAY_PRODUCT in the harness had no
other callers and are gone.

* fix(desktop): time out the django model list after 10 seconds

The desktop and web pickers read the Django model list through
authenticatedFetch, whose default timeout is 30 seconds. A stalled request
held the picker and cloud run creation for that long. Both fetches now
pass a 10-second timeout, as the gateway fetches did before. A failed or
timed-out fetch yields an empty list, and the shared option builder then
selects DEFAULT_GATEWAY_MODEL.

* fix(desktop): refuse redirects on the proxied django model list

The auth proxy's Django model-list fetch followed redirects by default.
authenticatedFetch checks only the first origin, so a redirect could send a
main-process request elsewhere before the status check. The legacy
forwarder used redirect: "manual", and this fetch does again, so a
redirect lands on the existing non-ok path and answers 502.

feat(auth): require an emailed code on first IdP login (#136687)

* feat(auth): require an emailed code on first IdP login

An OIDC or SAML login starts a session without proving the user receives
mail at the address the identity provider asserted, and the provider's
email claim is now trusted as-is.

Hold the first login through an identity provider until the user enters a
code mailed to that address, then record the proof under the provider's
issuer so later logins through it skip the step. A second config fronting
the same issuer shares the proof; a different issuer needs its own.

The proof lives on a new model rather than on the social auth row, because
a SAML uid is prefixed with the config's relay state, not the issuer.

* fix(auth): register the model at app population and type its manager

The new model has to be imported from posthog/models/__init__ so it registers at app population, and it needs an explicit objects annotation for mypy.

* fix(auth): move the migration after master's latest

Merging master into the stack base brought newer migrations, so this one takes the next number and depends on 1436.

* fix(auth): list the new model in the IDOR semgrep rule

Repo checks require every model to appear in the IDOR rule or the excluded list, and a new model joins the user-scoped patterns.

* fix(auth): pass the inbox provider to the code step

The merged base added a second argument to setCodeVerificationRequired, and the undefined reducer value failed the auth logic test.

* chore(auth): tighten the comments this diff adds

* fix(auth): key the IdP proof by identity and gate before linking

The proof was scoped to the account and its issuer, so a second identity
at the same provider that asserted a proven address skipped the code and
took over the account. The gate also ran after `associate_user` and
`social_create_user`, so an unproven identity was linked, and an account
with unverified credentials had its password and passkeys dropped, before
any mailbox check.

Key the proof by the provider's issuer and its own subject for that user,
and compare the address it was mailed to, so neither a new identity nor a
config repointed to another provider inherits a proof.

Move the step ahead of `associate_user`, and move the credential clear out
of `social_create_user` to the points where the address is proven.

* fix(auth): link the proven identity inside the user's scope

Semgrep blocks an unscoped lookup on a user-scoped model, and get_or_create reports an identity linked elsewhere through the unique constraint.
