## Why

- **Restart from here** could leave the model seeing turns the user meant to discard. Answers to `ask_question` and rejection feedback are chat rows but tool results in the saved history, so every answer moved the cut one message too late. "Restart and revert files" also counted tool results as checkpoint runs and restored a far later checkpoint.
- Kimi K2.6 on FreeAuto wrote `<invoke name="read_files">…</invoke>` as plain text on a turn's first reply (session `1791310436747_6s0c1`). Nothing ran, the guard didn't fire, and the user had to type "please go on".
- BalanceAuto saw `terminated: SocketError: other side closed (UND_ERR_SOCKET)` mid-reply. The drop counted against Sonnet's health, the message promised "another model", and the recovery run reset the router's turn state.

## What changed

**Restart from here** (`SdkController.editMessageAndRegenerate`, `sdk-user-message-mapping.ts`, `sdk-checkpoints.ts`)
- New `answersTool` flag on `ClineMessage` (proto field 27), set on answer and rejection-feedback rows. Prompt rows are counted without those rows and checked against the row's text. When the ordinal and the text disagree, the nearest message with the row's text wins.
- Editing an answer row restarts after the question, with the answer taken out of the tool result. The edited answer goes out as the next message.
- Checkpoint runs use core's `countUserRunMessages`. Only earlier runs' checkpoints are carried over, and their refs are kept (`retainCheckpointRefs`, now exported from core) before the old session is deleted.
- Late edit diagnostics from the abandoned turns are forgotten. A refused file revert no longer cancels the running turn.
- Router and advisor state are keyed by the session's real id, read when a run starts. Before, the key was the previous session's id or the cwd, so the turn summary was missing, and the call log recorded the workspace path as its `sessionId`.
- New **PlinyCode: Show Last Model Request (debug)** command (`last-model-request.ts`).

**Tool calls written as text** (`sdk/packages/llms/src/providers/text-tool-calls.ts`)
- `createTextToolCallFilter` replaces the Kimi-only filter and runs for every model with tools. It reads Anthropic XML (with and without the namespace and the `function_calls` wrapper), Qwen3-Coder `<tool_call><function=…>`, Hermes JSON and Kimi tokens.
- Nothing is recovered when the markup is in a code fence, is followed by prose, names an unknown tool, has arguments that can't be read, comes alongside native calls, or is in a failed stream. All-or-nothing per section.
- New `text-tool-call` guard rule. It is active for paid models and on a run's first reply too, but not the judge.
- Router addendum: tool calls only through the interface; reply in the user's language.

**Dropped connections** (`router-integration.ts`, `ai-sdk-stream-events.ts`)
- The first transport error in a turn waits 2 s and retries without `recordFailure`. A second one in the same turn is a normal failure.
- A recovery run continues the turn (no `beginTurn`), so `maxFailoversPerTurn`, the call log, the classifier verdict and the reviewer's edits carry over.
- A stream cut while tool-call arguments were streaming adds `— cut off while writing a <tool> call` to its error. The continuation prompt then asks for the call to be made again rather than continued.
- Router rows use catalog names ("Claude Sonnet 5").

**Docs:** new `docs/restart-from-here.md` (linked from AGENTS.md). Updated `docs/pliny-free-auto-router.md` and `docs/pliny-balance-auto.md`.

## Testing

- `bun run build:sdk`, `bun run types`, `bun run check-types` (apps/vscode), `bun run lint`, `bun run format`, `bun run check:docs`, `bun -F plinycode-dev analyze:unused:prod`: all pass.
- Extension vitest `src/sdk/`: 90 files, 1534 passed. New tests:
  - restart mapping with answers, rejection feedback, the text check and checkpoint numbering against core's counter;
  - `forget()` on the edit-problems reporter;
  - the text-tool-call guard rule, including while inactive;
  - run recovery: transport retry, turn continuation, the lost-tool-call prompt and catalog names;
  - last-request capture.
- llms vitest: 736 passed. New `text-tool-calls.test.ts` uses the real failing replies from the user's sessions (Kimi `<invoke>`, BalanceAuto Qwen `<tool_call>`). The adapter test now covers a non-Kimi model's XML call.
- `test:unit` (bun): 997 pass, 43 fail. All the failures are in `src/core/hooks/__tests__`, caused by a stray `%TEMP%\package.json` with `"type": "module"` on this machine, which makes the CommonJS hook scripts the tests write there fail to load. Unrelated to this change.
- Not exercised in a dev host. The pre-release is for that: see "To try" in the release notes.

Pre-release: https://github.com/lgiaccar/PlinyCode/releases/tag/release_0.2.0-test.1

Three things from one request: let the routers compact later and make that tunable, show every compaction in the chat without feeding it to the model, and explain (and fix where it was a bug) the context bar dropping without a compaction.

## Router defaults and compaction budgets

- **Built-in model orders = the orders tuned in Settings → Router during the 0.2.4 runs.** FreeAuto: kimi-k2.6 → GLM-5.2 (internal-tests, vmodels) → nemotron ultra → nemotron super, pool limited to its routes' models. Smart: GLM-5.2 first. Fast: qwen3.5-397b first. BalanceAuto: Sonnet 4.6 → Sonnet 5 → kimi on every main route (coding included). Untouched rules files refresh to the new defaults; edited ones keep theirs.
- **Higher budgets, one table** (`plinyRouterBudget` in `pliny-models.ts`): FreeAuto 200k (was 150k), Smart 300k (was 150k), BalanceAuto 300k (was 128k), Fast 64k. The virtual windows grow to the largest window of the order (512k, 512k, 1M), so the bar's denominator changes.
- **Settings → Router → Compaction.** A budget and a post-compaction size per router, in tokens or %. Non-blocking notes say which models hand larger requests on before compaction starts, and warn when no model in the order fits the trigger, or when the target can't work. The engine gets absolute tokens through two new `CoreCompactionConfig` fields, `maxInputTokensOverride` and `targetTokensOverride`, read before every call. A model tuning's smaller context still wins. The bar's marker follows the tuned budget.
- **Calibrated size filter.** `fitsContext` measures each candidate in its own tokens (per-model `tokenCalibration`). The flat 3 chars/token dropped kimi at about 127k real tokens, before compaction ran. With calibration it takes about 167k.

## Compaction in the chat, not in the context

- Overflow-recovery compaction now gets a divider ("Context compacted (the model rejected it as too large)") instead of the raw `overflow-recovery-compacted` slug, and rescales the bar.
- An agentic compaction's divider has **Show summary**: the summary the model continues from (capped at 8k chars, carried on the `completed` notice).
- A reopened conversation rebuilds the latest compaction's divider where it ran, from the compaction sidecar.
- The Markdown export writes each finished compaction as a line, with the summary in `<details>`.
- Divider rows never reach the model; a new engine test asserts the compacted history holds no notice text. The model still gets the summary message, and the basic strategy keeps its one-line `<SYSTEM_NOTICE>Earlier context was compacted…`: it tells the model turns are missing and is not a chat notice.

## The context bar dropping without a compaction

Most drops are intended per-request trimming: stale tool output and earlier reasoning at each new prompt, in-turn aging on uncached models, superseded reads, side questions, model switches. The new hover line "Trimmed from the last request: −Xk" (`prunedTokens`) names them. docs/context-compaction.md explains each one.

Fixed:
- The bar counted the reply's output tokens. It now shows the request's input (`contextTokens`).
- A retried empty reply summed both attempts into one row, so the bar doubled and then fell. The same doubled count also fed the compaction trigger's previous-request count and the token calibration. Billing still sums every attempt, but the row, the trigger and the calibration now take the last attempt's input (`requestInputTokens`, stamped by `retry-empty-response.ts`).

## Tests

- `build:sdk`, `types` (incl. extension + webview), `lint` (same 8 warnings / 15 infos as stage), `format`, `check:docs`, knip: clean.
- shared 377, llms 745, extension unit 1026, extension vitest 2213, webview 746: all pass.
- core: 1732 pass, 5 fail. These are the hook-file and MCP-client tests, and they fail the same way on a clean `origin/stage` worktree on this machine (temp-file ENOENT, fake server `require` under ESM).

Not checked in a dev host yet: the Settings fields, the divider's summary and the marker position.

## What changes

**About page.** Settings → About → Community & Support now links only to the PlinyCode repository. The Cline links are gone: X, Discord, r/cline, the cline/cline GitHub, Issues, Feature Requests, docs.cline.bot and cline.bot. `package.json`'s `repository` field pointed at `cline/cline` too; it now points at this repo.

**FreeAuto classifier gave no verdict.** The smart profile now and then logged `classifier gave no verdict (unusable reply: The user wants to …) · using the heuristic routes`. The call log has 5 of these over two days.

- Cause: the classifier model (Qwen3.6 35B-A3B) reasons in its content. The same prompts replayed against the gateway:
  - With `chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking: false` (the off-switch we already send), it gave a verdict 28 of 28 times.
  - Without it, it wrote the "The user wants to …" paragraph and hit the 512-token cap before any JSON, 10 of 12 times.
  - So on the failing calls the off-switch didn't take effect. I couldn't find where, so this fix doesn't depend on the switch.
- Fix: the classifier and the completion judge also ask for `response_format: {"type": "json_object"}`. With that set and thinking **left on**, the 35B returned a clean verdict 6 of 6 times in about 300 ms. Qwen3 Coder 480B, Kimi K2.6, GLM-5.2 and Haiku 4.5 all accept the field over the gateway without error.
- Engine plumbing: a new `GatewayStreamRequest.responseFormat: "json"`, set from `AgentModelRequest` `options.responseFormat`. A Pliny-only provider-option rule maps it onto the wire; other providers are untouched.

## FreeAuto: reasoning effort, classifier, profiles and call log

Commit `57555a4` on `lgiaccar/few_impr`

### Why
FreeAuto picked a model per call, but it never controlled *how much the model thinks*. Small edits and deep planning got the same treatment. Several free models turned out to reason on every call, which is slow, and there was no way to compare routing strategies on real use.

### What changed

**Measured reasoning controls**
- `probe-pliny-free-models.ts --thinking` asks every free model a short trick question with six variants of the request. It records whether the model reasons by default and which request field turns reasoning on or off. Results are in `docs/pliny-free-auto-thinking.md`.
- Findings:
  - GLM-5.2, nemotron-3-super, qwen3.5-397b and the qwen3-27b family reason by default. `chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking=false` turns this off.
  - qwen3-coder, kimi-k2.6 and nemotron-3-ultra never reason.
  - qwen3-8-27b, qwen2.5-32b and llama-3.1-70b answer `reasoning_effort` with a **400**. Sending a generic "think" flag to them fails the call.
- These results are stored per model in `pliny-models.json`. A new Pliny provider-option rule sends only the off-switch the probe measured for that model. Models without a measured switch are left alone.

**Reasoning effort per route**
- Routes accept `effort: quick | think` and `reasoningEffort: low | medium | high`.
- Defaults: planning uses think/high. Coding, quick questions, sub-agents and huge-context use quick. The default route leaves each model's own behaviour.
- The routing row shows what was applied, for example `route: coding · quick`.

**Classifier (smart profile)**
- A small, fast model (qwen3-6-35b, which never reasons) runs once per turn. It returns `{tier: quick|code|reason|huge, think: bool}`.
- The tier maps to a route through the rules file, so the classifier never names a model. Its think verdict overrides the route's effort.
- It doesn't run for sub-agents or requests with images. If it times out or returns an unusable reply, the heuristic routes decide.

**Profiles**
Three FreeAuto models in the picker, each with its own rules file:
- `FreeAuto`: heuristic routes with effort set per route.
- `FreeAuto · fast`: reasoning off everywhere it can be turned off.
- `FreeAuto · smart`: the default routes plus the classifier.

**Call log**
- Every routed call is appended to `~/.cline/data/pliny-free-auto-calls.jsonl`. Each entry has the profile, route, tier, effort, model, estimated tokens, time to first token, duration and outcome.
- `bun apps/vscode/scripts/summarize-free-auto-log.ts` compares profiles and models.
- New command: **PlinyCode: Open FreeAuto Call Log**.

**Also**
- Fixed the generated rules file. Its regexes were written in double-quoted YAML, which made the file invalid, so FreeAuto silently ignored it. They're now single-quoted, and a test checks that the generated YAML parses.
- Sub-agents are now on by default.

### Known limitation
The engine can only turn reasoning on through `reasoning_effort`. A model whose only on-switch is the chat template can't be made to think. The only such model (gemma-4-31b-it-29cea) isn't used by any route.

### Testing
- Extension vitest: 1380 passing. Engine `llms`: 755 passing. The bun unit suite passes.
- `bun run types` and `bun run lint` are clean.
- The thinking probe was run against the live gateway.
- Not yet tried in a live chat.

### To try it
1. Pick `FreeAuto · fast` or `FreeAuto · smart` in the model picker.
2. Watch the routing rows in the chat.
3. After a few sessions, run the summarize script to compare profiles.

# feat(pliny): FreeAuto model router with automatic failover

## Summary

Adds a virtual **FreeAuto** model (`pliny/free-auto`), now the default, that
picks a free self-hosted Pliny model per call from a user-editable Markdown
rules file and recovers automatically when a model misbehaves. Also adds a
Settings entry point to locate/open that rules file.

## Why

The picker exposed ~22 free models behind one fixed default, and self-hosted
models fail in ways that killed the turn and left the user on a manual Retry:
output-token truncation, stalled streams, socket deaths, empty responses, and
streams ending without a finish reason. The rules file itself was only
reachable from the command palette, which is not discoverable.

## How it works

Two generic SDK hooks carry the routing logic, both optional and inert unless
a host sets them:

- **`agentModelFactory`** builds the run's `AgentModel`, with a
  `createDefault({modelId})` escape hatch for concrete delegates.
- **`onRunError`** recovers a failed run in place. `executeRunWithAuthRetry`
  becomes `executeRunWithRecovery`, keeping the existing auth behaviour and
  adding bounded, host-driven recovery.

Failure handling splits on **whether output was already streamed**:

| Situation | Behaviour |
| --- | --- |
| Fails before any output | Next candidate takes over invisibly |
| Fails after output | Reported as a finish event; turn retried in place, continuing |

After content it never re-streams and never rethrows: a throw would escape the
agent loop before the partial assistant message is built, losing it from the
transcript and duplicating text on retry. A `run-failed` event is held back
while recovery is pending, so a recovered turn never leaves the UI in its
terminal error state.

A per-call stall watchdog covers silent streams (Pliny's own timeout is 5
minutes and covers only the whole request). Every call and turn end is
timestamped with its model in the chat and output channel.

Existing free selections migrate to the router once, guarded by a persisted
flag; paid selections are untouched. The virtual id never reaches the gateway:
compaction and commit-message generation map it to a concrete model first.

**Settings entry point:** Settings → API Configuration now has an "Open rules
file" link under the Pliny paid-models checkbox. The webview passes a
`pliny://free-auto-rules` URI to the existing `openFile` service (alongside
`remote://`); the host resolves the real path and creates the file from
documented defaults if it doesn't exist yet.

## Results

Probed all 22 free models live. **The measurements corrected three guesses:**

- Both `snps-provider-sia` models are down, so they no longer sit near the front.
- The vmodels GLM replica beat the primary, so it now leads the huge-context route.
- `qwen3-8-27b` was slow (~975 ms TTFT), so the quick route prefers
  `qwen3-next-80b` and `nemotron-super`.

**A new test caught a real hang:** the stall watchdog awaited
`iterator.return()` on a generator parked on a never-settling await, which
deadlocked the process. Fixed to abandon the stuck iterator.

### Verification

| Suite | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Extension unit (81 files) | 1120 passed, 0 failed |
| Core orchestrator | 81 passed (12 new) |
| llms (incl. Pliny catalog) | 723 passed |
| shared | 425 passed |
| agents | 87 passed |
| Extension typecheck | clean |

Verified end to end in a Cursor dev host: extension activated, wrote its rules
file, persisted the migration flag, and opened the file via the new Settings link.

## What this changes

Two features: an **Ask mode** next to Plan and Act, and a reworked **history view** with a favorites filter that works, search, date filters and pinned conversations.

### Ask mode

- The mode switch has one segment per mode: **Plan**, **Act**, **Ask**. Clicking a segment selects it. The shortcut cycles Plan → Act → Ask.
- In ask mode the agent answers questions and cannot edit any file:
  - the engine's `ask` tool preset leaves `editor` and `apply_patch` out;
  - an ask-mode `beforeTool` guard rejects any write that still reaches those tools (markdown included) and the shell commands on the file-editing blacklist plan mode already uses;
  - the ask-mode prompt tells the model to show a change in its reply and ask the user to "toggle to Act mode", which the chat renders as a link.
- Ask mode runs on the act-mode model. For FreeAuto and BalanceAuto it routes like plan mode, and the completion judge does not run.
- Switching to ask never starts a run by itself.

### History

- **Favorites filter.** `getTaskHistory` paged the history first and then filtered each page. A favorite older than the newest 50 conversations never showed, and when the first page had no match the list stayed empty. Search and the workspace filter had the same limit. It now filters the whole history (from the metadata cache) and then pages. The filter is a **Favorites** button above the list instead of an entry in the sort menu.
- **Search** matches every word typed against the title and the workspace path.
- **Date filter**: Today, Last 7 days, Last 30 days, or a custom from/to date and time. A conversation is in the period when its span from start to last activity overlaps it.
- **Pins.** A pin button on each row. Pinned conversations that match the filters are listed first, in a **Pinned** section. The Recent preview marks them with a pin.
- **Flags that last.** Favorite and pin change only through their toggles (`setTaskFavorite`, `setTaskPinned`). Other history writes carried a `HistoryItem` read earlier or built from scratch, so a usage update racing a toggle could un-star a conversation, and a checkpoint restore or an edit-and-regenerate dropped the star. Those two flows now copy the flags to the new session.

Design notes: [docs/ask-mode.md](https://github.com/lgiaccar/PlinyCode/blob/lgiaccar/history-filters-pins-ask-mode/docs/ask-mode.md), [docs/conversation-history.md](https://github.com/lgiaccar/PlinyCode/blob/lgiaccar/history-filters-pins-ask-mode/docs/conversation-history.md).

## Decisions worth a look

- The proto enum value is `PlanActMode.ASK_MODE`, because `ASK` is already taken in the `cline` package by `ClineMessageType`.
- Choosing a model while in ask mode changes the act-mode model. Ask has no model selection of its own.
- An ask-mode answer renders like an act-mode result, and switching to Act afterwards does not auto-continue. The user says what to apply.
- A pin does not protect a conversation from deletion. Favorites still do.
- Starring or pinning writes the session record, which moves its last-activity time to now. That was already the case for favorites.

## Limits

- The command blacklist is a list of common file-editing commands, not a shell interpreter. A script that writes files can get past it, as in plan mode. MCP tools are not covered by the guard; they go through the normal approval.
- A conversation that exists only as a manifest file (not in the session store) cannot be pinned or starred: the write does not stick. I saw this with hand-seeded e2e records and did not look into whether real conversations can be in that state.

## Testing

- `bun run check-types`, `bun run lint`, `bun run format`, `bun run check:docs`, `bun -F plinycode-dev analyze:unused:prod`: pass.
- Extension vitest (88 files) and webview vitest (66 files): pass. New tests cover the history query, the sticky flags, the date ranges and sections, the mode switch, and ask mode in the session factory and the mode coordinator.
- Engine tests for `shared` and `llms` pass. `core` has 5 failures in `hook-file-hooks.test.ts` and `mcp/client.test.ts`; the same 5 fail on this machine with these changes stashed.
- `bun -F plinycode-dev test:unit`: 6 files fail, all under `src/core/hooks/__tests__`, which fail on this machine without these changes too.
- Playwright e2e, run locally on Windows against the packaged build: `chat.test.ts` (now switches Act → Ask → Plan) and a new `history.test.ts` case (favorite beyond the first page, search, date filter, clear filters, pin and the Pinned section) pass. The other e2e files were not run locally.
- Not tested by hand with a real model: an ask-mode conversation end to end. The guard, the preset and the prompt are covered by unit tests.

## Summary
Improvements to PlinyCode's chat input, its error messages, its terminal handling, and running several tasks at once.

### Background tasks
Starting a new task, or opening another task from History, no longer stops a task that is still running. The running task moves to the background (at most 3 at a time).
- **While in the background:**
  - Its output isn't shown. The SDK still saves its conversation.
  - Its edits are written without diff previews.
  - Its terminals don't pop up.
  - Its token usage is still recorded.
- **History badges:** background tasks show **Running**, or **Needs approval** when waiting on the user.
- **Approvals and questions:** anything that isn't auto-approved is held until the user reopens the task. A notification with an **Open** button tells the user.
- **When it finishes:** the task is stopped and the user gets a notification ("finished", "stopped with an error" or "was stopped").
- **Reopening a running task** takes over its live session and shows the held approval or question. There is no Resume button.
- **Stopping:** deleting a task, deleting all history, or shutting down stops background tasks. At the limit, the running task is stopped as before and a message says so.

### Send button modes
- The dropdown now picks a **mode** that is remembered, instead of sending immediately:
  - **Send**: waits for the current turn if the agent is busy.
  - **Send now**: interrupts the current reply.
  - **Schedule**: sends at a chosen time.
- The button icon shows the selected mode, and Enter uses it.
- **Queue** was removed because it did exactly what Send does.

### Clearer error messages
- **Max output tokens:** the error now names the model, the tokens produced, the cap and what set it (Max Tokens setting, model limit, remaining context window or 32k default), and the input and context-window sizes. It ends with a matching hint. The gateway now reports the cap it applied on max-tokens finishes.
- **Aborted commands:** the error now names the command, the working directory and why it stopped (cancelled by user / task stopped or switched / repeated errors). Output produced before the abort is kept.

### Terminals
- Terminals evicted from reuse were never closed. They are now closed once nothing is running in them.
- Idle terminals are closed when a task ends, at most 2 idle terminals are kept, and agent terminals aren't restored after a window reload.
- Terminals running a command, terminals the user has typed into, and SSH sessions are never closed automatically.
- Running a command shows the terminal without moving focus to it.

### Fix
- The FreeAuto router model now has zero pricing. Without it, the engine test for self-hosted pricing failed.

## Known limitations
- Reopening a task partway through a reply: text already streamed appears once that text block ends.
- Two tasks editing the same files at once aren't coordinated.
- Reusing an idle terminal for a background task can still reveal the terminal panel. It never takes focus.

## Testing
- `bun run types` and `bun run lint` pass.
- Extension tests: vitest 1,304 and bun unit 1,151 pass.
- Webview tests: 522 pass.
- Terminal tests in a real VS Code host (`vscode-test`): 20 pass.
- Engine: `shared`, `llms`, `agents`, core tool tests and the Node smoke test pass.
- New tests cover the background registry, detach/adopt/reattach, holding and replaying approvals, send modes, the cap source, aborted-command details and terminal cleanup.
- **Manual check:**
  1. Start a long task, click New Task and start another; History shows **Running**.
  2. Approve a held tool from the notification.
  3. Set Max Tokens low and check the new error text.
  4. Cancel a long command and check it is named in the error.

## Why

The router models (`free-auto`, `-fast`, `-smart`, and `balance-auto` when it lands on a free model) end runs before the task is done, mostly right after shell commands. Nothing in the router decides when to stop: the agent loop ends a run on the first tool-free reply. The only safety net was a regex on the last sentence that never nudged twice in a row.

26 saved FreeAuto sessions had 71 run endings. 57 of them came right after a tool result, 44 of those after `run_commands`. The endings fall into these failure classes:

| Class | Example ending | Before |
|---|---|---|
| Announce-and-stop | "Let me check the current status of the benchmark runs:" | Caught, but kimi-k2.6 answered the nudge with the same line in 3 of 4 cases and the guard gave up |
| Wait/monitor bail-out (largest) | "I'll check again at **15:28**… Stand by!", "I cannot sit in the chat for 7–10 hours" | Missed — the model had no way to wait (`run_commands` detaches at 300 s) |
| Permission question for an action already requested | "Would you like me to run the benchmark now?" (6× in one fast session) | Missed by design |
| Readiness instead of action | "The benchmark is ready to run immediately…" after "build **and run**" | Missed |
| Leaked reasoning | 8k chars ending "…Hmm, but I just killed all PowerShell after 3:30 AM in" | Missed |
| Degenerate output | 14k chars of ` .   .   .` accepted as the final answer | Missed |

`free-auto-smart`'s classifier also produced **no verdict in any of 185 logged calls**, so smart behaved exactly like default. The likely cause is the default classifier model hitting the 256-token output cap before it got to the JSON.

## What changes

**Engine** (`shared`, `agents`, `core`): small and backward compatible
- `CompletionGuard` now also receives `runMessages` and `messages`, and may return a promise. `withHostCompletionGuard` awaits both guards.
- Guard reminders carry `displayRole: "system"`, so they no longer show up as user bubbles.
- The act and yolo prompts now say: "a reply with no tool call ends the task… never end a reply saying you will check back later; use `wait`".

**Extension router** (`apps/vscode/src/sdk/router`)
- `completion-guard.ts` (new) applies the rules from `unfinished-turn-guard.ts`, most reliable first: degenerate → after-failed-command → after-detached-command → announcement → wait-bail-out → leaked-reasoning → readiness → judge.
  - A second stall in a row gets a firmer reminder, and the rest of the turn moves to the default route's lead model (`↪ switching to …`). A third stall is accepted.
  - At most 3 reminders per run. Chat rows name the rule that fired (`rule: wait-bail-out, 1/3`).
- `router-completion-judge.ts` (new): once per act-mode run that has made at least one tool call, if no rule fired, the utility model is asked whether the request was carried out.
  - "Not done" sends one reminder (`⚖ The task looks unfinished — …`). No verdict means the reply is accepted.
  - Rules-file settings: `guard.judge`, `guard.judgeTimeoutMs`, `utility.judge` (defaults to the classifier model).
- `routed-agent-model.ts`: a reply that collapses into repetition is cut off mid-stream and the call fails, so the run continues on another model with a "redo the step" prompt.
- `router-prompt.ts` (new): free candidates get a system-prompt addendum about how their turn ends. Paid candidates see the prompt unchanged.
- `router-hooks.ts` (new) layers two hooks over the session's hook scripts:
  - `afterTool` appends a note to failed and detached shell results ("do not end your turn now: fix and rerun…").
  - `afterRun` writes one line per run to `pliny-free-auto-runs.jsonl`: how it ended, last model and tool, rules fired, judge verdict, reply tail.
- Classifier fixes:
  - Output cap raised to 512 tokens, and the prompt asks for the JSON first.
  - Parsing handles fenced JSON, nested objects and an unclosed `<think>`.
  - The raw reply is logged, and `classifierError` is recorded on the turn's first call.
- `scripts/summarize-free-auto-log.ts` reads both logs: run endings per profile/model/route, rules fired, the classifier's verdict rate, and `--tails`.

**`wait` tool** (`apps/vscode/src/sdk/vscode-wait-tool.ts`, registered for every session): up to 10 min per call and 1 h per run, and it can be cancelled. Its result tells the model to check progress with a tool call.

## BalanceAuto (merged from `stage`, #33)

Stage renamed the router helpers (`isPlinyRouterModelId`, `plinyRouterProfile`). Conflicts in `router-integration.ts`, `router-rules.ts` and `router-integration.test.ts` are resolved as follows:

- **One predicate, checked per turn.** The guard, the judge and the command note apply to a BalanceAuto turn only when a free model is answering.
- **The guard checks the main agent's last call.** Sub-agents get no completion policy, so the guard only ever judges the main agent's reply. Stage's version checked `activeTurnKey`, which after a sub-agent run points at the sub-agent. That would nudge a reply from a paid model because a free sub-agent ran earlier in the turn. Stage's BalanceAuto test is updated to that behaviour.
- **The command note follows whichever agent ran the tool.** New test added.
- **Escalation on BalanceAuto** moves a stalled free-model turn to the lead of the `default` route, which is Claude Sonnet 5.
- The prompt addendum is added per candidate (free only). Degenerate-output failover applies to every model. Runs are logged with `profile: "balance"`.
- `defaultRules` keeps both BalanceAuto's classifier and the new guard settings.

**Docs**: `docs/pliny-free-auto-router.md` gets a "Keeping runs going" section, and `docs/pliny-balance-auto.md` explains how it applies to BalanceAuto. The seeded rules file documents `guard`.

**Version** → `0.1.3-test.3` for the pre-release auto-update.

> Pre-releases follow `<next release>-test.<N>`, now documented in `docs/releasing.md`. `0.1.3-test.3` sorts above the published `0.1.3-test.2`, so editors on it will update. (An earlier revision of this PR used `0.1.3-dev.N`, which the updater treats as older than `test.2`.)

## Verification

- `bun run build:sdk` and `bun run types`: clean. Biome: clean.
- `bun -F plinycode-dev test:unit`: 1191/1191.
- Router and wait tool: 237 router tests plus 5 wait-tool tests. They cover:
  - the real transcript endings above as fixtures
  - the escalation sequence
  - failover on degenerate output
  - when the judge runs and its cap
  - run-log records
  - BalanceAuto guard and note gating
- `bun -F @plinycode/agents test`: 90/90. `@plinycode/llms`: 762 passed. Webview model filter: 18/18.
- `@plinycode/core test:unit`: 2 failures in `hub/server/index.test.ts`. They are a `HubLockHeldError` caused by a live hub on the dev machine and are unrelated to this change.

Not yet verified live:
- that `free-auto-smart`'s classifier now returns a verdict (the first row should read `classifier: code`, or another tier)
- a benchmark-style task that uses `wait`
- a BalanceAuto turn routed to a free model

After a day of use, `bun apps/vscode/scripts/summarize-free-auto-log.ts --tails` shows early-stop rates per model and profile.

## What changes

**New**
- **Per-conversation spending limit.** New `plinycode.spending.conversationLimit` setting (default $5; 0 turns it off), also editable in Settings → General. Before each model call, if the conversation has spent the limit, the run stops and a message says what was spent and how to continue. Sending a message allows another round of the same amount. It works like the mistake limit: no blocking prompt while the agent loop is live.
- **Pliny budget display.** A new `getPlinyBudget` RPC reads `/api/svc/v1/llm-gateway/budgets/my-usage` with the same key and host as chat requests. The binding budget (the period with the least money left) shows under the home screen header and in the task header's expanded details. It turns red at 90% used or when the gateway reports the budget as blocked. It only shows while Pliny is the active provider, and refetches at most once a minute.
- **Conversation title in the task header.** The title is centered, with the workspace name (`parent/folder`) under it in smaller text, whether the header is collapsed or expanded.

**Fixes**
- **History cost differed from the conversation's cost.** Several writers raced on the history record: rename, favorite and active-time writes put back stale totals, and per-event deltas collided with the engine's own end-of-turn total. The history record now stores the same totals the task header computes (`getConversationApiMetrics`), and only usage writes can change them.
- **Claude on Bedrock rejected tool-call ids** (`tool_use.id: String should match pattern '^[a-zA-Z0-9-]+$'`). Mixed routing leaves ids such as `call_…`, `functions.x:0` or `tool_<nanoid>` in history. The OpenAI-compatible request body now rewrites every `tool_calls[].id` and `tool_call_id` to a deterministic, valid id, so each call and its result still match. Stored history keeps the original ids.
- **File paths in answers didn't open.** Absolute paths in plain text (e.g. `d:\…\report.md`, `/home/me/x.py`) and backslash or absolute paths in backticks now become "open in editor" links. Absolute paths open even with no workspace folder.
- **Scheduled prompts use a 24-hour clock.** The picker is a date field plus 00–23 hour and minute selects, defaulting to the next 5-minute mark at least 5 minutes out. The scheduled list shows 24-hour times.

## Tests
- New: `tool-call-ids.test.ts`, an `openai-compatible` wire test, `plinyBudget.test.ts`, `spending-limit.test.ts`, `scheduleTime.test.ts` and `filePathDetection.test.ts`. The history and event-coordinator tests are extended for the usage totals.
- Locally, these all pass: `bun run types`, lint, format, the full llms suite (787) and the extension `src/sdk` vitest suites (1410+).
- These fail locally on unchanged code too, so they are environmental:
  - React component tests in the webview (Bun 1.4.2 here vs the pinned 1.3.x)
  - hook-script tests (a stray `package.json` in `%TEMP%`)
  - DevOps `tools.test.ts`, which came from #54

CI runs the pinned toolchain.

Pre-release version: **0.1.5-test.7**.

## What changed

**Plan item 29b (track K).** The models.dev-derived generated catalog (`catalog.generated.ts`, `providers.generated.ts`, `provider-ids.generated.ts`) previously included every models.dev provider, even ones PlinyCode can never run because #84's `usesShippedAdapter` filter only excluded them from the runtime registry afterward, not from generation itself.

1. Extracted `usesShippedAdapter` (family must be `openai-compatible` or `anthropic`, and not `protocol: "openai-responses"` / `client: "openai"`) into `sdk/packages/llms/src/providers/builtin-types.ts` so it's a single predicate shared by:
   - `builtins.ts` (unchanged behavior — still filters `GENERATED_PROVIDER_SPECS` before merging into the runtime registry)
   - `catalog-live.ts`'s `getSelectedModelsDevProviders`, which now excludes non-shippable-family providers **before** they're written to any generated file.
2. Regenerated all three generated files against live models.dev data with `bun run build:models`.
3. Removed `catalog-cline-recommended.ts` / `cline-recommended.generated.ts` (the Cline-cloud recommended/free/ClinePass model-list fetch-and-merge machinery) — PlinyCode never calls Cline's cloud recommendation endpoint, and `core/services/llms/cline-recommended-models.ts` (the other consumer named in the plan) was already deleted by earlier PRs (confirmed absent). Removed the now-dead `includeClineCloudModels` option on `ModelCatalogConfig` and the `GENERATED_CLINE_RECOMMENDED_MODELS` re-export.
4. Fixed every consumer/test that exercised the removed behavior or asserted on now-excluded providers (`catalog-live.test.ts`, `builtins.test.ts`, `provider-defaults.test.ts`, `local-provider-service.test.ts`, `apps/vscode/test-setup.js`'s stale mock).

The other consumers named in the plan (`catalog.generated-access.ts`, core's `provider-defaults.ts`, `local-provider-registry.ts`, `provider-settings-legacy-migration.ts`, `provider-settings.ts`, extension's `cline-session-factory.ts`, `model-catalog/store.ts`, `shared/storage/provider-keys.ts`) only use generic catalog APIs (`getGeneratedModelsForProvider`, `getProviderCollectionSync`, etc.) and needed no changes — verified by reading each and by the full test suites passing. `providerSwitchNormalization.ts` no longer exists (removed by PR #90).

## Removed

Ten models.dev providers whose family isn't `openai-compatible`/`anthropic` are now excluded from generation entirely (previously merely hidden from the runtime registry): `bedrock`, `gemini`, `infer`, `meta`, `mistral`, `neosmith`, `openai-native`, `perplexity-agent`, `vertex`, `vivgrid`. Also removed: the Cline-recommended-models snapshot/fetch machinery, its generated file, and the dead `includeClineCloudModels` config option.

## Kept

Everything `openai-compatible`/`anthropic`-family (201 of the prior 203 generated providers — 2 fewer net, since models.dev's own listing also changed between generations). Pliny/FreeAuto/BalanceAuto are unaffected: `pliny-models.ts` builds `PLINY_*` models from `data/pliny-models.json` directly, never from the generated catalog (confirmed by reading the module and running `pliny-models.test.ts` / `pliny-thinking.test.ts`, both passing).

## Behaviour

No runtime behavior change for the extension: the ten removed providers were already unreachable (filtered by `usesShippedAdapter` in `builtins.ts` before this PR), so nothing that previously worked is now missing. The change moves the exclusion earlier (generation time) instead of later (registry time), shrinking the checked-in generated files and the shipped bundle by that much.

## Sizes

- `catalog.generated.ts`: 4,017,047 → 4,049,560 bytes (181,407 → 183,443 lines). Roughly flat: isolating just the 10 removed providers' old contribution (measured against the pre-change file) removes ~10,634 lines / ~5.9% of the old file, but normal upstream model-count growth between generations outweighs it in this snapshot.
- `providers.generated.ts`: 84,898 → 84,269 bytes (203 → 201 providers).
- `provider-ids.generated.ts`: 3,285 → 3,245 bytes.
- `dist/extension.js` (production esbuild): 16,926,234 → 16,933,262 bytes (+7,028 bytes / +0.04%), measured by building the same worktree at the pre-change commit and at this branch's tip. The catalog-size wash above explains why the bundle didn't shrink either.

## Checks run locally

- `bun run build:sdk`
- `apps/vscode`: `bun run check-types`
- `apps/vscode/webview-ui`: `bunx tsc -b`
- root: `bun run lint`, `bun run format`, `bun run types`, `bun run check:docs`
- `bunx vitest run` in `llms` (672 passed), `core` (1558 passed, 5 pre-existing environment failures unrelated to this change — reproduced identically on a clean `stage` checkout: Windows temp-dir ENOENT in `hook-file-hooks.test.ts`, ESM `require()` in `mcp/client.test.ts`), `shared` (356 passed)
- `bunx vitest run` in `apps/vscode` (1297 passed) and `webview-ui` (467 passed)
- `bun run test:unit` in `apps/vscode`: only the 7 pre-approved baseline failures (`hook-factory`, `taskcancel`, `taskcomplete`, `taskresume`, `taskstart`, `user-prompt-submit`, `devops-mcp/server/__tests__/tools.test.ts`)
- `apps/vscode`: `bun run build:webview` and `bun esbuild.mjs --production`

## Leftovers / risks

- The catalog-size and bundle-size deltas are essentially a wash in this snapshot because upstream models.dev data grew between generations; the real, isolated savings (~10,634 lines) only shows up when diffed against the pre-change file rather than against a hypothetical re-fetch of the old payload. An audit of what goes into each model request found two problems. The context was growing with material the model no longer needed. Meanwhile, the content it did need was being cut. This PR fixes both. Pre-release: [0.1.7-test.6](https://github.com/lgiaccar/PlinyCode/releases/tag/release_0.1.7-test.6).

The router's timestamped status rows (`auto-free-smart → model (call N · route …)`) were already UI-only; they never reach the model. They are unchanged here.

## Engine

- **Old reasoning is no longer resent.** The openai-compatible provider sent every earlier turn's reasoning back as `reasoning_content` on every request.
  - Reasoning from before the current user turn is now dropped at request time (`prior-turn-reasoning.ts`, applied in the orchestrator's `beforeModel` and in the compaction size estimate). It stays in history for the UI.
  - Inline `<think>` blocks in earlier assistant text are stripped too.
  - Signed Anthropic thinking is kept.
  - Injected reminders don't count as a new turn: `isUserRunMessage` decides where a turn starts.
- **Whole tool results.** `MessageBuilder` cut every tool-result string to 8k characters (a 4k head and 4k tail), while the tools return and advertise ~48k.
  - The per-string cap is now 50k.
  - Several large entries in one result share a 64k budget, never below 8k each.
  - The cap depends only on the block's own content, so prefix caches are unaffected.
- **Plain-text tool output.** `read_files`, `run_commands` and `search_codebase` results (`{query,result,success}[]`) are sent as `<result query="…">` text, not JSON-escaped strings.
- **Earlier compaction for the routers.** Compaction reads the virtual router's `ModelInfo`, not the routed model's.
  - FreeAuto's `maxInputTokens` is now 92k, so it compacts at ~83k tokens: where the 128k tier stops fitting (`(128k − 32k) / 1.15`). It used to compact at ~230k.
  - BalanceAuto's is now 128k, so it compacts at ~115k instead of ~180k.
  - The advertised `contextWindow` values are unchanged.
- **Loop-detection notices reach the model.** The soft notice was appended to the `ConversationStore` and then overwritten by the next `replaceMessages`. It now goes through a new `consumeSystemNotice` runtime hook, as a `displayRole: "system"` message.

## Rules and skills

- **One editor's files.** A new `setInstructionHost({ editor, globalRulesDirectory })` in `shared/storage/paths.ts` narrows the rule and skill search paths.
  - VS Code gets `.github`, Cursor gets `.cursor`, Windsurf gets `.windsurfrules`.
  - `AGENTS.md`, `.clinerules`, `.cline`, `.agents` and `.claude` load everywhere.
  - The Rules panel uses the same resolvers, so it follows too.
- **One global rules folder.** `Documents/Cline/Rules` is now the only global rules folder.
  - `~/.cline/rules` is no longer read. Its files are moved to `Documents/Cline/Rules` at activation, keeping their toggles. Name clashes are left in place and logged.
  - `~/Cline/Rules` and the OneDrive guesses are dropped when the host sets the folder.
- **Scoped rules on demand.** Rules with globs, `applyTo:` or `alwaysApply: false` are listed by path for the model to read when they apply, instead of being inlined in full.
- **Size caps.** Always-on rules are capped at 12k characters each and 40k in total; the overflow is listed by path.
- The system prompt names the real editor instead of always saying "VS Code".

## Extension

- **Mention caps.**
  - `@file` is capped at 100k characters (was 400 KB).
  - `@folder` is capped at 100k characters in total; files past that are named, not pasted.
  - `@url` is capped at 50k.
  - The truncation notice now names tools that exist.
- **DevOps MCP tools only where they work.** They are offered only when the session's repo has a GitHub or Azure DevOps remote (`BuiltinMcpSource.appliesTo`).

  - message-builder caps
  - `formatToolOperationResultsAsText`
  - router compaction budget
  - rule budgets and scoped listing
  - `setInstructionHost` paths
  - loop-notice hand-off

hits.body:
## Problem

PlinyCode finds agents, skills, rules, hooks, and workflows through several independent loaders. The customization panel, runtime, slash commands, and CI Board do not always use the same folders, validation, selection rules, or refresh behavior.

This leads to confusing results:

- An agent in a custom folder can appear in the panel but be unavailable to the running conversation.
- Same-name assets can resolve differently depending on where they are used, and CI Board can suggest disabled or malformed skills.
- A foreign agent file can load even when its tool or permission restrictions cannot be honored. New files or relative skill resources can also be missed or resolved incorrectly.

Users need to know which file PlinyCode will use, why it was selected, and whether it can actually work as intended.

## Proposal

Create one shared inventory that all these parts of PlinyCode use. Keep every candidate visible, with its source, workspace scope, enabled state, compatibility, and selection reason. Use that same source information for discovery and refresh.

Apply clear behavior:

- **Predictable selection:** explicit user choice first, then the conversation's workspace, personal assets, and packaged defaults. Ask the user to choose between same-name candidates within the same scope.
- **Clear availability:** fall back to the next enabled candidate when one is disabled. If the preferred candidate is invalid or has an unsupported restriction, explain the problem and require an explicit alternative.
- **Consistent activation:** resolve skill resources from the skill's own folder and apply changes between requests, showing any pending runtime rebuild. Discovering executable files must not automatically run them.

Start by unifying the inventory and reporting existing differences. Preserve current selections initially, then introduce the agreed selection rules with a preview of affected assets.

**Expected outcome:** the panel, runtime, slash commands, and CI Board agree on which applicable assets are usable, with understandable explanations when an asset is disabled, ambiguous, or incompatible.

Roadmap A9 (docs/roadmap.md). Fixes three ways usage went missing from a conversation's cost, and splits the token panel's side usage by source.

**Root causes found**
1. Sub-agent events carried no agent id, so the engine added a sub-agent's usage to the root's turn usage and then dropped it at turn end (the end-of-turn total is rebuilt from the root's own result). Sub-agent usage only came back on resume, through the message files; a failed or timed-out sub-agent persisted no messages, so its cost was lost for good.

**Engine:** the progress reporter tags forwarded events with `agentId`/`parentAgentId` (`spawn_agent` and `subagent_<name>`). A finished or failed sub-agent's totals (output figures on success, progress sums on failure) are settled into the session's aggregate under its id (`settleSubAgentUsage`), so it counts once, including after a resume. A turn that throws still persists the usage it built up.

**Extension:** advisor and compaction usage live under `extraUsage`, which the engine never writes. The history list (and the cost/token sorts) reads the engine's aggregate plus `extraUsage`, or the extension's running totals when larger, so history matches the header. Old sessions read as before. Background tasks also record compaction usage.

Third wave of the context-management audit (`docs/context-management-audit.md`), stacked on #125; retarget to `stage` once that merges. Sub-agents were nearly useless in the extension and their cost was invisible; this makes `spawn_agent` a real delegation primitive.

## Changes

**Engine (`sdk/packages/core`, `sdk/packages/shared`)**

- **A real system prompt.** A sub-agent got only the text the parent model wrote. It now gets the same base prompt as a root session (environment block with the conversation's git snapshot and pinned date, the session's mode), a short account of its role, the parent's instructions as rules and a host-supplied suffix (`subagent-prompts.ts`). The Cline CLI provider keeps its override shape.
- **Delegation guidance.** A rules extension (`subagent-guidance.ts`) adds a "Delegating to sub-agents" section to the system prompt while `spawn_agent` is in the request: when to delegate, what the sub-agent knows, what to put in `task`.
- **Tool input and output.** `task` plus optional `instructions` (`systemPrompt` kept as the older name); the description says what the tool is for and not for. The output carries cache tokens and `totalCost`.
- **Live progress and cost.** `createSubAgentProgressReporter` wraps the sub-agent's events and calls the parent tool call's `emitUpdate` after each model call and tool with `subAgentId`, tool count, tokens, cost and context size. Configured `subagent_<name>` agents use the same reporter.
- **Limits.** At most 3 runs in flight per tool (a semaphore), 20 minutes per run with a derived abort signal (the `timeoutMs` field was never enforced), 40 iterations by default (`subAgentMaxIterations`), delegation one level deep (`MAX_SUB_AGENT_DEPTH`), and the session's compaction (`prepareTurn`) for sub-agent runs.
- **Policies and approval** are threaded into sub-agent and configured-agent runs (`createSessionSpawnTool` options, `RuntimeBuilderInput.subAgentPrepareTurn`); the host's approval wrapper is shared by the lead and its sub-agents.
- **Host tools for sub-agents.** `CoreSessionConfig.subAgentExtraTools`: the built-in shell is suppressed in the extension in favour of its own `run_commands`, which lived in `extraTools`, so sub-agents had no shell at all.
- **Run identity for hosts.** `agentModelFactory` receives `agentId`; `onRunError` receives `agentId` and `parentAgentId`.

**Extension (`apps/vscode`)**

- Sub-agents get `run_commands` (always in the background executor), `wait`, the task list and MCP tools; not the advisor or the memory tools (`SUB_AGENT_DENIED_TOOLS`). `subAgentPrompt` carries the IDE, platform, snapshot, date and a read-only excerpt of the repository's important memory entries (`renderSubAgentMemoryExcerpt`, ≤ 2k chars).
- **Cost accounting.** The translator handles `spawn_agent` and `subagent_<name>` alike (`isSubAgentTool`), reads cost and cache tokens from the result into the `subagent_usage` row (disjoint buckets like the root's), and keeps the engine's agent id per entry. Background tasks record a sub-agent's totals from its tool result.
- **Approval.** A new **Delegate to sub-agents** auto-approve toggle (`useSubagents`, default on; `state.proto` field 9); a sub-agent's own calls follow the existing toggles, and its approval asks are preceded by a row naming the sub-agent (`describeAgent`).
- **Router per-run state.** `activeTurnKey` and `recoveringRootRun` were one closure shared by parallel sub-agents; a root failure after a sub-agent run benched the sub-agent's model. Runs are keyed by agent id (`runsByAgent`, `recoveringRuns`); hooks look up by the snapshot's agent id.

## Verification

- `bun run check`, `bun run check:docs`, knip: pass (two interfaces from wave 1 un-exported for knip).
- Core: team, host, orchestration and agent suites, 429 pass. Extension vitest: 1736 pass.
- New tests: `subagent-prompts.test.ts`, `spawn-tool.test.ts` (extra tools, no nested spawn, policies/approval/compaction threaded), `memory-section.test.ts`, translator sub-agent cost row, background sub-agent usage, router per-run keys, tool policy toggle.
- Docs: new "Sub-agents" section in `docs/agent-tools.md`; `memory.md`, `environment-context.md`, `advisor-tool.md`, `pliny-balance-auto.md`, the audit.

Not verified in the dev host yet: a real delegation on FreeAuto showing live cost in the SubagentStatusRow and a sub-agent running a command.

## Why

A report said Qwen3 Coder 480B (`snps-provider/qwen3-coder-480b-a35b-inst-fp8`), a free self-hosted model, was being billed. I could not reproduce that:

- the catalog prices every `snps-provider*` model at $0, and the budget check and paid-call cap already count them as free;
- the live gateway's replies for Qwen3 Coder (streamed and not) carry token counts and no cost, in the body or in the `x-litellm-response-cost` header;
- every one of the 139 Qwen3 Coder calls in the local router log, and the 139 replies in the local traces, recorded $0.

Two places would still have counted a cost if the gateway ever reported one for a free model. This PR closes them.

## What changes

- `router-integration.ts`: `callCostUsd` returns 0 for a self-hosted model. Before, it used the gateway's figure when there was one. This affects the router's call and run logs and the sub-agent spend in them.
- `one-shot-model-call.ts`: `resolveCallUsage` returns `totalCost: 0` for a self-hosted model. This covers the advisor, image descriptions and Improve prompt. Before, a gateway-reported cost was used as is.

The conversation's own cost (the task header and history) still takes the engine's usage figure. That figure is the gateway's cost, else the catalog price (which is $0 for these models), so it would show a cost only if the gateway started reporting one.

- New `one-shot-model-call.test.ts`: a self-hosted model is free with or without a reported cost, and a paid model keeps its reported cost or is priced from the catalog.
- New case in `router-integration.test.ts`: a free model's call is logged at $0 when the gateway reports $0.005.

## Summary

Four chat and cost fixes. The cache fix matters most, because it cuts paid BalanceAuto cost.

### 1. Prompt cache for paid Claude models (BalanceAuto)

**Evidence.** I joined 167 local sessions' per-message `metrics` with `pliny-free-auto-calls.jsonl` to see which model served each call:

- **Sonnet 5, when it writes no text between tool calls (the usual case).** Every call reads exactly the system prompt (13,022 tokens) and writes 0, while input grows from 44K to 128K tokens. Session `1791958896107_yy670` paid $5.00 where $1.39 was needed. Across all cache-enabled Claude calls, about half the input spend was wasted.
- **`aws-bedrock-vmodels/claude-4-6-sonnet-*-thinking` (BalanceAuto's planning route).** 0% cache reads and 0% writes, on every version.

**Root causes**

- `withContentBlockCacheBreakpoints` only marked user/assistant text. A tool-only assistant turn goes out as `content: null`, so the moving breakpoint fell back to the prompt that opened the turn. The function hasn't changed since #41. Hit rates swung with how much the model narrates: Sonnet 4.6 narrates more than Sonnet 5, so it hit more often.
- The thinking presets had no `cache_control` in `pliny-models.json`, so no breakpoints were sent for them at all.

**Fixes**

- Breakpoints now go on three places:
  - the system prompt
  - the newest message, usually the latest tool result, as a content-block marker on the tool message
  - the end of the previous step, so the previous call's cache entry is found even beyond Anthropic's 20-block lookback
- I measured on the live gateway that it honours a content-block marker on a tool message. It drops message-level markers, which the old comment had generalised to all tool-message markers.
- The thinking presets are flagged `cache_control`, with Sonnet cache prices. Both cache on the gateway, and its `costInUSD` matches $0.30 read / $3.75 write per million tokens.

**Live gateway, Sonnet 5, 4 agent steps** (`apps/vscode/scripts/probe-pliny-prompt-cache.ts`):

| step | legacy read / write | fixed read / write | uncached tokens (fixed) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 0 / 4,570 | 0 / 6,796 | 2 |
| 2 | 4,570 / 0 | 6,796 / 2,222 | 2 |
| 3 | 4,570 / 0 | 9,018 / 2,222 | 2 |
| 4 | 4,570 / 0 | 11,240 / 2,222 | 2 |

**Free models.** They report `cached_tokens: 0` from the backend. Parsing is correct, and they cost $0, so I left them unchanged.

**Follow-up, not done here.** `dropPriorTurnReasoning` rewrites the previous turn's unsigned reasoning at each new user turn. Now that the thinking presets are cached, that costs one cache miss per user turn on them.

### 2. Token usage panel (task header, under the context bar)

- **Bars:** one stacked bar per LLM call (cache read / cache write / input / output) for the last 80 calls. Hovering a bar shows that call. The colours are categorical slots that pass a colour-blindness check on VS Code's dark surface; on light mode the legend and text labels carry the values.
- **Summary:**
  - models, with call counts
  - calls and cost (shown only where the provider shows cost)
  - In, Out and Reason tokens
  - Cache R, W and hit rate
  - a line for sub-agent and advisor usage
- **Data plumbing:**
  - `routed-agent-model.ts` tags usage events with the model that served the call.
  - `AgentTokenUsage.modelId` carries it into saved message metrics. The live usage event's `reasoningTokens` and `modelId` go to `ClineApiReqInfo`, and history replay reads both back.
  - Older conversations show the router's own name.

### 3. Prompt navigation arrows

**Causes of the misses and no-ops**

- Prev/next used Virtuoso's `rangeChanged.startIndex`. That index includes the 3000px `increaseViewportBy` band above the view, so it pointed well above what the user was looking at.
- Prev/next never disabled auto-scroll, so streaming pulled the view back to the bottom.
- The scroll-to-bottom button mounted and unmounted, which shifted the stack under the cursor.

**Fix**

- Prev/next now read the top row from the DOM.
- They disable auto-scroll.
- They step from the last target while a smooth scroll is still running.
- They use `align: start` under the sticky header, and jump without animation to rows that aren't rendered.
- Prev above the first prompt goes to the top; Next past the last prompt goes to the bottom.
- The buttons sit in fixed slots: top, prev, next, bottom. The bottom button is hidden, not unmounted.
- The scroll listener does one layout read per frame. The scrollbar marker highlight uses the same top row.

### 4. Reloaded conversations lose prompt highlighting

- Replaying all local sessions found no case where a typed prompt became agent text. What does go missing on reload is any user text that is persisted only inside a tool result:
  - answers to `ask_question`
  - feedback typed when rejecting a tool
- Both are now rebuilt on replay, as the live path shows them: `ask:"followup"` with `selected` set, then `user_feedback` with `answersTool` set.
- A `say:"task"` row inside the list now renders with the prompt frame instead of as markdown.
- Not fixed: the session-start sanitizer can drop message metadata and merge user blocks. The safe fix is to keep each non-tool-result user message separate; that is left for a follow-up.

## Testing

- `bun run types`, `bun run lint`, `bun run format`, `bun run check:docs` and `analyze:unused:prod` pass.
- **llms:** 737 passed (the one failure was the preset-cache test; it is now updated). **shared:** 373 passed.
- **core:** 1,660 passed. 5 tests fail locally, in `hook-file-hooks` and `mcp/client`. Their temp `.js` fixtures hit Node 26 ESM `require`; this is an environment issue in untouched code.
- **Extension vitest:** 1,739 passed. **Webview vitest:** 579 passed.
- **Extension bun unit suite:** passes except the `src/core/hooks/__tests__` files, which fail with the same hook-script environment issue.
- **New tests:**
  - breakpoint placement
  - catalog cache flags
  - adapter reasoning and modelId
  - router usage tagging
  - replay of answers and rejection feedback
  - prompt navigation against a DOM fixture
  - fixed button slots
  - token panel and its helpers
- Live-gateway probe as in the table above.
- Not yet checked in the dev host.

## Problem

Custom agents in workspaces that follow the GitHub Copilot `.agent.md` convention were not loading because:

1. **`name:` was required** in frontmatter — files like `fm-dev.agent.md` only have `description:`, so they all failed to parse and the picker showed nothing.
2. **Subdirectories were not searched** — agents under `.github/agents/fm-agents/` and `.github/agents/prime-topo-agents/` were silently skipped.

## Changes (`configured-agent-config.ts` in `@plinycode/core`)

### `name:` and `description:` are now optional

Both fields are `optional()` in the Zod schema. When absent:
- **`name`** falls back to the file's basename with all recognised extensions stripped: `fm-dev.agent.md` → `fm-dev`, `code-review.agent.md` → `code-review`, `reviewer.md` → `reviewer`
- **`description`** falls back to an empty string

This matches the GitHub Copilot convention exactly.

### One level of subdirectory recursion

The loader now recurses exactly one level into subdirectories of each search path:
```

.github/agents/ top-agent.agent.md ← found ✓ fm-agents/ fm-dev.agent.md ← found ✓ (was skipped before) fm-planner.agent.md ← found ✓ fm-agents/nested/deep.md ← NOT found (depth > 1, intentional)

```javascript

Applies to all search paths: the built-in `.github/agents` default, `.cline/agents`, and any path in `chat.agentFilesLocations` / `github.copilot.chat.agentFilesLocations`.

## Tests

New tests cover: basename fallback, `.agent.md` compound extension stripping, missing `description`, subdirectory loading, depth limit, and deduplication.

## Result

All 18 agent files in the PRIME repo (including the 7 in `fm-agents/` and `prime-topo-agents/` subdirectories) load with no frontmatter changes needed.
```

## Summary

Adds a read-only **`ado_agents`** MCP tool to the built-in DevOps MCP server that lists self-hosted Azure DevOps agents in an agent queue, with their online/offline status and user-defined capabilities.

This unblocks queries like "which agents in queue 21 have `BUILD_CPU`, `BUILD_GPU`, `PERFORMANCE`, `BUILD_LIN_CPU`?" that the existing pipeline/PR-focused tools couldn't answer.

## How it works

`ado_agents(queue_id, capabilities?)`:
1. Resolves the agent **queue** to its agent **pool** (`GET {project}/_apis/distributedtask/queues/{id}`).
2. Lists the pool's agents at the **org-level** pools endpoint (`GET {org}/_apis/distributedtask/pools/{poolId}/agents`), since agent pools are organization-scoped, not project-scoped.
3. Requests `includeCapabilities=true` **only when a `capabilities` filter is given** (cheaper otherwise).
4. Keeps agents whose **user-defined** capabilities include every name listed, and returns a Markdown table: `| Agent | Status | Enabled | Capabilities |`.

Azure DevOps only — the tool rejects non-ADO remotes with a clear message.

## Changes

| File | Change |
| --- | --- |
| `providers/types.ts` | `AgentInfo` interface + optional `listAgents?(queueId, options?)` on `ToolProvider` (ADO-only, like `listExpiredBuildPolicies`) |
| `providers/azdo.ts` | `listAgents` impl + org-level `orgApi` helper (pools are org-scoped, not project-scoped) |
| `tools.ts` | `ado_agents` tool definition + `INSTRUCTIONS` line |
| `__tests__/providers.test.ts` | 3 provider tests (happy path, no-capability call omits the flag, queue-with-no-pool throws) |
| `__tests__/tools.test.ts` | 3 tool tests (filter by capability + online/offline, list all, no-match message) |
| `docs/devops-mcp.md` | Tool-table row + description paragraph |

6 files, +222 / -1.

## Verification

- `bun test` on the two affected test files: **53 pass, 0 fail** (incl. all 6 new tests).
- `biome lint` on all changed files: clean.
- `biome format` applied (no remaining diff).
- `tsc --noEmit` on the extension: **exit 0**.

## Notes

- The new tool is read-only, so it needs no approval gating (the write/destructive tools — `pr_comment`, `pr_review`, `pipeline_run`, `pipeline_cancel`, `pipeline_rerun` — remain the gated set).
- Agent pools are org-scoped on ADO, so the implementation adds a small `orgApi` helper alongside the existing project-scoped `api` helper rather than reusing it.

Fourth wave of the context-management audit (`docs/context-management-audit.md`), stacked on #126; retarget to `stage` once that merges. Compaction robustness and a context bar that tells the truth. New doc: `docs/context-compaction.md`, linked from `AGENTS.md`.

## Changes

- **Agentic compaction falls back to basic when it declines.** The agentic strategy never cuts before the latest typed prompt and folds nothing twice, so once everything before that prompt was summarized it returned nothing, and the request went out over budget until the provider rejected it (one overflow recovery per run, then the run ended). Basic compaction, which can trim inside the latest turn, now runs whenever agentic declines, including when the summarizer answers with no text. A summary that leaves the request over the trigger is not retried at once: the next model call compacts again and lands in this branch.
- **"Still too large" is said, not discovered.** When basic compaction leaves the request over the trigger (one typed message alone is too big), the engine emits `compaction-insufficient` and the chat shows an info row with the sizes.
- **The summarizer's cost is recorded.** `generateSummary` collects the stream's usage; the compaction result, the completed notice and the summary message's metadata carry `summarizerUsage`; the extension emits a `subagent_usage` row with `source: "compaction"` live and rebuilds it from the summary message on reopen.
- **Images count as images.** `serializeForTokenEstimate` replaces base64 blobs and data URLs with a placeholder worth `IMAGE_TOKEN_ESTIMATE` (1,600 tokens) in the request estimate, the compaction estimator and the context breakdown. A 1 MB screenshot was ~350k tokens, which triggered compaction and dropped the output-token clamp. Detection requires mixed base64 character classes, so long identifiers and hex digests stay text.
- **Context breakdown rules bucket.** The engine passes the rules it composed as request metadata (`AgentConfig.contextSources`); the provider's usage report already reads it. Skills/workflows buckets are still 0 (noted in the doc).
- **Threshold marker on the context bar.** The bar divides by the advertised window, while compaction fires at 90% of the input limit (FreeAuto: ~83k of 256k). `autoCompactThresholdFor` computes the share; the bar draws a marker with the token count; the hover card explains it in place of the old "click the bar to set a threshold" copy (no such control exists).
- **Cache breakpoint probe.** `PLINYCODE_CACHE_MARK_TOOL_CALLS=1` marks text-less tool-call messages with a one-character text so the moving breakpoint can follow a tool loop. Off by default until measured.

## Verification

- `bun run check`, `bun run check:docs`, knip: pass.
- Core: 1670 pass; the same 5 environment-only failures as before (hook tests need `bash`, MCP tests break on a stray `%TEMP%\package.json`). Shared 376, llms 737, extension vitest 1739, webview 552: pass.
- New tests: compaction fallback (nothing to fold, next-call trim, reasoning-only summarizer, insufficient notice, summarizer usage), `tokens.test.ts`, cache probe, translator compaction usage/insufficient/replay rows, context bar marker, summary copy, threshold helper.

Not verified in the dev host yet: a FreeAuto conversation past the 92k budget compacting instead of failing, and the marker's position.

## Problem

When the user switches agents mid-conversation via the dropdown, the session is rebuilt with the new agent's system prompt — but the model still sees its prior history which was generated under the old agent's identity. This causes confused replies ("I am Cline…") when asked "what agent are you?".

## Root Cause

The session rebuild already works correctly (history preserved, new system prompt active from the first subsequent turn). What was missing was an **in-conversation signal** telling the model that a new identity has taken effect — exactly the same problem that mode-switching solved with `<mode_notice>`.

## Fix

Mirrors the mode-switch notice pattern exactly:

1. **`formatAgentSwitchNotice(agentName)`** added to `@plinycode/shared/prompt/format.ts` — produces:
   ```
   <agent_notice>The user switched to the "Code Reviewer" agent before sending this message. Adopt the identity and instructions in the system prompt above for all subsequent replies.</agent_notice>
   ```
2. **`stripModeNotices`** updated to also strip `<agent_notice>` blocks, so users never see the XML in their chat bubble.
3. **`SdkModeCoordinator.recordAgentSwitchNotice` / `consumeAgentSwitchNotice`** — one-shot tracker scoped to the session ID (same pattern as `recordModeSwitchNotice`).
4. **`SdkSessionLifecycle.fireAndForgetSend`** — consumes the agent notice and prepends it to the next outbound prompt, alongside any pending mode notice.
5. **`SdkController.updateAgentPath`** — after rebuilding the session, derives the agent name from the file's frontmatter `name` field (fallback: basename) and records the notice.
6. **`unwrapUserInput`** (router) and **`defang`** (CI report) updated to strip/defang `<agent_notice>` tags.

## Result

After switching to "Code Reviewer" and sending the next message, the model receives:
```
System: [Code Reviewer identity and instructions]
…prior history…
User: <agent_notice>The user switched to the "Code Reviewer" agent … Adopt the identity and instructions in the system prompt above for all subsequent replies.</agent_notice>
      what can you do?
```
The model adopts its new identity, the chat history is fully preserved, and the XML is invisible to the user.

## Files Changed

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `sdk/packages/shared/src/prompt/format.ts` | Add `formatAgentSwitchNotice`; update `stripModeNotices` to strip `<agent_notice>` |
| `sdk/packages/shared/src/index.ts` + `index.browser.ts` | Export `formatAgentSwitchNotice` |
| `sdk/packages/shared/src/prompt/format.test.ts` | Tests for new function and stripping |
| `apps/vscode/src/sdk/sdk-mode-coordinator.ts` | Add `recordAgentSwitchNotice` / `consumeAgentSwitchNotice` |
| `apps/vscode/src/sdk/sdk-mode-coordinator.test.ts` | Tests for new methods |
| `apps/vscode/src/sdk/sdk-session-lifecycle.ts` | Consume agent notice in `fireAndForgetSend` |
| `apps/vscode/src/sdk/sdk-session-lifecycle.test.ts` | Tests for notice stamping and off-the-record guard |
| `apps/vscode/src/sdk/SdkController.ts` | Wire `consumeAgentSwitchNotice`; call `recordAgentSwitchNotice` + `deriveAgentName` in `updateAgentPath` |
| `apps/vscode/src/sdk/router/unfinished-turn-guard.ts` | Strip `<agent_notice>` in `unwrapUserInput` |
| `apps/vscode/src/services/devops-mcp/ci-watch/ci-report-text.ts` | Defang `agent_notice` |

## Problem

When a custom agent is selected in the picker before sending the first message, the correct agent-specific intro is shown in the chat. However, the agent picker dropdown immediately reverts to **"Generic Agent"** once the first message is submitted.

## Root Cause

`sdk-task-start-coordinator.ts` fires a fire-and-forget `postStateToWebview()` immediately after creating the task proxy (line 218), before `startNewSession()` has completed and before `pinAgentPath()` is called (line 245). During this first state push, `mergeTaskHistoryIntoState` builds a fallback synthetic `HistoryItem` for the just-started task — but:

1. The fallback `HistoryItem` did not include `agentPath`.
2. `sessionConfigBuilder.pinnedAgentPath(taskId)` returned `undefined` because `pinAgentPath` was called only after the async `await startNewSession()`.

So `ConversationAgentPicker` saw `currentTaskItem.agentPath = undefined`, and fell back through `propsAgentPath` (the local `selectedAgentPath` state), which may or may not be set at that point depending on render timing.

## Fix

Three changes working together:

1. **`sdk-task-start-coordinator.ts`** — Move `pinAgentPath()` (and `pinModel()`) calls to **before** the fire-and-forget `postStateToWebview()`. This ensures `sessionConfigBuilder.pinnedAgentPath(taskId)` returns the correct value during the first state push.

2. **`sdk-task-history.ts`** — Add `agentPath?: string` to `TaskProxyLike`. Include `task.agentPath` in the fallback synthetic `HistoryItem` inside `mergeTaskHistoryIntoState`, so the picker shows the correct agent even when the history record isn't persisted yet.

3. **`SdkController.ts`** — Annotate the `task` argument passed to `mergeTaskHistoryIntoState` with `agentPath: sessionConfigBuilder.pinnedAgentPath(task.taskId)`.

## Tests

- **`sdk-task-start-coordinator.test.ts`**: Verifies `pinAgentPath` is called before the first `postStateToWebview()` (invocation order assert), and that `agentPath` is stored in the history item.
- **`sdk-task-history.test.ts`**: Verifies the fallback `HistoryItem` in `mergeTaskHistoryIntoState` includes `agentPath` when the task has a pinned agent, and that it's absent for generic tasks.
- **`useMessageHandlers.test.tsx`**: Verifies `selectedAgentPath` is forwarded to `newTask` and is not cleared after the RPC resolves.

## Files Changed

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `apps/vscode/src/sdk/sdk-task-start-coordinator.ts` | Pin agent/model before first state push |
| `apps/vscode/src/sdk/sdk-task-history.ts` | Add `agentPath` to `TaskProxyLike` and fallback `HistoryItem` |
| `apps/vscode/src/sdk/SdkController.ts` | Thread `pinnedAgentPath` into task for `mergeTaskHistoryIntoState` |
| `apps/vscode/src/sdk/sdk-task-start-coordinator.test.ts` | New test for pin-before-push ordering |
| `apps/vscode/src/sdk/sdk-task-history.test.ts` | New tests for fallback `HistoryItem` agentPath |
| `apps/vscode/webview-ui/src/components/chat/chat-view/hooks/useMessageHandlers.test.tsx` | New test for agentPath forwarded to `newTask` |

Roadmap A11 (docs/roadmap.md).

**Before:** an image attached to a FreeAuto conversation made the router filter its candidates to image-capable models; no free model is one, so every call failed ("auto-free has no model that accepts images…"), and kept failing for the rest of the conversation because the image stays in the history. Images returned by tools reached free models as placeholders.

**Now** (`sdk/router/router-images.ts`, hooked into `routed-agent-model.ts`): a call with images is routed as if it had none. An image-capable model gets the request untouched; any other model gets a copy where each image (image parts and images inside tool results) is replaced by text. The stored conversation never changes. Setting `plinycode.router.images`:
- `describe` (default): each new image is described once by the cheapest image-capable catalog model (free preferred; today Claude Haiku 4.5, about $0.004 an image), cached per conversation by SHA-256, at most 8 new images per call; the model sees `<image_description sha="…">…</image_description>`. A first-time notice row says which model described it.
- `vision-model`: a turn that brings a new image runs on the image-capable model (route `images`); later turns use descriptions.
- `off`: the image is replaced by a note; nothing is spent.

**Paid-model gating:** paid models are used on BalanceAuto always, and on FreeAuto only when **Unlock Pliny paid models** is on. That toggle lived only in webview localStorage; it is now mirrored to the extension (`UpdateSettingsRequest` field 52, `plinyPaidModelsUnlocked`). Otherwise `describe`/`vision-model` fall back to `off` with a chat row explaining how to unlock. **Decision to confirm:** with paid unlocked, FreeAuto now spends a little on image descriptions by default (budget-checked, shown in the chat); set `off` to keep FreeAuto strictly free.

**Cost accounting:** checked against the conversation budget like the advisor; recorded as `subagent_usage` rows with `source: "vision"` (task header, history `extraUsage.vision`, an "Image descriptions" line in the token panel; background tasks too). The advisor's one-shot call helpers moved to `sdk/one-shot-model-call.ts` and are shared. The FreeAuto profiles now declare image input, so the prompt box no longer warns.

**New `view_image({ path })` tool:** PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP files inside the session's working directory (symlinks resolved, type detected from bytes), up to 3.75 MB; read approval, parallel; sub-agents and CI Board runs get it.

Docs: Images section in `pliny-free-auto-router.md`, `view_image` in `agent-tools.md`; small updates to `pliny-balance-auto.md`, `advisor-tool.md`.

Tests: scripted-model router tests (describe, cache, cost, vision-model, off, paid-locked fallback, budget refusal, untouched pass-through), 2 router-integration image tests, `view_image` tests. check-types, lint, format, test:vitest (1984), test:webview (622), test:unit (987), test:discovery, knip, build:sdk, types, llms tests (739), check:docs pass.

Live check pending: a real pasted screenshot on FreeAuto with paid unlocked and locked, `vision-model`, BalanceAuto's coding route with an image, `view_image` on a PNG.
