Roadmap A7 (docs/roadmap.md). Each item of the sub-agents row gets a chevron that opens that sub-agent's live transcript (its text, reasoning, tool and command rows, rendered with the main chat's `ChatRow`), compact and indented under the item. None of it enters the main chat.

- **Translator** (`message-translator/subagent-transcripts.ts`): sub-agent events (tagged with `parentAgentId`, or naming a known sub-agent) are translated against a translator state of their own (shared id minter, cwd, mode and model) and kept in a ring buffer: the last 300 messages per sub-agent, the 20 newest sub-agents per conversation. Asks are left out, so approvals stay in the main chat. A sub-agent's final answer shows as text, without the completion box's conversation-wide actions.
- **Bug fix:** removes the "drop every event while a sub-agent runs" fallback in `live-events.ts`, which also hid the root agent's own parallel read/search rows while a `spawn_agent` call was running.
- **Depth 2:** a second-level sub-agent opens nested under its parent's transcript, from the parent's own sub-agents row.
- **RPC:** new server-streaming `TaskService.subscribeToSubagentMessages(agent_id)`: a snapshot, then upserts by ts; collapsing the item cancels it.
- **Engine:** the spawn tool reports the sub-agent's id as soon as the run is bound, so the chevron (and the "which sub-agent asks" approval label) appears before the first model call ends.
- **Live only:** transcripts survive follow-up messages and are dropped when another conversation is opened or this one is cleared or resumed; a reopened conversation shows the final report as before. Documented in `docs/agent-tools.md` (Sub-agents → Transcript).

Tests: translator (routing, root's parallel tools still shown, concurrency, buffer caps, depth 2, a missing parent tag, surviving a root iteration), the streaming handler (snapshot, push, cancel, unknown agent, failing stream), the webview row (expand/collapse subscribes and unsubscribes, renders rows, empty states), and an engine test for the early progress update. build:sdk, types, check-types, lint, format, test:vitest (1976), test:webview (625), test:discovery, knip and check:docs pass.

Dev-host check pending: a real `spawn_agent` run (2–3 in parallel), expanding while it works, approvals staying in the main chat, depth 2, styling in the narrow panel.

## What changes

**A budget for each conversation.** The spending limit was one global number. Every conversation now has its own budget, shown next to its cost in the task header as `$cost / $budget`.

- Click the budget to change it for that conversation only. Enter or blur saves, Escape cancels, 0 means no limit. It turns red once the cost reaches it.
- It is stored as `spendingLimit` on the conversation's history record (session metadata). It survives resume and edit-and-regenerate, and writes that don't set it keep it. New RPC: `TaskService.setTaskSpendingLimit`.
- `plinycode.spending.conversationLimit` (Settings → General, now labeled "Default conversation budget") is the budget a conversation starts with. It is also the step a pause raises the budget by: at the budget, the run pauses as before, and the new budget is the amount spent plus one step, rounded up to the cent. Sending a message continues, and the header shows the new budget. This replaces the old in-memory threshold, which you couldn't see.
- **Free models are never limited.** When the active mode's model is free (a self-hosted `snps-provider*` model or an `auto-free*` router), the guard is skipped and the header shows no budget. `auto-paid-balanced` can call paid models, so it keeps a budget.

**DevOps MCP: publish a draft PR.** `pr_update` takes `draft`. `false` marks a draft PR ready for review, and `true` converts it back. Until now the agent had to ask the user to click Publish in the web UI.

- Azure DevOps: `isDraft` in the PR PATCH.
- GitHub: the REST API ignores `draft` on update. The server calls the GraphQL `markPullRequestReadyForReview` / `convertPullRequestToDraft` mutations (`api.github.com/graphql`, or `<host>/api/graphql` on GHES), and only when the status actually changes. GraphQL errors come back with HTTP 200, so the response body is checked for errors.
- The server instructions and `docs/devops-mcp.md` describe the new option.

## Testing

- `bun run check-types` (extension and webview), `bun run lint` and `bun run format` pass.
- `src/sdk` vitest suite: 82 files, 1423 tests pass. New tests cover `checkConversationBudget`, persisting the budget in task history, and the header's budget display, editor and `parseBudget`.
- DevOps MCP `providers.test.ts`: 19 pass. New tests cover the GitHub GraphQL publish and convert calls (including no call when the status is already right), GraphQL errors, and the Azure DevOps `isDraft` patch. The new `tools.test.ts` case can't run on this machine, because that file's `git commit` setup times out here, the known local issue. CI runs it.
- Not tested by hand in a running editor.

Pre-release: [0.1.5-test.11](https://github.com/lgiaccar/PlinyCode/releases/tag/release_0.1.5-test.11)

PlinyCode gains a standalone desktop preview for Windows and Ubuntu x64. Projects, saved chats, FreeAuto workers, per-task approvals, background commands and Git worktrees now run outside the editor. This PR includes the desktop implementation developed in this worktree and adds Linux support.

- Package bundled Electron/Bun and license notices in a per-user Windows installer, Ubuntu `.deb` and portable AppImage.
- Include browser companion integration, MCP stdio/HTTP/SSE settings, sub-agents, and GitHub/Azure DevOps PR controls.
- Share CLI credentials and redact configured secrets from persisted engine artifacts. Refuse insecure Linux keyring fallbacks and preserve the Chromium sandbox.
- Add Ubuntu 22.04/24.04 CI with isolated HOME/XDG, D-Bus, GNOME Keyring and Xvfb; test native credential sharing, process cleanup, worktrees, browser interaction, installed apps and package lifecycle.
- Fix test-order dependencies, architecture filename differences and stale-turn UI assertions found by the Linux matrix.

Validation at `781c29ea`: [desktop CI passed on Windows, Ubuntu 22.04 and Ubuntu 24.04](https://github.com/lgiaccar/PlinyCode/actions/runs/44917080777). Each platform passed 32 Bun tests, three Node browser protocol tests, Electron and browser acceptance. Both Linux formats ran the full packaged Electron suite; Debian install/reinstall/removal and Windows installer/uninstaller checks passed. All six workflows passed: desktop, CLI, engine, documentation, extension unit/integration/webview, and extension E2E (Ubuntu, Windows and macOS).

Local Windows: full Electron acceptance, all workspace types, desktop build, scoped formatting/lint and documentation checks passed; CLI tests passed with the optional Python test skipped because Python is unavailable locally.

Distribution is unsigned and no production updater is included. Ubuntu 24.04's namespace policy is adjusted only on disposable CI runners for unpacked/AppImage testing.

### Description

The `ext-vscode-test` workflow (type checks, lint, format, bun unit tests, vitest, VS Code integration tests on Ubuntu and Windows, and the testing-platform specs) only triggered on pull requests to `master`. PlinyCode PRs target `stage`, so none of those checks ran on them: #40, for example, ran only the e2e workflow, and #39 got engine tests only because it touched `sdk/**`.

This adds `stage` to the workflow's `pull_request` branches. The path filters are unchanged, so PRs that don't touch the extension or engine still skip the heavy jobs, and the `test` gate still passes for them.

This is step 1 of a series making the repo friendlier to AI coding agents: each later step (docs link checking, per-package `AGENTS.md` files) relies on CI actually running on `stage` PRs.

### Test Procedure

- The edited workflow parses (`Bun.YAML.parse`) with `pull_request.branches` = `["master", "stage"]`.
- The workflow file is in its own path filter, so this PR itself should run the full pipeline. A green run here also confirms `stage` is currently clean under these checks.

### Type of Change

-   [x] 🏃 Workflow Changes

### Additional Notes

CI-only change, so the extension version is not ticked: the shipped `.vsix` would be identical. Runtime cost: roughly 15-20 minutes of runner time per PR update that touches `apps/vscode/**` or `sdk/packages/**`.

## Why

Context management waves 2–5 (#125–#128) were stacked PRs. Each one merged into the previous wave's branch within seconds, before GitHub retargeted it to `stage`, so only wave 1 (#124) reached `stage`. #133 hit the same problem and was re-landed as #134.

- Testers had the waves in 0.2.2-test.3 to test.6, which were built from the wave branches.
- Every build from `stage` since test.7 silently dropped them.
- A 0.2.2 release from `stage` would have shipped without them. I found this while preparing that release.

The missing work was 105 files. For example: `nested-guides.ts`, `subagent-guidance.ts`, `autoCompactThreshold.ts`, `docs/rules.md` and `docs/context-compaction.md`.

## What

This PR merges `lgiaccar/context_management_4`, which holds all five waves (identical in content to `context_management_5`), into `stage`: 101 files, +3,304/−306.

- **Wave 2:** a session's mode, folder and side-question flag are its own.
- **Wave 3:** sub-agents get a real prompt, the host's tools, cost, approval and limits.
- **Wave 4:** compaction falls back to the basic summary, records the summarizer's cost, counts image tokens properly, and shows a threshold marker on the context bar.
- **Wave 5:**
  - nested `AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md` guides reach the model
  - conversation search is per workspace
  - the memory budget counts everything
  - distillation state is persisted
  - memory writes across windows are ordered by a lock

## Conflict resolutions

- **Prompt cache.** I kept #132's breakpoint placement and dropped wave 4's `PLINYCODE_CACHE_MARK_TOOL_CALLS` experiment, which #132 supersedes. The experiment put its `"."` text only on the message being marked, so the next request's prefix no longer matched the cache. The docs now point to `docs/prompt-cache.md`, and audit finding #19 is marked fixed by #132.
- **CI Board runs.** A run's session is now built in the action's own mode: Agent, or Ask for Investigate, as #131 introduced. Following wave 2, the global mode switch is no longer flipped; a notice explains when the two differ. The run's model and title from #131 are kept.
- **Session mode.** Every session keeps the mode it was built with (wave 2), which also covers background starts from #130. Kept from `stage`:
  - the `newConversation` guard
  - the background coordinator
  - the pinned model on resume (which now uses the switch's mode)
- **Docs.** For the audit and `memory.md` I took the waves' text. `AGENTS.md` now lists `docs/rules.md` and `docs/context-compaction.md`.

## Fixed along the way

The waves' PRs never ran the extension CI, because it only runs on PRs to `stage`/`master`. One test was therefore stale:

- The legacy YOLO / auto-approve-all migration enabled every approval except wave 3's new `useSubagents`. It now enables that too, and the test expects it.

## Testing (local)

- `bun run build:sdk`, `bun run types`, lint, format, `check:docs` and `analyze:unused:prod` pass.
- **Engine:** llms 738, shared 376 and core 1,676 passed. The 5 core hook-file/MCP failures are this machine's Node 26 issue (temp `.js` fixtures use `require`) and are unrelated.
- **Extension vitest:** 1,762 passed. **Webview:** 587 passed.
- **Extension bun unit suite:** passes except the `src/core/hooks/__tests__` files, which hit the same Node 26 environment issue.
- Not yet checked in the dev host. A tester check with 0.2.2-test.12 is suggested before the 0.2.2 release.

## Summary

This PR adds **BalanceAuto** (`pliny/balance-auto`), a fourth router profile beside the three FreeAuto profiles (`pliny/free-auto`, `-fast`, `-smart`). It runs on the same router code, with one difference: its rules may route to **paid hosted Pliny models**. Difficult work goes to high-end paid models; simple requests and every sub-agent call go to free or cheap models. It is only visible in the picker while paid models are unlocked.

Every call is billed at the concrete model it lands on. The virtual id carries no price, and the cost shown per call comes from the delegate model's pricing, so a BalanceAuto turn reports real spend.

## Why

FreeAuto proved the router: per-call model choice, failover, health benching, a classifier and a rules file. The missing piece for people who *have* paid access is a way to spend it only where it pays off. Sub-agents are the clearest case: they do bounded explore-and-report work, run many calls per turn, and a free model handles them well. A single strong model for the main agent's hard steps plus free models for the rest is the balance this profile encodes.

## Default routing

The classifier is on for this profile, so once per turn a small free model reads the request and returns a tier. The tier picks the route; the keyword heuristics decide only when the classifier gives no verdict.

| Route | When | Models, best first |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `huge-context` | request ≥ 180k tokens | free GLM-5.2 (512k), vmodels replica first |
| `subagent` | any sub-agent call | free kimi-k2.6, free qwen3-coder, then Haiku 4.5 |
| `plan-and-reasoning` | tier `reason`, or plan mode with a design/review prompt | Sonnet 4.6 high-thinking preset, Sonnet 5, GPT-5.2 |
| `coding` | tier `code`, or act mode with a coding prompt | Sonnet 5, Sonnet 4.6, free qwen3-coder |
| `quick` | tier `quick`, or a short question | free kimi-k2.6, free nemotron super, then Haiku 4.5 |
| `default` | anything else | Sonnet 5, Sonnet 4.6, free kimi-k2.6 |

The pool leads with the paid models, so a turn whose free candidates all fail still lands on a strong one. Utility jobs (classifier, compaction summaries, commit messages) stay on free models by default; the rules file may point any of them at a paid model.

## What changed

**Model catalog (`@plinycode/llms`)**
- Profiles move to `PLINY_ROUTER_PROFILES`, each with `id`, `family` (`free` | `balance`) and a chat `label`. `PLINY_FREE_AUTO_PROFILES` is now the free subset, so existing callers keep working.
- New helpers: `isPlinyBalanceAutoModelId`, `isPlinyRouterModelId`, `plinyRouterProfile`, `plinyRouterModelId`, `plinyRouterProfileAllowsPaid`, `plinyHostedPoolIds`. `isPlinyFreeModelId` keeps its meaning: BalanceAuto is a router but **not** a free model.
- BalanceAuto's `ModelInfo` declares `images` (the hosted Claude models accept them), the 200k hosted context, no pricing, and `metadata.paid: true`.
- `resolvePlinyConcreteModelId` maps BalanceAuto to the same free fallback as FreeAuto, since its callers are utility jobs.

**Router (`apps/vscode/src/sdk/router`)**
- Rules sanitisation is per profile. Only the balance family may list paid ids in `pool`, `use` and `utility`; the FreeAuto files keep rejecting them, and a virtual router id is never a candidate.
- BalanceAuto has its own global rules file (`pliny-balance-auto.md`) and workspace file (`.cline/pliny-balance-auto.md`). The FreeAuto profiles still share `.cline/pliny-free-auto.md`, so a project's free-only overrides can never displace BalanceAuto's paid routes.
- The starter rules file explains the paid routing instead of the free-only guard, and its classifier guidance says which tiers are free and which are paid.
- Chat rows, the turn summary, the failover notice and error messages name the profile (`BalanceAuto → **global.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5** (call 1 · route: coding · classifier: code …)`). The call log records `profile: "balance"`, so the existing summarizer script compares it against the free profiles.
- The unfinished-turn nudge fires on a BalanceAuto turn only when the last call ran on a free model. Paid models do not stop early, and a nudge would cost a call.

**Picker and settings (webview)**
- BalanceAuto is neither free-auto nor self-hosted, so the existing paid branch of `filterPlinyModels` hides it until "Unlock Pliny paid models" is on. The toggle's description and the routing-rules paragraph mention it.

**Extension**
- The rules quick pick lists all four profiles. Command titles become "Open Routing Rules (FreeAuto / BalanceAuto)" and "Open Router Call Log (FreeAuto / BalanceAuto)".

**Docs**: `docs/pliny-balance-auto.md`.

## Known limits

- **Thinking on hosted models.** Only self-hosted models have a measured reasoning switch, so per-route `effort` leaves hosted models at their default. The reasoning route uses the `aws-bedrock-vmodels/claude-4-6-sonnet-high-thinking` preset instead.
- **Context beyond 200k.** Hosted entries have no measured window, so they are budgeted at the 200k default. A request above roughly 118k estimated tokens (window minus the output reserve) skips them for a free large-context model.
- Hosted model prices in the catalog are public-list stand-ins, as before.

## Testing

- `bun run build:sdk`; extension and webview typecheck clean; Biome check per package.
- Extension vitest (router + shared Pliny): 188 passed. Llms catalog tests: 29 passed. Webview filter tests: 18 passed.
- New tests cover: the paid gate in the picker, per-profile sanitisation (free profiles drop paid ids, balance keeps them, virtual ids always dropped), balance route shape (paid leads hard routes, free leads quick and sub-agent routes, every routed id is in the pool), the starter file round-trip, the BalanceAuto chat rows and log records for main and sub-agent calls, and the guard firing only after a free-model call.
- Not yet exercised against the live gateway. Suggested manual check: unlock paid models, pick BalanceAuto, send a coding prompt and a short question, and confirm the rows show Sonnet for the first and a free model for the second; spawn a sub-agent and confirm it runs on kimi.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

## Changes

Adds **Pipelines → Agents** so PlinyCode can monitor an Azure DevOps agent pool without leaving the editor. New workspaces reuse the locally saved pool URL; existing workspace URLs remain unchanged. Internal endpoints are never embedded in the published source or VSIX. Windows hosts can use integrated sign-in, with existing DevOps authentication available as an alternative.

The view filters capability names (including `FFI_BUILD_*`), shows online/offline, enabled/disabled and assigned-job state, and refreshes in the background. Optional notifications report online/offline and enabled/disabled transitions, showing both changes together when they occur in one poll. Initial observations and unchanged polls stay quiet; connection failures preserve and label the last known snapshot. Capability values are discarded.

Includes explicit first-time setup guidance and bumps the extension and Bun lockfile to **0.2.7-test.4**.

Published prerelease: https://github.com/lgiaccar/PlinyCode/releases/tag/release_0.2.7-test.4

## Validation

- Monitor backend: 11 tests passed, including local default migration, simultaneous transitions, disabled-agent connection changes, unknown statuses, stopped/in-flight requests and failure recovery.
- Monitor and pipeline-launch UI: 10 tests passed, including entering a URL before starting and preserving unsaved edits during refresh.
- Live Windows-authenticated query verified against the configured pool (408 agents).
- Production unused-code check, documentation links and focused formatting passed.
- Full extension unit suite: 1,054 tests passed across 88 files before the local-default adjustment; focused backend/UI tests and the production build passed after it.

hits.body:
## Why

The models behind PlinyCode, the free ones especially, lose most of their time to the harness, not to reasoning: an edit that misses by one indent fails with "text not found", a search hides most matches, nothing tells the model that its edit broke the build, a long run forgets its remaining steps, and the model knows neither the repo state nor what the user is looking at. This PR closes those gaps and adds a second model where that helps.

Every new behaviour has a `plinycode.*` setting to turn it off. Each feature has a design note in `docs/` (linked from AGENTS.md).

## What changes

### Feedback loop

- **New errors after every edit** (`docs/edit-problems.md`). After `editor` / `apply_patch` writes, the tool result lists the errors VS Code reports for the edited files that were not there before. The wait is event-driven, at most 3 s, and skips file types that never produce diagnostics. Headless edits open the file in a background tab while it is checked.
  - VS Code re-publishes a file's *old* diagnostics a few ms after a disk write. Events count only once the document version has moved past the pre-write version.
  - Setting: `plinycode.edits.reportNewProblems`.
- **Edit recovery** (`docs/agent-tools.md`).
  - An `old_text` that differs only in indentation depth or trailing whitespace, and fits one place, is applied, with `new_text` re-indented.
  - A miss quotes the closest lines and the first line that differs.
  - Several matches list their lines, and `replace_all` replaces them all.
  - The diff preview uses the same matcher.
- **Search.** `search_codebase` takes `path` (directory or single file) and `glob`.
- **`find_files`.** New tool that finds files by glob or by part of the path, so the model does not shell out to `find` / `dir`.
- **Parallel read-only tools.** `read_files`, `search_codebase`, `find_files` and `fetch_web_content` run concurrently when called together.
  - The chat translator held a single "current tool"; it now keeps open tools by call id, so concurrent tools finish into their own rows.
- **Task list.** New `update_todo_list` tool. The model keeps a list and the chat shows it after each update (`TodoListRow`, reusing the dormant `task_progress` message).
- **Environment context** (`docs/environment-context.md`).
  - **Git snapshot.** Branch, default branch, short status and last 5 commits go into the system prompt's `<env>`. The snapshot is taken once per conversation and stored in the session record, so the cached prompt prefix stays stable across rebuilds and restarts.
  - **Editor state.** The active file, cursor or selection, and open tabs are attached to each user message, only when they changed. They stay out of the chat, titles and history.
  - Settings: `plinycode.context.gitSnapshot`, `plinycode.context.editorState`.

### More than one model

- **Reviewer pass** (`docs/review-pass.md`). Before a FreeAuto / BalanceAuto act-mode run that changed files ends, a different free model reads the diff and returns JSON issues; likely defects go back to the working model once.
  - The diff comes from the run's checkpoint, or from the edit calls when there is no checkpoint.
  - The reviewer is picked from the profile's reasoning route, never the author, with reasoning off.
  - The reviewer is always free. On BalanceAuto, turns a paid model answered are reviewed too, and the fix round is billed like any call there; on the FreeAuto profiles nothing is billed (a paid model answering there, only possible through a rules file, skips the review).
  - Engine change: the completion guard now receives the run's abort signal, so cancelling stops a review at once.
  - Setting: `plinycode.review.beforeFinish`.
- **`ask_advisor`** (`docs/advisor-tool.md`). A free or cheaper model can ask Sonnet 5 for advice at a hard step.
  - Offered on BalanceAuto by default (`plinycode.advisor.use`), with at most 5 calls per conversation.
  - Each call is budget-checked like a paid call. Its cost is recorded as a `subagent_usage` row, so the task header, history and later budget checks include it.
- **Execute plan with another model** (`docs/plan-mode.md`). Execute plan is now a split button naming the model it will run on: act-mode model, FreeAuto, BalanceAuto, or the planner.
  - The choice is remembered in `plinycode.plan.executeWith`.
  - Plan-mode instructions now ask for plans an executor that never saw the conversation can follow.

### CI

- **`watch_ci`** (`docs/devops-mcp.md`). Offered where the DevOps tools are. The extension polls GitHub Actions / Azure Pipelines through the existing provider code, without using the model, and posts the result into the conversation when CI finishes: failed jobs, steps and log excerpts.
  - Delivery: it starts a turn when idle, queues when mid-turn, and shows a notification with Open when the conversation is not loaded.
  - At most 5 automatic wake-ups without a user message.
  - Log text is neutralised so it cannot trigger `@` mentions or tags.
  - Setting: `plinycode.ci.watch`.

## Things to decide or know

- **Execute plan changes a setting and the act-mode model.** Choosing an executor different from the planner turns on "Use different models for Plan and Act modes". Model selection is global, so the act-mode model changes for every conversation.
- **Protobuf changes, all additive optional fields:**
  - `proto/host/window.proto`: selection lines and `is_file` on `GetActiveEditorResponse`.
  - `proto/cline/state.proto`: `execute_plan_with` on `TogglePlanActModeRequest`.
- **No new state keys.** All new settings are VS Code settings.
- **knip.** Following the existing pattern, `knip.json` lists the new `src/sdk/context/*` and `router-review*` files whose test-only exports the Vitest plugin hides from the strict test entries.
- **Smaller package.** `.vscodeignore` now excludes `dist-standalone/` (the build of the removed standalone host, ~1,000 files and ~100 MB uncompressed, which 0.1.8 shipped), `dist/release/`, `AGENTS.md` and `skills-lock.json`. The `.vsix` goes from 32 MB / 1,069 files to 6.4 MB / 38 files; nothing in the bundle referenced the removed files.

## Test procedure

On the merged branch (Windows):

- `bun run build:sdk`, `bun run types`, `bun run lint`, `bun run format`, `bun run check:docs`: pass.
- `bun -F plinycode-dev analyze:unused:prod` (knip): pass.
- Engine: `@plinycode/shared` 372 passed. Core `src/extensions/tools`, `src/runtime`, `src/services`: 1137 passed.
- Extension `test:vitest`: 1623 passed. `test:webview`: 522 passed. DevOps MCP bun tests: 86 passed.
- Extension `test:unit`: 933 passed, 44 failed. All failures are in the six `src/core/hooks/__tests__` suites, which fail locally because a `package.json` in Temp makes Node load the test hook scripts as ESM; they fail the same way on `stage`.
- In a real VS Code host:
  - The diagnostics source passes mocha integration tests against VS Code 1.139.1's JSON server and a probe against TypeScript.
  - The new Playwright e2e test for the split Execute plan button passes against the mock gateway.
- Live, read-only:
  - The reviewer prompt was probed with about 30 calls to free models on a diff with two planted defects; with reasoning off the default reviewer found both in 3 of 4 runs and was clean on the clean diff.
  - The CI watcher was run against this repo's real runs, including PR #111, a moved branch head and a failing commit.
- **Not verified:**
  - End to end in a dev host: the chat rows (todo, advisor, review, CI), editor-state hiding on reopen, and CI delivery through the UI.
  - The advisor request against live Sonnet 5.
  - Azure DevOps CI watching against a real server.

Pre-release: `0.1.9-test.2`, https://github.com/lgiaccar/PlinyCode/releases/tag/release_0.1.9-test.2 (`0.1.9-test.1` had everything except the last two changes above).

## Type of Change

-   [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
-   [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

- **Live usage counter** in the task header: running time, tokens and cost together (`⏱ 3m 12s · 45.5k tok · $0.0123`). The time ticks every second while the agent runs; tokens and cost update after each request. The tooltip has the start time and a token breakdown. The `$` part only appears when the provider reports cost, as before. The counter is one component (`TaskUsageCounter`), so a time/token/$ limit can be added there later.

First of five waves from the context-management audit (`docs/context-management-audit.md`, new, linked from `AGENTS.md`): sub-agents, task isolation, context compression, memory and knowledge, 25 ranked findings with the wave that fixes each. This wave ships the audit and the fixes that are a few lines each.

## Changes

- **Routed sessions respect auto-condense off.** `installRouter` set `compaction.enabled ?? true`, so FreeAuto and BalanceAuto compacted even when the user had turned auto-condense off. It now only attaches the free summarizer and leaves the setting to the session factory.
- **The prompt date is pinned per conversation.** `{{CURRENT_DATE}}` was filled from the clock on every rebuild, which changed the system prompt's cached prefix on the first rebuild of each day. `ConversationPromptDates` fixes it when the conversation starts and stores it in session metadata (`promptDate`) next to the git snapshot; `buildClineSystemPrompt` takes `currentDate`.
- **New memories are no longer the first thing cut.** `save_memory` appended normal notes at the end of `## Notes` while the budget keeps the top of the file, so a fresh note in a file over the budget was dropped while the tool said later conversations would see it. Notes now go in newest first, and the tool result says when the saved entry falls outside the budget.
- **Search snippet ellipsis** was the mojibake literal `â€¦` in the FTS query.
- **Slash-command bodies are capped** at 24k characters (`MAX_COMMAND_INSTRUCTION_CHARS`, `capInstructionText`) with a note naming the file, in core's runtime commands so both expansion paths get it.
- **Transcript writes** (`<id>.messages.json`, rewritten after every model call) are compact JSON through a temp file and rename, one write in flight per session with the newest contents winning.

## Verification

- `bun run check`, `bun run check:docs`: pass.
- Core unit suite: 1659 pass; 5 failures are environmental (hook tests need `bash`, MCP tests break on a stray `package.json` in `%TEMP%` forcing ESM), unchanged by this PR.
- Shared tests, extension vitest (1723 pass): pass. Extension bun suite: only the hook-script tests fail, same cause.
- New tests: `conversation-prompt-date.test.ts`, `session-manifest-store.test.ts`, plus cases in `cline.test.ts`, `rules.test.ts`, `runtime-commands.test.ts`, `memory-file.test.ts`, `memory-store.test.ts`, `sdk-session-config-builder.test.ts`.

## Follow-up waves

2 per-session isolation (mode, workspace root, side-question flag) → 3 sub-agents (tools, cost, approvals, limits, prompt) → 4 compaction robustness and context UI → 5 memory, search, knowledge.

Release **0.1.4**: bumps `plinycode-dev` from `0.1.3-test.8` to `0.1.4`. Includes everything on `stage` up to #41 (prompt caching).

This is the first official GitHub release, so `/releases/latest` will serve it to the auto-updater. Only `0.1.3-test.*` pre-releases have been published so far. Tag `release_0.1.4` is pushed and points at this branch's head (`60f9b85`).

**Also fixes an update-settings regression from #41.** When #41 merged, it reverted part of #40 in `apps/vscode/package.json`: it brought back the dead `plinycode.updates.folder` setting (nothing reads it since the OneDrive source was removed) and descriptions that still mention the PlinyCodeRelease folder. This PR restores #40's settings.

- `PlinyCode-0.1.4.vsix` sha256: `ddfd915c707393693715f967d71e3fbb1864b00b5e717095f82ee2718e7672a6`
- Checks: `bun run build:sdk`, `bun run types`, `bun -F plinycode-dev test:unit`, `apps/vscode` `check-types` and `bun -F @plinycode/llms test` all pass.

### Before publishing
- [ ] Smoke test the `.vsix` in VS Code and in Cursor: install from VSIX, reload, send one message (including one on a Claude model, to see cache hits)
- [ ] `bun run release:publish -- --dry-run`, then `bun run release:publish` (from `apps/vscode`)
- [ ] Run **PlinyCode: Check for Updates** on a machine with a `0.1.3-test.*` build

The release notes below become the GitHub release description.

---


Internal Synopsys release of the PlinyCode VS Code / Cursor extension.

**Package:** `PlinyCode-0.1.4.vsix`  
**Install:** this is the first release that updates itself. If you run 0.1.2 or earlier, install it by hand once:
download the `.vsix` from this release, then Extensions -> ... -> **Install from VSIX...** and reload the window.
From now on, new releases install automatically: click **Reload Now** when asked.

**Gateway:** `https://snps-inference.internal.synopsys.com` (Synopsys network only)

---

### Highlights in 0.1.4 (since 0.1.2)

### PlinyCode now updates itself

- About 30 seconds after startup, and every 6 hours after that, PlinyCode checks GitHub Releases. When a newer
  version exists it downloads it, verifies its checksum, installs it and offers **Reload Now** and
  **Release Notes**.
- **PlinyCode: Check for Updates** in the Command Palette, or the **Check for Updates** button in
  **Settings -> About**, checks right away and always tells you the result: an update, "up to date", or why
  GitHub couldn't be reached.
- Developers and testers can tick **Install pre-releases** in **Settings -> About** to also get `-test.N` builds.
  Turning it off never downgrades you.
- `plinycode.updates.enabled` turns automatic updates off.
- If the old PlinyCode 0.1.0 (`claude-dev`) is still installed next to this one, it's removed automatically on
  startup. Reload when asked.

### BalanceAuto: paid models for the hard work, free models for the rest

- New router model **`pliny/auto-paid-balanced`**. Reasoning and coding turns go to Claude Sonnet, while short
  questions and sub-agent calls go to free models (with Haiku as fallback). Very large requests go to the free
  512k-context model.
- It appears in the model picker only when **Unlock Pliny paid models** is on in **Settings -> API
  configuration**. Every call is billed at the model it actually runs on.

### Prompt caching for Claude models on Pliny

- Claude calls through Pliny were never cached before, so every turn paid full price for the whole conversation.
  Now the system prompt and the conversation up to your latest message are cached, and later turns read them
  from the cache. Long tasks on Claude cost noticeably less.
- Cache writes are now counted, so the cost PlinyCode shows matches what the gateway reports.

### Router models renamed

- The free routers are now `pliny/auto-free`, `pliny/auto-free-fast` and `pliny/auto-free-smart`, and
  BalanceAuto is `pliny/auto-paid-balanced`.
- The old ids (`pliny/free-auto...`, `pliny/balance-auto`) still work, and a saved selection switches to the new
  name automatically. Your routing rules files keep their names.

### Free models finish the job more often

- Free models used to stop before the task was done. They would announce a step without taking it, promise to
  "check back later", ask permission for something you already asked for, or end on a plan. PlinyCode now spots
  these endings and tells the model to continue. If a model stalls twice, the turn moves to a stronger model.
- When no rule fires, a quick check asks a small model whether the request was actually carried out.
- New **wait** tool: the agent can wait for a long build or test run (up to 10 minutes at a time) and then read
  the output, instead of ending its turn.
- Better handling of models that think inside their answer (Kimi K2.6, Qwen3 35B, Nemotron 3 Ultra). Qwen3 Coder
  now leads the default free route, with Kimi as fallback.

Fifth and last wave of the context-management audit (`docs/context-management-audit.md`), stacked on #127; retarget to `stage` once that merges. Memory, past-conversation search and project knowledge. New doc: `docs/rules.md`, linked from `AGENTS.md`.

## Changes

- **Per-directory agent guides reach the model.** Only the root `AGENTS.md` was read, so this repository's own `apps/vscode/AGENTS.md` and `sdk/AGENTS.md` never did. `discoverNestedGuideFiles` finds `AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md` below the root (depth 3, dependency/build/hidden folders skipped, at most 30, shallowest first). They are listed by path, never inlined: a nested guide is scoped to its folder (`apps/vscode/**`) unless it sets a scope; a root `CLAUDE.md` is listed "read when AGENTS.md does not answer something".
- **The workspace `AGENTS.md` is inlined first.** Rules were sorted by name, so `a-style.md` could push `AGENTS.md` out of the 40k budget.
- **Search filters by workspace in the index.** The engine stores and queries normalized roots (slashes, case on Windows), so other workspaces no longer crowd this one out of the candidate list; the extension passes the folder through. `<editor_state>`/`<mode_notice>` blocks are left out of the index and of `read_conversation` (index version 4).
- **Memory budget accounting.** The instruction block, the topic list (now capped at 12 per memory with a count of the rest) and the "N more entries" note come out of `plinycode.memory.maxTokens`; the context row uses the same three characters per token.
- **Distillation remembers.** Progress and dismissed/unchecked memories are stored in `memory/distill/<conversation>.json`, so a reload neither re-reads the whole conversation nor proposes a turned-down memory again. Proposals are compared as whole entries (`memoryEntryKeys`) rather than substrings.
- **Cross-window memory writes** hold `<file>.lock` (exclusive create, stale after 10 s, best-effort after 2 s), so two windows saving at once no longer lose an entry.
- **`/remember` while memory is off** expands into a note telling the model memory is off, instead of instructions to call a tool the session lacks.

## Verification

- `bun run check`, `bun run check:docs`, knip: pass.
- Core: 1675 pass; the same 5 environment-only failures as before. Extension vitest: 1746 pass.
- New tests: `nested-guides.test.ts` (discovery, scope, prompt rendering and order), core search (normalized roots, editor state), `memory-section.test.ts` budget, coordinator persistence across a reload, whole-entry dedupe, two-store concurrent saves and stale lock, `/remember` while off, search adapter passes the folder and strips editor state.

Four fixes to plan mode, reloaded conversations and Run in worktree.

## Plans are kept outside the workspace

Plan mode wrote its plans to `plans/<slug>/PLAN.md` in the workspace, where they could be committed or deleted by accident. They now go to PlinyCode's data folder, one folder per workspace:

```
~/.cline/data/plans/<workspace name>-<8 hex of the path's SHA-256>/<slug>/PLAN.md
```

- `resolvePlansDataDir()` (`@plinycode/shared/storage`, `CLINE_PLANS_DATA_DIR` overrides it) and `workspacePlanFolder()` (`apps/vscode/src/core/workspace/plan-folder.ts`) work out the folder.
- `buildClineSystemPrompt` takes a new `planDirectory` option. With it, the plan-mode instructions name absolute paths under that folder, with forward slashes. Without it (the CLI), they keep `plans/<slug>/`. The extension always passes it.
- The plan row's link shows `<slug>/PLAN.md` and has the full path in its title.
- New command **PlinyCode: Open Plan…** lists the workspace's plans, newest first, and can reveal the folder.
- The edit and read approvals don't depend on the path, so nothing else changes. Plans that earlier versions wrote to the workspace stay where they are.

## Switching to Agent mode no longer runs the plan

After a plan, flipping the mode switch to Agent sent "Continue with the approved plan now." by itself (along with any draft in the prompt box). That approved the plan without the user asking. Now only the **Execute plan** button runs the plan (`togglePlanActModeProto` passes `executePlan` when the request has `executePlanWith`). A plain switch only rebuilds the session, and the draft stays in the box. The plan-mode prompt also tells the model that the switch alone is not approval.

## Reloaded conversations keep their prompt rows

A prompt sent while a command ran in the background is saved in the same message as that command's `<hook_context>` block. On replay, the whole message counted as hook context. The prompt lost its highlighted row, and the turn before it lost its completion styling. Restart-from-here also skipped the message, because `isSyntheticSdkUserMessage` treated it as runtime-only. History replay and that check now strip the hook blocks and treat what is left as the prompt. I checked this against 150 local sessions: every typed prompt now replays as a prompt row. The only ones still hidden are `[TASK RESUMPTION]` prompts, which are meant to be hidden.

## Run in worktree branches are named after the user

Branches are now `<OS user>/<slug>-<4 hex>` (e.g. `lgiaccar/fix-login-3f2a`), not `plinycode/…`. A name prefix can't tell them apart from the user's own branches, so each one gets `branch.<name>.plinycodetask = true` in git config, and the daily cleanup checks for that. `plinycode/*` branches are still recognised.

## Tests

- New unit tests: the replay of a prompt sharing a message with hook context, `isSyntheticSdkUserMessage`, the mode coordinator (a switch without Execute plan sends nothing), the proto handler flag, `planDirectory` in the prompt, `workspacePlanFolder`/`listSavedPlans`, `planFileLabel`, `taskBranchPrefix`, and the branch marker in the worktree and cleanup tests (an unmarked `<user>/…` branch next to them is left alone).
- e2e `plan-execute.test.ts`: the plan lands in the data folder and not in the workspace. A new case checks that switching to Agent mode doesn't run the plan, and that asking for it does.
- Run locally: `bun run types`, the extension's `check-types`, lint, format, knip, `check:docs`, the extension unit suite (87 files) and its vitest suite, the webview tests and the shared engine tests all pass. Core's unit suite has 5 failures, in `hook-file-hooks` and the MCP stdio client tests. Those files aren't touched here, and they fail locally under this Node version.

Docs: `docs/plan-mode.md` (plan folder, Open Plan…, switching to Agent mode), `docs/task-worktrees.md` (branch names, the marker), `AGENTS.md`.

Roadmap A10 (docs/roadmap.md). Pliny models had no way to search the web. The engine's `web_search` is a provider-native model tool that the Pliny gateway never offers, so the Settings → Features → Web Search switch did nothing for them. The extension now runs the search itself.

- **`web_search({ query, site?, count? })`** returns a numbered list of `Title — host`, URL and a snippet of at most 200 characters, then tells the model to read pages with `fetch_web_content` before relying on them. Parallel with the other read tools, retried once, 30 s timeout. Added only when the provider has no native web search, so Anthropic-direct configs keep theirs. Sub-agents get it too.
- **Backends** (`plinycode.webSearch.provider`): DuckDuckGo HTML (default, no key, scraped; ads skipped, bot-check pages reported as such), SearXNG (recommended for teams, `plinycode.webSearch.endpoint`), Brave Search API, Google Programmable Search (`plinycode.webSearch.googleCx`). All go through the extension's proxy/CA-aware fetch with a 15 s timeout; an HTTP error reports the status and a short body.
- **API key**: "PlinyCode: Set Web Search API Key" stores it per provider in SecretStorage (the OS keychain), never in settings; it applies to running conversations.
- **Settings toggle**: Settings → Features → Web Search now controls `plinycode.webSearch.enabled`, and the engine's native web_search flag follows it (synced at activation, on setting change and on toggle).
- **Chat row**: the web search row shows the query and expands to the results.
- **Docs**: "Web search (`web_search`)" in `docs/agent-tools.md`: backends, settings, key command, proxy, and a privacy note (queries leave the network for the chosen provider).

Tests: vitest suites for the backends (recorded DuckDuckGo HTML and SearXNG/Brave/Google JSON fixtures, error paths, timeouts, cancel) and the tool (formatting, caps, empty results, gating). check-types, lint, format, test:vitest, test:webview, test:discovery, knip, check:docs pass. A live DuckDuckGo query from this machine returned 5 relevant results (outside the extension's fetch).

Dev-host check pending: a real search through the extension's fetch and the corporate proxy (and no bot check from the corporate egress), the row, toggle ↔ setting sync, the key command with Brave or Google.

## What changes

**New**
- **Per-conversation spending limit.** New `plinycode.spending.conversationLimit` setting (default $5; 0 turns it off), also editable in Settings → General. Before each model call, if the conversation has spent the limit, the run stops and a message says what was spent and how to continue. Sending a message allows another round of the same amount. It works like the mistake limit: no blocking prompt while the agent loop is live.
- **Pliny budget display.** A new `getPlinyBudget` RPC reads `/api/svc/v1/llm-gateway/budgets/my-usage` with the same key and host as chat requests. The binding budget (the period with the least money left) shows under the home screen header and in the task header's expanded details. It turns red at 90% used or when the gateway reports the budget as blocked. It only shows while Pliny is the active provider, and refetches at most once a minute.
- **Conversation title in the task header.** The title is centered, with the workspace name (`parent/folder`) under it in smaller text, whether the header is collapsed or expanded.

**Fixes**
- **History cost differed from the conversation's cost.** Several writers raced on the history record: rename, favorite and active-time writes put back stale totals, and per-event deltas collided with the engine's own end-of-turn total. The history record now stores the same totals the task header computes (`getConversationApiMetrics`), and only usage writes can change them.
- **Claude on Bedrock rejected tool-call ids** (`tool_use.id: String should match pattern '^[a-zA-Z0-9-]+$'`). Mixed routing leaves ids such as `call_…`, `functions.x:0` or `tool_<nanoid>` in history. The OpenAI-compatible request body now rewrites every `tool_calls[].id` and `tool_call_id` to a deterministic, valid id, so each call and its result still match. Stored history keeps the original ids.
- **File paths in answers didn't open.** Absolute paths in plain text (e.g. `d:\…\report.md`, `/home/me/x.py`) and backslash or absolute paths in backticks now become "open in editor" links. Absolute paths open even with no workspace folder.
- **Scheduled prompts use a 24-hour clock.** The picker is a date field plus 00–23 hour and minute selects, defaulting to the next 5-minute mark at least 5 minutes out. The scheduled list shows 24-hour times.

## Tests
- New: `tool-call-ids.test.ts`, an `openai-compatible` wire test, `plinyBudget.test.ts`, `spending-limit.test.ts`, `scheduleTime.test.ts` and `filePathDetection.test.ts`. The history and event-coordinator tests are extended for the usage totals.
- Locally, these all pass: `bun run types`, lint, format, the full llms suite (787) and the extension `src/sdk` vitest suites (1410+).
- These fail locally on unchanged code too, so they are environmental:
  - React component tests in the webview (Bun 1.4.2 here vs the pinned 1.3.x)

- Records the known local failure: two `core` hub tests fail with `HubLockHeldError` while a PlinyCode editor is running on the same machine.

**Wrong commands fixed**
- `bun run types` typechecks the **engine packages only**. None of the extension workspaces has a `typecheck` script, so the extension needs `cd apps/vscode && bun run check-types`. The root `AGENTS.md` said otherwise, and so did `sdk/AGENTS.md`: I introduced that error in #44, and this PR corrects it.
- `bun run test` also runs the extension's VS Code integration tests, so it needs a display. That's now stated.
- `sdk/AGENTS.md` no longer recommends `bun run check`, which fails (see Additional Notes).

**`REPOMAP.md`** had drifted. It listed a root `.cline/` folder that doesn't exist, called `src/core` "Agent Engine" and `src/core/task` "Agent loop" (the loop runs in `@plinycode/core`, behind `src/sdk/SdkController.ts`), put `StateManager` in the wrong directory, and left out `devops-mcp/`. Those rows are fixed. Its build-commands and gotchas sections repeated the `AGENTS.md` files, repeated the `types` error and cited snapshot tests that no longer exist. They're replaced by a pointer to the `AGENTS.md` files and a corrected key-files table, so the file is now purely a directory map.

**Flaky Windows engine test fixed** (the first CI run of this PR failed on it)

The Windows `engine-test` job failed in `bash.test.ts` > "tracks the detached command across host restarts until it exits": a detached command's log directory still existed when `expect.poll`'s 1s default ran out. A re-run passed, but the flake points at a real gap:

- Detached command logs are deleted by a one-shot timer (`scheduleDetachedLogCleanup` in `sdk/packages/core/src/extensions/tools/executors/bash.ts`), and its `rm` error is swallowed. On Windows, a scanner or indexer briefly holding a file open makes a recursive `rm` fail with `EBUSY`. Nothing retried, so the directory stayed until the next host startup. Both cleanup `rm` calls now pass Node's `maxRetries: 5, retryDelay: 100`. Node retries only the transient `EBUSY`/`EPERM`/`ENOTEMPTY`/`EMFILE`/`ENFILE` codes.
- The five tests that wait for a log directory to disappear now poll for up to 5s. That covers the retention timer plus up to 1.5s of retries on a busy runner.

Version ticked to `0.1.5-test.1`, since this changes shipped code.

- **Flake fix:** on this Windows machine, a second process held a file open inside a log directory. The old `rm` call failed with `EBUSY` and left the directory behind. The same call with the new options succeeded once the lock was released. The test itself didn't fail locally, in 15 isolated runs or 24 runs under load, so the longer poll covers the CI-load case. `bash.test.ts` passes (42 passed, 6 platform-skipped), and the core typecheck and `bun run lint` pass.

Adding `typecheck` and `build` scripts to the extension would fix them and let `bun run types` cover the extension. That changes package scripts and CI behaviour, so it should be a separate PR.

Cleanup plan items 31 (engine telemetry plumbing) and 36 (merge `@plinycode/agents` into core).

The extension already stopped handing ClineCore a telemetry service, so every capture call in the engine was a no-op. This PR removes that plumbing, then folds the agent loop package into core, its only consumer.

## Removed

**Item 31, core** (`Engine: remove telemetry from core`)
- `TelemetryService`, `ITelemetryAdapter`, `TelemetryLoggerSink`, the scoped telemetry wrappers, `core-events`, `session-telemetry`, `workspace-telemetry`, the `session.started` emitter and the account telemetry identity helpers, with their tests.
- The `telemetry` option on `ClineCoreOptions`, `CoreSessionConfig` and every internal option that only carried it: the runtime host, bootstrap, runtime builder, session runtime, tool definitions, auth (Cline, Codex, OCA), checkpoint hooks, session versioning, the plugin loader and `FeatureFlagsService`.
- The sandboxed plugin telemetry bridge and `ctx.telemetry` for plugins.
- The `telemetryOptOut` global setting and `isTelemetryOptedOutGlobally` / `setTelemetryOptOutGlobally`.
- State that only fed events: the `task.completed` observers (`submitAndExitObserved`, `taskCompletedEmitted`), sub-agent start timestamps, `run_commands` timeout reporting, the mistake-tracker telemetry hook, and the timing and VCS fields on the workspace metadata builder.
- `resolveCoreDeviceId`, which only `TelemetryService` used.

**Item 31, shared/llms/agents** (`Engine: remove telemetry from shared, llms and agents`)
- shared: `ITelemetryService`, the telemetry value and metadata types, `captureSdkError`, `normalizeSdkError`, the task lifecycle and reasoning-token capture helpers, the `sdk.error` rate limiter, the OTLP relay markers, and the telemetry fields on `AgentConfig`, `AgentRuntimeConfig`, `ExtensionContext`, the plugin setup context and the gateway config.
- llms: `sdk.error` capture at the provider boundary and the `errorReported` flag on the `finish` event.
- agents: `agent.*` event mirroring, the task lifecycle events and `sdk.error` reporting.

**Item 36** (`Engine: merge @plinycode/agents into core`)
- The `sdk/packages/agents` package. Its code moved with `git mv` to `sdk/packages/core/src/runtime/agent/` (`agent-runtime.ts`, both test files, a slimmed barrel).
- Workspace wiring: the `@plinycode/agents` entries in core's and the extension's `package.json`, the tsconfig path maps (core, llms, `sdk/`, `apps/`, the VS Code compat config), biome's import restrictions, the root `test:unit` script and vitest projects, the Node smoke test and code metrics. `bun.lock` was regenerated with bun 1.3.14.
- `@plinycode/agents` as a host-provided module for plugins.

## Kept
- `distinctId` and `resolveCoreDistinctId`. The distinct ID is sent to the gateway as request metadata (`userId`). It moved from `services/telemetry/distinct-id.ts` to `services/distinct-id.ts`.
- Local logging. Every catch block that logged before still logs.
- `OpenTelemetryClientConfig` in `shared/src/services/telemetry.ts`, because the remote-config bundle schema still uses it. Remote config belongs to another track.
- `EnterpriseSyncResponse.hasTelemetryOverrides` (an RPC contract, remote-config track).
- The per-session agent identity snapshot in `AgentEventBridge`. It no longer feeds telemetry, but it still sets `teamRole` on events a team lead emits after its session is deregistered. The type is renamed to `AgentEventContextOverrides`.
- The model-stream wrapper in the agent loop, which ends the stream quietly when steering aborts a request. It is now `openModelStream`.
- `posthog-node` in core's `package.json`. It is now unused and is left for the dependency track.

## Behaviour
- No user-visible change. Production never passed a telemetry service, so every removed path was already a no-op.
- `global-settings.json` files that contain `telemetryOptOut` load fine. The key is dropped on the next write, because the schema strips unknown keys.
- Plugins that import `@plinycode/agents` no longer resolve. `createTool` is available from `@plinycode/core` and `@plinycode/shared`.
- The webview never imported `@plinycode/agents`, and neither did the extension source (only config files named it), so nothing browser-side needed a new home.
- The agent tests are now covered by core's typecheck. That exposed type errors they already had (they were never typechecked before), and those are fixed: a local `withResolvers` helper (the engine targets ES2022), full `AgentMessage` literals, and an explicit `return undefined` in one hook.

- `bun run lint`, `bun run format`, `bun run types`, `bun run check:docs`

- Engine `bunx vitest run`:

  - shared: 417 pass.

- Extension:
  - `bunx vitest run`: 1543 pass.
  - `bun run test:unit`: the failures are exactly the 7 known baseline files.

### Description

Cancelling a running PlinyCode task could show **Resume Task** while queued prompts, retry recovery, or prepared sends continued executing. Cancellation now spans the complete turn, immediately displays **Request Cancelled**, holds queued input, and waits for cleanup before Resume continues the same conversation.

- Preserve cancellation through host preparation and recovery; prevent overlapping runs and automatic queue draining after a user abort.
- Check cancellation between tool executions and immediately before editor/patch writes after previews. Ignore cancelled sends' late callbacks and content while retaining usage accounting.
- Cancel the model request alongside background-command cleanup. Retain an original unsent request and its attachments for Resume.
- Keep agent command terminals hidden until **PlinyCode: Show Agent Terminal** is requested, with a picker when several terminals exist.
- Add `plinycode.chat.fontSize` (10–24 px, default 13) with live updates to the chat panel, and keep cancellation notices visible outside collapsed activity groups.

- Full `bun run check`: lint, formatting, SDK build, extension/webview build, and all package type checks.

### Description

Step 4b of making the repo friendlier to AI coding agents. Several root scripts that agents (and people) reach for first were broken or quietly did nothing:

- `bun run types` skipped the extension: it runs every workspace's `typecheck` script, and the extension had none.
- `bun run check`, `bun run build` and `bun run build:apps` failed: each calls `bun -F plinycode-dev build`, and the extension had no `build` script.
- `bun run check`, `bun run format` and `bun run fix` also failed immediately. They run Biome from the repo root over `apps/vscode/`, which has its own root Biome config ("Found a nested root configuration").
- **Formatting was never checked in CI.** The extension's `format` script, run by `ext-vscode-test`'s quality checks, used `--changed --since main`, but there is no `main` branch, so it checked 0 files. The engine job's "Lint & Format" step only ran `biome lint`. As a result, 49 files had drifted from Biome's formatting.

This PR is pushed one commit at a time, so CI verifies each on its own:

1. **Format the 49 files.** Biome's safe fixes only: formatting and import order in 41 engine files, and formatting plus two lint safe-fixes (a redundant `else` after `return`, import order) in 8 extension files. No behaviour change. The full engine and extension pipelines run on it.
2. **Scripts and CI.** Add `build` and `typecheck` scripts to the extension. Make the root `check`, `format` and `fix` run Biome per workspace. Make the extension's `format` check the whole tree. Make both CI jobs actually check formatting.
3. **Docs.** The guides currently say `bun run types` skips the extension; update them.

None of the 49 files is touched by the open PR #47, so this won't cause merge conflicts there.

### Test Procedure

For commit 1:
- `bun run build:sdk`, `bun run types`, `bun run lint` and `cd apps/vscode && bun run check-types` all pass after formatting.
- The changed host-bridge code generator still runs.
- The set of changed files matches exactly the 49 that Biome reported.
- CI's engine tests, extension tests and e2e are the behaviour check.

**CI results, per commit:**
1. Formatting: all 16 checks passed on the first run, so there was no behaviour change.

### Description

Step 2 of making the repo friendlier to AI coding agents. Agents rely on the markdown docs to find their way around, and a link to a file that doesn't exist sends them hunting for it, or makes them create it. Nothing checked those links, and a docs-only PR ran no CI at all.

**Commit 1: link checker.** `sdk/scripts/check-doc-links.ts`, run with `bun run check:docs`, reads every git-tracked markdown file and fails on any relative link, image or reference definition whose target doesn't exist. It skips code blocks, code spans, external URLs and `#anchor` links, and doesn't check anchors. A new `docs-check` workflow runs it on every PR and on pushes to `master` and `stage`. It has no path filter: the check takes seconds and needs no `bun install`, and renaming or deleting *any* file can break a link in a markdown file the PR didn't touch.

**Commit 2: fix what it found.** The first push of this PR is expected to fail `docs-check`, on 5 links:

- `sdk/AGENTS.md` links `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `ARCHITECTURE.md` and `DOC.md`, none of which exist in `sdk/`. It also tells agents to update `ARCHITECTURE.md` after hub changes, which would lead them to create one from scratch.
- `sdk/packages/shared/README.md` links `../README.md` and `./ARCHITECTURE.md`, which don't exist either.

The second commit fixes both files. While checking `sdk/AGENTS.md` against the repo, it also fixes instructions that were wrong rather than just broken: it said to run commands from `sdk/`, but `sdk/` has no `package.json` (the repo root is the Bun workspace root). It also listed a test command for a `@plinycode/cli` package that doesn't exist, left out `@plinycode/ui`, and showed CLI and desktop apps as engine consumers. Every command the file now quotes was run from the repo root.

### Test Procedure

- Ran the checker on the repo: it reports exactly those 5 links across 51 tracked markdown files.
- Ran it against hand-written fixtures in a scratch git repo: it catches missing targets in plain links, `<angle>` links, reference definitions, root-relative `/…` links and links with `#fragment` or a title. It ignores existing files and directories, `%20`-encoded names, code spans, backtick and tilde fences, external URLs and anchors.
- `biome check` and `tsc --strict` pass on the script.
- CI: the first push's `docs-check` run should fail on the 5 links above. The second push should pass, and `engine-test` also runs because `sdk/**` changed.

Long conversations drifted, especially after compaction. This PR comes out of an audit of the stored conversations (192 sessions, traces for the 18 since 2026-10-15) and the code behind each symptom. Details and numbers are in `docs/context-compaction.md`, `docs/memory.md`, `docs/trace-and-logs.md` and `docs/agent-tools.md`.

## What was wrong

- **FreeAuto compacted every ten or so iterations** (11 times in one 166-call run, at estimates of 35k-80k tokens against an 83k trigger) and re-read the same files after each one. The trigger divided the previous request's real count by the *current* estimate, so right after a compaction it kept firing; the compacted projection was sized unpruned; tool loops counted as "pairs" and forced a target that, after a 22k-token fixed overhead, left one tool pair.
- **Summaries narrowed the goal** ("execute the plan in PLAN.md" became "add Communicator plumbing to SurfaceTetMesh" after eight summaries of summaries), kept file names only, and took the completion guard's `[SYSTEM]` reminders for the user's newest request.
- **Kimi thought out loud in content**: 6% of assistant messages (over 10k chars) held 52% of all assistant text; one 72k-char reply stayed in the request for sixteen calls because the pruning protected a prompt-cache prefix the free pool does not have. The prompt told the model its plan "can be quite long".
- **Noise and thrash**: 159 "failed with exit code 1 ... do not end your turn" notes (any non-zero exit, uncapped, tool name mangled to `run__commands`); `run_commands` ran a stringified Python list verbatim and `ask_question` told the model to shorten its options to 5 characters, which ended a run in a doom loop; the unfinished-turn guard flagged finished answers; `<editor_state>` listed 20 tabs plus "and 22 more".
- **Repository memory was a change log** ("Fixed LineFilterBuf::sync() bug", three near-identical "release workflow" entries), saved from distiller proposals with important ones pre-checked and no gate on the save path.
- **Debugging context was lost**: every trace request was rewritten whole (ids regenerated per call; the longest trace hit the 20 MB cap), compaction diagnostics logged no numbers, and the token calibration file was never written because the llms package bundled its own copy of `@plinycode/shared`.

## What changes

- **Compaction** (`sdk/packages/core/src/extensions/context`): the under-estimate factor is the previous request's count over its *own* estimate (`previousRequest` on the prepare-turn context); the compacted projection is sized pruned (`pruneForApi`); typed turns, not tool pairs, make a conversation long; message target and preserved tail have floors; a compaction that is still over the trigger and not 10% smaller falls through to basic trimming on top of the summary, else the session rests six iterations; summaries pin the original request, the task list and the last failure, keep earlier notes verbatim (condensed past 12k chars), and dedupe Windows paths; reminders and notices are no longer turn starts. FreeAuto's budget goes from 92k to 150k (sized to kimi-k2.6, the coding route's lead).
- **Pruning**: a model without a `prompt-cache` capability (the routers, the free pool) ages the current turn at once: a monologue before a tool call keeps a 1,500-char head and a 600-char tail, results over 8k are middle-cut from the third newest call. Cached models keep the block scheme.
- **Prompt and tools**: short planning instruction, duplicated turn-end / parallelism / verify text removed, two-line mode tags, relative rules list, lean tool estimates, 8 workspace tabs in the editor state, skills listing capped.
- **Tool inputs and guards**: list-shaped string arguments are repaired (jsonrepair) or rejected with a clear message; hook attributes no longer mangle underscores; failed-command notes capped at 2 per run and skipped for quiet query exits; the leaked-reasoning rule needs density and skips structured or hand-back replies; message ids and metadata survive the request build.
- **Memory**: one change-log gate on every write path (tool and proposals), importance has to be earned (rule-like text, fewer than 15 Important entries), dedupe at 0.7, 8 saves per conversation, proposals start unchecked, cleanup proposals for change-log and duplicate entries already on disk.
- **Trace and calibration**: `compaction` trace records with the trigger numbers, `estimatedTokens` on every `request` record, incremental requests work again, one `@plinycode/shared` instance (llms keeps it external; the build verifies it), so `token-calibration.json` is written and the calibration factor reaches compaction.

## Verification

- Engine: `bun run build:sdk`, core, shared and llms unit suites (the `hooks/` and `mcp/client` failures are the known local-environment ones).
- Extension: `bun run check-types`, `bun run test:unit`, knip.
- Replay of the recorded sessions and a dev-host run are listed in the plan's verification section; the trace of a new FreeAuto run shows the `compaction` records and `reset: false` requests.

## Why

The benchmark session exported as `plinycode-hanging-conversation-20260925-0819.md` (FreeAuto·smart, GPUSurfer) stalled six times. Reading it against the call log, the catalog and the thinking probe data showed four distinct causes. This PR fixes all four and bumps the pre-release to **0.1.3-test.6**.

## What changed

**1. Models that reason inside their content are now catalogued as reasoners** (`pliny-models.json`, `probe-pliny-free-models.ts`)
The gateway exposes no reasoning channel for `kimi-k2.6`, `qwen3-6-35b-a3b-1-28dd3`, `nemotron-3-ultra-550b-a55` and the sia `qwen3-5-397b-a17b`: their deliberation arrives as ordinary content. The probe only counted reasoning deltas, so all four were `defaultOn: false` and the off-switch was never sent. The smart profile's classifier and the judge both run on the 35B, got a paragraph of thinking truncated before the JSON verdict, and reported "no verdict" on every turn of that session. The probe now treats a long answer to its one-word question as reasoning; the three models with a working `chat_template_kwargs` off-switch get it on quick and utility calls, kimi is marked always-on.

**2. The guard catches a reply that ends on the model's plan** (`unfinished-turn-guard.ts`, `router-prompt.ts`, `router-rules.ts`)
kimi past ~80k tokens ends with "I need to: 1. Check what's running 2. … 4. Give a clear status update" and no tool call (0 tool calls in 7 calls that session). `endsWithPlanList` flags a first-person plan intro followed by imperative list items with nothing after; results lists and option lists for the user do not match. The free-model prompt addendum names the shape. `qwen3-coder` now leads the `default` route with kimi as fallback (the `subagent` route is unchanged).

**3. The call log records what each call produced** (`routed-agent-model.ts`, `router-call-log.ts`, `summarize-free-auto-log.ts`)
Every line of `pliny-free-auto-calls.jsonl` gains `finishReason`, `textChars`, `reasoningChars` and `toolCalls`. The summary script has a "Text-only stops" column per model, so stop rates can be read from real use instead of transcripts.

**4. The agent terminal disables git's pager and prompts** (`agent-terminal-env.ts`)
`git branch` in that session paged and waited almost three minutes for a keypress the model could not send. Both terminal factories now set `GIT_PAGER=cat`, `PAGER=cat` and `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`.

`docs/pliny-free-auto-router.md` documents all three behaviours.

## Verification

- `bun run test:vitest -- src/sdk/router`: 243 passed, including new tests for the plan-list rule (the four kimi endings from the transcript plus three non-matching endings) and for the call shape.
- `@plinycode/llms` suite: 762 passed.
- `bun run types`: clean. Biome clean on every touched file.
- The probe was not re-run against the gateway; the catalog edits are hand-applied from the existing `pliny-free-auto-thinking-probe.json` numbers (baseline 1339/1017/205/1106 content chars for the four, 5 with template-off for three of them).

## Note for testers

Rules files are only written when missing, so an existing `~/.cline/data/pliny-free-auto*.md` keeps its own route order. Move it aside to pick up the new `default` order.

hits.body:
## Why

Three problems found while reviewing how the agent searches and edits code.

**1. `search_codebase` silently skipped whole languages.** The engine runs `rg` from PATH. It is rarely there (never on a stock Windows install), so the search fell back to a JavaScript scan that only opened files whose extension was on a fixed list. `.cc`, `.cxx`, `.hh`, `.sv`, `.v`, `.tcl`, `.cs`, `.proto` and many others were not on it, so a search in those files answered "No results found" and the model concluded the symbol did not exist.

**2. Where `rg` was on PATH, the results were garbled.** The parser built each result from ripgrep's `context` events and expected the matching line to be among them. Ripgrep reports the match as a `match` event, so:

- the matching line itself was never printed;
- the lines before a match were attached to the previous result, usually a different file;
- `--max-count=1` showed one match per file.

For a file `B.txt` followed by `A.txt`, the model saw:

```
B.txt:4:1
  5: b5
  1: a1      <- from A.txt
  2: a2      <- from A.txt
```

**3. The diff preview kept its own copy of the editor's matching logic** (`computeNewEditorContent`), so any change to how `old_text` is matched had to be made twice or the preview and the write would disagree.

## What changes

- **The extension runs the search with VS Code's own ripgrep.** `VscodeSessionHost` passes a search executor built with `rgPath: () => getBinaryLocation("rg")`, the same lookup file search already uses. `createSearchExecutor` takes the new `rgPath` option, tries it first and then `rg` on PATH.
- **The fallback reads every file that is not binary.** The extension allow-list is replaced by a deny-list of binary extensions, a 2 MB size limit and a NUL-byte check. `includeExtensions` still restricts the scan when a caller passes it.
- **Ripgrep results are parsed by event type** (`parseRipgrepEvents`): the match line is printed and marked `>`, leading and trailing context stay with their own match, and paths use forward slashes.
- **Up to 10 matches per file** (`maxMatchesPerFile`), in both paths, with a closing note naming the files that have more. Ripgrep showed 1; the fallback showed every match, so one busy file could fill the 100-result limit.
- **"No matches" from ripgrep is final.** It used to fall through to a second, full JavaScript scan.
- **A pattern starting with `-`** is passed with `-e`, so ripgrep no longer reads it as a flag.
- **`replaceTextInContent`** (new `executors/text-replace.ts`) holds the replacement logic. The editor executor and the VS Code diff preview both call it. Matching behaviour and error messages are unchanged.

The `search_codebase` description gains one sentence saying that matching is case-insensitive, that the matching line is marked `>`, and that only the first matches per file are shown.

## Behaviour changes to be aware of

- Searches now go through ripgrep in the extension, so they respect `.gitignore` and skip hidden files, as ripgrep does by default. The fallback did neither.
- The fallback counted every match on a line as a result; a line now counts once, as in ripgrep.

## Test procedure

- New engine tests: `text-replace.test.ts`; in `search.test.ts`, the fallback finds matches in `.cc`, `.sv` and `.tcl` files and skips a binary one, shows the marked match line with its context, caps matches per file and names the capped file, and `parseRipgrepEvents` is checked against event streams in ripgrep's real order (context before the match, a line between two close matches, the per-file cap).
- Ran the built engine against a small fixture through VS Code's bundled `rg.exe` and through the fallback: both find the `.cc`, `.sv` and `.tcl` matches with the right lines.
- `bun run build:sdk`, `bun run types`, `bun run lint`, `bun run format`: clean.
- Engine tool tests (`sdk/packages/core/src/extensions/tools`): 375 pass.
- Extension `test:vitest`: 1326 pass.
- Extension `test:unit`: 63 of 69 files pass. The 6 failing files are the hook suites under `src/core/hooks/__tests__`, which fail on my machine because a `package.json` in the Temp directory makes Node load the test hook scripts as ES modules; they do not touch this code.
- Not run locally: integration and e2e tests, and the search has not been exercised inside a running extension host.

## Type of Change

-   [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
-   [x] ♻️ Refactor Changes

hits.body:
## Problem

**Send now (steering)** waited for the end of the task instead of reaching the agent. The message was only read before the agent's next model call. Since the `wait` tool (0.1.3-test.3), the agent often spends minutes inside a `wait` (up to 600 s) or a long foreground command. So the steering message stayed queued until the task ended or was cancelled.

Evidence from the 0.1.3-test.7 log: a steering message sent at 17:24:54 sat in the queue through model calls 23–28 and ran only after the user cancelled at 17:26:12. On 0.1.2 and 0.1.3-dev.1, steering messages were consumed within ~50 ms.

## Fix

- **Engine** (`@plinycode/agents`, `@plinycode/shared`): `AgentToolContext.userMessageSignal` fires when a steering message arrives (`notifyPendingUserMessage`). It is reset when pending messages are read and at the start of each run, so a message that was already read or drained never cuts later tools short.
- **`wait`** ends early and tells the model that the user sent a new message.
- **Foreground commands** are detached the same way as **Proceed While Running**: the command keeps running in the terminal, further output goes to a log file, and the model reads the message now. The result text matches the unfinished-turn guard's "detached" detection.
- The follow-up log line now records the delivery (`queue` / `steer`).
- The Send now tooltip describes the new behaviour.
- Version bumped to `0.1.5-test.2`.

## Tests

- `agent-runtime.test.ts`: a running tool is signalled by a steer and the message is read at the next step; a steer notified between runs does not leak into the next run's tools. 84/84 pass.
- `vscode-wait-tool.test.ts`: a steer ends the wait with the explanatory result.
- `vscode-run-commands-tool.test.ts`: a steer detaches a running foreground command, and later output lands in the log.
- 5 existing `vscode-run-commands-tool` tests fail under bun on Windows with or without this change (`vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync` is missing, plus terminal-profile tests). The hook tests need `bash`.

## Why

Long conversations drift. The logs since 2026-10-10 (2,146 calls, 102 runs, 14 long sessions) show where:

- **Routing.** Every `huge` verdict (164 of 164, median context 70k) and every `quick` verdict past 30k tokens fell through to the `default` route, Sonnet 5: 77 of Sonnet 5's 85 calls. `reason` verdicts for chores ("please create a PR", `[CI WATCHER] CI failed`, "not sure why the build takes so long") kept whole turns on the Sonnet thinking preset: 124 calls of one build-polling turn. Guard escalations sent the last one or two calls of 100k-token turns to Sonnet 5, a full cache write each.
- **Context.** One run compacted five times (at iterations 3, 20, 33, 62 and 86); after each compaction the model re-read the same files and edited from stale content. Tool results of 100-224k chars (`search_codebase` with 4-7 queries) and Kimi's in-content deliberation (25 replies of 30-130k chars of "Wait… Actually… Let me…") stayed in the history for the rest of the conversation. Failed oversized `editor` writes (plans and reports) left 10-25k chars of input behind, three times per session.
- **Memory.** The distiller added twenty entries to one repository's memory in a day, most of them change-logs and code facts, each then sent with every request.
- **Skills.** `skills` was called as `{skill: "commit", args: "-m …"}` seven times: its own description gave that as the example.

## What changes

**Router (BalanceAuto)**
- A verdict whose route refuses the request's size falls back by tier (`quick` → `coding`; `huge` → `coding` in act mode, `plan-and-reasoning` in plan mode) instead of the catch-all. The classifier no longer offers `huge` and spells out that chores are `code`.
- The classifier and the keyword routes read only what the user typed: `<editor_state>` and `<mode_notice>` stripped, reminders, hook context and compaction summaries skipped.
- `health.maxPaidCallsPerTurn` (default 20, `0` off): past the cap the rest of the turn runs on the coding route's free lead, once per turn, with a chat row and `paidCapHit` in the run log.
- The guard's first stall escalation goes to the next free model; only the second, or six failed commands, to the default lead. `escalatedTo` in the run log.

**Engine**
- `pruneStaleContext` (core, on the request copy only): earlier turns' tool results over 2k chars become a stub; aged in-turn results are middle-cut in blocks of eight iterations (one cache rewrite per block); the deliberation before an earlier tool call is cut to its last 600 chars; the inputs of failed oversized tool calls are elided. Replaying four long sessions through it sends 69-77% fewer characters. Compaction sizing sees the pruned request, so it triggers later.
- `search_codebase` returns at most 32k chars per call across its queries, `read_files` 64k across its files.
- The editor accepts a large `new_text` when creating a file or writing a markdown/text document.
- Loop detection resets per run (a repeated user request across turns could trip the hard stop) and notices the third non-adjacent identical call of a run, once.
- The `skills` tool example is no longer git-shaped, and says the tool runs no command.
