## Why

`watch_ci` watches one pull request for one conversation, and only the agent can start it. When several PRs are in flight (GPUSurfer's five pipelines per PR, plus merge conflicts with `stage`), there is no single place that shows which ones are red or conflicting, and no quick way to have PlinyCode fix one without switching branches in your own checkout.

## What changes

- **CI Board view** (pulse icon in the panel's title bar). It watches:
  - pull request links: GitHub, GitHub Enterprise, Azure DevOps cloud, and on-premises servers like `ado.internal.synopsys.com/tfs/…/pullrequest/N`;
  - branches of the window's repositories (the branch's open PR, else its pushed head);
  - a repository's open PRs, the user's own or everyone's.
- **One dot per pipeline** on the PR's head commit: green passed, red failed, yellow running, grey no run on this commit. Clicking a dot opens the run. A **Conflicts** badge shows a PR that does not merge cleanly.
- **Notifications** when a pipeline turns red or a PR starts conflicting, once per commit, with **Open CI Board** and a button that runs the entry's first action.
- **Actions** run a prompt against a PR. Each entry starts with the built-in **Fix CI & conflicts**, a general version of GPUSurfer's `pipelines_failures_investigation.md`: sync, merge the target branch keeping both intents, triage with `pr_checks`/`pipeline_runs`/`pipeline_report`, fix the build, update tests only the way the repo documents (never recalibrate a regression), push, `watch_ci`, report. An action can also use a prompt file (relative paths resolve in the worktree, then the repo; front matter is dropped) or typed text, with `{{prId}}`, `{{targetBranch}}`, `{{worktree}}`… placeholders.
- **Git worktree per PR.** Run fetches the branch and creates or reuses `<repo>.worktrees/<branch>` (or `plinycode.ci.worktreeRoot`), fast-forwarding only a clean copy. If the branch is already checked out, the run works in that checkout. The conversation is bound to the worktree, kept out of the recent-workspaces list, and linked from the board row.
- **Autonomy** (Manual / Auto / Full auto) is stored per entry. Only Manual runs now; Auto and Full auto, with background starts, per-session auto-approve and caps, are the next PR.
- **Providers** (`server/providers/`): `listOpenPrs`, `branchHead`, merge state, fork detection, and pipeline name and id on runs. On Azure DevOps, run names carry the build number and could not be grouped by name. GitHub GETs are revalidated with ETags (304s don't count against the rate limit), and the remaining rate limit is tracked.
- **DevOps tools in a worktree conversation** default `workspace` to the conversation's folder (`BuiltinMcpSource.providerFor`). Before, they used the window's first folder, the wrong branch.
- **Polling**: every 60 s while the board is open and every 180 s otherwise. Each cycle lists PRs but fetches a PR's runs only when its head moved, runs are still going, its merge state is pending, or 10 minutes have passed. 20 idle PRs cost about 60 listing requests an hour plus a refresh every 10 minutes. With fewer than 500 GitHub requests left, the board slows down 4×.
- The board is saved per window workspace in `ci-board.json` in the shared data directory, like recent workspaces, so two windows don't overwrite each other.
- Docs: `docs/ci-board.md`, plus links from `AGENTS.md`, `apps/vscode/AGENTS.md`, `docs/devops-mcp.md` and `REPOMAP.md`.

## Testing

- `bun test src/services/devops-mcp`: 140 passed. New suites cover:
  - PR link parsing, including on-premises Azure DevOps;
  - grouping runs into dots, and transitions (once per commit, none on first sight);
  - the poller's request gating, timings, rate-limit backoff, and a 20-PR, one-hour request budget;
  - the shared store across windows;
  - worktrees against real temporary git repos (create, reuse, fast-forward, dirty copy, missing branch);
  - prompt composition, and preparing a run end to end;
  - provider mapping: merge state (including merged PRs, which GitHub never computes), forks, `listOpenPrs` mine/all, `branchHead`, pipeline ids, ETag 304.
- `bun run test:vitest`: 1642 passed (adds `recordRecentWorkspace: false` and `providerFor` / `withDefaultArgument` tests).
- `bun run test:webview`: 533 passed (adds `CiItemRow` dots, conflict badge, run and error states).
- Live, read-only, against this repository's GitHub API: open PR listing, `branchHead`, workflow names and ids, dots for #114 and #115 (four green workflows each), ETag revalidation not counting against the rate limit.
- `bun run check-types`, Biome on changed files, `lint:proto`, `check:docs`, `analyze:unused:prod`: clean.
- `bun run test:unit`: the CI Board suites pass. 43 hook tests (`src/core/hooks`) fail locally because a stray `package.json` with `"type": "module"` in `%TEMP%` makes Node load the tests' `.js` hook scripts as ES modules. Unrelated to this change.
- Not yet tried: clicking through the board in a dev host, and an on-premises Azure DevOps board (needs `AZURE_DEVOPS_PAT`).

Roadmap A1 (docs/roadmap.md). The agent found code by regex only: `search_codebase` returns every `foo` in comments and strings, several calls per question, and nothing says which hit is the definition. The window already runs language servers that know.

**Two extension tools** (`apps/vscode/src/sdk/code-intel/`, host side in `apps/vscode/src/hosts/vscode/code-intel-source.ts`):
- `find_symbol({ query?, path? })`: a file's outline (`kind name  line`, indented, filtered by `query`), or the workspace symbols matching `query` (`kind name  path:line:col`, at most 40).
- `code_navigate({ action, path, symbol, line? })`: `definition`, `references` or `hover` for a symbol as written in a file. The tool locates the identifier (nearest to `line` when given), so the model never computes a column. Definitions and references come back grouped by file as `line:col  preview`, 30 lines at most then `+N more in M files`; hovers are reduced to their code-fenced signature lines plus a few lines of prose.

Two tools with an `action` argument rather than six, because free models mis-fill wide schemas. VS Code cannot say whether a language server is registered for a file, so an empty answer is retried once after 1.5 s and then ends with a line sending the model to `search_codebase`; a file extension that answers nothing twice is not waited for again.

Wiring: registered in `createVscodeExtraTools` for the root and sub-agents, approved with the read tools, run in parallel. New chat rows `findSymbol` / `codeNavigate` show the tool's answer (the translator now copies the output into the row's `content` for these two tools). Setting `plinycode.codeIntel.enabled` (default on) applies to the next conversation. Docs: new section in `docs/agent-tools.md`.

## Mode switch: Plan, Agent, Ask

- The **Act** mode is now labelled **Agent**. The internal value stays `act`, so settings, the wire protocol and old conversations are unchanged.
- Each mode has its own color on the selected segment and on the outline of the focused prompt box: **Plan** yellow, **Agent** red (`statusBarItem.errorBackground`), **Ask** green.
  - Before, Act used the blue focus color.
  - Ask borrowed `statusBarItem.remoteBackground`, which is blue in VS Code's current default themes, so it didn't look green either.
- User-facing text follows the new name:
  - the model-settings tabs and the "Use different models for Plan and Agent modes" option;
  - the Execute plan button and its menu;
  - the setting descriptions;
  - the ask-mode guard errors.
- The model is now told to say "toggle to Agent mode". The chat turns both that and the old "to Act mode" into the toggle link.

## Side questions (off-the-record prompts)

A **Side question** checkbox next to the mode switch marks the next message as off the record:
- The agent answers it, but later model requests leave out the question, the answer and every tool call made for it.
- The chat keeps showing the exchange, labelled **Side question · not in the context**, also after the conversation is reopened.
- The checkbox is enabled only when a conversation exists and the agent is idle, and it clears after each send.

Design and limits are in [docs/side-questions.md](docs/side-questions.md). In short:

- **Kept, then filtered.** The turn stays in `messages.json`, tagged `metadata.offTheRecord`, because the chat is rebuilt from that transcript. `dropOffTheRecordTurns` removes it before every model request and before compaction, keeping the turn while it is being answered. Manual `/compact` filters the same way, so the saved compaction state stays consistent.
- **Read-only.** While a side question runs, a `beforeTool` guard rejects:
  - file writes and file-editing commands;
  - `update_todo_list`;
  - sub-agents and teammates.

  The message goes out as `<user_input mode="ask">` in any mode. The prompt prefix and tool list don't change, so the prompt cache still hits.
- **Per-message context.** A side question does not use up the mode-switch notice. Its `<editor_state>` block is not recorded as sent, so the next normal message still gets it.
- **Routing.** FreeAuto and BalanceAuto treat a side question like plan mode, so the completion judge and the reviewer don't run on it.

### Why not subagents or a fork

- **Subagents:** the model decides when to start one, and its result lands back in the main context.
- **Fork:** a copy of the conversation keeps the original clean, but you have to switch conversations and come back.

## Testing

- **New tests:**
  - engine: the filter helper, the tool guard, the run loop (tagging, filtering, guard only during the side question), and the host passing the flag;
  - extension: follow-up routing, the send path, editor state, history replay, manual compaction;
  - webview: the checkbox, the send handler, the mode colors.
- **Checks:** `bun run types`, `lint` and `format` pass, and knip is clean.
- **Suites:**
  - Engine core 1649 passed. The local failures are the known environment-only ones in `hook-file-hooks` and the MCP client, plus a `subprocess-runner` timing test that passes when run alone.
  - Shared 372 passed.
  - Extension vitest and webview vitest pass.
  - Extension `test:unit`: only the known `src/core/hooks/__tests__` environment failures.
- **E2e:** `chat.test.ts` and `plan-execute.test.ts`, which click the renamed Agent switch, pass locally.

# FreeAuto v2 — Phase (a) + (b) summary

Branch `lgiaccar/few_impr`, commit `9e9cddc`, pushed to `origin/lgiaccar/few_impr`.
Full design context: [freeauto-strategy-and-models.md](freeauto-strategy-and-models.md)
and the plan at `~/.claude/plans/please-lay-down-a-atomic-crane.md`.

## Phase (a) — Hygiene fixes

### Sub-agent turn-state isolation
Sub-agents (spawned via `spawn_agent`) reuse the parent session's routing
closure. Previously, a sub-agent call re-entered the same turn state as the
parent, silently resetting the parent's call log, sticky model, and failover
budget mid-turn.

**Fix:** each run is now keyed by whether `agentConfig.parentAgentId` is set.
A sub-agent run gets its own turn key (`<sessionId>:sub:<n>`); the parent's
turn state is untouched. Model health (which models are benched) stays
global, as intended — only per-turn bookkeeping is isolated. Sub-agent keys
are cleaned up automatically when the next parent turn starts.

**Visible effect:** FreeAuto routing rows from a sub-agent are now prefixed
`↳ sub-agent` in chat, so it's clear which model activity belongs to a
delegated task versus the main conversation.

### Image requests fail fast
No free Pliny model accepts image input, but FreeAuto previously routed
image-bearing requests through the normal candidate list anyway, likely
producing a confusing failure deep in the call.

**Fix:** the router now checks model capabilities up front. If a request
carries an image and no candidate supports it, the call fails immediately
with: *"FreeAuto routes only to free Pliny models, none of which accept
images. Pick a vision-capable model or remove the image."*

### Summarizer model id refresh
The compaction summarizer's model id was fixed to the built-in default at
session install time, before the rules file had actually loaded — so a
custom `utility.summarizer` in `pliny-free-auto.md` was silently ignored.
Now it updates in place once the rules file is read.

## Phase (b) — Sub-agents enabled + routing improvements

### Sub-agents turned on
`spawn_agent` was hard-disabled in the extension regardless of settings.
It's now gated on the existing `subagentsEnabled` setting, which gets a new
toggle: **Settings → Features → Advanced → Sub-agents** (off by default,
applies to new tasks).

### Spawn visibility
The PlinyCode output channel now logs a line when a sub-agent starts and
when it finishes:
```
[Subagent] spawned: <task prompt, truncated>
[Subagent] completed · in <N> / out <N> tok
```

### New `subagent` route
Delegated tasks are typically short and bounded, so a new default route
sends sub-agent calls to fast models first (`qwen3-coder-480b`,
`nemotron-3-super-120b`, `kimi-k2.6`) ahead of the general-purpose routes.

### Default route reorder (field experience + probe data)
- `qwen3-coder-480b` now leads both the `coding` and `default` routes, and
  heads the fallback pool — it's fast (356ms TTFT) and, per your testing,
  reliably good at fixing conflicts.
- `GLM-5.2` is removed from `coding` and `default` — it's slow (1279ms
  TTFT, 7.6 tok/s) and is kept only on the `huge-context` route, where its
  512k window is the only option.
- The `coding` route's trigger phrases now also catch merge conflicts,
  rebase, lint errors, and type errors (previously only fix/implement/refactor-style wording matched).

## Verification

- 1319 vitest tests + 1151 bun unit tests pass; `tsc` and Biome are clean.
- New tests cover: sub-agent turn isolation, image-request rejection, the
  `subagent` route, the reordered defaults, and the `subagentsEnabled` →
  `enableSpawnAgent` wiring.
- Not verified by this pass: live behavior against the Pliny gateway in a
  running extension host (no gateway access from this environment) — worth
  confirming manually per the checklist below.

## What to check manually

1. Enable **Settings → Features → Advanced → Sub-agents**.
2. Start a task, ask it to delegate something to a sub-agent — confirm:
   - `[Subagent] spawned` / `[Subagent] completed` lines in the output channel.
   - `↳ sub-agent` prefixed rows in chat, route shown as `subagent`.
   - The turn summary at the end still reflects only the parent's own calls.
3. Ask something like "fix the merge conflicts in X" — confirm it routes to
   `qwen3-coder-480b` under the `coding` route.
4. Paste an image while on FreeAuto — confirm the immediate error message,
   no model call attempted.
5. Your existing `~/.cline/data/pliny-free-auto.md` was regenerated (the old
   one was moved to `.bak`) so these new defaults actually apply — if you'd
   customized that file, diff it against the backup before discarding it.

This branch makes PlinyCode conversations easier to read and navigate without removing access to the agent's work. The goal is an answer-first chat: users should be able to find their prompt and the resulting answer quickly, then inspect reasoning, tools, edits, and command output when they need the details.

#### 1. Keep answers visible and put process details behind Show activity

Reasoning, tool calls, progress, and automatic file-edit records are grouped under a collapsed **Show activity** control. The final answer stays visible, including answers delivered as several adjacent text blocks. Expanding activity shows the original records in their original order; collapsing it returns to the shorter reading view. Expansion state is retained as rows scroll out of and back into view, within the current chat view.

The latest fix closes a gap in that behavior: **completed terminal commands and their output now collapse too**, including commands that exit with an error. Previously, command rows were unconditionally exempted from activity grouping, so a completed command could still occupy the main conversation. Running commands remain visible for progress and cancellation, and pending command approvals remain visible for user action. A failed command's output remains available inside activity; standalone error notifications are not hidden by this change.

Actionable file approvals, memory proposals, hook notices, and standalone errors remain visible. User prompts and CI watcher reports remain separate from the agent's process details. The compact working indicator also avoids a duplicate waiting row when activity already communicates that work is in progress.

#### 2. Make thinking an explicit, accessible disclosure

Thinking no longer forces itself open just because reasoning is streaming. Users can open or close it themselves, including while the model is working. The disclosure exposes its expanded state to assistive technology and supports keyboard interaction. Open streaming reasoning follows new content; reopening completed reasoning starts from the beginning rather than jumping to its end.

#### 3. Improve Markdown reading quality

Assistant answers are no longer clipped by the generic three-line paragraph preview rule. More consistent heading, paragraph, list, quote, and link styling provides a clearer reading hierarchy. Wide code and tables scroll within the message instead of forcing the conversation wider. Table scroll regions can receive keyboard focus. Existing Markdown content and controls, including code copying, remain available.

#### 4. Make follow-ups and side questions easier to distinguish

Visible, labeled turn boundaries separate follow-up prompts and side questions from the preceding answer. Replies to tool approvals are not mistaken for new user turns or sticky prompts. Boundaries stay attached to existing message rows, preserving message timestamps and virtualized-list indices rather than introducing synthetic chat messages.

#### 5. Keep the development preview reliable

F5 readiness now waits for the required builds, and a successful companion bundle cannot mask a failed extension build. Protobuf generation stages output before updating live files, replaces only changed content, and avoids exposing half-written generated files to watchers. This reduces transient missing-import failures during development; it does not change the wire protocol.

These changes are presentation and development-workflow improvements, not changes to model selection, tool execution, approval policy, or stored conversation content.

## What changed

**Plan item 29b (track K).** The models.dev-derived generated catalog (`catalog.generated.ts`, `providers.generated.ts`, `provider-ids.generated.ts`) previously included every models.dev provider, even ones PlinyCode can never run because #84's `usesShippedAdapter` filter only excluded them from the runtime registry afterward, not from generation itself.

1. Extracted `usesShippedAdapter` (family must be `openai-compatible` or `anthropic`, and not `protocol: "openai-responses"` / `client: "openai"`) into `sdk/packages/llms/src/providers/builtin-types.ts` so it's a single predicate shared by:
   - `builtins.ts` (unchanged behavior — still filters `GENERATED_PROVIDER_SPECS` before merging into the runtime registry)
   - `catalog-live.ts`'s `getSelectedModelsDevProviders`, which now excludes non-shippable-family providers **before** they're written to any generated file.
2. Regenerated all three generated files against live models.dev data with `bun run build:models`.
3. Removed `catalog-cline-recommended.ts` / `cline-recommended.generated.ts` (the Cline-cloud recommended/free/ClinePass model-list fetch-and-merge machinery) — PlinyCode never calls Cline's cloud recommendation endpoint, and `core/services/llms/cline-recommended-models.ts` (the other consumer named in the plan) was already deleted by earlier PRs (confirmed absent). Removed the now-dead `includeClineCloudModels` option on `ModelCatalogConfig` and the `GENERATED_CLINE_RECOMMENDED_MODELS` re-export.
4. Fixed every consumer/test that exercised the removed behavior or asserted on now-excluded providers (`catalog-live.test.ts`, `builtins.test.ts`, `provider-defaults.test.ts`, `local-provider-service.test.ts`, `apps/vscode/test-setup.js`'s stale mock).

The other consumers named in the plan (`catalog.generated-access.ts`, core's `provider-defaults.ts`, `local-provider-registry.ts`, `provider-settings-legacy-migration.ts`, `provider-settings.ts`, extension's `cline-session-factory.ts`, `model-catalog/store.ts`, `shared/storage/provider-keys.ts`) only use generic catalog APIs (`getGeneratedModelsForProvider`, `getProviderCollectionSync`, etc.) and needed no changes — verified by reading each and by the full test suites passing. `providerSwitchNormalization.ts` no longer exists (removed by PR #90).

## Removed

Ten models.dev providers whose family isn't `openai-compatible`/`anthropic` are now excluded from generation entirely (previously merely hidden from the runtime registry): `bedrock`, `gemini`, `infer`, `meta`, `mistral`, `neosmith`, `openai-native`, `perplexity-agent`, `vertex`, `vivgrid`. Also removed: the Cline-recommended-models snapshot/fetch machinery, its generated file, and the dead `includeClineCloudModels` config option.

## Kept

Everything `openai-compatible`/`anthropic`-family (201 of the prior 203 generated providers — 2 fewer net, since models.dev's own listing also changed between generations). Pliny/FreeAuto/BalanceAuto are unaffected: `pliny-models.ts` builds `PLINY_*` models from `data/pliny-models.json` directly, never from the generated catalog (confirmed by reading the module and running `pliny-models.test.ts` / `pliny-thinking.test.ts`, both passing).

## Behaviour

No runtime behavior change for the extension: the ten removed providers were already unreachable (filtered by `usesShippedAdapter` in `builtins.ts` before this PR), so nothing that previously worked is now missing. The change moves the exclusion earlier (generation time) instead of later (registry time), shrinking the checked-in generated files and the shipped bundle by that much.

## Sizes

- `catalog.generated.ts`: 4,017,047 → 4,049,560 bytes (181,407 → 183,443 lines). Roughly flat: isolating just the 10 removed providers' old contribution (measured against the pre-change file) removes ~10,634 lines / ~5.9% of the old file, but normal upstream model-count growth between generations outweighs it in this snapshot.
- `providers.generated.ts`: 84,898 → 84,269 bytes (203 → 201 providers).
- `provider-ids.generated.ts`: 3,285 → 3,245 bytes.
- `dist/extension.js` (production esbuild): 16,926,234 → 16,933,262 bytes (+7,028 bytes / +0.04%), measured by building the same worktree at the pre-change commit and at this branch's tip. The catalog-size wash above explains why the bundle didn't shrink either.

## Checks run locally

- `bun run build:sdk`
- `apps/vscode`: `bun run check-types`
- `apps/vscode/webview-ui`: `bunx tsc -b`
- root: `bun run lint`, `bun run format`, `bun run types`, `bun run check:docs`
- `bunx vitest run` in `llms` (672 passed), `core` (1558 passed, 5 pre-existing environment failures unrelated to this change — reproduced identically on a clean `stage` checkout: Windows temp-dir ENOENT in `hook-file-hooks.test.ts`, ESM `require()` in `mcp/client.test.ts`), `shared` (356 passed)
- `bunx vitest run` in `apps/vscode` (1297 passed) and `webview-ui` (467 passed)
- `bun run test:unit` in `apps/vscode`: only the 7 pre-approved baseline failures (`hook-factory`, `taskcancel`, `taskcomplete`, `taskresume`, `taskstart`, `user-prompt-submit`, `devops-mcp/server/__tests__/tools.test.ts`)
- `apps/vscode`: `bun run build:webview` and `bun esbuild.mjs --production`

## Leftovers / risks

- The catalog-size and bundle-size deltas are essentially a wash in this snapshot because upstream models.dev data grew between generations; the real, isolated savings (~10,634 lines) only shows up when diffed against the pre-change file rather than against a hypothetical re-fetch of the old payload. Future regenerations will keep the 10 excluded providers out, so the gap should hold or grow over time.
- `fetchLiveProviderModels`/`getLiveModelsCatalog` (runtime live model-catalog refresh, separate from the checked-in generated files) were left as-is other than dropping the now-unused third parameter — out of this track's scope.

Roadmap A3 (docs/roadmap.md). A terminal command that `run_commands` stops waiting for (after 5 minutes, "Proceed While Running", or a steering message) used to leave the model a log path and nothing else. It is now registered as a background process (`p1`, `p2`, …) in a per-window registry owned by `SdkController`.

- `run_commands` gains an optional `background: true`: the commands start as child processes (in either terminal mode and in sub-agents), their output goes to a log file, and the call returns at once with the process id. Calls without it behave as before. A background process is stopped after 24 hours.
- New tools: `process_list` (id, status, elapsed time, command, log), `process_output` (the end of the log, up to 400 lines / 32 KB, never the terminal buffer) and `process_kill` (Ctrl+C, then the terminal is closed after 2 s if still busy; the whole process tree for child processes). List and output are parallel reads with read approval; kill uses command approval. CI Board runs may use all three on their own processes.
- `cancelBackgroundCommand` was a stub. It now stops every running process of the displayed conversation, and the webview's background-command flag is derived from the registry. **Behaviour to confirm:** the webview calls it on Cancel and on an interrupting message, so Cancel now also stops a dev server the model started with `background: true`.
- Child processes are stopped when the window closes. Terminals do not survive a reload; logs do.
- Docs: `docs/agent-tools.md` ("Background processes" plus the `run_commands` updates).

Tests: registry (8) and tool (10) vitest suites, 6 new `vscode-run-commands-tool` cases (hand-off registers its log and end status; a kill asked before the terminal exists applies on start; Ctrl+C then close; `background: true` returns at once, streams, is aborted by a kill, keeps its exit code), approval-group cases. check-types, lint, format, test:vitest (1818), test:webview, test:discovery, knip, check:docs pass.

Dev-host checks still to do: Ctrl+C through ConPTY on Windows, closing the terminal after the grace period, the exit code arriving through shell integration, the Cancel / interrupt path, the new rows.

Follow-up: side questions are meant to be read-only, but `process_kill` and `background: true` are not blocked there yet (needs an engine change in `isOffTheRecordBlockedTool`).

Version: 0.2.3-test.5 (every-third-PR tick).

### Description

Step 5 of making the repo friendlier to AI coding agents. `.github/copilot-instructions.md` was upstream Cline's file, and almost everything in it pointed Copilot at the wrong places:

- It told Copilot to read `.clinerules/general.md`, which doesn't exist.
- It said to build with `bun run compile` and described `src/` and `webview-ui/` at the repo root; both are now under `apps/vscode`.
- Its step-by-step guides for adding tools, slash commands and system-prompt changes went through `src/core/prompts/system-prompt/`, `src/core/slash-commands/`, `src/core/task/tools/handlers/` and `ToolExecutor.ts`, none of which exist here. The agent loop now runs in `@plinycode/core`.

It's replaced with links to the `AGENTS.md` files, which are now the single place for agent instructions, and a rule not to add instructions to this file. Copilot Chat doesn't always follow links, so it also keeps five rules inline:
- use Bun
- rebuild the engine after `sdk/` changes
- typecheck the extension with `check-types`
- PRs target `stage`
- the PlinyCode naming rule

Its one still-valid rule, writing scratch files to `ai_output/`, is in the root `AGENTS.md` since #46.

Recent Copilot versions (the coding agent, and VS Code's agent mode) also read `AGENTS.md` directly. This file mainly matters for Copilot in IDEs that only read `copilot-instructions.md`. PlinyCode itself reads workspace and nested `AGENTS.md` files (`user-instruction-config-loader.ts`), so no PlinyCode-specific rules file is needed.

### Test Procedure

- `bun run check:docs` passes on all 52 tracked markdown files, including the four new relative links from `.github/`. CI's `docs-check` job runs the same check.
- The inline rules match the `AGENTS.md` files. The `bun run types` note matches the root `package.json`: none of the extension workspaces has a `typecheck` script.

### Type of Change

-   [x] 📚 Documentation update

### Additional Notes

Documentation only, so the extension version is not ticked. This PR is independent of #46: it touches a different file, and every file it links to is already on `stage`.

# PlinyCode 0.1.2

Internal Synopsys release of the PlinyCode VS Code / Cursor extension.

**Package:** `PlinyCode-0.1.2.vsix`  
**Install:** Extensions -> ... -> **Install from VSIX...** -> select this folder's `.vsix` file, then reload the window.

**Gateway:** `https://snps-inference.internal.synopsys.com` (Synopsys network only)

---

## Highlights in 0.1.2 (since 0.1.1)

### Fix: "unable to verify the first certificate"

- On some machines, especially with **Cursor**, every request failed with *Cannot connect to API: unable to verify the first certificate (UNABLE_TO_VERIFY_LEAF_SIGNATURE)*, and FreeAuto kept failing over from model to model.
- The cause: the Pliny gateway does not send its intermediate certificate. Windows fills it in automatically, but the extension's runtime (Node) does not, unless the editor passes it the Windows certificate store.
- PlinyCode now ships the public Synopsys CA certificates (SNPSica2 and SNPSOfflineCA). When a certificate check fails, it retries using them together with the Windows certificate store. This only adds trust; it never turns certificate checking off.
- **No `--use-system-ca` flag or `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` setup is needed.** If you set either as a workaround, you can remove it.

### Background tasks

- Starting a new task or opening another one from **History** no longer stops the task that is running. That task keeps going in the background (up to **3** at once).
- A background task applies edits without diff previews and does not bring its terminals to the front.
- Approvals and questions that are not auto-approved are held until you return. History marks the task **Needs approval**, and a notification with an **Open** button tells you.
- When a background turn finishes, the task stops and you get a notification. Reopening the task picks up the live session and replays anything that was held.
- Deleting the task, clearing history or shutting down stops background tasks. At the limit, the running task is stopped as before, with a notice.

### Send modes

- The send button's dropdown now **picks a mode** that stays selected, instead of sending straight away. The button shows that mode's icon, and **Enter** uses it.
  - **Send** - waits for the current turn to finish if the agent is busy.
  - **Send now** - interrupts the agent's current reply. Tools that are already running finish first.
  - **Schedule** - lets you pick a time to send the message.
- The mode you pick is remembered.

### FreeAuto routing improvements

- **`qwen3-coder-480b`** now comes first in the `coding` and `default` routes and in the fallback pool.
- **`GLM-5.2`** has been removed from `coding` and `default` because it is slow. It stays on the `huge-context` route, the only one that needs its 512k window.
- The `coding` route now also triggers on merge conflicts, rebase, lint errors and type errors.
- **Image requests fail immediately** with a clear message, since no free Pliny model accepts images. Pick a vision-capable model or remove the image.
- A custom `utility.summarizer` set in the rules file is now used. Before, it was silently ignored.

### Sub-agents (opt-in)

- New toggle: **Settings -> Features -> Advanced -> Sub-agents**. It is off by default and applies to new tasks.
- A new `subagent` route sends delegated work to fast models first (`qwen3-coder-480b`, `nemotron-3-super-120b`, `kimi-k2.6`).
- Chat rows for sub-agent calls start with `↳ sub-agent`. Sub-agent calls no longer reset the main task's routing state.
- The PlinyCode output channel logs when each sub-agent starts and finishes, with its token usage.

### Model picker

- Free self-hosted models and paid hosted models now have **separate checkboxes**, both off by default.
- **FreeAuto** is always visible and remains the default model.

### Clearer error messages

- **Max output tokens:** the error now names the model, the cap that was applied and which limit set it (setting, model limit, remaining context or default). It also shows input and context sizes, with a hint on what to change.
- **Aborted commands:** the error shows the command, its working directory and why it was aborted, and keeps any partial output.

### Terminal housekeeping

- Idle agent terminals are closed when a task ends, and at most 2 idle terminals are kept.
- Agent terminals are no longer restored after a window reload.
- Terminals that are running a command, or that you have typed into, are never closed.
- Running a command shows its terminal **without taking focus** from the editor.

### History

- The **workspace root** is shown for each task in History.
- You can now **edit the opening prompt** of a task and restart from it.

---

## Upgrade note: FreeAuto rules file

Your FreeAuto rules file (`~/.cline/data/pliny-free-auto.md`) is created only on first use and is **never overwritten**. If you are upgrading from 0.1.1, you will not get the new default routes above (qwen3-coder first, the `subagent` route, the new `coding` triggers) until you reset it:

1. If you customized the file, back it up.
2. Rename or delete it, then reload the window. PlinyCode writes a new file with the 0.1.2 defaults.
3. Copy your customizations back into the new file if you need them.

---

## Requirements

- VS Code `^1.101.0` or compatible **Cursor** build
- Network access to the Pliny gateway
- Git repository in the workspace for checkpoints and file-change summaries

---

## Build info

- Extension version: **0.1.2**
- Git branch: `lgiaccar/release_0_1_2` (from `stage` @ `d779b8b`)
- Commit: `f2b226f`
- Tag: `release_0.1.2`

## Why

The router models (`free-auto`, `-fast`, `-smart`, and `balance-auto` when it lands on a free model) end runs before the task is done, mostly right after shell commands. Nothing in the router decides when to stop: the agent loop ends a run on the first tool-free reply. The only safety net was a regex on the last sentence that never nudged twice in a row.

26 saved FreeAuto sessions had 71 run endings. 57 of them came right after a tool result, 44 of those after `run_commands`. The endings fall into these failure classes:

| Class | Example ending | Before |
|---|---|---|
| Announce-and-stop | "Let me check the current status of the benchmark runs:" | Caught, but kimi-k2.6 answered the nudge with the same line in 3 of 4 cases and the guard gave up |
| Wait/monitor bail-out (largest) | "I'll check again at **15:28**… Stand by!", "I cannot sit in the chat for 7–10 hours" | Missed — the model had no way to wait (`run_commands` detaches at 300 s) |
| Permission question for an action already requested | "Would you like me to run the benchmark now?" (6× in one fast session) | Missed by design |
| Readiness instead of action | "The benchmark is ready to run immediately…" after "build **and run**" | Missed |
| Leaked reasoning | 8k chars ending "…Hmm, but I just killed all PowerShell after 3:30 AM in" | Missed |
| Degenerate output | 14k chars of ` .   .   .` accepted as the final answer | Missed |

`free-auto-smart`'s classifier also produced **no verdict in any of 185 logged calls**, so smart behaved exactly like default. The likely cause is the default classifier model hitting the 256-token output cap before it got to the JSON.

## What changes

**Engine** (`shared`, `agents`, `core`): small and backward compatible
- `CompletionGuard` now also receives `runMessages` and `messages`, and may return a promise. `withHostCompletionGuard` awaits both guards.
- Guard reminders carry `displayRole: "system"`, so they no longer show up as user bubbles.
- The act and yolo prompts now say: "a reply with no tool call ends the task… never end a reply saying you will check back later; use `wait`".

**Extension router** (`apps/vscode/src/sdk/router`)
- `completion-guard.ts` (new) applies the rules from `unfinished-turn-guard.ts`, most reliable first: degenerate → after-failed-command → after-detached-command → announcement → wait-bail-out → leaked-reasoning → readiness → judge.
  - A second stall in a row gets a firmer reminder, and the rest of the turn moves to the default route's lead model (`↪ switching to …`). A third stall is accepted.
  - At most 3 reminders per run. Chat rows name the rule that fired (`rule: wait-bail-out, 1/3`).
- `router-completion-judge.ts` (new): once per act-mode run that has made at least one tool call, if no rule fired, the utility model is asked whether the request was carried out.
  - "Not done" sends one reminder (`⚖ The task looks unfinished — …`). No verdict means the reply is accepted.
  - Rules-file settings: `guard.judge`, `guard.judgeTimeoutMs`, `utility.judge` (defaults to the classifier model).
- `routed-agent-model.ts`: a reply that collapses into repetition is cut off mid-stream and the call fails, so the run continues on another model with a "redo the step" prompt.
- `router-prompt.ts` (new): free candidates get a system-prompt addendum about how their turn ends. Paid candidates see the prompt unchanged.
- `router-hooks.ts` (new) layers two hooks over the session's hook scripts:
  - `afterTool` appends a note to failed and detached shell results ("do not end your turn now: fix and rerun…").
  - `afterRun` writes one line per run to `pliny-free-auto-runs.jsonl`: how it ended, last model and tool, rules fired, judge verdict, reply tail.
- Classifier fixes:
  - Output cap raised to 512 tokens, and the prompt asks for the JSON first.
  - Parsing handles fenced JSON, nested objects and an unclosed `<think>`.
  - The raw reply is logged, and `classifierError` is recorded on the turn's first call.
- `scripts/summarize-free-auto-log.ts` reads both logs: run endings per profile/model/route, rules fired, the classifier's verdict rate, and `--tails`.

**`wait` tool** (`apps/vscode/src/sdk/vscode-wait-tool.ts`, registered for every session): up to 10 min per call and 1 h per run, and it can be cancelled. Its result tells the model to check progress with a tool call.

## BalanceAuto (merged from `stage`, #33)

Stage renamed the router helpers (`isPlinyRouterModelId`, `plinyRouterProfile`). Conflicts in `router-integration.ts`, `router-rules.ts` and `router-integration.test.ts` are resolved as follows:

- **One predicate, checked per turn.** The guard, the judge and the command note apply to a BalanceAuto turn only when a free model is answering.
- **The guard checks the main agent's last call.** Sub-agents get no completion policy, so the guard only ever judges the main agent's reply. Stage's version checked `activeTurnKey`, which after a sub-agent run points at the sub-agent. That would nudge a reply from a paid model because a free sub-agent ran earlier in the turn. Stage's BalanceAuto test is updated to that behaviour.
- **The command note follows whichever agent ran the tool.** New test added.

An audit of what goes into each model request found two problems. The context was growing with material the model no longer needed. Meanwhile, the content it did need was being cut. This PR fixes both. Pre-release: [0.1.7-test.6](https://github.com/lgiaccar/PlinyCode/releases/tag/release_0.1.7-test.6).

The router's timestamped status rows (`auto-free-smart → model (call N · route …)`) were already UI-only; they never reach the model. They are unchanged here.

## Engine

- **Old reasoning is no longer resent.** The openai-compatible provider sent every earlier turn's reasoning back as `reasoning_content` on every request.
  - Reasoning from before the current user turn is now dropped at request time (`prior-turn-reasoning.ts`, applied in the orchestrator's `beforeModel` and in the compaction size estimate). It stays in history for the UI.
  - Inline `<think>` blocks in earlier assistant text are stripped too.
  - Signed Anthropic thinking is kept.
  - Injected reminders don't count as a new turn: `isUserRunMessage` decides where a turn starts.
- **Whole tool results.** `MessageBuilder` cut every tool-result string to 8k characters (a 4k head and 4k tail), while the tools return and advertise ~48k.
  - The per-string cap is now 50k.
  - Several large entries in one result share a 64k budget, never below 8k each.
  - The cap depends only on the block's own content, so prefix caches are unaffected.
- **Plain-text tool output.** `read_files`, `run_commands` and `search_codebase` results (`{query,result,success}[]`) are sent as `<result query="…">` text, not JSON-escaped strings.
- **Earlier compaction for the routers.** Compaction reads the virtual router's `ModelInfo`, not the routed model's.
  - FreeAuto's `maxInputTokens` is now 92k, so it compacts at ~83k tokens: where the 128k tier stops fitting (`(128k − 32k) / 1.15`). It used to compact at ~230k.
  - BalanceAuto's is now 128k, so it compacts at ~115k instead of ~180k.
  - The advertised `contextWindow` values are unchanged.
- **Loop-detection notices reach the model.** The soft notice was appended to the `ConversationStore` and then overwritten by the next `replaceMessages`. It now goes through a new `consumeSystemNotice` runtime hook, as a `displayRole: "system"` message.

## Rules and skills

- **One editor's files.** A new `setInstructionHost({ editor, globalRulesDirectory })` in `shared/storage/paths.ts` narrows the rule and skill search paths.
  - VS Code gets `.github`, Cursor gets `.cursor`, Windsurf gets `.windsurfrules`.
  - `AGENTS.md`, `.clinerules`, `.cline`, `.agents` and `.claude` load everywhere.
  - The Rules panel uses the same resolvers, so it follows too.
- **One global rules folder.** `Documents/Cline/Rules` is now the only global rules folder.
  - `~/.cline/rules` is no longer read. Its files are moved to `Documents/Cline/Rules` at activation, keeping their toggles. Name clashes are left in place and logged.
  - `~/Cline/Rules` and the OneDrive guesses are dropped when the host sets the folder.
- **Scoped rules on demand.** Rules with globs, `applyTo:` or `alwaysApply: false` are listed by path for the model to read when they apply, instead of being inlined in full.
- **Size caps.** Always-on rules are capped at 12k characters each and 40k in total; the overflow is listed by path.
- The system prompt names the real editor instead of always saying "VS Code".

## Extension

- **Mention caps.**
  - `@file` is capped at 100k characters (was 400 KB).
  - `@folder` is capped at 100k characters in total; files past that are named, not pasted.
  - `@url` is capped at 50k.
  - The truncation notice now names tools that exist.
- **DevOps MCP tools only where they work.** They are offered only when the session's repo has a GitHub or Azure DevOps remote (`BuiltinMcpSource.appliesTo`).

## Testing

- New tests:
  - `prior-turn-reasoning.test.ts`
  - message-builder caps
  - `formatToolOperationResultsAsText`
  - router compaction budget
  - rule budgets and scoped listing
  - `setInstructionHost` paths
  - loop-notice hand-off
  - `instruction-sources.test.ts` (editor detection, `~/.cline/rules` move)
  - `hasSupportedRemote`
  - a folder-mention budget test (mocha, integration host)
- Engine suites pass, except the hook-file and MCP-client tests, which also fail locally on unmodified `stage` (they spawn bash and child processes).
- Extension unit tests pass, except the hook tests (the same environment issue, also failing on `stage`) and the DevOps tool tests. The DevOps tool tests only fail because the local shell sets `DEVOPS_MCP_PROVIDER=ado`; they pass with it unset.
- `bun run types`: the engine packages and the extension `src` pass. The webview has React-types errors locally, and they also appear on unmodified `stage`.
- Lint, format, knip (`analyze:unused:prod`) and `check:docs` all pass.

## What changes

Plan mode now writes its plan as markdown files that the user can edit, and adds an **Execute plan** button that runs the plan in act mode.

- **Plan files.** The agent writes the root file `plans/<slug>/PLAN.md` first. It holds the goal, context, ordered steps, verification, and links to sub-files. Large parts of a plan go in sub-files next to it, such as `plans/<slug>/01-backend.md`. On feedback, the agent updates the existing files. The turn ends with a short summary that names the root file.
- **Markdown-only writes.** The plan tool preset now turns the `editor` on. The existing plan-mode `beforeTool` guard (`command-guard-extension.ts`) also rejects any `editor` or `apply_patch` write to a non-markdown path before approval, and that includes sub-agents. Shell commands that edit files are still blocked. Allowed `.md` writes go through the normal edit approval and the **Edit files** auto-approve toggle.
- **Execute plan button.** `planFiles.ts` finds the root file from the turn's markdown editor rows: the latest `PLAN.md`, otherwise the first `.md` file written. The plan row then shows a link that opens the file, plus an **Execute plan** button. The button appears only while the extension is in plan mode and the row is the latest result. It calls `togglePlanActModeProto(ACT)` with the message `execute the plan in <root file>`, and the mode coordinator sends that message as the act-mode continuation, so no new RPC is needed.
- **Docs.** `docs/plan-mode.md` describes the design, and the root `AGENTS.md` links to it.

## Pre-release

`0.1.7-test.11` is published as a GitHub pre-release: https://github.com/lgiaccar/PlinyCode/releases/tag/release_0.1.7-test.11

## Tests

- Engine:

- Not yet checked by hand in a dev host: writing a plan, editing it, then clicking Execute plan.

hits.body:
## Why

On FreeAuto, Kimi K2.6 kept stopping for no visible reason: it announced a step and ended the turn, or it called tools that "do not exist":

```
Tool call  functions-read-files-5-w53hn3x5d032008 {"files": [...]} <|tool_call_end|> <|tool_calls_section_end|>
was rejected before execution: no tool is named " functions-read-files-5-…
```

The cause is the tool-call ids in the history PlinyCode sends.

Kimi writes a call as `<|tool_call_begin|>functions.read_files:3<|tool_call_argument_begin|>{…}`. The id holds the tool's name and a running index, and the model's chat template shows it its earlier calls by that id. Since 0.1.5-test.7 (#56), `withSafeToolCallIds` rewrites every id on the wire to `[a-zA-Z0-9-]` plus a hash, because Claude on Bedrock rejects anything else. Kimi therefore read its own earlier calls as `functions-read-files-3-9tb01v` and imitated that. Its server could no longer parse the result, and the call reached us in one of three ways:

- glued into the tool name, with empty arguments (the error above)
- as raw tokens in the reply text
- not at all, which is the "announced a step and stopped" the completion guard kept catching

## Measurement

`apps/vscode/scripts/probe-kimi-tool-call-ids.ts` replays one history (six earlier calls, the next step is clearly another call) against `snps-provider/kimi-k2.6` with three id styles, 24 runs each:

| Ids in the history | Usable tool call |
| --- | --- |
| rewritten for Bedrock, as sent until 0.1.7-test.9 | 6 / 24 |
| another model's ids (`call-…`, `toolu-…`) | 17 / 24 |
| Kimi's own, `functions.<tool>:<index>` | 23 / 24 |

The one miss in the last row was a direct answer, not a broken call.

## What changes

All Kimi handling is in the new `sdk/packages/llms/src/providers/kimi-tool-calls.ts`, and applies only to Kimi models (`isKimiModel`: family or model id contains `kimi`, since the Pliny catalog gives its self-hosted models no family).

- **Kimi's history carries its own ids.** `withKimiToolCallIds` renumbers every call in the outgoing request as `functions.<tool>:<index>`, whichever model made it, and its tool result with it. `withSafeToolCallIds` skips requests whose model is Kimi. Stored messages keep their ids; other models get exactly what they got before.
- **A call glued into the tool name is taken apart.** `repairMalformedToolCall` reads the tool and the JSON arguments out of the name when the call's own arguments are empty. `resolveMisnamedTool` (moved here from `ai-sdk-message-convert.ts`) also resolves a call id (`functions.read_files:3`, `functions-read-files-5-w53hn3x`) and camelCase (`readFiles`) to the tool.
- **A call left in the reply text is run.** Text from `<|tool_call` on is held back while streaming. When the reply ends normally, the calls that name an available tool and carry JSON arguments are emitted as tool calls and the section is not shown. If no call can be read from it, or the reply failed or was aborted, the text is shown as it arrived.
- **Shorter unknown-tool error.** It quotes at most 80 characters of the name, without control tokens, so the model is not handed two more copies of the bad call.
- **Guard.** `endsWithPlanList` now catches an announced action followed by the things it applies to ("Let me read:" and a list of files). That was the second stall in the reported conversation, which went unnoticed. "Let me summarize:" plus a list is still accepted as an answer.

`docs/pliny-free-auto-router.md` has a new section, "Kimi and tool-call ids".

## Tests

- `kimi-tool-calls.test.ts` (new) uses the names, ids and text exactly as they arrived in real sessions:
  - name resolution, with negatives (`chatcmpl-tool-…`, `read_files_v2`, two tools that read the same without separators)
  - taking a glued call apart, and keeping the call's own arguments when it has any
  - id renumbering: reused ids, orphaned results, stored messages untouched
  - the text filter at delta sizes 1, 7 and 1000; several calls; garbage shown as text; nothing run from a failed reply
  - the real adapter against a fake gateway: a glued call runs, a leaked call runs and is hidden, a non-Kimi model gets the text and the ids unchanged, Kimi gets `functions.run_commands:0 … functions.read_files:3` on the wire
- `tool-call-ids.test.ts`: Kimi requests keep their ids; the same history to another model is still rewritten.
- `unfinished-turn-guard.test.ts`: the real stalled reply is flagged; two answer-with-a-list replies are not.

`bun -F @plinycode/llms test`: 724 passed. Extension `src/sdk` vitest: 1204 passed. `bun run types`, `check:docs` and `analyze:unused:prod` are clean.

Not run in a dev host: the fix is verified by the tests and by the probe against the live gateway, not by a full agent session in the editor.

## FreeAuto: reasoning effort, classifier, profiles and call log

Commit `57555a4` on `lgiaccar/few_impr`

### Why
FreeAuto picked a model per call, but it never controlled *how much the model thinks*. Small edits and deep planning got the same treatment. Several free models turned out to reason on every call, which is slow, and there was no way to compare routing strategies on real use.

### What changed

**Measured reasoning controls**
- `probe-pliny-free-models.ts --thinking` asks every free model a short trick question with six variants of the request. It records whether the model reasons by default and which request field turns reasoning on or off. Results are in `docs/pliny-free-auto-thinking.md`.
- Findings:
  - GLM-5.2, nemotron-3-super, qwen3.5-397b and the qwen3-27b family reason by default. `chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking=false` turns this off.
  - qwen3-coder, kimi-k2.6 and nemotron-3-ultra never reason.
  - qwen3-8-27b, qwen2.5-32b and llama-3.1-70b answer `reasoning_effort` with a **400**. Sending a generic "think" flag to them fails the call.
- These results are stored per model in `pliny-models.json`. A new Pliny provider-option rule sends only the off-switch the probe measured for that model. Models without a measured switch are left alone.

**Reasoning effort per route**
- Routes accept `effort: quick | think` and `reasoningEffort: low | medium | high`.
- Defaults: planning uses think/high. Coding, quick questions, sub-agents and huge-context use quick. The default route leaves each model's own behaviour.
- The routing row shows what was applied, for example `route: coding · quick`.

**Classifier (smart profile)**
- A small, fast model (qwen3-6-35b, which never reasons) runs once per turn. It returns `{tier: quick|code|reason|huge, think: bool}`.
- The tier maps to a route through the rules file, so the classifier never names a model. Its think verdict overrides the route's effort.
- It doesn't run for sub-agents or requests with images. If it times out or returns an unusable reply, the heuristic routes decide.

**Profiles**
Three FreeAuto models in the picker, each with its own rules file:
- `FreeAuto`: heuristic routes with effort set per route.
- `FreeAuto · fast`: reasoning off everywhere it can be turned off.
- `FreeAuto · smart`: the default routes plus the classifier.

**Call log**
- Every routed call is appended to `~/.cline/data/pliny-free-auto-calls.jsonl`. Each entry has the profile, route, tier, effort, model, estimated tokens, time to first token, duration and outcome.
- `bun apps/vscode/scripts/summarize-free-auto-log.ts` compares profiles and models.
- New command: **PlinyCode: Open FreeAuto Call Log**.

**Also**
- Fixed the generated rules file. Its regexes were written in double-quoted YAML, which made the file invalid, so FreeAuto silently ignored it. They're now single-quoted, and a test checks that the generated YAML parses.
- Sub-agents are now on by default.

### Known limitation
The engine can only turn reasoning on through `reasoning_effort`. A model whose only on-switch is the chat template can't be made to think. The only such model (gemma-4-31b-it-29cea) isn't used by any route.

### Testing
- Extension vitest: 1380 passing. Engine `llms`: 755 passing. The bun unit suite passes.
- `bun run types` and `bun run lint` are clean.
- The thinking probe was run against the live gateway.
- Not yet tried in a live chat.

### To try it
1. Pick `FreeAuto · fast` or `FreeAuto · smart` in the model picker.
2. Watch the routing rows in the chat.
3. After a few sessions, run the summarize script to compare profiles.

  - **Bug fixed in core:** the async path took the lock, returned, and ran the mutation only after the `await` resumed, so a second update started in the same window during that gap was rejected as "Reentrant MCP settings update" instead of waiting. ## Summary

PlinyCode now **ships a built-in MCP server** that lets an agent create and update pull requests and report CI pipeline runs on **GitHub** (Actions) and **Azure DevOps** (Repos + Pipelines). Users need no repository checkout, Python or Node. The server is bundled with the extension (`dist/devops-mcp.js`) and runs on the editor's own runtime (`ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1`).

The first version of this PR was a standalone Python tool in `tools/devops-mcp`. It's replaced by this TypeScript port, with the same tools and behaviour.

## Where it shows up

- **PlinyCode's agent:** its tools are available automatically, and follow the normal MCP approval setting.
- **Copilot Chat (VS Code):** registered through VS Code's MCP server definition provider API, as **PlinyCode DevOps**.
- **Cursor's agent:** registered through `vscode.cursor.mcp.registerServer`, as `plinycode-devops`.
- **MCP Servers view:** a new **PlinyCode DevOps** card shows status and tool count, with on/off and restart. Expanded, it covers sign-in, step-by-step use from Copilot Chat or Cursor, and **Copy MCP config** for any other client.

## Tools

`repo_context` · `pr_create` (draft by default; refuses branches that aren't pushed or already have a PR) · `pr_get` · `pr_update` (whole description, or one `<!-- devops-mcp:name -->` section) · `pipeline_runs` · `pipeline_report` (failed steps, errors, and the log lines around the failure) · `pr_checks`. ADO's 4000-character description limit is enforced with a clear message.

## Sign-in

It tries, in order:
1. `GITHUB_TOKEN` / `AZURE_DEVOPS_PAT`
2. the editor's existing GitHub / Microsoft session
3. `gh` / `az` login
4. the editor's sign-in prompt, the first time a tool needs it

Steps 2 and 4 use a per-window local pipe (`token-broker.ts`) with a random secret, because the server runs in its own process and can't call `vscode.authentication`.

## Design notes

- **Kept separate:** the code is confined to `src/services/devops-mcp/`. `server/` has no `vscode` import and is its own esbuild bundle. The built-in server lives beside McpHub, not in it, so the user's `cline_mcp_settings.json` is never modified.
- **No `vscode` import in shared code:** `builtin-mcp-registry.ts` lets the SDK session code and the gRPC handlers reach the service without importing `vscode`, because both are also compiled into the standalone build.
- **Changes outside the folder:** three small hooks in `vscode-runtime-builder.ts`, `sdk-tool-policies.ts` and `SdkController.ts`, which add the tools, set their approval policy, and reload tools when the server starts or stops. There are also 4 RPCs in `mcp.proto`.
- **Settings:** `plinycode.devops.enabled` and `plinycode.devops.registerWithEditor`, both on by default.
- **Version:** bumped to **0.1.3-test.5**.
- **Docs:** `docs/devops-mcp.md`.

## Testing

- 35 new `bun:test` tests covering both providers, remote parsing, section editing, log excerpts, the tool guards against a temporary git repo, and the broker protocol. The full extension unit suite passes (1226 tests), and so does `check-types`.
- The bundled server runs under both `Code.exe` and `Cursor.exe`. It worked live against this repo, including a report on a real failed e2e run.
- **VS Code dev host (fresh profile):** logs `Running with 7 tools` and `Registered with the editor (vscode)`.
- **Cursor dev host (fresh profile):** Cursor's MCP log shows `Successfully connected to stdio server` for `extension-plinycode-devops`.
- **Not yet checked by hand:** the card in the GUI, a tool call approved from PlinyCode chat, the editor sign-in prompt, and Azure DevOps against a live org.

## After merge

Publish the pre-release (`release_0.1.3-test.5`, `bun run release:publish -- --prerelease`) so test installs update.

## Summary
Improvements to PlinyCode's chat input, its error messages, its terminal handling, and running several tasks at once.

### Background tasks
Starting a new task, or opening another task from History, no longer stops a task that is still running. The running task moves to the background (at most 3 at a time).
- **While in the background:**
  - Its output isn't shown. The SDK still saves its conversation.
  - Its edits are written without diff previews.
  - Its terminals don't pop up.
  - Its token usage is still recorded.
- **History badges:** background tasks show **Running**, or **Needs approval** when waiting on the user.
- **Approvals and questions:** anything that isn't auto-approved is held until the user reopens the task. A notification with an **Open** button tells the user.
- **When it finishes:** the task is stopped and the user gets a notification ("finished", "stopped with an error" or "was stopped").
- **Reopening a running task** takes over its live session and shows the held approval or question. There is no Resume button.
- **Stopping:** deleting a task, deleting all history, or shutting down stops background tasks. At the limit, the running task is stopped as before and a message says so.

### Send button modes
- The dropdown now picks a **mode** that is remembered, instead of sending immediately:
  - **Send**: waits for the current turn if the agent is busy.
  - **Send now**: interrupts the current reply.
  - **Schedule**: sends at a chosen time.
- The button icon shows the selected mode, and Enter uses it.
- **Queue** was removed because it did exactly what Send does.

### Clearer error messages
- **Max output tokens:** the error now names the model, the tokens produced, the cap and what set it (Max Tokens setting, model limit, remaining context window or 32k default), and the input and context-window sizes. It ends with a matching hint. The gateway now reports the cap it applied on max-tokens finishes.
- **Aborted commands:** the error now names the command, the working directory and why it stopped (cancelled by user / task stopped or switched / repeated errors). Output produced before the abort is kept.

### Terminals
- Terminals evicted from reuse were never closed. They are now closed once nothing is running in them.
- Idle terminals are closed when a task ends, at most 2 idle terminals are kept, and agent terminals aren't restored after a window reload.
- Terminals running a command, terminals the user has typed into, and SSH sessions are never closed automatically.
- Running a command shows the terminal without moving focus to it.

### Fix
- The FreeAuto router model now has zero pricing. Without it, the engine test for self-hosted pricing failed.

## Known limitations
- Reopening a task partway through a reply: text already streamed appears once that text block ends.
- Two tasks editing the same files at once aren't coordinated.
- Reusing an idle terminal for a background task can still reveal the terminal panel. It never takes focus.

## Testing
- `bun run types` and `bun run lint` pass.
- Extension tests: vitest 1,304 and bun unit 1,151 pass.
- Webview tests: 522 pass.
- Terminal tests in a real VS Code host (`vscode-test`): 20 pass.
- Engine: `shared`, `llms`, `agents`, core tool tests and the Node smoke test pass.
- New tests cover the background registry, detach/adopt/reattach, holding and replaying approvals, send modes, the cap source, aborted-command details and terminal cleanup.
- **Manual check:**
  1. Start a long task, click New Task and start another; History shows **Running**.
  2. Approve a held tool from the notification.
  3. Set Max Tokens low and check the new error text.
  4. Cancel a long command and check it is named in the error.

### Description

Adds the standalone PlinyCode CLI for terminal conversations and invocation from existing YAML pipelines or Python. `run` accepts prompts/files/stdin, validates caller-supplied JSON schemas, streams JSON events, and reports generated artifacts. Omitting `--model` now selects FreeAuto; explicit concrete models remain supported. MCP configuration supports stdio/SSE/HTTP, credentials use secure local storage or CI injection, and unattended tools require explicit opt-in.

FreeAuto shares the extension's built-in routing policy, defaults and stream guards through an engine module. It uses only free models, bounds failover, stops on authentication errors/cancellation, and prevents replay after partial output. A single tool-free schema repair tries a different free model. The extraction also fixes streamed authentication errors being treated as retryable model failures.

Portable Windows/Linux x64 packages include the pinned Bun runtime. Chat retains history while running and exports transcripts. There is no server, YAML job parser, persistent resume, extension memory import, or full-screen UI. Only the default FreeAuto profile is included; extension completion/reviewer passes and router-settings import remain deferred.

Roadmap A9 (docs/roadmap.md). Fixes three ways usage went missing from a conversation's cost, and splits the token panel's side usage by source.

**Root causes found**
1. Sub-agent events carried no agent id, so the engine added a sub-agent's usage to the root's turn usage and then dropped it at turn end (the end-of-turn total is rebuilt from the root's own result). Sub-agent usage only came back on resume, through the message files; a failed or timed-out sub-agent persisted no messages, so its cost was lost for good.
2. Background tasks expected `parentAgentId` on sub-agent events, never got it, and counted sub-agents twice (usage events plus tool-result totals).
3. The engine and the extension both write `metadata.totalCost`; the engine's root-only write at turn end could land last and drop advisor, compaction and sub-agent cost from the history list (the task header was unaffected: it sums chat rows).

**Engine:** the progress reporter tags forwarded events with `agentId`/`parentAgentId` (`spawn_agent` and `subagent_<name>`). A finished or failed sub-agent's totals (output figures on success, progress sums on failure) are settled into the session's aggregate under its id (`settleSubAgentUsage`), so it counts once, including after a resume. A turn that throws still persists the usage it built up.

**Extension:** advisor and compaction usage live under `extraUsage`, which the engine never writes. The history list (and the cost/token sorts) reads the engine's aggregate plus `extraUsage`, or the extension's running totals when larger, so history matches the header. Old sessions read as before. Background tasks also record compaction usage.

**Token panel:** Sub-agents, Advisor and Compaction each get a labelled line (×N, tokens, cost).

Docs: advisor-tool (race caveat replaced; a narrower background-task window remains, documented), prompt-cache, agent-tools, context-compaction.

Tests: 4 new core tests (counted once with repeated end and late events; settled from the result; kept when the turn fails; resume + re-aggregation does not double count), 2 spawn-tool tests, 4 history tests (history total == header total whichever write lands last; background advisor cost survives; old sessions), coordinator/background updates, panel tests. build:sdk, types, lint, format, check-types, test:vitest, test:webview, test:discovery, knip, check:docs pass; core test:unit has only the 5 pre-existing local-environment failures.

## Summary

Four chat and cost fixes. The cache fix matters most, because it cuts paid BalanceAuto cost.

### 1. Prompt cache for paid Claude models (BalanceAuto)

**Evidence.** I joined 167 local sessions' per-message `metrics` with `pliny-free-auto-calls.jsonl` to see which model served each call:

- **Sonnet 5, when it writes no text between tool calls (the usual case).** Every call reads exactly the system prompt (13,022 tokens) and writes 0, while input grows from 44K to 128K tokens. Session `1791958896107_yy670` paid $5.00 where $1.39 was needed. Across all cache-enabled Claude calls, about half the input spend was wasted.
- **`aws-bedrock-vmodels/claude-4-6-sonnet-*-thinking` (BalanceAuto's planning route).** 0% cache reads and 0% writes, on every version.

**Root causes**

- `withContentBlockCacheBreakpoints` only marked user/assistant text. A tool-only assistant turn goes out as `content: null`, so the moving breakpoint fell back to the prompt that opened the turn. The function hasn't changed since #41. Hit rates swung with how much the model narrates: Sonnet 4.6 narrates more than Sonnet 5, so it hit more often.
- The thinking presets had no `cache_control` in `pliny-models.json`, so no breakpoints were sent for them at all.

**Fixes**

- Breakpoints now go on three places:
  - the system prompt
  - the newest message, usually the latest tool result, as a content-block marker on the tool message
  - the end of the previous step, so the previous call's cache entry is found even beyond Anthropic's 20-block lookback
- I measured on the live gateway that it honours a content-block marker on a tool message. It drops message-level markers, which the old comment had generalised to all tool-message markers.
- The thinking presets are flagged `cache_control`, with Sonnet cache prices. Both cache on the gateway, and its `costInUSD` matches $0.30 read / $3.75 write per million tokens.

**Live gateway, Sonnet 5, 4 agent steps** (`apps/vscode/scripts/probe-pliny-prompt-cache.ts`):

| step | legacy read / write | fixed read / write | uncached tokens (fixed) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 0 / 4,570 | 0 / 6,796 | 2 |
| 2 | 4,570 / 0 | 6,796 / 2,222 | 2 |
| 3 | 4,570 / 0 | 9,018 / 2,222 | 2 |
| 4 | 4,570 / 0 | 11,240 / 2,222 | 2 |

**Free models.** They report `cached_tokens: 0` from the backend. Parsing is correct, and they cost $0, so I left them unchanged.

**Follow-up, not done here.** `dropPriorTurnReasoning` rewrites the previous turn's unsigned reasoning at each new user turn. Now that the thinking presets are cached, that costs one cache miss per user turn on them.

### 2. Token usage panel (task header, under the context bar)

- **Bars:** one stacked bar per LLM call (cache read / cache write / input / output) for the last 80 calls. Hovering a bar shows that call. The colours are categorical slots that pass a colour-blindness check on VS Code's dark surface; on light mode the legend and text labels carry the values.
- **Summary:**
  - models, with call counts
  - calls and cost (shown only where the provider shows cost)
  - In, Out and Reason tokens
  - Cache R, W and hit rate
  - a line for sub-agent and advisor usage
- **Data plumbing:**
  - `routed-agent-model.ts` tags usage events with the model that served the call.
  - `AgentTokenUsage.modelId` carries it into saved message metrics. The live usage event's `reasoningTokens` and `modelId` go to `ClineApiReqInfo`, and history replay reads both back.
  - Older conversations show the router's own name.

### 3. Prompt navigation arrows

**Causes of the misses and no-ops**

- Prev/next used Virtuoso's `rangeChanged.startIndex`. That index includes the 3000px `increaseViewportBy` band above the view, so it pointed well above what the user was looking at.
- Prev/next never disabled auto-scroll, so streaming pulled the view back to the bottom.
- The scroll-to-bottom button mounted and unmounted, which shifted the stack under the cursor.

**Fix**

- Prev/next now read the top row from the DOM.
- They disable auto-scroll.
- They step from the last target while a smooth scroll is still running.
- They use `align: start` under the sticky header, and jump without animation to rows that aren't rendered.
- Prev above the first prompt goes to the top; Next past the last prompt goes to the bottom.
- The buttons sit in fixed slots: top, prev, next, bottom. The bottom button is hidden, not unmounted.
- The scroll listener does one layout read per frame. The scrollbar marker highlight uses the same top row.

### 4. Reloaded conversations lose prompt highlighting

- Replaying all local sessions found no case where a typed prompt became agent text. What does go missing on reload is any user text that is persisted only inside a tool result:
  - answers to `ask_question`
  - feedback typed when rejecting a tool
- Both are now rebuilt on replay, as the live path shows them: `ask:"followup"` with `selected` set, then `user_feedback` with `answersTool` set.
- A `say:"task"` row inside the list now renders with the prompt frame instead of as markdown.
- Not fixed: the session-start sanitizer can drop message metadata and merge user blocks. The safe fix is to keep each non-tool-result user message separate; that is left for a follow-up.

## Testing

- `bun run types`, `bun run lint`, `bun run format`, `bun run check:docs` and `analyze:unused:prod` pass.
- **llms:** 737 passed (the one failure was the preset-cache test; it is now updated). **shared:** 373 passed.
- **core:** 1,660 passed. 5 tests fail locally, in `hook-file-hooks` and `mcp/client`. Their temp `.js` fixtures hit Node 26 ESM `require`; this is an environment issue in untouched code.
- **Extension vitest:** 1,739 passed. **Webview vitest:** 579 passed.
- **Extension bun unit suite:** passes except the `src/core/hooks/__tests__` files, which fail with the same hook-script environment issue.
- **New tests:**
  - breakpoint placement
  - catalog cache flags
  - adapter reasoning and modelId
  - router usage tagging
  - replay of answers and rejection feedback
  - prompt navigation against a DOM fixture
  - fixed button slots
  - token panel and its helpers
- Live-gateway probe as in the table above.
- Not yet checked in the dev host.

## What changes

**A budget for each conversation.** The spending limit was one global number. Every conversation now has its own budget, shown next to its cost in the task header as `$cost / $budget`.

- Click the budget to change it for that conversation only. Enter or blur saves, Escape cancels, 0 means no limit. It turns red once the cost reaches it.
- It is stored as `spendingLimit` on the conversation's history record (session metadata). It survives resume and edit-and-regenerate, and writes that don't set it keep it. New RPC: `TaskService.setTaskSpendingLimit`.
- `plinycode.spending.conversationLimit` (Settings → General, now labeled "Default conversation budget") is the budget a conversation starts with. It is also the step a pause raises the budget by: at the budget, the run pauses as before, and the new budget is the amount spent plus one step, rounded up to the cent. Sending a message continues, and the header shows the new budget. This replaces the old in-memory threshold, which you couldn't see.
- **Free models are never limited.** When the active mode's model is free (a self-hosted `snps-provider*` model or an `auto-free*` router), the guard is skipped and the header shows no budget. `auto-paid-balanced` can call paid models, so it keeps a budget.

**DevOps MCP: publish a draft PR.** `pr_update` takes `draft`. `false` marks a draft PR ready for review, and `true` converts it back. Until now the agent had to ask the user to click Publish in the web UI.

- Azure DevOps: `isDraft` in the PR PATCH.
- GitHub: the REST API ignores `draft` on update. The server calls the GraphQL `markPullRequestReadyForReview` / `convertPullRequestToDraft` mutations (`api.github.com/graphql`, or `<host>/api/graphql` on GHES), and only when the status actually changes. GraphQL errors come back with HTTP 200, so the response body is checked for errors.
- The server instructions and `docs/devops-mcp.md` describe the new option.

Roadmap A11 (docs/roadmap.md).

**Before:** an image attached to a FreeAuto conversation made the router filter its candidates to image-capable models; no free model is one, so every call failed ("auto-free has no model that accepts images…"), and kept failing for the rest of the conversation because the image stays in the history. Images returned by tools reached free models as placeholders.

**Now** (`sdk/router/router-images.ts`, hooked into `routed-agent-model.ts`): a call with images is routed as if it had none. An image-capable model gets the request untouched; any other model gets a copy where each image (image parts and images inside tool results) is replaced by text. The stored conversation never changes. Setting `plinycode.router.images`:
- `describe` (default): each new image is described once by the cheapest image-capable catalog model (free preferred; today Claude Haiku 4.5, about $0.004 an image), cached per conversation by SHA-256, at most 8 new images per call; the model sees `<image_description sha="…">…</image_description>`. A first-time notice row says which model described it.
- `vision-model`: a turn that brings a new image runs on the image-capable model (route `images`); later turns use descriptions.
- `off`: the image is replaced by a note; nothing is spent.

**Paid-model gating:** paid models are used on BalanceAuto always, and on FreeAuto only when **Unlock Pliny paid models** is on. That toggle lived only in webview localStorage; it is now mirrored to the extension (`UpdateSettingsRequest` field 52, `plinyPaidModelsUnlocked`). Otherwise `describe`/`vision-model` fall back to `off` with a chat row explaining how to unlock. **Decision to confirm:** with paid unlocked, FreeAuto now spends a little on image descriptions by default (budget-checked, shown in the chat); set `off` to keep FreeAuto strictly free.

**Cost accounting:** checked against the conversation budget like the advisor; recorded as `subagent_usage` rows with `source: "vision"` (task header, history `extraUsage.vision`, an "Image descriptions" line in the token panel; background tasks too). The advisor's one-shot call helpers moved to `sdk/one-shot-model-call.ts` and are shared. The FreeAuto profiles now declare image input, so the prompt box no longer warns.

**New `view_image({ path })` tool:** PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP files inside the session's working directory (symlinks resolved, type detected from bytes), up to 3.75 MB; read approval, parallel; sub-agents and CI Board runs get it.

Docs: Images section in `pliny-free-auto-router.md`, `view_image` in `agent-tools.md`; small updates to `pliny-balance-auto.md`, `advisor-tool.md`.

Tests: scripted-model router tests (describe, cache, cost, vision-model, off, paid-locked fallback, budget refusal, untouched pass-through), 2 router-integration image tests, `view_image` tests. check-types, lint, format, test:vitest (1984), test:webview (622), test:unit (987), test:discovery, knip, build:sdk, types, llms tests (739), check:docs pass.

Live check pending: a real pasted screenshot on FreeAuto with paid unlocked and locked, `vision-model`, BalanceAuto's coding route with an image, `view_image` on a PNG.
