## What changes

**New**
- **Per-conversation spending limit.** New `plinycode.spending.conversationLimit` setting (default $5; 0 turns it off), also editable in Settings → General. Before each model call, if the conversation has spent the limit, the run stops and a message says what was spent and how to continue. Sending a message allows another round of the same amount. It works like the mistake limit: no blocking prompt while the agent loop is live.
- **Pliny budget display.** A new `getPlinyBudget` RPC reads `/api/svc/v1/llm-gateway/budgets/my-usage` with the same key and host as chat requests. The binding budget (the period with the least money left) shows under the home screen header and in the task header's expanded details. It turns red at 90% used or when the gateway reports the budget as blocked. It only shows while Pliny is the active provider, and refetches at most once a minute.
- **Conversation title in the task header.** The title is centered, with the workspace name (`parent/folder`) under it in smaller text, whether the header is collapsed or expanded.

**Fixes**
- **History cost differed from the conversation's cost.** Several writers raced on the history record: rename, favorite and active-time writes put back stale totals, and per-event deltas collided with the engine's own end-of-turn total. The history record now stores the same totals the task header computes (`getConversationApiMetrics`), and only usage writes can change them.
- **Claude on Bedrock rejected tool-call ids** (`tool_use.id: String should match pattern '^[a-zA-Z0-9-]+$'`). Mixed routing leaves ids such as `call_…`, `functions.x:0` or `tool_<nanoid>` in history. The OpenAI-compatible request body now rewrites every `tool_calls[].id` and `tool_call_id` to a deterministic, valid id, so each call and its result still match. Stored history keeps the original ids.
- **File paths in answers didn't open.** Absolute paths in plain text (e.g. `d:\…\report.md`, `/home/me/x.py`) and backslash or absolute paths in backticks now become "open in editor" links. Absolute paths open even with no workspace folder.
- **Scheduled prompts use a 24-hour clock.** The picker is a date field plus 00–23 hour and minute selects, defaulting to the next 5-minute mark at least 5 minutes out. The scheduled list shows 24-hour times.

## Tests
- New: `tool-call-ids.test.ts`, an `openai-compatible` wire test, `plinyBudget.test.ts`, `spending-limit.test.ts`, `scheduleTime.test.ts` and `filePathDetection.test.ts`. The history and event-coordinator tests are extended for the usage totals.
- Locally, these all pass: `bun run types`, lint, format, the full llms suite (787) and the extension `src/sdk` vitest suites (1410+).
- These fail locally on unchanged code too, so they are environmental:
  - React component tests in the webview (Bun 1.4.2 here vs the pinned 1.3.x)
  - hook-script tests (a stray `package.json` in `%TEMP%`)
  - DevOps `tools.test.ts`, which came from #54

CI runs the pinned toolchain.

Fifth and last wave of the context-management audit (`docs/context-management-audit.md`), stacked on #127; retarget to `stage` once that merges. Memory, past-conversation search and project knowledge. New doc: `docs/rules.md`, linked from `AGENTS.md`.

## Changes

- **Per-directory agent guides reach the model.** Only the root `AGENTS.md` was read, so this repository's own `apps/vscode/AGENTS.md` and `sdk/AGENTS.md` never did. `discoverNestedGuideFiles` finds `AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md` below the root (depth 3, dependency/build/hidden folders skipped, at most 30, shallowest first). They are listed by path, never inlined: a nested guide is scoped to its folder (`apps/vscode/**`) unless it sets a scope; a root `CLAUDE.md` is listed "read when AGENTS.md does not answer something".
- **The workspace `AGENTS.md` is inlined first.** Rules were sorted by name, so `a-style.md` could push `AGENTS.md` out of the 40k budget.
- **Search filters by workspace in the index.** The engine stores and queries normalized roots (slashes, case on Windows), so other workspaces no longer crowd this one out of the candidate list; the extension passes the folder through. `<editor_state>`/`<mode_notice>` blocks are left out of the index and of `read_conversation` (index version 4).
- **Memory budget accounting.** The instruction block, the topic list (now capped at 12 per memory with a count of the rest) and the "N more entries" note come out of `plinycode.memory.maxTokens`; the context row uses the same three characters per token.
- **Distillation remembers.** Progress and dismissed/unchecked memories are stored in `memory/distill/<conversation>.json`, so a reload neither re-reads the whole conversation nor proposes a turned-down memory again. Proposals are compared as whole entries (`memoryEntryKeys`) rather than substrings.
- **Cross-window memory writes** hold `<file>.lock` (exclusive create, stale after 10 s, best-effort after 2 s), so two windows saving at once no longer lose an entry.
- **`/remember` while memory is off** expands into a note telling the model memory is off, instead of instructions to call a tool the session lacks.

## Verification

- `bun run check`, `bun run check:docs`, knip: pass.
- Core: 1675 pass; the same 5 environment-only failures as before. Extension vitest: 1746 pass.
- New tests: `nested-guides.test.ts` (discovery, scope, prompt rendering and order), core search (normalized roots, editor state), `memory-section.test.ts` budget, coordinator persistence across a reload, whole-entry dedupe, two-store concurrent saves and stale lock, `/remember` while off, search adapter passes the folder and strips editor state.

## Why

The benchmark session exported as `plinycode-hanging-conversation-20260925-0819.md` (FreeAuto·smart, GPUSurfer) stalled six times. Reading it against the call log, the catalog and the thinking probe data showed four distinct causes. This PR fixes all four and bumps the pre-release to **0.1.3-test.6**.

## What changed

**1. Models that reason inside their content are now catalogued as reasoners** (`pliny-models.json`, `probe-pliny-free-models.ts`)
The gateway exposes no reasoning channel for `kimi-k2.6`, `qwen3-6-35b-a3b-1-28dd3`, `nemotron-3-ultra-550b-a55` and the sia `qwen3-5-397b-a17b`: their deliberation arrives as ordinary content. The probe only counted reasoning deltas, so all four were `defaultOn: false` and the off-switch was never sent. The smart profile's classifier and the judge both run on the 35B, got a paragraph of thinking truncated before the JSON verdict, and reported "no verdict" on every turn of that session. The probe now treats a long answer to its one-word question as reasoning; the three models with a working `chat_template_kwargs` off-switch get it on quick and utility calls, kimi is marked always-on.

**2. The guard catches a reply that ends on the model's plan** (`unfinished-turn-guard.ts`, `router-prompt.ts`, `router-rules.ts`)
kimi past ~80k tokens ends with "I need to: 1. Check what's running 2. … 4. Give a clear status update" and no tool call (0 tool calls in 7 calls that session). `endsWithPlanList` flags a first-person plan intro followed by imperative list items with nothing after; results lists and option lists for the user do not match. The free-model prompt addendum names the shape. `qwen3-coder` now leads the `default` route with kimi as fallback (the `subagent` route is unchanged).

**3. The call log records what each call produced** (`routed-agent-model.ts`, `router-call-log.ts`, `summarize-free-auto-log.ts`)
Every line of `pliny-free-auto-calls.jsonl` gains `finishReason`, `textChars`, `reasoningChars` and `toolCalls`. The summary script has a "Text-only stops" column per model, so stop rates can be read from real use instead of transcripts.

**4. The agent terminal disables git's pager and prompts** (`agent-terminal-env.ts`)
`git branch` in that session paged and waited almost three minutes for a keypress the model could not send. Both terminal factories now set `GIT_PAGER=cat`, `PAGER=cat` and `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`.

`docs/pliny-free-auto-router.md` documents all three behaviours.

## Verification

- `bun run test:vitest -- src/sdk/router`: 243 passed, including new tests for the plan-list rule (the four kimi endings from the transcript plus three non-matching endings) and for the call shape.
- `@plinycode/llms` suite: 762 passed.
- `bun run types`: clean. Biome clean on every touched file.
- The probe was not re-run against the gateway; the catalog edits are hand-applied from the existing `pliny-free-auto-thinking-probe.json` numbers (baseline 1339/1017/205/1106 content chars for the four, 5 with template-off for three of them).

## Note for testers

Rules files are only written when missing, so an existing `~/.cline/data/pliny-free-auto*.md` keeps its own route order. Move it aside to pick up the new `default` order.

## Why

Three problems found while reviewing how the agent searches and edits code.

**1. `search_codebase` silently skipped whole languages.** The engine runs `rg` from PATH. It is rarely there (never on a stock Windows install), so the search fell back to a JavaScript scan that only opened files whose extension was on a fixed list. `.cc`, `.cxx`, `.hh`, `.sv`, `.v`, `.tcl`, `.cs`, `.proto` and many others were not on it, so a search in those files answered "No results found" and the model concluded the symbol did not exist.

**2. Where `rg` was on PATH, the results were garbled.** The parser built each result from ripgrep's `context` events and expected the matching line to be among them. Ripgrep reports the match as a `match` event, so:

- the matching line itself was never printed;
- the lines before a match were attached to the previous result, usually a different file;
- `--max-count=1` showed one match per file.

For a file `B.txt` followed by `A.txt`, the model saw:

```
B.txt:4:1
  5: b5
  1: a1      <- from A.txt
  2: a2      <- from A.txt
```

**3. The diff preview kept its own copy of the editor's matching logic** (`computeNewEditorContent`), so any change to how `old_text` is matched had to be made twice or the preview and the write would disagree.

## What changes

- **The extension runs the search with VS Code's own ripgrep.** `VscodeSessionHost` passes a search executor built with `rgPath: () => getBinaryLocation("rg")`, the same lookup file search already uses. `createSearchExecutor` takes the new `rgPath` option, tries it first and then `rg` on PATH.
- **The fallback reads every file that is not binary.** The extension allow-list is replaced by a deny-list of binary extensions, a 2 MB size limit and a NUL-byte check. `includeExtensions` still restricts the scan when a caller passes it.
- **Ripgrep results are parsed by event type** (`parseRipgrepEvents`): the match line is printed and marked `>`, leading and trailing context stay with their own match, and paths use forward slashes.
- **Up to 10 matches per file** (`maxMatchesPerFile`), in both paths, with a closing note naming the files that have more. Ripgrep showed 1; the fallback showed every match, so one busy file could fill the 100-result limit.
- **"No matches" from ripgrep is final.** It used to fall through to a second, full JavaScript scan.
- **A pattern starting with `-`** is passed with `-e`, so ripgrep no longer reads it as a flag.
- **`replaceTextInContent`** (new `executors/text-replace.ts`) holds the replacement logic. The editor executor and the VS Code diff preview both call it. Matching behaviour and error messages are unchanged.

The `search_codebase` description gains one sentence saying that matching is case-insensitive, that the matching line is marked `>`, and that only the first matches per file are shown.

## Behaviour changes to be aware of

- Searches now go through ripgrep in the extension, so they respect `.gitignore` and skip hidden files, as ripgrep does by default. The fallback did neither.
- The fallback counted every match on a line as a result; a line now counts once, as in ripgrep.

## Test procedure

- New engine tests: `text-replace.test.ts`; in `search.test.ts`, the fallback finds matches in `.cc`, `.sv` and `.tcl` files and skips a binary one, shows the marked match line with its context, caps matches per file and names the capped file, and `parseRipgrepEvents` is checked against event streams in ripgrep's real order (context before the match, a line between two close matches, the per-file cap).
- Ran the built engine against a small fixture through VS Code's bundled `rg.exe` and through the fallback: both find the `.cc`, `.sv` and `.tcl` matches with the right lines.
- `bun run build:sdk`, `bun run types`, `bun run lint`, `bun run format`: clean.
- Engine tool tests (`sdk/packages/core/src/extensions/tools`): 375 pass.
- Extension `test:vitest`: 1326 pass.
- Extension `test:unit`: 63 of 69 files pass. The 6 failing files are the hook suites under `src/core/hooks/__tests__`, which fail on my machine because a `package.json` in the Temp directory makes Node load the test hook scripts as ES modules; they do not touch this code.
- Not run locally: integration and e2e tests, and the search has not been exercised inside a running extension host.

## Type of Change

-   [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
-   [x] ♻️ Refactor Changes

## Why

On FreeAuto, Kimi K2.6 kept stopping for no visible reason: it announced a step and ended the turn, or it called tools that "do not exist":

```
Tool call  functions-read-files-5-w53hn3x5d032008 {"files": [...]} <|tool_call_end|> <|tool_calls_section_end|>
was rejected before execution: no tool is named " functions-read-files-5-…
```

The cause is the tool-call ids in the history PlinyCode sends.

Kimi writes a call as `<|tool_call_begin|>functions.read_files:3<|tool_call_argument_begin|>{…}`. The id holds the tool's name and a running index, and the model's chat template shows it its earlier calls by that id. Since 0.1.5-test.7 (#56), `withSafeToolCallIds` rewrites every id on the wire to `[a-zA-Z0-9-]` plus a hash, because Claude on Bedrock rejects anything else. Kimi therefore read its own earlier calls as `functions-read-files-3-9tb01v` and imitated that. Its server could no longer parse the result, and the call reached us in one of three ways:

- glued into the tool name, with empty arguments (the error above)
- as raw tokens in the reply text
- not at all, which is the "announced a step and stopped" the completion guard kept catching

## Measurement

`apps/vscode/scripts/probe-kimi-tool-call-ids.ts` replays one history (six earlier calls, the next step is clearly another call) against `snps-provider/kimi-k2.6` with three id styles, 24 runs each:

| Ids in the history | Usable tool call |
| --- | --- |
| rewritten for Bedrock, as sent until 0.1.7-test.9 | 6 / 24 |
| another model's ids (`call-…`, `toolu-…`) | 17 / 24 |
| Kimi's own, `functions.<tool>:<index>` | 23 / 24 |

The one miss in the last row was a direct answer, not a broken call.

## What changes

All Kimi handling is in the new `sdk/packages/llms/src/providers/kimi-tool-calls.ts`, and applies only to Kimi models (`isKimiModel`: family or model id contains `kimi`, since the Pliny catalog gives its self-hosted models no family).

- **Kimi's history carries its own ids.** `withKimiToolCallIds` renumbers every call in the outgoing request as `functions.<tool>:<index>`, whichever model made it, and its tool result with it. `withSafeToolCallIds` skips requests whose model is Kimi. Stored messages keep their ids; other models get exactly what they got before.
- **A call glued into the tool name is taken apart.** `repairMalformedToolCall` reads the tool and the JSON arguments out of the name when the call's own arguments are empty. `resolveMisnamedTool` (moved here from `ai-sdk-message-convert.ts`) also resolves a call id (`functions.read_files:3`, `functions-read-files-5-w53hn3x`) and camelCase (`readFiles`) to the tool.
- **A call left in the reply text is run.** Text from `<|tool_call` on is held back while streaming. When the reply ends normally, the calls that name an available tool and carry JSON arguments are emitted as tool calls and the section is not shown. If no call can be read from it, or the reply failed or was aborted, the text is shown as it arrived.
- **Shorter unknown-tool error.** It quotes at most 80 characters of the name, without control tokens, so the model is not handed two more copies of the bad call.
- **Guard.** `endsWithPlanList` now catches an announced action followed by the things it applies to ("Let me read:" and a list of files). That was the second stall in the reported conversation, which went unnoticed. "Let me summarize:" plus a list is still accepted as an answer.

`docs/pliny-free-auto-router.md` has a new section, "Kimi and tool-call ids".

## Tests

- `kimi-tool-calls.test.ts` (new) uses the names, ids and text exactly as they arrived in real sessions:
  - name resolution, with negatives (`chatcmpl-tool-…`, `read_files_v2`, two tools that read the same without separators)
  - taking a glued call apart, and keeping the call's own arguments when it has any
  - id renumbering: reused ids, orphaned results, stored messages untouched
  - the text filter at delta sizes 1, 7 and 1000; several calls; garbage shown as text; nothing run from a failed reply
  - the real adapter against a fake gateway: a glued call runs, a leaked call runs and is hidden, a non-Kimi model gets the text and the ids unchanged, Kimi gets `functions.run_commands:0 … functions.read_files:3` on the wire
- `tool-call-ids.test.ts`: Kimi requests keep their ids; the same history to another model is still rewritten.
- `unfinished-turn-guard.test.ts`: the real stalled reply is flagged; two answer-with-a-list replies are not.

`bun -F @plinycode/llms test`: 724 passed. Extension `src/sdk` vitest: 1204 passed. `bun run types`, `check:docs` and `analyze:unused:prod` are clean.

Not run in a dev host: the fix is verified by the tests and by the probe against the live gateway, not by a full agent session in the editor.

## Why

Long conversations drift. The logs since 2026-10-10 (2,146 calls, 102 runs, 14 long sessions) show where:

- **Routing.** Every `huge` verdict (164 of 164, median context 70k) and every `quick` verdict past 30k tokens fell through to the `default` route, Sonnet 5: 77 of Sonnet 5's 85 calls. `reason` verdicts for chores ("please create a PR", `[CI WATCHER] CI failed`, "not sure why the build takes so long") kept whole turns on the Sonnet thinking preset: 124 calls of one build-polling turn. Guard escalations sent the last one or two calls of 100k-token turns to Sonnet 5, a full cache write each.
- **Context.** One run compacted five times (at iterations 3, 20, 33, 62 and 86); after each compaction the model re-read the same files and edited from stale content. Tool results of 100-224k chars (`search_codebase` with 4-7 queries) and Kimi's in-content deliberation (25 replies of 30-130k chars of "Wait… Actually… Let me…") stayed in the history for the rest of the conversation. Failed oversized `editor` writes (plans and reports) left 10-25k chars of input behind, three times per session.
- **Memory.** The distiller added twenty entries to one repository's memory in a day, most of them change-logs and code facts, each then sent with every request.
- **Skills.** `skills` was called as `{skill: "commit", args: "-m …"}` seven times: its own description gave that as the example.

## What changes

**Router (BalanceAuto)**
- A verdict whose route refuses the request's size falls back by tier (`quick` → `coding`; `huge` → `coding` in act mode, `plan-and-reasoning` in plan mode) instead of the catch-all. The classifier no longer offers `huge` and spells out that chores are `code`.
- The classifier and the keyword routes read only what the user typed: `<editor_state>` and `<mode_notice>` stripped, reminders, hook context and compaction summaries skipped.
- `health.maxPaidCallsPerTurn` (default 20, `0` off): past the cap the rest of the turn runs on the coding route's free lead, once per turn, with a chat row and `paidCapHit` in the run log.
- The guard's first stall escalation goes to the next free model; only the second, or six failed commands, to the default lead. `escalatedTo` in the run log.

**Engine**
- `pruneStaleContext` (core, on the request copy only): earlier turns' tool results over 2k chars become a stub; aged in-turn results are middle-cut in blocks of eight iterations (one cache rewrite per block); the deliberation before an earlier tool call is cut to its last 600 chars; the inputs of failed oversized tool calls are elided. Replaying four long sessions through it sends 69-77% fewer characters. Compaction sizing sees the pruned request, so it triggers later.
- `search_codebase` returns at most 32k chars per call across its queries, `read_files` 64k across its files.
- The editor accepts a large `new_text` when creating a file or writing a markdown/text document.
- Loop detection resets per run (a repeated user request across turns could trip the hard stop) and notices the third non-adjacent identical call of a run, once.
- The `skills` tool example is no longer git-shaped, and says the tool runs no command.

**Memory**: at most four proposals, change-logs and code facts filtered out, ordinary proposals start unchecked.

**Measurement**: the summary script lists paid turns and counts the verdicts that left their route; ten chore labels added to the classifier label set.

Docs: `pliny-balance-auto.md`, `pliny-free-auto-router.md`, `context-compaction.md`, `memory.md`, `agent-tools.md`.

## Checks

`bun run lint`, `bun run format`, `bun run types`, `bun run check:docs` pass. Core unit suite: 1692 passed, 5 failed in `hooks/hook-file-hooks.test.ts` and `extensions/mcp/client.test.ts`, which fail on this machine without the change too. Extension vitest: 2087 passed. The `MemoryProposalRow` webview test passes.

## Problem

Programs lay their output out to the terminal's width before PlinyCode reads a byte. In a terminal panel docked beside the editor (30–60 columns), PowerShell drops table columns and breaks error messages across many lines, and native tools that ask the console for its width do the same. Nothing after the fact can rebuild what was dropped. Until now PlinyCode only told the model and warned the user ("PlinyCode's terminal is only 60 columns wide…").

## Change

Commands in PowerShell terminals now run through a small wrapper (`apps/vscode/src/hosts/vscode/terminal/wide-output.ts`), still in the user's terminal, with its profile and environment:

- **What the terminal shows.** It shows `. plinyrun '<command>'`. `plinyrun` is defined once per terminal from the `PLINYCODE_RUN` environment variable, which PlinyCode sets on the PowerShell terminals it creates. The terminal's first line defines it, and only in full language mode.
- **Same scope as typed.** The function is dot-sourced, so variables, imported modules and `cd` persist as if the command had been typed.
- **Output that isn't laid out to the terminal's width.** The output goes through the pipeline, so native programs write to a pipe instead of the console. `Out-String -Width 400` formats PowerShell objects. Error, warning and verbose records come out one line each, not through the console-width error view.
- **Environment during the command.** `COLUMNS=200` is set, as Background Exec does, and so is `PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1`.
- **Exit status.** The `$?` of the command's last statement is handed back (`$PSCmdlet.WriteError` with errors silenced), so a failure is still reported as exit code 1.
- **When the wrapper is not used:**
  - with the new setting **`plinycode.terminal.wideOutput`** turned off (it is on by default);
  - in Constrained Language mode (AppLocker/WDAC), where the method calls the wrapper needs are blocked;
  - in shells other than PowerShell.

  In these cases the command runs as typed, and the existing narrow-terminal note and warning still apply to it.

`ConptyWrapJoiner` also gets two fixes found while recording ConPTY output:
- a cursor move to the start of a row now counts as a line break, so the line after a table no longer runs into it (`meGet-Item : …`);
- `ESC[nX` (erase characters) is now stripped, so it no longer leaves a stray `X` in the text.

## Verification

- Recorded a 40-column ConPTY (VS Code's node-pty, powershell.exe 5.1):
  - **Without the wrapper:** a four-column table lost two columns and cut the third short, and a `Get-Item` error took 17 lines.
  - **With it:** all four columns came through, and the error took 3 lines with its message on one.
- Ran a temporary integration test in the VS Code test host with a real PowerShell terminal and real shell integration:
  - the one-time setup ran, and a 5-column table came through whole;
  - `cmd /c "exit 5"` was reported as exit code 1;
  - a variable set in one command was readable in the next;
  - errors came out one per line.
- In PowerShell 5.1, also checked:
  - `Set-Location`, variables, `Import-Module` and functions persist;
  - native failures, cmdlet failures, parse errors and `throw` all report failure;
  - successful commands report success;
  - output streams live;
  - in Constrained Language mode the function is not defined.
- Automated checks run:
  - `bun run check-types`
  - Biome on the changed files
  - `test:discovery`
  - vitest for `src/hosts`, including the new `wide-output.test.ts`
  - `conptyWrapJoiner.test.ts`, with the recorded bytes
  - mocha `VscodeTerminalProcess.test.ts`: 30 passing, including a new wrapped-path test
  - knip
- The `vscode-run-commands-tool.test.ts` bun suite fails locally with `createTool is not a function` (local Bun 1.4.2 vs the 1.3.14 pin). It fails the same way on `stage`, so CI is the check for it.

## Known limits

- **Partial lines appear late.** A native program's prompt without a line break (`Continue? [y/N]`) only shows once the line ends. The keyboard-prompt check doesn't see it, so the command is handed over after 5 minutes like any other long one.
- **No colours or progress bars from native programs**, since they now write to a pipe.
- **PowerShell 7 not tested.** I checked Windows PowerShell 5.1 only; no pwsh 7 was available locally. The constructs used are the same in 7.

Three things from one request: let the routers compact later and make that tunable, show every compaction in the chat without feeding it to the model, and explain (and fix where it was a bug) the context bar dropping without a compaction.

## Router defaults and compaction budgets

- **Built-in model orders = the orders tuned in Settings → Router during the 0.2.4 runs.** FreeAuto: kimi-k2.6 → GLM-5.2 (internal-tests, vmodels) → nemotron ultra → nemotron super, pool limited to its routes' models. Smart: GLM-5.2 first. Fast: qwen3.5-397b first. BalanceAuto: Sonnet 4.6 → Sonnet 5 → kimi on every main route (coding included). Untouched rules files refresh to the new defaults; edited ones keep theirs.
- **Higher budgets, one table** (`plinyRouterBudget` in `pliny-models.ts`): FreeAuto 200k (was 150k), Smart 300k (was 150k), BalanceAuto 300k (was 128k), Fast 64k. The virtual windows grow to the largest window of the order (512k, 512k, 1M), so the bar's denominator changes.
- **Settings → Router → Compaction.** A budget and a post-compaction size per router, in tokens or %. Non-blocking notes say which models hand larger requests on before compaction starts, and warn when no model in the order fits the trigger, or when the target can't work. The engine gets absolute tokens through two new `CoreCompactionConfig` fields, `maxInputTokensOverride` and `targetTokensOverride`, read before every call. A model tuning's smaller context still wins. The bar's marker follows the tuned budget.
- **Calibrated size filter.** `fitsContext` measures each candidate in its own tokens (per-model `tokenCalibration`). The flat 3 chars/token dropped kimi at about 127k real tokens, before compaction ran. With calibration it takes about 167k.

## Compaction in the chat, not in the context

- Overflow-recovery compaction now gets a divider ("Context compacted (the model rejected it as too large)") instead of the raw `overflow-recovery-compacted` slug, and rescales the bar.
- An agentic compaction's divider has **Show summary**: the summary the model continues from (capped at 8k chars, carried on the `completed` notice).
- A reopened conversation rebuilds the latest compaction's divider where it ran, from the compaction sidecar.
- The Markdown export writes each finished compaction as a line, with the summary in `<details>`.
- Divider rows never reach the model; a new engine test asserts the compacted history holds no notice text. The model still gets the summary message, and the basic strategy keeps its one-line `<SYSTEM_NOTICE>Earlier context was compacted…`: it tells the model turns are missing and is not a chat notice.

## The context bar dropping without a compaction

Most drops are intended per-request trimming: stale tool output and earlier reasoning at each new prompt, in-turn aging on uncached models, superseded reads, side questions, model switches. The new hover line "Trimmed from the last request: −Xk" (`prunedTokens`) names them. docs/context-compaction.md explains each one.

Fixed:
- The bar counted the reply's output tokens. It now shows the request's input (`contextTokens`).
- A retried empty reply summed both attempts into one row, so the bar doubled and then fell. The same doubled count also fed the compaction trigger's previous-request count and the token calibration. Billing still sums every attempt, but the row, the trigger and the calibration now take the last attempt's input (`requestInputTokens`, stamped by `retry-empty-response.ts`).

## Tests

- `build:sdk`, `types` (incl. extension + webview), `lint` (same 8 warnings / 15 infos as stage), `format`, `check:docs`, knip: clean.
- shared 377, llms 745, extension unit 1026, extension vitest 2213, webview 746: all pass.
- core: 1732 pass, 5 fail. These are the hook-file and MCP-client tests, and they fail the same way on a clean `origin/stage` worktree on this machine (temp-file ENOENT, fake server `require` under ESM).

Not checked in a dev host yet: the Settings fields, the divider's summary and the marker position.

## What changes

The CI Board stops being a wall of dots with one "Fix CI & conflicts" button. It now says what failed and how serious it is, offers the fix that fits, and can fix the safe cases by itself. Everything runs on free Pliny models.

### Failure triage
- When an item fails or conflicts, the board reads the failed runs (`runReport`) and asks the router's free utility summarizer for a JSON verdict per pipeline: build, test regression, small test delta, infrastructure, stale or unknown. Severity (blocker → info) and the recommended actions are computed from the categories, so they stay stable.
- When the model doesn't answer, rules on job, step and error text classify the failures. Rules never return a small test delta, so auto-watch can't recalibrate on their word.
- Triage runs once per item state (head commit, red runs, conflict), including what was already red at startup. It reads at most 4 runs per item and defers while the GitHub rate limit is low.
- Long details go to `.plinycode/ci-reports/<pr-N>-<sha>.md` in the checkout. `/.plinycode/` is added to `.git/info/exclude` in the common git dir, so the worktrees share it. No tracked `.gitignore` is touched.
- New setting `plinycode.ci.board.triage`: `auto`, `onDemand` or `off`.

### Actions
- Four built-in actions: Fix conflicts, Recalibrate, Fix CI, and Investigate (Ask mode, read-only). They come with new prompts written for free models, with the hard rules repeated: only push `HEAD:<branch>`, no force, never recalibrate a regression.
- The row's main button fits the item's state; the rest are in a split-button menu. The menu adds **Run a custom prompt…** (text or file, can be saved as an action) and **Analyze again**.
- The prompt header carries the triage, the report path, and the repository's matching skills, detected by name in the project skill folders (e.g. GPUSurfer's `fix-conflicts`, `recalibrate-unit-tests`, `analyze-pipeline-deltas`).
- Runs default to `pliny/auto-free`. New `TaskStartOptions.modelId` keeps that model through rebuilds (`SdkSessionConfigBuilder.pinModel`) and reloads (`HistoryItem.pinnedModelId`), and `handleProviderConfigChange` leaves a pinned session alone.

### Auto-watch
- A per-entry switch replaces the unused Manual / Auto / Full auto setting.
- It runs Fix conflicts on a conflicting PR. It runs Recalibrate only when all of these hold: the model is at least 70% sure every failure is a small delta, nothing is still running, and a recalibration skill or a prompt override exists. Everything else gets a "needs you" notification.
- Runs start straight in the background with the new `startBackgroundTask`. It never touches the displayed task: it builds with `newConversation: true`, so the run doesn't pick up the displayed conversation's snapshots or router key.
- Caps: 2 runs per commit, 3 per PR until it turns green, 1 run at a time, and one background slot always left for the user. The branch checked out in the user's own folder is refused.
- New `ci-run-policy.ts`, checked first through `sessionPolicy` in `SdkInteractionCoordinator`:
  - auto-watch runs approve what fits (worktree edits, `git push <remote> HEAD:<branch>`, the read-only DevOps tools) and refuse everything else with a reason;
  - runs the user starts get only the refusals (force push, other branches, edits outside the worktree).

### Store / proto / UI
- `ci-board.json` moves to version 2 with a migration from version 1.
- Proto: `autonomy` and `trigger` are reserved; `CiItem.triage`, `CiItem.auto` and `CiItem.actions` are added, plus the `analyzeCiItem` and `runCiCustomPrompt` RPCs.
- Webview: severity chip and colored row edge, expandable details, split action button, auto-watch badge and switch, actions editor, custom prompt panel, summary chip with a "Failing only" filter. Every control has a Radix tooltip.
- `docs/ci-board.md` is rewritten (triage, actions, auto-watch, approvals table).

## Tests
- `bun test src/services/devops-mcp`: 201 pass. New: triage, report-dir (with a real worktree), skills, actions, auto-runner, store migration.
- `vitest --config vitest.config.ts` (all extension vitest suites): 1736 pass. New: `ci-run-policy.test.ts`, plus session policy, model pin and background start cases.
- webview `vitest`: 557 pass. New: `CiTargetSection.test.tsx`; `CiItemRow.test.tsx` is rewritten.
- Typecheck, Biome lint and format, knip (`analyze:unused:prod`) and `check:docs` are clean.
- `test:unit`: 1054 pass. The 43 failures are the known local hook-test environment issue (a stray `%TEMP%\package.json`), unrelated to this change.
- **Not yet done:** a manual pass in a dev host against a live failing PR, including auto-watch end to end.

Pre-release: https://github.com/lgiaccar/PlinyCode/releases/tag/release_0.2.2-test.8

## Summary

### Scheduled prompts are scoped to their conversation
The schedule was a single webview list that no conversation owned. `ChatView` never unmounts, and the timer sent through the displayed conversation's `handleSendMessage`. So a prompt scheduled in A appeared in B and was sent into B.
- Each `ScheduledPrompt` now carries the `taskId` it was scheduled in (`currentTaskItem.id`, or undefined on the welcome screen).
- The banner lists only the open conversation's prompts.
- The timer sends only prompts that are due for the open conversation. Others wait, however overdue, until their conversation is open again.
- When a prompt scheduled on the welcome screen starts a conversation, its repeats are bound to that conversation.
- Sends now happen outside the React state updater. StrictMode could run the updater twice and send twice.
- The logic is in `chat-view/utils/scheduledPrompts.ts`, with tests.

### Conversation budget edits take effect (engine)
`LocalRuntimeHost.getSession()` answers a loaded session from its in-memory `sessionMetadata`, and `updateSession()` wrote only to disk.
- The budget check (`findHistoryItem`) therefore never saw a `spendingLimit` set from the header, and fell back to the $5 global default.
- The next usage write (`updateTaskUsage`) then rebuilt metadata from that stale copy and erased the edit from disk.

`updateSession()` now re-reads the stored manifest into the loaded session after a successful metadata, title or prompt update. There is a regression test; it fails without the fix.

### Favorite models survive restarts
Each window's `ClineFileStorage` loaded `globalState.json` once and rewrote the whole file from that snapshot. A window that loaded before a favorite was starred erased the favorite on its next write of any key; `initializeWebview` → `refreshWorkflowToggles` writes on every webview mount.
- `setBatch` now starts from the file on disk, replaces only its own keys, and skips values that are unchanged. An unreadable file never wipes the store.
- `toggleFavoriteModel` starts from the list on disk (`StateManager.reloadGlobalStateKey`).
- After a successful Pliny catalog resolve, favorites whose model is gone are removed (`pruneFavoriteModels`). Router ids from before the `auto-*` rename are carried over to the current id. A failed or empty catalog removes nothing. The Pliny catalog is bundled, so the check is deterministic.

### Unknown-tool errors say more
Namespaced tool names (`functions-read_files`) were already repaired in #103. This PR adds end-to-end stream tests for that. A call that is still unknown now:
- names the provider and model that emitted it;
- suggests the closest tool, by edit distance or suffix;
- lists the exact names;
- is logged as a warning.

The AI SDK delivers the error as a string on the stream part, so it is matched by its `AI_NoSuchToolError` text.

### Not changed
Opening files by clicking them in the chat works (per the reporter), so this PR leaves it alone.

## Testing
- `bun run build:sdk`; `bun run types` and `bun run check-types`: clean.
- `bun run lint`: clean. Biome format: clean on the changed files.
- llms: `vitest run`: 683 passed. core: `src/runtime/host`: 111 passed.
- New suites: `ClineFileStorage.test.ts` (bun), `pruneFavoriteModels.test.ts` (bun), `scheduledPrompts.test.ts` (webview vitest).
- `bun run test:unit`: the new tests pass. The failures are local-environment artifacts:
  - hook-runner suites fail because of how bash hook scripts run on this Windows machine;
  - `devops-mcp` `tools.test.ts` fails because `DEVOPS_MCP_PROVIDER=ado` is set locally.
- Pre-release `0.1.7-test.8` is published: https://github.com/lgiaccar/PlinyCode/releases/tag/release_0.1.7-test.8

## Problem

When the user switches agents mid-conversation via the dropdown, the session is rebuilt with the new agent's system prompt — but the model still sees its prior history which was generated under the old agent's identity. This causes confused replies ("I am Cline…") when asked "what agent are you?".

## Root Cause

The session rebuild already works correctly (history preserved, new system prompt active from the first subsequent turn). What was missing was an **in-conversation signal** telling the model that a new identity has taken effect — exactly the same problem that mode-switching solved with `<mode_notice>`.

## Fix

Mirrors the mode-switch notice pattern exactly:

1. **`formatAgentSwitchNotice(agentName)`** added to `@plinycode/shared/prompt/format.ts` — produces:
   ```
   <agent_notice>The user switched to the "Code Reviewer" agent before sending this message. Adopt the identity and instructions in the system prompt above for all subsequent replies.</agent_notice>
   ```
2. **`stripModeNotices`** updated to also strip `<agent_notice>` blocks, so users never see the XML in their chat bubble.
3. **`SdkModeCoordinator.recordAgentSwitchNotice` / `consumeAgentSwitchNotice`** — one-shot tracker scoped to the session ID (same pattern as `recordModeSwitchNotice`).
4. **`SdkSessionLifecycle.fireAndForgetSend`** — consumes the agent notice and prepends it to the next outbound prompt, alongside any pending mode notice.
5. **`SdkController.updateAgentPath`** — after rebuilding the session, derives the agent name from the file's frontmatter `name` field (fallback: basename) and records the notice.
6. **`unwrapUserInput`** (router) and **`defang`** (CI report) updated to strip/defang `<agent_notice>` tags.

## Result

After switching to "Code Reviewer" and sending the next message, the model receives:
```
System: [Code Reviewer identity and instructions]
…prior history…
User: <agent_notice>The user switched to the "Code Reviewer" agent … Adopt the identity and instructions in the system prompt above for all subsequent replies.</agent_notice>
      what can you do?
```
The model adopts its new identity, the chat history is fully preserved, and the XML is invisible to the user.

## Files Changed

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `sdk/packages/shared/src/prompt/format.ts` | Add `formatAgentSwitchNotice`; update `stripModeNotices` to strip `<agent_notice>` |
| `sdk/packages/shared/src/index.ts` + `index.browser.ts` | Export `formatAgentSwitchNotice` |
| `sdk/packages/shared/src/prompt/format.test.ts` | Tests for new function and stripping |
| `apps/vscode/src/sdk/sdk-mode-coordinator.ts` | Add `recordAgentSwitchNotice` / `consumeAgentSwitchNotice` |
| `apps/vscode/src/sdk/sdk-mode-coordinator.test.ts` | Tests for new methods |
| `apps/vscode/src/sdk/sdk-session-lifecycle.ts` | Consume agent notice in `fireAndForgetSend` |
| `apps/vscode/src/sdk/sdk-session-lifecycle.test.ts` | Tests for notice stamping and off-the-record guard |
| `apps/vscode/src/sdk/SdkController.ts` | Wire `consumeAgentSwitchNotice`; call `recordAgentSwitchNotice` + `deriveAgentName` in `updateAgentPath` |
| `apps/vscode/src/sdk/router/unfinished-turn-guard.ts` | Strip `<agent_notice>` in `unwrapUserInput` |
| `apps/vscode/src/services/devops-mcp/ci-watch/ci-report-text.ts` | Defang `agent_notice` |

## CI Board

- **Per-pipeline view.** The row's chevron expands the compact line of dots into one line per pipeline (plus the merge when the PR conflicts): `pipeline → problem → [fix]`, with **Fix them all** at the bottom. Green pipelines show **OK**; running, queued and not-run pipelines say so.
- **A fix per pipeline.** Each failed pipeline gets the single fix that fits its triage category, run on that pipeline only: **Fix build** (build, test regression, unclear, or not triaged yet), **Recalibrate** (small delta), **Fix conflicts** (merge). Infrastructure and stale runs get no fix. A chevron menu runs Fix build, Recalibrate or Investigate on the pipeline instead, for when the free model's triage is wrong.
- **New built-in action `fix-build`** with its own prompt: fix the code and never touch expected values; infrastructure failures are reported for a re-run instead of edited around. Skills matching `build|compil` are suggested to it.
- **Fix CI → Fix them all.** Same id (`fix-ci`). The prompt is rewritten to list each problem, then fix them in order (conflicts, build, regression, small delta via the repo's tooling, infrastructure reported). It now hears of every matching skill (conflict, build, recalibrate, pipeline). The store renames the untouched default label "Fix CI"; a label the user chose stays.
- **Main button:** the single fix when one thing is wrong (scoped to the pipeline when it's a pipeline). It's Fix them all when several things are wrong, or when the one problem has no single fix. A PR whose every failure is a small delta still gets Recalibrate.
- **Scoped runs:** `RunCiActionRequest.pipeline` → `prepareRun` checks the pipeline still exists on the item. The header gets a **Scope** section (that pipeline and run, its triage, and the other failed pipelines to leave alone). Prompts can use `{{pipeline}}` and `{{runId}}`. The run's link records the pipeline, so the expanded row can mark it "fixing". One board run per PR at a time still applies, since runs share the worktree.
- Proto: `CiItem.fixes` (`CiPipelineFix`), `run_action_id`, `run_pipeline`, `CiItemAction.pipeline`, `RunCiActionRequest.pipeline`.

## Chat: conversation vs. prompt box

A long prompt (or a large saved prompt-box size, up to 40 rows) could squeeze the conversation to nothing, because the layout grid was `1fr auto`.

- `ChatLayout` now uses `minmax(min(max(120px, 25vh), 50vh), 1fr) auto`, so the conversation always keeps a minimum height.
- `useFittingRows` measures the footer around the textarea on window and footer resize, and caps the textarea's `maxRows` to what fits beside that minimum. Dragging the handle starts from and stops at what fits. The saved `chatInputMaxRows` is kept, so a taller panel gets it back. The prompt box keeps at least 1–3 rows.

Four fixes to plan mode, reloaded conversations and Run in worktree.

## Plans are kept outside the workspace

Plan mode wrote its plans to `plans/<slug>/PLAN.md` in the workspace, where they could be committed or deleted by accident. They now go to PlinyCode's data folder, one folder per workspace:

```
~/.cline/data/plans/<workspace name>-<8 hex of the path's SHA-256>/<slug>/PLAN.md
```

- `resolvePlansDataDir()` (`@plinycode/shared/storage`, `CLINE_PLANS_DATA_DIR` overrides it) and `workspacePlanFolder()` (`apps/vscode/src/core/workspace/plan-folder.ts`) work out the folder.
- `buildClineSystemPrompt` takes a new `planDirectory` option. With it, the plan-mode instructions name absolute paths under that folder, with forward slashes. Without it (the CLI), they keep `plans/<slug>/`. The extension always passes it.
- The plan row's link shows `<slug>/PLAN.md` and has the full path in its title.
- New command **PlinyCode: Open Plan…** lists the workspace's plans, newest first, and can reveal the folder.
- The edit and read approvals don't depend on the path, so nothing else changes. Plans that earlier versions wrote to the workspace stay where they are.

## Switching to Agent mode no longer runs the plan

After a plan, flipping the mode switch to Agent sent "Continue with the approved plan now." by itself (along with any draft in the prompt box). That approved the plan without the user asking. Now only the **Execute plan** button runs the plan (`togglePlanActModeProto` passes `executePlan` when the request has `executePlanWith`). A plain switch only rebuilds the session, and the draft stays in the box. The plan-mode prompt also tells the model that the switch alone is not approval.

## Reloaded conversations keep their prompt rows

A prompt sent while a command ran in the background is saved in the same message as that command's `<hook_context>` block. On replay, the whole message counted as hook context. The prompt lost its highlighted row, and the turn before it lost its completion styling. Restart-from-here also skipped the message, because `isSyntheticSdkUserMessage` treated it as runtime-only. History replay and that check now strip the hook blocks and treat what is left as the prompt. I checked this against 150 local sessions: every typed prompt now replays as a prompt row. The only ones still hidden are `[TASK RESUMPTION]` prompts, which are meant to be hidden.

## Run in worktree branches are named after the user

Branches are now `<OS user>/<slug>-<4 hex>` (e.g. `lgiaccar/fix-login-3f2a`), not `plinycode/…`. A name prefix can't tell them apart from the user's own branches, so each one gets `branch.<name>.plinycodetask = true` in git config, and the daily cleanup checks for that. `plinycode/*` branches are still recognised.

## Tests

- New unit tests: the replay of a prompt sharing a message with hook context, `isSyntheticSdkUserMessage`, the mode coordinator (a switch without Execute plan sends nothing), the proto handler flag, `planDirectory` in the prompt, `workspacePlanFolder`/`listSavedPlans`, `planFileLabel`, `taskBranchPrefix`, and the branch marker in the worktree and cleanup tests (an unmarked `<user>/…` branch next to them is left alone).
- e2e `plan-execute.test.ts`: the plan lands in the data folder and not in the workspace. A new case checks that switching to Agent mode doesn't run the plan, and that asking for it does.
- Run locally: `bun run types`, the extension's `check-types`, lint, format, knip, `check:docs`, the extension unit suite (87 files) and its vitest suite, the webview tests and the shared engine tests all pass. Core's unit suite has 5 failures, in `hook-file-hooks` and the MCP stdio client tests. Those files aren't touched here, and they fail locally under this Node version.

Docs: `docs/plan-mode.md` (plan folder, Open Plan…, switching to Agent mode), `docs/task-worktrees.md` (branch names, the marker), `AGENTS.md`.

## Why

A review of the four router models against the local call log (4225 calls, 125 runs) and session transcripts found that the routers underperformed single models for concrete, fixable reasons.

- **Kimi's stops were a tool-name bug.** It emits tool names with its chat template's namespace (`functions-read_files`). The AI SDK rejected them as unavailable tools and the model never recovered, which is most of its 25% text-only stop rate. The old "ends on its plan past 80k tokens" explanation did not hold: it happens at small contexts too.
- **Skills under `.github/skills` were invisible in Cursor** since #102 scoped skills to the running editor. Flat `.mdc` files in a skills folder were never loaded.
- **Nothing showed which rules and skills were loaded**, and the `skills` tool listed names only.
- **A command waiting for keyboard input blocked the turn for 5 minutes**, then came back as "still running".
- **BalanceAuto put about 70% of its calls on Sonnet**, mostly routine edits.

## What changes

**Routing** (`router-rules.ts`)
- `auto-free`, `auto-free-smart`: kimi-k2.6 leads coding, default, sub-agent and reasoning routes; the coder is second and the escalation target.
- `auto-free-fast`: Qwen only, kimi on no route.
- `auto-balanced`: coding leads with free kimi and coder; Sonnet 5 comes through failover, the `default` route and guard escalation. Reasoning still goes to the Sonnet thinking preset.
- The first routed call waits (max 1.5 s) for the rules file. Generated rules files carry a seed marker so an unedited seed is refreshed when defaults change (old copy kept as `.bak`).

**Gateway**: `resolveMisnamedTool` maps namespaced, hyphenated and differently cased tool names onto the real tool.

**Rules and skills**: skills load from every editor's folder; rules stay editor-scoped. Single `.md`/`.mdc` files in a skills folder are skills. The `skills` tool description carries each skill's description. Each turn shows a `Context:` chat row naming the rules and skills the request carries.

**Terminal**: a started command silent for 8 s whose last line reads as a question gets Ctrl+C; the result names the question and says to rerun non-interactively. The agent terminal env also silences Git Credential Manager, pip, apt and npx prompts.

**DevOps MCP**: numeric fields accept numeric strings (24 validation errors in transcripts).

Docs: `docs/pliny-free-auto-router.md`, `docs/pliny-balance-auto.md`.

## Verification

`bun run lint`, `format`, `types`, `check:docs` and knip pass. New or updated tests: gateway tool-name repair, skill loading and descriptions, editor scoping, route leads per profile, rules-file seed refresh, input-prompt detection, the run-commands result, and the context row. Full extension vitest run: 1313 passed.

## Notes for reviewers

- Existing rules files predate the seed marker and are treated as edited, so they keep old routes. Delete or move `~/.cline/data/pliny-*.md` to pick up the new defaults.
- No `.vsix` is published from this PR yet.
- Local `test:unit` failures in `hooks/__tests__` and `devops-mcp` `tools.test.ts` are pre-existing and environmental.

### Description

<!-- 
Help reviewers understand your changes by making this PR readable and well-organized:

- What problem does this PR solve?
- Why were these changes introduced and what purpose do they serve?
- For larger changes, provide context about your approach and reasoning

Small PRs may need minimal description, but larger changes benefit from explaining where you're coming from. Much of this context can be in the linked issue above, so feel free to reference it rather than repeating everything here.
-->

This branch makes PlinyCode conversations easier to read and navigate without removing access to the agent's work. The goal is an answer-first chat: users should be able to find their prompt and the resulting answer quickly, then inspect reasoning, tools, edits, and command output when they need the details.

#### 1. Keep answers visible and put process details behind Show activity

Reasoning, tool calls, progress, and automatic file-edit records are grouped under a collapsed **Show activity** control. The final answer stays visible, including answers delivered as several adjacent text blocks. Expanding activity shows the original records in their original order; collapsing it returns to the shorter reading view. Expansion state is retained as rows scroll out of and back into view, within the current chat view.

The latest fix closes a gap in that behavior: **completed terminal commands and their output now collapse too**, including commands that exit with an error. Previously, command rows were unconditionally exempted from activity grouping, so a completed command could still occupy the main conversation. Running commands remain visible for progress and cancellation, and pending command approvals remain visible for user action. A failed command's output remains available inside activity; standalone error notifications are not hidden by this change.

Actionable file approvals, memory proposals, hook notices, and standalone errors remain visible. User prompts and CI watcher reports remain separate from the agent's process details. The compact working indicator also avoids a duplicate waiting row when activity already communicates that work is in progress.

#### 2. Make thinking an explicit, accessible disclosure

Thinking no longer forces itself open just because reasoning is streaming. Users can open or close it themselves, including while the model is working. The disclosure exposes its expanded state to assistive technology and supports keyboard interaction. Open streaming reasoning follows new content; reopening completed reasoning starts from the beginning rather than jumping to its end.

#### 3. Improve Markdown reading quality

Assistant answers are no longer clipped by the generic three-line paragraph preview rule. More consistent heading, paragraph, list, quote, and link styling provides a clearer reading hierarchy. Wide code and tables scroll within the message instead of forcing the conversation wider. Table scroll regions can receive keyboard focus. Existing Markdown content and controls, including code copying, remain available.

#### 4. Make follow-ups and side questions easier to distinguish

Visible, labeled turn boundaries separate follow-up prompts and side questions from the preceding answer. Replies to tool approvals are not mistaken for new user turns or sticky prompts. Boundaries stay attached to existing message rows, preserving message timestamps and virtualized-list indices rather than introducing synthetic chat messages.

#### 5. Keep the development preview reliable

F5 readiness now waits for the required builds, and a successful companion bundle cannot mask a failed extension build. Protobuf generation stages output before updating live files, replaces only changed content, and avoids exposing half-written generated files to watchers. This reduces transient missing-import failures during development; it does not change the wire protocol.

These changes are presentation and development-workflow improvements, not changes to model selection, tool execution, approval policy, or stored conversation content.

Roadmap A1 (docs/roadmap.md). The agent found code by regex only: `search_codebase` returns every `foo` in comments and strings, several calls per question, and nothing says which hit is the definition. The window already runs language servers that know.

**Two extension tools** (`apps/vscode/src/sdk/code-intel/`, host side in `apps/vscode/src/hosts/vscode/code-intel-source.ts`):
- `find_symbol({ query?, path? })`: a file's outline (`kind name  line`, indented, filtered by `query`), or the workspace symbols matching `query` (`kind name  path:line:col`, at most 40).
- `code_navigate({ action, path, symbol, line? })`: `definition`, `references` or `hover` for a symbol as written in a file. The tool locates the identifier (nearest to `line` when given), so the model never computes a column. Definitions and references come back grouped by file as `line:col  preview`, 30 lines at most then `+N more in M files`; hovers are reduced to their code-fenced signature lines plus a few lines of prose.

Two tools with an `action` argument rather than six, because free models mis-fill wide schemas. VS Code cannot say whether a language server is registered for a file, so an empty answer is retried once after 1.5 s and then ends with a line sending the model to `search_codebase`; a file extension that answers nothing twice is not waited for again.

Wiring: registered in `createVscodeExtraTools` for the root and sub-agents, approved with the read tools, run in parallel. New chat rows `findSymbol` / `codeNavigate` show the tool's answer (the translator now copies the output into the row's `content` for these two tools). Setting `plinycode.codeIntel.enabled` (default on) applies to the next conversation. Docs: new section in `docs/agent-tools.md`.

**Verified:** 13 vitest cases on the tools and formatting (fake source), translator/runtime-builder/policy suites green, `check-types`, lint, knip clean. Still to check in a dev host: a real TypeScript project (definition across files, hover reduction, the warm-up on a cold file) and the two rows' rendering.

Roadmap R3 (docs/roadmap.md). Router routes and prompts have been tuned on single live probes; nothing measured whether a change made the agent better. This adds an eval harness in `sdk/scripts/eval` that runs each case as a headless engine session and checks the result.

- `@plinycode/shared`: `startVcr()` (one cassette per call, optional global patch, `stop()` restores fetch and writes recordings) and `installVcrFromEnv()` (`PLINYCODE_VCR_*`, with `CLINE_VCR_*` as aliases, no-op when unset). `initVcr` keeps its behaviour.
- Case format: `cases/<id>/case.yaml` (fixture, prompt, mode, model, maxIterations, six assertion types: `file_contains`, `file_exists`, `command_exit_code`, `no_tool_errors`, `iterations_lte`, `final_text_contains`) with `cassette.json` beside it; documented in `sdk/scripts/eval/README.md`.
- `run.ts`: one-shot `ClineCore` session per case with all tools auto-approved and an isolated engine home (temp `~/.cline`, `CLINE_*` cleared). Offline playback by default, `--record` against the live gateway. Writes `ai_output/eval/results-<ts>.jsonl` and a summary table; exits non-zero on any failure.
- Four seed cases (create a file, fix a failing `bun test`, answer a question, plan-mode markdown) with **hand-written cassettes**, since the gateway was not reachable while writing them; they should be re-recorded with `--record`.
- `engine-test.yml`: `eval-offline` job (build, typecheck the harness, run the cases, upload results). It lives under `sdk/` so the existing `sdk/**` filter, lint and format cover it.
- Docs: `docs/eval-harness.md` (why, format, offline and record runs, adding a case; next: router profiles and a live nightly).

**Finding:** the extension's proxy/CA-aware fetch (`apps/vscode/src/shared/net.ts`) captures `globalThis.fetch` at module load, so patching the global later would not intercept extension inference. The runner passes the VCR fetch explicitly; recording the extension itself would need the session factory to use the fetch `installVcrFromEnv()` returns.

**Limits:** playback replays a fixed trajectory (it validates the engine's handling, not model behaviour); router profiles are not runnable yet (their model factory lives in the extension); one run per case.

Verified: 4/4 cases pass offline; broken assertions and an exhausted cassette fail with clear messages; record mode checked against a local fake gateway. `build:sdk`, `types`, sdk lint and format, shared (383) and llms (738) tests, `check:docs` green. Not yet run on CI's Bun 1.3.14.

## Why

- **Restart from here** could leave the model seeing turns the user meant to discard. Answers to `ask_question` and rejection feedback are chat rows but tool results in the saved history, so every answer moved the cut one message too late. "Restart and revert files" also counted tool results as checkpoint runs and restored a far later checkpoint.
- Kimi K2.6 on FreeAuto wrote `<invoke name="read_files">…</invoke>` as plain text on a turn's first reply (session `1791310436747_6s0c1`). Nothing ran, the guard didn't fire, and the user had to type "please go on".
- BalanceAuto saw `terminated: SocketError: other side closed (UND_ERR_SOCKET)` mid-reply. The drop counted against Sonnet's health, the message promised "another model", and the recovery run reset the router's turn state.

## What changed

**Restart from here** (`SdkController.editMessageAndRegenerate`, `sdk-user-message-mapping.ts`, `sdk-checkpoints.ts`)
- New `answersTool` flag on `ClineMessage` (proto field 27), set on answer and rejection-feedback rows. Prompt rows are counted without those rows and checked against the row's text. When the ordinal and the text disagree, the nearest message with the row's text wins.
- Editing an answer row restarts after the question, with the answer taken out of the tool result. The edited answer goes out as the next message.
- Checkpoint runs use core's `countUserRunMessages`. Only earlier runs' checkpoints are carried over, and their refs are kept (`retainCheckpointRefs`, now exported from core) before the old session is deleted.
- Late edit diagnostics from the abandoned turns are forgotten. A refused file revert no longer cancels the running turn.
- Router and advisor state are keyed by the session's real id, read when a run starts. Before, the key was the previous session's id or the cwd, so the turn summary was missing, and the call log recorded the workspace path as its `sessionId`.
- New **PlinyCode: Show Last Model Request (debug)** command (`last-model-request.ts`).

**Tool calls written as text** (`sdk/packages/llms/src/providers/text-tool-calls.ts`)
- `createTextToolCallFilter` replaces the Kimi-only filter and runs for every model with tools. It reads Anthropic XML (with and without the namespace and the `function_calls` wrapper), Qwen3-Coder `<tool_call><function=…>`, Hermes JSON and Kimi tokens.
- Nothing is recovered when the markup is in a code fence, is followed by prose, names an unknown tool, has arguments that can't be read, comes alongside native calls, or is in a failed stream. All-or-nothing per section.
- New `text-tool-call` guard rule. It is active for paid models and on a run's first reply too, but not the judge.
- Router addendum: tool calls only through the interface; reply in the user's language.

**Dropped connections** (`router-integration.ts`, `ai-sdk-stream-events.ts`)
- The first transport error in a turn waits 2 s and retries without `recordFailure`. A second one in the same turn is a normal failure.
- A recovery run continues the turn (no `beginTurn`), so `maxFailoversPerTurn`, the call log, the classifier verdict and the reviewer's edits carry over.
- A stream cut while tool-call arguments were streaming adds `— cut off while writing a <tool> call` to its error. The continuation prompt then asks for the call to be made again rather than continued.
- Router rows use catalog names ("Claude Sonnet 5").

**Docs:** new `docs/restart-from-here.md` (linked from AGENTS.md). Updated `docs/pliny-free-auto-router.md` and `docs/pliny-balance-auto.md`.

## Testing

- `bun run build:sdk`, `bun run types`, `bun run check-types` (apps/vscode), `bun run lint`, `bun run format`, `bun run check:docs`, `bun -F plinycode-dev analyze:unused:prod`: all pass.
- Extension vitest `src/sdk/`: 90 files, 1534 passed. New tests:
  - restart mapping with answers, rejection feedback, the text check and checkpoint numbering against core's counter;
  - `forget()` on the edit-problems reporter;
  - the text-tool-call guard rule, including while inactive;
  - run recovery: transport retry, turn continuation, the lost-tool-call prompt and catalog names;
  - last-request capture.
- llms vitest: 736 passed. New `text-tool-calls.test.ts` uses the real failing replies from the user's sessions (Kimi `<invoke>`, BalanceAuto Qwen `<tool_call>`). The adapter test now covers a non-Kimi model's XML call.
- `test:unit` (bun): 997 pass, 43 fail. All the failures are in `src/core/hooks/__tests__`, caused by a stray `%TEMP%\package.json` with `"type": "module"` on this machine, which makes the CommonJS hook scripts the tests write there fail to load. Unrelated to this change.
- Not exercised in a dev host. The pre-release is for that: see "To try" in the release notes.

## Mode switch: Plan, Agent, Ask

- The **Act** mode is now labelled **Agent**. The internal value stays `act`, so settings, the wire protocol and old conversations are unchanged.
- Each mode has its own color on the selected segment and on the outline of the focused prompt box: **Plan** yellow, **Agent** red (`statusBarItem.errorBackground`), **Ask** green.
  - Before, Act used the blue focus color.
  - Ask borrowed `statusBarItem.remoteBackground`, which is blue in VS Code's current default themes, so it didn't look green either.
- User-facing text follows the new name:
  - the model-settings tabs and the "Use different models for Plan and Agent modes" option;
  - the Execute plan button and its menu;
  - the setting descriptions;
  - the ask-mode guard errors.
- The model is now told to say "toggle to Agent mode". The chat turns both that and the old "to Act mode" into the toggle link.

## Side questions (off-the-record prompts)

A **Side question** checkbox next to the mode switch marks the next message as off the record:
- The agent answers it, but later model requests leave out the question, the answer and every tool call made for it.
- The chat keeps showing the exchange, labelled **Side question · not in the context**, also after the conversation is reopened.
- The checkbox is enabled only when a conversation exists and the agent is idle, and it clears after each send.

Design and limits are in [docs/side-questions.md](docs/side-questions.md). In short:

- **Kept, then filtered.** The turn stays in `messages.json`, tagged `metadata.offTheRecord`, because the chat is rebuilt from that transcript. `dropOffTheRecordTurns` removes it before every model request and before compaction, keeping the turn while it is being answered. Manual `/compact` filters the same way, so the saved compaction state stays consistent.
- **Read-only.** While a side question runs, a `beforeTool` guard rejects:
  - file writes and file-editing commands;
  - `update_todo_list`;
  - sub-agents and teammates.

  The message goes out as `<user_input mode="ask">` in any mode. The prompt prefix and tool list don't change, so the prompt cache still hits.
- **Per-message context.** A side question does not use up the mode-switch notice. Its `<editor_state>` block is not recorded as sent, so the next normal message still gets it.
- **Routing.** FreeAuto and BalanceAuto treat a side question like plan mode, so the completion judge and the reviewer don't run on it.

### Why not subagents or a fork

- **Subagents:** the model decides when to start one, and its result lands back in the main context.
- **Fork:** a copy of the conversation keeps the original clean, but you have to switch conversations and come back.

## Testing

- **New tests:**
  - engine: the filter helper, the tool guard, the run loop (tagging, filtering, guard only during the side question), and the host passing the flag;
  - extension: follow-up routing, the send path, editor state, history replay, manual compaction;
  - webview: the checkbox, the send handler, the mode colors.
- **Checks:** `bun run types`, `lint` and `format` pass, and knip is clean.
- **Suites:**
  - Engine core 1649 passed. The local failures are the known environment-only ones in `hook-file-hooks` and the MCP client, plus a `subprocess-runner` timing test that passes when run alone.
  - Shared 372 passed.
  - Extension vitest and webview vitest pass.
  - Extension `test:unit`: only the known `src/core/hooks/__tests__` environment failures.
- **E2e:** `chat.test.ts` and `plan-execute.test.ts`, which click the renamed Agent switch, pass locally.

## FreeAuto: reasoning effort, classifier, profiles and call log

Commit `57555a4` on `lgiaccar/few_impr`

### Why
FreeAuto picked a model per call, but it never controlled *how much the model thinks*. Small edits and deep planning got the same treatment. Several free models turned out to reason on every call, which is slow, and there was no way to compare routing strategies on real use.

### What changed

**Measured reasoning controls**
- `probe-pliny-free-models.ts --thinking` asks every free model a short trick question with six variants of the request. It records whether the model reasons by default and which request field turns reasoning on or off. Results are in `docs/pliny-free-auto-thinking.md`.
- Findings:
  - GLM-5.2, nemotron-3-super, qwen3.5-397b and the qwen3-27b family reason by default. `chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking=false` turns this off.
  - qwen3-coder, kimi-k2.6 and nemotron-3-ultra never reason.
  - qwen3-8-27b, qwen2.5-32b and llama-3.1-70b answer `reasoning_effort` with a **400**. Sending a generic "think" flag to them fails the call.
- These results are stored per model in `pliny-models.json`. A new Pliny provider-option rule sends only the off-switch the probe measured for that model. Models without a measured switch are left alone.

**Reasoning effort per route**
- Routes accept `effort: quick | think` and `reasoningEffort: low | medium | high`.
- Defaults: planning uses think/high. Coding, quick questions, sub-agents and huge-context use quick. The default route leaves each model's own behaviour.
- The routing row shows what was applied, for example `route: coding · quick`.

**Classifier (smart profile)**
- A small, fast model (qwen3-6-35b, which never reasons) runs once per turn. It returns `{tier: quick|code|reason|huge, think: bool}`.
- The tier maps to a route through the rules file, so the classifier never names a model. Its think verdict overrides the route's effort.
- It doesn't run for sub-agents or requests with images. If it times out or returns an unusable reply, the heuristic routes decide.

**Profiles**
Three FreeAuto models in the picker, each with its own rules file:
- `FreeAuto`: heuristic routes with effort set per route.
- `FreeAuto · fast`: reasoning off everywhere it can be turned off.
- `FreeAuto · smart`: the default routes plus the classifier.

**Call log**
- Every routed call is appended to `~/.cline/data/pliny-free-auto-calls.jsonl`. Each entry has the profile, route, tier, effort, model, estimated tokens, time to first token, duration and outcome.
- `bun apps/vscode/scripts/summarize-free-auto-log.ts` compares profiles and models.
- New command: **PlinyCode: Open FreeAuto Call Log**.

**Also**
- Fixed the generated rules file. Its regexes were written in double-quoted YAML, which made the file invalid, so FreeAuto silently ignored it. They're now single-quoted, and a test checks that the generated YAML parses.
- Sub-agents are now on by default.

### Known limitation
The engine can only turn reasoning on through `reasoning_effort`. A model whose only on-switch is the chat template can't be made to think. The only such model (gemma-4-31b-it-29cea) isn't used by any route.

### Testing
- Extension vitest: 1380 passing. Engine `llms`: 755 passing. The bun unit suite passes.
- `bun run types` and `bun run lint` are clean.
- The thinking probe was run against the live gateway.
- Not yet tried in a live chat.

### To try it
1. Pick `FreeAuto · fast` or `FreeAuto · smart` in the model picker.
2. Watch the routing rows in the chat.
3. After a few sessions, run the summarize script to compare profiles.

## Why

In a FreeAuto run on Kimi K2.6, the model repeatedly announced a step ("Let me read the pipeline file…") and ended its reply without a tool call. Each reminder worked: Kimi called the tool on the next reply. Then it stalled again on the step after that. The completion guard handled this badly in two ways:

- Every reminder counted against the run's budget of three, including the ones Kimi obeyed. The fourth stall was accepted as the final answer.
- Escalation (a firmer reminder plus a switch to another model) only fired on two stalls **in a row**. A stall, act, stall, act run never reached that, so Kimi was never replaced.

The turn then showed a plain "Completed" while the task was half done. The first turn of the same conversation ended the same way, with no sign that the guard had stopped asking.

## What changes

`apps/vscode/src/sdk/router/completion-guard.ts`:

- **Two budgets instead of one.** There are at most 3 *unanswered* reminders per run, and a reminder followed by a tool call is refunded. A total cap of 8 reminders per run (was 3) still stops any loop. The guard detects action through the run's tool-call count, or through a gap in iterations when the host doesn't provide that count.
- **Escalate on a repeating pattern.** The 3rd stall in a run escalates even when the model acted in between (`REPEATED_STALL_REMINDER` plus `onEscalate`). The count restarts after each escalation, so the model switched in gets its own three. The existing rule still applies: a second stall in a row escalates and a third in a row is accepted.
- **Say when it gives up.** A new `onGiveUp` callback reports `repeated-stall`, `unanswered-budget` or `total-budget`. The router shows `⏹ The model stopped again after "…" · not asking again: <why>. The task may be unfinished; send a message to continue.`, and records `guardGaveUp` in the run log. `summarize-free-auto-log.ts` gets a "Guard gave up" column.

The docs (`pliny-free-auto-router.md`, `pliny-balance-auto.md`) describe the new budgets and escalation. On BalanceAuto, the pattern escalation also moves a stalling free model to the `default` route's lead, Sonnet 5.

## Tests

- `completion-guard.test.ts`:
  - replays the Kimi pattern: eight stall-then-act cycles escalate on stalls 3 and 6 and never give up, and the 9th stall hits the total cap
  - checks the unanswered budget
  - checks that `onGiveUp` fires for each of the three reasons and never on a finished reply
- `router-integration.test.ts`:
  - the stall, act, stall, act pattern switches Kimi to qwen3-coder with the `(3/8)` row
  - a third stall in a row writes the give-up row and sets `guardGaveUp`

`bunx vitest run src/sdk/router/`: 253 passed. `bun run check-types` is clean.
