hits.body:
## Why

The router models (`free-auto`, `-fast`, `-smart`, and `balance-auto` when it lands on a free model) end runs before the task is done, mostly right after shell commands. Nothing in the router decides when to stop: the agent loop ends a run on the first tool-free reply. The only safety net was a regex on the last sentence that never nudged twice in a row.

26 saved FreeAuto sessions had 71 run endings. 57 of them came right after a tool result, 44 of those after `run_commands`. The endings fall into these failure classes:

| Class | Example ending | Before |
|---|---|---|
| Announce-and-stop | "Let me check the current status of the benchmark runs:" | Caught, but kimi-k2.6 answered the nudge with the same line in 3 of 4 cases and the guard gave up |
| Wait/monitor bail-out (largest) | "I'll check again at **15:28**… Stand by!", "I cannot sit in the chat for 7–10 hours" | Missed — the model had no way to wait (`run_commands` detaches at 300 s) |
| Permission question for an action already requested | "Would you like me to run the benchmark now?" (6× in one fast session) | Missed by design |
| Readiness instead of action | "The benchmark is ready to run immediately…" after "build **and run**" | Missed |
| Leaked reasoning | 8k chars ending "…Hmm, but I just killed all PowerShell after 3:30 AM in" | Missed |
| Degenerate output | 14k chars of ` .   .   .` accepted as the final answer | Missed |

`free-auto-smart`'s classifier also produced **no verdict in any of 185 logged calls**, so smart behaved exactly like default. The likely cause is the default classifier model hitting the 256-token output cap before it got to the JSON.

## What changes

**Engine** (`shared`, `agents`, `core`): small and backward compatible
- `CompletionGuard` now also receives `runMessages` and `messages`, and may return a promise. `withHostCompletionGuard` awaits both guards.
- Guard reminders carry `displayRole: "system"`, so they no longer show up as user bubbles.
- The act and yolo prompts now say: "a reply with no tool call ends the task… never end a reply saying you will check back later; use `wait`".

**Extension router** (`apps/vscode/src/sdk/router`)
- `completion-guard.ts` (new) applies the rules from `unfinished-turn-guard.ts`, most reliable first: degenerate → after-failed-command → after-detached-command → announcement → wait-bail-out → leaked-reasoning → readiness → judge.
  - A second stall in a row gets a firmer reminder, and the rest of the turn moves to the default route's lead model (`↪ switching to …`). A third stall is accepted.
  - At most 3 reminders per run. Chat rows name the rule that fired (`rule: wait-bail-out, 1/3`).
- `router-completion-judge.ts` (new): once per act-mode run that has made at least one tool call, if no rule fired, the utility model is asked whether the request was carried out.
  - "Not done" sends one reminder (`⚖ The task looks unfinished — …`). No verdict means the reply is accepted.
  - Rules-file settings: `guard.judge`, `guard.judgeTimeoutMs`, `utility.judge` (defaults to the classifier model).
- `routed-agent-model.ts`: a reply that collapses into repetition is cut off mid-stream and the call fails, so the run continues on another model with a "redo the step" prompt.
- `router-prompt.ts` (new): free candidates get a system-prompt addendum about how their turn ends. Paid candidates see the prompt unchanged.
- `router-hooks.ts` (new) layers two hooks over the session's hook scripts:
  - `afterTool` appends a note to failed and detached shell results ("do not end your turn now: fix and rerun…").
  - `afterRun` writes one line per run to `pliny-free-auto-runs.jsonl`: how it ended, last model and tool, rules fired, judge verdict, reply tail.
- Classifier fixes:
  - Output cap raised to 512 tokens, and the prompt asks for the JSON first.
  - Parsing handles fenced JSON, nested objects and an unclosed `<think>`.
  - The raw reply is logged, and `classifierError` is recorded on the turn's first call.
- `scripts/summarize-free-auto-log.ts` reads both logs: run endings per profile/model/route, rules fired, the classifier's verdict rate, and `--tails`.

**`wait` tool** (`apps/vscode/src/sdk/vscode-wait-tool.ts`, registered for every session): up to 10 min per call and 1 h per run, and it can be cancelled. Its result tells the model to check progress with a tool call.

## BalanceAuto (merged from `stage`, #33)

Stage renamed the router helpers (`isPlinyRouterModelId`, `plinyRouterProfile`). Conflicts in `router-integration.ts`, `router-rules.ts` and `router-integration.test.ts` are resolved as follows:

- **One predicate, checked per turn.** The guard, the judge and the command note apply to a BalanceAuto turn only when a free model is answering.
- **The guard checks the main agent's last call.** Sub-agents get no completion policy, so the guard only ever judges the main agent's reply. Stage's version checked `activeTurnKey`, which after a sub-agent run points at the sub-agent. That would nudge a reply from a paid model because a free sub-agent ran earlier in the turn. Stage's BalanceAuto test is updated to that behaviour.
- **The command note follows whichever agent ran the tool.** New test added.
- **Escalation on BalanceAuto** moves a stalled free-model turn to the lead of the `default` route, which is Claude Sonnet 5.
- The prompt addendum is added per candidate (free only). Degenerate-output failover applies to every model. Runs are logged with `profile: "balance"`.
- `defaultRules` keeps both BalanceAuto's classifier and the new guard settings.

**Docs**: `docs/pliny-free-auto-router.md` gets a "Keeping runs going" section, and `docs/pliny-balance-auto.md` explains how it applies to BalanceAuto. The seeded rules file documents `guard`.

**Version** → `0.1.3-test.3` for the pre-release auto-update.

> Pre-releases follow `<next release>-test.<N>`, now documented in `docs/releasing.md`. `0.1.3-test.3` sorts above the published `0.1.3-test.2`, so editors on it will update. (An earlier revision of this PR used `0.1.3-dev.N`, which the updater treats as older than `test.2`.)

## Verification

- `bun run build:sdk` and `bun run types`: clean. Biome: clean.
- `bun -F plinycode-dev test:unit`: 1191/1191.
- Router and wait tool: 237 router tests plus 5 wait-tool tests. They cover:
  - the real transcript endings above as fixtures
  - the escalation sequence
  - failover on degenerate output
  - when the judge runs and its cap
  - run-log records
  - BalanceAuto guard and note gating
- `bun -F @plinycode/agents test`: 90/90. `@plinycode/llms`: 762 passed. Webview model filter: 18/18.
- `@plinycode/core test:unit`: 2 failures in `hub/server/index.test.ts`. They are a `HubLockHeldError` caused by a live hub on the dev machine and are unrelated to this change.

Not yet verified live:
- that `free-auto-smart`'s classifier now returns a verdict (the first row should read `classifier: code`, or another tier)
- a benchmark-style task that uses `wait`
- a BalanceAuto turn routed to a free model

After a day of use, `bun apps/vscode/scripts/summarize-free-auto-log.ts --tails` shows early-stop rates per model and profile.

# FreeAuto v2 — Phase (a) + (b) summary

Branch `lgiaccar/few_impr`, commit `9e9cddc`, pushed to `origin/lgiaccar/few_impr`.
Full design context: [freeauto-strategy-and-models.md](freeauto-strategy-and-models.md)
and the plan at `~/.claude/plans/please-lay-down-a-atomic-crane.md`.

## Phase (a) — Hygiene fixes

### Sub-agent turn-state isolation
Sub-agents (spawned via `spawn_agent`) reuse the parent session's routing
closure. Previously, a sub-agent call re-entered the same turn state as the
parent, silently resetting the parent's call log, sticky model, and failover
budget mid-turn.

**Fix:** each run is now keyed by whether `agentConfig.parentAgentId` is set.
A sub-agent run gets its own turn key (`<sessionId>:sub:<n>`); the parent's
turn state is untouched. Model health (which models are benched) stays
global, as intended — only per-turn bookkeeping is isolated. Sub-agent keys
are cleaned up automatically when the next parent turn starts.

**Visible effect:** FreeAuto routing rows from a sub-agent are now prefixed
`↳ sub-agent` in chat, so it's clear which model activity belongs to a
delegated task versus the main conversation.

### Image requests fail fast
No free Pliny model accepts image input, but FreeAuto previously routed
image-bearing requests through the normal candidate list anyway, likely
producing a confusing failure deep in the call.

**Fix:** the router now checks model capabilities up front. If a request
carries an image and no candidate supports it, the call fails immediately
with: *"FreeAuto routes only to free Pliny models, none of which accept
images. Pick a vision-capable model or remove the image."*

### Summarizer model id refresh
The compaction summarizer's model id was fixed to the built-in default at
session install time, before the rules file had actually loaded — so a
custom `utility.summarizer` in `pliny-free-auto.md` was silently ignored.
Now it updates in place once the rules file is read.

## Phase (b) — Sub-agents enabled + routing improvements

### Sub-agents turned on
`spawn_agent` was hard-disabled in the extension regardless of settings.
It's now gated on the existing `subagentsEnabled` setting, which gets a new
toggle: **Settings → Features → Advanced → Sub-agents** (off by default,
applies to new tasks).

### Spawn visibility
The PlinyCode output channel now logs a line when a sub-agent starts and
when it finishes:
```
[Subagent] spawned: <task prompt, truncated>
[Subagent] completed · in <N> / out <N> tok
```

### New `subagent` route
Delegated tasks are typically short and bounded, so a new default route
sends sub-agent calls to fast models first (`qwen3-coder-480b`,
`nemotron-3-super-120b`, `kimi-k2.6`) ahead of the general-purpose routes.

### Default route reorder (field experience + probe data)
- `qwen3-coder-480b` now leads both the `coding` and `default` routes, and
  heads the fallback pool — it's fast (356ms TTFT) and, per your testing,
  reliably good at fixing conflicts.
- `GLM-5.2` is removed from `coding` and `default` — it's slow (1279ms
  TTFT, 7.6 tok/s) and is kept only on the `huge-context` route, where its
  512k window is the only option.
- The `coding` route's trigger phrases now also catch merge conflicts,
  rebase, lint errors, and type errors (previously only fix/implement/refactor-style wording matched).

## Verification

- 1319 vitest tests + 1151 bun unit tests pass; `tsc` and Biome are clean.
- New tests cover: sub-agent turn isolation, image-request rejection, the
  `subagent` route, the reordered defaults, and the `subagentsEnabled` →
  `enableSpawnAgent` wiring.
- Not verified by this pass: live behavior against the Pliny gateway in a
  running extension host (no gateway access from this environment) — worth
  confirming manually per the checklist below.

## What to check manually

1. Enable **Settings → Features → Advanced → Sub-agents**.
2. Start a task, ask it to delegate something to a sub-agent — confirm:
   - `[Subagent] spawned` / `[Subagent] completed` lines in the output channel.
   - `↳ sub-agent` prefixed rows in chat, route shown as `subagent`.
   - The turn summary at the end still reflects only the parent's own calls.
3. Ask something like "fix the merge conflicts in X" — confirm it routes to
   `qwen3-coder-480b` under the `coding` route.
4. Paste an image while on FreeAuto — confirm the immediate error message,
   no model call attempted.
5. Your existing `~/.cline/data/pliny-free-auto.md` was regenerated (the old
   one was moved to `.bak`) so these new defaults actually apply — if you'd
   customized that file, diff it against the backup before discarding it.

## What this changes

Two features: an **Ask mode** next to Plan and Act, and a reworked **history view** with a favorites filter that works, search, date filters and pinned conversations.

### Ask mode

- The mode switch has one segment per mode: **Plan**, **Act**, **Ask**. Clicking a segment selects it. The shortcut cycles Plan → Act → Ask.
- In ask mode the agent answers questions and cannot edit any file:
  - the engine's `ask` tool preset leaves `editor` and `apply_patch` out;
  - an ask-mode `beforeTool` guard rejects any write that still reaches those tools (markdown included) and the shell commands on the file-editing blacklist plan mode already uses;
  - the ask-mode prompt tells the model to show a change in its reply and ask the user to "toggle to Act mode", which the chat renders as a link.
- Ask mode runs on the act-mode model. For FreeAuto and BalanceAuto it routes like plan mode, and the completion judge does not run.
- Switching to ask never starts a run by itself.

### History

- **Favorites filter.** `getTaskHistory` paged the history first and then filtered each page. A favorite older than the newest 50 conversations never showed, and when the first page had no match the list stayed empty. Search and the workspace filter had the same limit. It now filters the whole history (from the metadata cache) and then pages. The filter is a **Favorites** button above the list instead of an entry in the sort menu.
- **Search** matches every word typed against the title and the workspace path.
- **Date filter**: Today, Last 7 days, Last 30 days, or a custom from/to date and time. A conversation is in the period when its span from start to last activity overlaps it.
- **Pins.** A pin button on each row. Pinned conversations that match the filters are listed first, in a **Pinned** section. The Recent preview marks them with a pin.
- **Flags that last.** Favorite and pin change only through their toggles (`setTaskFavorite`, `setTaskPinned`). Other history writes carried a `HistoryItem` read earlier or built from scratch, so a usage update racing a toggle could un-star a conversation, and a checkpoint restore or an edit-and-regenerate dropped the star. Those two flows now copy the flags to the new session.

Design notes: [docs/ask-mode.md](https://github.com/lgiaccar/PlinyCode/blob/lgiaccar/history-filters-pins-ask-mode/docs/ask-mode.md), [docs/conversation-history.md](https://github.com/lgiaccar/PlinyCode/blob/lgiaccar/history-filters-pins-ask-mode/docs/conversation-history.md).

## Decisions worth a look

- The proto enum value is `PlanActMode.ASK_MODE`, because `ASK` is already taken in the `cline` package by `ClineMessageType`.
- Choosing a model while in ask mode changes the act-mode model. Ask has no model selection of its own.
- An ask-mode answer renders like an act-mode result, and switching to Act afterwards does not auto-continue. The user says what to apply.
- A pin does not protect a conversation from deletion. Favorites still do.
- Starring or pinning writes the session record, which moves its last-activity time to now. That was already the case for favorites.

## Limits

- The command blacklist is a list of common file-editing commands, not a shell interpreter. A script that writes files can get past it, as in plan mode. MCP tools are not covered by the guard; they go through the normal approval.
- A conversation that exists only as a manifest file (not in the session store) cannot be pinned or starred: the write does not stick. I saw this with hand-seeded e2e records and did not look into whether real conversations can be in that state.

## Testing

- `bun run check-types`, `bun run lint`, `bun run format`, `bun run check:docs`, `bun -F plinycode-dev analyze:unused:prod`: pass.
- Extension vitest (88 files) and webview vitest (66 files): pass. New tests cover the history query, the sticky flags, the date ranges and sections, the mode switch, and ask mode in the session factory and the mode coordinator.
- Engine tests for `shared` and `llms` pass. `core` has 5 failures in `hook-file-hooks.test.ts` and `mcp/client.test.ts`; the same 5 fail on this machine with these changes stashed.
- `bun -F plinycode-dev test:unit`: 6 files fail, all under `src/core/hooks/__tests__`, which fail on this machine without these changes too.
- Playwright e2e, run locally on Windows against the packaged build: `chat.test.ts` (now switches Act → Ask → Plan) and a new `history.test.ts` case (favorite beyond the first page, search, date filter, clear filters, pin and the Pinned section) pass. The other e2e files were not run locally.
- Not tested by hand with a real model: an ask-mode conversation end to end. The guard, the preset and the prompt are covered by unit tests.

# feat(pliny): FreeAuto model router with automatic failover

## Summary

Adds a virtual **FreeAuto** model (`pliny/free-auto`), now the default, that
picks a free self-hosted Pliny model per call from a user-editable Markdown
rules file and recovers automatically when a model misbehaves. Also adds a
Settings entry point to locate/open that rules file.

## Why

The picker exposed ~22 free models behind one fixed default, and self-hosted
models fail in ways that killed the turn and left the user on a manual Retry:
output-token truncation, stalled streams, socket deaths, empty responses, and
streams ending without a finish reason. The rules file itself was only
reachable from the command palette, which is not discoverable.

## How it works

Two generic SDK hooks carry the routing logic, both optional and inert unless
a host sets them:

- **`agentModelFactory`** builds the run's `AgentModel`, with a
  `createDefault({modelId})` escape hatch for concrete delegates.
- **`onRunError`** recovers a failed run in place. `executeRunWithAuthRetry`
  becomes `executeRunWithRecovery`, keeping the existing auth behaviour and
  adding bounded, host-driven recovery.

Failure handling splits on **whether output was already streamed**:

| Situation | Behaviour |
| --- | --- |
| Fails before any output | Next candidate takes over invisibly |
| Fails after output | Reported as a finish event; turn retried in place, continuing |

After content it never re-streams and never rethrows: a throw would escape the
agent loop before the partial assistant message is built, losing it from the
transcript and duplicating text on retry. A `run-failed` event is held back
while recovery is pending, so a recovered turn never leaves the UI in its
terminal error state.

A per-call stall watchdog covers silent streams (Pliny's own timeout is 5
minutes and covers only the whole request). Every call and turn end is
timestamped with its model in the chat and output channel.

Existing free selections migrate to the router once, guarded by a persisted
flag; paid selections are untouched. The virtual id never reaches the gateway:
compaction and commit-message generation map it to a concrete model first.

**Settings entry point:** Settings → API Configuration now has an "Open rules
file" link under the Pliny paid-models checkbox. The webview passes a
`pliny://free-auto-rules` URI to the existing `openFile` service (alongside
`remote://`); the host resolves the real path and creates the file from
documented defaults if it doesn't exist yet.

## Results

Probed all 22 free models live. **The measurements corrected three guesses:**

- Both `snps-provider-sia` models are down, so they no longer sit near the front.
- The vmodels GLM replica beat the primary, so it now leads the huge-context route.
- `qwen3-8-27b` was slow (~975 ms TTFT), so the quick route prefers
  `qwen3-next-80b` and `nemotron-super`.

**A new test caught a real hang:** the stall watchdog awaited
`iterator.return()` on a generator parked on a never-settling await, which
deadlocked the process. Fixed to abandon the stuck iterator.

### Verification

| Suite | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Extension unit (81 files) | 1120 passed, 0 failed |
| Core orchestrator | 81 passed (12 new) |
| llms (incl. Pliny catalog) | 723 passed |
| shared | 425 passed |
| agents | 87 passed |
| Extension typecheck | clean |

Verified end to end in a Cursor dev host: extension activated, wrote its rules
file, persisted the migration flag, and opened the file via the new Settings link.

## Why

A FreeAuto run in GPUSurfer ("Execute AI_prompts\run_surfer_target_cases.md", Kimi K2.6) looked like an infinite loop. Three things went wrong in a row:

1. **The model looped on one sentence.** In its 8th call Kimi wrote the right fix, then repeated the same 236-character sentence about 430 times instead of making the tool call. That ran for 104 KB and four minutes, until the 32k output cap. `looksDegenerate` only caught repeating units of 8 characters or less (`. . .`, `]]]]`), so it never fired.
2. **Command output came back mangled.** The terminal was 33 columns wide, so `run_commands` returned paths like `…\20261006_1` / `124919` for `…\20261006_124919`. One call went to a directory that didn't exist, and the next spent most of its thinking decoding paths.
3. **The model backgrounded the benchmark itself.** It launched the benchmark with `Start-Process`, and nested quoting turned `-Build "cpu_mt,cuda"` into `cpu_mt cuda`, so the script threw. The prompt asked for a `background_process` tool, which PlinyCode doesn't have, and the `run_commands` description never mentions that a long command keeps running after 5 minutes and the call returns.

## What changes

- **Repetition detector** (`unfinished-turn-guard.ts`, `routed-agent-model.ts`): `looksDegenerate` now also flags text whose end is one chunk of 9–1,500 characters repeated at least 4 times back to back (and covering at least 800 characters). It works wherever the stream stopped, including in the middle of a repeat. The routed model checks the reasoning stream as well as the reply text. Replayed against the real call 8, the old detector never fires; the new one fires at 33k of 130k characters, as soon as the drifting near-repeats settle into exact ones. The existing degenerate-output retry then takes over.
- **ConPTY line wraps** (`conptyWrapJoiner.ts`, used by `VscodeTerminalProcess`): this format comes from recordings of `powershell.exe` in a 33-column ConPTY, made with VS Code's own `node-pty`. When a long line scrolls off the bottom row, ConPTY writes `\r\n`, moves the cursor back to the row's last column (`\x1b[29;33H`) and writes that row's last character again. The joiner rejoins those rows before the output is split into lines. A cursor move only counts as a continuation when the repeated character matches, and chunks that split the sequence are held back until the next chunk.
- **Narrow terminals** (`vscode-run-commands-tool.ts`): the VS Code API doesn't expose a shell terminal's width, but the column ConPTY jumps back to does, and it's reported as `terminalColumns`. Below 80 columns the result ends with a note: the output was formatted to that width, and the model can use `Out-String -Width 300` or a file. The first time this happens in a window, the user is warned to widen the panel or switch to Background Exec. PowerShell's own layout (tables, error messages) can't be repaired after the fact. I tested widening the buffer: ConPTY then scrolls sideways and the output gets worse.
- **Long-running commands**: `createShellTool` takes an optional `longRunningNote`. In VS Code Terminal mode it replaces the generic "background it yourself" advice with: a command still running after 5 minutes keeps going and the result has a log path; don't detach it with `Start-Process`/`Start-Job`/`nohup`/`&`; follow it with `wait`.
- Docs: a `run_commands` section in `docs/agent-tools.md`, and the repetition paragraph in `docs/pliny-free-auto-router.md`.

## Testing

- `bunx vitest run --config vitest.config.ts src/sdk/router src/sdk/vscode-run-commands-tool.test.ts`: 380 passed. Includes new tests for sentence and paragraph loops, loops cut off mid-repeat, varied whitespace, near-duplicate prose and logs that must not be flagged, reasoning loops, the narrow-terminal note and one-time warning, and the long-running note per mode.
- `bun test src/hosts/vscode/terminal/conptyWrapJoiner.test.ts`: uses recorded ConPTY output (`git log` lines, colored text, lines exactly 1× and 2× the terminal width) plus continuations split at every position across chunks.
- Engine: `vitest run src/extensions/tools/definitions.test.ts`: 76 passed.
- `bun run test:integration`: 157 passing, including the `TerminalProcess` integration tests.
- `bun run check-types`, `bun run lint`, `bun run format`, `bun run check:docs`, `analyze:unused:prod`: all clean.

An audit of what goes into each model request found two problems. The context was growing with material the model no longer needed. Meanwhile, the content it did need was being cut. This PR fixes both. Pre-release: [0.1.7-test.6](https://github.com/lgiaccar/PlinyCode/releases/tag/release_0.1.7-test.6).

The router's timestamped status rows (`auto-free-smart → model (call N · route …)`) were already UI-only; they never reach the model. They are unchanged here.

## Engine

- **Old reasoning is no longer resent.** The openai-compatible provider sent every earlier turn's reasoning back as `reasoning_content` on every request.
  - Reasoning from before the current user turn is now dropped at request time (`prior-turn-reasoning.ts`, applied in the orchestrator's `beforeModel` and in the compaction size estimate). It stays in history for the UI.
  - Inline `<think>` blocks in earlier assistant text are stripped too.
  - Signed Anthropic thinking is kept.
  - Injected reminders don't count as a new turn: `isUserRunMessage` decides where a turn starts.
- **Whole tool results.** `MessageBuilder` cut every tool-result string to 8k characters (a 4k head and 4k tail), while the tools return and advertise ~48k.
  - The per-string cap is now 50k.
  - Several large entries in one result share a 64k budget, never below 8k each.
  - The cap depends only on the block's own content, so prefix caches are unaffected.
- **Plain-text tool output.** `read_files`, `run_commands` and `search_codebase` results (`{query,result,success}[]`) are sent as `<result query="…">` text, not JSON-escaped strings.
- **Earlier compaction for the routers.** Compaction reads the virtual router's `ModelInfo`, not the routed model's.
  - FreeAuto's `maxInputTokens` is now 92k, so it compacts at ~83k tokens: where the 128k tier stops fitting (`(128k − 32k) / 1.15`). It used to compact at ~230k.
  - BalanceAuto's is now 128k, so it compacts at ~115k instead of ~180k.
  - The advertised `contextWindow` values are unchanged.
- **Loop-detection notices reach the model.** The soft notice was appended to the `ConversationStore` and then overwritten by the next `replaceMessages`. It now goes through a new `consumeSystemNotice` runtime hook, as a `displayRole: "system"` message.

## Rules and skills

- **One editor's files.** A new `setInstructionHost({ editor, globalRulesDirectory })` in `shared/storage/paths.ts` narrows the rule and skill search paths.
  - VS Code gets `.github`, Cursor gets `.cursor`, Windsurf gets `.windsurfrules`.
  - `AGENTS.md`, `.clinerules`, `.cline`, `.agents` and `.claude` load everywhere.
  - The Rules panel uses the same resolvers, so it follows too.
- **One global rules folder.** `Documents/Cline/Rules` is now the only global rules folder.
  - `~/.cline/rules` is no longer read. Its files are moved to `Documents/Cline/Rules` at activation, keeping their toggles. Name clashes are left in place and logged.
  - `~/Cline/Rules` and the OneDrive guesses are dropped when the host sets the folder.
- **Scoped rules on demand.** Rules with globs, `applyTo:` or `alwaysApply: false` are listed by path for the model to read when they apply, instead of being inlined in full.
- **Size caps.** Always-on rules are capped at 12k characters each and 40k in total; the overflow is listed by path.
- The system prompt names the real editor instead of always saying "VS Code".

## Extension

- **Mention caps.**
  - `@file` is capped at 100k characters (was 400 KB).
  - `@folder` is capped at 100k characters in total; files past that are named, not pasted.
  - `@url` is capped at 50k.
  - The truncation notice now names tools that exist.
- **DevOps MCP tools only where they work.** They are offered only when the session's repo has a GitHub or Azure DevOps remote (`BuiltinMcpSource.appliesTo`).

## Testing

- New tests:
  - `prior-turn-reasoning.test.ts`
  - message-builder caps
  - `formatToolOperationResultsAsText`
  - router compaction budget
  - rule budgets and scoped listing
  - `setInstructionHost` paths
  - loop-notice hand-off
  - `instruction-sources.test.ts` (editor detection, `~/.cline/rules` move)
  - `hasSupportedRemote`
  - a folder-mention budget test (mocha, integration host)
- Engine suites pass, except the hook-file and MCP-client tests, which also fail locally on unmodified `stage` (they spawn bash and child processes).
- Extension unit tests pass, except the hook tests (the same environment issue, also failing on `stage`) and the DevOps tool tests. The DevOps tool tests only fail because the local shell sets `DEVOPS_MCP_PROVIDER=ado`; they pass with it unset.
- `bun run types`: the engine packages and the extension `src` pass. The webview has React-types errors locally, and they also appear on unmodified `stage`.
- Lint, format, knip (`analyze:unused:prod`) and `check:docs` all pass.

## PlinyCode improvements (branch `lgiaccar/few_impr`, commit `c6f5845`)

### Send button: sticky send mode
- The dropdown next to Send now **chooses a send mode** instead of sending immediately: **Send**, **Steer** (send now), **Queue** (after the current turn) or **Schedule**.
- The main button's icon shows the chosen mode (send / ⚡ / list / clock). **Enter** uses the same mode.
- The mode is remembered across reloads.
- In Schedule mode the button opens the time picker; clicking again schedules the message.

### "Maximum output token limit" error now says why
The message now names the model and the sizes involved. Example:
> Model reached the maximum output token limit before completing the turn (model X: 8,192 output tokens, cap 8,192 [model output limit]; input ≈95,000 / context window 128,000 tokens). This is the model's own output limit; switch to a model with a larger output limit or ask for smaller steps.

- The cap comes from one of four places: your **Max Tokens setting**, the **model's own output limit**, the **space left in the context window**, or the **32k default**.
- The hint changes with the cause: raise Max Tokens, switch model, or compact the task.

### "Command execution aborted" now names the command
- Example: ``Command failed: Command execution aborted (cancelled by user): `npm test` in D:\proj``
- The reason is one of *cancelled by user*, *task stopped or switched*, or *stopped after repeated errors*.
- Any output produced before the abort is kept.

### Fewer leftover terminals
- **Main leak fixed:** a terminal that couldn't be reused (for example, its change of directory couldn't be confirmed) was dropped from tracking but never closed. It is now closed once nothing is running in it.
- Idle PlinyCode terminals are **closed when a task ends** (new task or task switch).
- At most **2 idle terminals** are kept open; the least recently used are closed first.
- Agent terminals are no longer **restored when the window reloads**.
- **Never closed automatically:** a terminal still running a command, one you've typed into, or an SSH/nested shell session.
- Known limitation: if a shell never reports that a command finished, its terminal is kept open, so a running command is never killed by mistake.

### Focus no longer jumps to terminals
- Running a command still shows its terminal but **keeps your cursor where it was**. File edits already did this.

### Not included (postponed)
- **Keeping a running task alive** when you start a new task or open one from History. Today that still stops the running task. It needs background-session support and was deferred.

### Testing
- Engine typecheck and lint pass.
- New and updated tests: gateway cap source, runtime error text, aborted-command mapping, send-mode UI, and terminal cleanup (run in a real VS Code test host).
- Full suites pass: extension vitest 1,272, extension bun unit 1,151, webview 517.
- VSIX to try: `ai_output/build/plinycode-dev.vsix`

Roadmap A3 (docs/roadmap.md). A terminal command that `run_commands` stops waiting for (after 5 minutes, "Proceed While Running", or a steering message) used to leave the model a log path and nothing else. It is now registered as a background process (`p1`, `p2`, …) in a per-window registry owned by `SdkController`.

List and output are parallel reads with read approval; kill uses command approval. CI Board runs may use all three on their own processes.

It now stops every running process of the displayed conversation, and the webview's background-command flag is derived from the registry. **Behaviour to confirm:** the webview calls it on Cancel and on an interrupting message, so Cancel now also stops a dev server the model started with `background: true`.

# PlinyCode 0.1.2

Internal Synopsys release of the PlinyCode VS Code / Cursor extension.

**Package:** `PlinyCode-0.1.2.vsix`  
**Install:** Extensions -> ... -> **Install from VSIX...** -> select this folder's `.vsix` file, then reload the window.

**Gateway:** `https://snps-inference.internal.synopsys.com` (Synopsys network only)

---

## Highlights in 0.1.2 (since 0.1.1)

### Fix: "unable to verify the first certificate"

- On some machines, especially with **Cursor**, every request failed with *Cannot connect to API: unable to verify the first certificate (UNABLE_TO_VERIFY_LEAF_SIGNATURE)*, and FreeAuto kept failing over from model to model.
- The cause: the Pliny gateway does not send its intermediate certificate. Windows fills it in automatically, but the extension's runtime (Node) does not, unless the editor passes it the Windows certificate store.
- PlinyCode now ships the public Synopsys CA certificates (SNPSica2 and SNPSOfflineCA). When a certificate check fails, it retries using them together with the Windows certificate store. This only adds trust; it never turns certificate checking off.
- **No `--use-system-ca` flag or `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` setup is needed.** If you set either as a workaround, you can remove it.

### Background tasks

- Starting a new task or opening another one from **History** no longer stops the task that is running. That task keeps going in the background (up to **3** at once).
- A background task applies edits without diff previews and does not bring its terminals to the front.
- Approvals and questions that are not auto-approved are held until you return. History marks the task **Needs approval**, and a notification with an **Open** button tells you.
- When a background turn finishes, the task stops and you get a notification. Reopening the task picks up the live session and replays anything that was held.
- Deleting the task, clearing history or shutting down stops background tasks. At the limit, the running task is stopped as before, with a notice.

### Send modes

- The send button's dropdown now **picks a mode** that stays selected, instead of sending straight away. The button shows that mode's icon, and **Enter** uses it.
  - **Send** - waits for the current turn to finish if the agent is busy.
  - **Send now** - interrupts the agent's current reply. Tools that are already running finish first.
  - **Schedule** - lets you pick a time to send the message.
- The mode you pick is remembered.

### FreeAuto routing improvements

- **`qwen3-coder-480b`** now comes first in the `coding` and `default` routes and in the fallback pool.
- **`GLM-5.2`** has been removed from `coding` and `default` because it is slow. It stays on the `huge-context` route, the only one that needs its 512k window.
- The `coding` route now also triggers on merge conflicts, rebase, lint errors and type errors.
- **Image requests fail immediately** with a clear message, since no free Pliny model accepts images. Pick a vision-capable model or remove the image.
- A custom `utility.summarizer` set in the rules file is now used. Before, it was silently ignored.

### Sub-agents (opt-in)

- New toggle: **Settings -> Features -> Advanced -> Sub-agents**. It is off by default and applies to new tasks.
- A new `subagent` route sends delegated work to fast models first (`qwen3-coder-480b`, `nemotron-3-super-120b`, `kimi-k2.6`).
- Chat rows for sub-agent calls start with `↳ sub-agent`. Sub-agent calls no longer reset the main task's routing state.
- The PlinyCode output channel logs when each sub-agent starts and finishes, with its token usage.

### Model picker

- Free self-hosted models and paid hosted models now have **separate checkboxes**, both off by default.

## Problem

**Send now (steering)** waited for the end of the task instead of reaching the agent. The message was only read before the agent's next model call. Since the `wait` tool (0.1.3-test.3), the agent often spends minutes inside a `wait` (up to 600 s) or a long foreground command. So the steering message stayed queued until the task ended or was cancelled.

Evidence from the 0.1.3-test.7 log: a steering message sent at 17:24:54 sat in the queue through model calls 23–28 and ran only after the user cancelled at 17:26:12. On 0.1.2 and 0.1.3-dev.1, steering messages were consumed within ~50 ms.

## Fix

- **Engine** (`@plinycode/agents`, `@plinycode/shared`): `AgentToolContext.userMessageSignal` fires when a steering message arrives (`notifyPendingUserMessage`). It is reset when pending messages are read and at the start of each run, so a message that was already read or drained never cuts later tools short.
- **`wait`** ends early and tells the model that the user sent a new message.
- **Foreground commands** are detached the same way as **Proceed While Running**: the command keeps running in the terminal, further output goes to a log file, and the model reads the message now. The result text matches the unfinished-turn guard's "detached" detection.
- The follow-up log line now records the delivery (`queue` / `steer`).
- The Send now tooltip describes the new behaviour.
- Version bumped to `0.1.5-test.2`.

## Tests

- `agent-runtime.test.ts`: a running tool is signalled by a steer and the message is read at the next step; a steer notified between runs does not leak into the next run's tools. 84/84 pass.
- `vscode-wait-tool.test.ts`: a steer ends the wait with the explanatory result.
- `vscode-run-commands-tool.test.ts`: a steer detaches a running foreground command, and later output lands in the log.
- 5 existing `vscode-run-commands-tool` tests fail under bun on Windows with or without this change (`vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync` is missing, plus terminal-profile tests). The hook tests need `bash`.

## Problem

When a custom agent is selected in the picker before sending the first message, the correct agent-specific intro is shown in the chat. However, the agent picker dropdown immediately reverts to **"Generic Agent"** once the first message is submitted.

## Root Cause

`sdk-task-start-coordinator.ts` fires a fire-and-forget `postStateToWebview()` immediately after creating the task proxy (line 218), before `startNewSession()` has completed and before `pinAgentPath()` is called (line 245). During this first state push, `mergeTaskHistoryIntoState` builds a fallback synthetic `HistoryItem` for the just-started task — but:

1. The fallback `HistoryItem` did not include `agentPath`.
2. `sessionConfigBuilder.pinnedAgentPath(taskId)` returned `undefined` because `pinAgentPath` was called only after the async `await startNewSession()`.

So `ConversationAgentPicker` saw `currentTaskItem.agentPath = undefined`, and fell back through `propsAgentPath` (the local `selectedAgentPath` state), which may or may not be set at that point depending on render timing.

## Fix

Three changes working together:

1. **`sdk-task-start-coordinator.ts`** — Move `pinAgentPath()` (and `pinModel()`) calls to **before** the fire-and-forget `postStateToWebview()`. This ensures `sessionConfigBuilder.pinnedAgentPath(taskId)` returns the correct value during the first state push.

2. **`sdk-task-history.ts`** — Add `agentPath?: string` to `TaskProxyLike`. Include `task.agentPath` in the fallback synthetic `HistoryItem` inside `mergeTaskHistoryIntoState`, so the picker shows the correct agent even when the history record isn't persisted yet.

3. **`SdkController.ts`** — Annotate the `task` argument passed to `mergeTaskHistoryIntoState` with `agentPath: sessionConfigBuilder.pinnedAgentPath(task.taskId)`.

## Tests

- **`sdk-task-start-coordinator.test.ts`**: Verifies `pinAgentPath` is called before the first `postStateToWebview()` (invocation order assert), and that `agentPath` is stored in the history item.
- **`sdk-task-history.test.ts`**: Verifies the fallback `HistoryItem` in `mergeTaskHistoryIntoState` includes `agentPath` when the task has a pinned agent, and that it's absent for generic tasks.
- **`useMessageHandlers.test.tsx`**: Verifies `selectedAgentPath` is forwarded to `newTask` and is not cleared after the RPC resolves.

## Files Changed

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `apps/vscode/src/sdk/sdk-task-start-coordinator.ts` | Pin agent/model before first state push |
| `apps/vscode/src/sdk/sdk-task-history.ts` | Add `agentPath` to `TaskProxyLike` and fallback `HistoryItem` |
| `apps/vscode/src/sdk/SdkController.ts` | Thread `pinnedAgentPath` into task for `mergeTaskHistoryIntoState` |
| `apps/vscode/src/sdk/sdk-task-start-coordinator.test.ts` | New test for pin-before-push ordering |
| `apps/vscode/src/sdk/sdk-task-history.test.ts` | New tests for fallback `HistoryItem` agentPath |
| `apps/vscode/webview-ui/src/components/chat/chat-view/hooks/useMessageHandlers.test.tsx` | New test for agentPath forwarded to `newTask` |

## Why

In GPUSurfer (opened in Cursor), a prompt asking for a markdown table comparing pasted benchmark results showed:

```
Context: 1 rule in the prompt: `.cursor/rules/ai-output.mdc` · 25 skills: `analyze-pipeline-deltas`, `benchmark-branches`, …
```

It looked like too many skills were loaded. Running the engine's own loader against that workspace showed the opposite:

| What | How it reaches the model | Per request |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 24 skills | name + description (≤160 chars) in the `skills` tool description | ~1k tokens |
| skill bodies | only when a skill is invoked | 0 until used |
| rules | full bodies in the system prompt | **~6.7k tokens, 8 files** |

The row under-reported the rules. `rulesSection()` cut the `# Rules` section at the first `\n# `, and the first inlined rule's body opens with `# Agent Output Directory`, so every rule after it went uncounted. The same heading also reads, to the model, as a new top-level section of the system prompt outside `# Rules`.

Three more things were inflating or weakening the context:

- Cursor rules with no frontmatter (`benchmark-branches.mdc`, `testing.md`, …) were inlined. Cursor treats them as Manual rules, used only when @-mentioned.
- Flat pointer files in `.cursor/skills/*.mdc` (`→ skill: .github/skills/grilling/SKILL.md`) replaced the full `.github/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`, because `.cursor` is scanned later and the watcher is last-wins. Invoking `grilling` returned the pointer.
- Two files were UTF-16LE without a BOM (PowerShell output). Read as UTF-8 they were text full of NULs, so `clean-repo-from-untracked-files` lost its description and a rule lost its scope.

## What changes

- **Rule headings nest under the rule** (`nestRuleHeadings` in `runtime/safety/rules.ts`). Inlined bodies have their headings pushed down two levels (`# Title` → `### Title`); fenced code is left alone.
- **Accurate context row** (`instruction-context-rows.ts`). Fenced code is masked before scanning, and the row shows approximate sizes: `2 rules in the prompt (~3.4k tokens) … · 24 skills (~1.2k tokens)`.
- **Cursor rule types** (`describeCursorRuleScope`). In `.cursor/rules`, only `alwaysApply: true` is inlined. Description-only rules are listed as "apply when relevant", and Manual rules as "read it when the user mentions it or the task is about it". `.clinerules` and other folders are unchanged.
- **A `SKILL.md` folder beats a flat skill file** of the same name, through a new optional `keepExisting` hook on `UnifiedConfigDefinition`. Two flat files, or two folders, still resolve last-wins as before.
- **Skill warnings in the Skills panel.** `parseSkillConfigFromMarkdown` records `warnings` (no description; `name:` unlike the folder). They flow through `CoreSettingsItem.warnings` and `SkillInfo.warnings` (proto field 7) to a warning icon with a tooltip on the skill's row. Rows now show the skill's name rather than its parent folder, which showed `skills` for flat files.
- **`skills` tool wording.** "invoking this tool is a blocking requirement before any other response" is replaced by: invoke a skill when the user asks for the task it describes, not because the request shares a topic or a word with it.
- **UTF-16 config files** (`decodeConfigText` in the config watcher): UTF-16LE/BE with or without a BOM are decoded; everything else reads as UTF-8 as before.

`docs/pliny-free-auto-router.md` ("What the model was given") describes the new behaviour.

## Measured on GPUSurfer

| | Row says | Rules inline | Skills without description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| stage | 1 rule | ~6.7k tokens (8 files) | 2, plus 4 replaced by pointers |
| this PR | 3 rules, 18 on demand | ~5.9k tokens | 1 (`benchmark-branches`, now flagged) |
| this PR + GPUSurfer cleanup PR | 2 rules, 19 on demand | ~3.4k tokens | 0 |

The GPUSurfer side (`code-generation.mdc` was `alwaysApply: true` with globs, missing frontmatter, the UTF-16 files) is a separate PR in that repo.

## Tests

- `rules.test.ts`: Cursor rule types (alwaysApply, description-only, Manual, Windows paths, `.clinerules` untouched); `nestRuleHeadings` with fenced code, `~~~` fences and level-6 headings.
- `user-instruction-config-loader.test.ts`: the folder wins over a flat file in a later directory and in the same directory, and two flat files are still last-wins; skill warnings.
- `unified-config-file-watcher.test.ts`: UTF-8, UTF-16LE and UTF-16BE, with and without a BOM.
- `instruction-context-rows.test.ts`: a rule with nested headings and a fenced `# comment` counts correctly; size hints.

`bun run lint`, `format`, `types`, `check-types`, `check:docs` and the touched engine and extension suites pass locally. The engine's hook and MCP child-process tests fail on this Windows machine on clean `stage` too.

### Related Issue

No linked issue.

### Description

PlinyCode previously loaded memory in file order under a fixed token budget. Distillation cut proposals at 200 characters, pending proposals were easy to miss, and the conversation save limit reset after a reload.

This change adds a stable system-prompt tier and BM25 retrieval into the first user message, with `recall_memory` for later lookups. The default budget is the smaller of 4,000 tokens or 4% of the selected model's context window; explicit numeric settings remain supported, alongside percentage budgets.

- Preserve complete proposals through the 600-character entry limit and route longer explanations to topic files. Deduplicate across scopes, reject task narratives disguised as rules, and persist save counts across reloads.
- Add typed entries, organization/ADO-project group memory with overrides, and repository aliases/adoption after remote host changes.
- Add a proposals inbox, pending badges and Review banner, cleanup without distillation, and Plan/Ask decision proposals. Opt-in automatic distillation saves Normal proposals with Undo; Important proposals still require review.
- Add entry editing, deletion, pinning, scope moves, importance/type controls, filtering, `/forget`, correction/removal through `save_memory`, and draft promotion to AGENTS.md.
- Show the actual loaded and omitted entries through the context breakdown, and record selection IDs, tiers and estimated tokens in session traces. Update the memory guide and correct the dedupe/date documentation.

### Test Procedure

Validated with Bun 1.3.14:

- `bun run check`: repository lint, formatting, SDK/extension builds and all package type checks.
- Final extension/webview type checks and extension bundle rebuild.
- 151 focused host tests covering memory, session configuration, slash commands, tool policies and traces; 20 webview tests covering memory settings, proposal rows and context controls.
- `bun run check:docs`, test discovery, and `analyze:unused:prod`.
- Synthetic 32k-context fixture: estimated memory input decreased from 2,652 to 977 tokens, and changing the retrieval query preserved the system prefix. No personal memory files were accessed for this measurement.

Live VS Code/gateway smoke testing and UI screenshots were not performed.

### Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [x] Documentation update

### Additional Notes

Memory remains outside the repository. Existing untyped Markdown entries and explicit numeric budgets remain supported. Automatic saving is opt-in, and promotion opens a draft that must be reviewed and saved before the original memory is removed.

### Description

Adds the standalone PlinyCode CLI for terminal conversations and invocation from existing YAML pipelines or Python. `run` accepts prompts/files/stdin, validates caller-supplied JSON schemas, streams JSON events, and reports generated artifacts. Omitting `--model` now selects FreeAuto; explicit concrete models remain supported. MCP configuration supports stdio/SSE/HTTP, credentials use secure local storage or CI injection, and unattended tools require explicit opt-in.

FreeAuto shares the extension's built-in routing policy, defaults and stream guards through an engine module. It uses only free models, bounds failover, stops on authentication errors/cancellation, and prevents replay after partial output. A single tool-free schema repair tries a different free model. The extraction also fixes streamed authentication errors being treated as retryable model failures.

Portable Windows/Linux x64 packages include the pinned Bun runtime. Chat retains history while running and exports transcripts. There is no server, YAML job parser, persistent resume, extension memory import, or full-screen UI. Only the default FreeAuto profile is included; extension completion/reviewer passes and router-settings import remain deferred.

hits.body:
## Summary

Four chat and cost fixes. The cache fix matters most, because it cuts paid BalanceAuto cost.

### 1. Prompt cache for paid Claude models (BalanceAuto)

**Evidence.** I joined 167 local sessions' per-message `metrics` with `pliny-free-auto-calls.jsonl` to see which model served each call:

- **Sonnet 5, when it writes no text between tool calls (the usual case).** Every call reads exactly the system prompt (13,022 tokens) and writes 0, while input grows from 44K to 128K tokens. Session `1791958896107_yy670` paid $5.00 where $1.39 was needed. Across all cache-enabled Claude calls, about half the input spend was wasted.
- **`aws-bedrock-vmodels/claude-4-6-sonnet-*-thinking` (BalanceAuto's planning route).** 0% cache reads and 0% writes, on every version.

**Root causes**

- `withContentBlockCacheBreakpoints` only marked user/assistant text. A tool-only assistant turn goes out as `content: null`, so the moving breakpoint fell back to the prompt that opened the turn. The function hasn't changed since #41. Hit rates swung with how much the model narrates: Sonnet 4.6 narrates more than Sonnet 5, so it hit more often.
- The thinking presets had no `cache_control` in `pliny-models.json`, so no breakpoints were sent for them at all.

**Fixes**

- Breakpoints now go on three places:
  - the system prompt
  - the newest message, usually the latest tool result, as a content-block marker on the tool message
  - the end of the previous step, so the previous call's cache entry is found even beyond Anthropic's 20-block lookback
- I measured on the live gateway that it honours a content-block marker on a tool message. It drops message-level markers, which the old comment had generalised to all tool-message markers.
- The thinking presets are flagged `cache_control`, with Sonnet cache prices. Both cache on the gateway, and its `costInUSD` matches $0.30 read / $3.75 write per million tokens.

**Live gateway, Sonnet 5, 4 agent steps** (`apps/vscode/scripts/probe-pliny-prompt-cache.ts`):

| step | legacy read / write | fixed read / write | uncached tokens (fixed) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 0 / 4,570 | 0 / 6,796 | 2 |
| 2 | 4,570 / 0 | 6,796 / 2,222 | 2 |
| 3 | 4,570 / 0 | 9,018 / 2,222 | 2 |
| 4 | 4,570 / 0 | 11,240 / 2,222 | 2 |

**Free models.** They report `cached_tokens: 0` from the backend. Parsing is correct, and they cost $0, so I left them unchanged.

**Follow-up, not done here.** `dropPriorTurnReasoning` rewrites the previous turn's unsigned reasoning at each new user turn. Now that the thinking presets are cached, that costs one cache miss per user turn on them.

### 2. Token usage panel (task header, under the context bar)

- **Bars:** one stacked bar per LLM call (cache read / cache write / input / output) for the last 80 calls. Hovering a bar shows that call. The colours are categorical slots that pass a colour-blindness check on VS Code's dark surface; on light mode the legend and text labels carry the values.
- **Summary:**
  - models, with call counts
  - calls and cost (shown only where the provider shows cost)
  - In, Out and Reason tokens
  - Cache R, W and hit rate
  - a line for sub-agent and advisor usage
- **Data plumbing:**
  - `routed-agent-model.ts` tags usage events with the model that served the call.
  - `AgentTokenUsage.modelId` carries it into saved message metrics. The live usage event's `reasoningTokens` and `modelId` go to `ClineApiReqInfo`, and history replay reads both back.
  - Older conversations show the router's own name.

### 3. Prompt navigation arrows

**Causes of the misses and no-ops**

- Prev/next used Virtuoso's `rangeChanged.startIndex`. That index includes the 3000px `increaseViewportBy` band above the view, so it pointed well above what the user was looking at.
- Prev/next never disabled auto-scroll, so streaming pulled the view back to the bottom.
- The scroll-to-bottom button mounted and unmounted, which shifted the stack under the cursor.

**Fix**

- Prev/next now read the top row from the DOM.
- They disable auto-scroll.
- They step from the last target while a smooth scroll is still running.
- They use `align: start` under the sticky header, and jump without animation to rows that aren't rendered.
- Prev above the first prompt goes to the top; Next past the last prompt goes to the bottom.
- The buttons sit in fixed slots: top, prev, next, bottom. The bottom button is hidden, not unmounted.
- The scroll listener does one layout read per frame. The scrollbar marker highlight uses the same top row.

### 4. Reloaded conversations lose prompt highlighting

- Replaying all local sessions found no case where a typed prompt became agent text. What does go missing on reload is any user text that is persisted only inside a tool result:
  - answers to `ask_question`
  - feedback typed when rejecting a tool
- Both are now rebuilt on replay, as the live path shows them: `ask:"followup"` with `selected` set, then `user_feedback` with `answersTool` set.
- A `say:"task"` row inside the list now renders with the prompt frame instead of as markdown.
- Not fixed: the session-start sanitizer can drop message metadata and merge user blocks. The safe fix is to keep each non-tool-result user message separate; that is left for a follow-up.

## Testing

- `bun run types`, `bun run lint`, `bun run format`, `bun run check:docs` and `analyze:unused:prod` pass.
- **llms:** 737 passed (the one failure was the preset-cache test; it is now updated). **shared:** 373 passed.
- **core:** 1,660 passed. 5 tests fail locally, in `hook-file-hooks` and `mcp/client`. Their temp `.js` fixtures hit Node 26 ESM `require`; this is an environment issue in untouched code.
- **Extension vitest:** 1,739 passed. **Webview vitest:** 579 passed.
- **Extension bun unit suite:** passes except the `src/core/hooks/__tests__` files, which fail with the same hook-script environment issue.
- **New tests:**
  - breakpoint placement
  - catalog cache flags
  - adapter reasoning and modelId
  - router usage tagging
  - replay of answers and rejection feedback
  - prompt navigation against a DOM fixture
  - fixed button slots
  - token panel and its helpers
- Live-gateway probe as in the table above.
- Not yet checked in the dev host.

Roadmap A9 (docs/roadmap.md). Fixes three ways usage went missing from a conversation's cost, and splits the token panel's side usage by source.

**Root causes found**
1. Sub-agent events carried no agent id, so the engine added a sub-agent's usage to the root's turn usage and then dropped it at turn end (the end-of-turn total is rebuilt from the root's own result). Sub-agent usage only came back on resume, through the message files; a failed or timed-out sub-agent persisted no messages, so its cost was lost for good.
2. Background tasks expected `parentAgentId` on sub-agent events, never got it, and counted sub-agents twice (usage events plus tool-result totals).
3. The engine and the extension both write `metadata.totalCost`; the engine's root-only write at turn end could land last and drop advisor, compaction and sub-agent cost from the history list (the task header was unaffected: it sums chat rows).

**Engine:** the progress reporter tags forwarded events with `agentId`/`parentAgentId` (`spawn_agent` and `subagent_<name>`). A finished or failed sub-agent's totals (output figures on success, progress sums on failure) are settled into the session's aggregate under its id (`settleSubAgentUsage`), so it counts once, including after a resume. A turn that throws still persists the usage it built up.

**Extension:** advisor and compaction usage live under `extraUsage`, which the engine never writes. The history list (and the cost/token sorts) reads the engine's aggregate plus `extraUsage`, or the extension's running totals when larger, so history matches the header. Old sessions read as before. Background tasks also record compaction usage.

**Token panel:** Sub-agents, Advisor and Compaction each get a labelled line (×N, tokens, cost).

Docs: advisor-tool (race caveat replaced; a narrower background-task window remains, documented), prompt-cache, agent-tools, context-compaction.

Tests: 4 new core tests (counted once with repeated end and late events; settled from the result; kept when the turn fails; resume + re-aggregation does not double count), 2 spawn-tool tests, 4 history tests (history total == header total whichever write lands last; background advisor cost survives; old sessions), coordinator/background updates, panel tests. build:sdk, types, lint, format, check-types, test:vitest, test:webview, test:discovery, knip, check:docs pass; core test:unit has only the 5 pre-existing local-environment failures.

Dev-host check pending: a paid-model conversation with a sub-agent, an advisor call and /compact; compare header and history totals before and after a reload, and with the task in the background.

## Why

A report said Qwen3 Coder 480B (`snps-provider/qwen3-coder-480b-a35b-inst-fp8`), a free self-hosted model, was being billed. I could not reproduce that:

- the catalog prices every `snps-provider*` model at $0, and the budget check and paid-call cap already count them as free;
- the live gateway's replies for Qwen3 Coder (streamed and not) carry token counts and no cost, in the body or in the `x-litellm-response-cost` header;
- every one of the 139 Qwen3 Coder calls in the local router log, and the 139 replies in the local traces, recorded $0.

Two places would still have counted a cost if the gateway ever reported one for a free model. This PR closes them.

## What changes

- `router-integration.ts`: `callCostUsd` returns 0 for a self-hosted model. Before, it used the gateway's figure when there was one. This affects the router's call and run logs and the sub-agent spend in them.
- `one-shot-model-call.ts`: `resolveCallUsage` returns `totalCost: 0` for a self-hosted model. This covers the advisor, image descriptions and Improve prompt. Before, a gateway-reported cost was used as is.

The conversation's own cost (the task header and history) still takes the engine's usage figure. That figure is the gateway's cost, else the catalog price (which is $0 for these models), so it would show a cost only if the gateway started reporting one.

## Tests

- New `one-shot-model-call.test.ts`: a self-hosted model is free with or without a reported cost, and a paid model keeps its reported cost or is priced from the catalog.
- New case in `router-integration.test.ts`: a free model's call is logged at $0 when the gateway reports $0.005.
- Both new cost cases fail without the fix and pass with it (42/42 in the two files). `check-types` and Biome are clean.

Third wave of the context-management audit (`docs/context-management-audit.md`), stacked on #125; retarget to `stage` once that merges. Sub-agents were nearly useless in the extension and their cost was invisible; this makes `spawn_agent` a real delegation primitive.

## Changes

**Engine (`sdk/packages/core`, `sdk/packages/shared`)**

- **A real system prompt.** A sub-agent got only the text the parent model wrote. It now gets the same base prompt as a root session (environment block with the conversation's git snapshot and pinned date, the session's mode), a short account of its role, the parent's instructions as rules and a host-supplied suffix (`subagent-prompts.ts`). The Cline CLI provider keeps its override shape.
- **Delegation guidance.** A rules extension (`subagent-guidance.ts`) adds a "Delegating to sub-agents" section to the system prompt while `spawn_agent` is in the request: when to delegate, what the sub-agent knows, what to put in `task`.
- **Tool input and output.** `task` plus optional `instructions` (`systemPrompt` kept as the older name); the description says what the tool is for and not for. The output carries cache tokens and `totalCost`.
- **Live progress and cost.** `createSubAgentProgressReporter` wraps the sub-agent's events and calls the parent tool call's `emitUpdate` after each model call and tool with `subAgentId`, tool count, tokens, cost and context size. Configured `subagent_<name>` agents use the same reporter.
- **Limits.** At most 3 runs in flight per tool (a semaphore), 20 minutes per run with a derived abort signal (the `timeoutMs` field was never enforced), 40 iterations by default (`subAgentMaxIterations`), delegation one level deep (`MAX_SUB_AGENT_DEPTH`), and the session's compaction (`prepareTurn`) for sub-agent runs.
- **Policies and approval** are threaded into sub-agent and configured-agent runs (`createSessionSpawnTool` options, `RuntimeBuilderInput.subAgentPrepareTurn`); the host's approval wrapper is shared by the lead and its sub-agents.
- **Host tools for sub-agents.** `CoreSessionConfig.subAgentExtraTools`: the built-in shell is suppressed in the extension in favour of its own `run_commands`, which lived in `extraTools`, so sub-agents had no shell at all.
- **Run identity for hosts.** `agentModelFactory` receives `agentId`; `onRunError` receives `agentId` and `parentAgentId`.

**Extension (`apps/vscode`)**

- Sub-agents get `run_commands` (always in the background executor), `wait`, the task list and MCP tools; not the advisor or the memory tools (`SUB_AGENT_DENIED_TOOLS`). `subAgentPrompt` carries the IDE, platform, snapshot, date and a read-only excerpt of the repository's important memory entries (`renderSubAgentMemoryExcerpt`, ≤ 2k chars).
- **Cost accounting.** The translator handles `spawn_agent` and `subagent_<name>` alike (`isSubAgentTool`), reads cost and cache tokens from the result into the `subagent_usage` row (disjoint buckets like the root's), and keeps the engine's agent id per entry. Background tasks record a sub-agent's totals from its tool result.
- **Approval.** A new **Delegate to sub-agents** auto-approve toggle (`useSubagents`, default on; `state.proto` field 9); a sub-agent's own calls follow the existing toggles, and its approval asks are preceded by a row naming the sub-agent (`describeAgent`).
- **Router per-run state.** `activeTurnKey` and `recoveringRootRun` were one closure shared by parallel sub-agents; a root failure after a sub-agent run benched the sub-agent's model. Runs are keyed by agent id (`runsByAgent`, `recoveringRuns`); hooks look up by the snapshot's agent id.

## Verification

- `bun run check`, `bun run check:docs`, knip: pass (two interfaces from wave 1 un-exported for knip).
- Core: team, host, orchestration and agent suites, 429 pass. Extension vitest: 1736 pass.
- New tests: `subagent-prompts.test.ts`, `spawn-tool.test.ts` (extra tools, no nested spawn, policies/approval/compaction threaded), `memory-section.test.ts`, translator sub-agent cost row, background sub-agent usage, router per-run keys, tool policy toggle.
- Docs: new "Sub-agents" section in `docs/agent-tools.md`; `memory.md`, `environment-context.md`, `advisor-tool.md`, `pliny-balance-auto.md`, the audit.

Not verified in the dev host yet: a real delegation on FreeAuto showing live cost in the SubagentStatusRow and a sub-agent running a command.

## Summary

Three improvements to the custom-agents feature that make it work like the skills feature:

### 1. Multi-vendor agent file discovery

`resolveAgentConfigSearchPaths()` in `sdk/packages/shared/src/storage/paths.ts` now scans four vendor directories instead of only `.cline/agents`:

- `.cline/agents` (PlinyCode)
- `.cursor/agents` (Cursor)
- `.github/agents` (GitHub Copilot)
- `.claude/agents` (Claude Code)

The new `EXTERNAL_AGENTS_CONFIG_DIRS` constant (exported from `@plinycode/shared/storage`) lists all four, paralleling `EXTERNAL_RULES_CONFIG_DIRS`.

### 2. `chat.agentFilesLocations` from `.vscode/settings.json`

A new host helper `apps/vscode/src/hosts/vscode/agent-file-locations.ts` reads the `chat.agentFilesLocations` VS Code workspace setting and returns extra agent search paths. `refreshAgents.ts` passes these into `resolveAgentLocations()` so user-defined directories are included in discovery.

### 3. Agent selector in the new-task UI

A compact **Agent:** `<select>` dropdown appears above the chat textarea when:
- The current mode is `act` (Agent)
- At least one enabled agent is discovered

The selected agent's system-prompt body is prepended to the main session system prompt when the task starts. Choosing "Generic" (default) uses the unmodified system prompt.

Implementation:
- `AgentPicker.tsx` — new webview component
- `AgentStateEntry` — new lightweight type in `ExtensionState` (avoids proto dependency)
- `globalAgents` / `localAgents` fields added to `ExtensionState` and populated in `getStateToPostToWebview`
- `agent_path` field added to `NewTaskRequest` proto
- `agentPath` threaded through `newTask.ts` → `sdk-task-start-coordinator` → `SessionConfigInput` → `buildSessionConfig` in `cline-session-factory.ts`, which reads and parses the agent file with `parseConfiguredAgentConfig`
- `selectedAgentPath`/`setSelectedAgentPath` added to `ChatState` and reset after task send

## Files changed

| Area | Files |
|------|-------|
| SDK paths | `sdk/packages/shared/src/storage/paths.ts`, `index.ts`, `paths.test.ts` |
| Agent discovery | `configured-agents.ts`, `refreshAgents.ts`, new `agent-file-locations.ts` |
| Proto | `proto/cline/task.proto` |
| Task start | `newTask.ts`, `sdk-task-start-coordinator.ts`, `cline-session-factory.ts` |
| State | `ExtensionMessage.ts`, `getStateToPostToWebview.ts` |
| Webview | new `AgentPicker.tsx`, `InputSection.tsx`, `InputSection.test.tsx`, `useChatState.ts`, `useMessageHandlers.ts`, `useMessageHandlers.test.tsx`, `chatTypes.ts` |

## Testing

- CI runs `bun run protos` as part of `check-types`, regenerating the TypeScript from the updated `.proto` file
- Updated mocks in `InputSection.test.tsx` and `useMessageHandlers.test.tsx` keep existing tests passing
- `paths.test.ts` has new tests for the expanded search paths

hits.body:
Fourth wave of the context-management audit (`docs/context-management-audit.md`), stacked on #126; retarget to `stage` once that merges. Compaction robustness and a context bar that tells the truth. New doc: `docs/context-compaction.md`, linked from `AGENTS.md`.

## Changes

- **Agentic compaction falls back to basic when it declines.** The agentic strategy never cuts before the latest typed prompt and folds nothing twice, so once everything before that prompt was summarized it returned nothing, and the request went out over budget until the provider rejected it (one overflow recovery per run, then the run ended). Basic compaction, which can trim inside the latest turn, now runs whenever agentic declines, including when the summarizer answers with no text. A summary that leaves the request over the trigger is not retried at once: the next model call compacts again and lands in this branch.
- **"Still too large" is said, not discovered.** When basic compaction leaves the request over the trigger (one typed message alone is too big), the engine emits `compaction-insufficient` and the chat shows an info row with the sizes.
- **The summarizer's cost is recorded.** `generateSummary` collects the stream's usage; the compaction result, the completed notice and the summary message's metadata carry `summarizerUsage`; the extension emits a `subagent_usage` row with `source: "compaction"` live and rebuilds it from the summary message on reopen.
- **Images count as images.** `serializeForTokenEstimate` replaces base64 blobs and data URLs with a placeholder worth `IMAGE_TOKEN_ESTIMATE` (1,600 tokens) in the request estimate, the compaction estimator and the context breakdown. A 1 MB screenshot was ~350k tokens, which triggered compaction and dropped the output-token clamp. Detection requires mixed base64 character classes, so long identifiers and hex digests stay text.
- **Context breakdown rules bucket.** The engine passes the rules it composed as request metadata (`AgentConfig.contextSources`); the provider's usage report already reads it. Skills/workflows buckets are still 0 (noted in the doc).
- **Threshold marker on the context bar.** The bar divides by the advertised window, while compaction fires at 90% of the input limit (FreeAuto: ~83k of 256k). `autoCompactThresholdFor` computes the share; the bar draws a marker with the token count; the hover card explains it in place of the old "click the bar to set a threshold" copy (no such control exists).
- **Cache breakpoint probe.** `PLINYCODE_CACHE_MARK_TOOL_CALLS=1` marks text-less tool-call messages with a one-character text so the moving breakpoint can follow a tool loop. Off by default until measured.

## Verification

- `bun run check`, `bun run check:docs`, knip: pass.
- Core: 1670 pass; the same 5 environment-only failures as before (hook tests need `bash`, MCP tests break on a stray `%TEMP%\package.json`). Shared 376, llms 737, extension vitest 1739, webview 552: pass.
- New tests: compaction fallback (nothing to fold, next-call trim, reasoning-only summarizer, insufficient notice, summarizer usage), `tokens.test.ts`, cache probe, translator compaction usage/insufficient/replay rows, context bar marker, summary copy, threshold helper.

Not verified in the dev host yet: a FreeAuto conversation past the 92k budget compacting instead of failing, and the marker's position.

hits.body:
## Prompt bubbles you can resize

Long prompts used to show at full length, so the conversation's first prompt in the task header could fill the view. The edit box sized itself by counting newlines, and its `resize-vertical` class doesn't exist in Tailwind v4, so it couldn't be resized.

- Prompts in the chat are cut to about 14 lines (the task header's to about 9), with a scrollbar to read the rest.
- A grip on the bottom edge drags a prompt taller or shorter, from two lines up to the whole prompt. Double-clicking the grip (or Enter on it) switches between the whole prompt and the default height, and the arrow keys resize it from the keyboard. The height is kept per message, so it survives scrolling and folding the header. Using the grip or the scrollbar doesn't open the prompt for editing.
- The edit box opens fitted to the prompt (up to half the view), grows as you type, and can be resized by dragging its corner.

New component: `ResizablePromptText.tsx`, used by `UserMessage`.

## {} prompt after Restart from here

`editMessageAndRegenerate` added the kept rows and the edited prompt to the new task **without `seq`/`epoch` stamps**, after several awaits. The webview's reducer drops rows from an older epoch, and an unstamped row counts as epoch 0. When a state post (or a row of the new turn) reached the webview before the restart's snapshot, the kept rows and the edited prompt were dropped. The new turn's first `api_req_started` row, whose text is `{}`, then became row 0, and the task header rendered it as the conversation's prompt.

Fixes:
- **`SdkController.editMessageAndRegenerate`**: the rows are put on the new task through the message coordinator (so they're stamped with the new epoch) right after the task is installed, before any await. The edited row's id comes from the shared id minter, not `Date.now()`.
- **`SdkController.getStateToPostToWebview`**: the transcript and its epoch are read together. The epoch used to be read after several awaits, so a snapshot holding the old transcript could carry the new epoch.
- **`messageReducer.applyStateSnapshot`**: if a row of the new epoch arrives first, the reducer keeps the old transcript under the new epoch. A same-epoch snapshot now drops the rows from older epochs it doesn't contain (the abandoned turns) and takes the snapshot's order. Rows of the current epoch are still never removed.

`docs/restart-from-here.md` has a new section on this.

## Tests

- New `ResizablePromptText.test.tsx` (grip visibility, drag limits, height kept across remounts, double-click, keyboard, no edit on grip use) and restart race cases in `messageReducer.test.ts`.
- Webview vitest: 80 files, 600 tests pass. `bun run check-types` (extension and webview) passes. Biome is clean on the changed files.
- `bun -F plinycode-dev test:unit`: 6 hook test files fail. They fail the same way on unmodified `stage` on this Windows machine (an environment issue: they need `bash`).
- Not yet checked in a dev host: dragging the grip, and restarting from a prompt several times in a row.

Desktop supports ordinary folders and local-only Git worktrees, but projects saved before 0.1.4 still defaulted to remote mode after upgrading. This change migrates entries without a saved source setting to Local branch when no remotes exist, while preserving explicit choices and source files.

Add native Copy controls for prompts/responses, right-click copy/paste, and Edit and restart on earlier prompts. Restart replaces the selected prompt and removes later messages from the active chat and model context without reverting files or external actions. It preserves prior model/tool context using pre-turn snapshots, starts a fresh engine session, and archives the old chat. Legacy chats use a unique matching prompt; ambiguous or compacted-away prompts fail without modifying the original chat. Active tasks, background commands and PR operations block restart.

The PR includes the local-worktree fix published in 0.1.4 and prepares Desktop 0.1.5 with migration and chat controls. Earlier commits remain available at desktop-v0.1.4.

Validation:
- Real Electron tests passed for native clipboard copy/paste, legacy prompt editing, repeated restart, subsequent model context and reopening without discarded turns.
- A persisted legacy local-only project migrates automatically and successfully retries its missing-origin task.
- All 51 Desktop unit tests and 3 browser protocol tests passed locally. Targeted tests cover retained tool results, snapshot redaction, archived revisions, ambiguous history and active-work guards.
- The existing full Electron suite passed for ordinary folders, worktrees, approvals, browser/MCP, background commands, delegation, saved history and GitHub/Azure PR controls.
- Desktop typecheck, formatting/build and documentation checks passed. All 26 PR checks passed on c022e7ab8f309e43d8de77b50cda13d4f6d4608f. Windows and Ubuntu 22.04/24.04 packages, actual self-update, corrupt-download recovery and saved history passed in [desktop-test](https://github.com/lgiaccar/PlinyCode/actions/runs/45058459169). The [upgrade from 0.1.4](https://github.com/lgiaccar/PlinyCode/actions/runs/45058459262) also passed.

No changes were made to Magik's files, Git configuration or running Desktop state. Leave this PR open for review.

Published [Desktop 0.1.5](https://github.com/lgiaccar/PlinyCode/releases/tag/desktop-v0.1.5) from this exact tested commit. All seven uploaded assets matched SHA-256; updater metadata matched binary SHA-512. Anonymous metadata, checksum and installation-guide downloads were verified. The editor latest release remains unchanged.
