Restart from here keeps later turns out of context, text-written tool calls run, dropped connections retry (0.2.0-test.1) (#118)

* Restart from here keeps later turns out of context; text-written tool calls run; dropped connections retry

Restart from here (editMessageAndRegenerate):
- Answers to ask_question and rejection feedback are tool results in the
  saved history, not user messages. Their chat rows now carry answersTool and
  are left out of the prompt count, which previously cut the history one
  message too late after every answer, so the model kept the original turn.
- A prompt row maps to its persisted message by ordinal and text, falling back
  to the nearest message with the row's text (queued prompts that never ran).
- Editing an answer row restarts after the question with the answer taken out
  of the tool result, and sends the edited answer as the next message.
- Checkpoint runs are numbered with core's countUserRunMessages. The extension
  counted every role-"user" message, tool results included, so "Restart and
  revert files" restored a much later checkpoint.
- Only checkpoints of earlier runs are carried over, and their refs are kept
  before the old session is deleted. Late edit diagnostics of the abandoned
  turns are forgotten. A refused file revert no longer cancels the running turn.
- The router keys its state by the session's real id (read when a run starts),
  so the turn summary appears and the call log records the conversation id.
- New "Show Last Model Request (debug)" command opens the last request the
  active conversation sent (system prompt, compacted messages, tools).

Tool calls written as text:
- createTextToolCallFilter (llms) turns Anthropic <invoke>, Qwen3-Coder
  <tool_call><function=…>, Hermes JSON and Kimi token sections in a reply into
  real tool calls, for every model; markup in code fences, followed by prose,
  naming unknown tools or with unreadable arguments is left as text.
- New text-tool-call guard rule, active for paid models and the first reply too.
- The router addendum tells free models to call tools only through the
  interface and to reply in the user's language.

Dropped connections (BalanceAuto/FreeAuto):
- The first transport error in a turn waits 2s and retries without counting
  against the model's health; a recovery run continues the turn (call log,
  failover budget, classifier, edits) instead of starting a new one.
- A stream cut while tool-call arguments were streaming says so, and the
  continuation prompt asks for the call to be made again, not continued as text.
- Chat rows name models by catalog name ("Claude Sonnet 5").

Docs: restart-from-here.md (new), pliny-free-auto-router.md, pliny-balance-auto.md.

Error feedback after edits, edit recovery, file search, a task list, environment context, a reviewer and an advisor, plan executors and a CI watcher (0.1.9-test.2) (#113)

* Recover from near-miss edits, scope searches, find files by name, and run read-only tools together

editor:
- An old_text that differs from the file only in indentation depth or
  trailing whitespace now matches, when it fits exactly one place; new_text
  is shifted to the file's indentation and the result says so. Tabs against
  spaces, or a different shift per line, is not guessed at.
- When old_text is not found, the error quotes the closest lines of the file
  and the first line that differs, instead of only "text not found".
- When it matches several places, the error lists the lines.
- replace_all replaces every occurrence.
- The VS Code diff preview uses the same matcher, so it shows these edits.

search_codebase:
- path limits the search to a directory or a file (every match is shown for
  a single file), and glob limits the file names.

find_files (new tool, enabled with search_codebase):
- Finds files by glob, or by part of the path when the pattern has no
  wildcards, ignoring case. Lists through ripgrep when one is available and
  walks the directory otherwise. The extension passes VS Code's ripgrep and
  auto-approves it with the other read tools.

Read-only tools run concurrently:
- read_files, search_codebase, find_files and fetch_web_content are marked
  parallel, so several in one model response overlap instead of queueing.
- The chat translator kept one "current tool"; it now keeps every open tool
  by call id, so concurrent tools finish into their own rows. A stale
  completion still cannot displace a running command's row.

* Give the model a task list it keeps and the user sees

update_todo_list is a new tool the extension adds to every session. The
model sends the whole list each time, each task pending, in_progress or
completed, and gets back the count and what is in progress or next. A long
run on a small model otherwise loses track of the steps it has not done.

- Input is read leniently: a markdown checklist in one string, bare strings,
  and other names for the fields are accepted rather than costing a turn.
- The chat shows the list after each update, as a task_progress message
  rendered by the new TodoListRow. That message type was left over from the
  removed focus chain and was hidden; old conversations that carry a
  markdown checklist in it render too.
- docs/agent-tools.md describes this tool and the editing and search
  behaviour from the previous commit.

* Hand the completion guard the run's abort signal, so a guard that waits on a model call stops when the run is cancelled.

* Have a second free model review the diff before a routed act-mode run ends, and hand likely defects back to the working model once.

* Give the model a git snapshot of the conversation's start and the editor state with each message

The system prompt's <env> block gains the branch, default branch, a short status and the last 5 commits, gathered once per conversation within 2 seconds and kept in the session record so rebuilds and resumes reuse it. hits.message:
Merge pull request #189 from lgiaccar/improve-pliny-chat-interface

Related Issue
Issue: No linked issue; this work follows the PlinyCode chat-interface review and user feedback.

Description
This branch makes PlinyCode conversations easier to read and navigate without removing access to the agent's work. The goal is an answer-first chat: users should be able to find their prompt and the resulting answer quickly, then inspect reasoning, tools, edits, and command output when they need the details.

1. Keep answers visible and put process details behind Show activity
Reasoning, tool calls, progress, and automatic file-edit records are grouped under a collapsed Show activity control. The final answer stays visible, including answers delivered as several adjacent text blocks. Expanding activity shows the original records in their original order; collapsing it returns to the shorter reading view. Expansion state is retained as rows scroll out of and back into view, within the current chat view.

The latest fix closes a gap in that behavior: completed terminal commands and their output now collapse too, including commands that exit with an error. Previously, command rows were unconditionally exempted from activity grouping, so a completed command could still occupy the main conversation. Running commands remain visible for progress and cancellation, and pending command approvals remain visible for user action. A failed command's output remains available inside activity; standalone error notifications are not hidden by this change.

Actionable file approvals, memory proposals, hook notices, and standalone errors remain visible. User prompts and CI watcher reports remain separate from the agent's process details. The compact working indicator also avoids a duplicate waiting row when activity already communicates that work is in progress.

2. Make thinking an explicit, accessible disclosure
Thinking no longer forces itself open just because reasoning is streaming. Users can open or close it themselves, including while the model is working. The disclosure exposes its expanded state to assistive technology and supports keyboard interaction. Open streaming reasoning follows new content; reopening completed reasoning starts from the beginning rather than jumping to its end.

3. Improve Markdown reading quality
Assistant answers are no longer clipped by the generic three-line paragraph preview rule. More consistent heading, paragraph, list, quote, and link styling provides a clearer reading hierarchy. Wide code and tables scroll within the message instead of forcing the conversation wider. Table scroll regions can receive keyboard focus. Existing Markdown content and controls, including code copying, remain available.

4. Make follow-ups and side questions easier to distinguish
Visible, labeled turn boundaries separate follow-up prompts and side questions from the preceding answer. Replies to tool approvals are not mistaken for new user turns or sticky prompts. Boundaries stay attached to existing message rows, preserving message timestamps and virtualized-list indices rather than introducing synthetic chat messages.

5. Keep the development preview reliable
F5 readiness now waits for the required builds, and a successful companion bundle cannot mask a failed extension build. Protobuf generation stages output before updating live files, replaces only changed content, and avoids exposing half-written generated files to watchers. This reduces transient missing-import failures during development; it does not change the wire protocol.

These changes are presentation and development-workflow improvements, not changes to model selection, tool execution, approval policy, or stored conversation content.

Test Procedure
Validation for the latest pushed fix, commit 46e306a, on Windows:

From the repository root, bun run check — passed. Includes lint/proto lint, formatting, SDK build, extension/webview build, and all package typechecks.
From apps/vscode/webview-ui, bun run test — passed: 772 tests across 94 files.
From apps/vscode/webview-ui, bun run test src\components\chat\chat-view\utils\activityGroups.test.ts src\components\chat\chat-view\components\messages\MessageRenderer.activity.test.tsx src\components\chat\chat-view\components\layout\MessagesArea.test.tsx — passed: 24 tests.
From the repository root, bun -F plinycode-dev check-types — passed.
From the repository root, bun -F plinycode-dev build:webview — passed.
From the repository root, bun run check:docs — passed.
Normal commit hooks — passed, including secret scanning and staged-file Biome checks.
The full check and full webview suite were rerun successfully with Bun 1.3.14 and Node 22.23.4 on the process PATH. Initial attempts without the complete toolchain failed (Bash unavailable to proto lint; Node unavailable to the webview runner); the successful reruns supersede those environment failures.

Regression coverage checks that completed commands (including non-zero exits) are grouped even before a final answer arrives, command/output content is hidden until expansion and restored when opened, unfinished commands stay visible, and pending command/file approvals remain accessible. The broader suite covers thinking, Markdown, turn boundaries, scrolling, and existing webview behavior.

Earlier branch validation recorded passing Windows file-edit E2E coverage for single-root and multi-root workspaces after adapting the assertions to the collapsed activity layout. Those E2E tests were not rerun for this latest terminal-command fix. Fresh hosted CI and cross-platform results for 46e306a are not yet verified.

Type of Change
 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
 ✨ New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
 💥 Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected)
 ♻️ Refactor Changes
 💅 Cosmetic Changes
 📚 Documentation update
 🏃 Workflow Changes
Screenshots
No new screenshots are attached to this PR description. The latest user report showed a completed command still occupying the main chat. With this fix, that record and its output should appear only after expanding Show activity, while running commands and pending approvals remain visible. The webview was rebuilt locally; visual review of the latest terminal fix in a reloaded extension remains outstanding.

Additional Notes
Target branch: stage.
No breaking API, model-routing, tool-execution, or approval-policy change is intended.
Activity-control styling, dismissed-memory presentation, and broader clickable file references remain outside this branch's completed scope.
User approval of the terminal-activity fix was received before committing and pushing it.

* Stop free models ending on their plan: in-content reasoning, plan-list guard, call shapes, git pager (0.1.3-test.6)

A benchmark session on 2026-09-25 stalled six times. Four causes, four fixes:

- Four self-hosted models (kimi-k2.6, qwen3-6-35b, nemotron-3-ultra, the sia
  qwen3.5) reason inside their content; the gateway exposes no reasoning
  channel for them. The thinking probe only counted reasoning deltas, so the
  catalog marked them as non-reasoners and never sent the off-switch. The
  smart profile's classifier and the judge run on the 35B, got a paragraph of
  thinking truncated before the JSON verdict, and gave "no verdict" every
  time. The probe now counts a long answer to its one-word question as
  reasoning; the catalog marks the four defaultOn with the measured
  template-kwargs off-switch where one works.
- kimi-k2.6 has no measured off-switch and, past ~80k tokens, ends on its plan
  ("I need to: 1. Check ... 3. Report ...") with no tool call: 0 tool calls in
  7 calls that session. The guard now flags a reply that ends on a first-person
  plan with imperative list items, the free-model prompt names that shape, and
  qwen3-coder leads the default route with kimi as fallback.
- Every call-log line records finishReason, textChars, reasoningChars and
  toolCalls, and the summary script shows "Text-only stops" per model, so stop
  rates come from the log instead of transcripts.
- The agent terminal sets GIT_PAGER=cat, PAGER=cat and GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0:
  `git branch` paged and waited three minutes for a keypress the model could
  not send.

* Count tool calls from tool-call-delta only: the model stream has no tool-call event

Wide output: run PowerShell commands so narrow terminals stop garbling what the model reads (0.2.5-test.2) (#185)

* Terminal: run PowerShell commands through a wide-output wrapper so narrow terminals stop garbling what the model reads

Programs lay their output out to the terminal's width before PlinyCode reads
it, so in a 30-60 column panel PowerShell tables lost columns and error
messages were broken over many lines. Commands in PowerShell terminals now run
as `. plinyrun '<command>'`, a function defined once per terminal from the
PLINYCODE_RUN environment variable: native programs write to a pipe, objects
are formatted 400 columns wide, error/warning records come out on one line,
and the command's $? is handed back so failures still report exit code 1. The
command stays in the user's terminal, in the prompt's scope. Constrained
Language mode and the plinycode.terminal.wideOutput setting fall back to the
command as typed; the narrow-terminal note and warning only apply then.

ConptyWrapJoiner also treats ConPTY's cursor move to the start of a row as a
line break, and erase-character codes (ESC[nX) are stripped, which left "X"
in the text and ran the line after a table into it.

  session host runs hook files; the temporary compaction, restore and
  history hosts run none.

  same text as before ({ hookName, toolName?, status }); the terminal status
  reuses the running row's ts so it replaces the row. Background sessions'
  rows are dropped and failures are logged with their reason.
- Per-file toggles live in new state keys: the globalHooksToggles setting
  and the localHooksToggles workspace state (path -> enabled). toggleHook
  writes them instead of chmod, so toggles work on Windows and apply to live
  sessions. A file with no toggle runs, except an extensionless file without
  the executable bit on macOS/Linux (the old chmod "off"), which stays off
  until switched on. New hooks from the tab start switched off.
- refreshHooks lists the files the engine discovers (listHookConfigFiles):
  Documents/Cline/Hooks and ~/.cline/hooks globally, .clinerules/hooks and
  .cline/hooks per workspace, any supported extension. Toggle and delete take
  the file's path and refuse files the engine would not run.
- The Hooks tab drops the Windows "toggling not supported" banner, shows each
  file's name, offers TaskError and SessionShutdown and drops PreCompact
  (the engine has no PreCompact event).
- Delete the extension's hook stack: core/hooks/{hook-factory, HookProcess,

  sdk/hooks-adapter.ts, proto/cline/hooks.proto, their tests and fixtures,
  and the bun:test hook-management suites that tested chmod toggles (replaced
  by vitest suites for the handlers). The spending-limit beforeModel wrapper
  stays.
- The e2e hooks fixture is a single UserPromptSubmit.js (node on every
  platform) and the spec also checks the hook_status row.
- docs/rules.md gains a Hooks section: files and interpreters, the events
  and which are waited for, toggles and the status rows.

* Tick pre-release version to 0.2.3-test.8

* Engine: announce the seeded user message so UserPromptSubmit hooks run

SessionRuntime appends each run's user message to the conversation store,
seeds the AgentRuntime with it and calls run(""), so the runtime never
emitted message-added for a user message. The file-hook runner starts
UserPromptSubmit (prompt_submit) hook files from an onEvent hook on a user
message-added, so they never ran in a ClineCore session, and no hook_status
row appeared: the hooks e2e failed on every OS.

AgentRuntimeConfig gains seededInputMessageCount: the last N
initialMessages are this run's input, and the first run announces them
with message-added right after run-started, as it does for input passed to
run(). SessionRuntime sets it to 1 when the run carries a user message
(start and every send), and 0 for a continue without one.

twice) and a SessionRuntime test with a real AgentRuntime and an extension
onEvent hook (fails without the fix). The hooks e2e now checks the hook's
marker file before the hook_status row, with messages that say which half
broke.

header once the message scrolls away, so getByText could match two

DevOps PR review tools, pipeline cancel/rerun and agent-triggered launches (#158)

* DevOps server: PR review tools, pipeline run/cancel/rerun, unattended refusals

New tools on the built-in DevOps MCP server, for GitHub and Azure DevOps
(Services and Server):

- pr_comments: review threads, inline comments (file:line), general comments
  and review verdicts, newest first, with resolved state and reply ids.
- pr_comment: general comment, inline comment on a changed line (PR head
  commit / latest iteration), or a reply in a thread.
- pr_review: approve, request_changes or comment. Azure DevOps sets the
  reviewer vote: approve = 10, request_changes = waiting for author (-5).
- pipeline_run: queue a workflow or YAML pipeline by name, id or workflow
  file, with inputs checked by the Pipelines view's validation.
- pipeline_cancel and pipeline_rerun (all jobs or failed jobs only).

Unattended CI Board runs may read pr_comments and are refused pr_review,
pr_comment, pipeline_run, pipeline_cancel and pipeline_rerun with a reason.
Approval prompts for built-in MCP tools now show the tool's description.

* Pipelines view: cancel, rerun, completion notifications, agent launches

- Launch history entries with a run get Cancel (queued or running) and
  Rerun / Rerun failed jobs (finished) buttons. A rerun is a new entry; a
  rerun of the same run id waits for the new attempt instead of repeating
  the previous result.
- A notification when a run in the history finishes, from the history's
  existing polling, once across windows sharing the history
  (plinycode.pipelines.notify, default on).
- PlinyCode's pipeline_run calls for a repository in the window go through
  the view's queueing code, so the launch is recorded ("Started by the
  agent"), tracked and announced; refusals come back to the agent.
- Docs: pipeline-runs.md drops the old limits and describes cancel, rerun,
  notifications and agent-triggered launches.

* Drop the redundant Queue send mode.

A plain Send already waits for the current turn to finish when the agent
is busy, so Queue did exactly the same thing. The send modes are now Send
(waits for current turn), Send now (interrupts) and Schedule, with labels

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Keep running tasks going in the background.

Starting a new task or opening another one from History no longer stops a
running task. It moves to a background registry (up to 3 tasks):

- its chat output is dropped (the SDK still persists the conversation),
  edits apply without previews, and its terminals are not revealed;
- approvals and questions that are not auto-approved are held, flagged in
  History ("Needs approval") and announced with an Open notification;
- when its turn ends it is stopped and the user is notified;
- reopening it adopts the live session and replays anything held.

Deleting a task, deleting all history and shutdown stop background tasks.
At the limit the running task is stopped as before, with a notice.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Gate free Pliny models behind their own checkbox, default off

Split the single "unlock paid models" toggle into two independent
checkboxes (free self-hosted / paid hosted), both defaulting to off.
The virtual FreeAuto router stays visible unconditionally so it
remains the out-of-the-box default model.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Isolate sub-agent turns in FreeAuto, enable sub-agents, reorder default routes

Sub-agent runs reuse the parent's agentModelFactory, so each run now gets
its own turn key instead of resetting the parent's call log, sticky model
and failover budget; their routing rows are prefixed "↳ sub-agent". Image
requests fail fast with a clear message because no free Pliny model accepts
images. The compaction summarizer id is refreshed once the rules file loads.

spawn_agent is now gated on the existing subagentsEnabled setting, which
gets a toggle under Features › Advanced, and the output channel logs when a
sub-agent is spawned and finishes. A dedicated "subagent" route favours
fast models for delegated work.

Default routes follow the probe and field experience: qwen3-coder leads
coding/default and the pool, GLM-5.2 is kept only for huge-context, and the
coding regex also catches merge conflicts, lint and type errors.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Add FreeAuto reasoning effort, classifier, profiles and call log

A live thinking probe (probe-pliny-free-models.ts --thinking) measured, per
free model, whether it reasons by default and which request field switches
it: GLM-5.2 and several Qwen/Nemotron models reason on every call and turn
off via chat_template_kwargs, while some backends reject reasoning_effort
with a 400. The catalog now records these controls, a Pliny provider-option
rule sends only the measured off-switch, and routes gain effort
(quick/think) and reasoningEffort, applied per candidate model.

The smart profile runs a small classifier once per turn that picks a tier
and whether to think, reused for the rest of the turn and falling back to
the heuristic routes on any failure. Three FreeAuto models (default, fast,
smart) each have their own rules file, and every routed call is appended to
pliny-free-auto-calls.jsonl with a script to summarise it by profile and
model.

Also fixes the generated rules file, whose double-quoted regexes were
invalid YAML so the file was silently ignored, and turns sub-agents on by
default.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Keep FreeAuto runs going when a model announces a step without acting

Free models, qwen3-coder above all, often end a reply with "Let me check
the log:" and no tool call, which the agent loop treats as the end of the
run, so tasks stopped half done. The completion guard now receives the
no-tool reply, the host can supply its own guard through CoreSessionConfig,
and the extension nudges such replies once (never twice in a row, at most
three times per run). The heuristic is calibrated on 16 real run-ending
replies: 7 premature stops caught, 9 genuine answers left alone.

kimi-k2.6 leads the default and subagent routes again, since qwen3-coder is
quick at targeted edits but stalls on long tasks; it still leads coding.
The context check now reserves the model's full output, so a near-full
request no longer lands on qwen3-coder's 128k window and fails.

Rules and skills written for other agents were auto-detected in a way that

Ask mode, and history filters, search and pinned conversations (0.1.7-test.13) (#110)

* Ask mode, and history filters, search and pinned conversations

Ask mode

A third mode next to Plan and Act. In ask mode the agent answers questions
about the code and cannot edit any file.

- The mode switch has one segment per mode (Plan, Act, Ask); clicking a
  segment selects it and the shortcut cycles through them.
- The engine's ask tool preset leaves the editor and apply_patch tools out,
  and an ask-mode guard rejects any write that still reaches them, markdown
  included, plus the shell commands on the file-editing blacklist plan mode
  already uses.
- The ask-mode prompt tells the model to show a change in its reply and to
  ask the user to toggle to Act mode to apply it.
- Ask mode runs on the act-mode model and routes like plan mode.

History

- The favorites filter is a button above the list and finds every favorite.
  getTaskHistory paged the history first and filtered each page, so a
  favorite older than the newest 50 conversations never showed; search and
  the workspace filter had the same limit. It now filters the whole history,
  then pages.
- Search matches every word against the title and the workspace path.
- A date filter (today, last 7 or 30 days, or a custom from/to date and
  time) keeps the conversations active in the period.
- Conversations can be pinned. Pinned ones are listed first, in a Pinned
  section.
- The favorite and pin flags change only through their toggles. Other
  history writes carried a HistoryItem read earlier or built from scratch,
  which could un-star a conversation; a checkpoint restore and an
  edit-and-regenerate dropped the star too.

docs/ask-mode.md and docs/conversation-history.md describe the design.

* Bind conversations to workspaces: filter history, start elsewhere, share across windows

A conversation now belongs to a workspace: the folder the window is open

  the native dialog. The task runs in that workspace's first folder and

  edits, slash commands and session rebuilds stay in that workspace.
- The last ten workspaces used are kept in a shared JSON file under the
  data directory, read on demand so every window sees the same list.
- The sessions directory is watched so conversations added, renamed or
  deleted by another window show up without a restart.

Per-session trace files and a rotating log file (0.2.3-test.3) (#145)

* Per-session trace files and a rotating log file

After a bad run only the chat transcript survived: the Output channel goes
with the window, Show Last Model Request keeps a few requests in memory and
the router's JSONL logs cover only auto-free / auto-paid-balanced calls.

Trace: sdk/trace/session-trace.ts writes <dataDir>/traces/<sessionId>.jsonl,
one JSON line per step. SdkSessionConfigBuilder installs it after the router
and the advisor; it wraps the model factory (request and stream records) and
the beforeModel/beforeTool/afterTool/afterRun hooks (tool_call, tool_result,
run_end, error records). The router reports each attempt's decision and
outcome through the new RouterInstallDeps.onCallEvent (router records); its
own JSONL logs are unchanged. Messages, tool arguments and results are
copied with secret keys and secret-looking values redacted and long text cut
(4k / 2k characters); the system prompt is recorded as a sha256 and a length.
A file stops at 20 MB with a final truncated line, the folder is pruned to
200 MB at extension start, and writes are queued and never reach the agent
loop. plinycode.trace.enabled (default on) is read per record.

Log file: shared/services/file-log-sink.ts appends every Logger line to
<dataDir>/logs/plinycode.log, rotated at 5 MB with five files kept, through
a queue flushed on deactivate. extension.ts passes it to HostProvider as the
logToChannel sink that used to be a no-op. New command PlinyCode: Open Log
File (cline.openLogFile).

Docs: docs/trace-and-logs.md, linked from AGENTS.md; restart-from-here.md
points to the trace for requests older than the in-memory one.

* Trace: write request records incrementally

The agent sends the whole conversation on every iteration, so a request
record that copied the whole message list grew a long conversation's trace
quadratically and reached the 20 MB cap within a few dozen iterations.

Per agent, the trace now remembers how many messages it has written and the
id of the last one. A request record keeps messageCount and totalChars for
the whole list but its messages array holds only the messages after that
position, with fromIndex and newMessages saying where it starts and how many
it holds. When the list is shorter than remembered, or the message at the
remembered position has another id (compaction, restart-from-here,
truncation), the whole list is written again with reset: true. The first
request of a session, and of each sub-agent, writes everything from index 0.
Redaction and the per-part caps are unchanged.

docs/trace-and-logs.md describes the scheme and how to rebuild what the
model saw at an iteration.

* Release 0.1.2: bump extension version.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Trust the Pliny gateway's chain when the editor host does not.

The gateway serves only its leaf certificate, without the SNPSica2
intermediate. Node verifies against its bundled roots only, so unless the
editor injects an OS store that already holds the intermediate (VS Code
usually does; some Cursor builds and fresh machines do not), every request
fails with UNABLE_TO_VERIFY_LEAF_SIGNATURE and FreeAuto fails over through
every model.

The shared fetch now retries a certificate-trust failure once with Node's
roots, the OS store (when this Node can read it) and the bundled public
SNPSica2 / SNPSOfflineCA certificates, then keeps using that trust for the
origin. It only adds trust; expired or wrong-host certificates still fail.
Working setups never take the fallback path, and it honors proxy env vars.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Auto-update PlinyCode from the shared PlinyCodeRelease folder.

PlinyCode is not on a marketplace, so installs from a .vsix never update.
The extension now reads latest.json from the PlinyCodeRelease folder that
OneDrive syncs to disk, shortly after startup and every 6 hours. When there
is a newer release it copies the .vsix, verifies its sha256, installs it and
offers a reload. "PlinyCode: Check for Updates" checks on demand, and the
plinycode.updates.enabled / plinycode.updates.folder settings control it.

Releases are cut with scripts/release.ts (release:package and
release:publish), which writes the .vsix and notes before latest.json. The
/release skill and docs/releasing.md document the whole process.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Update PlinyCode from GitHub Releases, with the OneDrive folder as fallback.

OneDrive sync is unavailable on Linux and Remote-SSH hosts. The updater now
reads latest.json from the latest GitHub release first
(plinycode.updates.url), through the shared fetch so proxies and the
bundled Synopsys CAs apply, and installs the newest version offered by
either source, falling back to the other if a download or checksum fails.
GitHub manifests pin the .vsix and notes to the release tag and may only
point at https URLs on the manifest's own host.

release:publish now creates the GitHub release as a draft, uploads the
.vsix and latest.json, then publishes it, after checking gh auth, that the
release tag is on origin at HEAD, and that the version is newer than what
each source serves. The OneDrive folder is still written afterwards. The
docs and the /release skill describe the new order: tag, then package.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Add a --prerelease option to release:publish.

A pre-release is published to GitHub only, is never marked latest and
is never copied to the OneDrive folder, so /releases/latest keeps serving
the current release. Testers point plinycode.updates.url at the
pre-release's own latest.json; the script prints that URL and checks
that /releases/latest does not serve the pre-release.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Remove the old claude-dev (0.1.0) build and document pre-releases.

PlinyCode 0.1.0 shipped as synopsys-plinycode.claude-dev; later builds
are synopsys-plinycode.plinycode-dev. VS Code keeps both installed side
by side, fighting over the same cline.* commands and sidebar view. On
activation, before anything that could trip over those commands,
PlinyCode now uninstalls the old build if present and offers a reload.
Verified in a separate VS Code profile with the real 0.1.0 .vsix: it
was removed about 7 s after startup.

docs/releasing.md gains a "Testing a release before users get it"
section for --prerelease, and release.ts lists --prerelease in its usage
and no longer tells a pre-release publisher that all users will get it.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Keep FreeAuto runs going: completion guard v2, judge, wait tool, run log

Free models end runs before the task is done: they announce a step without
the tool call, promise to "check back at 15:28", ask permission for something
the user already asked for, report a failed command as if it were the result,
or degenerate into a repeated character. 26 saved FreeAuto sessions show 57 of
71 run endings right after a tool result (44 after run_commands), and the old
regex guard caught only the announcement case — and gave up when the model
answered its reminder with the same announcement.

Engine (shared/agents/core): `CompletionGuard` now receives the run's messages
(`runMessages`, `messages`) and may be async; reminders are marked
`displayRole: "system"` so they no longer render as user bubbles. The act and
yolo prompts explain that a tool-free reply ends the task and point at `wait`.

Extension (router):
- completion-guard.ts replaces the single-rule guard: rules for a failed or
  detached shell result, wait/monitor bail-outs, leaked reasoning, degenerate
  output and "ready to run" after being asked to run; a second consecutive
  stall gets a firmer reminder and moves the turn to the default route's lead
  model; three reminders per run at most. Rows name the rule that fired.
- router-completion-judge.ts asks the utility model, once per agentic act-mode
  run when no rule fired, whether the request was carried out; no verdict
  accepts the reply. `guard.judge` / `guard.judgeTimeoutMs` / `utility.judge`
  in the rules file.
- routed-agent-model.ts cuts off a reply that collapses into repetition and
  fails the call so the run continues on another model; free candidates get a
  system-prompt addendum (router-prompt.ts) about how their turn ends.
- An afterTool hook (router-hooks.ts) appends a note to failed and detached
  shell results, and an afterRun hook writes pliny-free-auto-runs.jsonl: how
  each run ended, last model and tool, rules fired, judge verdict, reply tail.
  summarize-free-auto-log.ts reports early-stop rates per profile/model/route
  and the classifier's verdict rate.
- The smart classifier never produced a verdict in 185 logged calls: the
  default model overran the 256-token cap before the JSON. Cap raised to 512,
  JSON asked for first, brace-balanced parsing (fenced, nested, unclosed
  <think>), raw reply logged and `classifierError` recorded on the call.
- vscode-wait-tool.ts: a `wait` tool (≤10 min per call, ≤1 h per run,
  abortable) so a model can wait → read the log → wait again instead of ending
  its turn.

Version 0.1.3-dev.2 so the pre-release auto-update picks it up.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Version 0.1.3-test.3 and document the pre-release numbering

The updater compares pre-release tags alphabetically, so 0.1.3-dev.3 sorted
below the published 0.1.3-test.2 and would never have been offered to an
editor running it. Pre-releases now always use `<next release>-test.<N>`,
ticking N by one each time; docs/releasing.md spells out the rule.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Type the wait tool as a plain AgentTool so the extension compiles

`createWaitTool` returned `AgentTool<WaitToolInput, string>`, which is not
assignable to the `AgentTool[]` the extension's tool list holds (its
`execute` parameter is narrower than `unknown`). The e2e jobs caught it in
`vscode:prepublish`; the root `bun run types` does not run the extension's
`check-types`, so it slipped through locally. `execute` now takes `unknown`
like every runtime tool and reads the fields it needs.

Keep the agent's context lean: drop old reasoning, whole tool results, earlier router compaction, one editor's rules (0.1.7-test.6) (#102)

* Keep the agent's context lean: drop old reasoning, send whole tool results, compact routers earlier, one editor's rules

An audit of what goes into each model request found that the context grew
with material the model no longer needed while useful content was cut.

Engine:
- Drop reasoning from earlier user turns before each request (kept in
  history for the UI). The openai-compatible provider resent every past
  turn's reasoning as reasoning_content. Inline <think> blocks in earlier
  assistant text are stripped too. Signed Anthropic thinking is kept.
- Raise the per-string tool-result cap from 8k to 50k chars, just above
  the tools' own 48k windows, so the model sees a read or command output
  as the tool shaped it instead of a 4k head and 4k tail. Several large
  entries in one result share a 64k budget (never below 8k each).
- Send read_files / run_commands / search_codebase results as plain text
  (<result query="...">) instead of JSON-escaped strings.
- FreeAuto compacts against a 92k input budget (~83k tokens), where the
  128k tier of the pool stops fitting, instead of ~230k. BalanceAuto
  compacts at ~115k instead of ~180k. The advertised windows are unchanged.
- Loop-detection notices reach the model: they were appended to the
  conversation store and overwritten before the next request.

Rules and skills:
- The host tells the engine its editor: VS Code loads .github (Copilot)
  rules and skills, Cursor loads .cursor, Windsurf .windsurfrules. AGENTS.md,
  .clinerules, .cline, .agents and .claude load everywhere.
- One global rules folder: the Documents/Cline/Rules folder the Rules panel
  uses. ~/.cline/rules is no longer read; its files move there at startup,
  keeping their toggles.
- Rules scoped to file globs or "apply when relevant" are listed by path
  for the model to read when they apply, instead of inlined in every request.
- Always-on rules are capped at 12k chars each and 40k in total.
- The system prompt names the real editor instead of always "VS Code".

Extension:
- @file mentions are capped at 100k chars (was 400 KB), @folder at 100k in
  total (files past it are named, not pasted), @url at 50k. The truncation
  notice names tools that exist.
- The built-in DevOps MCP tools are only offered in a repository with a
  GitHub or Azure DevOps remote.

* Tick pre-release version to 0.1.7-test.6

* Show workspace root in history and allow editing the opening prompt.

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

* docs: remove boilerplate community files and add REPOMAP.md

* Sticky send modes, clearer failure messages, terminal cleanup and focus fixes.

- Send button: the dropdown now picks a sticky send mode (send / steer /
  queue / schedule) instead of sending; the main button shows the mode's
  icon and Enter uses it. Persisted per webview.
- Max output token error now names the model, output tokens, the applied
  cap and which limit set it (setting, model limit, remaining context or
  default), plus input/context sizes and a matching hint. The gateway
  reports the resolved cap on max-tokens finish events.
- Aborted commands report the command, cwd, abort cause and keep partial
  output (new CommandAbortedError).
- Terminals: evicted terminals are tracked and closed once provably idle,
  idle terminals are closed when a task ends, the idle pool is capped at 2,
  and agent terminals are transient so reloads don't restore them.
  Terminals running a command or typed into by the user are never closed.
- Running a command reveals its terminal without stealing focus.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Drop the redundant Queue send mode.

A plain Send already waits for the current turn to finish when the agent
is busy, so Queue did exactly the same thing. The send modes are now Send
(waits for current turn), Send now (interrupts) and Schedule, with labels
that say how each behaves. A stored "queue" mode falls back to Send.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Give the FreeAuto router model zero pricing.

FreeAuto is the default Pliny model and routes only to free self-hosted
models, but it had no pricing, failing the "explicit zero pricing" engine
test on CI.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Keep running tasks going in the background.

Starting a new task or opening another one from History no longer stops a
running task. It moves to a background registry (up to 3 tasks):

- its chat output is dropped (the SDK still persists the conversation),
  edits apply without previews, and its terminals are not revealed;
- approvals and questions that are not auto-approved are held, flagged in
  History ("Needs approval") and announced with an Open notification;
- when its turn ends it is stopped and the user is notified;
- reopening it adopts the live session and replays anything held.

Deleting a task, deleting all history and shutdown stop background tasks.
At the limit the running task is stopped as before, with a notice.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

hits.message:
Lgiaccar/few impr (#27)

# FreeAuto v2 — Phase (a) + (b) summary

Branch `lgiaccar/few_impr`, commit `9e9cddc`, pushed to `origin/lgiaccar/few_impr`.
Full design context: [freeauto-strategy-and-models.md](freeauto-strategy-and-models.md)
and the plan at `~/.claude/plans/please-lay-down-a-atomic-crane.md`.

## Phase (a) — Hygiene fixes

### Sub-agent turn-state isolation
Sub-agents (spawned via `spawn_agent`) reuse the parent session's routing
closure. Previously, a sub-agent call re-entered the same turn state as the
parent, silently resetting the parent's call log, sticky model, and failover
budget mid-turn.

**Fix:** each run is now keyed by whether `agentConfig.parentAgentId` is set.
A sub-agent run gets its own turn key (`<sessionId>:sub:<n>`); the parent's
turn state is untouched. Model health (which models are benched) stays
global, as intended — only per-turn bookkeeping is isolated. Sub-agent keys
are cleaned up automatically when the next parent turn starts.

**Visible effect:** FreeAuto routing rows from a sub-agent are now prefixed
`↳ sub-agent` in chat, so it's clear which model activity belongs to a
delegated task versus the main conversation.

### Image requests fail fast
No free Pliny model accepts image input, but FreeAuto previously routed
image-bearing requests through the normal candidate list anyway, likely
producing a confusing failure deep in the call.

**Fix:** the router now checks model capabilities up front. If a request
carries an image and no candidate supports it, the call fails immediately
with: *"FreeAuto routes only to free Pliny models, none of which accept
images. Pick a vision-capable model or remove the image."*

### Summarizer model id refresh
The compaction summarizer's model id was fixed to the built-in default at
session install time, before the rules file had actually loaded — so a
custom `utility.summarizer` in `pliny-free-auto.md` was silently ignored.
Now it updates in place once the rules file is read.

## Phase (b) — Sub-agents enabled + routing improvements

### Sub-agents turned on
`spawn_agent` was hard-disabled in the extension regardless of settings.
It's now gated on the existing `subagentsEnabled` setting, which gets a new
toggle: **Settings → Features → Advanced → Sub-agents** (off by default,
applies to new tasks).

### Spawn visibility
The PlinyCode output channel now logs a line when a sub-agent starts and
when it finishes:
```
[Subagent] spawned: <task prompt, truncated>
[Subagent] completed · in <N> / out <N> tok
```

### New `subagent` route
Delegated tasks are typically short and bounded, so a new default route
sends sub-agent calls to fast models first (`qwen3-coder-480b`,
`nemotron-3-super-120b`, `kimi-k2.6`) ahead of the general-purpose routes.

### Default route reorder (field experience + probe data)
- `qwen3-coder-480b` now leads both the `coding` and `default` routes, and
  heads the fallback pool — it's fast (356ms TTFT) and, per your testing,
  reliably good at fixing conflicts.
- `GLM-5.2` is removed from `coding` and `default` — it's slow (1279ms
  TTFT, 7.6 tok/s) and is kept only on the `huge-context` route, where its
  512k window is the only option.
- The `coding` route's trigger phrases now also catch merge conflicts,
  rebase, lint errors, and type errors (previously only fix/implement/refactor-style wording matched).

## Verification

- 1319 vitest tests + 1151 bun unit tests pass; `tsc` and Biome are clean.
- New tests cover: sub-agent turn isolation, image-request rejection, the
  `subagent` route, the reordered defaults, and the `subagentsEnabled` →
  `enableSpawnAgent` wiring.
- Not verified by this pass: live behavior against the Pliny gateway in a
  running extension host (no gateway access from this environment) — worth
  confirming manually per the checklist below.

## What to check manually

1. Enable **Settings → Features → Advanced → Sub-agents**.
2. Start a task, ask it to delegate something to a sub-agent — confirm:
   - `[Subagent] spawned` / `[Subagent] completed` lines in the output channel.
   - `↳ sub-agent` prefixed rows in chat, route shown as `subagent`.
   - The turn summary at the end still reflects only the parent's own calls.
3. Ask something like "fix the merge conflicts in X" — confirm it routes to
   `qwen3-coder-480b` under the `coding` route.
4. Paste an image while on FreeAuto — confirm the immediate error message,
   no model call attempted.
5. Your existing `~/.cline/data/pliny-free-auto.md` was regenerated (the old
   one was moved to `.bak`) so these new defaults actually apply — if you'd
   customized that file, diff it against the backup before discarding it.

Split largest extension files: SdkController, message-translator, McpHub, ChatTextArea (#98)

* Split SdkController.ts: extract checkpoint, slash/mention, workspace-root coordinators

Code moves only, no behavior changes. SdkController.ts: 2260 -> 1799 lines.

New modules:
- sdk-checkpoint-coordinator.ts (370 lines): restoreCheckpoint, checkpoint
  changes summary, per-file/multi-file diff viewing (SdkCheckpointCoordinator)
- sdk-slash-mention-resolver.ts (164 lines): /workflow and /skill slash
  command expansion plus @-mention resolution (SdkSlashMentionResolver)
- sdk-workspace-root-resolver.ts (149 lines): workspace root resolution,
  window workspace identity, no-workspace fallback, WorkspaceRootManager
  (SdkWorkspaceRootResolver)

SdkController keeps thin delegating methods with the same public signatures
for every moved method, so no external caller changed. SdkController.test.ts
updated to construct SdkCheckpointCoordinator directly instead of binding
fake objects to Controller.prototype.

* Split message-translator.ts into a message-translator/ module folder

Code moves only, no behavior changes. message-translator.ts: 2814 -> folder
of 7 modules + a 53-line barrel (index.ts) that re-exports every symbol the
old file exported, so every external import of ./message-translator is
unaffected.

New modules:
- translator-state.ts (511 lines): TranslationResult, normalizeUsageEvent,
  MessageTranslatorState (streaming-message state tracking)
- tool-mapping.ts (443 lines): display-path relativization, SDK tool name to
  ClineSayTool mapping, MCP tool detection
- tool-input-parse.ts (187 lines): pure tool-input parsing helpers used by
  tool-mapping.ts
- ask-builders.ts (131 lines): tool-approval ask messages, compaction notice
  building
- live-events.ts (992 lines): translateAgentEvent, translateSessionEvent —
  the live SDK-event-to-ClineMessage translators
- history-replay.ts (391 lines): sdkMessagesToClineMessages and its helpers,
  for replaying persisted SDK message history
- error-reshape.ts (208 lines): reshapeErrorForWebview and its error
  classification helpers

message-translator.test.ts moved alongside as message-translator/
message-translator.test.ts (173 tests, same count as before the split).

* Split McpHub.ts into settings-store, transport-factory, capability-fetcher and rpc-facade modules

Code moves only, no behavior/logic changes. McpHub.ts: 2082 -> 532 lines,
now a thin class shell (fields, constructor, delegating methods) composing
the four new modules. Fields that were `private` are now plain instance
fields (documented in McpHub.ts) because the extracted modules take `this`
as an explicit host parameter and TypeScript's structural typing rejects a
`private` member against those host interfaces' public shape.

New modules:
- mcp-settings-store.ts (295 lines): settings file path resolution,
  reading/validating/writing the MCP settings JSON, the settings file
  watcher, and connection fingerprinting (getMcpSettingsFilePath,
  recordSettingsFingerprint, readPostWriteMcpSettings,
  readAndValidateMcpSettingsFile, watchMcpSettingsFile,
  computeConnectionFingerprint, configsRequireRestart,
  serverGainedOAuthTokens, stableJsonStringify)
- transport-factory.ts (473 lines): connectToServer (stdio/SSE/streamableHttp
  transport construction) plus the per-server stdio file watchers
  (setupFileWatcher, removeAllFileWatchers)
- capability-fetcher.ts (405 lines): post-connection tool/resource/prompt
  discovery and the list_changed notification debounce/refresh machinery
  (fetchServerCapabilities, fetchToolsList, fetchResourcesList,
  fetchResourceTemplatesList, fetchPromptsList, scheduleListChangedRefresh,
  refreshChangedList, appendErrorMessage)
- mcp-rpc-facade.ts (865 lines): the RPC-facing surface the webview/
  controller call (updateServerConnectionsRPC, restartConnectionRPC,
  toggleServerDisabledRPC, toggleToolAutoApproveRPC, addRemoteServer,
  deleteServerRPC, updateServerTimeoutRPC, callTool,
  reconcileMcpServersFromSettingsRPC, initiateOAuth, and related server
  lifecycle management)

McpHub's public API (every method signature, including addRemoteServer)
is unchanged, so every external caller (SdkController, gRPC handlers,
tests) is unaffected. The built-in DevOps MCP server does not import
McpHub at all (see docs/devops-mcp.md), so it is unaffected by
construction. Verified the full apps/vscode/src/services/mcp/__tests__/
suite passes with the same result as before the split (a pre-existing,
unrelated test-pollution failure only appears when running the suite as
one combined `bun test` invocation across files, not under the isolated
per-file `bun run test:unit` runner, and reproduces identically on
unmodified origin/stage).

* Split ChatTextArea.tsx into hooks and components under chat-textarea/

Code moves only, no behavior/prop changes. ChatTextArea.tsx: 1896 -> 831
lines, now orchestration: state wiring plus the render tree, importing the
extracted hooks/components below.

New modules under webview-ui/src/components/chat/chat-textarea/:
- hooks/useContextMenu.ts (280 lines): the @-mention context menu state and
  handlers (file search, selection, cursor tracking)
- hooks/useDropHandling.ts (467 lines): drag-and-drop / paste file and image
  handling, dimension validation, unsupported-file/dimension error timers
- hooks/useResizableRows.ts (106 lines): the draggable textarea max-height/
  rows behavior
- hooks/useComposerKeyboardHandler.ts (334 lines): keyboard handling for the
  composer (send, mode toggle, slash/mention navigation keys)
- hooks/useSlashCommandMenu.ts (81 lines) and hooks/useSchedulePicker.ts
  (50 lines): slash-command menu state and the schedule-send picker,
  cleanly separable state that didn't fit the plan's five required hooks
  but was cohesive enough to extract too
- components/ModeSwitch.tsx (81 lines): the Plan/Act toggle UI
- components/ModelButton.tsx (164 lines): the toolbar row (context/files
  buttons, MCP/rules toggles, model picker)

getRowHeightPx/rowsFromDrag are re-exported from ChatTextArea.tsx so
ChatTextArea.test.tsx and any other existing import of them keeps working
unchanged. Verified with the mandatory `bunx tsc -b` in webview-ui (clean)
and the full webview-ui vitest suite (467 passed).

  edits apply without previews, and its terminals are not revealed;
- approvals and questions that are not auto-approved are held, flagged in
  History ("Needs approval") and announced with an Open notification;
- when its turn ends it is stopped and the user is notified;
- reopening it adopts the live session and replays anything held.

Deleting a task, deleting all history and shutdown stop background tasks.
At the limit the running task is stopped as before, with a notice.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Gate free Pliny models behind their own checkbox, default off

Split the single "unlock paid models" toggle into two independent
checkboxes (free self-hosted / paid hosted), both defaulting to off.
The virtual FreeAuto router stays visible unconditionally so it
remains the out-of-the-box default model.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Isolate sub-agent turns in FreeAuto, enable sub-agents, reorder default routes

Sub-agent runs reuse the parent's agentModelFactory, so each run now gets
its own turn key instead of resetting the parent's call log, sticky model
and failover budget; their routing rows are prefixed "↳ sub-agent". Image
requests fail fast with a clear message because no free Pliny model accepts
images. The compaction summarizer id is refreshed once the rules file loads.

spawn_agent is now gated on the existing subagentsEnabled setting, which
gets a toggle under Features › Advanced, and the output channel logs when a
sub-agent is spawned and finishes. A dedicated "subagent" route favours
fast models for delegated work.

Default routes follow the probe and field experience: qwen3-coder leads
coding/default and the pool, GLM-5.2 is kept only for huge-context, and the
coding regex also catches merge conflicts, lint and type errors.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Add FreeAuto reasoning effort, classifier, profiles and call log

A live thinking probe (probe-pliny-free-models.ts --thinking) measured, per
free model, whether it reasons by default and which request field switches
it: GLM-5.2 and several Qwen/Nemotron models reason on every call and turn
off via chat_template_kwargs, while some backends reject reasoning_effort
with a 400. The catalog now records these controls, a Pliny provider-option
rule sends only the measured off-switch, and routes gain effort
(quick/think) and reasoningEffort, applied per candidate model.

The smart profile runs a small classifier once per turn that picks a tier
and whether to think, reused for the rest of the turn and falling back to
the heuristic routes on any failure. Three FreeAuto models (default, fast,
smart) each have their own rules file, and every routed call is appended to
pliny-free-auto-calls.jsonl with a script to summarise it by profile and
model.

Also fixes the generated rules file, whose double-quoted regexes were
invalid YAML so the file was silently ignored, and turns sub-agents on by
default.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* Keep FreeAuto runs going when a model announces a step without acting

Free models, qwen3-coder above all, often end a reply with "Let me check
the log:" and no tool call, which the agent loop treats as the end of the
run, so tasks stopped half done. The completion guard now receives the
no-tool reply, the host can supply its own guard through CoreSessionConfig,
and the extension nudges such replies once (never twice in a row, at most
three times per run). The heuristic is calibrated on 16 real run-ending
replies: 7 premature stops caught, 9 genuine answers left alone.

kimi-k2.6 leads the default and subagent routes again, since qwen3-coder is
quick at targeted edits but stalls on long tasks; it still leads coding.
The context check now reserves the model's full output, so a near-full
request no longer lands on qwen3-coder's 128k window and fails.

## Why

The last 20 generated shoots looked robotic. In five face-visible poses, the model gave the same frontal stare into the lens and the same smile, with both arms hanging. Uploaded reference poses and expressions were not followed. An audit of those shoots, their references and SKUs, the prompts, the DB and the Railway logs found these root causes:

1. **Monotonous plans.** Every recent plan wrote nearly the same expression for each frame, e.g. "calm soft smile, eyes to camera" five times. The v36 expression plan prints one shoot-wide gaze for every frame, and the LangGraph planner's fallback expression repeats that gaze.
2. **Expression baked into identity.** `modelIdentity.face` carried a gaze and a smile as if they were features, e.g. "almond dark brown eyes glancing sideways … lips in soft closed-mouth smile". That text reached every frame through LOCKED SUBJECT, the face lock and the IDENTITY CHECK. The APPROVED POSE 1 anchor then pulled its own expression and head angle into Poses 2–6.
3. **Reference look thrown away.** The face lock said "discard that image's … pose", and v36 recorded only the reference *posture*. It recorded no camera angle, expression, gaze or hand gesture. In B45-Raha-Maroon, the reference model looks down with her hands clasped, while every generated frame stared into the lens.
4. **The new planning had never run.** All 20 recent jobs, and every session in the last 7 days (230 on v35, 11 on v32), were analysed before v36. There are 0 `pose_plan_outcomes` rows and no `thread_plan_*` checkpoints, because regeneration never re-plans.

## What changed

- **New `lib/expressionDirection.ts`**
  - Each face-visible frame gets its own gaze target, head angle, mouth and one natural gesture:
    - Pose 1: eye contact;
    - Pose 2: just past the lens over the turn;
    - Pose 4: away into the set;
    - Pose 5: a quarter turn, looking back to the lens;
    - Pose 6: toward the featured garment.
  - The smile level shifts per frame and is capped by the shoot's energy.
  - It is stated once, in an uncompacted closing-tail block (`THIS FRAME'S EXPRESSION, GAZE & BODY LANGUAGE`). Other lines point at it.
  - It applies to existing v35 sessions on regeneration, with no re-analysis needed.
  - The block also says to copy only the face itself from the identity image and Pose 1, never their expression, gaze or head tilt.
- **Identity locks carry features only.** `modelIdentity.face` is stripped of gaze and smile phrases at prompt time.
- **Planner mood vs. gaze.** The planner's per-frame `expressions` now give only the frame's mood. Their gaze words are dropped, and they get the same posture, stride and held-object scrub as every expression line. `expressionAttitudeLine` and the Python `build_expressions` no longer print a shared gaze.
- **Analysis v37** (`generation-session-v37-reference-look-per-frame-expression`)
  - The face lock describes features only.
  - Each pose gets its own expression.
  - `referencePose` records `cameraAngle`, `expression`, `gaze` and `hands`, in both TypeScript and Python, with the parity fixture regenerated by its script.
  - Pose 4 takes the reference person's look whenever the reference shows a person. Folded-posture hands are dropped from a standing frame, and the camera angle applies only when the posture is adopted. An adopted Pose 6 keeps its own showcase look.
- **Tier 5 keeps ALLOWED DELTA.** The emergency cut used to slice ALLOWED DELTA ("only pose, angle, framing and expression change") first. It now keeps it with POSE REQUIREMENT.
- **QA:** `model_face` judges identity only. It never fails for a different expression, gaze or head angle. A frozen stare or a stock smile fails `face_realism`.
- **Docs:** CLAUDE.md (rule 4), AGENTS.md, MEMORY.md 2.6 and the release notes are updated.

## Real image tests

Real references were run through this branch's prompts with gpt-image-2.6-sunburst, medium quality.

![Before/after](https://github.com/pawanshukla500/aistudio-youthnic/blob/feat/natural-expression-gaze-reference-look/docs/qa/expression/expression_gaze_before_after.jpg?raw=true)

- **B45-Raha-Maroon:** new Pose 1, then Poses 2, 4, 5 and 6 anchored to it. The v37 reference look was simulated: eyes lowered, head tilted, hands clasped.
  - Pose 4 now takes the reference look.
  - Poses 2, 5 and 6 each have their own gaze.
  - The garment, face and set are unchanged.
- **BT218-Cat-Beige:** a legacy v35 session, with Poses 2, 4, 5 and 6 anchored to the live Pose 1.
  - Before, all four copied Pose 1's gaze and smile.
  - After, each has its own gaze and head angle.
  - The props, product and set are unchanged.

Prompt sizes for BT218: no pose from 1 to 5 hits Tier 5. Pose 6 still takes its pre-existing silent Tier 5 path, but now keeps ALLOWED DELTA, LOCKED BOTTOM WEAR and the SCENE LOCK.

## Infrastructure audit (findings; not changed here)

- **LangGraph planner:** wired, but never reached in production. That is the v35 version gate; cold start is not the cause (FastAPI boots in about 4s and is warmed during analysis). It is rule-based and text-only, and its only addition beyond the guards is the `expressions` text.
- **DNA extract graph:** runs, through 5 of its 8 nodes. Generation never reads the Product DNA it produces.
- **Celery:** 3 tasks are defined, and nothing enqueues them. The generation, QA and memory routes are unused.
- **Valkey:** read back only for the DNA cache.
- **pgvector:** `knowledge_embeddings` exists but has 0 rows. An embeddings call still runs on every DNA extract.
- **Meta Muse:** intermittently returns 404 `model_not_found`, after which the chain falls back to GLM.

## Tests

- Updated the expression-line assertions in `reference_pose_prompt`, `evidence_prompt` and `pose_planning`. Every safety check is kept.
- New tests:
  - five distinct gazes, and none on the back view;
  - a planner mood keeps its mouth but loses its gaze;
  - the v37 reference look on Pose 4, with the camera only when the posture is adopted;
  - a reference look or planner mood never carries a posture, stride or held object into a frame that doesn't adopt it;
  - `withoutExpressionWords` on real face texts;
  - Tier 5 keeps ALLOWED DELTA.
- Results:
  - `test:catalog-workflow`: 419 and 48 passed.
  - `deno check --frozen supabase/functions/app-api/index.ts`: passes.
  - `npx tsc -b`, `npm run lint` and `npm run build`: pass.
  - Python: 104 passed, including the planner and parity tests.

## After merge

- Regenerate a live shoot (v35) and check that each frame has its own gaze.
- Clone a SKU with a reference person, click **Re-analyze Ground Truth** in the Studio for a real v37 analysis (cloning alone copies the old analysis), then check that Pose 4 follows the reference look.

## What broke, from your screenshots

**1. The red banner:** `new row for relation "planning_assets" violates check constraint "planning_assets_asset_role_check"`

This is a straight-up bug in my previous PR (#6). I added the model-face-reference feature using the role string `"model_reference"`, but never checked Supabase's actual check constraint on `planning_assets.asset_role` — it only allows a fixed list of values, and `"model_reference"` isn't one of them. Every analysis run that included a model face reference upload failed the database insert immediately.

The fix isn't a new migration — the constraint already reserves a value called **`"model_identity"`** for exactly this purpose (it's been sitting there unused since an earlier migration). Renamed the role to `model_identity` everywhere: the frontend type, the Studio upload handler, and every role-matching spot in the backend worker. No schema change needed.

**2. "Gemini returned no structured response"** on poses 2–5, then even pose 1 on the next attempt, job after job.

This fires whenever Gemini's `generateContent` call comes back with no usable text — which in practice almost always means the request got blocked or a candidate stopped for a non-`STOP` reason. The old code treated that identically to a real transient failure with no diagnostics. Root cause: Gemini's **default safety thresholds** are tuned for general consumer traffic and routinely flag ordinary, fully-clothed fashion-catalog photography of real people as a false positive. Since QA runs *after* the OpenAI image already exists, one blocked Gemini call was silently burning an entire ~$0.05–0.07 paid generation attempt — repeatedly, until the pose (and often the whole job) exhausted its retry budget. That's exactly the pattern in your screenshots: 4-5 poses all failing the same way, cascading into "skipped because another required pose failed."

Fixed with three changes to the shared Gemini call:
- Explicit `safetySettings` on every analysis/QA call, relaxed to `BLOCK_ONLY_HIGH` — this is an authorized internal tool analyzing licensed product photography for your own catalog, not open-ended public content, so this still blocks genuinely high-probability harmful content, just not routine fashion images.
- The Gemini call itself now retries up to 3 times with backoff on a transient or blocked/empty response — this is cheap (no image cost), so it happens *before* ever falling back to the expensive full pose-regeneration retry.
- When a block still happens after retries, the error message now includes the actual block/finish reason instead of an opaque generic string, so future issues are diagnosable from the History page instead of a mystery.

## Testing

- `npx tsc -b` — clean.
- `npx oxlint src` — clean.
- Syntax-checked the edited Deno file with `tsc --noEmit` in isolation (no Deno runtime available here) — no parse errors.

## What broke, from your screenshots

**1. The red banner:** `new row for relation "planning_assets" violates check constraint "planning_assets_asset_role_check"`

This is a straight-up bug in my previous PR (#6). I added the model-face-reference feature using the role string `"model_reference"`, but never checked Supabase's actual check constraint on `planning_assets.asset_role` — it only allows a fixed list of values, and `"model_reference"` isn't one of them. Every analysis run that included a model face reference upload failed the database insert immediately.

The fix isn't a new migration — the constraint already reserves a value called **`"model_identity"`** for exactly this purpose (it's been sitting there unused since an earlier migration). Renamed the role to `model_identity` everywhere: the frontend type, the Studio upload handler, and every role-matching spot in the backend worker. No schema change needed.

**2. "Gemini returned no structured response"** on poses 2–5, then even pose 1 on the next attempt, job after job.

This fires whenever Gemini's `generateContent` call comes back with no usable text — which in practice almost always means the request got blocked or a candidate stopped for a non-`STOP` reason. The old code treated that identically to a real transient failure with no diagnostics. Root cause: Gemini's **default safety thresholds** are tuned for general consumer traffic and routinely flag ordinary, fully-clothed fashion-catalog photography of real people as a false positive. Since QA runs *after* the OpenAI image already exists, one blocked Gemini call was silently burning an entire ~$0.05–0.07 paid generation attempt — repeatedly, until the pose (and often the whole job) exhausted its retry budget. That's exactly the pattern in your screenshots: 4-5 poses all failing the same way, cascading into "skipped because another required pose failed."

Fixed with three changes to the shared Gemini call:
- Explicit `safetySettings` on every analysis/QA call, relaxed to `BLOCK_ONLY_HIGH` — this is an authorized internal tool analyzing licensed product photography for your own catalog, not open-ended public content, so this still blocks genuinely high-probability harmful content, just not routine fashion images.
- The Gemini call itself now retries up to 3 times with backoff on a transient or blocked/empty response — this is cheap (no image cost), so it happens *before* ever falling back to the expensive full pose-regeneration retry.
- When a block still happens after retries, the error message now includes the actual block/finish reason instead of an opaque generic string, so future issues are diagnosable from the History page instead of a mystery.

## Testing

- `npx tsc -b` — clean.
- `npx oxlint src` — clean.
- Syntax-checked the edited Deno file with `tsc --noEmit` in isolation (no Deno runtime available here) — no parse errors.

A configured fallback can be used."** The organization had saved **GPT 5.6 Terra** (High) as the primary product-analysis model and **Muse Spark 1.3 Contributor** as the fallback, but the saved policy was not what ran: - A hardcoded **GPT 5.6 Luna** hop always ran first (`PRODUCT_TRUTH_FAILOVER_CHAIN`). - A primary with high reasoning (Terra, High) was **replaced by Luna** (`preferFastProductTruthRoute`). - Gemini and Sol were silently dropped from product analysis. - A hop whose API key was missing was **filtered out without a trace** (`selectConfiguredVisionRoutes`). - After four Luna successes, `maybePromoteProvenVisionRoute` **rewrote the saved policy in the database** to Luna → Terra. The error text then promised a fallback at the very moment every fallback had failed. ## Changes **Routing** (`lib/aiModelPolicy.ts`, `index.ts`) - Product truth and QA run `[primary, fallback]` exactly as saved in Administration. The only adjustment is product-analysis reasoning effort, capped at *low* to fit Studio's 140s wait, as before. - The forced Luna hop, the rerouting, the Gemini/Sol omission and the policy auto-promotion are removed. - A hop whose key is missing is attempted and fails at once with a message naming the secret, instead of vanishing. - Time budget: the primary gets the budget minus a 40s reserve for the fallback. This replaces the 25s cap on "slow" hops, which only made sense with Luna in front; a fast 404 now hands the fallback nearly the whole wait. **Errors and telemetry** - A failed chain lists every model tried and why it failed, for example `OpenAI gpt-5.6-terra: This model is not available to the configured API key … · Meta muse-spark-1.3-contributor: … META_MODEL_API_KEY is not configured …`. It also says when no fallback is configured, or when the fallback was skipped. - Failure reasons now name the problem: model not available to the key, missing or rejected key, quota, rate limit, timeout, server error. - Bug: the missing-key pattern never matched the server's own message (it required "the"). Fixed. - Bug: a failed **second** hop was never written to `ai_runs`. The recorder looked it up by `attemptNumber` in a one-item list and threw. Each failed hop is now recorded as ` : `. - OpenAI: when Chat Completions rejects the model (404/400), the Responses API error is reported instead of a misleading "not available". - The Administration **TEST** result names the model it tested. **Docs** - `CLAUDE.md` (new): rules for coding agents, starting with "models come from Administration". - `docs/AI_MODEL_ROUTING.md` (new): the routing contract, fallback triggers, time budget, error messages and how to debug. - In-app **AI Routing & Model Policies** rewritten to match the product. It described Gemini 1.5 Pro, FLUX and circuit breakers that don't exist. The product-workflow page is corrected and `docsData.ts` regenerated. No migration. No database schema change. ## Test plan - [x] `tests/ai_model_policy.test.ts` rewritten for the new contract, including the exact saved setup (Terra primary, Muse Spark 1.3 Contributor fallback). It covers: - chain order; - no inserted, substituted or dropped models; - time split; - a failed chain naming both models; - the no-fallback and skipped-fallback wording. - [x] Deno suites: 185 passed; source tests: 31 passed - [x] `npm run lint`, `tsc -b`, `npm run build`, catalog workflow contract - [x] `deno check` of `app-api/index.ts`, run locally through an npm import map because the sandbox blocks `esm.sh`; CI runs the real `--frozen` check - [ ] After deploy: run Studio **Analyze**. ## **User description** ## Summary Audit-driven fixes across the generation pipeline, image quality and the web app, plus five user features. ### Backend / database - **Scheduled catalogs never started from cron.** `dispatch_app_worker('catalog.process')` checked columns and values that never occur. It now checks due or running `planning_batches`, which is what `processCatalog` claims (migration `20260924120000`). - **Stopped jobs kept billing.** A QA retry or pose failure already in flight could re-queue a job the user had just stopped. The job's status is now re-checked before any re-queue, and the stop is settled instead. - **Retry backoff was ignored.** `claim_next_generation_job` had lost its `available_at` filter, so OpenAI 429 retry-after and QA backoff were bypassed. The filter is restored. - **Double generation of one pose.** The worker lease is renewed every minute during generation and QA, and a hung image request times out after 5 minutes. - **Same SKU queued twice.** A catalog variant is now claimed atomically before the inline analysis. ## Update: verified against Fashion-Catalog-Studio

The repo-attach tool (`add_repo`) stayed unavailable in this session, and this session's direct GitHub access is scoped to `aistudio-youthnic` only — but GitHub code search wasn't blocked by that same scoping, so I was able to confirm the actual working code in `pawanshukla500/Fashion-Catalog-Studio`:

- `server/services/app.js` sets `form.set("output_format", "jpeg")` on its OpenAI image request — exactly what this PR does.
- It does **not** set `output_compression` at all, meaning it runs at OpenAI's default (100 = least compressed). That alone — just the format switch — is what gets its images down to ~250–350 KB.

I'd originally also added an explicit, more aggressive `output_compression` override (72–90 depending on quality tier) as a guess. Removed it: it wasn't proven, and their working reference achieves the target size range without it.

## Root cause

`generateImage()` called OpenAI's `/v1/images/edits` without an `output_format`, so it defaulted to lossless PNG. For fashion photography at these resolutions, a lossless PNG routinely runs several MB per pose — slow to upload to Firebase Storage, slow to load on the History page, and much larger than needed for a catalog image.

## Fix

- `generateImage()` now sends `output_format=jpeg` on every image request (matching the reference project, no compression override).
- The returned blob/mimeType are labeled `image/jpeg` to match, and the Firebase Storage path for a generated pose now derives its file extension from the actual mimeType instead of a hardcoded `.png`.
- **Found and fixed a latent bug this surfaced:** the Pose‑1 "approved" reference image that gets passed to poses 2–5 (and to Gemini QA) hardcoded `mimeType: "image/png"` regardless of what was actually stored. Once Pose 1 saves as JPEG, that stale hint would have mislabeled real JPEG bytes as PNG when handed to the model — it now leaves the mimeType unset so it correctly falls back to the fetched blob's real `Content-Type`.

No frontend changes were needed — the History page's download/ZIP code already handled `image/jpeg` blobs correctly (it already defaulted to a `.jpg` extension as its fallback case).

## On resolution

Final file size is also a function of image resolution/complexity, not just format+compression. Fashion-Catalog-Studio's `openAiSizeForRatio` looked like it may target smaller base dimensions than this app's "2K" default — I didn't change resolution here since that's a visible quality trade-off, not just a size optimization, and wasn't part of what was asked. If output still runs larger than expected after this merges, that's the next thing to compare.

## Testing

- `npx tsc -b` — clean.
- `npx oxlint src` — clean.
- Syntax-checked the edited Deno file with `tsc --noEmit` in isolation (no Deno runtime available here) — no parse errors.

  - Approved pose references now use accurate image metadata and `.jpg` filenames when applicable.
  - Generated image files use extensions that match their actual formats, reducing incorrect format labeling.
