* Stop double billing and stuck/duplicate catalog runs; fix cost accounting

- Renew the worker lease every minute during generation and QA, and time
  out a hung image request after 5 minutes. Recovery used to requeue a
  pose that was still running, so the same image was generated twice.
- Claim a catalog variant atomically before the inline analysis, and only
  treat queued/processing variants as stale after 10 minutes, so two
  concurrent kicks can no longer queue the same SKU twice.
- Regenerate pose and re-run QA resolve the job that produced the pose
  (newest as fallback) instead of .single() on session_id, which threw
  once a session had been re-run.

  analysis cost only since the previous job for that product/session.

  2 minutes (reference changes still retry immediately); the cron work
  check mirrors this so idle sleeps are not interrupted.

  writing.

hits.message:
perf: switch generated images to compressed JPEG instead of PNG

Image generation asked OpenAI for its default output (lossless PNG),
which routinely runs several MB per pose — slow to upload to Firebase
Storage, slow to load in History, and unnecessarily large for catalog
photography. Request compressed JPEG output instead:

- generateImage() now sends output_format=jpeg and output_compression
  to the OpenAI images/edits call, scaled with the existing quality
  setting (low/medium/high -> 72/82/90) so a higher quality tier still
  buys back some of the size the lower tiers trade away.
- The returned blob/mimeType are labeled image/jpeg to match, and the
  generated-image storage path now derives its extension from the
  actual mimeType instead of a hardcoded .png.
- Fixed a latent bug this surfaced: the Pose-1 "approved" reference
  image passed to poses 2-5 (and to Gemini QA) hardcoded
  mimeType: "image/png" regardless of what was actually stored. Once
  Pose 1 is saved as JPEG that hardcoded hint would have mislabeled
  real JPEG bytes as PNG. It now leaves mimeType unset so it correctly
  falls back to the fetched blob's real Content-Type.

The History page's download/ZIP code already handled image/jpeg blobs
correctly (it already defaulted to a .jpg extension), so no frontend
changes were needed.

hits.message:
Keep the Studio usable when one read is cut off (#109)

Two symptoms, both from the gateway cutting a call short.

The output panel read "route unavailable" and disabled the picker while the
badge beside it still named GPT Image 2. useQuery keeps the last good value when
a refresh fails, so the panel held the route the whole time; ordering the error
ahead of the data threw it away on the first transient failure. Data now wins.

ai.routing.effective is the only useQuery endpoint that goes through the Edge
Function rather than PostgREST, so it is the one read that queues behind a long
analyze and takes a 504 for it. Being side-effect-free, it is now retried once,
guarded by an allow-list so no mutation can ever be repeated and charged twice.
Its timeout advice no longer tells the operator to shrink images for a read that
runs one select.

Analysis was interrupted before OpenAI could finish, on runs the server would
have completed: the budget spent the client's entire wait, but the vision chain
starts its clock after auth, the workspace RPC and reference loading, leaving
all of that plus the trip home outside the per-hop reserve.
VISION_REQUEST_OVERHEAD_MS now names that outside-the-chain allowance, with a
test pinning the invariant: a lone hop plus both reserves is exactly the client
wait.

hits.message:
feat: optional model face reference for exact identity lock

Adds a way to pin the generated model's face to a specific uploaded
photo, instead of letting the shoot design its own consistent face.

Studio:
- New optional "Model face lock" upload (single photo) next to the
  product references, wired through the same upload/analysis/queue
  pipeline as front/back/style references (new "model_reference" role).

Analysis + generation pipeline (shared by Studio and Bulk, since both
go through lib/profiles.ts / composeGenerationPrompt / qa.ts):
- Reference authority list and Model Identity Profile instructions now
  tell Gemini to describe the uploaded face exactly when a MODEL FACE
  REFERENCE is present, instead of inventing one.
- selectReferences() now includes the model reference in every pose's
  image set (not just poses that also get the pose-1 anchor), always
  first in the manifest.
- composeGenerationPrompt()'s FACE & IDENTITY LOCK section gives the
  model reference top priority over the approved-pose-1 anchor when
  both are present - the anchor still governs scene/lighting/styling
  continuity, never the face.
- QA (buildPoseQaPrompt) compares the generated pose against the model
  reference directly when present, as a strict identity match, and
  fails model_face for any noticeable deviation - caught and retried
  within the existing 3-attempt budget.
- Bumped ANALYSIS_VERSION so this takes effect on the next analysis
  run instead of reusing a pre-change cache hit.

Bulk/Catalog generation runs through this same backend engine, so a
model_reference-tagged upload would already be honored there too, but
Planning.tsx has no UI to attach one yet - Studio only for now.

Note: this maximizes identity fidelity through the strongest available
prompt-level lock and QA rejection/retry, since neither OpenAI's images
API nor this pipeline has a dedicated face-ID/face-swap parameter -
it's not a literal pixel-guarantee, but the model reference now
overrides every other face source and gets enforced by QA.

* fix(studio): raise product-truth timeout and fail over Muse→Luna→Terra→Gemini

The 28s product_truth abort killed real multi-image analyze (Gemini Flash
often needs 30–37s) and then burned a second 28s on Luna, so Studio showed
a timeout at ~60s with only the last hop in ai_runs.

Give each hop 50s, clamp analyze thinking to low, continue the chain on
timeout, log every attempt, and auto-promote Luna/Terra after four
consecutive successful analyses.

* fix(studio): persist every vision hop before failover and promote Gemini from live completions

v144 only wrote the last attempt, which is why Muse timeouts never appeared as
meta rows while Luna showed the 58–65s banner. Log each hop immediately, keep
failing over Muse→Luna→Terra→Gemini Flash, and auto-promote Gemini when it
already has the completed ai_runs.

Co-authored-by: Pawan Shukla <returnorders@vbexports.co.in>

* docs: note immediate hop logging and Gemini auto-promotion from live ai_runs

Co-authored-by: Pawan Shukla <returnorders@vbexports.co.in>

CodeAnt review on PR #91: append extra stored fallbacks after Luna/Terra/Gemini, race each hop against timeoutMs, and do not retry the same product-truth route.

fix: model-reference DB constraint violation and flaky Gemini QA failures

Two separate root causes behind the reliability issues showing up in
History (failed jobs, "Gemini returned no structured response", and
a raw Postgres error banner in Studio):

1. planning_assets_asset_role_check violation. The model-face-reference
   feature (previous commit) used the role string "model_reference",
   but Supabase's check constraint on planning_assets.asset_role never
   allowed that value - it already reserved "model_identity" for
   exactly this purpose, unused until now. Every analyze() call that
   included a model reference upload failed the DB insert outright.
   Renamed the role to "model_identity" everywhere (frontend type,
   Studio upload handler, and every role-matching site in the backend
   worker) to match the existing constraint instead of writing a new
   migration - no schema change needed, just using the slot that was
   already there.

2. "Gemini returned no structured response." This fires whenever
   Gemini's generateContent call returns no usable text, which almost
   always means the request was blocked or a candidate stopped for a
   non-STOP reason - both look identical to the old code ("no text"),
   but Gemini's *default* safety thresholds are tuned for general
   consumer traffic and routinely flag ordinary, fully-clothed fashion
   catalog photography of real people as a false positive. Since QA
   runs after the (paid) OpenAI image already exists, one blocked
   Gemini call was silently burning a whole ~$0.05-0.07 generation
   attempt, repeatedly, until the pose (and often the whole job)
   exhausted its retry budget.

   Fixed by:
   - Sending explicit safetySettings on every Gemini analysis/QA call,
     relaxed to BLOCK_ONLY_HIGH for an authorized internal tool
     analyzing licensed product photography (not open-ended public
     content) - blocks genuinely high-probability harmful content,
     not routine catalog images.
   - Retrying the Gemini call itself (cheap, no image cost) up to 3
     times with backoff on a transient/empty response before ever
     surfacing a failure, instead of only retrying at the expensive
     full-pose-regeneration level.
   - Surfacing the actual block/finish reason in the error message
     when a block still happens, instead of an opaque generic string.

feat(planning): reference-led Pose 4/6, expression plan, DNA gate and LangGraph planner (#178)

* feat(planning): reference-led Pose 4/6, expression plan, DNA gate and LangGraph planner

Pose planning now follows both the style reference and the product type:

- Analysis records the style-reference person's posture, signature pose and
  suitability (referencePose) plus a shoot-wide expressionPlan. Pose 4
  (creative) and Pose 6 (showcase) copy that posture when the stored
  posePlanning adopts it; Poses 1, 2, 3 and 5 stay catalog frames. Outfit,
  face, hair and handheld objects stay quarantined in every frame. Hard guards
  (lib/posePlanning.ts) block no-person, generic standing, unsuitable, walking,
  Farshi + folded postures, saree + reclining, tight showcase crops and an
  explicit sit request for a non-seated reference.
- New LangGraph planning graph in FastAPI (POST /api/v1/plan):
  analyze_references -> recall_outcomes -> plan_poses -> plan_expression ->
  validate_plan, with per-node RetryPolicy and Postgres checkpoints. Edge calls
  it after the analysis vision call (no second vision call) and falls back to
  the same guards locally. A shared parity fixture keeps TS and Python in step.
- Always-on product DNA consistency check (shape, color, material, logo,
  details) before a pose is accepted. Failures are archived and retried within
  the existing limit; after the last attempt the frame is kept for human
  review; a check outage ships unverified. With full QA on, the verdict is
  derived from QA scores. Job cost estimates include it.
- Learning: pose_plan_outcomes records how each copy-the-reference vs
  product-led decision fared (DNA results and human verdicts) and the planner
  prefers what worked; generation_learnings stores the plan and per-pose
  scores. A style-reference profile cache skips re-sending a known style image
  to the analysis model.
- ANALYSIS_VERSION v36. Analyses without posePlanning keep today's pose
  behaviour. CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, MEMORY.md, docs and in-app docs updated.
  New Deno suites registered in both lists; CI runs the planner pytest.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs(troubleshooting): note that a sit request keeps Pose 4 seated

Reanalysing with a standing style reference does not override a sitting
request in the product notes, so the standing-frames advice now says to
remove that request first. Regenerates the in-app docs data.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Studio: make Scene direction / Garment summary editable and refresh the pose plan on edit

Both fields in AnalysisProfile were rendered readOnly even though their own
placeholders already said "Edit anytime" - a stale promise the UI never kept.

name already do: editing them calls the existing markAnalysisStale() path, so
the "Inputs changed - analysis and the pose plan are stale and will rebuild
automatically" flow (already wired for every other input) picks them up and
reruns analysis+pose-plan generation automatically after the same debounce.

analysis result - it's sent as an extra director's note merged into the
existing sceneDirection/productDetails params Gemini already reads as
"requested scene direction" / "user product notes", so the product identity
and five-pose plan get re-derived around the correction instead of just
re-labelling the old plan.

Because those same params already feed the backend's analysis cache key
(productHash in supabase/functions/app-api/index.ts), repeating an edit you've
already made - or reverting one - now hits the existing 30-day analysis_cache
instead of a fresh Gemini call, the same "reused to reduce latency and cost"
path the Model & scene context panel already surfaces for cache hits.

fix: strengthen face realism and identity-consistency guardrails

Reviewed the full face-generation pipeline (analysis prompt, pose
plan, generation prompt, QA validator, and the History regenerate
flow) and closed the gaps that let faces drift, look synthetic, or go
unvalidated:

- Analysis prompt now asks for a concrete, specific Model Identity
  Profile (face shape, eyes, brows, nose, lips, jawline) instead of
  generic filler, plus a new modelIdentity.faceRealism lock: natural
  skin texture/pores, correct eye anatomy and catchlights, naturally
  aligned teeth, no plastic/waxy/mirror-symmetric "AI face". Extended
  creativeDirection.realismRules the same way.
- Generation prompt gets a new, highest-priority "FACE & IDENTITY
  LOCK" section: for poses 2-5 it points explicitly at the APPROVED
  POSE 1 reference image as the non-negotiable identity ground truth
  (facial bone structure, eyes, nose, lips, jawline, skin); for pose 1
  it commits to one specific photorealistic face for the rest of the
  set to match. Added explicit eye/teeth/skin realism bullets
  (skipped for the back pose, where the face isn't in frame).
- QA validator gets a dedicated face_realism check (separate from
  model_face identity-match) with a concrete failure bar - distorted/
  misaligned eyes, warped or uniform teeth, waxy/airbrushed skin - so
  a bad face is caught and retried (up to the existing 3-attempt
  budget) instead of silently passing.
- History's regenerate-pose dialog now warns when regenerating Pose 1
  specifically, since it's the face/shoot anchor the other four poses
  were generated to match, and regenerating it can change the face
  without touching poses 2-5.
- Bumped ANALYSIS_VERSION so existing cached/stored analyses pick up
  the new face-realism lock instead of reusing pre-change output.

supabase/functions/app-api/index.ts:
- saveReferenceOperation's shared-reference branch (style_reference/model_identity) and

  already tolerates 404s, so this stays safe even if a concurrent request cleaned up the
  same path first.

supabase/migrations/20260813120000_planning_batch_reference_atomic_update.sql:

applyCatalogMemory replays the stored scene over every later analysis, so
without this a new reference appeared to change nothing - the catalog kept

hits.message:
Fix mutate_planning_batch_reference_images: lock row before deriving removed/updated arrays

CodeRabbit review on PR #9 flagged that the removed and updated CTEs each read
batch.reference_images independently: `removed` was a plain SELECT sharing the
statement's start-of-query snapshot, while the UPDATE only re-checks the latest
committed row for its own SET clause (via Postgres's read-committed recheck).
Under a concurrent model_identity replacement, those two reads could disagree,
so the "removed" entries returned for storage cleanup would not necessarily
match what the UPDATE actually wrote.

Verified this is real: loaded the function into a scratch Postgres 16 database
and ran two overlapping transactions replacing the same batch's model_identity
entry. Confirmed the second transaction's returned "removed" entry (used to
drive Firebase Storage cleanup) matched the first transaction's newly-committed
entry, not the pre-transaction stale value.

Fixed by adding a `locked` CTE that takes the row lock with FOR UPDATE first;
both `removed` and the UPDATE's replacement-array subquery now derive from
`locked.reference_images`, and the UPDATE targets the row via `FROM locked`
instead of re-filtering by p_batch_id independently. Re-ran the same concurrent
test against the fixed function - the second transaction now correctly reports
the first transaction's committed entry as removed. No signature or call-site
changes; saveReferenceOperation and removeCatalogStyleReferenceOperation in
index.ts are unaffected.

hits.message:
fix: stop a hedged QA score from rejecting a frame it just approved

A live shoot rejected pose 1 with "Consistency QA failed: Image A
successfully aligns with model facial features, garment details, and scene
requirements. Lowest matches: model_face 75%, garment_identity 75%,
colors 75%." The validator approved the frame in prose and then returned a
flat 75 on every attribute, and the gate treated those numbers as a verdict -
discarding a correct image and paying for another generation to find out.

Two causes.

The scale had no anchor, so 75 was a hedge rather than a measurement. The
prompt now defines what each band means (100 indistinguishable, 95 acceptable
rendering difference, 85 a buyer would notice, 70 a different arrangement of
the same idea, 40 a different product), forbids lowering every attribute
together to signal general uncertainty, and requires any critical score below
85 to name the defect and fail that check. A defect that cannot be named is
not a defect.

And a bare number could veto an explicit pass. A critical score now rejects
only when it is severe enough to be a claim on its own (below 60) or when the
validator also flagged that check. Between 60 and 85 with a passing verdict
the frame is delivered, carrying its score and a review-recommended flag that
History surfaces, instead of being destroyed. The weighted floor no longer
rejects at all - it only marks a frame as worth a visual check.

The failure message also leads with the deciding rule now, so a rejection can
no longer read "QA failed: Image A successfully aligns".

  continuing decoration across panels.

hits.message:
feat: geometry-bearing Product DNA and a product-fidelity gate

The generator was reinterpreting prints and embroidery into a plausible
lookalike, and QA passed every frame anyway - all five poses of the bandhani
kurta shipped COMPLETED with redrawn motifs and a different yoke lattice.

Two causes, both fixed here.

The structured DNA had no geometry: pattern, print and embroidery were four
free-text strings, so nothing in the prompt could pin motif scale, spacing,
orientation, per-panel placement or embroidery construction. Analysis now
produces patternGeometry and embroideryGeometry, the prompt carries them as a
hard lock, and the fabric/pattern image is named pixel-level authority for
motif scale. ANALYSIS_VERSION is bumped so cached v8 profiles re-analyse.

QA had no geometry check and no weighting: every check was an equal pass/fail
and the verdict was the validator's own boolean. It now scores each attribute
0-100, weights the seven SKU-defining ones double, and fails a frame whose
critical attribute drops below 85% or whose weighted fidelity drops below 88%
even when the validator called it a pass. Failures flow into the existing
retry path with the weakest attributes named, and History shows the score
with a per-attribute breakdown.

Also: the model-identity reference is now explicitly face/skin/hair only, so
a different garment in that photo cannot bleed into the SKU; the close-up
trades its style-reference slots for product detail once the anchor exists;
and the session records its Product DNA version and per-pose fidelity in
Supabase, which stays the single record of the shoot.

fix: strengthen face realism and identity-consistency guardrails

Reviewed the full face-generation pipeline (analysis prompt, pose
plan, generation prompt, QA validator, and the History regenerate
flow) and closed the gaps that let faces drift, look synthetic, or go
unvalidated:

- Analysis prompt now asks for a concrete, specific Model Identity
  Profile (face shape, eyes, brows, nose, lips, jawline) instead of
  generic filler, plus a new modelIdentity.faceRealism lock: natural
  skin texture/pores, correct eye anatomy and catchlights, naturally
  aligned teeth, no plastic/waxy/mirror-symmetric "AI face". Extended
  creativeDirection.realismRules the same way.
- Generation prompt gets a new, highest-priority "FACE & IDENTITY
  LOCK" section: for poses 2-5 it points explicitly at the APPROVED
  POSE 1 reference image as the non-negotiable identity ground truth
  (facial bone structure, eyes, nose, lips, jawline, skin); for pose 1
  it commits to one specific photorealistic face for the rest of the
  set to match. Added explicit eye/teeth/skin realism bullets
  (skipped for the back pose, where the face isn't in frame).
- QA validator gets a dedicated face_realism check (separate from
  model_face identity-match) with a concrete failure bar - distorted/
  misaligned eyes, warped or uniform teeth, waxy/airbrushed skin - so
  a bad face is caught and retried (up to the existing 3-attempt
  budget) instead of silently passing.
- History's regenerate-pose dialog now warns when regenerating Pose 1
  specifically, since it's the face/shoot anchor the other four poses
  were generated to match, and regenerating it can change the face
  without touching poses 2-5.
- Bumped ANALYSIS_VERSION so existing cached/stored analyses pick up
  the new face-realism lock instead of reusing pre-change output.

Backend

  occur, so cron never started scheduled catalogs. Check due/running
  planning_batches instead; also skip catalog.preflight calls when nothing
  is pending so the functions service can sleep.

  retry backoff and OpenAI 429 retry-after are honoured.

  already in flight and keep generating and billing. Re-check the status
  before requeueing and settle the cancellation instead.

  smoothing (was 1280px / 0.85), so weave and small motifs survive.

  continuity anchor, so poses 2-6 stop drifting.
- Generated images are stored and sent to QA with their real MIME type.
- Prompt no longer forces an 85mm lens or Pose 1 camera distance on every
  frame (fought close-ups), nor a smile on every pose.
- Fallback image quality for jobs without a stored value is "high".

- Polling: one request at a time, paused in hidden tabs.

  Stopping/Stopped states; handle a deleted or failing submission.

- Renew the worker lease every minute during generation and QA, and time
  out a hung image request after 5 minutes. Recovery used to requeue a
  pose that was still running, so the same image was generated twice.
- Claim a catalog variant atomically before the inline analysis, and only
  treat queued/processing variants as stale after 10 minutes, so two

- Regenerate pose and re-run QA resolve the job that produced the pose

hits.message:
feat: styling memory on Supabase, read back into analysis

Switches the AI memory store from Firestore to Supabase, and closes the loop
rather than only storing rows.

styling_decisions records each decision as AI proposal, approved plan, and the
exact fields a human rewrote, org-scoped with RLS and readable by planning.view.
Both save paths write it: catalogue approval and Studio session edits.

The analysis reads it back. Before proposing a styling plan it pulls the recent
approved decisions for that organization and category, keeps only the fields a
stylist actually rewrote, and passes the most recent correction per field into
the prompt as house preference - ranked below product truth and below the style
reference, so it informs taste without overriding what the images show. Repeated
corrections carry their count, so "heavy gold changed to minimal oxidised, three
times" reads as a preference rather than a one-off.

Only rewritten fields travel: an unchanged proposal says nothing about taste,
and the brief stays a few hundred characters however long the history grows.
Studio's cached analyses skip the lookup entirely, so a repeat product costs no
extra query.

Recording failures are logged and swallowed - memory is an enhancement, never a
reason to fail a stylist's save.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

hits.message:
feat: geometry-bearing Product DNA and a product-fidelity gate

The generator was reinterpreting prints and embroidery into a plausible
lookalike, and QA passed every frame anyway - all five poses of the bandhani
kurta shipped COMPLETED with redrawn motifs and a different yoke lattice.

Two causes, both fixed here.

The structured DNA had no geometry: pattern, print and embroidery were four
free-text strings, so nothing in the prompt could pin motif scale, spacing,
orientation, per-panel placement or embroidery construction. Analysis now
produces patternGeometry and embroideryGeometry, the prompt carries them as a
hard lock, and the fabric/pattern image is named pixel-level authority for
motif scale. ANALYSIS_VERSION is bumped so cached v8 profiles re-analyse.

QA had no geometry check and no weighting: every check was an equal pass/fail
and the verdict was the validator's own boolean. It now scores each attribute
0-100, weights the seven SKU-defining ones double, and fails a frame whose
critical attribute drops below 85% or whose weighted fidelity drops below 88%
even when the validator called it a pass. Failures flow into the existing
retry path with the weakest attributes named, and History shows the score
with a per-attribute breakdown.

Also: the model-identity reference is now explicitly face/skin/hair only, so
a different garment in that photo cannot bleed into the SKU; the close-up
trades its style-reference slots for product detail once the anchor exists;
and the session records its Product DNA version and per-pose fidelity in
Supabase, which stays the single record of the shoot.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

hits.message:
Choose the sixth frame's subject per product, and learn from the outcome (#107)

The sixth frame ran a fixed template per garment family, so a kurta set
always got "complete set, head to toe" - which is the hero frame again,
paid for and adding no catalog coverage.

Its subject is now a per-SKU decision the vision analysis records in
showcasePlan: the one feature a buyer judges this product by (a yoke,
neckline, sleeve, print, the cut and flare of the bottom wear, a hem or
border, a dupatta, a saree's pallu or drape), the shot type that sells it,
the evidence that proves it, and how the frame differs from the others.
The pose slot, the generation hard rule, the shoot memory and the feedback
key are all resolved from one shared helper, so a frame widened to avoid
colliding with the pose 5 close-up is described and scored as the frame
that actually shipped.

Non-duplication is enforced rather than requested: the analysis prompt
forbids both a second hero shot and a re-shoot of pose 5's subject, and a
tight shot whose subject collides with the recorded close-up detail is
widened in code.

showcase_feature_outcomes scores each (category, garment family, feature
region, shot type) by what operators do - approving the pose version or
the whole set, rejecting it, asking for a regeneration, or QA refusing it.
Writes are compare-and-set and never block the decision that produced
them; reads are org, category and family scoped, and a caller that does
not yet know the family gets no guidance rather than another family's. A
completed frame is not a success; only a human keeping it is.

ANALYSIS_VERSION moves to v22, so each SKU re-analyses once rather than
reusing a cached plan carrying the fixed brief.

studio-f4a24983 lost all five poses and $0.7527 because Gemini answered the

but the thrown error was treated as one: the image was discarded, retried
three times into the same block, and the anchor failure then cascaded.

- A QA call that cannot return a verdict (safety block, provider outage,
  malformed response) now delivers the generated frame with qa_status
  'unverified' and an explanatory note instead of destroying it. No QA
  review row is written, so an unchecked frame leaves no "passed" audit
  trail, and Studio/History badge it as needing manual review.
- The QA and analysis prompts asked Gemini to verify that two images show
  "the same person" at facial-feature level - person identification, which
  its policy blocks. They now compare visual appearance attributes and
  explicitly disclaim identifying anyone, which is what QA actually needs.

Mannequin and flat-lay shots become a first-class reference role: Studio
gains an upload slot, the analysis reads worn shape, proportion, length and
drape from it, and generation ranks it with primary product truth while

hits.message:
fix: stop a hedged QA score from rejecting a frame it just approved

A live shoot rejected pose 1 with "Consistency QA failed: Image A
successfully aligns with model facial features, garment details, and scene
requirements. Lowest matches: model_face 75%, garment_identity 75%,
colors 75%." The validator approved the frame in prose and then returned a
flat 75 on every attribute, and the gate treated those numbers as a verdict -
discarding a correct image and paying for another generation to find out.

Two causes.

The scale had no anchor, so 75 was a hedge rather than a measurement. The
prompt now defines what each band means (100 indistinguishable, 95 acceptable
rendering difference, 85 a buyer would notice, 70 a different arrangement of
the same idea, 40 a different product), forbids lowering every attribute
together to signal general uncertainty, and requires any critical score below
85 to name the defect and fail that check. A defect that cannot be named is
not a defect.

And a bare number could veto an explicit pass. A critical score now rejects
only when it is severe enough to be a claim on its own (below 60) or when the
validator also flagged that check. Between 60 and 85 with a passing verdict
the frame is delivered, carrying its score and a review-recommended flag that
History surfaces, instead of being destroyed. The weighted floor no longer
rejects at all - it only marks a frame as worth a visual check.

The failure message also leads with the deciding rule now, so a rejection can
no longer read "QA failed: Image A successfully aligns".

hits.message:
feat: footwear, jewellery and styling plan for Studio and catalogues

Styling was one free-text line - creativeDirection.suggestedAccessories -
rendered read-only, so nothing decided footwear and jewellery deliberately and
nothing kept them steady across a catalogue.

Analysis now produces a structured stylingPlan: footwear, jewellery,
ornaments, makeup, hair, stylist notes and a reading of the reference theme.
The prompt asks for choices a stylist could pull off a shelf - metal and
family named, each piece listed - decided from the product references first
and the style reference second, and it is held apart from productIdentity so
footwear the customer receives is never confused with footwear the stylist
adds. Generation locks the plan into all five frames and QA fails a frame that
invents a piece, drops one, or changes the metal.

Studio shows the plan as editable fields saved onto the session. Styling is
not a product fact, so the analysis fingerprint is untouched and queueing
still validates against the references.

For catalogues the first analysed colourway proposes the plan and generation
waits: the batch parks in awaiting_styling_approval until someone reviews it,
then every SKU inherits the approved plan through catalog_memory instead of
each one guessing its own jewellery. Approving hands the batch back to the
runner that owns it, since the scheduler only claims rows still marked
scheduled. Batches predating styling plans have none and keep running
untouched.

The AI's original proposal is kept beside the edited copy as
stylingPlanProposed. Comparing what was proposed against what was approved is
the raw material the Firestore learning layer needs, and it is unrecoverable
once the plan is edited in place.

hits.message:
feat: optional model face reference for exact identity lock

Adds a way to pin the generated model's face to a specific uploaded
photo, instead of letting the shoot design its own consistent face.

Studio:
- New optional "Model face lock" upload (single photo) next to the
  product references, wired through the same upload/analysis/queue
  pipeline as front/back/style references (new "model_reference" role).

Analysis + generation pipeline (shared by Studio and Bulk, since both
go through lib/profiles.ts / composeGenerationPrompt / qa.ts):
- Reference authority list and Model Identity Profile instructions now
  tell Gemini to describe the uploaded face exactly when a MODEL FACE
  REFERENCE is present, instead of inventing one.
- selectReferences() now includes the model reference in every pose's
  image set (not just poses that also get the pose-1 anchor), always
  first in the manifest.
- composeGenerationPrompt()'s FACE & IDENTITY LOCK section gives the
  model reference top priority over the approved-pose-1 anchor when
  both are present - the anchor still governs scene/lighting/styling
  continuity, never the face.
- QA (buildPoseQaPrompt) compares the generated pose against the model
  reference directly when present, as a strict identity match, and
  fails model_face for any noticeable deviation - caught and retried
  within the existing 3-attempt budget.
- Bumped ANALYSIS_VERSION so this takes effect on the next analysis
  run instead of reusing a pre-change cache hit.

Bulk/Catalog generation runs through this same backend engine, so a
model_reference-tagged upload would already be honored there too, but
Planning.tsx has no UI to attach one yet - Studio only for now.

Note: this maximizes identity fidelity through the strongest available
prompt-level lock and QA rejection/retry, since neither OpenAI's images
API nor this pipeline has a dedicated face-ID/face-swap parameter -
it's not a literal pixel-guarantee, but the model reference now
overrides every other face source and gets enforced by QA.

## Summary
- Dockerfiles for gateway (Cloud Run Service) and agents (Cloud Run Worker Pool), both built and smoke-tested locally
- `.github/workflows/deploy.yml`: builds/pushes images to Artifact Registry and deploys via Workload Identity Federation (no long-lived service-account keys), with per-service `--set-secrets` wiring Secret Manager into each Cloud Run resource
- `scripts/push-secrets-to-gcp.sh` and `scripts/grant-secret-access.sh` to populate Secret Manager from `.env.prod` and grant each service account least-privilege read access to only the secrets it uses
- `SECURITY.md` — vulnerability disclosure policy
- `docs/deploy/` — architecture and reasoning behind the all-serverless shape (Cloud Run + Neon/Qdrant Cloud/Redis Cloud managed free tiers, chosen for cost and reduced attack surface over GKE/self-hosted alternatives)

hits.message:
fix(agents): fix security agent diff source and asyncpg event loop crash

Security agent was rebuilding the diff from file.patch objects, which
GitHub truncates at ~3000 chars for large files, silently dropping content
the scanners needed to fire. Now it receives the same pre-fetched unified
diff string that quality and testing agents use (passed through graph state).

Coordinator was calling asyncio.run(_persist(...)) which creates a new event
loop, but the shared async engine was bound to a different loop (created at
import time or on the gateway loop), causing asyncpg to raise:
  RuntimeError: Future attached to a different loop

Fix: add fresh_session_context() to shared.db that creates and disposes a
throw-away engine scoped to the current asyncio.run() loop. _persist uses
this instead of the shared session_context.

F-15 (FR-15), human-in-the-loop (NFR-13): a chat panel reachable from every workspace screen that answers with real catalog surfaces grounded in the field's own data, never changing state without a confirmed tap.

## Plan
- `packages/ui-kit/catalog/react/`: an `@a2ui/react` renderer wired to a custom `app-catalog/v1` registry mapping every catalog component to ui-kit/app components; client-side validation before render, predefined fallback layout on failure.
- `apps/web/src/assistant/`: chat panel (`@ai-sdk/react`'s `useChat` against the gateway's stream), browser-executed client tools (`get_field_summary`, `compare_rotations`, `run_backtest`, `get_season`, `explain_exclusion`, `define_term`, `navigate`), `set_priorities`/`set_constraints` only through a rendered `ConfirmForm` applied on Confirm, `ActionChips` that run real tools and patch the surface's data model, `SourceChips`/`TraceDrawer`, and "Ask about this" wired on evidence cards and the selected season.
- Mounted as a global panel in `RootLayout`, lazy-loaded so it doesn't inflate the initial bundle.

## Checks
- `pnpm check` (27 tasks) and `pnpm build` pass. Initial JS is 163.5 KB gz (+3.8 KB over dev, budget is 300 KB); the assistant itself is a separate 152.6 KB gz chunk loaded on first open.
- Verified in headless Chrome against a scripted mock gateway (the real `createGateway` handler with a fake model): a scripted question gets >=1 tool call and >=2 catalog components; "Try barley instead" updates the surface in 11-22 ms on a 3-season fixture; priorities/constraints stay unchanged until Confirm and apply after it; an invalid surface falls back to the predefined layout and an unknown chip action is dropped; a navigation chip closes the panel and routes; keyboard-only open/focus-return/reopen-keeps-conversation; gateway-down shows an error; no horizontal overflow at 375 px.
- Not verified: a real LLM/provider (Gemini/Groq) end to end, timings at full 25-season scale, and screen-reader behavior.

## Deviations
- Rotation ids (40+ chars) exceed the catalog's 32-char handle limit, so the model sees short handles (`r1`, `r2`); tools resolve them back.
- The model's own `updateDataModel` writes are ignored; the app fills the data model from tool results, so numbers never come from model text.
- Tool outputs sent to the model are compact (to stay under the gateway's 64 KB body cap); the fuller view data stays client-side.
- "Ask about this" is wired on evidence cards and the selected season only, not individual chart bars or map zones.
- `MapFocus` for a zones layer shows a placeholder note since zones (#23) don't exist yet.
- `ClimateStrip` is backed by per-season mean scores rather than the monthly anomaly fingerprint from #21.

Closes #33

The Arena/zones/NISAR step still calls the science API, so the script is not yet fully offline.

- `apps/web/src/demo/`: a step engine (`useDemo` store) holding fixed field/rotation/priority/scenario values per step (documented in a constants file, not scattered inline), ten step renderers reusing the real `FieldTwin`, Field Memory, Climate Fingerprint, compare, sliders, future and arena screens, and an offline `ScriptedAnswer` component using the assistant's own template system (no LLM call) for the Q&A beat.
- `apps/web/src/routes/demo.tsx`: a standalone full-screen route (outside the normal workspace nav), keyboard advance (→/space, ←back) and a Reset that clears the field store back to initial state.

- The assistant step asks the template system's guaranteed-to-match example question ("Why is the top rotation ranked first?") rather than the illustrative "why chickpea" line from the script, since that exact phrasing isn't guaranteed to match a template; there's no "Try barley instead" action chip, since the template builder doesn't generate one for any intent yet.

Records the changes made while deploying the assistant gateway (`itza-si-gateway`, Cloudflare Worker) to production, and fixes two faults found in the live Worker.

## What changed
- `wrangler.jsonc`: `ALLOWED_ORIGINS` now lists the two production web addresses next to localhost.
- `providers.ts`: models updated to `gemini-3.1-flash-lite` and `openai/gpt-oss-120b`. The old defaults (`gemini-2.5-flash`, `llama-3.3-70b-versatile`) are retired, so every chat ended in `provider_error`.
- `tools.ts`: the NASA MCP client asked `fetch` for `redirect: "error"`, which Cloudflare Workers does not implement; every request logged `mcp_unavailable` with `TypeError: Invalid redirect value`. The transport now uses a fetch with `redirect: "manual"` (redirects are returned, never followed).

## Checks
- Gateway lint, format, types, 68 tests and build pass.
- Deployed Worker (already live): chat streams an answer; a question about weather made the assistant call the NASA POWER tool (`power_get_point_statistics`) and answer from its output; no `mcp_unavailable` in the production log afterwards.

## Known issues, not fixed here
- The small model often returns an invalid `render_answer` surface; the gateway then falls back to plain text.
- The CMR MCP server timed out at initialization (8 s) when tried from Node; not re-checked from the Worker.

hits.title: Science API: climate projection factors endpoint (/v1/projection) with shared HTTP and cache layer

hits.body:
## What and why

Adds `GET /v1/projection?lat=&lon=&ssp=`: monthly 2041-2060 vs 1995-2014 climate change factors (additive for temperature/humidity, multiplicative-capped for precip/wind/srad), per SSP, with ensemble median and per-model min/max spread. Establishes the shared async HTTP client (timeouts, retries with backoff, descriptive User-Agent) and content-addressed file cache that later science-api endpoints will reuse.

## Design note: baseline source

POWER Projection only serves 2015-2100, so it cannot supply the 1995-2014 historical baseline the issue calls for. Reading the NEX-GDDP-CMIP6 S3 archive per request is also infeasible (~245 MB per model/variable/year, ~5 min for a single point/year in testing). Instead, a precomputed per-0.25°-cell baseline table (`data/baselines/projection/{lat}_{lon}.json`) is read at request time; building that table is the hero-field precompute pipeline's job (#17). Until a cell's baseline exists, the endpoint returns a 502 gap body rather than fabricated numbers, consistent with the "every number carries provenance" constraint. POWER supplies the live future-period data and per-model spread; when POWER has no data for a point (the documented Sétif -999 gap), the endpoint falls back to a future climatology stored in the same baseline record.

## What's included

- `core/factors.py`: change-factor math (additive/multiplicative with cap) and ensemble spread.
- `clients/http.py`: shared `httpx.AsyncClient` wrapper with retry/backoff and a descriptive User-Agent.
- `clients/power_projection.py`: POWER Projection API client, fetches all models concurrently, folds daily-keyed monthly series into monthly means, skips fill values (-999).
- `clients/baseline.py`: precomputed-baseline record store, snaps lat/lon to the 0.25° cell.
- `cache/files.py`: content-addressed JSON file cache.
- `core/errors.py`: `UpstreamError` → HTTP 502 with a `{gaps: [...]}` body.
- `api/projection.py`: the endpoint, wired into `main.py`'s lifespan.
- `schemas/projection.schema.json`: generated from the Pydantic response model.
- `fixtures/power/`: two real captured POWER Projection responses (Akron, full data; Sétif, all fill values) used by the client and integration tests.

## Checks run

- `uv run ruff check . && uv run ruff format --check .` — clean
- `uv run mypy` — strict, no issues
- `uv run pytest` — 40 passed, 99% coverage (gate: 90%)
- `uv build --wheel` — builds
- Repo-wide `pnpm check` could not run: the local pnpm version-manager (pinned to 12.16.1) is broken on this machine, unrelated to this change. CI should confirm the web/turbo side.

Closes #12

Stage 1 of the assistant upgrade: the assistant answers in the user's language, and its generated screens stop failing validation.

## What changed
- **Language mirroring.** `detectLanguage` (`packages/ui-kit/catalog/language.ts`) tells English, French, and Darija in Arabic script or Latin letters (arabizi) apart. The gateway adds one language line to the system prompt per request (`policy.ts` rule 4 replaced; `chat.ts` passes the language of the last user message).
- **Grounding in every digit style.** `normalizeDigits` reads Arabic-Indic digits, `٫` and `٪`, the French decimal comma, (narrow) no-break and plain-space thousands, and a space before `%`. Before, a number written that way was not seen at all and passed unchecked. Negative tests: an invented number in each style still fails.
- **Fallback text in French and Arabic.** Predefined fallback captions and the offline templates (answers, example questions, layer names, errors) exist in `apps/web/src/copy/assistant-locales/{fr,ar}.json`, chosen from the language of the question; offline intent matching has French and Arabic keyword rules. Arabic text is used for Darija in either script. Text and captions render with `dir="auto"`.
- **Simple `render_answer`.** The model can call it with just `{intent, caption}` (plus `year`, `rotation`, `layer` or `kind`); the gateway and the browser build the predefined layout with the same `fallbackSurface`, so it is always valid. Free-form A2UI `messages` still work. Hints for a failed call show the simple form. Contract: `schemas/assistant-tools.schema.json` `RenderInput` (types regenerated, one fixture example added).
- Docs amended: PRD FR-11 and FR-15, `docs/TECHNICAL_ARCHITECTURE.md` §10.4, `AGENTS.md`.

## Checks
`pnpm check` and `pnpm build` pass. Makes the generated answers talk back to the assistant: the model suggests follow-up questions as chips, and tapping one sends it as the user's next message. No new model call and no new service, so no extra cost: a tap costs the same one request as typing the question.

## What changed
- **`ask` chip action** (`packages/ui-kit/catalog/actions.ts`): a new allow-listed action whose context is one plain-text question (3 to 120 characters). It changes nothing by itself; the browser sends the text as the user's next message. Text rules are unchanged: markup, links and control characters are rejected.
- **Follow-up chips in `render_answer`**: the simple call (`{intent, caption}`) takes up to 3 `chips` of `{label, question}`; the prompt asks for 2 or 3 in the user's language. The predefined layouts place them after the data component and before the sources (`fallbackSurface` option `chips`). Contract updated (`schemas/assistant-tools.schema.json`, types regenerated).
- **Browser** (`AssistantRoot.tsx`, `surface.ts`): a tapped chip is sent like a typed question and ignored while an answer is still coming, as the input box is. Malformed chips are skipped.
- **Offline help**: the first four example questions are now chips to tap (they were plain bullet text); the rest stay listed.
- **Retry**: an error message gets a "Try again" button that asks the last question again.
- Fixed while testing: `fallbackSurface` could change a shared list for the `general` and `define_term` layouts, which would have piled up duplicate chips across calls. Covered by a regression test.

## Checks
`pnpm check` and `pnpm build` pass. New tests: the `ask` action (valid and invalid contexts, plain-text rule), chip placement for all ten intents, at most four chips, no leakage between calls, gateway tool with chips (accepted, unsafe question rejected, more than four refused), browser surface builder, offline help chips.

## Not done / to know
- Not tried with the real models yet: whether Gemini writes good follow-up chips, especially in Darija, is unchecked.
- Order of deploy: web release first, then `wrangler deploy` for the Worker (an old web build would drop the chips).
- Tapping a chart or table inside an answer to ask about it (for example a season bar) is not in this PR.

## Plan
- `packages/ui-kit/catalog/react/`: an `@a2ui/react` renderer wired to a custom `app-catalog/v1` registry mapping every catalog component to ui-kit/app components; client-side validation before render, predefined fallback layout on failure.
- `apps/web/src/assistant/`: chat panel (`@ai-sdk/react`'s `useChat` against the gateway's stream), browser-executed client tools (`get_field_summary`, `compare_rotations`, `run_backtest`, `get_season`, `explain_exclusion`, `define_term`, `navigate`), `set_priorities`/`set_constraints` only through a rendered `ConfirmForm` applied on Confirm, `ActionChips` that run real tools and patch the surface's data model, `SourceChips`/`TraceDrawer`, and "Ask about this" wired on evidence cards and the selected season.
- Mounted as a global panel in `RootLayout`, lazy-loaded so it doesn't inflate the initial bundle.

## Checks
- `pnpm check` (27 tasks) and `pnpm build` pass. Initial JS is 163.5 KB gz (+3.8 KB over dev, budget is 300 KB); the assistant itself is a separate 152.6 KB gz chunk loaded on first open.
- Verified in headless Chrome against a scripted mock gateway (the real `createGateway` handler with a fake model): a scripted question gets >=1 tool call and >=2 catalog components; "Try barley instead" updates the surface in 11-22 ms on a 3-season fixture; priorities/constraints stay unchanged until Confirm and apply after it; an invalid surface falls back to the predefined layout and an unknown chip action is dropped; a navigation chip closes the panel and routes; keyboard-only open/focus-return/reopen-keeps-conversation; gateway-down shows an error; no horizontal overflow at 375 px.
- Not verified: a real LLM/provider (Gemini/Groq) end to end, timings at full 25-season scale, and screen-reader behavior.

## Deviations
- Rotation ids (40+ chars) exceed the catalog's 32-char handle limit, so the model sees short handles (`r1`, `r2`); tools resolve them back.
- The model's own `updateDataModel` writes are ignored; the app fills the data model from tool results, so numbers never come from model text.
- Tool outputs sent to the model are compact (to stay under the gateway's 64 KB body cap); the fuller view data stays client-side.
- "Ask about this" is wired on evidence cards and the selected season only, not individual chart bars or map zones.
- `MapFocus` for a zones layer shows a placeholder note since zones (#23) don't exist yet.
- `ClimateStrip` is backed by per-season mean scores rather than the monthly anomaly fingerprint from #21.

## What and why

Adds `GET /v1/projection?lat=&lon=&ssp=`: monthly 2041-2060 vs 1995-2014 climate change factors (additive for temperature/humidity, multiplicative-capped for precip/wind/srad), per SSP, with ensemble median and per-model min/max spread. Establishes the shared async HTTP client (timeouts, retries with backoff, descriptive User-Agent) and content-addressed file cache that later science-api endpoints will reuse.

## Design note: baseline source

POWER Projection only serves 2015-2100, so it cannot supply the 1995-2014 historical baseline the issue calls for. Reading the NEX-GDDP-CMIP6 S3 archive per request is also infeasible (~245 MB per model/variable/year, ~5 min for a single point/year in testing). Instead, a precomputed per-0.25°-cell baseline table (`data/baselines/projection/{lat}_{lon}.json`) is read at request time; building that table is the hero-field precompute pipeline's job (#17). Until a cell's baseline exists, the endpoint returns a 502 gap body rather than fabricated numbers, consistent with the "every number carries provenance" constraint. POWER supplies the live future-period data and per-model spread; when POWER has no data for a point (the documented Sétif -999 gap), the endpoint falls back to a future climatology stored in the same baseline record.

## What's included

- `core/factors.py`: change-factor math (additive/multiplicative with cap) and ensemble spread.
- `clients/http.py`: shared `httpx.AsyncClient` wrapper with retry/backoff and a descriptive User-Agent.
- `clients/power_projection.py`: POWER Projection API client, fetches all models concurrently, folds daily-keyed monthly series into monthly means, skips fill values (-999).
- `clients/baseline.py`: precomputed-baseline record store, snaps lat/lon to the 0.25° cell.
- `cache/files.py`: content-addressed JSON file cache.
- `core/errors.py`: `UpstreamError` → HTTP 502 with a `{gaps: [...]}` body.
- `api/projection.py`: the endpoint, wired into `main.py`'s lifespan.
- `schemas/projection.schema.json`: generated from the Pydantic response model.
- `fixtures/power/`: two real captured POWER Projection responses (Akron, full data; Sétif, all fill values) used by the client and integration tests.

## Checks run

- `uv run ruff check . && uv run ruff format --check .` — clean
- `uv run mypy` — strict, no issues
- `uv run pytest` — 40 passed, 99% coverage (gate: 90%)
- `uv build --wheel` — builds
- Repo-wide `pnpm check` could not run: the local pnpm version-manager (pinned to 12.16.1) is broken on this machine, unrelated to this change. CI should confirm the web/turbo side.

Closes #12

Fixes the raw JSON that showed up in a reply, makes the assistant faster, and gives it a second model that works. Stacked on #154 (the base branch is that PR's branch; it retargets to `dev` when #154 merges).

## The bug
Greeting "salam, labas?" produced a normal reply followed by `{"intent": "general", "caption": ..., "chips": [...]}`. Every request offered the model every tool and told it to use `render_answer`; for a greeting no tool is needed, so the model answered in text and printed the call as text. The language was also wrong: the detector did not know Darija greetings, so the prompt said "Reply in English".

## What changed
- **Tools per step** (`chat.ts`, `prepareStep`): before any tool result exists `render_answer` is not offered (a data tool or plain text only); once results exist the only tool is `render_answer`, forced; the loop stops when an answer is accepted (`renderSettled` in `render.ts`). The prompt says never to write JSON or a tool call in a reply.
- **Safety net in the browser** (`apps/web/src/assistant/leak.ts`): a trailing answer call printed as text is hidden, also while it streams; if it is complete, valid and grounded against the turn's tool results it is drawn as the answer.
- **Language** (`language.ts`): Darija greetings and fillers (labas, hamdullah, marhba, chwiya, kolchi, لاباس, شوية ...); a new `sure` flag, and when nothing points to a language the prompt says to mirror the user instead of forcing English.
- **Speed** (`route.ts`): the NASA POWER and CMR servers are connected only when the question asks for weather or catalogue data (English, French, Arabic, Latin-letter Darija), and not again once results are back.
- **Fallback model**: one retry on 429 and 5xx, a 15 s limit for a provider to start answering, and a prompt-size test. Groq no longer rejects requests as too large.
- Docs: `docs/TECHNICAL_ARCHITECTURE.md` §10.

## Checks
`pnpm check` and `pnpm build` pass. New tests: step control (no render tool for a greeting, forced render tool after results, no MCP for a greeting, MCP for weather questions in four languages, loop stops after an accepted answer), the router table, retry, timeout and caller-cancel behaviour, the prompt size budget, `splitLeakedCall` (complete, fenced, partial, wrong shape, unrelated JSON), the Darija greetings and the unsure state.

Live, local gateway with the real Gemini and Groq keys (4 questions, 3 runs each): no JSON in any reply, replies in the user's language (a Darija greeting got a Darija reply), data questions called the browser tool, time to first byte 5 to 25 ms (was about 2.6 s) and 1 to 2 s total for a greeting (was about 6 s). One Gemini request took 40 s, which the new 15 s limit now cuts. With only the Groq key, a greeting and a data question both worked.

## Not done / to know
- Not yet shown in the real app with the new code; the waiting animation and other UX polish are a separate PR.
- The router is keyword based: a data question without a weather word will not get the NASA tools; the assistant then says so.
- Deploy order: web release first, then `wrangler deploy` for the Worker.

> **Path 3 · Science API & pipelines (Python)** · 2050 factors for the real hero fields · needs GCP access to the team project
> **Blocked by:** none (can start immediately) · **Blocks:** none

## Context
FR-14 / F-14 (Your Field in 2050), IN-08, PRD §4.2 hero fields. On every real hero field (`setif-story`, `akron-proof-1..3`) the 2050 view shows *"no precomputed baseline for the 0.25 degree cell ..."*: `/v1/projection` needs one NEX-GDDP-CMIP6 baseline record per 0.25° cell (`itza_science.clients.baseline.BaselineRecord`), and none exists. Two cells cover all hero fields: **Sétif (36.125, 5.625)** and **Akron (40.125, -103.125)**. POWER Projection returns no data at Sétif, so its record must also carry the 2041–2060 futures.

Work so far is on branch `feat/projection-baselines` (draft PR linked below):
- `pipelines/projection_baselines.py` (+ tests, 92 % pipeline coverage): reads NEX-GDDP-CMIP6 v2.0 daily files from the AWS Open Data bucket `nex-gddp-cmip6` (us-west-2, CC0), 6 POWER models × 7 variables × (1995–2014 baseline + 3 SSPs × 2041–2060), keeps only the hero cells, writes `<lat>_<lon>.json`. Full run = 3,360 files (~820 GB read once), so it runs on a short-lived GCP VM next to the bucket.
- `BaselineStore` now also reads `derived/nex-gddp-climatologies/v1/` from the dataset store (Cloud Run mount or `sync.py pull`), local `data/baselines/projection/` first.
- `pipelines/README.md` documents the run.

## State of the GCP run (project `project-f2044c65-6557-4ca2-9fd`)
- VM `itza-projection-baselines` (us-west1-b, n2-standard-8, service account `itza-data`) exists and is **stopped**; its startup script runs the pipeline, copies results to `gs://project-f2044c65-6557-4ca2-9fd-itza-data/derived/nex-gddp-climatologies/v1/`, uploads its log and shuts down.
- Inputs in `gs://project-f2044c65-6557-4ca2-9fd-itza-data/tmp/projection-run/`: `code.tgz` (branch HEAD), `startup.sh`, `run.log` (last run).
- Run 1 failed: uv picked Python 3.15 and h5py had no wheel (fixed: `--python 3.13` in `startup.sh`).
- Run 2 reached the listing and failed with `LookupError: no file for 1995` before any download: one model/experiment/variable folder has no 1995 file. The latest commit makes the error name the folder.

## Implementation requirements
- Re-run the VM (refresh `code.tgz` from the branch first), read the named failing folder in `run.log`, and fix the cause (missing variable for a model, a different ensemble member or grid label, or listing pagination). If a model truly lacks a variable, skip it with a recorded gap rather than dropping the cell; `complete()` must reflect the rule.
- After a successful run, check units: compare the Akron record's 2041 January `srad` for `cesm2`/`ssp126` with POWER Projection's `ALLSKY_SFC_SW_DWN` (≈ 133 for that month) and fix the conversion if they disagree; spot-check `tmax` and `precip` the same way.
- Register the set: download the two JSON files to `pipelines/data_store/data/derived/nex-gddp-climatologies/v1/`, run `uv run python sync.py register nex-gddp-climatologies`, commit the manifest.
- Delete the VM (`gcloud compute instances delete itza-projection-baselines --zone us-west1-b`) and `tmp/projection-run/` when done. No credentials committed.
- Verify locally: with the store pulled (or files copied to `services/science-api/data/baselines/projection/`), `GET /v1/projection?lat=36.12&lon=5.33` and `?lat=40.15&lon=-103.15` return factors, and the app's 2050 view renders for the Sétif and Akron demo fields.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Baseline records for both hero cells in the bucket, registered in `manifest.yaml` with SHA-256.
- [ ] `/v1/projection` returns factors for Sétif (archive path) and Akron (POWER path).
- [ ] The 2050 view shows resilience changes for the Sétif and Akron demo fields.
- [ ] Shortwave, temperature and rainfall factors checked against POWER Projection values.
- [ ] VM and temporary bucket files deleted.

## Branch
`feat/projection-baselines` (exists); PR targets `dev`. Use `/implement-issue 137`.

## Definition of done
- Acceptance criteria above are met and checked.
- `pnpm check` and `pnpm build` pass; backend changes include unit and integration tests (coverage gate 90%).
- Every displayed number carries provenance (source · resolution · period); gaps degrade gracefully (NFR-02, NFR-12).
- User-facing text is plain English and lives in the copy files (F-11); accessible (keyboard, contrast, labels; NFR-07).
- Matching file in `docs/` updated if behavior or a contract changed.

Sourced from pydantic-settings's releases.

v2.16.3

Highlights

This patch release fixes a security issue in the default secrets source, a regression from 2.14.2 that dropped nested secrets on Kubernetes, and a CliApp.serialize round-trip bug with CliUnknownArgs.

Security

  • SecretsSettingsSource no longer follows symlinks that resolve outside secrets_dir (#1138, fixes #1137). A secret file that is a symbolic link to a file outside secrets_dir was read into the matching field, so anyone who could place a link in secrets_dir could make the application load any file it can read. This is the plain-source counterpart of GHSA-4xgf-cpjx-pc3j, whose fix in 2.14.2 covered only NestedSecretsSettingsSource.   • A secret file that resolves outside secrets_dir is now skipped with a warning instead of being read (#1138). If you deliberately point secret files at targets elsewhere on disk, move or copy the targets into secrets_dir, or point secrets_dir at the directory that holds them.

C-3, T1 exit criterion: a resettable, keyboard-advanced scripted walkthrough of DEMO_STRATEGY.md's 3-minute live demo script, built on the real screens with fixed state applied per step so judges see live output, not a recording.

**Not a full close.** All 10 script beats are wired on real screens with fixed data (title/globe opening, Field Memory, Climate Fingerprint, Season Replay, assistant Q&A, rain-slider scenario, 2050, proof-field validation, Model Arena/zones/NISAR, close/disclaimer). The proof-field step shows #39's validation view on its labeled synthetic placeholder data without flying to a second field, since no real US Great Plains hero bundle exists yet (#17). The Arena/zones/NISAR step still calls the science API, so the script is not yet fully offline.

## Plan
- `apps/web/src/demo/`: a step engine (`useDemo` store) holding fixed field/rotation/priority/scenario values per step (documented in a constants file, not scattered inline), ten step renderers reusing the real `FieldTwin`, Field Memory, Climate Fingerprint, compare, sliders, future and arena screens, and an offline `ScriptedAnswer` component using the assistant's own template system (no LLM call) for the Q&A beat.
- `apps/web/src/routes/demo.tsx`: a standalone full-screen route (outside the normal workspace nav), keyboard advance (→/space, ←back) and a Reset that clears the field store back to initial state.
- Copy in `apps/web/src/copy/en/demo.json`.

## Checks
- `pnpm check` (28 tasks) and `pnpm build` pass.
- Verified in headless Chrome: stepped through all ten beats and Reset on a separate port (not touching another session's dev server); every screen rendered with no page errors; the assistant step's evidence card is genuinely computed (real scores, real provenance), not hardcoded; Next/Back correctly disable at the ends.
- Offline check: 8 of 10 steps touch no network. The Arena/zones/NISAR step calls the science API directly (`/v1/ml/stress`, `/v1/zones`, `/v1/nisar`) and degrades gracefully (same gap/error UI as elsewhere) when unreachable, but is not strictly offline — documented in `docs/DEMO_STRATEGY.md`.
- Not verified: actual narration-paced timing against the real <3-minute target — only confirmed no step hangs or errors.

## Deviations
- The assistant step asks the template system's guaranteed-to-match example question ("Why is the top rotation ranked first?") rather than the illustrative "why chickpea" line from the script, since that exact phrasing isn't guaranteed to match a template; there's no "Try barley instead" action chip, since the template builder doesn't generate one for any intent yet.

## What

The demo fields now hold a full daily record for 2001 to 2025, sit on real farm boundaries instead of rectangles, and show a sharp 1 m picture in 3D for the US fields. When a field opens in 3D, its outline starts as the old rectangle and morphs into the real boundary.

Refs #160 (closed early; this PR delivers its data).

## How

- **Full history** (`pipelines/refresh_history.py`): weather from POWER, rain from IMERG Final, soil moisture from SMAP L4 (from 2015-03-31), NDVI and ET from one AppEEARS point task (`pipelines/appeears.py`). It reads single pixels through NASA cloud OPeNDAP and caches every response. Ran on a GCP VM; bundles copied back here.
- **Real outlines**: Sétif and the three Akron fields are traced on real field boundaries (`hero_fields.yaml`, `apps/web/src/data/hero.ts`).
- **Coverage test** (`pipelines/tests/test_bundle_coverage.py`): all 44 field and variable pairs now meet their targets, so the known-gaps list is gone. A series that goes hollow again fails CI.
- **Soil and relief**: SSURGO and USGS NAIP/3DEP did not answer from the VM, so the Akron soil, relief picture and elevation were refreshed again from here. All three Akron fields now have SSURGO soil, NAIP at about 1 m and 3DEP at 1 m. Sétif stays on SoilGrids and EOX at 10 m.
- **3D view**:
  - The outline morphs from the bounding rectangle into the real field over 1.8 s, in both the relief view and the map twin (`twin/outlineTrace.ts`). It is skipped under reduced motion.
  - The greenness frames are cut to the field outline, so the 30 m pixels no longer spill past it.
- **Fix**: the 3D view sent the bundle's whole NDVI period (now 25 years) to `/v1/zones`, which allows at most 1,825 days, so it got a 422. Hero fields now load their precomputed `zones.json`, and other fields send the latest five years.
- **Validation**: the replay and cross-checks were regenerated. With the full history, 16 wheat seasons match the county yields instead of 15, and the Spearman correlation went from 0.59 to 0.62. Test expectations updated.
- **Fixture**: the Akron SSURGO capture was refreshed for the traced outline (AWC 185.9 to 184.5 mm/m).
- **Merge**: `dev`'s Esri detail imagery replaces my USGS map layer, since it covers every field.

## Not in this PR

The Prithvi crop maps were made for the old rectangles. They need a rerun on the new outlines (model weights needed) or should be hidden. This is still open.

## Checks

- [x] Backend tests added or updated (required for `services/`)
- [x] `pnpm check` passes locally (28 of 28 tasks)
- [x] Docs updated if behavior or contracts changed (`pipelines/README.md`)

> **Path 3 · Science API & pipelines (Python)** · 2026 data infrastructure · feeds #95 and #17 runs
> **Blocked by:** none (can start immediately) · **Blocks:** none

## Context
Real hero-field bundles (#95) and the ML and projection pipelines need data that is slow or heavy to fetch per person (SMAP L4 alone is ~144 MB per 3-hourly global granule). Each teammate currently re-downloads. We already deploy on GCP (`europe-west1`, project in the `GCP_PROJECT_ID` repo variable, `infra/README.md`). This issue creates one shared, versioned, read-only-for-the-team dataset store. **Do not download or upload anything large before the size table below is reviewed and the bucket plan is approved by the team.**

## Scope (owned paths)
`pipelines/data_store/` (new: `manifest.yaml`, `sync.py`, `README.md`), `infra/README.md` (bucket section), `docs/NASA_DATA_SOURCES.md` (link). No change to the Cloud Run services or the release workflow.

## Size estimates (CMR granule metadata, 2026-11-13)
Store **area-of-interest clips and derived products**, never global archives:

| Product | Native granule size | Global archive (do not mirror) | What we store | Est. size |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| SMAP L4 `SPL4SMGP` | ~144 MB, 8 per day | ~4–5 TB (2015→) | Daily series clipped to hero boxes (or POWER SMAP zarr extract) | < 1 GB |
| GPM IMERG Final/Late daily | ~25–31 MB per day | ~300 GB (2000→) | Hero-box clips, daily | < 1 GB |
| HLS L30/S30 VI (COG bands) | a few MB per band | very large | Field-clipped NDVI COGs, 2015–2025, hero fields | 1–5 GB |
| GRACE/GRACE-FO mascon RL06.3 | one 44 MB file | 44 MB | Full file | 0.05 GB |
| NASADEM_HGT | ~3.5 MB per 1° tile | n/a | Tiles covering hero regions | < 0.1 GB |
| NISAR L3 SME2 provisional | ~32 MB per granule | ~100k granules | Granules over hero boxes | < 2 GB |
| ECOSTRESS L2T LSTE / L4T ESI | ~13 / ~6 MB per tile scene | very large | Hero-tile scenes | 1–3 GB |
| GEDI L2A | ~700 MB per granule | very large | Footprints within 2 km of hero fields (clipped) | < 0.5 GB |
| GLDAS Noah monthly | ~24 MB per month | ~8 GB | Hero-box clips (if the GLDAS issue lands) | < 0.1 GB |
| USDA CDL (US) | national raster per year (verify size) | n/a | Colorado clips, 2008–2025 | 1–3 GB |
| NEX-GDDP-CMIP6 | ~245 MB per model/variable/year | hundreds of GB | Derived per-cell monthly climatologies (#17) | < 0.5 GB |
| Prithvi-EO-2.0 weights (#18) | model checkpoint (verify size) | n/a | One checkpoint | 1–3 GB |
| Demo bundles, frames, zones (#17) | | | Derived outputs | < 1 GB |

Target total **under 50 GB**. Update the table with measured sizes after the first sync.

## Implementation requirements
- **Bucket** (created by a GCP project admin, documented, not by CI): one regional bucket in `europe-west1`, Standard class, uniform bucket-level access, public access prevention enforced, object versioning on with a lifecycle rule deleting noncurrent versions after 30 days. Layout: `raw/<source>/<version>/...`, `derived/<pipeline>/<version>/...`, `manifests/`.
- **Access:** team members get `roles/storage.objectViewer` through a Google group; writes only by a dedicated pipeline service account and one data maintainer (`roles/storage.objectAdmin` on this bucket only). No public objects; the public app keeps serving its own static bundles.
- **Manifest** `pipelines/data_store/manifest.yaml`: per object set, source product, version, original URL or DOI, retrieval date, spatial and temporal subset, license, citation, byte size and SHA-256 per file; `sync.py verify` recomputes checksums.
- **Sync** `pipelines/data_store/sync.py`: `pull` (team, `gcloud storage rsync` from the bucket), `fetch` (maintainer, downloads from the original sources with `earthaccess`, clips, checksums, writes the manifest) and `push` (maintainer, uploads with checksums); idempotent and resumable.
- **Secrets:** Earthdata credentials from `~/.netrc` or Secret Manager only; GCP auth through the user's `gcloud auth login` or the service account via workload identity; nothing secret in the repository, the manifest or logs.
- **Costs** documented in `infra/README.md`: storage at the current regional Standard price (verify on the GCS pricing page), operations, and egress when teammates pull outside GCP; expected monthly cost for ~50 GB.
- **Updates:** re-running `fetch` for a new version writes a new version path and a new manifest entry; old versions stay until removed on purpose.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Size table reviewed and bucket plan approved before the first large transfer.
- [ ] A teammate with viewer access runs `sync.py pull` and gets hero-field data with all checksums verified.
- [ ] Every object set in the manifest has source, version, license, citation, size and SHA-256.
- [ ] No credentials or project-specific secrets committed (checked in review).
- [ ] `sync.py` unit tests cover manifest validation, checksum verification and resumable transfers (no network in CI).

- User-facing text is plain English and lives in the copy files (F-11); accessible (keyboard, contrast, labels; NFR-07).

## What and why

The 2026 Terms need an OSI license on our original content and every third-party dataset, service, library, model and literature source identified with its license. This adds the license, the register, and a gate that keeps it true.

- `LICENSE`: Apache 2.0 (NASA's default).
- `data-sources.yaml`: `license`, `citation` and `doi` on all 11 entries, appended after `coverage`; no reordering. The TS and Python manifest parsers ignore the new keys.
- `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`: NASA products with DOIs, non-NASA data and services (SoilGrids, OpenFreeMap/OSM, AWS terrain tiles, CDL), knowledge-pack literature, the stress model, fonts/icons/images, and a generated list of 319 production dependencies (JS and the three uv projects).
- `scripts/licenses.mjs`: regenerates the dependency list; `--check` fails on a non-OSI/non-public-domain license, a stale list, or a source entry without license/citation/DOI. Exceptions live in `scripts/licenses.allow.json` with a reason (only Pillow's MIT-CMU).
- `docs/CHALLENGE_RULES_2026.md` §6 points to the register.
- Flagged, not hidden: the EOX CC BY-NC-SA basemap is marked "not acceptable" in the register (replaced in #100); FAO-56, GIEWS and UNL EC137 are marked "team to confirm".

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] `LICENSE` present, OSI-approved (Apache 2.0).
- [x] Every `data-sources.yaml` entry has `license` and `citation`; NASA DAAC products carry a DOI (all DOIs resolve; `node --test scripts/licenses.test.mjs`).
- [x] `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` lists every dataset, service, library, model, font and image with license and source link.
- [x] `node scripts/licenses.mjs --check` exits non-zero on an unlisted non-OSI dependency: tested with a fixture lockfile (`scripts/fixtures/licenses-bad`).

## How it was checked

- `pnpm turbo run lint format:check typecheck`: 21/21. `pnpm schemas:check`: up to date.
- `pnpm check`: all tasks pass except two `@itza/engine` tests (`candidates`, `replay golden`) that time out at the 5 s default on this machine (Node 22, the repo needs 26); this change does not touch the engine. Please confirm in CI.

- FAO-56 / GIEWS (© FAO, generally CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO) and UNL EC137: we use transcribed values only; the team should confirm that is acceptable.

## What and why

The decisions layer of the engine (FR-06, FR-08, FR-09, FR-14): it generates candidate rotations, applies slider, preset and 2050 scenarios to the weather, builds schema-valid evidence cards with confidence, and answers "Why not X?". It unblocks #6, #26, #33, #37 and #39.

## Plan

1. `scenarios`: slider and preset scenarios applied to the bundle's weather (ET0 recomputed), robustness readout; the replay now applies the input's scenario instead of rejecting non-history ones.
2. `candidates` and `constraints`: crop-level hard filters, sequence enumeration with pest break intervals, replay pre-scoring, diversity, `explainExclusion`.
3. `confidence` and `evidence`: five weighted factors with reasons; cards with evidence provenance, benefits, gaps, risks and an input slot for Model Arena disagreements.
4. `projection`: parse the `/v1/projection` payload, build median/low/high scenarios per SSP, report score shifts with model spread.
5. Tests, benchmarks, a synthetic projection fixture, docs.

## Decisions worth a look

- **Pest break as a hard rule means the same crop's return interval**, not every host-to-host gap. With the strict reading the proof field's wheat-millet-fallow rotation is impossible under the US pack's own pest table (Fusarium needs 2 seasons between any of 4 cereal hosts). Cross-crop pressure is still scored by the pest criterion. Documented in §6.
- **The pack data narrows the Algerian candidates.** Broomrape needs 5 seasons between plantings, so lentil, faba bean, pea and vetch can never appear in a 2 to 5 season rotation, and the feasible set is mostly cereal-fallow-cover cycles. These values are team estimates marked `needs_expert_review`; an agronomist should look at `min_break_years` before field use.
- **Structural rules** (my choice, documented): a crop at most twice, fallow and cover at most once each, at least one harvested crop. Without the last, the pre-score favoured `cover-fallow` rotations that grow nothing.
- **Equipment limits:** the packs have no machinery data, so only `no_row_crop_planter` is applied (a rule on crop ids); other limits are reported as information gaps rather than silently ignored.
- **Ground truth:** observed soil values and `sowing_doy` already override derived values in the replay. Dates, yields and irrigation events enter confidence as counts (`GroundTruth`). I did not add them to the `engine-input` schema: the form in #6 defines their shape, and schema changes are cross-cutting.
- **Contract fix:** `engine-input` `scenario.ssp` allowed `ssp585` but not `ssp370`, which is what `/v1/projection` serves (additive, v1.0 unchanged, generated TS and Python regenerated).
- **Sentence templates live in the engine** (`templates.ts`), because they carry computed numbers; UI chrome copy stays in `en.json`.
- **Model-satellite agreement** uses monthly anomalies of modeled root-zone water for the current rotation against the satellite series. The "season timing" half of the agreement named in §6.4 is not implemented.

## Checks run

- `pnpm check`: 26/26 tasks; engine 276 tests, 99.3 % statements and 93.8 % branches (gate 90 %).
- `pnpm build`: passes. `generate.mjs --check`: current. science-api tests and mypy pass with the regenerated contracts.
- `pnpm --filter @itza/engine bench`: 500 candidates generated and replayed in about 0.25 s (budget 0.5 s); scenario rerun of 10 rotations with 200 draws about 0.7 s (budget 1 s); replay budgets from #4 unchanged. Apple M-series, Node 26.
- Property tests: no alternative breaks a hard constraint (independent oracle that unrolls the cycle), cards valid and contributions summing to the score for any priorities, scenario bounds.

## Not verified

- Candidate and card quality on real Sétif and Akron bundles: tests use the synthetic fixtures and a seeded 25-year generator.
- The decisions are plain functions; no worker messages for them yet. #26 defines what the compare workspace needs.
- The benchmarks are not in `pnpm test` (coverage instrumentation distorts timing) and CI does not run `bench`.

Closes #5

The assistant in the web app fell back to templates with `{"error":"budget_exhausted","fallback":"templates"}`. The cause is the gateway's own per-session cap, not the language model.

## Cause
A session was limited to 30 requests and 60,000 tokens. The browser makes two or three requests per question (it answers a tool call, then asks again), and every request carries the instructions, tool definitions and tool results, so a few questions used the whole token budget and the rest of the session got HTTP 429.

## Change
`budget.ts`: 150 requests and 400,000 tokens per session, and 40 requests per minute per IP (a shared event network would otherwise hit 20 quickly). The free-tier provider quotas remain the real ceiling; the Groq fallback still applies when Gemini is out of quota.

## Checks
Gateway lint, types and 68 tests pass (they use the limit constants). The Worker is deployed with this change; three requests in a new session return 200. Counters live in the Worker, so the redeploy also reset sessions that had already hit the cap.
