Click-to-field now runs as a background job, so a first click no longer ends in a 504 (#89). The wait itself is still minutes on a new place; this PR makes it visible and cancellable instead of failing.

## What and why
- `POST /v1/boundaries` starts a job and answers 202 at once with `{id, status, progress}`. The same click (to about 10 m) and period share one job, and a finished proposal is returned again without reading anything.
- `GET /v1/boundaries/{id}` reports `running`, `done` or `error`, progress as date windows read out of the total, and the proposal or an error with `kind` (`no-field`, `timeout`, `unavailable`). Jobs are in memory only (at most 64; 503 when all run; cut off after 30 minutes).
- The web mode polls every 3 s, shows "date windows read" progress and a Discard button. The evaluation script (#81) starts and polls jobs too.

## Plan
`boundaries.py` job model, store and the two routes; integration tests for the job flow (progress, shared jobs, restart after error, timeout, unexpected failure, full store, 404); web `api.ts` polling and `ClickToField.tsx` progress; §8.3, API table and service README updated.

## Verified on real imagery
Against the live API (Sétif, 2025-07-01 to 2026-03-27, partly cached): the start answered in 22 ms, progress reached 5 of 27 windows after about 25 s, and a repeat click returned the same job id.

## Not done

hits.body:
Add offline proof-field comparisons for seasonal IMERG–PRISM rainfall, modeled actual ET–OpenET monthly water use, and season scores–USDA NASS county winter wheat yields. All three checks now have measurements, provenance, agreement statistics and inspectable paired observations on all three proof fields.

The rain comparison uses the official NASA IMERG Final Monthly V07 product, not extrapolation from the store's sampled daily data. Monthly mean rates are converted from mm/hour using each calendar month's exact length, then summed over complete September–August seasons. The replay retains its original POWER forcing; this check compares rainfall products. The nearby fields share one IMERG cell, and IMERG and PRISM may share gauge observations.

Implementation plan:
- Capture source responses and their license/citation register in pipelines/validation/.
- Align complete agricultural seasons and months, compute bias/RMSE and tie-aware rank/direction statistics offline.
- Display every check for every proof field with source periods, coverage and limitations.
- Verify conversions, input rejection, source-to-report integrity and offline rendering; run full repository checks and build.

Measured results:
- Rain: 213 IMERG monthly observations (2008-01 through 2025-09), giving 17 paired seasons per field (2009–2025). Spearman 0.838 / 0.814 / 0.850; bias +32.9 / +17.6 / +20.0 mm/season; RMSE 61.7 / 57.4 / 51.5 mm/season (IMERG minus PRISM). The three unavailable end-of-2025 months remain null.
- OpenET: 204 paired months per field. Spearman 0.685 / 0.771 / 0.785; bias -3.0 / -5.7 / -2.9 mm/month; RMSE 27.3 / 22.1 / 20.3 mm/month.
- Quick Stats: 15 paired years per field. Spearman 0.597 / 0.592 / 0.592; adjacent-year direction agreement 7 of 12 changes on each field. Explicitly directional context, never a yield forecast; scores use a fixed continuous-wheat counterfactual, default soil, equal priorities and no irrigation.

Review fixes:
- Preserve validated OpenET observations when a refresh has no credentials, including their original retrieval date.
- Include validation lint, strict types and tests in the existing CI pipeline job.
- Fail CI when the shipped artifact differs from its sources and builder; check raw subset hashes, coordinates, unit conversion, leap years, missing months, ties and missing years.
- Update source registration, copy and documentation to match the measured results.

Validation:
- `pnpm check` and `pnpm build` pass; pre-existing lint/chunk warnings remain.
- 79 offline pipeline tests pass with 92.31% coverage in the existing gated modules; 23 of these tests cover validation.
- Pipeline Ruff and strict mypy pass; the artifact freshness check passes.
- Server-side rendering verifies all nine measured comparison cards, observation tables, provenance and forecast caveats without live source access.
- Visual browser review remains unverified: browser host unavailable; native Chrome access was rejected by automatic approval with no further reason.

All scientific acceptance criteria for #105 are now met. Review recommendation: merge after the user confirms the final head's CI is green.

## What and why

Season Replay (FR-07 / F-07) for the engine: each rotation is replayed through every usable historical season on the FAO-56 physics from #3, scored on eight criteria with priority weights, summarized as a resilience profile, and wrapped in seeded Monte Carlo bands. A Web Worker exposes `runReplay` and a weights-only `rescore`. This unblocks #5 and, through it, the compare workspace (#26) and the Model Arena (#38).

## Plan

1. `replay/`: soil health, pests, erosion, simulate (rotation x season loop), score, resilience, montecarlo, run (`simulateReplay` / `scoreReplay`).
2. `worker/`: `postMessage` protocol, pure handler, promise client, worker entry; inputs and outputs validated against `engine-input` / `engine-output`.
3. `physics/`: behavior-preserving speed-up so the 1 s budget is reachable (see below).
4. Tests: golden snapshots, property tests (fast-check), worker tests; budgets in a separate `bench` target.
5. Docs: `TECHNICAL_ARCHITECTURE.md` §6 layout and implementation notes, engine README.

## Decisions worth a look

- **Rotation laid over history:** season n uses position n mod N, so a rotation repeats through the record. The baseline is replayed too and appears in the results if it is not already one of the rotations.
- **Only the `history` scenario** is replayed here. Slider and 2050 scenarios change the forcing first (`scenarios.ts`, #5); until then they are rejected with a clear error rather than silently replayed as history. Constraints are applied by the candidate generator (#5); the replay is rainfed.
- **Pest window:** each earlier host within W = max(persistence, minimum break) adds (W - gap + 1)/W. The strict form in §6.2 (gap < persistence) ignores a cereal after a cereal when persistence is 1 year, which is exactly the case the packs describe. Documented in §6.
- **Lower median:** a rotation's score and `resilience.median` are the composite of its lower-median season, so the reported contributions sum to the score exactly (needed by the evidence cards in #26).
- **Criteria are weight-independent**, which is what makes `rescore` (about 15 ms for 10 rotations) possible without re-simulating.
- **Knowledge-pack values** that drive these scores are still team estimates marked `needs_expert_review`; the replay inherits that.

## Physics changes (same workstream as #3, outside the paths this issue lists)

`10 rotations x 25 seasons x 200 draws` is 2,010 timelines of 9,131 days and was 1.7 s, almost all in the daily water balance. To reach the 1 s budget I changed `physics/crops.ts` and `physics/waterBalance.ts` without changing results (all 83 existing physics and climate tests pass unchanged, and the golden replays were generated after, then re-checked after each step): allocation-free stage lookups, `stepInPlace` on a flat array (`stepWaterBalance` now wraps it), shared per-crop daily curves, an exact shortcut for a dry bare day on a dry topsoil, a `daily: false` option on `simulateTimeline`, and plain comparisons instead of `Math.min/max` in the hot loop. New tests cover the fast paths against the general path.

## Checks run

- `pnpm check`: 26/26 tasks, including 180 engine tests, 99.6 % statements and 94.5 % branches (gate 90 %), Biome, `tsc`, and the contracts check.
- `pnpm build`: passes.
- `pnpm --filter @itza/engine bench`: replay 10 x 25 x 200 about 0.7 s (budget 1 s), re-score about 15 ms (budget 100 ms) on an Apple M-series laptop, Node 26.
- Worker API typechecks from `apps/web` (DOM `Worker` into `createReplayClient`, `?worker` import) and Vite bundles the entry as its own chunk (checked with a temporary import, reverted).

## Not verified

- The timing budgets are not part of `pnpm test`: V8 coverage instrumentation slows the replay about nine times, so they run in `bench`. CI does not run `bench`; adding it is a pipeline change I left to you. Margin on this machine is about 30 %, so a slower CI runner should be tried before gating on it.
- Replay quality on real Sétif and Akron bundles: the tests use the two synthetic bundles and a seeded synthetic 25-year generator.
- Replay view and cards (#26) are not built; this PR is the engine side only.

Closes #4

> **Path 3 · Science API & pipelines (Python)** · relief package for the 3D Field Twin
> **Blocked by:** none (can start immediately) · **Blocks:** the web relief view issue

## Context
F-12 (3D Field Twin). Measured on the deployed `/twin` (Akron field 1, 2026-11-14): about 250 tile requests to three third-party hosts, last elevation tile at 10.5 s, and a mesh too coarse to show one field (bundle terrain rasters are 30×30 px at 30 m). The fix is one small per-field "relief package" served from our own origin.

Checked the same day:
- USGS 3DEP `3DEPElevation/ImageServer/exportImage` returns a float32 GeoTIFF on a lon/lat grid for the Akron fields (570×567 px, 1390 to 1409 m, 21 s per call, so it must be cached).
- Outside the US the same call returns HTTP 200 with every value 0.0: treat a constant raster as no coverage.
- USDA NAIP `USGSNAIPPlus/ImageServer/exportImage` returns a sharp aerial JPEG for the same box.
- `tiles.maps.eox.at/wms` is 404; non-US imagery must be a mosaic of the EOX 2016 WMTS tiles already licensed in `docs/NASA_DATA_SOURCES.md`.

## Implementation requirements
- `terrain/models.py`: `Relief` model (`heightmap`, `imagery`, `width`, `height` ≤ 1024, `bounds` WGS84, `size_m`, `min_elevation_m`, `max_elevation_m`, `elevation_source`, `imagery_source`) and optional `TerrainIndex.relief`.
- `terrain/relief.py`: `ReliefGrid.for_field(geometry, buffer_m=150, max_side=1024)` (raster linear in lon/lat, row 0 north, cells about 1 m and square on the ground, longer side capped) and `encode_heights` (8-bit RGB PNG, `v = round((z-min)/(max-min)*65535)`, `R = v >> 8`, `G = v & 255`; NaN holes filled from the nearest valid cell; flat and all-NaN cases handled).
- `terrain/relief_sources.py`: `UsgsReliefSource` (3DEP elevation, NAIP imagery, 90 s timeout, no-coverage detection, any HTTP error → no coverage), `EoxImagerySource` (zoom-15 WMTS mosaic, at most 16 tiles), `build_relief` (3DEP → NASADEM resampled with `coarse=True`; NAIP → EOX; each fallback recorded as an info gap).
- `SpatialService`: builds, caches and lists the relief package with the terrain index; a relief failure never fails the terrain request (`relief = null` plus a warning gap). Size caps: heightmap ≤ 1.5 MB, imagery ≤ 400 KB.
- `pipelines/build_demo.py`: copy relief assets into each hero bundle; rebuild the four hero bundles.
- Docs: `services/science-api/README.md`, `docs/NASA_DATA_SOURCES.md` (3DEP and NAIP rows, public-domain note), `docs/TECHNICAL_ARCHITECTURE.md` §9.
- Tests never call the network: small captured rasters in `fixtures/relief/`, `httpx.MockTransport`.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `GET /v1/bundles/{id}/terrain` and each hero `terrain.json` carry `relief`; the heightmap and imagery hrefs resolve.
- [ ] The three Akron bundles use 3DEP and NAIP; Sétif falls back to NASADEM and EOX with `coarse: true`.
- [ ] A constant-zero 3DEP response, a timeout and a JSON error body each produce the fallback, not a flat mesh or a 500.
- [ ] Existing terrain tests pass unchanged when no relief source is configured.

## Branch
`feat/<n>-relief-package`; PR targets `dev`.

## Definition of done
- Acceptance criteria above are met and checked.
- `pnpm check` and `pnpm build` pass; backend changes include unit and integration tests (coverage gate 90%).
- Every displayed number carries provenance (source · resolution · period); gaps degrade gracefully (NFR-02, NFR-12).
- Matching file in `docs/` updated if behavior or a contract changed.

Makes the generated answers talk back to the assistant: the model suggests follow-up questions as chips, and tapping one sends it as the user's next message. No new model call and no new service, so no extra cost: a tap costs the same one request as typing the question.

## What changed
- **`ask` chip action** (`packages/ui-kit/catalog/actions.ts`): a new allow-listed action whose context is one plain-text question (3 to 120 characters). It changes nothing by itself; the browser sends the text as the user's next message. Text rules are unchanged: markup, links and control characters are rejected.
- **Follow-up chips in `render_answer`**: the simple call (`{intent, caption}`) takes up to 3 `chips` of `{label, question}`; the prompt asks for 2 or 3 in the user's language. The predefined layouts place them after the data component and before the sources (`fallbackSurface` option `chips`). Contract updated (`schemas/assistant-tools.schema.json`, types regenerated).
- **Browser** (`AssistantRoot.tsx`, `surface.ts`): a tapped chip is sent like a typed question and ignored while an answer is still coming, as the input box is. Malformed chips are skipped.
- **Offline help**: the first four example questions are now chips to tap (they were plain bullet text); the rest stay listed.
- **Retry**: an error message gets a "Try again" button that asks the last question again.
- Fixed while testing: `fallbackSurface` could change a shared list for the `general` and `define_term` layouts, which would have piled up duplicate chips across calls. Covered by a regression test.

## Checks
`pnpm check` and `pnpm build` pass. New tests: the `ask` action (valid and invalid contexts, plain-text rule), chip placement for all ten intents, at most four chips, no leakage between calls, gateway tool with chips (accepted, unsafe question rejected, more than four refused), browser surface builder, offline help chips.

## Not done / to know
- Not tried with the real models yet: whether Gemini writes good follow-up chips, especially in Darija, is unchecked.
- Order of deploy: web release first, then `wrangler deploy` for the Worker (an old web build would drop the chips).
- Tapping a chart or table inside an answer to ask about it (for example a season bar) is not in this PR.

Fixes the raw JSON that showed up in a reply, makes the assistant faster, and gives it a second model that works. Stacked on #154 (the base branch is that PR's branch; it retargets to `dev` when #154 merges).

## The bug
Greeting "salam, labas?" produced a normal reply followed by `{"intent": "general", "caption": ..., "chips": [...]}`. Every request offered the model every tool and told it to use `render_answer`; for a greeting no tool is needed, so the model answered in text and printed the call as text. The language was also wrong: the detector did not know Darija greetings, so the prompt said "Reply in English".

## What changed
- **Tools per step** (`chat.ts`, `prepareStep`): before any tool result exists `render_answer` is not offered (a data tool or plain text only); once results exist the only tool is `render_answer`, forced; the loop stops when an answer is accepted (`renderSettled` in `render.ts`). The prompt says never to write JSON or a tool call in a reply.
- **Safety net in the browser** (`apps/web/src/assistant/leak.ts`): a trailing answer call printed as text is hidden, also while it streams; if it is complete, valid and grounded against the turn's tool results it is drawn as the answer.
- **Language** (`language.ts`): Darija greetings and fillers (labas, hamdullah, marhba, chwiya, kolchi, لاباس, شوية ...); a new `sure` flag, and when nothing points to a language the prompt says to mirror the user instead of forcing English.
- **Speed** (`route.ts`): the NASA POWER and CMR servers are connected only when the question asks for weather or catalogue data (English, French, Arabic, Latin-letter Darija), and not again once results are back.
- **Fallback model**: one retry on 429 and 5xx, a 15 s limit for a provider to start answering, and a prompt-size test. Groq no longer rejects requests as too large.
- Docs: `docs/TECHNICAL_ARCHITECTURE.md` §10.

## Checks
`pnpm check` and `pnpm build` pass. New tests: step control (no render tool for a greeting, forced render tool after results, no MCP for a greeting, MCP for weather questions in four languages, loop stops after an accepted answer), the router table, retry, timeout and caller-cancel behaviour, the prompt size budget, `splitLeakedCall` (complete, fenced, partial, wrong shape, unrelated JSON), the Darija greetings and the unsure state.

Live, local gateway with the real Gemini and Groq keys (4 questions, 3 runs each): no JSON in any reply, replies in the user's language (a Darija greeting got a Darija reply), data questions called the browser tool, time to first byte 5 to 25 ms (was about 2.6 s) and 1 to 2 s total for a greeting (was about 6 s). One Gemini request took 40 s, which the new 15 s limit now cuts. With only the Groq key, a greeting and a data question both worked.

## Not done / to know
- Not yet shown in the real app with the new code; the waiting animation and other UX polish are a separate PR.
- The router is keyword based: a data question without a weather word will not get the NASA tools; the assistant then says so.
- Deploy order: web release first, then `wrangler deploy` for the Worker.

Stage 1 of the assistant upgrade: the assistant answers in the user's language, and its generated screens stop failing validation.

## What changed
- **Language mirroring.** `detectLanguage` (`packages/ui-kit/catalog/language.ts`) tells English, French, and Darija in Arabic script or Latin letters (arabizi) apart. The gateway adds one language line to the system prompt per request (`policy.ts` rule 4 replaced; `chat.ts` passes the language of the last user message).
- **Grounding in every digit style.** `normalizeDigits` reads Arabic-Indic digits, `٫` and `٪`, the French decimal comma, (narrow) no-break and plain-space thousands, and a space before `%`. Before, a number written that way was not seen at all and passed unchecked. Negative tests: an invented number in each style still fails.
- **Fallback text in French and Arabic.** Predefined fallback captions and the offline templates (answers, example questions, layer names, errors) exist in `apps/web/src/copy/assistant-locales/{fr,ar}.json`, chosen from the language of the question; offline intent matching has French and Arabic keyword rules. Arabic text is used for Darija in either script. Text and captions render with `dir="auto"`.
- **Simple `render_answer`.** The model can call it with just `{intent, caption}` (plus `year`, `rotation`, `layer` or `kind`); the gateway and the browser build the predefined layout with the same `fallbackSurface`, so it is always valid. Free-form A2UI `messages` still work. Hints for a failed call show the simple form. Contract: `schemas/assistant-tools.schema.json` `RenderInput` (types regenerated, one fixture example added).
- Docs amended: PRD FR-11 and FR-15, `docs/TECHNICAL_ARCHITECTURE.md` §10.4, `AGENTS.md`.

## Checks
`pnpm check` and `pnpm build` pass. New tests: language detection table, grounding in each digit style, gateway prompt per language and language switch mid-conversation, simple `render_answer` for all ten intents, scripted eval cases in French and Arabic number styles, French and Arabic offline answers and keyword matching, `surfaceFromInput`.

## Not done / to know
- Only checked with scripted models so far: no live check of Darija quality yet. After merging, release the web app first, then deploy the Worker (`wrangler deploy` in `services/si-gateway`): an old web build shows the English fallback caption for the new simple call.
- `compose_answer` was folded into `render_answer` rather than added as a second tool. Chips and new catalog components are not in this PR.
- The assistant's replies may now be in French or Arabic when the user writes in them; the challenge rules (E5) ask for English on the project page and linked material, so the demo and the written submission should keep to English questions.
- Memory, vector search and the agent loop are Stage 2 and not part of this PR.

The assistant chat, made minimal and single-language, on top of the thinking steps and the scroll that follows them. Stacked on #156 (retargets when that merges); `dev` is merged in, including the space-glass redesign.

## What changed
- **Removed:** Pin and Add to card, the Pinned tab (and with it the tab bar), the assistant avatar, the sources row and "How I got this" drawer, and the folded "Worked for 6 s in 3 steps" summary. The printed rotation card no longer has a pinned-answers section; `report/pinnedStore.ts` is gone. Send, stop, reset, the jump arrow and the step marks stay.
- **One language per answer:** the prompt names the language and forbids mixing; `render_answer` checks the caption and every chip with the language detector and answers `LANGUAGE_MISMATCH` (one retry, then the predefined layout, written in the user's language); when an answer card is shown, the model's own text is no longer shown next to it.
- **Look:** an inline thinking row without a box (orbit dot, current step, finished steps as quiet lines), relaxed text spacing, a quieter disclaimer; answers are the caption, one data component and follow-up chips. Reuses `glass-control`, `IconButton`, `Skeleton`, `cn`, `focusRing`.
- Two bugs the live run exposed and this PR fixes: English text was read as French because "rotation" is in the French word list (and French now needs more French than English words), and the 3 in a Latin-letter Darija word like `3ando` was read as a number by the grounding check (a single digit 2, 3, 5, 7, 8 or 9 glued to two letters is a word; `5mm` and `12ha` are still numbers).
- Docs: `docs/FEATURES.md` F-15, `docs/TECHNICAL_ARCHITECTURE.md` §10.

## Checks
`pnpm check` and `pnpm build` pass. New tests: no sources footer in any layout, `withoutSources` for model-written surfaces, the language names and `matchesLanguage` (match, mismatch, ambiguous, script), `LANGUAGE_MISMATCH` on the caption, chips and model-written surfaces, the two bug fixes above.

Live, local gateway with the real Gemini, six questions (English, French, Darija in Arabic script, Darija in Latin letters, two greetings): each reply came back in one language, caption and chips together, and every data answer was accepted on the first try.

## To know
- **Provenance:** answers no longer show their sources (NFR-02 and the challenge rules value sources); they stay on the Sources page and in the other views. The catalog still has the two components, so bringing the row back is a one-line change in `fallback.ts`.
- The fixed labels inside answer cards (for example column names) are still English, as agreed.
- The language check is a heuristic; a false mismatch costs the one retry and then the predefined layout.
- Not seen in a real browser yet.

7.0.173

Patch Changes

  • 3c09e00: Prevent in-place schema validation or input refinement from changing approved tool arguments during approval replay.

  • f43ee39: fix(workflow): log the default step limit warning when WorkflowAgent.generate() stops at the default limit.

  • 7ce7ffc: fix(workflow): log provider warnings in WorkflowAgent

    WorkflowAgent.generate() and WorkflowAgent.stream() now log the warnings of every model call through the AI SDK warning logger, like ToolLoopAgent. The AI_SDK_LOG_WARNINGS global controls the output.

  • f6809e3: fix(workflow): align the prepareStep results of WorkflowAgent with ToolLoopAgent. Returned instructions (or the deprecated system) replace the instructions of the step and carry forward to later steps, returned providerOptions are merged with the agent options, and returned headers are merged over the headers of the call.

  • 2559173: feat(workflow): support toolApproval in WorkflowAgent

    WorkflowAgent accepts a toolApproval configuration in the constructor and per generate() or stream() call. The configuration takes precedence over a tool's needsApproval setting, and its functions run in workflow context, outside of the durable model steps. Calls that the configuration approves run in the same step, and calls that it denies receive an execution-denied tool result without pausing the workflow.

  • f1de9cb: feat(workflow): support the timeout object in WorkflowAgent

    generate() and stream() accept timeout: { totalMs, stepMs, firstChunkMs, chunkMs } in addition to a number. stepMs limits each model call. In stream(), firstChunkMs and chunkMs limit the wait for model output. Invalid timeout values are rejected with an InvalidArgumentError. A timeout now also ends a model step when the provider stream ignores the abort signal.

7.0.172

Each part is now validated against the schemas for its type only, validation stops at the first invalid message or part, and an invalid JSON value in provider or tool metadata is reported as a single issue.

Add a fetch option to createDownload so core downloads can also use guarded-fetch for opt-in DNS validation on Node.js. hits.body: ## Summary Implements **DIDI-377 (Pass 3c-1)**: operator-confirmed write-back proposals against completed council messages, with refinement via feedback — no GitHub or Linear side effects. Also fixes intermittent integration-test hangs caused by orphaned websocket pipeline tasks leaving idle-in-transaction DB connections. ### Persistence - Migration `004`: nullable `chat_messages.council_decision` JSONB (populated when `response_kind == council_result`) - New `write_back_proposals` table with one proposal per council message, feedback history, and status lifecycle - Migration `005`: `write_back_proposals.project_id` copied from source message for proper scoping ### Classification - `WriteBackPlan` schema with doc/roadmap flags - Planner reuses `supervisor_model` with structured output - `existing_doc_path` chosen deterministically from citation frequency across `persona_opinions[].citations` — the LLM never generates file paths ### API (both gated by `can_access()`) 1. `POST /chat/messages/{message_id}/write-back` — create proposal, classify, return plan (`409` if one already exists) 2. `PATCH /write-back-proposals/{id}` — fold in operator feedback, re-classify, update same row ### WebSocket pipeline cleanup - Per-message `try/finally` cancels and awaits `pipeline_task` when incomplete - Handler-level cleanup on `WebSocketDisconnect`, `CancelledError`, and generic exceptions - Pipeline DB session invalidated on cancellation to prevent asyncpg savepoint leaks ### Documentation - hits.body: ## Summary **PR 3 of 3** for DIDI-453. Stacks on #22 (uv lockfile). Merge after PR 1 and PR 2. Lifts the SQLAlchemy `<2.1` cap; `uv.lock` now pins **2.1.1**. ## Root cause (SQLAlchemy 2.1) The WebSocket pipeline held one `AsyncSession` for the entire `process_message` call. After inserting the user message, `_persist_message` ran `commit()` then `refresh()`, which started a **new implicit transaction** (a `SELECT` for the row). While `run_council` blocked on LLM/graph work, that transaction stayed **idle in transaction**. When the client disconnected, the pipeline task was cancelled and awaited, but under 2.1 the connection was not reliably returned to the pool until the session was explicitly rolled back—so `pg_stat_activity` still showed a leaked backend. `run_council` did not use the pipeline session at all (persona nodes open their own sessions); the leak was from holding a checked-out session (and/or an implicit transaction from `refresh`) across the council await. ## Fix - `process_message` uses **short-lived sessions** for user and assistant persists; council runs with **no** pipeline session checked out. - `route_message` opens a DB session only for retrieval paths (not strategic council). - WebSocket pipeline no longer wraps `process_message` in a long-lived session. - Skip `refresh` on user-message persist; roll back fixture sessions before `pg_stat_activity` checks. - Set Postgres `application_name` from settings; disconnect integration tests filter on it. - ADR 0002 changelog entry for session hygiene. ## Tests - Existing disconnect integration test (scoped `application_name`). - New `test_pipeline_task_cancelled_mid_council_releases_db_connection`. ## Test plan - [ ] Full CI green on SQLAlchemy 2.1.1 with no `SAWarning` for non-checked-in connections - [ ] `uv lock --check` passes Linear Issue: [DIDI-453](https://linear.app/didi-build/issue/DIDI-453/ci-fix-pin-sqlalchemy-21-add-uv-lockfile-fix-websocket-disconnect)

hits.body: ## Summary Lifts the SQLAlchemy `<2.1` cap (lockfile pins **2.1.1**) and fixes WebSocket disconnect / chat-path connection leaks on SQLAlchemy 2.1. ## Investigation (leaked connection) ### What CI showed before this commit - SQL echo after the user-message path: `INSERT INTO chat_messages …` + `COMMIT`, then **no further ORM SQL** while council was mocked/hung. - `pg_stat_activity` still reported **one** `domain-pytest` backend in `idle in transaction`. - So the leak was a **checked-out pool connection** not visible as ongoing ORM work—not an open transaction during council itself. ### Diagnostics added (disconnect tests) 1. On failure, `_wait_for_no_idle_transactions` now prints per-backend: **pid, application_name, backend_start, xact_start, state_change, query** (last statement on that connection). 2. Disconnect module enables **`sqlalchemy.pool` DEBUG** and sets `DATABASE_ECHO_POOL=1` before first engine use (lazy engine factory) so CI logs show checkouts/checkins. 3. `list_database_session_sources()` documents every session entry point. ### Engine / session inventory | Source | Kind | `application_name` | Notes | |--------|------|-------------------|--------| | `get_engine()` | Single `AsyncEngine` (lru_cache) | `database_application_name` | All asyncpg connections; `pool_reset_on_return=rollback` | | `get_async_session_factory()` | `async_sessionmaker` | same | Used everywhere | | `get_db` | FastAPI dependency | same | HTTP routes; **rollback in `finally`** (fixes write-back `SAWarning`) | | `managed_session()` | context manager | same | Auth, lifespan bootstrap, chat persists, retrieval, persona nodes | | `persona_node` | `managed_session` | same | Own short session per persona (not used when `run_council` is mocked) | | LangGraph checkpointer | **none** | n/a | No SQLAlchemy checkpointer in this repo | ### Root cause (confirmed mechanism) 1. **Short read-only sessions** (`validate_api_key` on WebSocket connect, `AuthMiddleware`, lifespan `ensure_bootstrap_api_key`) ran `SELECT` and could leave the backend **`idle in transaction`** if the session exited without an explicit rollback under 2.1. 2. **`get_db`** yielded a session without a `finally` rollback, so HTTP follow-ups (e.g. write-back in `test_chat_writeback_live_id`) could garbage-collect a **non-checked-in** connection (`SAWarning`). 3. Chat persists used **manual `commit()`** on a session that stayed open across later awaits; combined with pool check-in behavior on 2.1, the user-message connection could remain **`idle in transaction`** with `query` still showing the `INSERT INTO chat_messages`. The earlier `refresh=False` change helped but did not guarantee check-in because other session scopes and `get_db` still leaked. ## Fix - **Lazy** `get_engine()` / session factory so tests can enable `DATABASE_ECHO_POOL` before first use. - **`managed_session()`**: always `rollback()` open transactions in `finally`. - **Chat persists**: `async with session.begin()` + `flush` (no cross-await session). - **`process_message`**: no long-lived session; council runs with **no** pipeline DB session checked out. - **`get_db`**: rollback in `finally`. - **Status sentinel** on cancel: `put_nowait` if `put` is cancelled. - Disconnect tests: fixture `rollback()` before `pg_stat_activity` assertion. ## Test plan - [ ] CI green on SQLAlchemy 2.1.1 - [ ] No `SAWarning` for non-checked-in connections in integration suite - [ ] Disconnect failure messages include full `pg_stat_activity` row(s) if they ever fail again Linear Issue: [DIDI-453](https://linear.app/didi-build/issue/DIDI-453/ci-fix-pin-sqlalchemy-21-add-uv-lockfile-fix-websocket-disconnect)

hits.body: ## Summary **PR 3 of 3** for DIDI-453. Stacks on #22 (uv lockfile). Merge after PR 1 and PR 2. Lifts the SQLAlchemy `<2.1` cap; `uv.lock` now pins **2.1.1**. ## Root cause (SQLAlchemy 2.1) The WebSocket pipeline held one `AsyncSession` for the entire `process_message` call. After inserting the user message, `_persist_message` ran `commit()` then `refresh()`, which started a **new implicit transaction** (a `SELECT` for the row). While `run_council` blocked on LLM/graph work, that transaction stayed **idle in transaction**. When the client disconnected, the pipeline task was cancelled and awaited, but under 2.1 the connection was not reliably returned to the pool until the session was explicitly rolled back—so `pg_stat_activity` still showed a leaked backend. `run_council` did not use the pipeline session at all (persona nodes open their own sessions); the leak was from holding a checked-out session (and/or an implicit transaction from `refresh`) across the council await. ## Fix - `process_message` uses **short-lived sessions** for user and assistant persists; council runs with **no** pipeline session checked out. - `route_message` opens a DB session only for retrieval paths (not strategic council). - WebSocket pipeline no longer wraps `process_message` in a long-lived session. - Skip `refresh` on user-message persist; roll back fixture sessions before `pg_stat_activity` checks. - Set Postgres `application_name` from settings; disconnect integration tests filter on it. - ADR 0002 changelog entry for session hygiene. ## Tests - Existing disconnect integration test (scoped `application_name`). - New `test_pipeline_task_cancelled_mid_council_releases_db_connection`. ## Test plan - [ ] Full CI green on SQLAlchemy 2.1.1 with no `SAWarning` for non-checked-in connections - [ ] `uv lock --check` passes Linear Issue: [DIDI-453](https://linear.app/didi-build/issue/DIDI-453/ci-fix-pin-sqlalchemy-21-add-uv-lockfile-fix-websocket-disconnect)

hits.body: ## Summary Applies the same IPv6 loopback fix already proven for `domain-landing` to `domain-frontend`. Inside the container, `localhost` resolves to `::1` first, but nginx was only listening on IPv4 (`listen 80;`). The healthcheck's `wget http://localhost/app/` therefore failed with a connection refused on the IPv6 loopback. ## Changes - **`deploy/frontend/nginx.conf`** — add `listen [::]:80;` alongside `listen 80;` so nginx accepts connections on both stacks. - **`docker-compose.prod.yml`** — change `domain-frontend` healthcheck to `wget -qO- http://127.0.0.1/app/` (explicit IPv4 loopback), matching `domain-landing`. ## Verification After deploy/rebuild: ```bash docker inspect domain-frontend --format='{{json .State.Health}}' # expect "Status":"healthy" docker exec domain-frontend wget -qO- http://localhost/app/ # confirms dual-stack fix ```

hits.body: ## Problem `domain-landing`'s Docker healthcheck (`wget -qO- http://localhost/`) fails with "Connection refused" even though nginx starts cleanly and its config validates. Root cause: `nginx.conf` only had `listen 80;` (IPv4), but `localhost` resolves to the IPv6 loopback (`::1`) first inside the container, so the healthcheck hits an address nothing is listening on. ## Fix 1. **`deploy/landing/nginx.conf`** — add `listen [::]:80;` alongside the existing `listen 80;` so nginx binds on both IPv4 and IPv6. 2. **`docker-compose.prod.yml`** — change the healthcheck to `wget -qO- http://127.0.0.1/` (explicit IPv4 loopback) to remove hostname-resolution ambiguity. ## Verification After redeploy: ```bash docker inspect domain-landing --format='{{json .State.Health}}' # Status: "healthy" docker exec domain-landing wget -qO- http://localhost/ # succeeds (dual-stack fix) ```

This exercises the same non-editable wheel build path used by the Dockerfile (`RUN pip install --no-cache-dir .`), closing the gap where CI only ever ran `pip install -e ".[dev]"`. ## Test plan - [x] `pip install --no-cache-dir .` completes successfully (wheel builds and installs without duplicate-path error) - [ ] CI `package-build` job passes on this PR - [ ] Existing `test` job (editable install, lint, typecheck, tests) unchanged

Also fixes intermittent integration-test hangs caused by orphaned websocket pipeline tasks leaving idle-in-transaction DB connections. ### Persistence - Migration `004`: nullable `chat_messages.council_decision` JSONB (populated when `response_kind == council_result`) - New `write_back_proposals` table with one proposal per council message, feedback history, and status lifecycle - Migration `005`: `write_back_proposals.project_id` copied from source message for proper scoping ### Classification - hits.body: ## Summary Implements **Pass 1** of the domAIn knowledge layer: a deployable FastAPI backend where users can OAuth-connect GitHub and Linear, attach knowledge sources, index content into pgvector + Postgres FTS, and query via a shared hybrid retrieval function. Closes DIDI-370. ## What's included ### Application skeleton - FastAPI app (`src/domain/`) with health/readiness endpoints - API key auth middleware (`X-API-Key` header) - Docker + `docker-compose.yml` (Postgres/pgvector + API) - `environment.json` for Cloud Agent builds ### OAuth (authlib, hand-rolled per ADR 0002) - GitHub: `/oauth/github/authorize` → `/oauth/github/callback` - Linear: `/oauth/linear/authorize` → `/oauth/linear/callback` - `Connection` entity stores encrypted OAuth tokens per provider per user ### Knowledge sources - CRUD at `/sources` (create, list, get, delete, refresh) - `KnowledgeSource` with `github_repo` and `linear` source types (no file upload) - Four-state lifecycle: `pending` → `indexing` → `ready` / `error` - Background indexing pipeline: fetch → chunk (~512 tokens) → Voyage `voyage-context-4` embed → pgvector + `tsvector` ### Retrieval layer - `POST /retrieval/query` — shared entry point for all consumers - Parallel vector + keyword search → RRF merge (k=60) → coverage check - `can_access()` enforced on all reads ### Database - SQLAlchemy models: `Connection`, `KnowledgeSource`, `APIKey`, `Chunk` - Alembic migration with pgvector extension and GIN FTS index ### CI/CD - **CI** (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`): ruff, mypy, pytest on PR/push - **Deploy** (`.github/workflows/deploy.yml`): build/push image → Cloud Run on merge to `main` ## Testing - Unit tests: `can_access()`, RRF merge, coverage check, chunking (8 passing) - Integration smoke test: health endpoint (requires Postgres in CI) ## Deploy prerequisites Before Cloud Run deploy works, configure GitHub secrets: - `GCP_WORKLOAD_IDENTITY_PROVIDER`, `GCP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT`, `GCP_PROJECT_ID`, `GCP_REGION`, `GCP_ARTIFACT_REPO` - `APP_BASE_URL`, `GITHUB_REDIRECT_URI`, `LINEAR_REDIRECT_URI` - GCP Secret Manager secrets referenced in deploy workflow Register GitHub and Linear OAuth Apps with callback URLs matching the deployed service. ## Out of scope (later passes) - LangGraph supervisor + council subgraph - WebSocket chat streaming - Write-back handlers (GitHub PR, Linear update) - Frontend Linear Issue: [DIDI-370](https://linear.app/didi-build/issue/DIDI-370/pass-1-deployable-kl-foundation)

hits.body: ## Summary Implements Pass 2 of the Phase 1 unified chat surface (Linear DIDI-371): a supervisor intent router, simple handlers, WebSocket transport with manual API-key auth, chat persistence, and router eval dataset. ## Changes ### Unified chat API - **WebSocket** `GET /chat/ws?api_key=` — validates API key manually on connect (middleware does not cover WebSockets) - **REST** `GET /chat/sessions/{session_id}/messages` — retrieves persisted chat history for the authenticated actor - **Migration `002`** — adds `chat_messages` table (session id, role, content, classified intent, response kind, citations, timestamps) ### Supervisor router (`claude-haiku-4-5`) Classifies each message into one of five intents and dispatches: | Intent | Handler | Response kind | |--------|---------|---------------| | `greeting` | Template short-circuit (no retrieval) | `direct_answer` | | `simple_retrieval` | RAG via `retrieve()` + Claude answer with citations | `direct_answer` | | `strategic_session` | Council handoff stub (`domain.council.run_council`) | `council_pending_handoff` | | `linear_read` / `linear_write` | Stubs | `stub_not_implemented` | ### Chat wire contract - Pydantic schemas in `src/domain/schemas/chat.py` (`ChatMessageIn`, `ChatResponse`, `ResponseKind`, `ChatIntent`) - `response_kind` maps to design-system voice classes (`dom-msg--direct`, `dom-msg--pending`, plain text for stubs) ### Router eval - 72 labeled examples in `src/domain/chat/data/router_eval_dataset.json` - Scoring harness in `src/domain/chat/eval.py` + `scripts/eval_router.py` - Unit tests validate dataset coverage and scoring harness ### Model tier separation - Supervisor: `anthropic:claude-haiku-4-5` - Retrieval answers: `anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-20250514` - Council chair (Pass 3): separate stronger model config (`council_chair_model`) ### ADR updates - **ADR 0002** — Authentication model (API-key HTTP auth + WebSocket manual validation exception) - **ADR 0005** — Chat request/response data contract ## Test plan - [x] `ruff check src tests` - [x] `mypy src/domain` - [x] `pytest tests/unit` (22 passed) - [ ] `pytest tests/integration` (requires Postgres + `alembic upgrade head`) - [ ] Manual: connect WebSocket without API key → rejected - [ ] Manual: greeting → no retrieval call; knowledge question → grounded answer with citations - [ ] Optional: `python scripts/eval_router.py` with `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` set (targets ≥85% accuracy) ## Notes for Pass 3 `domain.council.run_council()` is a stub returning `council_pending_handoff`. Pass 3 should replace it with the full orchestrator-worker LangGraph subgraph without changing the router interface. Linear Issue: [DIDI-371](https://linear.app/didi-build/issue/DIDI-371/pass-2-unified-chat-router-simple-retrieval)

hits.body: ## Summary Implements Pass 2 of the Phase 1 unified chat surface (Linear DIDI-371): a supervisor intent router, simple handlers, WebSocket transport with manual API-key auth, chat persistence, and router eval dataset. ## Changes ### Unified chat API - **WebSocket** `GET /chat/ws?api_key=` — validates API key manually on connect (middleware does not cover WebSockets) - **REST** `GET /chat/sessions/{session_id}/messages` — retrieves persisted chat history for the authenticated actor - **Migration `002`** — adds `chat_messages` table (session id, role, content, classified intent, response kind, citations, timestamps) ### Supervisor router (`claude-haiku-4-5`) Classifies each message into one of five intents and dispatches: | Intent | Handler | Response kind | |--------|---------|---------------| | `greeting` | Template short-circuit (no retrieval) | `direct_answer` | | `simple_retrieval` | RAG via `retrieve()` + Claude answer with citations | `direct_answer` | | `strategic_session` | Council handoff stub (`domain.council.run_council`) | `council_pending_handoff` | | `linear_read` / `linear_write` | Stubs | `stub_not_implemented` | ### Chat wire contract - Pydantic schemas in `src/domain/schemas/chat.py` (`ChatMessageIn`, `ChatResponse`, `ResponseKind`, `ChatIntent`) - `response_kind` maps to design-system voice classes (`dom-msg--direct`, `dom-msg--pending`, plain text for stubs) ### Router eval - 72 labeled examples in `src/domain/chat/data/router_eval_dataset.json` - Scoring harness in `src/domain/chat/eval.py` + `scripts/eval_router.py` - Unit tests validate dataset coverage and scoring harness ### Model tier separation - Supervisor: `anthropic:claude-haiku-4-5` - Retrieval answers: `anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-20250514` - Council chair (Pass 3): separate stronger model config (`council_chair_model`) ### ADR updates - **ADR 0002** — Authentication model (API-key HTTP auth + WebSocket manual validation exception) - **ADR 0005** — Chat request/response data contract ## Test plan - [x] `ruff check src tests` - [x] `mypy src/domain` - [x] `pytest tests/unit` (22 passed) - [ ] `pytest tests/integration` (requires Postgres + `alembic upgrade head`) - [ ] Manual: connect WebSocket without API key → rejected - [ ] Manual: greeting → no retrieval call; knowledge question → grounded answer with citations - [ ] Optional: `python scripts/eval_router.py` with `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` set (targets ≥85% accuracy) ## Notes for Pass 3 `domain.council.run_council()` is a stub returning `council_pending_handoff`. Pass 3 should replace it with the full orchestrator-worker LangGraph subgraph without changing the router interface. Linear Issue: [DIDI-371](https://linear.app/didi-build/issue/DIDI-371/pass-2-unified-chat-router-simple-retrieval)

hits.body: ## Checkpoint (DIDI-434 scope 1) Records the **research spike** and planned browser auth model in ADR 0002. **No application code** in this PR — implementation waits until external GitHub/env setup is confirmed. ### Spike outcome **Use the existing GitHub App’s OAuth Client ID + secret** for “Sign in with GitHub” (`read:user`). Keep repo connection on the current installation flow (`/oauth/github/*`). Add a **separate** user OAuth callback at `/auth/github/callback`. Do **not** enable “Request user authorization (OAuth) during installation.” --- ## Manual checklist for Didi (outside the repo) Complete these before the implementation PR: ### GitHub App settings Open the domAIn GitHub App in GitHub → **Settings** (developer settings → GitHub Apps → your app). 1. **Identifying and authorizing users** - Set **Callback URL** to: `https://domain.didi.build/auth/github/callback` - For local dev (optional): GitHub Apps allow one user callback URL; either temporarily point it at `http://localhost:8000/auth/github/callback` while developing, or use only production and test login on the droplet. - **Generate a client secret** if none exists; store it securely (see env vars below). - Copy the **Client ID** shown on this page (this is **not** the numeric App ID used for `GITHUB_APP_ID` / JWT `iss`). 2. **Leave unchecked:** “Request user authorization (OAuth) during installation” — login and install stay separate UX flows. 3. **Do not change** installation / Setup URL behavior: - **Setup URL** (post-install redirect) remains: `https://domain.didi.build/oauth/github/callback` - Permissions stay repository-scoped as today (Contents, Pull requests, Metadata). 4. **Connections OAuth:** No changes to `/oauth/github/authorize` or installation callback semantics. ### Droplet / production env vars Add or update on the server (and in your secrets store for deploy): | Variable | Value / notes | |----------|----------------| | `GITHUB_APP_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID` | Client ID from “Identifying and authorizing users” | | `GITHUB_APP_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET` | Client secret from the same section | | `GITHUB_AUTH_REDIRECT_URI` | `https://domain.didi.build/auth/github/callback` | | `AUTH_ALLOWED_GITHUB_IDS` | Comma-separated **numeric** GitHub user IDs (no `@` handles) | | `SESSION_SECRET` | Long random string (e.g. `openssl rand -hex 32`) | | `SESSION_COOKIE_NAME` | Optional; default `domain_session` | | `SESSION_TTL_DAYS` | Optional; default `30` | | `WS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` | `https://domain.didi.build` (comma-separate if multiple) | Existing vars (`GITHUB_APP_ID`, `GITHUB_APP_SLUG`, `GITHUB_APP_PRIVATE_KEY_BASE64`, `APP_BASE_URL`, `BOOTSTRAP_API_KEY`, etc.) stay as they are. ### Find your numeric GitHub user ID for `AUTH_ALLOWED_GITHUB_IDS` Any of: ```bash curl -s https://api.github.com/users/ | jq .id ``` Or: sign in once after implementation and read `id` from server logs / DB — but for first deploy you need at least one ID preloaded. Example: `AUTH_ALLOWED_GITHUB_IDS=12345678` (use your real numeric id). --- **When the above is done**, confirm on the Linear issue and the agent can continue with migrations, `/auth/*` routes, session resolver, frontend screens `1f`/`1g`, and tests per DIDI-434. Linear Issue: [DIDI-434](https://linear.app/didi-build/issue/DIDI-434/auth-github-login-allowlist-session-cookies-replace-api-key-entry)

hits.body: ## Summary Implements **Pass 1** of the domAIn knowledge layer: a deployable FastAPI backend where users can OAuth-connect GitHub and Linear, attach knowledge sources, index content into pgvector + Postgres FTS, and query via a shared hybrid retrieval function. Closes DIDI-370. ## What's included ### Application skeleton - FastAPI app (`src/domain/`) with health/readiness endpoints - API key auth middleware (`X-API-Key` header) - Docker + `docker-compose.yml` (Postgres/pgvector + API) - `environment.json` for Cloud Agent builds ### OAuth (authlib, hand-rolled per ADR 0002) - GitHub: `/oauth/github/authorize` → `/oauth/github/callback` - Linear: `/oauth/linear/authorize` → `/oauth/linear/callback` - `Connection` entity stores encrypted OAuth tokens per provider per user ### Knowledge sources - CRUD at `/sources` (create, list, get, delete, refresh) - `KnowledgeSource` with `github_repo` and `linear` source types (no file upload) - Four-state lifecycle: `pending` → `indexing` → `ready` / `error` - Background indexing pipeline: fetch → chunk (~512 tokens) → Voyage `voyage-context-4` embed → pgvector + `tsvector` ### Retrieval layer - `POST /retrieval/query` — shared entry point for all consumers - Parallel vector + keyword search → RRF merge (k=60) → coverage check - `can_access()` enforced on all reads ### Database - SQLAlchemy models: `Connection`, `KnowledgeSource`, `APIKey`, `Chunk` - Alembic migration with pgvector extension and GIN FTS index ### CI/CD - **CI** (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`): ruff, mypy, pytest on PR/push - **Deploy** (`.github/workflows/deploy.yml`): build/push image → Cloud Run on merge to `main` ## Testing - Unit tests: `can_access()`, RRF merge, coverage check, chunking (8 passing) - Integration smoke test: health endpoint (requires Postgres in CI) ## Deploy prerequisites Before Cloud Run deploy works, configure GitHub secrets: - `GCP_WORKLOAD_IDENTITY_PROVIDER`, `GCP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT`, `GCP_PROJECT_ID`, `GCP_REGION`, `GCP_ARTIFACT_REPO` - `APP_BASE_URL`, `GITHUB_REDIRECT_URI`, `LINEAR_REDIRECT_URI` - GCP Secret Manager secrets referenced in deploy workflow Register GitHub and Linear OAuth Apps with callback URLs matching the deployed service. ## Out of scope (later passes) - LangGraph supervisor + council subgraph - WebSocket chat streaming - Write-back handlers (GitHub PR, Linear update) - Frontend Linear Issue: [DIDI-370](https://linear.app/didi-build/issue/DIDI-370/pass-1-deployable-kl-foundation)

hits.body: ## Summary Implements [DIDI-456](https://linear.app/didi-build/issue/DIDI-456): production env maintenance on the droplet without re-prompting every variable, deploy-time validation, and safe rewrites when the template grows. - **`deploy/generate-env.sh`** - `--missing` — prompts only for template keys absent from the env file (empty-but-present keys are not missing); exits without rewriting when up to date; summarizes added keys; supports `--env-file`. - `--check` — non-interactive; lists missing template keys and exits 1; never prints values. - Preserves keys in the env file that are not in `.env.production.example`, appended under `# Not in .env.production.example (kept):` with a warning (no values). - `SESSION_SECRET` generator (same flow as `BOOTSTRAP_API_KEY`). - **`deploy/deploy.sh`** — runs `generate-env.sh --check` after the env file existence check; aborts with the `--missing` fix command. - **`.env.production.example` / `.env.example`** — eight browser-login variables per ADR 0002 (DIDI-434). - **README** — “Adding a new env var” workflow and note that deploy runs `--check`. - **CI** — `deploy/tests/test_generate_env.sh` job. ## Verification ```bash bash deploy/tests/test_generate_env.sh ``` Covers `--check` (incomplete/complete), `--missing` (heredoc input, blank `VOYAGE_BASE_URL`, unknown key preservation, no rewrite when up to date), and `deploy.sh` failing before `source` when keys are missing. Linear Issue: [DIDI-456](https://linear.app/didi-build/issue/DIDI-456/env-script-missing-and-check-modes-preserve-unknown-keys-add-didi-434)

hits.body: ## Summary Implements the Pass 4b core chat UI as a Vite + React + TypeScript PWA served at `/app`. - **Project scaffold:** Vite + React + TypeScript with `vite-plugin-pwa` (manifest + service worker) - **WebSocket client:** connects to `/chat/ws?api_key=...`, sends `ChatMessageIn`, handles `ChatStatusUpdate` frames before the final `ChatResponse` - **`ChatMessage` voices:** `you`, `direct`, `ux`, `dx`, `biz`, `chair`, and extended `pending` (supervisor status band + per-seat UX/DX/BP chips that settle independently) - **Persona mapping:** backend `PERSONA_IDS` (`ux`, `dev_experience`, `business`) → design-system marks (`UX`, `DX`, `BP`) - **`Composer`:** textarea + ready-source-count hint + Send only — no routing control - **`VerdictBadge`:** rendered on persona messages and the chair block - **Chat history:** loaded via `GET /chat/sessions/{id}/messages` on connect / refresh ## Design constraints honored - No mode selector anywhere in the composer - Pending council state occupies the same thread slot as the eventual chair block (in-place swap, no insert-then-remove) - Status is conveyed by text labels (supervisor band + seat captions), not color alone ## Review fixes - **`activeCouncilIdRef`:** now a real `useRef(null)` instead of a `useMemo`-created object - **`ChatMessageOut`:** includes `write_back_proposal: WriteBackProposalOut | null` matching `domain/schemas/writeback.py` (type only; no UI yet) - **Design-system CSS import:** confirmed in browser via `npm run dev` — tokens and component styles apply (`--color-bg-canvas`, `--color-accent`, Inter typography) ## Deploy / CI - Adds `domain-frontend` nginx container and Caddy `/app/*` routing - CI builds, type-checks, tests, and verifies the frontend bundle ## Test plan - [x] `npm test` (persona mapping, frame guards, pending state updates) - [x] `npm run build` - [x] `npm run dev` — design-system CSS confirmed rendering in browser - [ ] Manual: connect with API key, send greeting (direct voice) - [ ] Manual: send strategic review prompt, observe live council status then council result - [ ] Manual: refresh mid-session and confirm history reload Linear Issue: [DIDI-380](https://linear.app/didi-build/issue/DIDI-380/pass-4b-core-chat-ui)

Closes the gap between this repo and what current budgeting apps (Monarch, Copilot, YNAB) do, and fixes several defects found along the way.

## Features

| Feature | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| **Categorisation rules** | ~100 built-in UK merchant rules run *before* the AI classifier — deterministic, free, instant. Pattern preview and backfill of existing transactions. |
| **Accounts & net worth** | Six asset + three liability types with balance-snapshot history. Net worth over time cannot be derived from transactions alone — opening balances, investment growth and property revaluations never appear as one. |
| **Recurring detection** | Statistical rather than a merchant list: groups by a normalised merchant key and matches the median gap against six cadences. Works on plain CSV data, needs no maintenance. |
| **Savings goals** | Required monthly contribution, projected completion, on-track/behind pacing. A linked account is the single source of truth, so the two figures cannot drift. |
| **Insights & anomalies** | Month-over-month category moves, unusual charges vs. the median for that merchant, month-end projection. Renders nothing when there is nothing worth saying. |
| **Bulk editing & filters** | Multi-select, bulk recategorise/delete, uncategorised and money-in/out filters. |
| **Email** | Wired to real triggers for the first time: welcome, budget alerts, weekly summary, plus a cron endpoint. |

## Bugs fixed

Several were silently broken in ways that mattered:

- **Imports never set `categoryId`.** AI classification wrote only the free-text `aiClassified`, so imported transactions appeared uncategorised in the UI while analytics saw a category.
- **New users got zero categories.** They were only ever created by the seed script, so a fresh account could not categorise anything.
- **Search was case-sensitive.** Postgres `LIKE` meant searching `tesco` matched nothing, because bank descriptions are uppercase. Now `ILIKE`, and it searches merchant as well as description.
- **The `necessityType` filter did nothing.** Present in the schema, never applied by the router.
- **`@finance/analytics` pulled the Postgres driver into the browser** via a value import from `@finance/db` in a client-safe export. Broke every page importing that package.
- **Turbo strict env mode hid `DATABASE_URL`**, making `db:generate` / `db:migrate` unusable. Migrations now work; the existing `0000` migration has been baselined.
- **Playwright and dev fought over `apps/web/.next`** — Playwright started `next dev` without `--turbopack` while the dev script uses it, so running E2E poisoned the dev server with mixed chunks.
- **Weekly summary subject was hardcoded to `$`** in a GBP app.
- **Middleware whitelisted `/api/webhooks(.*)`**, which matched no route; the actual Stripe webhook is at `/api/stripe/webhook`.

## Verification

- `pnpm typecheck` — clean
- `pnpm lint` — clean, zero warnings
- **231 unit tests**, **61 integration tests** against real Postgres
- `pnpm test:e2e` — passing
- `pnpm build` — clean, all new routes present

## Not covered

The new pages compile, build, respond correctly and their backends are integration-tested, but they have not been reviewed visually by a signed-in user. Worth a look before relying on them.

Credential setup (Clerk, OpenAI, Stripe, Plaid, Resend, cron secret) is collected in `HUMAN_TASKS.md` rather than done here.

hits.body:
## Summary

De-slops the project into a first-class portfolio piece: removes the AI-generated mascot sprite system and unifies the web and mobile apps on a single, cleanly-coded lucide icon language. Net **~3,600 lines deleted vs ~1,700 added** — the codebase got substantially smaller.

- Deletes the 29-pose mascot PNG set, two sprite sheets, the `Mascot` component, and the `MascotName` type
- Introduces `IconChip` in `@finance/ui` (lucide icon on the existing pastel surface), mirrored by an identical component in the Expo app so web + mobile read as one product
- Deletes purely decorative sprites outright (plus the negative-margin hacks and wrapper divs that only existed to position them) rather than swapping in replacements
- Replaces the smiley-coin brand mark with a clean geometric SVG, now wired as the favicon
- Rewrites marketing/product copy that shipped internal strategy-memo language ("pricing hypothesis", "a safer wedge") and mascot voice ("Buddy tracks these") into user-facing text
- Removes AI design-prompt packs and dated planning logs from `docs/`

## Bugs fixed along the way (not cosmetic)

- **Dashboard month scoping** — the Expenses card showed an all-time transaction count under a month-scoped amount, and Recent Activity ignored the month picker entirely. Both now follow the selected month.
- **Currency formatting** — the monthly overview chart formatted money as US dollars via a local formatter while the rest of the app used GBP.
- **Chart render** — a React key warning fired on every chart render; the spending chart's reveal animation never completed under a throttled frame rate, leaving the line visibly truncated.
- **Mobile accessibility** — the icon-only tab bar exposed no accessible name, role, or selected state (VoiceOver announced six unlabeled buttons); now matches the web nav's `sr-only` labels.

## New capability

- Month navigation on the mobile dashboard, via a tested `stepMonth` helper + `useMonthCursor` hook that also de-duplicates the month-rollover logic previously copied across screens.

## Testing

- `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, **106 unit tests**, and `pnpm build` all pass
- New logic went in test-first (`IconChip`, `stepMonth`)
- Web verified against a seeded Postgres (145 transactions / 8 months) signed in as a real Clerk user — every dashboard page read via screenshot; CSV import confirmed end-to-end (35 rows landed); month navigation re-scopes data (July 20 tx, June 17)
- Mobile app builds and runs on the iPhone 17 Pro simulator and reaches the API

### Caveat
- Mobile screens were exercised in mock-auth mode, which sends no Clerk token, so they rendered £0 — the server log confirms requests arrived and were simply unauthorized, so the data path is sound, but real data was not seen rendering on the phone.

## Operational blast radius
None. No migrations, no env-var changes, no data backfills. Pure code/asset changes. Rollback = revert the branch.

Closes the gap between this repo and what current budgeting apps (Monarch, Copilot, YNAB) do, and fixes several defects found along the way.

## Features

| Feature | Notes |
| --- | --- |
| **Categorisation rules** | ~100 built-in UK merchant rules run *before* the AI classifier — deterministic, free, instant. Pattern preview and backfill of existing transactions. |
| **Accounts & net worth** | Six asset + three liability types with balance-snapshot history. Net worth over time cannot be derived from transactions alone — opening balances, investment growth and property revaluations never appear as one. |
| **Recurring detection** | Statistical rather than a merchant list: groups by a normalised merchant key and matches the median gap against six cadences. Works on plain CSV data, needs no maintenance. |
| **Savings goals** | Required monthly contribution, projected completion, on-track/behind pacing. A linked account is the single source of truth, so the two figures cannot drift. |
| **Insights & anomalies** | Month-over-month category moves, unusual charges vs. the median for that merchant, month-end projection. Renders nothing when there is nothing worth saying. |
| **Bulk editing & filters** | Multi-select, bulk recategorise/delete, uncategorised and money-in/out filters. |
| **Email** | Wired to real triggers for the first time: welcome, budget alerts, weekly summary, plus a cron endpoint. |

## Bugs fixed

Several were silently broken in ways that mattered:

- **Imports never set `categoryId`.** AI classification wrote only the free-text `aiClassified`, so imported transactions appeared uncategorised in the UI while analytics saw a category.
- **New users got zero categories.** They were only ever created by the seed script, so a fresh account could not categorise anything.
- **Search was case-sensitive.** Postgres `LIKE` meant searching `tesco` matched nothing, because bank descriptions are uppercase. Now `ILIKE`, and it searches merchant as well as description.
- **The `necessityType` filter did nothing.** Present in the schema, never applied by the router.
- **`@finance/analytics` pulled the Postgres driver into the browser** via a value import from `@finance/db` in a client-safe export. Broke every page importing that package.
- **Turbo strict env mode hid `DATABASE_URL`**, making `db:generate` / `db:migrate` unusable. Migrations now work; the existing `0000` migration has been baselined.
- **Playwright and dev fought over `apps/web/.next`** — Playwright started `next dev` without `--turbopack` while the dev script uses it, so running E2E poisoned the dev server with mixed chunks.
- **Weekly summary subject was hardcoded to `$`** in a GBP app.
- **Middleware whitelisted `/api/webhooks(.*)`**, which matched no route; the actual Stripe webhook is at `/api/stripe/webhook`.

- `pnpm lint` — clean, zero warnings
- **231 unit tests**, **61 integration tests** against real Postgres
- `pnpm test:e2e` — passing
- `pnpm build` — clean, all new routes present

## Not covered

The new pages compile, build, respond correctly and their backends are integration-tested, but they have not been reviewed visually by a signed-in user. Worth a look before relying on them.

Credential setup (Clerk, OpenAI, Stripe, Plaid, Resend, cron secret) is collected in `HUMAN_TASKS.md` rather than done here.

## Summary

De-slops the project into a first-class portfolio piece: removes the AI-generated mascot sprite system and unifies the web and mobile apps on a single, cleanly-coded lucide icon language. Net **~3,600 lines deleted vs ~1,700 added** — the codebase got substantially smaller.

- Deletes the 29-pose mascot PNG set, two sprite sheets, the `Mascot` component, and the `MascotName` type
- Introduces `IconChip` in `@finance/ui` (lucide icon on the existing pastel surface), mirrored by an identical component in the Expo app so web + mobile read as one product
- Deletes purely decorative sprites outright (plus the negative-margin hacks and wrapper divs that only existed to position them) rather than swapping in replacements
- Replaces the smiley-coin brand mark with a clean geometric SVG, now wired as the favicon
- Rewrites marketing/product copy that shipped internal strategy-memo language ("pricing hypothesis", "a safer wedge") and mascot voice ("Buddy tracks these") into user-facing text
- Removes AI design-prompt packs and dated planning logs from `docs/`

## Bugs fixed along the way (not cosmetic)

- **Dashboard month scoping** — the Expenses card showed an all-time transaction count under a month-scoped amount, and Recent Activity ignored the month picker entirely. Both now follow the selected month.
- **Currency formatting** — the monthly overview chart formatted money as US dollars via a local formatter while the rest of the app used GBP.
- **Chart render** — a React key warning fired on every chart render; the spending chart's reveal animation never completed under a throttled frame rate, leaving the line visibly truncated.
- **Mobile accessibility** — the icon-only tab bar exposed no accessible name, role, or selected state (VoiceOver announced six unlabeled buttons); now matches the web nav's `sr-only` labels.

## New capability

- Month navigation on the mobile dashboard, via a tested `stepMonth` helper + `useMonthCursor` hook that also de-duplicates the month-rollover logic previously copied across screens.

## Testing

- `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, **106 unit tests**, and `pnpm build` all pass
- New logic went in test-first (`IconChip`, `stepMonth`)
- Web verified against a seeded Postgres (145 transactions / 8 months) signed in as a real Clerk user — every dashboard page read via screenshot; CSV import confirmed end-to-end (35 rows landed); month navigation re-scopes data (July 20 tx, June 17)
- Mobile app builds and runs on the iPhone 17 Pro simulator and reaches the API

### Caveat
- Mobile screens were exercised in mock-auth mode, which sends no Clerk token, so they rendered £0 — the server log confirms requests arrived and were simply unauthorized, so the data path is sound, but real data was not seen rendering on the phone.

## Operational blast radius
None. No migrations, no env-var changes, no data backfills. Pure code/asset changes. Rollback = revert the branch.

hits.message:
feat: add categorisation rules engine with account provisioning

Frontier budgeting apps categorise deterministically before reaching for a
model. This adds a rules layer that runs ahead of the AI classifier.

- categorization_rules table with match type/field, priority and usage counters
- pure matcher (contains/starts_with/equals/regex) with specificity tiebreaks
- ~100 built-in UK merchant rules seeded per user, editable like any other
- rules CRUD router with pattern preview and apply-to-existing backfill
- rules management page, linked from the sidebar

Fixes two defects found along the way:

1. createMany wrote aiClassified (free text) but never categoryId, so imported
   transactions showed as uncategorised in the UI while analytics saw a
   category. Both fields plus necessityScore are now written together.

2. Categories are per-user and were only ever created by the seed script, so a
   brand-new account had none at all. ensureUserDefaults provisions categories
   and starter rules on signup, import, and rules access.

Also declares env vars in turbo.json globalEnv — strict env mode was filtering
DATABASE_URL out of task environments, which made db:generate/db:migrate
unusable. Baselined the existing 0000 migration so db:migrate now works.

126 unit tests, 24 integration tests against real Postgres.
